children.text: // nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhi</s> (Purification of the Import of the <s>Nyāyavārttika</s>) //

children.text: mātaḥ sarasvati punaḥ punaraṣa natvā
children.translated_text: O Mother <s>Sarasvatī</s>, having bowed to you again and again,

children.text: baddhāñjaliḥ kimapi vijñapayāmyavaihi /
children.translated_text: with palms joined, I humbly submit something — please know:

children.text: vākcetasormama tathā bhava sāvadhānā
children.translated_text: may you be so attentive to my speech and mind

children.text: vācaspatervacasi na skhalato yathaite //
children.translated_text: that these [words] may not stumble in the utterance of <s>Vācaspati</s> (the Lord of Speech).

children.text:
viśvārādhya ityatra viśvaśabdena saṃsāricetanavargo vivakṣitaḥ, tasyaiva tadārādhakatvāt /
viśveśāna ityatra samīhitaphalasaṃdohaḥ, tasya bhagavadekādhīnatvāt /
viśvakṛdityatropādānasamūhaḥ, tasyaiva tatkṛtivyāpyatvāt /
viśvasaṃhārakārītyatra yāvadanityanivahaḥ, tasyaiva tadvināśyatvāt /
viśvaśaktirityatra yāvatkāryāstomaḥ, tasyaiva tacchaktiviṣayatvāt /
viśvajñātetyatra yāvañjñeyaprapañcaḥ, tasyaiva pajjñānaviṣayatvāt /
viśvavyāpīyatra yāvanmūrttimaddravyarāśiḥ, tasyaiva viśeṣatastadvyāpyatvāt /
itarasya tu taddvārā /
viśvamūrtirityatra yāvatkārakagrāmaḥ, tasyaiva sākṣāt tatprayatnādhiṣṭheyatayā asmadādiśarīrasamānatvāt /
ata eva na tatra śarīrāntarāpekṣā, sākṣātprayantānadhiṣṭheyeṣu hi sā syāt daṇḍādivat /
na tu sākṣātprayatnādhiṣṭheyeṣu śarīravat /
children.translated_text: but not in things directly governed by effort, like the body.

children.text: pinākīti tu viśiṣṭaśastradhāradhamittaka nāmasaṃkortanena prārabdhavighnasya protsāraṇameva samīhitamiti sūcayati /
children.translated_text: The epithet '<s>Pinākī</s>' (bearer of the trident) indicates, by the mere mention of the name signifying the bearer of a distinguished weapon, the purpose of driving away obstacles already begun.

children.text: hetuhetumadbhāvena śaḍkottarābhyāṃ yojanā jyāyasī /
children.translated_text: The interpretation [of the two verses] in terms of cause and effect is better than the one [combining them] as one unit.

children.text: yathāvasthitayojanāyāṃ tu arthapaunarūktyaprasarktā stutitvameva samādhānamadhyavaseyam iti //
children.translated_text: In the interpretation that takes [the words] as they stand, since repetition of meaning would follow, one should conclude that the justification is simply that it is a hymn of praise.

In the expression '<s>viśvārādhya</s>' (worshipped by all), the word '<s>viśva</s>' (all) refers to the class of conscious beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of transmigration), since it is they alone who worship Him. In the expression '<s>viśveśāna</s>' (lord of all), it refers to the totality of desired fruits, since these depend on the Blessed One alone. In the expression '<s>viśvakṛt</s>' (maker of all), it refers to the totality of material causes, since it is these alone that are pervaded by His creative activity. In the expression '<s>viśvasaṃhārakārī</s>' (destroyer of all), it refers to the totality of impermanent things, since it is these alone that are subject to His destruction. In the expression '<s>viśvaśakti</s>' (omnipotent), it refers to the totality of effects, since it is these alone that are the domain of His power. In the expression '<s>viśvajñāta</s>' (knower of all), it refers to the entire expanse of knowable objects, since it is these alone that are the domain of His knowledge. In the expression '<s>viśvavyāpī</s>' (all-pervading), it refers to the totality of corporeal substances, since it is these that are specifically pervaded by Him; but in the case of the other [i.e., non-corporeal], it is through those [corporeal substances]. In the expression '<s>viśvamūrti</s>' (of universal form), it refers to the totality of agents, since it is these alone that, being directly governed by His effort, are analogous to our own bodies. For that very reason, no dependence on another body is needed there, for that [dependence] would exist in things not directly governed by effort, like a stick,

children.text:
namāmītyādi /
dharmo nivartakaḥ /
vijñānaṃ śarīrādiviviktātmasākṣātkāraḥ /
vairāgyaṃ rāgābhāvaḥ /
aiśvaryaṃ bhūtendriyajayaḥ /
tacchānipe, ata eva nidhaye vāgviśaddhīnām /
adharmahetuko hyavivekaḥ /
avivekahetukamavairāgyam, avairāgyamūlamanaiśvaryam /
tanmūlāśca vacasāmaviśuddhayaḥ /
tisraḥ khalvetāḥ /
tatra prathamā nirabhidhayatā /
dvitīyā viparītāmidheyatā /
tṛtīyā niṣprayojanāmigheyatā /
tā etāḥ kathaṃ bhūtendriyajayino mahāmunerbhaviṣyanti? ajitabhūtasya hi vivakṣostathāvidhaprayatnāniṣpatternirabhidheyā vāk bhavati /
ajitendriyasya ca viparyāsavipralipsāhetuko viparītārtho vacanasandarbhaḥ /
ajitamanasaśca pramādonmādavato niṣprayojanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And for one who has not conquered the mind, being subject to carelessness and madness, [speech is] purposeless.

children.text: etāśca vacasāmaviśuddhīḥ chalajātinigrahasthāneṣu sūtrakāra eva prapañcayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: These impurities of speech will be elaborated by the <s>sūtra</s>-author himself in the sections on sophistry (<s>chala</s>), futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>), and points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>).

children.text: so 'yaṃ na tatheti bhavati vāgviśuddhīnāṃ nidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since he is not like that, he is the repository of purities of speech.

children.text: ata eva tāyī tattvādhyavasāyasaṃrakṣaṇakṣamasaṃpradāyapravartakaḥ //
children.translated_text: For that very reason, he is the Protector — the one who propagates the tradition capable of safeguarding the ascertainment of reality.

'I bow' and so forth. <s>Dharma</s> (merit) is the remover [of suffering]. <s>Vijñāna</s> (knowledge) is the direct realization of the self as distinct from the body and the like. <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion) is the absence of attachment. <s>Aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) is mastery over the elements and the senses. Of the one who possesses that [sovereignty], therefore [he is] the repository of purities of speech. For non-discrimination is caused by <s>adharma</s> (demerit); non-dispassion is caused by non-discrimination; lack of sovereignty is rooted in non-dispassion; and the impurities of speech are rooted in that [lack of sovereignty]. There are indeed three [impurities of speech]. Among them, the first is non-expressiveness [i.e., failing to convey meaning]. The second is conveying the wrong meaning. The third is conveying a purposeless meaning. How could these arise for the Great Sage who has mastery over the elements and the senses? For the speech of one who has not conquered the elements, when he desires to speak, becomes non-expressive due to the failure of the requisite effort. And for one who has not conquered the senses, the composition of words conveys wrong meaning due to error and the desire to deceive.

children.text:
evaṃ parāparagurūn natvā śiṣyabuddhisamādhānāya samāhitavaiśiṣṭyaṃ darśayati--grantheti /
nanu tātparyaṭīketi vadatā pravṛttipāṭavārthaṃ granthasaṃkṣepo darśitaḥ, na ca śiṣyāṇāṃ kathantāsaṃboghavidhurāṇāṃ rāddhāntamātraparigrahaḥ saṃkṣepato vivakṣitaḥ /
tathātve vā upaniṣada eva santu /
children.translated_text: If that were the case, let there simply be <s>Upaniṣads</s> (i.e., short aphoristic statements).

children.text: santu vā śavamuṣṭinyāyenācāryopadeśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Or let there be the instructions of the teacher, in the manner of the fist-holding-the-corpse principle [i.e., blindly following without understanding].

children.text: kimanenetyata āha--nirastākhiladūṣaṇeti /
children.translated_text: What is the use of this [further elaboration]? To that he says: 'with all objections removed.'

children.text: nanvevaṃ granthatātparyāṃ vyākhyeyam, dūṣaṇāni ca nirasyānīti punarapi granthagauravamityata āha--granthavyākhyācchalenaiveti //
children.translated_text: Now, if the import of the work is to be explained and objections are to be removed, that again results in prolixity of the work — to that he says: 'under the pretext of explaining the work itself.'

Having thus bowed to the teachers of both [the earlier and later traditions], he displays the established distinction [of his work] for the purpose of satisfying the understanding of students — with 'the work' (<s>grantha</s>). Now, by saying 'a commentary on the import' (<s>tātparyaṭīkā</s>), brevity of the work has been indicated for the purpose of ease of practice. But the intent is not merely the grasp of conclusions in summary form, for students who are not free from the affliction of wondering 'how so?'

children.text:
nanu cirantare 'smin nibandhe mahājanaparigṛhīte bahavo nibandhāstathāvidhāḥ santīti kṛtamanene ityata āha-- icchāmīti /
nanu yadi granthakārasaṃpradāyavicchedena te nibandhāḥ, kathaṃ kunibandhāḥ? atha saṃpradāyo vicchinnaḥ, kathaṃ tavāpīyaṃ vicchinnasaṃpradāyā tātparyaṭīkā sunibandha ityata āha--atijaratīnāmiti /
uddyotakarasaṃpradāyo hyamūṣāṃ yauvanam /
children.translated_text: The tradition of <s>Uddyotakara</s> was indeed the youth of those [commentaries].

children.text: tacca kālaparipākavaśād galitamiva /
children.translated_text: And that [youth] has, as it were, faded away due to the maturation of time.

children.text: kiṃ nāmātra trilocanaguroḥ sakāśādupadeśarasāyanamāsāditamamūṣāṃ punarnavībhāvāya dīyata iti yujyate /
children.translated_text: What is meant is that it is fitting to administer the elixir of instruction obtained from the teacher <s>Trilocana</s> (Three-Eyed [<s>Śiva</s>]) for the rejuvenation of those [aged commentaries].

children.text: na ca kunibandhapaṅkamagnānāṃ taddātumucitamatastasmādutkṛṣya svanibandhasthale sanniveśanarūpasamuddharaṇameva sāṃpratamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But it is not proper to give that [elixir] to those sunk in the mud of poor commentaries; therefore, the present course of action is to rescue them by lifting them out and placing them on the ground of one's own commentary.

Now, in the case of this long-standing composition [the <s>Nyāyavārttika</s>], accepted by the learned, there already exist many commentaries of such a kind — so what is the use of this one? To that he says: 'I desire.' Now, if those commentaries are [deficient] due to the break in the tradition of the original author, how are they poor commentaries? Or if the tradition is broken, how is your commentary too, with its broken tradition, a good commentary? To that he says: 'of those that have grown very old.'

children.text:
tatra bhagavato 'kṣapādasya muniṣu madhye pravaratvaṃ śrutyādibhya eva suprasiddham kimanena saṃkīrtanena? na caitadatiśayena sāṃpratamupayujyate /
jagadupaśamanidānaśāstrapraṇetṛtvaṃ ca tasya tatpraṇayanameva prakaṭayadasti /
tenāpi kiṃ prakaṭitena? svanibandhasya tadviṣayatāpi tadvyākhyānādeva labhyata iti /
kiṃ tayāpi kathitayā? na cāsya nyāyamahodadherūttānatāpratibhāsa evāgrataḥ kartumucitaḥ /
tasmād bhavitavyamatra tātparyeṇa /
tadāha--atheti /
tadapanīyata iti /
taditi digrāgādisamutthāpitaṃ śāstrācchādakaṃ kuhetusaṃtamasamapaneyatvena parāmṛśatā śāstrasyaivāyaṃ nibandha iti darśitam /
bhāṣyasya ca tadvivaraṇarūpasya śāstraśarīrarūpatayā na śāstrādādhikyaṃ manyate, mīmāṃsāyā iva vedāt /
ata eva nātratyaṭīkāyāḥ vāttikāntena virodhaḥ /
etena śāstrasya yo nibandho bhāṣyagranthaḥ sa kutārkikājñānanivṛttihetuḥ kariṣyata iti vyākhyānaṃ ṭīkāvirodhenopekṣaṇīyam /
nanu sūtroktaprayojanānuvādaḥ punaḥ kimartham? na hīdamanūdya kiñcid vidheyaṃ pratiṣedhyaṃ veha vidyate ityata āha--sūtreti /
atha svanibandhasya prayojanavattāpradarśanena kiṃ siddhyatītyata āha--prekṣāvaditi /
nanu vyutpitsavo vyutpattimaghikṛtya pravartante /
ato vyutpādanapravṛttau vyutpattirevāmīṣāṃ prayojanamiti kimapareṇa prayojanenetyata āha--vyutpādamātrasyeti /
children.translated_text: Now, the pre-eminence of the Blessed One <s>Akṣapāda</s> among sages is already well-established from scripture and the like — what is the use of mentioning it? Nor is this extravagance currently beneficial. And his authorship of the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) that is the means of the world's pacification is already made manifest by its very composition. What is the use of manifesting that too? The fact that his own commentary relates to that [subject] is already obtained from the commentary itself. What is the use of stating that too? And one should not create the false appearance of shallowness in this ocean of logic at the very outset. Therefore, there must be a deeper purport here. To that he says: 'Now' (<s>atha</s>). 'That is to be removed' — by the word 'that,' referring to the obscuring mass of bad arguments and doctrines raised by opponents and the like, and by treating it as something to be removed, it is shown that this commentary is about the <s>śāstra</s> itself. And since the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary), being an exposition of that [<s>śāstra</s>], has the nature of the body of the <s>śāstra</s>, it is not considered to be in excess of the <s>śāstra</s>, just as the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> [commentary] is not in excess of the <s>Veda</s>. For that very reason, there is no contradiction between the present sub-commentary and the end of the <s>Vārttika</s>. By this, the interpretation that 'the commentary on the <s>śāstra</s>, namely the <s>Bhāṣya</s> text, will be the cause of removing the ignorance of false reasoners' should be set aside as contradicting the sub-commentary. Now, what is the purpose of repeating the purpose already stated in the <s>sūtra</s>? For there is nothing here to be prescribed or prohibited by restating it — to that he says: 'in the <s>sūtra</s>.' Now, what is accomplished by demonstrating the purposefulness of one's own work? To that he says: 'a discerning person.' Now, those desiring instruction proceed with reference to instruction [as the goal]. So instruction itself is their purpose in engaging in the act of instruction — what need is there for another purpose? To that he says: 'of mere instruction.'

children.text:
dvividhaṃ hi prayojanaṃ mukhyaṃ gauṇa ca /
tatra mukhyaṃ puruṣārtha eva /
itarat tu tadaṅgamiti /
tatra mukhyārthinaḥ tatsādhānamabhyarthayamānāḥ tatra pravartanta iti tadapi prayojanamevati /
ato mukhye prayojane sati gauṇaṃ prayojanam,
children.translated_text: Purpose is indeed twofold: primary and secondary. The primary purpose is nothing other than the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human goal) itself. The secondary is an ancillary to that. Those who seek the primary goal, desiring the means to it, engage in that [secondary activity] too, so that too is indeed a purpose. Thus, given the primary purpose, the secondary purpose [also exists],

children.text:
tasmistvasati tadapi na syāditi niṣprayojanataivāvatiṣṭhate /
na ca svātantryeṇaivāsya mukhyaṃ prayojanamastītyato yasyedamaṅga tasya mukhyaṃ prayojanamastīti darśite prekṣāvān pravarttito bhavatītyabhisandhiḥ vārttikakṛta ityarthaḥ /
ito 'pi ṭīkākhaṇḍalakādantarbhāvitaphalavatsannidhāvaphalaṃ tadaṅgamiti nyāyāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, by the principle that what is proximate to the result — as included within the [hierarchy from] sub-commentary to the main text — is purposeless [on its own] when taken as merely ancillary to the result-bearing [main text],

children.text: śāstrāṅgāmevedaṃ na bhāṣyāṅgamiti mantavyam /
children.translated_text: this [sub-commentary] should be understood as ancillary to the <s>śāstra</s> itself, not as ancillary to the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: na hi bhāṣyasya svātantryeṇa mukhyaṃ prayojanamasti yena vārttikaṃ tadaṅgatāmiyāt /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Bhāṣya</s> does not independently have a primary purpose by virtue of which the <s>Vārttika</s> would attain ancillary status to it.

children.text: tasmād yathāśruti sundaramiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the reading] 'beautiful as it stands' is correct.

but in the absence of the former, the latter too would not exist — so purposelessness alone remains. And since this [instruction] does not independently have a primary purpose, it is when the primary purpose of that [human goal] to which this is ancillary has been shown that the discerning person is motivated to engage — this is the intention of the <s>Vārttika</s>-author.

children.text:
nanu karmendriyaniyamaḥ śama iti suprasiddhaṃ śānto dānta ityādi upaniṣatsu, na cāsau puruṣārthaḥ /
ato na mukhyaṃ prayojanamityata āha--atra ceti /
nanu jagataḥ śamāyeti durghaṭam, asaṃbhāvitātvādaśakyātvācca /
na tāvat kaścit jagadupacikīrṣuḥ kvacit pravartate yato munerapi tathātvaṃ saṃbhāvayāmaḥ /
paṭhanti ca--munerapi vanasthasyetyādi /
na ca śakyametat, bubhukṣūṇāṃ pravartayitumaśakyatvāt /
na ca jagadeva mumukṣati /
tasmādanuṣṭhātaiva vyutpādyaḥ śāstrāntaralabdhabrāhmaṇatvadirūpaḥ śiṣyaḥ /
tasya ca rūpāṇi śamadamādisaṃpattiḥ nityānityavivekaḥ aihikāmuṣmikabhāgavairāgyaṃ mumukṣutā ceti /
yastu anadhikāryeva pravartate karmakāṇḍa iva brahmakāṇḍe sa na phalabhāg bhavati /
tatraitat syāt /
na tāvadupeyaviṣayeyamadhikāracintā, tasya puruṣaprayatnāviṣayatvāt, iṣyamāṇatāmātrasya cāniṣadhāt /
kiṃ nāma upāyaviṣayā, tasyaiva śāstraviṣayatvāt, puruṣapravṛttiviṣayatvācca /
iha cāpavarga iva tadarthatayā tattvajñānamapyupeyameva, asiddhatvāt /
upāyastu pramāṇam, na ca vedādhyayanavadanumānasya pratyakṣasya copādānaṃ śūdrādikaṃ prati niṣiddham, yena tatrāpyetasyānadhikāraḥ syāt /
tathā sati dhūmādapi vahimadhigacchan pratyakṣād vā pratyavāyī syāt, adhīyāna iva vedam /
na cātmagocare pratyakṣānumāne śūdrāderviśeṣato niṣiddhe snātasya caṇḍāladarśanamiva brāhmaṇādeḥ prāyaścittānupadeśāt pratyuta
children.translated_text: Now, the restraint of the action-senses is <s>śama</s> (tranquility) — this is well-known from the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, such as 'tranquil, self-controlled,' etc. But that is not a <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human goal). So there is no primary purpose — to that he says: 'and here.' Now, [the purpose] 'for the pacification of the world' is far-fetched, since it is neither plausible nor possible. No one ever undertakes activity with the intention of benefiting the entire world, so how can we attribute such an intention even to the Sage? As they recite: 'Even for a sage dwelling in the forest,' etc. Nor is this possible, since it is impossible to motivate those who are hungry [for sense-pleasures]. Nor does the entire world desire liberation. Therefore, the student to be instructed is only the practitioner — one who has obtained the qualification of being a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the like from other <s>śāstras</s>. And his qualifications are: the collection of <s>śama</s> (tranquility), <s>dama</s> (self-control), and the like; discrimination between the eternal and non-eternal; dispassion toward enjoyments in this life and the next; and the desire for liberation. But one who undertakes [the study] without proper qualification, as one might study the <s>Brahma</s>-section [of the <s>Veda</s>] without being qualified, like [studying] the <s>Karma</s>-section — he does not obtain the fruit. In that regard, this [objection] might arise: This consideration of qualification does not pertain to the goal (<s>upeya</s>), since that is not within the scope of human effort, and since mere desirability does not exclude [other claimants]. Rather, it pertains to the means (<s>upāya</s>), since that alone is the domain of the <s>śāstra</s> and of human activity. And here, knowledge of reality too, like liberation itself, is a goal insofar as it serves that purpose, since it is not yet accomplished. The means, however, is <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), and the employment of inference and perception — unlike Vedic study — is not prohibited for <s>śūdras</s> and the like, so that there should be lack of qualification for them too in this regard. If that were the case, one who ascertains fire from smoke or through perception would incur sin, just as one who studies the <s>Veda</s> [without qualification]. And since perception and inference, which are within one's own domain, are not specifically prohibited for <s>śūdras</s> and the like — unlike the sight of a <s>caṇḍāla</s> for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has just bathed, for which expiation is prescribed — rather,

children.text: striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrā ye cānye pāpayonayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Women, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and likewise <s>Śūdras</s>, and whoever else are of sinful birth' —

children.text:
ityādismṛteradhikāra evāvasīyate /
tasmād yathā sa eva viśiṣṭaḥ svargo vaidikayāgādyanadhikṛtenāpi upāyāntareṇa traivarṇikaśuśrūṣādinā sādhyate, tathopāyānteṇānumānādinā yadyātmādhigamaḥ kriyate śūdreṇāpi, tadā kīdṛśo doṣaḥ? satyam, kiṃ tvanumānamapyāgamāvirodhenānusandhīyamānamathaniścāyakam, natu tadviruddhamapi /
yadāha--yattu pratyakṣāgamaviruddhaṃ nyāyābhāsaḥ saḥ iti /
sa cāgamāvirodhādavirodhaniścayaḥ tadarthaniścayādhīnaḥ /
tatra cānadhikṛta evāyaṃ śūdrāti /
tannirapekṣastu anumānamātraśaraṇo naraśiraḥpāvitryādivadanarthameva samāsādayet /
tasmādāgamaikavākyatayā pravṛtte śāstre tadadhikāryevādhikārīti śūdrādayo 'nadhikṛtā iva /
ato yāvadadhikāriparo 'yaṃ jagacchabda iti kecit /
tatrāha--paramakārūṇiko hīti /
santyeva hi kecit karuṇāmṛdumanaso yeṣāṃ jagadeva mitram /
anyathā bhūtevo 'bhayaṃ dattveti vidhivaiyarthyaprasaṅgaḥ /
niṣkāraṇameva paraduḥkhaprahāṇecchā kāruṇyam /
sā ca yathaikaṃ duḥkhita paśyato bhavati, tathā jagadeva duḥkhita paśyataḥ kiṃ na syāt? bhavati cet--tatprahāṇopāyapravṛttau kā nāmānupapattiḥ? nanu
children.translated_text: from such <s>smṛti</s> texts, their qualification is indeed established. Therefore, just as that very distinguished heaven, though not obtainable through Vedic sacrifices and the like by one who is not qualified [for them], is achievable through other means such as service to the three upper classes — similarly, if knowledge of the self is accomplished by a <s>Śūdra</s> too through other means such as inference, what fault is there? True. But inference too, when applied in conformity with scripture, is determinative [of truth], but not when it contradicts scripture. As [the <s>sūtra</s>] says: 'That which contradicts perception and scripture is a semblance of reasoning.' And the determination of non-contradiction with scripture depends on the determination of the meaning of scripture. And in that regard, this <s>Śūdra</s> is indeed unqualified. But one who, disregarding that [scriptural basis], takes refuge in inference alone — like [the belief in] the purity of a human skull — would merely arrive at harm. Therefore, since the <s>śāstra</s> proceeds in unity with scripture, only one who is qualified for that [scripture] is qualified [for this <s>śāstra</s>] — thus <s>Śūdras</s> and the like are as if unqualified. Therefore, some say this word 'world' (<s>jagat</s>) extends only to those who are qualified. To that he says: 'For [the Sage] is supremely compassionate.' For there are indeed some people of tender heart filled with compassion, for whom the entire world is a friend. Otherwise, the injunction 'having given fearlessness to all beings' would become pointless. Compassion is the desire to remove another's suffering without any self-interested cause. And just as that [compassion] arises when one sees a single suffering person, why should it not arise when one sees the entire world as suffering? If it does arise — then what impossibility is there in engaging in the means for removing that [suffering]? Now,

children.text: karuṇārdrahṛdayo 'pyaṃ vyutpisumeva vyutpādayenna tu viparītam, na hi badhireṣu gāyano gāyatītyata āha--tatra yadi na kaściditi /
children.translated_text: even one whose heart is softened by compassion should instruct only those who can be instructed, not others — for a singer does not sing for the deaf — to that he says: 'But if there is no one [qualified].'

children.text: na hi rogī mandabhāgyatayā carakādyupadeśe na pravartata iti tadarthatā tasya nivartata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a sick person does not cease to be the intended [beneficiary] of <s>Caraka</s>'s and other [physicians'] instruction merely because, due to his misfortune, he does not act upon it.

children.text:
nanvanadhikṛtavyutpādane pratyavāyamātrakamapaśyannayaṃ kathamavadheyavacanaḥ syāt, paśyan vā na pravarteta? kāruṇikatayā paśyannapi pravartate cet, pramādī syāt /
tathā ca paralokādabibhyato 'sya vacane kaḥ śraddhāsyatītyata āha--na ceti /
yadyapi prahīnamohatvādevāsya pāpapuṇyayorutpattireva nāsti, vakṣyati hi
children.translated_text: Now, if one who has not been authorized for instruction sees only fault [in teaching], how could he be a trustworthy speaker? Or if he does see [the fault] yet still proceeds — would he not be negligent? If it is said that out of compassion he proceeds even though he sees [the fault], then he would be careless. And since one who does not fear the next world — who would trust his words? Therefore he says 'na ca' (and not). Although, because he has eliminated delusion, the arising of sin and merit does not exist for him at all — for it will be stated:

children.text: na pravṛttiḥ pratisandhānāya hīnakleśasyeti /
children.translated_text: 'There is no continued activity for one whose afflictions have been diminished' —

children.text:
tathāpi kleśahānerdurūhatvāt pratyavāyotpattimabhyupagamya tadabhāvāya tapaḥprabhāva uktaḥ /
nanvevamapi prakṣālanāddhi paṅkasya dūrādasparśanaṃ varam /
children.translated_text: nevertheless, since the elimination of afflictions is difficult to ascertain, assuming the possibility of fault arising, the power of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is stated for its removal. Now even so, 'Rather than washing off mud, it is better not to touch it from afar' —

children.text:
ityata āha--tathā ceti /
na hi gāḥ paṅkamagnāḥ paṅkapralepabhayādanukampāparavaśāḥ samarthā noddharanti /
api tūddhṛtya paḍkaṃ prakṣālayantītyarthaḥ /
nanu yadyanadhikṛtaḥ kathaṃ phalabhāgī, tathā cet kathamanadhikṛta ityabhisandhāyoktaṃ prapañcayati--tapaḥprabhāva eva hīti /
yathā hi teṣāṃ tapaḥprabhāvādevaṃvidhāḥ pāpmāno vilīyante, tathā tapaḥprabhāvādeva satyasaṃkalpatayā anadhikāriṇo 'pi phalabhāgina iti na kaścid virodhaḥ /
na ca phalāpekṣayā teṣāmanadhikāraḥ /
kiṃ tarhi? karmāpekṣayā /
anadhikṛtena tu kṛtaṃ karma viguṇaṃ sanna phalāṃya paryāptamityapi na, viśiṣṭayājakasādguṇyādeva tasya paripūrṇatvāt /
yājaka eva tvayājyaṃ yājayan pratyavāyamāsādayet, rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇanniva vidvān /
sa ca tīvratadeṇa tapasaiva vilīyata ityarthaḥ /
tarhi mahājano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore he says 'tathā ca' (and so). For those who are compassionate do not refrain from rescuing cows stuck in mud out of fear of being smeared with mud. Rather, having pulled them out, they wash off the mud — this is the meaning. Now if one is unauthorized, how can he be a partaker of the fruit? And if so, how is he unauthorized? Intending this, he elaborates: 'tapaḥprabhāva eva hi' (for it is indeed the power of austerity). For just as sins of that kind dissolve through the power of their austerity, so too through the very power of austerity, by the truth of their resolve, even those who are unauthorized become partakers of the fruit — thus there is no contradiction. And their lack of authorization is not with respect to the fruit, but rather with respect to the ritual action. But a ritual performed by an unauthorized person, being deficient, is not adequate for the fruit — this too is not the case, because the ritual is made complete by the excellence of the distinguished officiant. However, the officiant who causes an unqualified person to sacrifice would incur fault, like a learned person accepting [gifts] from a king. And that [fault] dissolves through intense austerity alone — this is the meaning. Then, 'the path is where the great multitude has gone' —

children.text: iti nyāyena vayamapyanadhikṛtān vyutpādayāma ityata āha--na ceti /
children.translated_text: by this maxim, 'we too shall instruct the unauthorized' — therefore he says 'na ca' (and not).

children.text: nanu kutārkikāṇāmajñānaṃ nivartayatā kimanena śāstrasyopakṛtaṃ syādityāha--kutārkikairiti /
children.translated_text: Now, what benefit to the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) would there be in dispelling the ignorance of sophists? — to this he says 'kutārkikaiḥ' (by sophists).

children.text: ajñānamasamyagjñānam //
children.translated_text: <s>Ajñāna</s> (ignorance) means erroneous knowledge.

children.text:
iha karmārambhe prārabdhasyāntarāyaviraheṇa parisamāpti kāmayamānā abhīṣṭadevatā namaskārapūrvakaṃ prekṣāvantaḥ pravartante /
dṛśyate ca tatra tatra bahuśoṃ vyabhicāraḥ kṛtanamaskārasyāpi samīhitāsiddheḥ, viparītasyāpi samīhitasiddhaḥ,
children.translated_text: Here, when undertaking an action, discerning persons proceed by first paying homage to their chosen deity, desiring the completion of the undertaken task without obstruction. And it is seen here and there repeatedly that there are deviations — even for one who has made obeisance, the desired goal is not achieved; and even for one who has done the opposite, the desired goal is achieved;

children.text:
viparītasyāpi samīhitāsiddheḥ /
na cātra vṛṣṭikāmaḥ kārīrī nirvapet /
children.translated_text: and even for one who has done the opposite, the desired goal is not achieved. And here, there is no Vedic injunction like 'One who desires rain should perform the <s>kārīrī</s> sacrifice' —

children.text:
itivat prārabdhaparisamāptikāmo devatāṃ namaskuryāditi śrutirasti, yena vyabhicore 'pi karmakartṛsādhanavaiguṇyaṃ kalpayāmaḥ /
tasmādar thakāma iha vaṭe prativasantaṃ yakṣaṃ pūjayeditiva daprāmāṇikaprasiddhivijṛmbhitametadityabhisandhāya kimu na kṛto vāttikakṛtā iṣṭadevatānamaskāra ityata āha--avigīteti /
pratyakṣamivāvigītaśiṣṭācāro 'pi śrutisadbhāve pramāṇameva, nirmūlasya ca śiṣṭācārasyāsambhavāt /
apramāṇamūlakasya ca prāmāṇikavigānavirahānupapatteḥ /
tathā ca satyabhāvaḥ karmakartṛsādhanavaiguṇyamavalambate /
asati ca bhāvo janmāntarīyasukṛtasaṃpattim /
anvayavyatirekābhāvadarśanaṃ tvāgametarapramāṇagocaraṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvamapākarotītyarthaḥ /
yadyavaṃ kimanena na kṛta ityata āha--parameti /
yadi kṛtaḥ tat kimindraluptena gataḥ, yena na dṛśyata ityata āha--na niveśita iti /
atraiva dṛṣṭānto na khalviti /
children.translated_text: Here itself is the example: 'na khalu' (surely not).

children.text: na khalviṣṭadevatānamaskāravat tanniveśanamapi kvacidupayujyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Surely, like the obeisance to the chosen deity, the placement [of that obeisance in the text] too is not required anywhere — this is the meaning.

children.text: nanvevaṃbhūtaṃ śiṣṭācāraṃ śiṣyā api grāhayitavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, students too should be made to adopt such conduct of the learned.

children.text: na ca tanniveśanavyatirekeṇa te grāhitāḥ syurityata āha--maṅgalyāntara vaditi //
children.translated_text: And they cannot be made to adopt it without placing it [in the text] — therefore he says 'maṅgalyāntaravat' (like another auspicious [formula]).

stating that one who desires the completion of an undertaken task should pay homage to the deity — by which, even in cases of deviation, we might postulate a deficiency in the ritual action, agent, or instrument. Therefore, this [practice of deity-worship] is merely a display of conviction established through popular tradition, like 'one who desires wealth should worship the <s>yakṣa</s> dwelling in a banyan tree.' Intending this, [one asks] why the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> did not make an obeisance to his chosen deity — to this he says 'avigītā' (uncontested). Like direct perception, uncontested conduct of the learned is also a valid means of knowledge when a Vedic text exists, since rootless conduct of the learned is impossible, and because conduct that has no authoritative source cannot lack censure by authoritative persons. And thus, the occurrence [of success] depends on deficiency in the ritual action, agent, or instrument; and the occurrence [of success] in the absence [of deficiency depends on] the accumulated merit from another birth. But the observation of the absence of positive and negative concomitance refutes the causal relation that falls within the scope of inference and other means of knowledge apart from scripture — this is the meaning. If so, why was it not done [by the author]? — to this he says 'parama' (supreme). If it was done, then why has it disappeared as if carried away by a disease? — to this he says 'na niveśitaḥ' (not placed).

children.text:
tatreti /
śāstre vyākhyātavye /
nanu daṇḍakasūtrasyānuvādo nāstītyata uktaṃ saṃkṣepata iti /
nanvādisūtratvamasya suprasiddhameva, abhisaṃbandhavākyatvāt, tatkimanena udīritenetyata āha--ādigrahaṇeneti /
nanu śāstraniḥśreyasayoranena saṃbandho varṇyate, tataḥ saṃbandhavākyamidamiti yuktam, abhistu kimarthamityata āha--abhimata iti /
asti hi śāstraniḥśreyasayorvācyavāyakabhāvalakṣaṇo 'pi saṃbandhaḥ, na cāsāvihābhimtaḥ, prekṣāvatpravṛttyanaṅgatvāt /
na hi vācakād vācyapratītervācyasya niṣpattiḥ, yato mumukṣurvācake pravartatām /
upāye tūpeyārtho pravartate /
tena hetuhetumadbhāva eva vivakṣita ityarthaḥ /
nanu nātra śāstram, tasya niḥśreyasahetutvaṃ vā śrūyata ityata āha--pramāṇādīti /
rūḍhapadātikrame kiṃ tātparyamityata āha--na hīti /
yadyapi śiṣyate anuśiṣyate pramāṇādikamaneneti śāstramiti vyutpattyā atrāpi kāraṇatā gamyate, tathāpi śāsakasaṃbaddhavyāpāravattayā, na tu śiṣyasaṃbaddhavyāpāravattayā /
sā ceha vivakṣitā /
anyathā pramāṇādīni tattvato jñātvāpi tāvanna mucyate
children.translated_text: 'Tatra' means: in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) that is to be expounded. Now, since the <s>daṇḍaka-sūtra</s> has no explanatory restatement, hence it is said 'saṃkṣepataḥ' (in brief). Now, the fact that this is the introductory <s>sūtra</s> is itself well-established, since it is a statement of connection — then what is the purpose of stating this? — to this he says 'ādigrahaṇena' (by the word 'ādi'). Now, by this [sūtra] the connection between the <s>śāstra</s> and the highest good is described; hence it is proper that this is a statement of connection — but what is the purpose of the word 'abhiḥ'? — to this he says 'abhimataḥ' (intended). For there is also a connection between the <s>śāstra</s> and the highest good in the form of the relation of signifier and signified, but that is not what is intended here, since it would not be relevant to the purposeful activity of discerning persons. For from the comprehension of the signified through the signifier, the signified is not produced, so that one seeking liberation should engage with the signifier. Rather, one engages with the means for the sake of the end to be attained. Therefore, the causal relation is what is intended — this is the meaning. Now, neither the <s>śāstra</s> nor its being the cause of the highest good is heard here — to this he says 'pramāṇādī' (means of valid knowledge, etc.). What is the purport when conventional word-meanings are transcended? — to this he says 'na hī' (for not). Although by the etymology 'that by which the subject-matter of valid knowledge etc. is taught and instructed is a <s>śāstra</s>,' causality is understood here too, nevertheless [it is understood] as having an operation connected to the teacher, not as having an operation connected to the student. And it is the latter that is intended here. Otherwise, even after truly knowing the categories of valid knowledge etc., one is still not liberated

children.text: yāvannānuśiṣyāditi /
children.translated_text: until one instructs [others] —

children.text: tadidamuktam--padārthatattvāvagamakaraṇatayeti na svarūpeṇeti ca /
children.translated_text: thus it is said: 'by way of causing the ascertainment of the true nature of categories' — and 'not by its own nature.'

children.text: nanu hetutvakaraṇatve na viṣayabhedena bhavitumarhata ityata āha--teneti //
children.translated_text: Now, causality and instrumentality should not differ by virtue of a difference in object — to this he says 'tena' (therefore).

children.text:
ubhayorapi hetuḥ śāstraṃ karaṇaṃ ca /
kiṃ tu padārthatattve jñāpakatayā niḥśreyase tadvyāpāravataḥ karaṇatayetyarthaḥ /
tadidamuktam--tathā ceti /
evaṃ ca sati śāstrasya niḥśreyase karttavye padārthatattvajñānasya nirūktibalena vyāpāratve darśite vyāpāravyāpāriṇoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ /
tathā vyāpāravatā śāstreṇa vyāpāraviṣayasya pramāṇādeḥ pratipādyapratipādakabhāvaḥ /
tathā vyāpāraviṣayeṇa pramāṇādinā vyāpārasya tattvajñānasya viṣayaviṣayībhāvaḥ /
tathā vyāpāreṇa tattvajñānena vyāpārulasya niḥśreyasasya kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ /
tathā vyāpāraviṣayaphalayorhetuhetumadbhāvaḥ saṃbandha sūcito nāntarīyakatvāt /
na hyataddhetukastadvacāpāro nāma, nāpyatatkarma tadvacāpāraviṣayaḥ, nāpi tatphalānanuguṇastadvacāpāraḥ, tadvacāpāraviṣayo veti pajcasu vaktavyeṣu upalakṣaṇārthaṃ dvayamāha--śāstrapramāṇāditi /
enameva vyutpattilabhyaṃ vyāpāramabhipretya tattvasya jñānamiti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī
children.translated_text: The <s>śāstra</s> is both the cause and the instrument of both [the knowledge of categories and the highest good]. However, with respect to the true nature of categories, it is [the instrument] by way of being the informer; with respect to the highest good, it is [the instrument] by way of being the instrument of the operation of that [knowledge] — this is the meaning. Thus it is said 'tathā ca' (and so). And this being so, since the operation of the <s>śāstra</s> upon knowledge of the true nature of categories in effecting the highest good has been demonstrated by the force of etymological analysis — [we have]: between the operation and its possessor, a cause-effect relation; between the <s>śāstra</s> possessing the operation and the object of the operation, namely valid knowledge etc., a relation of thing-to-be-expressed and its expresser; between the object of the operation, namely valid knowledge etc., and the operation itself, namely knowledge of truth, a relation of object and subject; between the operation, namely knowledge of truth, and the result of the operation, namely the highest good, a cause-effect relation; and between the object of the operation and the fruit, a relation of cause and effect is indicated as a connection, because of their necessary concomitance. For there is no operation of that [kind] that is not caused by that, nor is there an object of that operation that is not its effect, nor is there an operation incongruent with its fruit, nor an object of that operation — thus, of the five things to be stated, two are mentioned by way of illustration: 'śāstrapramāṇādī' (the treatise, valid knowledge, etc.). Intending precisely this operation obtainable through etymological analysis, the sixth case ending in 'knowledge of truth' is employed in the objective sense,

children.text: bhāṣyakāreṇa darśiteti na karaṇavyutpattirvirūddhā //
children.translated_text: as shown by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — thus the etymological derivation of instrumentality is not contradicted.

children.text:
nanu śiṣyācāryaśāstratadvyākhyānānāmapi saṃbandhāḥ kaiścit samānatāntrikaiḥ pradarśitāḥ /
te kasmānna pradarśyante ityata āha--tadidamabhidheyeti /
na hrāstītyetāvanmātreṇaiva pradarśanīyam /
kiṃ nāma? yāvatyapratipādite prekṣāvatpravṛttirna syāt, tāvat pradarśyate /
na ca śiṣyācāryādisaṃbandhāḥ prekṣāvatpravṛttyaṅgam, teṣāṃ pravṛttiphalatvāt /
pravṛttyuttarakālaṃ hi śiṣyaḥ pratipādyaḥ, pratipādakaścācāryaḥ, śāstraṃ vyākhyeyam, vyākhyātā ca sa ityādi sidhyati /
na ca śāstrācāryādīnāṃ svarūpapratipādanamapyupayujyate, pramāṇāntarasiddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is the presentation of the intrinsic nature of the <s>śāstra</s>, teacher, etc. useful, since they are established through other means of valid knowledge.

children.text: tasmāt prayojanamabhidhayaṃ tayoḥ saṃbandho 'bhidheyastaddvārā śāstrasya prayojanena saṃbandha ityetadarthatveme prathamasūtrasya nyāyyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the purpose is to be stated, the connection of those two [śāstra and purpose] is the subject-matter to be stated, and through that, the connection of the <s>śāstra</s> with the purpose [is established] — it is proper that this is the meaning of the first <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: nanu yasya mithyājñānaṃ saṃsāraṃ pratanoti tasyaiva tattvajñānaṃ niḥśreyasahetuḥ, ātmā ca tathā, tadanyeṣāṃ tu śāstrābhidheyānāmapi na niḥśreyasahetutvam /
children.translated_text: Now, it is only for one whose false knowledge extends <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) that knowledge of truth is the cause of the highest good; and the <s>ātman</s> (self) is such [an entity]. But for others among the objects described in the <s>śāstra</s>, there is no being a cause of the highest good.

children.text: tathā ca na niḥśreyasasaṃbandhaḥ ityata āha--yatpadārtheti //
children.translated_text: And thus there is no connection with the highest good — to this he says 'yatpadārtha' (that category).

Now, the connections of the student, teacher, <s>śāstra</s>, and its commentary have also been demonstrated by certain followers of the same tradition. Why are those not presented? — to this he says 'tadidamabhidheya' (this is the subject-matter). For it is not the case that something should be presented merely because it exists. What then? As much as is needed such that without its presentation, the purposeful activity of discerning persons would not arise — that much is presented. And the connections of student, teacher, etc. are not a factor in purposeful activity, since they are results of that activity. For it is only after engagement that the student becomes one to be instructed, the teacher becomes the instructor, the <s>śāstra</s> becomes the thing to be expounded, and he becomes the expositor — and so on.

children.text:
nanu pramāṇādipadārthatattvajñānasya yadi niḥśreyasahetutā śāstrapravṛtteḥ pūrvameva pramāṇasiddhā niṣprayojanaṃ śāstre prayojanābhidhānam, mānāntarasiddhe upadeśānapekṣaṇāt /
atheta eva tanniścayo dusttaramitaretarāśrayatvam /
pravṛtto hi prayojanaṃ niścinuyāt /
niścitaprayojanaśca pravarteta /
na ca pravṛtteḥ prāgeva munivacanānniścinoti, prathamasūtra eva prayojanāniścayena pravṛttyanupapatteḥ /
tatrāpi ca pravṛttyarthaṃ prayojanāntarābhidhāne 'navasthā /
tadaniśvaye 'pyādyā pravṛttiścet, uttarottarapravṛttāvapi tathātvaprasaṅgaḥ /
tasmāt prayojanādyabhidhānamanarthakamiti kecit /
tadanupapannam /
tridhā hi puṃsāṃ cittavṛttayaḥ, anubhava icchā prayatnaśceti /
tatrānubhavo necchāmanuvidhatte, aniṣṭasyāpyupalabdheḥ /
icchā tu puruṣārthe svarasotthitā, tatsādhane ca tathātvānumānotthāpyā /
prayatnastu sādhanaviṣaya eva /
tatra sādhanagocarāvicchaprayatnau /
ādyā pravṛttirityucyate, na tvanubhavaḥ /
phalagocarā vā icchā pravṛttiḥ, cena tayorapi prayojananiścayāpekṣā syāt /
na
children.translated_text: Now, if the fact that knowledge of the true nature of valid knowledge etc. is the cause of the highest good is already established through valid means of knowledge prior to the composition of the <s>śāstra</s>, then the statement of purpose in the <s>śāstra</s> is pointless, since what is already established through another means of knowledge does not require instruction. But if the certainty [of that purpose comes] from this very [śāstra], then there is the difficult fault of mutual dependence. For one who has commenced would ascertain the purpose; and one who has ascertained the purpose would commence. But one does not ascertain [the purpose] from the sage's words prior to commencing, since without ascertainment of the purpose in the very first <s>sūtra</s>, commencement is impossible. And if, for the purpose of that [commencement] too, another purpose needs to be stated, there is infinite regress. If there is commencement even without that ascertainment — the same contingency applies to each subsequent commencement as well. Therefore, some say that the statement of purpose etc. is useless. That is untenable. For the mental states of persons are threefold: experience, desire, and effort. Among these, experience does not follow desire, since even the undesired is perceived. But desire arises spontaneously toward the human goal, and toward the means of attaining it, it is to be aroused by inference of its being such. And effort has as its object only the means. There, desire and effort directed toward the means — the first [of these] is called 'activity,' not experience. Or, desire directed toward the fruit is 'activity' — even so, both of those require ascertainment of purpose. For

children.text:
hyupekṣaṇīyaṃ niṣprayojanamiti nānubhūyate /
nāpi sukhaṃ prayojanāntaraśūnyakiti neṣyate /
nāpi mumukṣuṇānapekṣite svarge yāgādikaṃ tatsādhanatayā nānubhūyate /
puruṣārthasādhane tvicchālakṣaṇā vā prayatnalakṣaṇā vā pravṛttirna svarasasiddhā /
na hi kaścit kṣudhī duḥkhaprahāṇaṃ tṛptisauhityasukha vā ananusaṃdhāyānnamattumicchati prayatate vā /
tasmād yatra yaḥ pravartayitavyaḥ sa tatsādhyamarthaṃ daśayitvā, yataśca yo nivartayitavyaḥ sa tatsādhyamanarthaṃ darśayitveti /
uktaṃ pracojanādikam /
tattu śrotā kathaṃ śraddhāsyati, aśraddadhāno vā kathaṃ pravartsyatītyavaśiṣyate /
tatrāha--viniściteti /
yadyapi munerāptatvāvadhāraṇe prayojanānabhidhāne 'pi prayojanasāmānyaniścayo bhavatyeva prayojanavadidaṃ śāstramāptoktatvāditi , tathāpi nāsau pravṛttyaṅgam /
na hi prayojanavadityeva pravartate /
kiṃ tarhi? asmadapekṣitaprayojanavadidamiti kṛtvā /
sa ca prayojanaviśeṣo vacanādevāvasīyata iti sārthakametadabhidhānam /
tadidamuktam--prayojanādi viniścitya /
viśeṣata iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'viśeṣataḥ' (specifically) is to be supplied.

children.text: viniścayaśca śāstropāyakamevedaṃ niḥśreyasamityākāro na tvavaśyaṃbhāviprayojanākāraḥ, kṛṣyādāvavagrahādivadatrāpyantarāyasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: And the ascertainment is of the form 'this highest good is attainable through the <s>śāstra</s> as its means,' not of the form 'the purpose will necessarily come about' — since here too, as with rainfall in agriculture and the like, there is the possibility of obstruction.

children.text: tadidaṃ prayojanasya pravartakatvamuddeśyatayā, na tu pravṛttiviṣayatayā /
children.translated_text: Thus, this motivating capacity of the purpose [is understood] as being what is to be aimed at, not as being the object of activity.

children.text: tena neṣṭābhyupāyatāvidhivirodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no contradiction with the rule of being a means to the desired end.

it is not the case that what is useless is not experienced. Nor is it the case that pleasure devoid of any other purpose is not desired. Nor is it the case that for one seeking liberation, if heavenly [reward] is not sought, ritual acts like sacrifice are not experienced as means to that [heaven]. But with respect to the means of attaining the human goal, activity — whether in the form of desire or in the form of effort — is not spontaneously established. For no one who is hungry desires to eat or makes effort [to eat] without considering the removal of suffering and the pleasure of satisfaction and satiety. Therefore, one who is to be engaged in something should be shown the goal to be attained thereby; and one who is to be dissuaded from something should be shown the harm to be produced thereby — thus the purpose etc. has been stated. But how will the listener trust that? And if he does not trust, how will he engage? — this remains [to be addressed]. To this he says 'viniścita' (ascertained). Although, when the sage's trustworthiness is established, even without stating the purpose, there arises a general certainty that 'this <s>śāstra</s> has purpose, since it is spoken by a trustworthy person,' nevertheless that is not a factor in [motivating] activity. For one does not engage merely because something has purpose, but rather thinking 'this has the purpose that I seek.' And that specific purpose is ascertained only from the [explicit] statement — thus this statement is meaningful. This is what is said: 'having ascertained the purpose etc.' —

children.text: nanu munerāptatvāniścaye kiṃ tadvacane pravṛttirnāstyeva? tathā sati tasyāptatvaniścayo 'pi kathamityata
children.translated_text: Now, if there is no certainty of the sage's trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>), does one simply not act upon his words? If so, how would one ever ascertain his trustworthiness? To this,

children.text:
āha--āptatvāniścaye tvarthasaṃśayāt /
śāstrasādhyatayeti śeṣaḥ /
nanu saṃśayānasya kathaṃ prekṣāvataḥ pravṛttiritya āha--na khalviti /
yadyapi ca sasyādhigamasya kṛṣyādisādhyatayā saṃśayo nāsti, tathāpi bhaviṣyattayā astyeva /
tathāpi
children.translated_text: he says: 'When there is uncertainty of trustworthiness, due to doubt about the subject matter' — the remainder is 'it is to be established through scripture.' Now, how does a discerning person act when in doubt? He says: 'Not indeed...' Although there is no doubt that the attainment of crops is accomplished through agriculture and other means, nevertheless doubt exists insofar as it pertains to the future. Still,

children.text:
tamuddiśya prekṣāvantaḥ pravartante /
yathā ca tatra śataikāṃśikaḥ phalābhāvaḥ phalakoṭistūtkaṭā tathātrāpi /
na hīndriyāpātajo 'yaṃ saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ nāma? āptatvāviniścayahetukāprāmāṇyaśaḍkyā samākṛṣṭaḥ /
vastutastu sūtrāt prayojanādiniścayākārameva vijñānamityarthaḥ /
nanu saṃśayaḥ prayojanādivākyābhāve 'pi sulabhaḥ, viśeṣasmṛtistu arthitvaviśeṣāt bhaviṣyatītyāha--na ceti /
yadvacanena hi yaḥ pravartate sa tadvacanādeva viśeṣasmṛtimapekṣate, na svātantryeṇa /
na hi rogārto mamedaṃ roganivṛttisādhanaṃ bhavenna veti yatra tatrocchṛḍkhalaḥ svayamutprekṣya pravartate /
kiṃ nāma? anavadhṛtāptatvasyāpi vaidyasyaiva vacanāt /
anyathā tvayaṃ prayojanābhidhānamanadhigacchan anarthamapyāśaṅketa, kiṃ niṣprayojanamidaṃ kākadantaparīkṣāgranthavat, utāśakyasādhanaprayojanaṃ mṛtyuharahimamahīdharottarasānusiddhasaṃjīvanīkathanavat, athānabhimataprayojanamāryāvartanivāsinaṃ prati dākṣiṇātyasya mātulakanyakāpariṇayaprakramopadeśavat, athābhimatasyāpi śakyasyāpi prayojanasya laghīyasyupāyāntare satyapi gururayamupāyaḥ pipāsuṃ prati gīrvāṇataraḍgiṇītīrasamīpakūpakhananopadeśavat /
etāsu cānarthasaṃbhāvanāsu na pravartate /
na ca prayojanābhidhāne 'pyetāsāmavakāśaḥ, lokavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgāt /
na hi kaścid vaidyavacanādeva māśaḍkya nivartate yathā
children.translated_text: discerning persons engage in action with that aim. And just as there the absence of result is one chance in a hundred while the possibility of result is preponderant, so too here. For this doubt does not arise from sensory experience. What then? It is drawn from the suspicion of unreliability due to the non-ascertainment of trustworthiness. In reality, however, the cognition from the <s>sūtra</s> has the very form of certainty regarding purpose and so forth — this is the meaning. Now, even without a statement of purpose, doubt is easily obtained, but specific recollection will arise due to the specific nature of the desire — to this he says: 'And not...' For one who acts upon a statement acts in dependence on that very statement for specific recollection, not independently. For a sick person does not independently conjecture and act on the thought 'this may or may not be a remedy for my disease.' What then? He acts on the word of a physician even when the physician's trustworthiness has not been ascertained. Otherwise, one who does not understand the statement of purpose would suspect even harm: 'Is this purposeless, like a treatise examining crows' teeth? Or does it have an unachievable purpose, like telling about the <s>Saṃjīvanī</s> herb on a peak north of the Himalayas that removes death? Or does it have an undesired purpose, like instructing a resident of <s>Āryāvarta</s> about the procedure for marrying a maternal uncle's daughter as practiced in the south? Or, even if the purpose is desired and achievable, is this a burdensome means when a lighter alternative exists, like instructing a thirsty person to dig a well near the bank of the celestial Ganges?' And in the face of such suspicions of harm, one does not act. Nor do such suspicions have scope even when the purpose is stated, for there would follow the disruption of all worldly transactions. For no one at all refrains from acting merely on account of such suspicion regarding a physician's words, as one would

children.text:
svayamutprekṣyeti bhāvaḥ /
tadanarthakaṃ niṣprayojanamityarthaḥ /
aśakyānuṣṭhānatvamupāyasyāsiddhamityata āha--tathā hīti /
children.translated_text: To the objection that the impossibility of practicing the means is unestablished, he says: 'For thus...'

children.text: iha dvividhaḥ pramāṇaśabdasyārthaḥ--pramīyate 'neneti ca pramāṇam, pramitiḥ pramāṇamiti /
children.translated_text: Here the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>' (means of valid knowledge) has two meanings: that by which something is measured is <s>pramāṇa</s>, and the act of measuring (<s>pramiti</s>) is <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: ca /
children.translated_text: And.

children.text: tatra prathamamadhikṛtyoktam--prameyādīnāṃ tattvajñānaṃ pramāṇatattvajñānādhīnamiti //
children.translated_text: There, with regard to the first meaning, it was stated: 'The true knowledge of the objects of valid cognition (<s>prameya</s>) and so forth depends on the true knowledge of the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>).'
by independently conjecturing — this is the meaning. That would be purposeless, i.e., devoid of any result — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanvidindrayādīnāmajñāyamānānāmeva svaviṣayaparicchedajanakatvaṃ paśyannapi kathamevaṃ brūyādityata āha--na hīti /
pramāṇatvenājñāyamānaṃ pramāṇaṃ svaviṣayaṃ paricchinatti, na tvavadhārayati /
tacceha vivakṣitamityarthaḥ /
kimiti nāvadhārayati? na hindriyamajñāyamānamaniścayākārameva jñānaṃ janayatītyata āha--tāvanmātrasyeti /
yadyapi niścayākārameva jñānamādhatte tathāpi tathābhūtasyaiva bhūyo bhūyaḥ prameyaviraholabdherviśeṣānupalabdheśca saṃdehastadavaskandatītyarthaḥ /
tatkiṃ kvacidapyavadhāraṇaṃ nāstyeva? tathā sati toyamevedamityādiko laukikaḥ pratyayaḥ, tathā pūrvapakṣiṇaḥ kvacidapi viniścayo nāstyevetyādikaścābhimāno viruddhyetetyata āha--api tviti /
yadi kvacit prameyatattvāvadhāraṇaṃ paramārthaḥ, tadā pramāṇatattvāvadhāraṇadvāreṇaiva /
pramārāntareṇa tu bhavanna pāramārthikamityarthaḥ /
bodhakatvaṃ bodhajanakatvaṃ bodhajananāvacchinnā satteti yāvat /
avyabhicāritvamaviparītānubhavajanakatvamaviparītānubhavajananāvacchi nnā satteti yāvat /
children.translated_text: <s>Avyabhicāritva</s> (non-deviation) means the capacity to generate non-erroneous experience; it refers to existence delimited by the condition of generating non-erroneous experience.

children.text: evaṃ copadhidvayāvacchinnāyāḥ sattāyā upādhibhedād bhinnāyā ivaikasminnarthe samavāyaḥ kṛtakatvānityatvayoriva na viruddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus the co-presence in a single entity of existence delimited by two different limiting conditions, appearing as if different due to the difference of limiting conditions, is not contradictory — just as with the properties of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and being impermanent (<s>anityatva</s>).

children.text: tenāvyabhicāritvena jñāyamāneneti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The remainder is: 'by that <s>avyabhicāritva</s> (non-deviation) being known.'

children.text: pramāṇyāvadhāraṇaṃ tarhi kkopayujyata ityata āha--tadeva hīti //
children.translated_text: If one asks where the ascertainment of validity is then needed, he says: 'For that very thing...'

Now, how can one say this when one sees that the sense-organs and other means, even when unknown themselves, produce the determination of their respective objects? To this he says: 'Not indeed...' A <s>pramāṇa</s> that is not known as a <s>pramāṇa</s> does determine its own object, but it does not ascertain it with certainty. And it is the latter that is intended here — this is the meaning. Why does it not ascertain with certainty? Because a cognition that does not know the sense-organ does not generate merely an uncertain cognition — to this he says: 'To that extent only...' Although the sense-organ does indeed produce cognition of a determinate character, nevertheless, because of the repeated failure to obtain the object in that form and the non-apprehension of distinguishing features, doubt assails even that — this is the meaning. Then is there no ascertainment anywhere at all? If so, ordinary judgments such as 'this is indeed water' and the objector's own conviction that 'there is certainly no determination anywhere' would be contradicted — to this he says: 'But rather...' If anywhere there is ascertainment of the true nature of the object of knowledge, then it is only through the door of ascertaining the true nature of the means of valid knowledge. Without a means of valid knowledge, however, such ascertainment would not be ultimate — this is the meaning. The capacity to produce awareness (<s>bodhakatva</s>) means the capacity to generate cognition; it refers to existence delimited by the condition of generating cognition.

children.text:
pramāṇaṃ hi pramākaraṇam /
na ca karaṇatvādayaḥ sāmānyaviśeṣāḥ santi /
sāmānyasaṃkaraprasaṅgāt /
kiṃ nāma? sādhakatamatvameva karaṇatvam /
tadviśeṣakastu kriyāviśeṣa eva /
sa cātra pramālakṣaṇaḥ /
pramā cāviparītopalabdhiḥ /
ato 'viparītānubhavajanakatvalakṣaṇamavyabhicāritvameva prāmāṇyamityarthaḥ /
yadyevaṃ tadavadhāraṇapūrvakameva prameyādyavadhāraṇamastvityata āha--tacceti /
pramākaraṇatvaṃ hi nānavadhāritāyāṃ pramāyāmavadhārayituṃ śakyamityarthaḥ /
tarhi pramātvamevāvadhāryatām, na hi tadapyaupādhikaṃ yenopādhyanavadhāraṇe naivāvadhāryetetyata āha--tathā hīti /
vijñānasya pramāyāḥ /
prāmāṇyaṃ pramātvam /
svato vetyasya svātmanā vā svagrāhakeṇa vetyarthaḥ /
tatra prathamaṃ dūṣayati--na khalviti /
dharmadharmiṇorabhedapakṣe anātmasaṃvedanamityetadeva dūṣaṇam /
ānātmasaṃvedanatā copapādayiṣyata iti hṛdayam /
bhedapakṣe prāgeveti /
yo hi yad gṛhṇāti sa taddharmamapi gṛhṇīyāditi saṃbhāvyetāpi /
yastu dharmiṇameva nākalayati, tasya dharmagrahaṇavārtāpi kva? yadyapi ca śabdagandhādayo vyomabhūmyādyagrahe 'pi gṛhyante, tathāpi na taddharmatayetyarthaḥ /
svagrāhakeṇa veti dūṣayati--nāpīti /
taddhi mānasaṃ vā syāt laiḍgikaṃ vā? ubhayamapi manaso jñātatālakṣaṇāt liṅgād vā aviśiṣṭāt jāyamānaṃ kathamiva tadābhāsaviśiṣṭaṃ gṛhṇīyat? viṣayaviśeṣāt tu tathātve apramāṇyasyāpi svata eva grahaṇaprasaṅgāt, tatrāpi viṣayavaiśiṣṭacasya sattvāt /
pramāyāḥ prāyikatayā tadvāsanāyāḥ samutkaṭatvādapramāpi samutkaṭatvādapramāpi prametyeva gṛhyate /
tato bādhakādhīnamevāprāmāṇyamāsaṃjitarajatatāyāmiva
children.translated_text: For <s>pramāṇa</s> is the instrument of valid cognition (<s>pramākaraṇa</s>). And instrumentality (<s>karaṇatva</s>) and similar properties are not universals and particulars, for there would follow the intermixture of universals. What then? Being the most efficient cause is instrumentality. And the particularizer of that is the specific action itself. And that here has the character of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>). And <s>pramā</s> is non-erroneous apprehension. Therefore, validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is just <s>avyabhicāritva</s> (non-deviation), characterized by the capacity to generate non-erroneous experience — this is the meaning. If so, let the ascertainment of objects of knowledge be preceded by the ascertainment of that — to this he says: 'And that...' For the instrumentality of valid cognition cannot be ascertained without the cognition (<s>pramā</s>) itself being ascertained — this is the meaning. Then let the nature of being valid cognition itself be ascertained, for it too is not conditional such that it could not be ascertained without ascertaining the condition — to this he says: 'For thus...' Of cognition, i.e., of valid cognition. Validity means the nature of being valid cognition. 'Intrinsically or' means either by itself or by its own apprehender — this is the meaning. There, he first refutes the first option: 'Not indeed...' On the view that there is no difference between property and property-bearer, the very fact of non-self-awareness is the refutation. And non-self-awareness will be established — this is the essence. On the view of difference: 'previously...' For it may be supposed that whatever apprehends something also apprehends its properties. But for one who does not apprehend even the property-bearer, where is the question of apprehending the property? And although sound, smell and so forth are apprehended even without apprehending space, earth and so forth, nevertheless they are not apprehended as properties of those — this is the meaning. He refutes 'or by its own apprehender': 'Nor...' Would that be mental or inferential? Either way, arising from the mind characterized by awareness or from an undifferentiated inferential mark, how could it apprehend that which is qualified by that appearance? But if it is so qualified due to a specific object, then there would follow the intrinsic apprehension of invalidity too, since specificity of object obtains there as well. Because valid cognition is predominant, its <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) being strong, even an invalid cognition is apprehended as if it were valid. Therefore invalidity depends only on a sublating cognition, just as the nature of being nacre in what is mistakenly perceived as silver

children.text: śuktikāyāṃ śuktikātvamiti yadi tathāpyāsaṃjakasyāpi yadyāsaṃjakatvamavagataṃ kathaṃ na svato 'prāmāṇyagrahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ? tatrāpi prāmāṇyārope tu kathaṃ nānavasthā? na ca kṛtrimaṃ rūpamaparibhūya grahaṇaṃ grahaṇāmityucyate, saṃśayenābhibhūtatvāt
children.translated_text: depends on recognizing it as nacre. If so, even for the non-mistaken cognition, if its non-mistaken character is cognized, how is there not the consequence of intrinsic apprehension of invalidity too? And regarding the superimposition of validity there as well, how would there not be an infinite regress? Nor is it the case that apprehension without setting aside the artificial form is called apprehension, because it is overwhelmed by doubt,

children.text: māyāliḍgini jhaṭiti parivrājakabuddhivat /
children.translated_text: like the sudden cognition of a renunciant upon seeing a conjurer's mark.

children.text: tasmāt jñānaṃ gṛhyata evetyeva na /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is simply not the case that cognition is apprehended as such.

children.text: yadi tu daivād gṛhyate, tadā jñānamityeva; na tu pramāṇamapramāṇaṃ vetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But if by chance it is apprehended, then it is apprehended merely as cognition, not as valid or invalid — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu yadi svīyāt svata iti na nirvahati, vakṣyamāṇena ca nyāyena nāpi parataḥ, asti cāyaṃ pramāṇāpramāṇapravibhāgavyavahāro niḥśaṅkaḥ /
tataḥ svasaṃvedananaya evāstu /
tena hyayaṃ nirvahet /
na hi tatra kiñcidanavasthādikaṃ paśyāma ityata āha--eteneti /
svasaṃvedananayo hi na tāvat pramāṇasiddhaḥ /
kadācit pramāṇavyavahārasauṣṭhavāt svīkriyetāpi yadyayaṃ tena nirvahet, na tvetadasti /
yathā hi pramāṇaṃ svātmānaṃ gṛhṇat prāmāṇyamapi gṛhṇāti tathā tadābhāsamapi tadābhāsatva gṛhṇīyāt /
tathā ca sarvamithyājñānāt apravṛttiprasaṅgastadavasthaḥ /
na ca tatrāpi pramāṇyāropāt pravṛttiḥ, svātmabhūtasyāpramāṇyasya svasavedanatayā grahaṇe samāropāsaṃbhāvāt /
agrahaṇe vā svasaṃvedananayānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, if there is no apprehension, then the principle of self-awareness itself is not tenable.

children.text: dharmadharmiṇorbhedāt svarūpagrahaṇe 'pi nāprāmāṇyarūpadharmagrahaṇamiti yadi, tadā prāmāṇyasyāpyagrahaṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: If one says that due to the difference between property and property-bearer, even though the intrinsic form is apprehended, the property that is invalidity is not apprehended, then the non-apprehension of validity too would follow.

children.text: tasmāt svasaṃvedananaye 'pi svarūpavedanamātraṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even on the principle of self-awareness, there would be mere awareness of the intrinsic form,

children.text: na tu prāmāṇyādivedanamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: but not awareness of validity and so forth — this is the meaning.

Now, if validity cannot be established intrinsically as discussed, nor extrinsically by the reasoning to be stated, and yet this distinction between valid and invalid cognition is an undoubted matter of everyday practice, then let it be established by the principle of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>). For this would account for it, and we see no infinite regress or similar fault therein — to this he says: 'By this...' For the principle of self-awareness is not itself established by a means of valid knowledge. Even if it were accepted on account of the elegance it lends to the practice of valid cognition, it still would not account for this. For just as valid cognition, in apprehending itself, would also apprehend its validity, so too it should apprehend its own semblance, along with its character of being a mere semblance. And thus the consequence that all erroneous cognitions would prevent action remains as before. Nor can action proceed from the superimposition of validity even there, because when invalidity is intrinsic to the cognition itself, its apprehension through self-awareness makes superimposition impossible.

children.text:
parato veti dūṣayati--nāpīti /
tadgocaraṃ tadgocaragocaraṃ madhyapadalopāt /
prātyakṣike ca vahnijñāne prātyakṣikameva vahnijñānāntaramiti yāvat /
tacca dvividham, samānendriyajamindriyāntarajaṃ ca /
evamanumāne 'pi anumānajñānāntaraṃ talliṅgajaṃ
children.translated_text: He refutes 'or extrinsically': 'Nor...' 'Having that as its object' means 'having the object of that as its object,' by elision of the middle word. And in the case of a perceptual cognition of fire, another perceptual cognition of fire itself — this is the meaning. And that is of two kinds: arising from the same sense-organ and arising from a different sense-organ. Similarly in the case of inference too, another inferential cognition: one arising from the same inferential mark

children.text:
liṅgāntarajaṃ ca /
evaṃ śābde 'pi śābdajñānānantaraṃ tadāptaśabdajamāptāntaraśabdajaṃ ceti samānajātīyasaṃvādo darśitaḥ /
arthakriyetyādinā kāryaliṅgakaṃ tadgocaretyādinā cākāryakāraṇaliṅgakamanumānatrayaṃ vijājīyasaṃvādarūpaṃ darśitam, upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
āptopadeśajamapi saṃvādakaṃ jñānaṃ bhavatyeva jñānaṃ bhavatyeva /
so 'yaṃ pramāṇye niścetavye saṃvādo yadyapi vyadhikaraṇastathapyarthatathātvamava dhārayannarthavattvaṃ pravartakasyāpyavadhārayatītyetāvatā tathaivopavarṇitaḥ /
children.translated_text: and one arising from a different inferential mark. Similarly in the case of verbal testimony too, another verbal cognition: one arising from the words of the same authoritative person and one arising from the words of a different authoritative person — thus concordance of the same type is shown. Through 'efficacy of action' and so forth, inference based on effect is shown; through 'having that as its object' and so forth, inference based on non-effect and causal mark — thus three types of inference as forms of concordance of different type are shown. And this is merely illustrative. Cognition arising from authoritative testimony too can be concordant. This concordance, though operating in different substrata when ascertaining validity, nevertheless, by ascertaining the conformity of the object to reality, also ascertains the meaningfulness of even the prompting cognition — to this extent it has been so described.

children.text:
dūṣayati--tacca sarvamiti /
evaṃ pramātvasya duradhigamatvamāpādya tadāyattāvadhāraṇe pramāṇānāṃ pramāṇatve yojayati--yadā ceti /
nanu yadi prāmāṇyāvadhāraṇenaivapravṛttiḥ, tadā saiva sārvalaukikī svata ityādivikalpān phalgūkariṣyati /
atha tadavadhāraṇavyatirekeṇāpi pravṛttirapratyūhā tadā māvadhāri prāmāṇyam, kiṃ naśchinnamityata āha--tadevamiti /
vaidikaṃ vyavahāramadhikṛtya cedaṃ śāstraṃ pravṛttam, na laukikamityabhisandhiḥ /
prakṛte yojayati--tasmāditi /
nanu nityayoge matubiti durghaṭam, pramāṇārthayorevānityatvāt, parasparasamavāyabhāvāccetyata āha--nityatā ceti /
nanvavyabhicāro 'pi vyāpyavyāpakabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ pramāṇaprameyayornāstītyata āha--iyameva ceti /
so 'yamavisaṃvadādo visaṃvādābhāvo 'vyabhicāralakṣaṇam /
avyabhicārasvarūpaṃ tu lakṣyabhūtaṃ bhūtārthaparicchedakatvam, lakṣyalakṣaṇayorabhinnāśrayatvāt /
avyabhicārasvarūpaṃ tu lakṣyabhūtaṃ bhūtārthaparicchedakatvam, lakṣyalakṣaṇayorabhinnāśrayatvāt
children.translated_text: He refutes: 'And all that...' Having thus shown the difficulty of ascertaining the nature of being a valid means of knowledge, he applies the means of valid knowledge to the ascertainment that depends on it: 'And when...' Now, if action proceeds only from the ascertainment of validity, then that very universal worldly practice would render the alternatives of 'intrinsic' and so forth trivial. But if action proceeds unimpeded even without such ascertainment, then let validity not be ascertained — what concern is that of ours? To this he says: 'Thus indeed...' The intention is that this treatise has been composed with reference to Vedic practice, not worldly practice. He applies it to the subject at hand: 'Therefore...' Now, the use of the possessive suffix in the sense of constant connection is difficult, since both <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) and <s>artha</s> (object) are impermanent, and because there is no inherence between them — to this he says: 'And the permanence...' Now, even <s>avyabhicāra</s> (non-deviation), characterized by the relation of pervaded and pervader, does not exist between <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> — to this he says: 'And this very...' This non-discordance, the absence of discordance, has the character of non-deviation. The intrinsic nature of non-deviation, which is the thing to be characterized, is the capacity to determine real objects; since the characterized and the characterizing have the same locus,

children.text:
sāmānādhikaraṇyamiti mantavyam /
yadyapi deśāvasthābhede kālabhedo 'pyarthasiddhastathāpi yathākathañcit kālabhedamātraṃ vivakṣitamatreti jñāpanārthaṃ tadgrahaṇam /
tathā hi dūrasthe sthāṇau puruṣarpatyayasya kālāntare 'pi visaṃvādo nāsti yāvat
children.translated_text: co-referentiality should be understood. Although difference in time is also established as a matter of course where there is difference in place and condition, nevertheless the word is included to indicate that mere difference in time is also intended here. For example, in the case of a distant post, the discordance of the cognition of a person or a snake does not arise even at a later time, as long as

children.text:
na pratipattā nikaṭastho bhavati /
pratyetavya eva vā yāvanna nediṣṭhaḥ syāt /
evaṃ svapnāvasthāyām arthapratyayasya kālabhede 'pi tāvanna visaṃvādo yāvanna jāgarāvasthānubhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the cognition of an object in the dream state also has no discordance even with difference in time, as long as there is no experience in the waking state.

children.text: na ca vācyamevaṃ sati kiṃ kālabhedagrahaṇeneti, deśāvasthayorabhede 'pi kālakrameṇāpi kvacid visaṃvādadarśanād yathā sunipuṇanibhālanādāpātajātasya kāmāturakāminījñānasya bhede 'pi kvacit kālāntare visaṃvādāt tadupagrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor should one say, 'In that case, what is the point of grasping temporal difference?' — because even when place and condition are unchanged, discrepancy is sometimes observed through temporal succession alone; just as knowledge arising spontaneously from superficial observation — like the knowledge of a love-struck [person regarding the] beloved — may be discrepant at some later time despite there being no difference [in the perceived object]. Hence its inclusion [in the definition].

children.text: tadanenendriyādīnāṃ kālakramabhāvinaḥ sahakāribhedāḥ sphuṭatarapratītihetavaḥ sarva eva saṃgṛhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, all the auxiliary conditions of the sense-faculties and so forth, which arise in temporal succession and serve as causes of increasingly clear cognition, are comprehended.

children.text: yadyapi ca pramāraviṣayāveva visaṃvādāvisaṃvādau saṃbhavavyabhicāralakṣaṇau tathāpyavisaṃvādasya dhruvaviṣayatvapratipādanārthaṃ svarūpagrahaṇaṃ sarvasya jñānasya dharmiṇyavisaṃvādāditi //
children.translated_text: Although non-discrepancy and discrepancy — characterized by possibility and deviation — pertain only to the object of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), nevertheless, the inclusion of 'non-discrepancy' in its own form is for the purpose of establishing that non-discrepancy pertains to a certain object — [the idea being] that all cognition is non-discrepant with respect to the qualified subject.
the perceiver does not come close. Or rather, it is to be expected to arise only when one is not very near.

children.text:
pravṛttisāmarthyāditi vyadhikāraṇo heturatastadarthamāha--samarthapravṛttijanakatvāditi /
yadyapi samarthapravṛtti tvādityuktesamañjasaṃ tathāpi pravṛttiryasyeti sambandhe ṣaṣṭhī /
sa ca pramāṇapravṛttyorjanyajanakabhāva eveti sa eva
children.translated_text: [The phrase] 'from the capacity for activity' — since this is a reason pertaining to a different locus, he states the purpose of that: 'because it generates effective activity.' Although saying 'from effective activity' would be inelegant, nevertheless, the genitive [case ending] is used in the sense 'activity of which,' establishing the relation of being produced and producer between <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) and activity — and that alone

children.text:
darśitaḥ /
nanu na tāvat pramāṇyasamarthapravṛtti janakatvayoravinābhāvaḥ pratyakṣeṇa śakyagrahaḥ, tayorevāpratyakṣatvāt /
prāmāṇyaṃ hi samarthapravṛttijanakatvānumeyam /
taccānvayavyatirekānumeyameveti /
nāpyanumānenānvayagrahaḥ /
prāmāṇyasya
children.translated_text: is demonstrated. Now, the invariable concomitance between validity and capacity to generate effective activity cannot be grasped by perception, because both are themselves imperceptible. For validity is to be inferred through the capacity to generate effective activity, and that is inferrable only through agreement in presence and agreement in absence. Nor can agreement in presence be grasped through inference,

children.text: kvacidapyasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: since validity is not established anywhere.

children.text: siddhau vā kimanumānena, anumānantarasiddhatve tvanavasthaivetyata āha--yadi punariti //
children.translated_text: Or, if it is established, what need is there for inference? And if it were established through another inference, there would be an infinite regress — therefore he says 'if, however...'

children.text:
atra copekṣājñānānāṃ pakṣatvenānupādānānna bhāgāsiddhiḥ /
vyatirekī ca sarvatra sapakṣābhāvamabhyupetya pravartata iti
children.translated_text: And here, since cognitions of indifference are not included as instances of the thesis, there is no fallacy of an unestablished part [of the thesis]. And the negative inference operates by accepting the absence [of the <s>sādhya</s>] in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (positive instance) in every case;

children.text: nāsādharaṇānaikāntikatā /
children.translated_text: therefore there is no fallacy of being an uncommon or inconclusive [reason].

children.text: na ca vācyam etasyaivānumānasyārthavattvānavadhāraṇe kathaṃ pramāṇānāmarthavattvasiddhiḥ? tadavadhāraṇe vā kathaṃ kevalavyatirekitvamiti? dvividhaṃ hyanumānasyārthavattvam, avinābhāvalakṣaṇaṃ pramājananalakṣaṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Nor should one say: 'If the efficacy of this very inference is not ascertained, how is the efficacy of <s>pramāṇas</s> established? Or, if that is ascertained, how can it be a purely negative inference?' For the efficacy of an inference is twofold: characterized by invariable concomitance, and characterized by generating valid cognition.

children.text: tatra svaviṣayaparicchede kartavye avinābhāvāvadhāraṇamevāpekṣate na pramākaraṇatvāvadhāraṇamityanavaghṛtaprāmāṇyenaivānena pramāṇānāṃ pramāṇaphalatvalakṣaṇaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ sādhyata iti sarvaṃ sundaram //
children.translated_text: Of these, for the task of determining its own object, [the inference] requires only the ascertainment of invariable concomitance, not the ascertainment of its being a valid instrument. Therefore, by this very [inference] whose validity is not yet ascertained, the validity of <s>pramāṇas</s> — characterized as the fruit of being a <s>pramāṇa</s> — is established. All is well.

children.text:
etenaitadapi nirastam yat prāmāṇyānavadhāraṇe aprāmāṇyānavadhāraṇamapi katham? prāmāṇyaniścayena hi tat niścīyate /
tadanavadhāraṇe tu vyatirekaniścayo 'pi katham, vipakṣasya tathātvāniścayāditi? svarūpato dharmataścānavadhāritenaiva satā pramāṇena svaviṣayaniścayasiddheḥ /
nanu nāstyevāsau vādī yaḥ prāmāṇyāniścaye 'pi vipratipadyeta /
na hi prāmāṇyaṃ svīkṛtya tanniścaye vipratipattiḥ, svīkārasya niścayamūlatvāt /
na cāsvīkṛtya, pramāṇaśūnyavipratipatteḥ sarvatra sulabhatayā sarvavādavidhiniṣedhavyavahāravilopaprasaṅgāt /
aniścite ca prāmāṇye tadatadrūpasaṃdeho 'pi kvacid durlabhaḥ, viśeṣasmṛterabhāvāt tatpūrvakatvācca sarvasaṃśayānām /
nāpi sarvatrāprāmāṇyāsañjanam, prāmāṇyagrahaṇopāyanirākaraṇasyāprāmāṇye 'pi tulyatvāt /
vikalpanirmitamavicāramanoharaṃ prāmāṇyādikamādāyāpi nāsya durvicārasya nirvāhaḥ /
prāmāṇyānabhyupagame vikalpanirmāṇasyāpyasiddheḥ /
na ca vikalpanirmite na saṃśayādivyavahāraḥ samasti /
nahi vājiviṣāṇaṃ veti kaścit sandigdhe, nāpi naraviṣāṇamiti kasyacid viparyayaḥ /
tasmādasti prāmāṇyādikaṃ tanniścayaśca /
tadupāyastu cintāmarhati /
evaṃ cānvayo 'styeva /
tat kathaṃ kevalavyatirekyanumānam ityāśaḍkya saṃpratipattirūttaram--anvayavyatirekī veti /
children.translated_text: By this, the following is also refuted: 'If validity is not ascertained, how can invalidity also not be ascertained? For the latter is ascertained through the ascertainment of the former. And if that is not ascertained, how can the ascertainment of the negative concomitance also [be established], since the counter-instance has not been ascertained as such?' — Because by a <s>pramāṇa</s> that exists, though not ascertained either in its own nature or in its properties, the determination of its own object is established. Now, there is no disputant who would dispute even when validity is not ascertained. For there is no disputation after accepting validity but while [its] ascertainment [is questioned], since acceptance is rooted in ascertainment. Nor [can there be disputation] without accepting [validity], because if a disputation devoid of <s>pramāṇa</s> were easily available everywhere, all the functions of assertion and negation in all doctrines would collapse. And when validity is not ascertained, doubt whether [a cognition] is or is not of such-and-such a nature would also be rare anywhere, due to the absence of a memory of the distinguishing feature, since all doubts are preceded by that. Nor is there universal attribution of invalidity, since the refutation of the means for grasping validity would equally apply to invalidity. Even taking validity and so forth, fabricated by conceptual construction and charming without scrutiny, this untenable [position] cannot be sustained. For if validity is not accepted, even conceptual construction is not established. And regarding what is fabricated by conceptual construction, the functions of doubt and the like do not exist — for no one doubts whether [something is] a horse's horn, nor does anyone have the misconception that [something is] a human horn. Therefore, validity and the like do exist, and so does their ascertainment. But the means thereof deserves reflection. Thus, agreement in presence does exist. Then how can it be a purely negative inference? — Anticipating this doubt, the reply is: 'it is one of agreement and disagreement [combined].'

children.text: kevalavyatirekivādastu anvayānabhyupagamena kṛta ityabhisandhiḥ /
