Therein, experience qualified by the essential form of the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) itself — thus when something is experienced in that form, validity itself has been experienced — this will become clear later. But experience with respect to the qualifier is of two kinds: some [experience] is qualified by the essential qualifier, and some is qualified even by a non-essential qualifier — hence there is sometimes doubt. Therein, to discriminate experience qualified by the essential qualifier, there are distinguishing qualifier-conditions. And these are invariably determined to be of the nature of qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and so forth, since they are incompatible with the objects of error. Thus, in general, being of the same class, as pertaining to cognition, is nothing but being a cognition whose object is the characterized thing (<s>lakṣya</s>) accompanied by the characterizing mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) — this is the understanding regarding perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). But when cognition is generated by a characterizing mark with respect to a non-perceptible characterized thing, that is inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and the understanding of that will be different. Therein, regarding substances (<s>dravya</s>): the cognition of earth in [something] possessing smell — this is an example in general. The cognition of a body in [something] possessing hands, feet, and the like — this is an example in particular. Regarding qualities (<s>guṇa</s>): the cognition of fragrance in <s>ketakī</s> and similar [flowers], the cognition of whiteness in a conch and similar [objects] — these are examples. Regarding action (<s>karman</s>): when a substance that is stationary, without wind, unaffected by intense velocity, and devoid of [the effect of] seeing through clear [mediums like] moving water and the like, is apprehended as moving — that is so. Thus, in those various particulars, the various distinguishing features that preclude deviation cannot be enumerated in each instance.

children.text:
pratyakṣasamānanyāyatayā āgamasya prāmāṇyaṃ samarthayati--evaṃ ceti /
atrāpi tajjātīyatvamāptapraṇetṛkatvam /
abhyāsadaśāpannatvaṃ punaretasya bhūyodarśanena mantrāyurvede tajjātīyatvāya prāmāṇyāvinābhāvasiddhiḥ /
mantrāyurvedasyānabhyāsadaśāpannatvaṃ tadasiddhaḥ nivedayiṣyate sūtrakāreṇa dvitīyādhyāye /
yathā ca prāmāṇyaṃ pravṛttisāmarthyenāvadhāryate anabhyāsadaśāpanneṣu tathāprāmāṇyamapi pravṛttiviparyayeṇa /
yathā ca pravṛtteḥ prāgevābhyāsadaśāpanneṣu
children.translated_text: He establishes the validity of <s>āgama</s> (scriptural testimony) by the same reasoning as perception: 'Thus...' Here too, being of the same class means being authored by an authoritative person (<s>āptapraṇetṛkatva</s>). Having reached the stage of repeated practice means the establishment of the invariable concomitance of validity through repeated observation in the case of <s>mantras</s> and <s>Āyurveda</s> as belonging to that class. That <s>mantras</s> and <s>Āyurveda</s> have not reached the stage of repeated practice — this will be communicated as unestablished by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> in the second chapter. And just as validity is ascertained through the capacity to generate activity in [cases] that have reached the stage of repeated practice, so too is invalidity [ascertained] through the reversal of activity. And just as even prior to activity, in [cases] that have reached the stage of repeated practice,

children.text:
tajjātīyatayā prāmāṇyamavadhāryate, tathāprāmāṇyamapīti mantavyam /
upādhivirodhaśca tajjātīyatvam /
tadabhyāsa evābhyāsadaśāpannatvam /
yathā candramasi candradvayajñānam /
children.translated_text: For example, the cognition of two moons in [the case of viewing] the moon.

children.text: śaḍkhe pītajñānam /
children.translated_text: The cognition of yellow in [the case of viewing] a conch.

children.text: guḍe tiktajñānamityādi /
children.translated_text: The cognition of bitter in [the case of tasting] jaggery — and so forth.

children.text: tasmāt sandigdhe pravṛttisāmarthyamavadhāraṇīyamiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in cases of doubt, the capacity to generate activity must be ascertained.

validity is ascertained through being of the same class, so too should invalidity be understood. And the opposition with a qualifying condition constitutes being of the same class. The repeated practice of that is what constitutes having reached the stage of repeated practice.

children.text:
syādetat /
sāmarthya punarasyāḥ phalenābhisaṃbandhaḥ /
atha phalajñānasyaiva prāmāṇyaṃ kathamavadhāraṇīyamityatra keṣāñcinmatamāha--na ceti /
na punarūdanyopaśamamapi parīkṣyata iti udanyopaśamanamapītyarthaḥ /
tadetadanupapannam /
phalajñānaṃ hi phalasya siddhāvasthasya sādhanānarhatayā niṣprayojanībhūtatvād vā na parīkṣyet tattajjātīyajñānasya sarvāsvavasthāsu arthāvyabhicāritayā niḥśaṅkatvād veti? na tāvadādyaḥ, phalasya siddhāvasthatve tadvat tatsādhanībhūtasyāpi niṣprayojanībhūtatvādaparīkṣyatvaprasaṅgāt /
uttarottarulābhisaṃdhānena tatsādhanaṃ parīkṣyata iti ceta?
children.translated_text: Now, the capacity [of cognition] is its connection with the result. But how is the validity of the cognition of the result itself to be ascertained? Regarding this, he states the view of some: 'Nor...' 'Nor is even the quenching of thirst examined' — the meaning is 'even the quenching of thirst.' This is untenable. Is it that the cognition of the result is not examined because the result, being in a state of accomplishment, has become purposeless due to being unfit for being proved? Or because cognition belonging to that class, in all states, is beyond suspicion due to its non-deviation from the object? Not the first, because if the result is in a state of accomplishment, then even its means, being equally accomplished, would absurdly become purposeless and not subject to examination. If one says that the means is examined due to its being connected with the intention of obtaining further [results],

children.text:
phale 'pyevamastu /
siddha eva hi phale parīkṣite tatsādhanasya tathātvasiddhāvuttarottarulābhisandhiḥ syāt /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, phalajñānasyāpi bhūyo bhūyaḥ spapnādyavasthāsu vyabhicāra darśanāt /
svasthāvasthasya phalajñānaṃ na vyabhicaratīti cet--evaṃ tarhi pirīkṣitameva phalajñānaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] that the result-cognition of one who is in a sound state does not deviate — then the result-cognition would already be examined.

children.text: tathā hi yat svasthāvasthasya phalajñānaṃ tadavyabhicārīti vyāptisiddhau yatraiva tathābhūtajñānatvaṃ paśyati, tatraivāvyabhicāramavadhārayatītyanenābhiprāyeṇāha--vayaṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: For when the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) is established — that the result-cognition of one who is in a sound state is non-deviating — wherever one perceives cognition of such a nature, there alone one ascertains non-deviation. With this intention he says: 'We, however...'

children.text: asyāpyabhyāsadaśāpannatvaṃ prāmāṇyāvināmūtaliḍgopalambhastathā tajjātīyatvaṃ punaḥ svasthāvasthasya phalajñānatvameva /
children.translated_text: For this [result-cognition] too, having reached the stage of repeated practice is the apprehension of a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) invariably concomitant with validity; and being of the same class is nothing but being a result-cognition of one who is in a sound state.

children.text: etenecchādveṣaprayatnajñānaṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: By this, cognition pertaining to desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and effort (<s>prayatna</s>) is [also] explained.

let the same apply to the result too. For when the result, already accomplished, is examined, the confirmation of the means as such would involve connection with the intention of further [results]. Nor the second, because even the cognition of the result is seen to deviate again and again in states such as dreams and the like.

children.text: nanu yadvijñāna dṛṣṭāntayitavyaṃ tasyāpi prāmāṇyaṃ kathaṃ sādhanīyam? evaṃ tattatsādhanasyāpi dṛṣṭāntaparamparāyāḥ kathamityata āha--na ceti /
children.translated_text: Now, the validity of that [cognition] which is to serve as the example — how is it to be established? And similarly, how [is the validity] of the chain of examples for the means of establishing each of those [cognitions]? — therefore he says: 'Nor...'

children.text: phalajñānasyetyupalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Of the cognition of the result' is used illustratively.

children.text: tajjātīyatvena liḍgena prāmāṇye sādhiyitavye yadyad dṛṣṭāntīkriyate tasya tasyeti mantavyam //
children.translated_text: Whatever is taken as an example in establishing validity through the mark of being of the same class — [the same reasoning applies] to each of those — this should be understood.

children.text: yadyavam, pravṛttisāmarthyamanavakāśameva, na hyasti tadvijñānaṃ yat sarvathaivāpūrvaviṣayam /
children.translated_text: If so, the capacity to generate activity becomes entirely without scope, for there is no cognition whatsoever that is entirely of a novel object.

children.text: tathā ca pramāṇator'thapratipattipravṛttisāmarthyayoḥ kathamanāditvamāha--vārttikakāra ityata āha--eteṣu ca madhya iti /
children.translated_text: And thus, how can the beginninglessness of the attainment of objects from <s>pramāṇas</s> and the capacity to generate activity [be explained]? The <s>Vārttika</s>-author says — therefore he says: 'Among these, in the middle...'

children.text: śaḍkitavyabhicāraṃ tajjātīyatvāparāmarśāditi śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The completion is: [there is doubt] due to not apprehending being of the same class in [cases] where deviation is suspected.

children.text: yadyapi phalaṃ na pravṛttiviṣayastathāpi tatsādhanagocarāyāḥ tatsaṃtānagocarāyā eva vā pravṛtteḥ tajjātīyaphalāntarasaṃbandhastannāntarīyakavijātīyaphalasaṃbandho vā svasya narāntarasya vā pravṛttisāmarthyaṃ phalajñānasya draṣṭāvyam //
children.translated_text: Although the result is not the object of activity, nevertheless, the capacity to generate activity of the result-cognition should be understood as the connection with a further result of the same class through the activity directed toward its means, or through the activity directed toward its [causal] continuum — whether for oneself or for another person.

children.text:
tadevaṃ samānanyāyatayā rūpādibāhyarthapratyakṣaprāmāṇyasamarthanānantaraṃ śabdraprāmāṇyaṃ samarthya tadubhayopapattaye samānanyāyatayaiva āntarapratyakṣajñāneṣu madhye phalajñānaprāmāṇyaṃ samarthitam /
samānanyāyatayaivecchādveṣaprayatnagocarasyāpi
children.translated_text: Thus, having established the validity of perception of external objects such as form and the like by the same reasoning, and then having established the validity of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), and for the establishment of both of those, having established the validity of the result-cognition among the internal perceptual cognitions by the very same reasoning — and having indicated, by the same reasoning, the establishment of the validity

children.text: jñānasya prāmāṇyasamarthanaṃ sūcitamityanaṃvyavasāyo 'vaśiṣyate /
tasya cānumānasamānanyāyatayā anumānaprāmāṇyasamarthanānantarameva samarthanaṃ kariṣyata ityabhiprāyavānāha--anumānasyeti /
children.translated_text: The establishment of that, by the same reasoning as inference, will be done right after the establishment of the validity of inference — with this intention he says: 'Of inference...'

children.text: dvidhā hi vyabhicāraśaḍkā kāraṇataḥ svarūpataśca /
children.translated_text: For the suspicion of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is of two kinds: from the cause and from the intrinsic nature [of the cognition].

children.text: sā ca vyāptipakṣadharmatāgrāhakaireva pramāṇairapanīyata iti bhavati nirastasamastavyabhicāraśaṅkamanumitijñānam /
children.translated_text: And that [suspicion] is removed by the very <s>pramāṇas</s> that apprehend <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) and <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of the thesis-locus) — thus the inferential cognition has all suspicion of deviation removed.

children.text: tasyaivaṃbhūtasya svata eva prāmāṇyaṃ niścīyata iti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The completion is: the validity of [inferential cognition] of such a nature is ascertained intrinsically.
even of cognition pertaining to desire, aversion, and effort — the [topic of] immediate apprehension (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) remains.

children.text:
nanu pramāṇatvāviśeṣe 'pi kathamanumitereva svataḥ, na pratyakṣāderityata āha--anumeyeti /
anumitijñānaṃ hyarthasya tathātvaṃ vyavacchindadevotpadyate vahnimānevāyamiti /
tathā cānuvyavasānenānuvyavasīyamānamidaṃ svasvārthāvadhāraṇātmakamevāvasīyate /
na cāviparītārthakatvamanubhavasyānadhyavasyatā avadhāraṇātmakatvamasyāvasitaṃ bhavati /
tathā ca tad avaśyamavaseyam /
tadeva ca prāmāṇyam /
kadācidevaṃbhūtānuvyavasāye 'pi viparyayatvaśaḍkā tadavaskandatītyavaśiṣyate /
sā ca liṅgasamutthatvādeva nāsti /
na hi viśeṣadarśanagrastotpattau śaḍkāvakāśaḥ /
tadetadāha--na hīti /
liṅgākāraṃ vijñānaṃ niścitāvyabhicāramiti śeṣaḥ /
pratyakṣaśābdajñāne tu nāyogavyavacchedātmake, api tvāropānārāpasādhāraṇaviṣayamātrāvabhāsinī /
tathā cānuvyavasāyenāpi tathaivānubhūyete /
children.translated_text: And thus, even by <s>anuvyavasāya</s>, they are experienced in just that way.

children.text: na tvavadhāraṇātmakatayeti na tayoḥ svataḥ prāmāṇyagrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: But not as being of a determinative nature — therefore there is no intrinsic grasp of validity for them.

children.text: atha daivādayogavyavacchedātmake evotpadyete anuvyavasīyete ca, tadā ca niyāmakamantarbhāvyaiva /
children.translated_text: Now, if by chance they do arise and are reflectively apprehended as being of the nature of positive-negative discrimination, then a determining factor must be incorporated.

children.text: tadabhāve tvaviśeṣādavadhāraṇātmakatvaṃ paribhūya tadatadrūpasādhāraṇamevāvatiṣṭheta ityāśayavān niyāmakābhāvamevāha--pratyakṣajñānaṃ tviti //
children.translated_text: In the absence of that [determining factor], due to there being no distinction, the [cognition] would remain merely common to both [veridical and non-veridical] forms, overriding [its] determinative nature — with this intention he states the absence of a determining factor: 'Perceptual cognition, however...'

Now, even though there is no difference in being a <s>pramāṇa</s>, why is [validity ascertained] intrinsically only for inference and not for perception and the like? — therefore he says: 'Of the inferable...' For inferential cognition arises only while discriminating the object's being of such-and-such a nature — 'this one indeed has fire.' And thus, when apprehended by <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (reflective apprehension), it is apprehended as having the nature of determining its own particular object. And the non-erroneousness of experience and its determinative nature are not [separately] ascertained [but are given together]. And thus that must necessarily be apprehended. And that alone is validity. Sometimes even in such <s>anuvyavasāya</s>, the suspicion of erroneousness may assail it — that remains. But that [suspicion] does not exist precisely because [the cognition] arises from the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>). For there is no room for suspicion in [a cognition] whose origination is permeated by the apprehension of the distinguishing feature. This is what he says: 'For...' The completion is: cognition bearing the form of the inferential mark is of ascertained non-deviation. But perceptual and verbal cognitions are not of the nature of positive-negative discrimination; rather, they merely manifest what is common to both veridical apprehension and non-veridical apprehension — [that is,] the bare object.

children.text:
dhūmādiyuktadhūmadhvajādijñāne hi yadyapyarthasyāpyarthenāvyabhicāro 'sti, yadyapi cārthādapi tathābhūtādeva tajjñānaṃ jāyate, tathāpyavyabhicāro vā, tadgraho vā? prāktanaḥ tatrākiścitkara eva, indriyāpātamātrādeva yugapadubhayorapyekajñānāvabhāsitayā parāmarśakālānapekṣaṇāt /
aparāmṛṣṭasya cāniyāmakatvāt /
tadidamuktam--api tu sattāmātreṇāvasthitāditi /
avyabhicāriṇo 'pīti śeṣaḥ /
etena śaḍkāmātramapanīyate jñānāntarairiti yaduktaṃ kaiścit tannirastam /
children.translated_text: By this, the view stated by some — that mere suspicion is removed by other cognitions — is refuted.

children.text: śaḍkā hi saṃśaya evābhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: For suspicion is referred to as doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) itself.

children.text: sa ca tattvanirṇayavyatirekeṇāpanetumaśakya eveti tattvanirṇayopāyo 'nusartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that cannot be removed without the determination of reality — therefore the means for determining reality must be pursued.

children.text: tathā ca jñānasvarūpagrāhiṇaḥ kauṇṭhye pratyakṣādyantarābhāve cānumānamevopāya iti tadāha--pravṛttisāmarthyamiti //
children.translated_text: And thus, when the [cognition] that apprehends the intrinsic nature of cognition is inadequate, and in the absence of an intermediate perception or the like, inference alone is the means — therefore he says: 'The capacity to generate activity...'

In the cognition of smoke-possessing [places] such as smoke and the like, or [cognition of] fire-possessing [places] and the like: although the non-deviation of the object from the [other] object does indeed exist, and although the cognition arises only from the object in such a state — nevertheless, is it the non-deviation, or the grasp of that [non-deviation]? The former is entirely ineffectual there, since both [the mark and what it marks] are simultaneously manifested in a single cognition through mere sensory contact, without depending on the time of reflective consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>). And what is not reflectively considered is not determinative. This is what is said: 'But as merely existing' — the completion being: 'even though non-deviating.'

children.text:
syādetat, yadi pratyakṣaśābdajñānayoḥ parataḥ prāmāṇyam, tat kimidānīmanuvyavasāyasyāpi parata eva? tathā ca liḍgaṃ niścitameva niścāyakamityanena nyāyena liṅgāntaraparamparājñānamanavasthāmavatārayatītyata āha--jñānagateti /
atrāpi saiva yuktiḥ /
atadrūpavyudāsenaiva svaviṣayamālambyaivotpattestathaivānubhavaḥ /
utpatterevārabhya viṣayaviśeṣagrahaṇagrastatvācca na śaḍkāvakāśaḥ /
viśeṣaścānuvyavasāyatvameva /
na hyajānannāpi kaścit jānāmītyanuvyavasyati /
na ca śuktikākāre jñāne rajataṃ jānāmīti syāditi tadidamuktam--tādṛśasyeti /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
sabāhyabhyantaraṃ dharmi mātragocaramapi pratyakṣaṃ svata eva pramāṇam, vibhramasyāpi nirālambanasye kvacidanupapatteriti /
uktuyuktiṃ hṛdi nidhāyātidiśati--eteneti /
upamānamupamitirityarthaḥ /
vyākhyātam /
svato 'vadhārya prāmāṇyatayeti śeṣaḥ /
na hyatideśavākyārthajñānasādṛśyajñānayoḥ prāmāṇye niśvite upamitirābhāsībhavati /

yadyapi cānumānopamānānuvyavasāyadharmijñānānāmapi prāmāṇyaṃ parato 'pi śakyagrahameva, santi hi tatrāpi yathāyogaṃ liṅgasādṛśyajñānasamutthatvādīni tajjātīyatvaliṅgāni tathāpi koṣṭhagatyā svata eva prāmāṇyagraho 'tra na svayamiti sa eva darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the validity of inference, analogy, <s>anuvyavasāya</s>, and cognition of the bare subject can also be grasped extrinsically — for there do exist, in their cases too, marks of being of the same class, such as arising from an inferential mark, arising from the cognition of similarity, and the like — nevertheless, by the natural course of things, the grasp of validity is intrinsic here; that it is not [merely] self-[evident] has been shown.

children.text: vipratipannaṃ prati tu parata eva sādhanīyaṃ taditi paramārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for one who is in disagreement [with the cognition], validity must be established extrinsically — that is the ultimate import.

children.text: ataḥ svata evetyavadhāraṇaṃ nāyogavyavacchede nāpyanyayogavyavacchede /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the restriction 'intrinsically alone' is neither a positive-negative exclusion nor an exclusion of other connections.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi? atyantāyogavyavaccheda iti //
children.translated_text: What then? It is an exclusion of absolute disconnection.

Now, if the validity of perceptual and verbal cognitions is [ascertained] extrinsically, then is the validity of <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (reflective apprehension) also extrinsic? And thus, by the principle that 'only a mark that is itself ascertained can serve as an ascertainer,' a chain of cognitions [each requiring] further inferential marks would introduce an infinite regress — therefore he says: 'Pertaining to cognition...' Here too the same reasoning [applies]. [The <s>anuvyavasāya</s>] arises apprehending its own object through the exclusion of what is not of that nature, and the experience is just so. And since from its very origination it is permeated by the apprehension of the particular distinguishing feature, there is no room for suspicion. And the distinguishing feature is nothing but its being an <s>anuvyavasāya</s>. For no one who does not know [something] reflectively apprehends 'I know.' Nor in a cognition having the form of mother-of-pearl would there be [the reflective apprehension] 'I know silver' — this is what is said: 'Of such a kind...' And this is illustrative. Even perception that has both external and internal [objects] as its subject and pertains merely to the bare subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is intrinsically a valid means of knowledge, since even error, being without a [real] substratum, is in some cases impossible. Keeping the stated reasoning in mind, he extends [the argument]: 'By this...' '<s>Upamāna</s>' means <s>upamiti</s> (analogical cognition) — this is the meaning. '[This is] explained.' The completion is: 'having ascertained validity intrinsically.' For when the validity of the cognition of the meaning of the sentence of comparison and of the cognition of similarity is ascertained, the analogical cognition does not become a semblance.

children.text:
nanvetāvatāpi vijñānakaraṇānamindriyādīnāṃ prāmāṇyasya kutaḥ siddhiḥ? na hi phalayathārthatvamevāmīṣāṃ prāmāṇyamityata āha--sevadanasya ceti /
nanvindriyādayo yadyarthavyāmicāriṇaḥ kathamarthadhiyamavyabhicāriṇī janayeyuḥ, tathātve vā rāsabho 'pi vahnadhiyamavyabhicāriṇī janacet, aviśeṣādityata āha--na ceti /
yathārdrendhanaṃ dahanavyamicāryapi dahanasaṃbandhāt
children.translated_text: Now, even so, from where is the validity of the sense-faculties and the like, which are the instruments of cognition, established? For it is not the case that the veridicality of the result is itself the validity of these — therefore he says: 'and of apprehension.' Now, if the sense-faculties and the like deviate from the object, how could they generate a cognition that does not deviate from the object? Or if they could, even a donkey would generate a non-deviating cognition of fire, since there would be no distinction — therefore he says: 'nor [is it so].' Just as wet fuel, though deviating from fire, through its connection with fire

children.text:
dahanāvyabhicāriṇaṃ dhūmaṃ janayanna niyogaparyanuyogāvarhati kāraṇasvābhāvyāt, tathendriyādyapyarthavyabhicāriṇaṃ tathāvidhasahakāryupabṛṃhitaṃ tenārthena saṃbandhāt tadarthāvyabhicāri jñānaṃ janayedityarthaḥ /
tadetatprāmāṇyaṃ nāvaśyaṃ sarvatrāvadhāryate, tadā śrayasyaiva saṃvedanasya sarvatrānavadhāraṇāt /
tathā sati cānavasthāyā viṣayasaṃcāro na syāt /
tasmāt tīvrasaṃvegitayā yattu saṃvedanamavaśyaṃ saṃvedanīyam, yatra yatra cāparo viśaṣataḥ
children.translated_text: generates smoke that does not deviate from fire, and deserves neither obligation nor reproach [for this], due to the natural character of the cause — in the same way, the sense-faculties and the like, though deviating from the object, when supplemented by appropriate auxiliary causes, through their connection with that object, can generate cognition that does not deviate from that object. This is the meaning. This validity is not necessarily ascertained in every case, since the apprehension that supports it is itself not ascertained in every case. Were that the case, there would be no engagement with objects, due to infinite regress. Therefore, whatever apprehension is necessarily apprehended due to the intensity of its impact, and wherever someone specifically

children.text: sāmānyato vā vipratipadyate jijñāsate vā tatra tatra prāmāṇyamuktenāpāyenāvadhāraṇīyamityato nānavasthetyāśayavānupasaṃhāravyājenoktamarthaṃ saṃkalayya āha--tasmādathasaṃdehāditi //
children.translated_text: or generally disputes or inquires — there, validity should be ascertained by the method stated. Therefore there is no infinite regress. With this intention, collecting the meaning stated under the guise of a non-conclusion, he says: 'therefore, from doubt about the object...'

children.text:
nanvarthāniśvayenāpi pravartamāno na hi tatsādhanatāmanumāya pravartitumarhati arthitvābhāvāt, na hi tatsādhanatvānumānaṃ vyāptigrahaṇaṃ vinā /
na ca so 'pi pravṛtti vineti tadavasthamevetaretarāśrayatvamityata āha--arthasyeti /
yadyapi prāmāṇyāniścayavadapekṣitopāyatvāniścayenāpi tatra tatra pravartate tathāpyapekṣitopāyatāṃ pākṣikīmapyurarīkṛtya pravṛttiḥ /
na ca tatsaṃśayastasyāmapyanupalabdhāyāmanyatrāpi syāt /
ataḥ punarapyupalabdhirāyāteti /
children.translated_text: Now, even one who acts under uncertainty about the object is not entitled to act by inferring the means-character [of the <s>pramāṇa</s>], since he has no desire [for proof of that]. For the inference of means-character is not possible without apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> (universal concomitance). And that [apprehension] also does not [occur] without activity — so the situation is the same, namely mutual dependence — therefore he says: 'of the object.' Although, just as in the case of non-ascertainment of validity, one acts here and there even without ascertainment of the desired means, nevertheless activity proceeds by accepting the means-character even as [merely] possible. And the doubt about that would not arise elsewhere when it has not been encountered [there]. Hence, the encounter arises again.

children.text:
ato 'nāditāmādāyaiva parihṛtam /
arthapratipattiriti vārttike yadyapyarthaśabdo 'pekṣitopāyamevāha tasyaiva pravṛttiviṣayatvāt,
children.translated_text: Therefore, by accepting [its] beginninglessness itself, [the objection of mutual dependence] is resolved. In the <s>Vārttika</s>, [the phrase] 'apprehension of the object' — although the word 'object' refers only to the desired means, since that alone is the object of activity,

children.text: aryamānatvācca, tathāpi dharmimātrapratipattyanumeyapratipattyorbhinnakālatvādapekṣitatvācca tathaiva vyācaṣṭe--arthapratipattiriti //
children.translated_text: and because it is what is being sought — nevertheless, since the apprehension of the mere qualified subject and the apprehension of what is to be inferred are at different times and are the objects of [different] expectations, he glosses it thus: 'apprehension of the object.'

children.text:
nanu pramāṇasya prayojanavattvamākṣiptaṃ vā samādhīyeta jijñāsitaṃ vā jñāpyeta? na tāvadādyaḥ /
na hyasti puruṣo yaḥ pramāṇaṃ niṣprayojanamiti brūyāt, tanmūlatvāt sarvapuruṣārthasiddheḥ /
yasya tu puruṣārtho nāsti sa nirūcchvāsa eva śīryeta /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, tasya saṃśayādivat sūtrapāṭhānantarameva jñāpayitumucitatvādityata āha--tatredamiti /
neyaṃ pramāṇaprayojanajijñāsā /
kiṃ nāma? śāstrārthaubhūtasya paramanyāyasya niḥśreyasaṃ prati gurupāyatve manyamānena laghīyati pravṛttyupāyaṃ vidyamāne śāstrārambha evākṣipyate /
sa ca samādhātumārabdha ityarthaḥ /
daśānāṃ duḥkhasaṃjñābhāvanaṃ mumukṣutādāḍhrayārtham /
ātmano yāthātmyaṃ sakalopādhivinirmuktatvam /
tasya bhāvanaṃ dhyānam /
ādigrahaṇena tu tadupāyabhūtāḥ pravṛttayo yamaniyamāsanaprāṇāyāmadhāraṇālakṣaṇa gṛhyante /
ātmatattvasākṣātkāra iti samādhiḥ /
vairāgyaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, is the efficacy of the <s>pramāṇa</s> something that is implied and needs to be resolved, or something that is inquired about and needs to be made known? Not the first. For there is no person who [questions whether] a <s>pramāṇa</s>

children.text:
paramā vaśīkāraḥ /
paripākaḥ savāsanakleśanirmokṣaḥ /
etena sāḍgopāḍgo yogo darśitaḥ /
śaḍkāmukvā bhāṣyamuttarayati--tatredamupaniṣṭhata iti tathāpi nyāyasya gurupāyatve na parihṛtam, nyāyanirṇotārthasyāpi pravṛttyapekṣāṇāt /
pravṛttasya nyāyānapekṣaṇādityata āha--etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
nanu ubhayorapi tulyatve kuto viśeṣāt pramāṇameva vyutpādyate na pravṛttiparītyata āha--tathāpīti /
śravaṇamanananididhyāsanasākṣātkāralakṣaṇāyā pravṛtteḥ svarūpataḥ phalataśca pramāṇāntarbhūtatvāt tadvyutpādanameva pravṛttivyutpādanam /
children.translated_text: Because the activity characterized by hearing, reflection, meditation, and direct realization is included within the <s>pramāṇas</s> both in its nature and in its result, the elucidation of that [<s>pramāṇa</s>] is itself the elucidation of [that] activity.

children.text: na ca pravṛttivyutpādanena pramāṇaṃ vyutpāditaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: And by the elucidation of activity, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is not [separately] elucidated.

children.text: na hi pravṛtteḥ phalaṃ pramāṇaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ vetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For neither the result of activity nor the nature of activity is the <s>pramāṇa</s> — that is the meaning.

children.text: nanu śāstrārthasya prayojanavyutpādanāvasare pramāṇamarthavaditi kutaḥ? na hi pramāṇaṃ śāstrarthaḥ, api tu nyāya ityata āha--sāmānyābhidhānaṃ ceti //
children.translated_text: Now, at the juncture of explaining the purpose of the <s>śāstra</s>'s content, from where [comes the assertion] that '<s>pramāṇa</s> is efficacious'? For the <s>pramāṇa</s> is not the content of the <s>śāstra</s>; rather, <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning) is — therefore

[has efficacy]. The supreme mastery [is described]. '<s>Paripāka</s>' (maturation) is the liberation from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) together with their residual impressions. By this, <s>yoga</s> (union) with all its limbs has been shown. Having raised the objection, he responds to the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary): 'that...'

children.text:
tadanena prabandhena niṣprayojanatvāśakyaprayojanatvānabhimataprayojanatvopāyagauravaśaḍkāḥ parihṛtāḥ /
tat kimaparamavaśiṣyate yadarthaṃ lokavṛttamanūdyata ityataḥ prathama tātparyamanusmārayanneva vārttikamavatārayati--prāmāṇyeti /
apramāṇenetyatrāpi yadyapi vāñmanasavisaṃvādaḥ niṣedhavidhyupāya eva hi pramāṇam /
tasmānniṣedhopāyatāṃ jānato 'pyapramāṇena niṣedhāmīti vacanaṃ manovisaṃvādyava /
tathāpi vyāmohādapyupapatterevaṃbhūtābhiprāyasthairye 'pi nāsmākaṃ kācit kṣatirityetāvatā anujñaivāttaraṃ dattam--vāḍmanasayorvisaṃvāda iti /
prāmāṇyāgrahe pramāṇenetyevaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate /
children.translated_text: by this sequence, the objections of purposelessness, impossibility of purpose, undesirable purpose, and excessive means are resolved. Then what more remains

children.text: tataḥ pramāṇenetyevaṃ vadato 'vaśyaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ manasi viparivartate /
children.translated_text: [to say]? Therefore, when one says 'by <s>pramāṇa</s>,' validity necessarily revolves in the mind.

children.text: tathā cāgṛhītaprāmāṇyeneti vacanaṃ manovisaṃvādītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Accordingly, the statement 'by one whose validity is not grasped' is self-contradictory — that is the meaning.

children.text: lokavṛttamabādhito vyavahāra ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Worldly practice' means uncontradicted conventional usage — that is the meaning.

children.text: nanu pramāṇena khalvayaṃ jñātetyādi, bhāṣyaṃ lokavṛttānuvādo 'stu /
children.translated_text: Now, 'Indeed, this is known by a <s>pramāṇa</s>' and so forth — let the <s>bhāṣya</s> be a restatement of worldly practice.

children.text: pramāṇata ityādi punaḥ kathamityata āha--kāraṇapradarśanadvāreṇeti /
children.translated_text: But how [does] 'from a <s>pramāṇa</s>' and so forth [function]? — therefore he says: 'through the indication of the cause.'

children.text: na hi lokavṛttaṃ svarūpeṇopayujyate /
children.translated_text: For worldly practice is not useful in its own form.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi? tasyāvaśyābhyupeyatayā tadupāyo 'pyavaśyābhyupeya ityanenābhisandhinā sopāyameva tadanūdyata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: What then? Since it must necessarily be accepted, its means also must necessarily be accepted — with this intention, worldly practice together with its means is restated. That is the meaning.

children.text:
āgāmibhāṣye heyādīnāṃ sphuṭatvāt tasyedānīmakṣarārtho vyākriyata iti mā śaḍkiṣṭhā ityāha--asyaiveti /
vārttikasaṃbaddho granthor'thapadānītyākāro vārttikagranthastasya /
tādṛśa eva bhāṣyagato bhāṣyasaṃbaddho granthastasyetyarthaḥ /
amidheyānāṃ paurvāparyaniyamāya guṇapradhānabhāve jijñāsyamāne abhidhānarūpasya śāstrasya kaḥ prastāva ityata āha--śāstraśabda iti /
evaṃ tarhi heyādīnāṃ śāstrārtharūpatayā na pṛthakkoṭitvam /
tathā caikakoṭikatayā kimapekṣya guṇapradhānabhāvacintetyata āha-atra ceti /
children.translated_text: Since the heya (what is to be abandoned) and the like will be clear in the forthcoming <s>bhāṣya</s>, lest one suspect 'the literal meaning of this is explained only now' — he says: 'of this very...' Connected with the <s>Vārttika</s>...

children.text:
kathaṃ punaranena pramāṇādicaturvargo 'tra labhyate iti vārttikamanuktopālabhbho mā bhūdityata āha--teneti /
tanmūlatvād itarasiddheriti /
siddhiḥ pratītirniṣpattiśca /
tatra heyopāyayoḥ pratītireva /
children.translated_text: Now, how is the fourfold group of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the like obtained here? — lest there be reproach for what is left unsaid in the <s>Vārttika</s>, he says: 'by that.' Because [the fourfold group] is rooted in that...

children.text:
adhigantavyasya tu pratītirniṣpattiśca /
yadyapi ca hānasyāpi pramāṇarūpasya pratītirastyeva, tathāpi pramāṇādeveti taditaretyuktam /
niṣpattistu hānasyājñānādeva yasmāt kiṃ tajjñānena? jñānāt tu yasmāt tasya pramāṇāyattatvameveti bhāvaḥ /
pramātrādicaturvarge tu pramātṛprameyayoḥ siddhiḥ pratītireva /
children.translated_text: But in the fourfold group of the knower and the like, the establishment of the knower and the knowable is cognition alone.

children.text: pramāyāśca niṣpattirapīti /
children.translated_text: And of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), [there is] accomplishment as well.

children.text: tadidamuktam--pramāyāśca tatkāryatvāditi /
children.translated_text: This is what is stated: 'and of <s>pramā</s>, because of being its effect.'

children.text: nanu pramātrādīnāmapi prayojanavattvādarthavadityanena kiṃ pramāṇasyādhikyamāhitamityata āha--atiśāyane matuciti //
children.translated_text: Now, since the fourfold group of the knower and the like is also efficacious, what additional [status] is conferred upon the <s>pramāṇa</s> by [the statement] 'it is efficacious'? — therefore he says: 'the possessive suffix <s>matup</s> [is used] for indicating superiority.'

But of what is to be attained, [there is both] cognition and accomplishment. Although the cognition of abandonment, which has the form of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, certainly exists, nevertheless, 'from the <s>pramāṇa</s> alone' — so that [statement stands].

children.text:
nanvasya caturvargadvayasya niḥśreyasādhigamaṃ prati vikalpaḥ, samuccayo vā? ubhayamāpyanupapannamabhinnatvāt tathā hi ya evārthaḥ pramātā prameyaṃ pramitiriti sa eva heyo 'dhigantavya iti ya evārtho hānopāyāviti sa eva pramāṇamiti /
saṃśayādīnāmapi nyāyaparikaratayā nyāyaśarīratvāt tasya ca pramāṇatvāditi /
tasmāt abhinnatvāt na vacanabhaḍgibhedamātreṇa vikalpaḥ /
nāpi samuccayaḥ /
na hi bhavati tarūṇā vā vṛkṣeṇa vedaṃ sādhanīyaṃ tarūvṛkṣābhyāṃ vetyata āha--vivakṣābhedenati /
tadanupapatterityata anena nimittabhedamabhipraiti /
tenāyamarthaḥ yadyapyubhayatrāpi ṣoḍaśaiva padārthāḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ, tathāpi yathā pramāṇtvena pramāṇaṃ jñeyaṃ tathā hānatvenāpi /
anyathā hānāntaramanuśriyeta /
nirarthakaṃ ca pramāṇaṃsyāt /
pramāṇatve cājñāte hānatā na nirvahet /
yathā ca svarūpeṇa saṃśayādayo jñeyāḥ pramāṇaparikaratayā tathā hānopāyatayāpi /
anyathopāyāntaramanuśriyeta /
nirarthakāścaite syuḥ /
parikaratve cājñāte upāyatā na nirvahet /
yathā ca śarīrādayo daśa prameyatayā jñeyāḥ tathā heyatayāpi, anyathā aheyāḥ syuḥ /
heyāntaraṃ cānuśriyeta /
prameyatve cājñāte heyatā na nirvahet /
yathā cāpavargaḥ prameyatayā jñeyaḥ, tathā adhigantavyatayāpi /
anyathā adhigamyāntaramanuśriyeta /
anupādeyaśca syāt /
prameyatayā cājñāte 'dhigantavyatā na nirvaheta /
yathā cātmā prameyatayā adhigantavyaḥ, tathā pramātṛtayāpi /
anyathā pramātrantaramanuśriyeta, anavasthā ca syāt /
prameyatve cājñāte sopādhinirūpādhirūpatayā
children.translated_text: Now, regarding this pair of fourfold groups — is their relation to the attainment of the highest good one of alternation or of aggregation? Both are untenable, because of non-difference [between the two]. For,

children.text: heyopādeyate na nirvahecātām /
yathā ca buddhirbuddhitvena tathā tabhdedaḥ pramititayāpi /
children.translated_text: And just as cognition [is known] through the property of being cognition, so too its differentiation [is known] through the property of being valid cognition.

children.text: anyathā pramityantaramanuśriyeta, niṣphalaṃ vā pramāṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, another [additional] valid cognition would be required, or the <s>pramāṇa</s> would be fruitless.

children.text: prameyatve cājñāte heyatā na nirvahediti /
children.translated_text: And when the to-be-known character [of the <s>prameya</s>] is not known, the to-be-abandoned character cannot be distinguished.

children.text: tasmāt ta eva pramāṇādayaḥ ubhayathā jñāyantāmiti vivakṣitvobhayacaturvargopādānaṃ kṛtamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, let those very <s>pramāṇas</s> and the like be known in both ways — with this intention, the adoption of both fourfold groups is made. That is the meaning.
the to-be-abandoned and the to-be-adopted would not be distinguished.

children.text:
yadapyuktaṃ kaiścit--heyahānopāyādhigantavyeṣveva caturṣu puruṣārthaḥ parisamāpyate /
yathā loke heyaḥ kaṇṭakaḥ /
hānamupānat /
tadupāyastu pādukākṛdātiḥ adhigantavyo duḥkhābhāvaḥ /
śāstre ca heyo rogaḥ /
cikitsā hānam /
tadupāyo nidānajñānam /
children.translated_text: is its extraction; the means is the knowledge of the cause;

children.text: adhigantavyamārogyamityataścaturṣu vaktavyeṣu ṣoḍaśapadārthavarṇanaṃ kkopayujyata iti tadāpi nirastam, caturvargasyaiva vivakṣābhedāt ṣoḍaśadhā bhedenābhidhānāt /
children.translated_text: and the to-be-attained is health' — and therefore, 'where among four things to be stated is the description of sixteen categories relevant?' — that too is refuted, since the fourfold group itself

children.text: vivakṣābhedasya copapatti pratipadaṃ bhāṣyakāra eva darśayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: encompasses [the sixteen]. The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) himself will show the justification of the difference in intention at each step.

children.text: etadavagamyaiva yenādhikaṃ coditaṃ tanmatamapākaroti--eteneti //
children.translated_text: Having understood this, he refutes the view of one who has objected further: 'by this...'

As for what some have said — 'the purpose of man is completed in just four: the to-be-abandoned, abandonment, the means, and the to-be-attained. Just as in ordinary life, the to-be-abandoned is the thorn; abandonment

children.text:
vyākhyāyate avayavaśa iti viśeṣaṇe kriyāyāstātparyam /
na tu viśeṣye ityarthaḥ /
etadevāttaratra sphuṭayati--tatrāsyāvayaveṣviti /
kasmāt pramāṇāditi nābhihitam? evaṃ hyasaṃdigdhaiva pañcamī syādityarthaḥ /
asyeti prakṛtapañcamīparāmarśe liṅgāsaṃgati rityata āha--asyeti /
pañcamyāḥ taseḥ prayogaṃ darśayitvā pañcamīvyatirekeṇa taseḥ ākṣepasamādhāne asaṃgate ityākṣepaṃ vyākhyāyāvatārayati--vacanavyāptyarthamiti /
nanu pramāṇābhyāṃ pramāṇairiti bhavataṃ saṃplavaḥ, pramāṇeneti tu kathamityata āha--yatra dvayoditi /
viṣayaikatāmātra saṃplavaḥ, na tu kāraṇānāṃ samuccayaḥ /
tathā sati phalabhedo na syāt /
nāpi samuccitānāṃ karaṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Nor would the accumulated [causes] function as instruments.

children.text: tathā sati vyāpārabhedo na syāditi jñāpanārthamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For if that were the case, there would be no difference of operation — this is meant as an indication, this is the meaning.

children.text: ata eveti /
children.translated_text: For this very reason.

children.text: evakāraḥ sādhakatamāntaraṃ vyavacchindan tasya vyāpāraṃ phalaṃ ca vyavacchinatti, na tvasya svavyāpārulayoritaretaranairapekṣyaṃ darśayati, tasya saṃplave 'pi saṃbhavādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The particle <s>eva</s> (indeed), by excluding another that is more effective, excludes its operation and result, but does not show mutual independence of its own operation and result, since [such independence] is possible even in conflation — this is the meaning.

It is explained: the purport of the verbal action is in the qualifier 'component-wise,' not in the qualified — this is the meaning. He makes this very point clear later: 'therein, in its components.' Why was it not stated 'from a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)'? For in that case, the ablative would have been unambiguous — this is the meaning. 'Of this' — since there is incongruity of gender in referring to the present ablative, to this he says: 'of this.' Having shown the usage of the ablative suffix <s>-tas</s>, he raises the objection that without the ablative the objection and resolution regarding <s>-tas</s> are incongruent, and then introduces [the resolution]: 'for the purpose of the scope of the expression.' Now, 'by two <s>pramāṇas</s>' or 'by [multiple] <s>pramāṇas</s>' — this would be conflation for you; but how [does it work] with 'by a <s>pramāṇa</s>' [in the singular]? To this he says: 'where there are two.' Conflation is merely identity of object, not the accumulation of causes. For if that were the case, there would be no difference of result.

children.text:
kasmāt punaḥ karaṇārtho gamyate? prakṛtipratyayayoḥ katarasmādityarthaḥ /
ayamāśayaḥ /
yadi tṛtīyayā karaṇatvamabhidhīyate kiṃ prakṛtisthena lyuṭpratyayena? atha tenaiva, kiṃ tṛtīyayeti? jñāpakasya kārakatvaśaḍkā mā bhūdityata āha--arthamarthādhigatimiti /
nanu hetukaraṇabhāvo 'vagamyatāmityetadarthaṃ vibhaktivyāptirāsthīyate pramāṇamiti, prātipadikādeva sākṣātkaraṇatvamarthato hetutvaṃ gamyata iti kiṃ vibhaktivyāptyetyata āha--atra ceti /
na ca vācyaṃ karaṇabhāvenāpi pramāṇaphalayostādātmyaṃ pratiṣedddhuṃ śakyam, tat ki tannāntarīyakahetutabhdāvāmidhānārthaṃ pañcamyeti, sādhākatvamātrasyaiva sāmarthye tamabarthasyāsamarthatvāt /
tatra vipratipatteśca /
kasmāditi praśnārthamabhipretyāha--pramāṇapratipadiketi /
tadevamanuvādakatvaṃ
children.translated_text: Why then is the instrumental sense understood? The meaning is: from which of the two — the stem or the suffix? This is the intention: if the instrumental case expresses instrumentality, then what is the purpose of the <s>lyuṭ</s>-suffix standing in the stem? If by that [suffix] alone [instrumentality is expressed], then what is the purpose of the instrumental case? Lest there be a suspicion that the indicator [also] has agency, to this he says: 'the object, the apprehension of the object.' Now, let the relation of cause and instrument be understood — for this purpose the scope of the case-ending is adopted [in the expression] '<s>pramāṇa</s>' — instrumentality is understood directly from the nominal stem itself, while causality [is understood] from the meaning; so what need is there for the scope of the case-ending? To this he says: 'and here.' Nor can it be said that even through instrumentality, the identity of <s>pramāṇa</s> and its result can be denied — then why the ablative for expressing the relation of non-separable causality? — because mere effectiveness is capable [of being expressed by the instrumental], while the meaning of the ablative [-tas] is incapable [of expressing that]. And because there is disagreement about that. Intending the interrogative sense 'why?', he says: 'the stem <s>pramāṇa</s>.' Thus, by establishing the corroborative nature,

children.text:
samarthayatā lyuṭtṛtīyayoḥ paunarūktyaṃ samāhitam /
na
children.translated_text: the redundancy of <s>lyuṭ</s> and the instrumental case is resolved.

children.text:
cānuvādakatvaṃ śabdābhyāsasya prayojanavattāvyatirekeṇa sidhyatītyataḥ prayojanaṃ darśayati--pramākārakāntarebhya iti /
laukike tu prayoge saṃkhyābhidhānādvibhakteḥ sārthakatvaṃ draṣṭavyamiti /
viśiṣṭaviṣayatvena saṃplavākṣepo 'saṃgata eva, agnyādiviśiṣṭe parvatādau pratyakṣānumānayoḥ saṃplavādityata āha--viśiṣṭo bhinna iti /
viṣayatvasāmānyābhiprāyamekavacanam /
children.translated_text: The singular is with the intention of the generality of being an object.

children.text: arthasamārthyasamutthaṃ pratyakṣaṃ yato 'tor'thagocaram /
children.translated_text: Perception, arising from the capacity of the object, is therefore object-directed.

children.text: tat kiṃ hetutvameva viṣayalakṣaṇam? netyāha--sa eva cārtha iti /
children.translated_text: Then is causality itself the defining characteristic of the object? No, he says: 'and that very object.'

children.text: kimato cadyevamityata āha--na ca sāmānyamiti //
children.translated_text: What follows from this? To this he says: 'and a universal is not.'

And since corroborative nature is not established without purposefulness of the repetition of words, he shows the purpose: 'from other agents of valid cognition.' But in ordinary usage, the meaningfulness of the case-ending is to be seen as [expressing] number. The objection of conflation on the ground of having a qualified object is indeed incongruent, since perception and inference do conflate regarding a mountain qualified by fire and the like — to this he says: 'the qualified is different.'

children.text:
nanu ca sāṃvyavahārikaṃ svalakṣaṇamapyevamevetyata āha--svalakṣaṇamiti /
deśakālānanugataṃ vicārasahamityarthaḥ /
nanu yadyapi pratyakṣaṃ na sāmānyarūpamavagāhate tathāpi yadyanumānamapi svalakṣaṇamavagāheta tata eva tāvatāpi saṃplavaḥ syādityata āha--na ceti /
nanu bhavatvanumānaṃ sāmānyamātraniyatam, pratyakṣamapi hyatra pravartsyati /
bhaviṣyati ca sāmānyamapi sattvādākārādhāyakamato 'pi saṃplavasiddhirityata āha--na ceti /
bhavitumarhati paramārthasaditi śeṣaḥ /
vicārāsahatvādityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The intention is: because it does not withstand critical examination.

children.text: tat kiṃ sāmānyasyāsattvāt svalakṣaṇe ca pratibandhagrahāsaṃbhavādanumānaṃ nirviṣayamevetyata āha--tadidamiti /
children.translated_text: Then, since the universal is unreal and since apprehension of invariable concomitance in the particular is impossible, is inference entirely without an object? To this he says: 'this then.'

children.text: tat kimanumānamapramāṇameva aparamārthagocaratvāt? yadyevaṃ kathaṃ tadanyadullikhyānyatra pravartayati /
children.translated_text: Then is inference not a valid means of knowledge at all, since it does not bear on ultimately real objects? If so, how does it initiate [cognition of] something else and direct [action] elsewhere?

children.text: kathaṃ ca tadavisaṃvādakam? kathaṃ ca bādhitākāraṃ pramāṇatayā vyavahiyata ityata āha-tasmāditi //
children.translated_text: And how is it non-deceptive? And how is [cognition with] a sublated form treated as a valid means of knowledge? To this he says: 'therefore.'

Now, even a conventionally recognized particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is just like that — to this he says: '<s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular).' Meaning: not pervading place and time, withstanding critical examination. Now, although perception does not apprehend the form of a universal, still, if inference too apprehends the particular, then even by that much there would be conflation — to this he says: 'and not.' Now, let inference be restricted to universals alone; perception too will operate here [on universals]. And since a universal too, being real (<s>sattva</s>) and so forth, can impose its form [on cognition], conflation would be established from that too — to this he says: 'and not.' The remainder is: it cannot be ultimately real.

children.text:
nanu pramāṇāntareṇa saha saṃplavo bhaviṣyatyanayorityata āha--na ceti /
nanvasti śabdādikamityata āha--pramāṇasyeti /
nanu nāntarbhavatyevāsvalakṣaṇaviṣayatvād viṣayāpratibaddhatvāccetyata āha--anantarbhāve ceti /
nanu svalakṣaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇayorvyavasthāyāmapi pratyakṣānumānayorviṣayāntare saṃplavo bhaviṣyatyanayoḥ /
asti hi viṣayāntaraṃ tadvadityāha--na ceti /
na hyasatā sāmānyena paramārthasat svalakṣaṇaṃ tadvad bhavitumarhati, sadasatoḥ saṃbandhābhāvādityarthaḥ /
so 'yaṃ gahanaḥ panthā ityāśayavān āha--yathā caitaditi /
viśeṣa ityatra yadi karmakārakaṃ na ca
children.translated_text: Now, there will be conflation of these [perception and inference] with another <s>pramāṇa</s> — to this he says: 'and not.' Now, there is verbal testimony and the like — to this he says: 'of a <s>pramāṇa</s>.' Now, it simply cannot be subsumed [under perception or inference], since it does not have a particular as its object and since it is not bound to an object [in the same way] — to this he says: 'and in the case of non-subsumption.' Now, even when the distinction between <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) and <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s> (universal characteristic) is maintained, there will be conflation of perception and inference with respect to another object. For there exists such another object — to this he says: 'and not.' For an unreal universal cannot be of the same nature as an ultimately real particular, since there is no relation between the real and the unreal — this is the meaning. 'This is a difficult path' — with this intention he says: 'and as this.' In 'particular,' if it is the object-case, then not

children.text:
tatastadvannāmāparo 'stītyata āha--viśeṣa iti saṃplavamamṛṣyamāṇa idamāha mīmāṃsaha iti śeṣaḥ /
adhigataṃ cārthamityādivārttikasyādhigatatvādivārttikādadhikārthatāṃ vivakṣatrāha--syādetādityādi /
adhigater'the pramāṇāntarasya na tāvadarthādhigamaṃ pratyupayogaḥ, tasya prāgave pramāṇāntarasiddhatvāt /
nāpyanttarottaravyavahārapravāhanirvāha prati, tasyāpi tajjanyasaṃskāraprabhavasmṛtisaṃtati siddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor for sustaining the flow of subsequent practical activity, since that too is established through the continuity of memory arising from the impressions produced by it [the first cognition].

children.text: na ca vācyaṃ smṛtisaṃtatiradhigatisaṃtatirvā astu vyavahārapravartinī na kaścidviśeṣa iti, smṛtivadupadarśitārthamātraviṣayatayā tāsāmapramātvena tatsādhānasyāpramāṇatvaprasaṃgāt /
children.translated_text: Nor can it be said: let the continuity of memory or the continuity of apprehension be the instigator of practical activity — there is no difference — because since those, like memory, have as their object only what has been previously presented, they would not be valid cognitions, and consequently the means establishing them would be non-<s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: tāsāṃ ca tata eva smṛtitvaprasaṃgāt /
children.translated_text: And those [continuities] would, for that very reason, have the status of memory.

children.text: smṛtisaṃtateścāvaśyaṃbhāvitayā tata eva vyavahārisiddhāvadhigatisaṃtatikalpanāyāṃ kalpanāgauravaprasaṃgādityāśayavān piṣṭapeṣaṇamevopasaṃharati--adhigatamiti //
children.translated_text: And since the continuity of memory is inevitable, practical activity being thereby established, the postulation of a continuity of apprehension would involve the fault of unnecessary complexity — with this intention he concludes that it is mere grinding of what is already ground: 'already apprehended.'

since there is nothing else of that nature — to this he says: the one who, unable to tolerate conflation, says 'particular' [and adds] 'let us examine' is the remainder. And since the <s>vārttika</s> beginning 'and the object already apprehended' has been apprehended, he expresses the additional meaning beyond that <s>vārttika</s>: 'this would be' and so forth. As for apprehension of the object, another <s>pramāṇa</s> has no utility for apprehending it, since that [object] is already established by the prior <s>pramāṇa</s> itself.

children.text:
nanu anyatheti vārttike yadi kāraṇagatamanyaprakāratvaṃ vivakṣitaṃ tadā kāraṇagataprakārabhede 'pi na kaścid viṣayagato viśeṣaḥ piṣṭapeṣaṇaparihāropayogī darśitaḥ syāt /
atha viṣayagata eva pramārabhado darśitaḥ, tadā anadhigatārthagantṛtayā kutaḥ saṃplavaḥ? na ca viṣayābhede 'pi pramāṇabhedāt kaścit phalaprakārabhedaḥ prakṛtopayogavānastītyata āha--ayamabhisandhiriti /
piṣṭapeṣaṇe niṣphalatvaṃ vā syāt, aviśiṣṭaphalatvaṃ vā, anapekṣitaphalatvaṃ vā, adhigate 'pyarthe kimityadhigatisādhanamadhigati karotīti praśnamātraṃ vā, sādhanāsaṃbhava eva veti /
children.translated_text: Now, in the <s>vārttika</s> 'otherwise,' if what is intended is a difference of mode residing in the cause, then even with a difference of mode residing in the cause, no difference residing in the object that would serve to avoid the charge of redundancy has been shown. If, on the other hand, the difference of <s>pramāṇa</s> shown is one residing in the object, then how can there be conflation, since it apprehends what has not [yet] been apprehended? And even when the objects are not different, there is no difference of result-mode due to the difference of <s>pramāṇa</s> that would be relevant to the present discussion — to this he says: 'this is the intention.' In the case of redundancy, there would be either fruitlessness, or having an undifferentiated result, or having an unneeded result, or it would merely be the question 'when the object is already apprehended, why does the means of apprehension produce [another] apprehension?', or there is simply the impossibility of [such] a means.

children.text:
tatra sādhanāsaṃbhavaṃ dūṣayati--na hīti /
svakāraṇapratibandhe hi pramāṇaṃ na syāt /
na ca viṣayādhigamaḥ pramākāraṇavirodhī, yena tasmin, satceva pramākāraṇamakāraṇaṃ bhavet /
tasmādālocya svayameva nivarterat yadi cetayeran, na caitadastītyarthaḥ /
praśnamātraṃ dūṣayati--nāpīti /
anapekṣitaphalatvamutthāpya nirākaroti--pramāturiti /
niṣphalatvaṃ nirākaroti--tasmāditi /
pratyutpannakāraṇasāmagrījanitatvaṃ tātkālikāsādhāraṇakāraṇaviśiṣṭasāmagrījanitatvam /
etenānubhavatvaṃ darśitam /
smṛterhyasādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ saṃskāraḥ, ātmāntaḥkaraṇādīnāṃ jñānāntarasādhāraṇyāt /
sa ca cirakālotpanno na pratyutpannaḥ /
yattu pratyutpannamudbodhāparanāma sahakāri na tadādhāraṇam /
children.translated_text: As for the presently existing auxiliary cause called 'awakening' (<s>udbodha</s>), it is not the basis [of the distinction].

children.text: anubhavasya tu catuṣṭayasannikārṣādyasādhāraṇam /
children.translated_text: But for experience, the fourfold contact (<s>catuṣṭayasannikarṣa</s>) and the like are distinctive.

children.text: tacca pratyutpannaṃ pratyagramutpannam /
children.translated_text: And that is presently existing — freshly arisen.

children.text: tathābhūtā buddhirabādhiteti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The remainder is: a cognition of such a nature is unsublated.

Among these, he refutes the impossibility of a means: 'for not.' For if [a <s>pramāṇa</s>] were restricted to [depending on] its own cause, it would not be a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And the apprehension of the object is not opposed to the cause of valid cognition, such that in its presence the cause of valid cognition would become a non-cause. Therefore, having considered [the matter], it would cease of its own accord, if [the <s>pramāṇas</s>] were conscious — but this is not the case, this is the meaning. He refutes the 'mere question': 'nor.' He raises and refutes the 'having an unneeded result': 'of the knower.' He refutes fruitlessness: 'therefore.' Being produced by a causal aggregate with a presently existing [cause] means being produced by a causal aggregate distinguished by a temporally immediate distinctive cause. By this, the character of being an experience (<s>anubhava</s>) is shown. For the distinctive cause of memory is the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>), since self, inner organ, and the like are common to other cognitions. And that [impression] arose long ago and is not presently existing.

children.text:
aviśaṣṭaphalatvamabhyupetya parābhiprāyaṃ nirākaroti--tajjanakānīti /
prathamapramāṇaphalato 'pyaviśiṣṭaphalatayā yadyānarthakyam, dvitīyavat prathamapramāṇasyāpi dvitīyāviśiṣṭaphalatayā ānarthakyaṃ syāt /
anapekṣatvat sārthakamiti
children.translated_text: Accepting the 'having an undifferentiated result,' he refutes the opponent's intention: 'the generators of that.' If, because the result is undifferentiated from that of the first <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is purposelessness [of the second], then there would also be purposelessness of the first <s>pramāṇa</s>, since its result is undifferentiated from [that of] the second. If [one says] it is meaningful because of independence —

children.text:
cet? evaṃ tarhi dvitīyasyāpi svaphale 'napekṣatvameva /
tatphalaṃ pramārūpameva na bhavati /
gṛhītamātragocaratvāt smṛtivadityapi na
children.translated_text: then the second too is independent with respect to its own result. That result simply does not have the form of a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor is it correct [to say] that it is like memory because it pertains only to what is already grasped —

children.text:
yuktam, yathārthānubhavatvaniṣedhe sādhye kālātītatvāt /
anadhikārthatve ca siddhasādhānāt, sādhyasamatvācca /
vyavahāraniṣedhe ca tannimittavirahopādhikatvāt, bādhitatvācca /
pramāvyavahāranimittaṃ ca vakṣyāma ityarthaḥ /
eve tarhi vārttikārthaḥ ka ityata āha--sa eva ceti /
nanu phalasyāpi sākṣātkārāsākṣātkārarūpaḥ prakārabhedo 'styeva, sa evānena kiṃ na pradarśyata ityata āha--yadyapīti /
ādigrahaṇena kāraṇagato 'pīndriyaliṅgādirūpaḥ prakārabhedaḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the word 'and so forth,' the difference of mode residing in the cause, too — in the form of sense-organ, inferential mark, and the like — is included.

children.text: kāraṇabhedasaṃplavanirāsārthameva hi paraḥ pratyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the opponent is established precisely for the purpose of refuting the conflation of causes.

children.text: sa kathaṃ tenaiva pratibodhanīyaḥ? parapratibodhaśca prakṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: How then should he be instructed by that very [method]? And the instruction of the opponent is the topic at hand.

children.text: tadidamuktam--prakṛtānupayogāditi //
children.translated_text: This is what was said: 'because of irrelevance to the topic at hand.'

because in proving the negation of its being a veridical experience, [the reason] is temporally past [i.e., irrelevant]. And in [proving] the absence of additional content, because of proving what is already established and because of being equivalent to what is to be proved. And in negating practical activity, because it is conditional upon the absence of its cause, and because it is sublated. And we shall state the cause of the practice of valid cognition — this is the meaning. Then what is the meaning of the <s>vārttika</s>? To this he says: 'and that very.' Now, the result too has a difference of mode in the form of direct apprehension versus non-direct apprehension — why is that not shown by this? To this he says: 'although.'

children.text:
evaṃ siddhaṃ pramāṇaṃ hṛdi kṛtvā saṃplavavyavasthe vicārite /
saṃprati pramāṇasvarūpaṃ nirūpyata ityāha--vibhaktyarthamiti /
avadhāraṇamiti /
yadi niścayo 'bhimataḥ syāt tasya nāvaśyaṃ saṃśayapūrvakatvamiti sandigdhasya praśna upapannaḥ syādata āha--avadhāryata iti /
tathā ca vicārasya parīkṣāyā avaśyaṃ saṃśayapūrvakatvādagre
children.translated_text: Thus, having established <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) in mind, the determination and distinction [of <s>pramāṇas</s> from non-<s>pramāṇas</s>] have been examined. Now the intrinsic nature of <s>pramāṇa</s> is being determined — he says: 'the meaning of the case-ending.' 'Ascertainment' — if certainty is what is intended, then since it is not necessarily preceded by doubt, the question of one who is in doubt would be appropriate — to this he says: 'it is ascertained.' And thus, since critical inquiry (<s>vicāra</s>) and examination (<s>parīkṣā</s>) are necessarily preceded by doubt, subsequently

children.text:
saṃdigdhasya praśno yukta iti bhāvaḥ /
saṃdehakāraṇatvana vipratipattimāha--keciditi /
pramāṇaṃ hi karaṇaviśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: For <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is a particular kind of instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).

children.text: karaṇaṃ ca sādhakatamam /
children.translated_text: And an instrument is the most effective means.

children.text: na ca sādhyasiddhau tajjātīyasya sādhakatamatvamasti, chinne vṛkṣe paraśoriva /
children.translated_text: And when the object to be accomplished is already accomplished, there is no 'most effective means' of the same kind — like an axe when the tree is already cut.

children.text: tasmād yathaivācchinnaviṣayatayā vyāpriyamāṇaḥ paraśuḥ chedanaṃ tathā pramite viṣaye vyāpriyamāṇamindriyādikaṃ pramāṇamiti momāṃsakāḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as an axe, operating with respect to an uncut object, is the cutter, so too the sense-organ and the like, operating with respect to an object not yet validly cognized, constitute the <s>pramāṇa</s> — so say the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>.
the question of one who is in doubt is appropriate — this is the purport. He states the disagreement as the cause of doubt: 'some say.'

children.text:
matāntaramāha--viṣayasārūpyamiti /
phalaṃ tāvat pramāṇasyārthapratītireva pramārūpatvāt /
na hi pramāṇasyārthe pramātiriktamapi kiñcit kartavyamasti /
prāptirapi pravṛttireva /
pravṛttirapi pravṛttiyogyārthopalambhanameva /
tasmāt pramāṇasyārthapramītyatiriktaṃ na /
kiñcit phalamiti, yadāha--tadeva pratyakṣajñānaṃ pramāṇaphalamarthapratītirūpatvāditi /
pramāṇamapi tadeva yadarthaṃ vyavasthāpayati /
arthamapi tadeva vyavasthāpayati yadarthapratītiṃ tadīyatayā niyamayati /
children.translated_text: He states the alternative view: 'correspondence with the object.' The result, to begin with, of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is none other than the cognition of the object, since it has the nature of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>). For the <s>pramāṇa</s> has nothing whatsoever to accomplish with respect to the object beyond valid cognition of it. Even 'attainment' is merely activity. And activity is merely the apprehension of an object fit for activity. Therefore, the <s>pramāṇa</s> has no result apart from valid cognition of the object. As it is said: 'That very perceptual cognition is the result of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, because it has the nature of apprehension of the object.' And the <s>pramāṇa</s> too is that very thing which determines the object. And it determines that very object which constrains the apprehension of the object as belonging to it.

children.text:
tathātvenāniyatāyāṃ tu tasyāṃ na kasyacit sā pratītiḥ /
sarvasya veti nārthena niyatā pratītiḥ syāt /
aniyatārthapratītijanakaṃ ca kathaṃ pramāṇa nāma? na cendriyādibhirjñānakaraṇairjñānaṃ tadīyatā niyamyate /
na hi cakṣuṣā janitatvādeva nīlasya nīlavijñānam, pītajñānasyāpi tathātprasaṅgāt /
api tu nīlākāratvādeva nīlajñānaṃ nīlasya /
children.translated_text: But when the cognition is not invariably related to the object as such, no one has that cognition [as valid]. If it were related to every object, then the cognition would not be invariably related to any particular object. And how can something that generates cognition of an indeterminate object be called a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)? Nor is the cognition's belonging to a particular object determined by the sense-organs and other instruments of knowledge. For a cognition of blue is not a cognition of blue merely because it is produced by the eye, since there would follow the absurd consequence that cognition of yellow too would be a cognition of blue. Rather, the cognition of blue is a cognition of blue precisely because it has the form of blue.

children.text:
tasmādarthākāra evabuddhigato buddhiṃ tadīyatā vyavasthāpannarthamapi tathā vyavasthāpayati /
tataścārthavyavasthāpanahetutvāt sa eva pramāṇaṃ yadāha--arthasārūpyamasya pramāṇam, tadvaśenārthapratītisiddheriti /
arthapratītisiddheḥ arthapratītivyavasthiteḥ, tathā cārthavyavasthiteriti yāvat /
na cābhinnātmani karaṇaphalabhāvo virudhyate, tatra kāraṇabhavasyaiva virodhāt /
sa hi vyāpāravyāpāribhāvo vā, gamyagamakabhāvo vā svīkriyate eva /
vṛkṣādibhiḥ saṃyujyamāna eva hi paraśuḥ saṃyogena vyāpāreṇa karaṇamiti vyavahniyate loke /
na ca saṃyogo nāma vigrahavānanyaḥ saṃyujyamānāt paraśorasti /
children.translated_text: And conjunction is not some embodied entity distinct from the axe that is being conjoined.

children.text: gamyagamakabhāvo 'pi svaprakāśe vijñāne bāhye ca vṛkṣe śiśapayā gamyamāne dṛṣṭa eva /
children.translated_text: The relation of indicated and indicator too is seen in self-luminous cognition and in an external tree, where 'tree' is indicated by 'rosewood.'

children.text: na hi śiṃśapātaḥ kaścidanyo vṛkṣo nā vṛkṣād vā śiṃśāpā /
children.translated_text: For rosewood is not something other than a tree, nor is a tree something other than rosewood.

children.text: vaikalpike tu vyavahāre yathātra vyāvṛttibhedastathā ākāratadvatorapīti na kaścid viśeṣa iti sautrāntikāḥ //
children.translated_text: But in conceptual usage, just as there is a difference of exclusions here, so too between the form and that which possesses the form — thus there is no real distinction — so say the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>.

Therefore, it is the form of the object present in the cognition that, by establishing the cognition as belonging to that object, also establishes the object accordingly. And since it is the cause of the determination of the object, that very form is the <s>pramāṇa</s> — as he says: 'The conformity to the object is its <s>pramāṇa</s>, since the cognition of the object is established by virtue of that.' 'Establishment of the cognition of the object' means 'the determination of the cognition of the object,' and thus 'the determination of the object' — this is the meaning. And there is no contradiction in the instrument-result relationship within an undivided entity, since it is only causation that would be contradicted there. For this relationship is accepted either as the relation of operation and operator, or as the relation of what is indicated and what indicates. For the axe, even as it is being conjoined with the tree and other things, is designated in common usage as an instrument through the operation of conjunction.

children.text:
matāntaramāha--vijñānasyaiveti /
arthaprakāśane hi yasya vyāpārastadeva pramāṇam /
prakāśanaṃ ca caitanyarūpaṃ tasyaiva yaścetayate /
na cendriyādīni karaṇānyapi tathā, jaḍarūpatvāt /
na hi jñānāniriktaḥ kaściccetano nāma /
children.translated_text: For there is no conscious entity whatsoever apart from cognition.

children.text: tasmād vijñānameva cetanatayā darśanavyāpāram /
children.translated_text: Therefore cognition alone, by virtue of being conscious, has the operation of seeing.

children.text: tathā ca pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: And as such it is the <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: vyāpāravyāpāriṇoścābheda evaṃ saṃyujyamānaparaśuvaditi nirākāravādino vaibhāṣikādayaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the identity of the operation and the operator is just like the axe that is being conjoined — so hold the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> and others who maintain the formless view of cognition.

He states another view: 'Of cognition itself...' For that which has the operation of illuminating the object is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. And illumination, being of the nature of consciousness, belongs to that which is conscious. And sense-organs and other instruments are not like that, being of an insentient nature.

children.text:
matāntaramāha--upalabdhīti /
vṛddhāḥ pramāṇavṛddhāḥ /
etena pūrveṣāṃ bālatvaṃ sūcayati /
bhāvapraśnavyākhyānena bhavitṛpraśno vyākhyāta iti tu sahetyaśyāhṛtya kecid vyācakṣate /
kecit tu bhāvapraśnavyākhyā boddhavyā anena bhavitṛpraśno vyākhyāta iti /
anye tu bhavāpraśnavyākhyānena hetunā bhavitṛpraśno vyākhyāto bhāvapraśnaṃ vyākhyātuṃ bhavitṛpraśno vyākhyātaḥ, tadantareṇa tadanupapatteriti /
lipipramādo 'yamiti saṃpradāyavidaḥ /
vyabhicāro visaṃvādaḥ /
anarthavattvaṃ viparītarthatvam /
ato na sādhyāviśiṣṭatā /
nanu sthāṇurvā puruṣo vetyatropadarśitayorantaraḥ prāpyata eva, tat kathaṃ visaṃvādakatvam? kathaṃ cārthavattvamitya āha--no khalviti /
yato na prāpyate, ata eva nārthakriyāsūpayujyate,
children.translated_text: He states another view: 'Apprehension...' '<s>Vṛddhas</s>' means those mature in the science of <s>pramāṇa</s>. By this he implies the immaturity of the previous thinkers. Some explain: 'By the explanation of the question of existence, the question of the agent is explained' — combining it with 'together with.' Others say: 'From the explanation of the question of existence, the question of the agent is to be understood as explained.' Still others: 'By the explanation of the question of existence as the reason, the question of the agent is explained — the question of the agent is explained in order to explain the question of existence, since without the former the latter is untenable.' Those learned in the tradition say: 'This is a scribal error.' 'Deviation' means discordance. 'Meaninglessness' means having a contrary meaning. Therefore there is no fault of being indistinguishable from what is to be proved. Now, in the case 'Is it a post or a person?', one of the two alternatives presented is indeed reached — so how can there be discordance? And how can there be meaningfulness? To this he says: 'Not indeed...' Since it is not reached, for that very reason it is not useful in purposive action.

children.text:
aprāpteranupayogācca nāstītyarthaḥ /
yadyapyanubhāvābhiprāyeṇopalabdhau vyākhyāyamānāyāṃ smṛtihetau nāsti prasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because it is not reached and because it is of no use — this is the meaning. Although, when apprehension is explained with the intention of experience, there is no such consequence with respect to the cause of memory,

children.text: smṛterananubhavatvāt, tathāpi--
children.translated_text: since memory is not experience — nevertheless,

children.text: buddhirūpalabdhirjñānamityanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text: cognition, apprehension, and knowledge are synonymous.

children.text:
iti sūtrayopalabdhiśabdo jñānaparyāyaḥ svīkṛtaḥ /
asti ca smṛterapi jñānatvamityanenābhiprāyeṇoktam--na hyasāviti /
atītārthe paramparayā tatkāryatayāpi śabdaliṅgāderarthasambandho 'sti, anāgate tu so 'pi nāstītyata āśaḍkitaṃ jñāpakatayeti /
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>sūtra</s>, the word 'apprehension' is accepted as a synonym of knowledge. And even memory has the nature of knowledge — with this intention it was said: 'For that is not...' There is a connection of the object with words, inferential marks, and so forth, even with regard to past objects, indirectly, by virtue of being their effects. But with regard to future objects, even that connection does not exist — hence the apprehension raised is: as an indicator.

children.text: saṃskārasyāpīti /
children.translated_text: Of the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) too.

children.text: tasyāpi taramparayā arthakāryatvamarthajñāpakatvaṃ ca sākṣāt samānamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even that, indirectly, has the nature of being an effect of the object and of being an indicator of the object, equally as directly — this is the meaning.

children.text: smṛtirūpopalabdhihetoḥ smṛtirūpajñānahetorityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of the cause that is in the form of memory' means 'of the cause of knowledge that is in the form of memory' — this is the meaning.

children.text: pariharati--naivamiti //
children.translated_text: He refutes: 'Not so...'

children.text:
nanu na smṛti /
prametyatraiva vivāda ityata āha--loketi /
anena pramāśabdapravṛttinimittgrāhakaṃ pramāṇamapalakṣayati /
tathā hi, na tāvad asya smṛtitvameva pravṛttinamittam, anubhavasyāpramātvaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi tadekārthamasavetaṃ jñānatvādikaṃ tannimittam, yena smṛtirapi pramā syāt, viparyayasyāpi tathātvaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi pramātvaṃ nāma sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ samasti jñānagatasya sāmānyaviśeṣasya manomātragrāhyatvāt /
pramātvasya cānumeyatayā prāgeva pratipāditatvāt /
kiṃ ca yadi pramātvaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ syāt, tadā tadabhāvavati tadviruddhasāmānyavati vā viparyayajñāne na samaveyāt /
tathā ca viparyayajñānaṃ dharmiṇyapi na pramāṇaṃ syāt /
evaṃ ca tat nirālambanamāpadyeta /
sāmānyaṃ ca sāmānyāntareṇa saha parāparabhāvena ekasyāṃ vyaktau samāviśet /
tatrānubhatvaṃ vā paraṃ pramātvaṃ vā? ādye smṛti kathaṃ pramā? dvitīye tvanubhavaḥ pramātvaṃ na vyabhicaret /
tathā ca viparyāyo 'pi dattajalāñjaliḥ syāt /
sākṣātkāritve ca yadi paraṃ tadā asākṣātkāravatyo 'numitiprabhṛtayo na pramāḥ syuḥ /
athāparam, viparyayabuddhirna sākṣātkāravatī syāt apramātvāditi /
tasmāt na pramāṇatvaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ /
yathārthatvamāyātamiti cet--na, smarāmītyatrāpi pramiṇomīti buddhivyapadeśaprasaṅgāt /
iṣṭa evāyamiti cet--na, riśvaretarecchāmātreṇa laukikaprayogāprayogayorniyantumaśakyatvāt /
tenaivāyaṃ pramāṇaśabdo yathārthajñānamātre niyataḥ kṛta iti cet--na,
children.translated_text: Now, memory is not valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) — the dispute is only about that — to this he says: 'Common usage...' By this he indicates the <s>pramāṇa</s> that apprehends the ground of application of the word <s>pramā</s>. For, to begin with, the ground of application is not merely its being memory, since there would follow the absurd consequence that experience too would not be valid cognition. Nor is the ground some property like 'being knowledge' that is co-extensive with memory but not unique to it, for then memory too would be valid cognition, and there would follow the absurd consequence that error too would be valid cognition. Nor does there exist a universal-particular called 'being valid cognition' (<s>pramātva</s>), since any universal-particular residing in cognition is apprehended by the mind alone, and being valid cognition has already been established as something to be inferred. Moreover, if being valid cognition were a universal-particular, then it would not inhere in erroneous cognition, which lacks it and possesses a contrary universal. And thus erroneous cognition, even in its property-bearer, would not be a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And thus it would become objectless. And the universal would enter into a single particular together with another universal in a higher-lower relation. Would the higher be 'being experience' or 'being valid cognition'? In the first case, how would memory be valid cognition? In the second case, experience would never deviate from being valid cognition — and thus error too would be conceded. If direct apprehension (<s>sākṣātkāritva</s>) is the higher, then inferences and the like, which lack direct apprehension, would not be valid cognitions. If it is the lower, then erroneous cognition would not possess direct apprehension because of being invalid — this would follow. Therefore, being valid cognition is not a universal-particular. If one says 'It amounts to being true to its object' — no, because even in 'I remember,' the designation 'I validly cognize' would follow. If one says 'That is accepted' — no, because ordinary usage and its absence cannot be regulated by mere wish. If one says 'The word <s>pramāṇa</s> is restricted to merely veridical cognition by convention' — no,

children.text: maharṣibhistadabhiyuktaiḥ smṛtiphalasya pramāṇatvenāparisaṃkhyāt /
children.translated_text: because the great sages, who are authoritative on the matter, have not excluded the result of memory from being a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: ukteṣvantarbhāvādaparisaṃkhyānamiti cet--na, pratyakṣasyāsākṣātkāriphalatvānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: If one says 'There is no exclusion because it is subsumed under the stated [types]' — no, because perception cannot have a result that is not direct apprehension.

children.text: liṅgaśabdādeśca sattāmātreṇa pratītyasādhanatvāditi //
children.translated_text: And because inference, verbal testimony, and the rest, merely by their existence, are not sufficient to establish cognition as valid.

children.text:
kiṃ ca smṛteryāthārthyamapi kṛtaḥ? na hi yādṛśor'thaḥ smaryate yadā tādṛśa evāsau tadā, pūrvāvasthāyā vartamāne nivṛttatvāt /
anavṛttau hi pūrvataiva na syāt /
na ca nivṛttapūrvāvasthatayaiva tamarthaṃ smṛtirālambate, pūrvāvasthānivṛtterananubhūtatvāt /
ananubhūte cārthe ananubhūtaṃ saṃskārābhāvāt /
nanu samānaviṣayatvepi smṛtyanubhavayoranubhavo yathārtho, na tṛ smṛtiriti kṛta etat? anubhavakāle tasyārthasya tādavasthyat, smṛtikāle tvatādavasthyāt /
nanu pūrvaṃ tāvattadavastha evāsāvāsīt, etāvataiva jñānamastu yathārtham /
na, pramārakte 'pi śyāmatāpratyasya yathārthatvaprasaṅgāt /
nanvatītaḥ śyāma iti pratyayaḥ tatra yathārtha eva /
satyam, tadviṣayasya tadānīmeva tadavasthatvāt /
na tu smaryamāṇārthaḥ tadānī tadavasthaḥ /
tasmāt smṛtirayathārthaiva /
yathānubhava tu bhavet /
tatrānubhavasya yathārthatvāt tadekaviṣayā smṛtirapi yathorthetyucyate /
ata evānubhavasyāyathārthatve smṛtiḥ avapirītāpyayathārthaiva /
yathā rajjuṃ bhujaṅgatayā anubhūya vidrutasya tathaiva smṛtiḥ /
tasmāt smṛteryāthārthyaṃ yācitakamaṇḍanaprāyam, nājānikam /
idameva pāratantryapadavācyaṃ kaiścinniruktikuṇṭhairanyathāpaplūta iti /
tasmādubhayathāpi smṛteranyasyānubhavatvaikaniyataṃ yathārthatvameva pramāpadasya pravṛttinimittaṃ loko 'vadhāritavān /
kathamanyathā tatraiva pramāśabdaṃ prayuḍkte nānyatreti yadyapi, tathāpi dharmiṇyapi smṛteḥ pramāṇyaṃ mābhūdityāśayavān prāguktayuktikaṃ lokaprayogamavāśritavān /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, how would the word <s>pramā</s> be applied only there and not elsewhere? — although this is so, nevertheless, intending that memory too should not be valid even in the property-bearer, he has relied upon the common usage supported by the aforementioned reasoning.

children.text: tadidamuktam--lokaśceti /
children.translated_text: This is what has been stated: 'And common usage...'

children.text: evaṃ tāvadyathārtho 'nubhavaḥ pramā /
children.translated_text: Thus far, then: veridical experience is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>).

children.text: tatsādhanaṃ ca pramāṇamiti svalakṣaṇamāśaḍkitātivyāptinirākaraṇenāduṣṭamiti samāhitam //
children.translated_text: And the means of that is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) — its definition is established as faultless through the refutation of the suspected over-extension.

Moreover, is the veridicality of memory even established? For the object as it is remembered — it is not exactly like that at the time of remembering, since the earlier state has ceased to exist at the present time. For if it had not ceased, it would not have been earlier. And memory does not take as its object the object as one whose prior state has ceased, since the cessation of the prior state was not experienced. And regarding an unexperienced object, there is no latent impression, since it was not experienced. Now, even if memory and experience share the same object, is it not settled that experience is veridical but memory is not — since at the time of experience the object is in that state, but at the time of memory it is not in that state? Now, at the earlier time it was indeed in that state — is not the cognition veridical by just that much? No, because there would follow the absurd consequence that a cognition of 'dark' would be veridical even regarding something tinged with red. Now, the cognition 'it was dark in the past' is indeed veridical there. True, because the object of that cognition was indeed in that state at that time.
