But the object as being remembered is not in that state at that time. Therefore memory is indeed non-veridical. But it may be veridical to the extent of conforming to experience. There, since the experience is veridical, memory too, having the same object, is called veridical. For this very reason, when the experience is non-veridical, even non-erroneous memory is non-veridical — just as the memory of one who, having experienced a rope as a snake, ran away. Therefore, the veridicality of memory is like borrowed ornament, not inherent. This very dependence is what some, unskillful in etymology, have distorted into something else. Therefore, in either case, common usage has determined that veridicality, which is uniquely restricted to experience as distinct from memory, is the ground of application of the word <s>pramā</s>.

children.text:
na caitanmīmāṃsakasyāpyanabhimatam /
na hi tenāpyatrāvyāptyativyāptī prasaṃjayituṃ śakyete /
na hyasti saṃbhavo mīmāṃsakasyāpi yathārthānubhavo na ca prameti /
tallakṣaṇe tvasmākaṃ kuto vipratipattirityata āha--anadhigatārthagantṛtvaṃ ceti /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
nityapadārtheṣu anadhigatatvaṃ nāma nāstyeva /
yadi neha janmani janmāntare 'pyadhigamāt /
yadi na pratyakṣeṇānumānopadeśābhyāmapi anityeṣvapi prāyaśaḥ upalabdhānāmevopalambhācca /
anyathā ca pratyabhijñānaṃ dattajalāñjali syāt /
tataśca svarūpato 'pyanadhigatatvaṃ bahvākulayet /
prakārato 'pi bhūyo
children.translated_text: Nor is this unacceptable even to the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>. For even he cannot adduce under-extension or over-extension here. For there is no possibility that even the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> could have a case where veridical experience is not valid cognition. But what is our disagreement regarding the definition? To this he says: 'And the property of apprehending a previously unapprehended object...' And this is merely illustrative. For with regard to eternal entities, there is simply no such thing as being previously unapprehended — if not in this life, then from apprehension in a previous life. If not through perception, then through inference and testimony as well. And even with regard to non-eternal things, mostly what is apprehended is what has already been apprehended. And otherwise, recognition would be conceded [as not being valid cognition]. Therefore, the condition of being unapprehended even in its essential nature would cause much difficulty. Even with respect to mode of presentation, repeatedly

children.text: bhūyastaṃmādiṣvanubhūyamāneṣu na kaścid guṇaprakāraḥ pratikṣaṇalabdhajanmāpavargaḥ paribhāvyate /
karmakṛto 'pyāśutaravināśī
children.translated_text: Even what is produced by action and perishes more quickly

children.text: na pratikṣaṇamapūrvaḥ /
children.translated_text: is not unprecedented at each moment.

children.text: na ca catuḥpañcakṣaṇāvasthāyinyapi tasminnekamevajñānaṃ janayitvendriyādikamudāsīnam anāgatakarmādijanma pratīkṣate /
children.translated_text: And even when an object persists for four or five moments, the sense-organ and other instruments, having generated just one cognition, do not remain idle awaiting the birth of a future action and so forth.

children.text: tataśca sarvajanmāntaropalambhādanye taduttarakālapratyayā dhārayā vicchedena vā bhavanto na pramāṇaṃ syurityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, since there has been apprehension in all previous births, other cognitions at subsequent times, whether in a stream or with interruption, would not be <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the meaning.
when things like darkness are experienced again and again, no qualitative mode is found that has its birth and end at each moment.

children.text:
śaṅkate--naceti /
yadyapi svarūpasya prakārasya vā tathāvidhasya tādavasthyam, tathāpi pratyakṣajñānadhārāyāṃ vartamāna evārthaḥ parisphurati /
na ca kramabhāvināmeka eva vartamānaḥ kālo viṣayaḥ, nānāpramātṛvajjñānayaugapadyaprasaṅgāt /
pratyabhijñānānupapattiśca, jñānānekatve 'pi ekakālāvasthānākalanāt /
tasmāt pūrvapūrvajñānairanākalita eva vartamānor'tha uttarottarairavasīyata ityanadhigatārthatvameva tatrāpītyarthaḥ /
pariharati--parameti /
na tāvat pratikṣaṇavartamānatvaṃ saugatavad vastunaḥ eva svarūpotpādaḥ /
nāpi saṃkhyavad vasturūpasthairye 'pi pariṇatibheda eva mīmāṃsakaiḥ svīkriyate /
nāpi dharmabheda eva kaścit
children.translated_text: He raises an objection: 'Not...' Although the essential nature or the mode is in that state, nevertheless, it is the present object alone that fully manifests in the stream of perceptual cognition. And the objects of successive cognitions do not have one and the same present moment as their object, for there would follow the absurd consequence that cognitions would be simultaneous, as with multiple perceivers. And recognition would be untenable, because even when cognitions are many, there is no ascertainment of abiding in one time. Therefore, the present object, unascertained by each preceding cognition, is determined by each succeeding one — thus even there the condition of apprehending what was previously unapprehended obtains — this is the meaning. He refutes: 'The ultimate...' To begin with, being present at each moment is not, as the Buddhists hold, the very origination of the entity. Nor do the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> accept, as the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> do, that even when the essential nature of the entity remains stable, only the difference of transformation constitutes presentness. Nor is there any distinct property

children.text: pratikṣaṇāpūrvo vartamānatvāparanāmā samasti /
na ca tairabhyupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor has this been accepted by them.

children.text: na ca kālaḥ pratyakṣagocaraḥ, nāpi bhinnasvabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: And time is not an object of direct perception, nor is it of a differentiated nature.

children.text: tasmāt kālakalābhedakā upādhaya eva kālabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the limiting conditions that differentiate portions of time are themselves the difference of time.

children.text: tatpratkṣameva kālabhedapratyakṣamiti paramārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the direct perception of those limiting conditions is itself the direct perception of temporal difference — this is the ultimate truth.
that is unprecedented at each moment and goes by the name 'presentness.'

children.text:
tatra na tāvat pratīyamānastaṃmādisaṃsṛṣṭā upādhayaḥ saṃbhavantītyuktam /
jñātatāyāśca nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt, dhāravahanabuddhiṣu tadabhāsānācca /
pratīyamānetarasaṃsṛṣṭāstūpādhayaḥ tajjñānasaṃsargiṇo vā syuranyathā vā? na tāvat stambhādiṣu taditarasaṃsargiṇaḥ kṣaṇabhaḍgurāḥ kecanāvaśyaṃ tajjñānasaṃsargabhājo bhavanti /
kvacid bhavantyapīti cet, tatraiva taddhiyāṃ pramāṇatā syāt /
yatra tu tadekajñānasaṃsargiṇa upādhayo na santi tatra dhārāvāhikabuddhīnāmapramāṇatvameva syāt /
tathāvidhā eva ca vicāraviṣayatvenābhipretā jñānāntaragocarā viṣayāntarasaṃsargiṇa upādhayo bhaviṣyantīti cet--evaṃ tarhi dhārāvahanabuddhayo na syureva iti lābhāya gato mūlamapi hāritavāt /
na khalu pramāṇāntareṇa indriyāntareṇa tenaiva vā taddharmiparityāgāddharmyantare anubhūyamāne vivakṣitaikaviṣayabuddhidhārasaṃbhavaḥ /
iṣṭa evāyamarthaṃ iti cet--na, apūrvāpūrvopādhyupanipātaniyame pramāṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: If [you say] this is exactly what is desired — no, because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means) for the rule that ever-new conditions must present themselves.

children.text: anupanipātināṃ ca jñānāntareṇāṣyanākalanāt /
children.translated_text: And because those [conditions] that do not present themselves cannot be ascertained even by another cognition.

children.text: ata eva ghaṭo 'yaṃ ghaṭo 'yamiti buddhisahasrasyāpi na viṣayakṛtaṃ viśeṣamūpalabhāmahe /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, even in a thousand cognitions 'this is a pot, this is a pot,' we do not apprehend any object-produced distinction.

children.text: anupalabhyamānasya tu viṣayatvakalpanāyāṃ sarvasarvajñatāpattiriti //
children.translated_text: And if one were to posit objecthood for what is not apprehended, the consequence would be omniscience of everything by everything.

Therein, it has been said that conditions (<s>upādhis</s>) associated with the apprehended pillar and the like are not possible. And because <s>jñātatā</s> (knownness) is about to be refuted, and because in stream-cognitions (<s>dhārāvāhika-buddhis</s>) there is no appearance of it. But conditions associated with apprehended other [objects] — would they be connected with that cognition, or otherwise? Not, to begin with, [are there] any momentary [entities] connected with that other [thing] in pillars and the like that necessarily partake of connection with that cognition. If [you say] they do exist somewhere — then validity would belong to those cognitions only there. But where there are no conditions connected with one and the same cognition, there the stream-cognitions would simply be invalid. If [you say] that conditions of just such a kind, as being objects of another cognition and connected with other objects, will be the subject of examination — then stream-cognitions would simply not exist, and having gone to gain, one would have lost even the root. For indeed, when something is being experienced in another substrate — through another means of knowledge, through another sense-organ, or through that very [sense-organ] — by abandoning the original property-bearer in a different property-bearer, there is no possibility of a stream of cognitions of one intended object.

children.text:
tasmāt stambhādireva prāgabhāvanivṛttipradhvaṃsābhāvānutpattirūpo vartamānaḥ /
tadavacchinnaḥ kālo 'pi vartamānaḥ /
saca tathāvidho 'nekajñānasādhāraṇa eva /
na caitāvatā jñānayaugapadyāpattiḥ, sūkṣmakālāpekṣayā kramasaṃbhavāt /
na ca sūkṣmopādhīnāmapratītiścedato 'saṃbhava eva, kāryakrameṇaivonnīyamānatvāt /
nāpi pratyabhijñānānupapattiḥ /
pūrvajñānaviṣayānusaṃdhānameva hi pratyabhijñānam /
children.translated_text: For recognition is nothing but the connecting-recollection (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) of the object of the prior cognition.

children.text: tacca jñānakramādevopapannam /
children.translated_text: And that is established precisely through the sequence of cognitions.

children.text: tasmāt kālatadupādhipratyakṣatve 'pi na sarvatra sūkṣmopādhisaṃsargaḥ, nāpi tatpratītiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when time and its conditions are perceptible, there is not everywhere contact with subtle conditions, nor is there apprehension of them.

children.text: tadidamuktam--paramasūkṣmāṇāmiti //
children.translated_text: This is what has been stated — 'of the supremely subtle' and so forth.

Therefore, the very pillar and the like — existing in the present as [having] the form of cessation of prior non-existence and of destruction-absence — [is the present object]. The time delimited by that is also present. And such [time] is common to multiple cognitions. Nor does this entail the consequence of simultaneity of cognitions, because sequence is possible with respect to subtle time. And if [you say] that the non-apprehension of subtle conditions [makes this] simply impossible — [we reply:] because they are inferred precisely through the sequence of effects. Nor is there any impossibility of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>).

children.text:
etenaitannirastam--siddhe sādhakatamatvābhāvāditi /
na hi sādhakatamasya tathātvaṃ sādhākatamāntarāpekṣayā, kiṃ tu pradhānakriyākārakāntarāpekṣayā /
anyathā yatra karaṇānāṃ samuccayastatra parasparāpekṣayā anatiśayitatvādakaraṇatvāpatteḥ karaṇānāṃ samuccayaḥ kvacidapi na syāt /
itarakārakāpekṣayā tu dhārāvāhikabuddhiṣvapi pramāṇasyātiśayitvamastyeva /
yattu chinne kuṭhārasyākāraṇatvamiti, tacchidā lakṣaṇaphalābhāvāt /
na ca chinne chidāntarābhāvavān /
na ca jñāte 'pi jñānāntarāsaṃbhavo yenātrāpyaphalatvādevākaraṇatvaṃ bhavet, dhārāvāhikajñānotpatteḥ /
tasmād yo 'nādhigatārthabodhanaṃ pramāṇamicchati, tasya dhārāvāhikabuddhayo 'pramāḥ prasajyerannityarthaḥ /
śaṅkate--na ceti /
pravṛttiṃ prāptiṃ ca janayadeva vijñānaṃ pramā, tadarthameva pramāṇānusaraṇāt /
ādyaṃ ca tathā /
tatastadeva pramā /
dvitīyādīnāṃ ca na pravṛttiprāptihetutvam /
ato naitāni pramārūpāṇi /
tatastajjanakānyapi na pramāṇānīti tadetadiṣyata evetyarthaḥ /
pariharati--nahīti /
na hyapravartayadeva vijñānamarthaṃ prāpayati /
nāpi haṭhādeva pravartayati /
kiṃ tvarthopadṛṣṭirūpatayā /
children.translated_text: But rather, by virtue of being a presentation (<s>upadṛṣṭi</s>) of the object.

children.text: sā ca sarvasamānetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [presentation] is equal in all [cognitions] — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadidamuktam--pradarśanaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: This is what has been stated — 'and the showing (<s>pradarśana</s>)...'

children.text: nanu tathāpi prathamādevāpekṣitasiddhaḥ puruṣasya kiṃ dvitīyādinetyata āha--puruṣeti //
children.translated_text: But even so, since the first [cognition] alone has already accomplished what is desired by the person, what [use] is the second and so forth? — to this he says: 'the person (<s>puruṣa</s>)...'

By this, the [objection] that 'because there is no superior efficacy when [the means] is already established' has been refuted. For the superior efficacy of the most efficacious [instrument] is not so designated with reference to another most efficacious [instrument], but rather with reference to the other <s>kārakas</s> (case-roles) of the principal action. Otherwise, where there is a collection of instruments, since each would be non-surpassing with reference to the others, and thus would incur the consequence of non-instrumentality, the collection of instruments would never exist anywhere. But with reference to the other <s>kārakas</s>, the surpassing nature of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means) exists even in stream-cognitions. As for [the objection] that an axe is not the cause of what is [already] cut — that is because the result characterized by cutting is absent [in what is already cut]. But it is not the case that in what is [already] cut, further cutting is absent. Nor is it the case that in what is [already] known, another cognition is impossible — whereby, here too, there would be non-instrumentality due to fruitlessness alone — since stream-cognitions do arise. Therefore, the meaning is: for one who holds that <s>pramāṇa</s> is the communication of a previously unattained object, stream-cognitions would turn out to be non-valid. He raises an objection — 'nor...' A cognition is valid (<s>pramā</s>) only insofar as it generates activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and attainment (<s>prāpti</s>), since the pursuit of <s>pramāṇa</s> is for that purpose alone. And the first [cognition] is indeed so. Therefore, that alone is valid. And the second and subsequent [cognitions] are not causes of activity and attainment. Hence, these do not have the form of valid cognition. Therefore, their generators too are not <s>pramāṇas</s> — the meaning is: this is exactly what is accepted. He resolves — 'not indeed...' For a cognition does not bring about the attainment of an object without generating activity. Nor does it generate activity by sheer force.

children.text:
syādetat /
vādivipratipattayo vārttikakṛtā na nirākṛtā /
nāpi viśeṣavidhānasya śeṣapratiṣedhaviṣayavāditi nyāyo nāvirodhāt /
na hyanadhigatārthagantari sārūpyevārthavyavasthāpayitari śaktau vā
children.translated_text: It may be [objected] thus: the objections of the opponent have not been refuted by the author of the <s>Vārttika</s>. Nor is the principle 'the prescription of a specific [item] entails the prohibition of the remainder' a topic of the [opponent's] position — since there is no contradiction. For in the case of one who comprehends a previously uncomprehended object, or in the case of the capacity to establish the object through similarity,

children.text: ātmānātmaprakāśayitryāmupalabdhihetutvaṃ virudhayate ityata āha--upalabdhīti /
children.translated_text: the status of being the cause of apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>) for [cognition] which illuminates both <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>anātman</s> (non-self) is not contradicted — to this he says: '<s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension)...'

children.text:
vyāpakasyāvyāpakaviruddhatvādanadhigatārthagantustena rūpeṇa pramāṇatvamevārthānniṣiddhamityarthaḥ /
sārūpyaśaktī nirākaroti--hetviti /
tadīyatayā hyarthapritītiṃ vyavasthāpayannākāraḥ pramāṇamiti kor'thaḥ? na tāvat tadīyatayā niyatāṃ pratītaṃ janayan, svātmani kriyāvirodhāt /
nāpi jñāpayan, svātmīmūtapratītiṃ prati jñānāntarājanakatvāt /
nāpi niścāyayan, ākāratadvatorekatvena vyāvṛttyoścaikaniścayagocaratvena niśceyaniścāyakatvaniyamānupapatteḥ /
nīlamahaṃ jānamīti hyakāraniścayaḥ /
na cāto 'paraḥ tadīyatāniścayo nāma /
nīlamidamityākāravyavasāyaḥ prarthamam, atha nīlamahaṃ jānāmītyarthakarmakapratītyanuvyavasāya iti cet--tat kiṃ buddhāvaniścitāyāmevākāro niścitaḥ? na caitat saṃbhavati, sāmānyāniścaye viśeṣāniścayāt /
niśrvīyata eva, paraṃ na tadīyatayeti cet--atha keyamarthākārādanyā tadīyatā nāma? tadudbhāvatvamiti cet--nanvevamanumitiṃ bhāvāyannākāraḥ pramāṇam /
omiti cet--hanta, hataṃ tarhi pāmarapratyakṣamatiriktamarthamanumāpayatā ākāreṇa vyavasthāpitatvāt /
api ca yā kriyā yatkaraṇaphalatvena vivakṣitā, janayadeva tāṃ tatkaraṇamiti lokasiddham /
na hi chidāmajanayanto 'pi cakṣurādayastanniścāyakatāmātreṇa chedanatayā vayavahniyante /
api tu aniścāyayanto 'pi janayanta eva kuṭhārādayaḥ /
tadatrāpi pramāṃ janayadevāniścāyakamapi pramāṇamiti vyavahniyatām /
na tu tāmajanayanniścāyako 'pyākāraḥ, evaṃ ca loke 'nukūlatā /
children.translated_text: Since the pervader is contradicted by [what is contradicted by] the contradictory of the pervaded, <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood in that form — i.e., as comprehending what was not previously comprehended — is itself precluded as a matter of fact — this is the meaning. He refutes similarity and capacity — 'cause (<s>hetu</s>)...' What is the meaning of [saying] that the <s>ākāra</s> (form/image) is a <s>pramāṇa</s> by establishing the cognition of the object through its belonging to that [object]? Not, to begin with, [does it mean] producing a cognition apprehended as necessarily belonging to that — because of the contradiction of action upon oneself. Nor [does it mean] making known — because it does not generate another cognition with respect to the cognition that is its own nature. Nor [does it mean] ascertaining — because, since the <s>ākāra</s> and its possessor are identical, and since both exclusions are objects of a single ascertainment, the rule that the ascertainable and the ascertainer [must be distinct] would be violated. For 'I know blue' is the ascertainment of the <s>ākāra</s>. And there is no other ascertainment of 'belonging to that' beyond this. If [you say:] first comes the determination 'this is blue' as the determination of the <s>ākāra</s>, then comes the re-determination 'I know blue' as a cognition having the object as its <s>karman</s> — then what, is the <s>ākāra</s> ascertained while the cognition is not yet ascertained? But this is not possible, since without ascertainment of the universal, there is no ascertainment of the particular. If [you say] it is indeed ascertained, but not as 'belonging to that' — then what is this 'belonging to that' other than the object-form? If [you say] it means 'being produced by that' — well then, the <s>ākāra</s>, while bringing about an inference, is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. If [you say] 'yes' — alas! Then ordinary perception is destroyed, since it would be established by the <s>ākāra</s> which causes inference of an object beyond [perception]. Moreover, whatever action is intended as that whose result is [produced by] a given instrument — it is established in the world that that instrument [acts] only by producing that [result]. For the eyes and the like, even though they do not produce cutting, are not designated as 'cutters' merely by ascertaining cutting. Rather, the axe and the like, even without ascertaining, are [so designated] simply by producing [cutting]. So here too, let that which produces valid cognition, even without ascertaining, be called <s>pramāṇa</s>. But not the <s>ākāra</s> which, while ascertaining, does not produce that [valid cognition]. And thus there would be conformity with worldly [usage].

children.text: anyathā tu piribhāṣāṃ kurvatā loko 'pratipāditaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, one who makes a stipulation would have left the world unexplained.

children.text: na ca janyajanakayostādātmyagandho 'pīti //
children.translated_text: And between the produced and the producer, there is not even a trace of identity.

children.text:
etena śaktiḥ pramāṇamiti pratyuktam, śakteḥ śakayaniṣṭhatvāt /
śakayaṃ ca kāryamucyate /
prakāśanaṃ cātmabhūtatvāt na tasyāḥ kāryamiti /
tadidamuktam--hetuhetumadbhāvasyeti /
nanu yadi pramāṇa siddham, kiṃ tatra pramātrādinā kartavyam? na hi siddhena siddhameva sādhyate /
na cānyatra caritārthasyānyatra kārakatvamasti /
athāsiddham, kathaṃ pramāṇam? na hyasiddhaṃ kārakaṃ nāma /
nāpyakārakaṃ karaṇam /
nāpyakaraṇaṃ pramāṇamityata āha--ayamartha iti /
karaṇībhūtasya paraśoḥ saṃyogasya vyāpārībhūrasyeti śeṣaḥ /
pariṇativiśeṣaḥ sahakārisamavadhānam /
karaṇaṃ vyāpāryotpādya
children.translated_text: By this, [the view that] capacity (<s>śakti</s>) is the <s>pramāṇa</s> is also answered, since capacity resides in that which is capable. And what is capable is called the effect. And illumination (<s>prakāśana</s>), being of the nature of the self [of cognition], is not its effect. This is what has been stated — 'of the relation of cause and effect (<s>hetu-hetumat-bhāva</s>)...' Now, if the <s>pramāṇa</s> is [already] established, what is to be done therein by the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) and the rest? For what is established is not established again by the already established. Nor does an instrument that has accomplished its purpose in one [context] have instrumentality in another. But if it is not established, how can it be a <s>pramāṇa</s>? For what is not established is not a <s>kāraka</s> (causal factor). Nor is a non-<s>kāraka</s> an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). Nor is a non-instrument a <s>pramāṇa</s> — to this he says: 'this is the meaning...' Of the axe that has become the instrument, of the contact that has become the operation — this is the complement. The specific transformation is the convergence of auxiliary [causes]. The instrument, having operated and produced,

children.text: vā phalārthaṃ kartavyāntarābhāvāt kartuścaritārthatā /
children.translated_text: or, because there is nothing further to be done for the sake of the result, the agent has accomplished its purpose.

children.text: karaṇasya tu phalena vinā aparyavasānamacaritārthatetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But the instrument, without the result, remains unaccomplished — that is, it has not fulfilled its purpose — this is the meaning.

children.text:
atha prameyasya kathaṃ pramāṇe caritārthatvam? na hi pramātṛvat tenāpi pramākaraṇamutpādyate vyāpāryate vetyata āha--prameyasya tviti /
ayamāśayaḥ /
sarvatra hi karmakārakakaraṇaphalatadvyāpārayorviṣayatayā vyavatiṣṭhate /
tatra phalaviṣayatvamasya na karmatvaṃ prati prayojakam, asattvenākārakasyāpi phalaviṣayatvāt, yadāha---kevalamityādi /
karaṇavyāpāraviṣayatvāt tu karmatvam, na hyasti saṃbhavaḥ karma ca, na ca karaṇavyāpāraviṣaya iti /
tatra karaṇasya vyāpāraviṣayatvābhāvāt vyāpāra eva na nirvahediti tannirvāha evāsya caritārthatvamiti /
tadidamuktam--tatrāpīndriyasaṃbandhamātra iti /
na ca karaṇamapi kartṛvyāpāraviṣayastāvanmātreṇaiva caritārthamadhikavyāpāravattvāt /
nāpi karmavyāpāraviṣayaḥ karaṇam /
nāpi phalaviṣayaḥ, taduddeśena karmaṇaḥ kartrā avyāpāritatvāt /
phalasya tannirūpaṇādhīnanirūpaṇatvāt, yena karmavadasya caritārthatvaṃ kalpyeta /
children.translated_text: Because the determination of the result depends on the determination of that [<s>karman</s>], whereby its accomplishment of purpose would be posited like that of the <s>karman</s>.

children.text: tasmāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore,

children.text: kartṛkarmaṇoścaritārthatve 'pyacaritārthameva karaṇamiti /
children.translated_text: even when the agent and <s>karman</s> have accomplished their purpose, the instrument alone remains unaccomplished.

children.text: samavāyitvaviṣayatvakṛtāṃ saṃnipatyopakārakabhrānti prayogāmyāṃ nirākaroti--tat siddhametaditi //
children.translated_text: He refutes the error — which arises from the inherence-substratum relation — of [thinking that there is] a 'convergent auxiliary' (<s>saṃnipatya-upakāraka</s>) [relationship] by [the text]: 'thus this is established...'

Now, how does the object of valid cognition (<s>prameya</s>) have its purpose accomplished in the <s>pramāṇa</s>? For it is not the case that, like the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), the <s>prameya</s> also produces or operates upon the instrument of valid cognition — to this he says: 'of the <s>prameya</s>, however...' The purport is as follows. Everywhere, the <s>karman</s> (object) <s>kāraka</s> stands as the locus of the result of the instrument's operation. Therein, being the locus of the result is not what makes it a <s>karman</s>, since even a non-<s>kāraka</s>, being non-existent, can be the locus of the result — as he says: 'merely...' and so forth. But <s>karman</s>-hood is due to being the locus of the instrument's operation; for it is not possible that something be a <s>karman</s> and yet not be the locus of the instrument's operation. Therein, because the instrument is not the locus of its own operation, the operation itself would not be accomplished — therefore, the accomplishment of [the operation] is itself the accomplishment of [the <s>karman</s>'s] purpose. This is what has been stated — 'therein, the mere contact with the sense-organ...' But the instrument too is the locus of the agent's operation, yet it is not accomplished by that alone, because it possesses additional operation. Nor is the <s>karman</s> the locus of the operation of the instrument. Nor is it the locus of the result, because the <s>karman</s> has not been operated upon by the agent for the sake of that [result].

children.text:
yadyapyanumeyādyatītādyahetureva, tathāpi sāmānyaniṣedho viśeṣaprakāramapyāśrayetetyetāvataiva dṛṣṭāntatvam /
tasmāt
children.translated_text: Although [the example] is not itself a reason [proving the point about] the inferable and the past and so forth, nevertheless, since a general negation encompasses even the specific mode, this much suffices for it to serve as an illustration. Therefore,

children.text:
tadeva phalahetuḥ /
saṃnipatyeti śeṣaḥ /
kathañciditi /
anāhatya ityarthaḥ /
tadanena kārakāntare 'caritārthasya hetutvameva karaṇatvamiti karaṇalakṣaṇaṃ darśayatā kartṛvyāpāragocaraḥ karaṇamityapi karaṇalakṣaṇaṃ sūcitam /
tathaiva ṭīkākṛtā vyākhyātam /
etacca yadvāniti vārttike sphuṭībhaviṣyati /
akaraṇā pramāṇotpattiḥ prasajyeta kartuḥ karaṇe caritārthatvāditi kiṃ kena saṃgatamityata āha--nākaraṇa iti /
vastusaddhipradhānakriyāsaṃbandhanibandhanaprabhṛtayaḥ kārakaśabdā ityāśayavataḥ codyaṃ yadītyādinā buddhisiddhapradhānakriyāsaṃbandhanibandhanapravṛttayaḥ kārakaśabdā ityāśayavataḥ samādhānam--na pācakaśabdādivadityādinā iti ṭīkāyāṃ vikṣiptasya vārttikatātparyasya saṃkṣepaḥ /
tulyavaditi tulayā saṃmitamiva na nyūnaṃ nātiriktaṃ vetyarthaḥ /
tadanena prapajcena pramāṃ pramātṛprameyayorakāraṇatvameva darśitamati bhramo mā bhūdityupasaṃhāravyājenāha--tatpramāṇamiti /
satyapi copalabdhisādhanatve sākṣāditi śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: that alone is the cause of the result. 'Convergently' — this is the complement. 'In some way' — meaning: without striking. By this, [the author], showing that the definition of instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is 'instrumentality is being the cause [of the result] when [the instrument] has not accomplished its purpose in another <s>kāraka</s>,' also indicates the definition of instrument as 'the instrument is the locus of the agent's operation.' The <s>Ṭīkā</s>-author has explained it in just that way. And this will become clear in the <s>Vārttika</s> [passage beginning] 'or alternatively...' [The objection] 'the production of a <s>pramāṇa</s> without an instrument would follow, since the agent has accomplished its purpose in the instrument' — what is connected with what here? — to this he says: 'not without an instrument...' The summary of the <s>Vārttika</s>'s purport, which is scattered in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, is: for one whose view is that <s>kāraka</s>-terms are grounded in the connection with the principal action [determined by] the establishment of the real entity, the objection is [raised] with 'if...' and so forth; for one whose view is that <s>kāraka</s>-terms are grounded in the connection with the principal action [determined by] establishment in cognition, the resolution is 'not like the word "<s>pācaka</s>" (cook)...' and so forth. 'Like a balance' — meaning: as if measured by a balance, neither less nor more — this is the meaning. By this elaboration, lest there be the error that valid cognition has been shown to be a non-cause of the knower and the knowable, he says by way of a concluding statement: 'that <s>pramāṇa</s>...' Even though it is the means of apprehension, 'directly' is the complement.

children.text: saṃpratyayo jhaṭitisphuṭapratyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃpratyaya</s> means an instantaneously clear cognition.

children.text: atra hetuḥ---sātiśayatveti //
children.translated_text: The reason for this is — 'because of surpassing [efficacy]...'

children.text:
sādhakatamārtha pṛcchatīti--na tāvat sādhakānāṃ phalakṛtāvatiśayānatiśayau, tasyaikasya sarvān pratyaviśeṣāt /
nāpi vyāpārakṛtau, parasparavyāpāravilakṣaṇavyāpāravattāmātrasya sarvasādhāraṇyāt /
phalānuguṇatvaṃ tu vyāpārasyāviśiṣṭamevetyāśayavāniti hṛdayaśeṣaḥ /
yadyapyayogavyavaccheda evātiśayaḥ, tathāpi tulyatve satyapyatiśayānatiśayau tasyaiva cintyete /
na tu vaidharmyamātramatiśaya ityabhisaṃdhāyānyayogavyavacchedo 'pi darśitaḥ ayogānyayogavyavacchedābhyāmiti /
amuṃ cārthamanantarameva vibhāvayiṣyati /
nanu yathā kartrādau sati phalaṃ nāvaśyakam, tathā karaṇe 'pi sati kadācinna bhavet, kārakatvāviśeṣāt /
dṛśyate ca /
na hi paraśau sati chidā bhavetyevetyata āha--pramātṛprameye hīti /
upakṣīṇavṛttinī iti vyāpāravataḥ kārakatvamabhipraiti /
tena paraśurapi vyāpāravāneva san karaṇam /
tathābhūtena ca phalasyāyogavyavaccheda eva, na tu vyāpāravatāpi kartrādinā, tadvyāpāreṇa karaṇavyāpārasya saṃpādanavilambanāt /
children.translated_text: And with respect to [the instrument] in such a state, there is exclusion of non-connection with the result — but not with the agent and the like even when they possess an operation, because the operation of the instrument is delayed in its accomplishment by the operation of those [other factors].

children.text: vyāpāravatastu karaṇasya nānyat saṃpādanīyamastītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for an instrument that possesses [its] operation, there is nothing else remaining to be accomplished — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadidamuktam--pramāṇavyāpāre sati tu bhavatyeveti /
children.translated_text: This is what is stated: 'When the operation of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is present, [the result] necessarily occurs.'

children.text: tadanena vyāpāravataḥ phalāvyabhicāritvaṃ sādhakatamatvamiti darśitam //
children.translated_text: By this, it has been shown that the non-deviation of the result from what possesses [its] operation is what constitutes being most efficacious.

He asks about what is most efficacious: 'Not, first of all, is there a distinction or non-distinction among the efficacious [causes] with respect to the production of the result, since for that single [result] there is no difference with respect to all [of them]. Nor [is there a distinction] with respect to the operation, since the mere possession of an operation distinct from the operations of the other [causes] is common to all. But the conformity of the operation to the result is itself undifferentiated' — such is his intention; the completion is 'in his heart.' Although the distinction is just the exclusion of other connections (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>), nevertheless, when there is equality, the distinction and non-distinction are considered with respect to that [most efficacious cause] itself. But intending that mere dissimilarity is not the [relevant] distinction, the exclusion of other connections too is shown: 'ayogānyayogavyavacchedābhyām' (by the exclusion of non-connection and other connections). And he will elaborate this very meaning immediately after. Now, just as when the agent and the like are present, the result is not inevitable, so too when the instrument is present it may sometimes not occur, since there is no difference in being a causal factor. And this is seen [in experience]. For it is not the case that when an axe is present, cutting necessarily occurs — therefore he says: 'pramātṛprameye hī' (for the knower and the knowable). 'Upakṣīṇavṛttinī' intends that being a causal factor belongs to what possesses an operation. Therefore the axe too is an instrument only when it possesses an operation.

children.text:
kalpāntaram--yadvāniti /
paratantreṇeti /
paravyāpāryeṇāśrīyate apekṣata ityarthaḥ /
etadeva pūrvamuktamiti smārayati--kartradhīnaṃ ceti /
yadyapi kartṛvyāpāryatvaṃ karaṇatvamiti na vyabhicaratyeva, tathāpi paramparāvyāpāryeṇāpi karmaṇā vyabhiyāro mā bhūdityāśaḍkya prakṛte 'vadhāraṇaṃ saṃbhavaprācuryāt kṛtam /
āgāmivārttikasya kalpāntaratvaṃ nivārayati--asyaiveti /
kalpāntaramiti /
pūrvakalpavivaraṇena paunarūktyabhiyā kalpāntaraṃ gṛhītaṃ kathañcit
children.translated_text: An alternative interpretation: 'yadvā' (or). 'Paratantreṇa' means: that which is operated upon by another — it depends [on another], this is the meaning. He reminds that this very thing was stated earlier: 'kartradhīnaṃ ca' (and dependent on the agent). Although the definition that instrumentality is being operated upon by the agent does not deviate [from the facts], nevertheless, lest there be deviation even with respect to the object (<s>karman</s>) which is operated upon in a mediate chain, the restriction in the present context is made on account of the preponderance of possibility. He prevents the forthcoming <s>Vārttika</s> from being [treated as] a mere alternative interpretation: 'asyaiva' (of this very one). 'An alternative interpretation' — he somehow justifies the adoption of an alternative interpretation out of fear of redundancy with the explanation of the former interpretation:

children.text:
samarthayati--pūrveṇeti /
karmaṇaḥ svātantryamasaṃbhavi, tato viśeṣaniṣedho 'nupapanna ityata āha--akatṛtvamiti /
kalpāntaram--saṃyogavaditi /
atrāpi kārakāntarebhyaḥ caramavyāpāraṃ karaṇamiti lakṣaṇam /
kalpāntaram--pratipatteriti /
atrāpyanantaraṃ phalaṃ karaṇamiti lakṣaṇam, vikalpasamuccayābhāvāt--co 'vadhāraṇe /
asmin pakṣe sa etātiśaya ityarthaḥ /
kalpāntaram--asādhāraṇeti /
sarvakaraṇeṣvasādhāraṇatvopapādanānupayogāt prakṛte pramāṇe ghaṭayati--catatra iti /
atrāpi pramāvivakṣitajātibhedavyapadeśakaṃ pramāṇamiti lakṣaṇam /
pramāṃ prati kāraṇānā sādhāraṇatvāsādhāraṇatve nirūpyamāṇe puruṣaviṣayasya sādhāraṇyasya kimāyātamityata āha--aśeṣa iti /
kalpāntaram--pramākāraṇeti /
atrāpi
children.translated_text: 'pūrveṇa' (by the former). The independence of the object is impossible; hence the specific negation [of its instrumentality] is untenable — therefore he says: 'akatṛtvam' (the state of not being an agent). An alternative interpretation: 'saṃyogavad' (like conjunction). Here too, the definition is: the instrument is that which has the ultimate operation among the other causal factors. An alternative interpretation: 'pratipatte' (of cognition). Here too, the definition is: the instrument is that which is proximate to the result — the absence of alternation and aggregation [in the definitions shows that] 'ca' is used in the sense of restriction. In this view, 'sa eva atiśayaḥ' (that very thing is the distinction) — this is the meaning. An alternative interpretation: 'asādhāraṇa' (uncommon). Since the demonstration of uncommonness among all instruments is not useful, he applies it to the present context of <s>pramāṇa</s>: 'ca atra' (and here). Here too, the definition is: <s>pramāṇa</s> is that which designates the intended class-distinction of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>). When the commonness and uncommonness of causes with respect to <s>pramā</s> are being determined, what does the commonness of the person-object [contribute]? — therefore he says: 'aśeṣa' (without remainder). An alternative interpretation: 'pramākāraṇa' (cause of valid cognition). Here too,

children.text: vivakṣitapramājātibhedaupayikatvena pramityasamavāyikāraṇaviśeṣakaṃ pramāṇamiti lakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: the definition is: <s>pramāṇa</s> is that which is the distinguishing feature of the non-inherent cause of valid cognition (<s>pramiti</s>), by way of its suitability for the intended class-distinction of <s>pramā</s>.

children.text: svarūpāt kāryātaḥ karturarvāk prāk kartṛkāryayoḥ /
children.translated_text: From intrinsic nature, from the effect, prior to the agent, prior to both agent and effect,

children.text: pramājāteḥ pramāhetuviśeṣānmānalakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: from the class of <s>pramā</s>, from the distinguishing feature of the cause of <s>pramā</s> — [these are] the definitions of <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the summary verse.

children.text:
tadebhirnimittaiḥ karaṇavyavahāre vyavasthāpyamāne yadi karmādivyavahāranimittasamāveśāt tadvyavahāro 'pi bhavati, bhavatu tasyeṣyamāṇatvāt /
ebhirnimittaistu karmādivyavahāro neṣyate /
sa tu nāstyeva /
tathā hi--sarvatra karmavyavahāraḥ karaṇavyāpāraviṣayatvādibhiḥ, karaṇavyavahāraśca kartṛvyāpāraviṣayatvādibhiḥ /
teṣāṃ ca nimittānāṃ bheda eveti nātiprasaṃgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, when the conventional usage of 'instrument' is being established by these criteria — if, due to the inclusion of the criteria for the conventional usage of 'object' and the like, that usage too obtains, let it, since it is [already] accepted. But by these criteria, the conventional usage of 'object' and the like is not intended. And that [confusion] simply does not [arise]. For everywhere, the usage of 'object' [is governed] by being the object of the instrument's operation and the like, and the usage of 'instrument' [is governed] by being the object of the agent's operation and the like. And these criteria are indeed different — hence there is no over-extension.

children.text:
tātparyato vyācaṣṭe--vākye 'sphuṭatvādityarthaḥ /
evaṃ ca satyagre arthyata iti vyutpattirapi tātparyaparatayaiveti manatavyam /
kasmāt punariti /
na hi pramāṇaviṣayasya pramāṇasyārthavattvamavyutpādanīyameveti śaḍkābījam /
tātparyāntaramiti /
kathañcid bhāgāsiddhatāparihārasya phalasyaikatvāt /
tat kiṃ pravṛttisāmarthyābhāvādapramāṇameva tadityata āha--na ceti /
kathaṃ tarhi tatprāmāṇyamavaseyamityata āha--tsyāpīti /
children.translated_text: How then is its validity to be ascertained? — therefore he says: 'tasyāpī' (of that too).

children.text: na tāvat sarvo viṣayaḥ sarvatra sarvasya sarvadopakṣaṇīyaḥ, nirmāṇavaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Not every object, in every context, of everything, is at all times to be examined — for there would follow the uselessness of all production.

children.text: tathā cānupekṣaṇīyatādaśāyāṃ pravṛttisāmarthyena tadviṣayasya jñānasya prāmāṇyamavadhārya gṛhītena tajjātīyatvenopekṣaṇīyatādaśāyamapi prāmāṇyaṃ sugrahameva /
children.translated_text: And thus, in the stage where [the object] is not to be examined, having ascertained the validity of the cognition pertaining to that object through the capacity to motivate activity, [one can] easily [ascertain] validity even in the stage where it is to be examined, through [its] being grasped as of the same class.

children.text: yatrāpyāhatya pravṛttirna bhūtā tatrāpyasaṃbhavadvādhasaṃvāditvaṃ prātyakṣikamānumānikamaupadeśikaṃ vā tajjātīyatvamavaseyamityakṣarārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even where activity in conjunction [with the object] has not occurred, the non-contradicted character of that which cannot be sublated — whether perceptual, inferential, or testimonial — is to be ascertained as being of the same class. This is the literal meaning.

He explains the purport: 'vākye 'sphuṭatvāt' — the meaning is 'because of the lack of clarity in the sentence.' And this being so, the etymology 'that which is sought first (<s>agre arthyate</s>)' should also be understood as having the purport [as its primary reference]. 'Kasmāt punaḥ' (from what again?) — for the grounds of doubt are that the meaningfulness of a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose object is the <s>pramāṇa</s> [itself] is not something that needs to be taught. 'Tātparyāntaram' (another purport) — because the removal of partial non-establishment has a single result [regardless]. Then is it simply not a <s>pramāṇa</s> due to the absence of the capacity to motivate activity? — therefore he says: 'na ca' (and not).

children.text:
śaḍkānivartane manda ityata āha--ayamabhisandhiriti /
sākṣāt janakatvaṃ gṛhītvā vyadhikāraṇatvaśaḍkā mā bhūdityavaśyaṃ darśanīyam /
tacca pramāṇasya pratītijanakatvakathanamantareṇāśakyamityarthaḥ /
kathamayamartho vārttikāllabhyate ityata āha--pramāṇasya viśeṣa iti /
etāvatāpi kimuktamityata āha--etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
nanu tavāyamāśayo na tu vārttikakṛta ityata āha--tadidamuktamiti /
tadidamaparam anarthasūtram /
na hi pratipattipravṛttisāmarthyayoḥ
children.translated_text: When one is slow to dispel the doubt — therefore he says: 'ayamabhisandhiḥ' (this is the intention). Having grasped [it as] a direct generator, the doubt of having a different locus must necessarily be dispelled. And that cannot be done without stating the capacity of the <s>pramāṇa</s> to generate cognition — this is the meaning. How is this meaning obtained from the <s>Vārttika</s>? — therefore he says: 'pramāṇasya viśeṣa' (the distinguishing feature of the pramāṇa). What is said by even this much? — therefore he says: 'etaduktaṃ bhavati' (this is what is said). Now, this is your intention, not that of the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> — therefore he says: 'tadidamuktam' (this is what is stated). This is yet another purposeless <s>sūtra</s>. For between the capacity to generate cognition and the capacity to motivate activity, there is no

children.text:
pratipādyapratipādakabhāva ityata āha--ayamartha iti /
nanu arthagrahaṇena sarvasaṃgraho 'yukta eva kimityāśaḍkyate?
children.translated_text: relation of thing-to-be-expressed and its expresser — therefore he says: 'ayamarthaḥ' (this is the meaning). Now, why would one doubt that the word 'artha' (object/meaning) encompasses everything?

children.text:
tathāvidhaśaḍkāyāmanavasthānādityata āha--ekadeśīti /
vyāghāta iti /
yadyapyapavargasya sukhaduḥkhataddhetubhāvo nāsti, ata eva tathātvenāryamāṇatayārthapadena sarvasaṃgraho 'pyaśakyaḥ, tathāpi tadabhyupagame vyāghāta eva sphuṭa iti sa evoktaḥ /
sa ca śāstrāvatāreṇa yadi hyapavargaḥ sukhaduḥkhataddhetutayā heyaḥ svīkṛtaḥ, tarhi śāstramapi viparītaprayojanatvādanārambhaṇīyam /
śāstrapramāṇayostu sāmānyato yadyapi duḥkhahetutvam, tathāpi vivakṣitaparamapuruṣārthaviṣayayostaddhetutayā duḥkhahetutāṃ paribhūyopādeyatvameva /
anyathā punarapi sa eva vyāghātaḥ /
itaraddheyaṃ tāvat pramāṇena hīyate /
children.translated_text: The other [side of the argument]: what is to be avoided is indeed diminished by the <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: pramāṇaṃ tu pramāṇāntareṇa heyaṃ sadanavasthāṃ sāvakāśayati /
children.translated_text: But the <s>pramāṇa</s>, being itself to be avoided through another <s>pramāṇa</s>, gives rise to an infinite regress.

children.text: tataśca saiva pramāṇavyaktiḥ tenaiva pramāṇena hātavyā /
children.translated_text: And then that very instance of <s>pramāṇa</s> must be avoided by that very <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: taccāśakyam //
children.translated_text: And that is impossible.

Because in the case of such a doubt there would be no stable [position] — therefore he says: 'ekadeśī' (the partial objector). 'Vyāghāta' (contradiction) — although <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) does not have the nature of pleasure, suffering, or their causes, and for that very reason, since it is not cognized as such, the word 'artha' cannot encompass everything either, nevertheless, upon accepting it [as such], the contradiction is itself evident — hence that alone is stated. And that [contradiction is] through the introduction of the <s>śāstra</s>: if <s>apavarga</s> is accepted as to-be-avoided because it has the nature of pleasure, suffering, or their cause, then the <s>śāstra</s> too, having a contrary purpose, should not be undertaken. But although <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>śāstra</s> are in general causes of suffering, nevertheless, with respect to the intended supreme human goal, their to-be-adopted nature overrides their suffering-causing nature, precisely because they are causes of that [goal]. Otherwise, the very same contradiction [returns].

children.text:
nanvaśakyatvenāheyatve sukhataddhetutvenopādeyetvamapi kathamityata āha--na cāsmāditi /
tasmādubhayathāpi svātmani kriyāvirodhena paramapuruṣārthahetutvena ca pramāṇaṃ na śakayahānam /
na caive satyahānirevāsya syāt, svocchedakakāraṇavaśenopādeyasya puruṣaprayatnenāśakyahānasyāpi sukhavaducchedādityarthaḥ /
adhikārādanuvṛtte rityanupapannam, ādivākyatvādityata āha--pravṛttisāmarthyeti /
adhikāro yogyatā /
sā cātra prakṛtatvāt pravṛtti pratītyarthaḥ /
iha hi prakaraṇe samarthapravṛttijanakatvaṃ heturabhipretaḥ /
sa ca sukhaduḥkhataddheturūpārthaviṣayāyā eva pratipatterasti /
tator'thaśabdena viṣayo 'bhidhīyamānaḥ tathāvidha eva vaktavyo 'taḥ prakaraṇaviśeṣaniyama evādhikāra itayarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the object being denoted by the word 'artha,' being described as precisely of that kind, must be stated — hence '<s>adhikāra</s>' means the restriction [imposed by] the particular context. This is the meaning.

children.text: ekadeśyupālambhe pūrvahetubhiḥ saha hetvantarasya samuccayaṃ darśayannāha--na kevalamiti /
children.translated_text: Showing the aggregation of a further reason with the previous reasons in the criticism of the partial objector, he says: 'na kevalam' (not only).

children.text: aśakyatvādapiṃ saṃvidi hetvorasiddheriti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Also because of impossibility — the completion being: 'because the reason is unestablished with respect to consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>).'

children.text: nanu asaṃvedyamānāyāḥ saṃvidaḥ pramāṇasadbhāve kathamasaṃvedyatvam, tadabhāve vā kathaṃ sattvavyavahāra ityata āha--na tāvaditi //
children.translated_text: Now, if consciousness is not experienced, how can it be unexperienceable when the <s>pramāṇa</s> for it exists? Or if [the pramāṇa] does not exist, how is the conventional usage of its existence [maintained]? — therefore he says: 'na tāvad' (not first).

Now, if it cannot be avoided because of [its] unavoidability, how can it also be to-be-adopted because it is a cause of pleasure? — therefore he says: 'na cāsmāt' (and not from this). Therefore, in both ways — by the impossibility of self-directed action and by being the cause of the supreme human goal — the <s>pramāṇa</s> cannot be avoided. Nor, this being so, would there be no cessation of it at all; for even what is to be adopted and cannot be abandoned by human effort, like pleasure, ceases through the force of a cause that destroys it — this is the meaning. [The objection that the sūtra] is carried over from [another] section is untenable, since it is an introductory statement — therefore he says: 'pravṛttisāmarthya' (the capacity to motivate activity). '<s>Adhikāra</s>' means fitness. And here, because of being the present context, it means the purpose of [motivating] activity and cognition. For in this section, the intended reason is the capacity to generate effective activity. And that belongs only to cognition whose object has the form of pleasure, suffering, or their causes.

children.text:
anavasthāprasaṅgalakṣaṇaṃ tarkaṃ darśayatā tadviparyaye mānasameva pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇamādarśitaṃ bhavati /
ajñātoparatajñānavyavahāre
children.translated_text: By showing the <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) characterized by the consequence of infinite regress, a mental perception alone has been indicated as the <s>pramāṇa</s> for the contrary [position]. In the case of a cessation of the convention of cognition whose [object] is unknown,

children.text:
tu kālāntare tadviṣayaṃ smaraṇameva nimittam /
evaṃ ca sāmānyākāreṇa jijñāsānurodhāt jajjñānamastyeva, ajñātasya vidhiniṣedhavyavahārāviṣayatvāt, tataśca sāmānyākāreṇa siddhamādāya vicāraṇā /
yadi jñānaviṣayaṃ jñānamavaśyaṃ jñāyeta, avaśyaṃ vā vijñāsyeta tadā jñānaparamparālakṣaṇā anasthā syāt /
sā
children.translated_text: it is merely the recollection pertaining to that object at a later time that is the cause. And thus, since there is necessarily [some] cognition in the general form, in conformity with the desire to know — for what is unknown cannot be the object of the practice of injunction and prohibition — therefore, taking what is established in the general form, investigation [proceeds]. If cognition having cognition as its object were necessarily cognized, or necessarily to be investigated, then there would be the infinite regress characterized by a chain of cognitions. And that

children.text: cānupalambhavādhitetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: is contradicted by non-apprehension — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadidamuktam--kasyāściditi /
children.translated_text: This is what is stated: 'kasyāścid' (of some).

children.text: bhāṣyagrantheneti vadatā na kevalamarthavirodhaḥ granthavirodhaścetyapi pratipāditaṃ draṣṭavyam //
children.translated_text: By saying 'bhāṣyagrantheṇa' (by the text of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>), it should be seen that not only the contradiction of meaning but also the contradiction of the text has been demonstrated.

children.text:
catuṣṭayasyomayatvavirodhaṃ pariharannāha--kāryakāraṇābhyāmiti /
nanvarthaśabdasya prayojanavattave 'pi virodhavyadhikaraṇatve tadavasthe evetyata āha--candanādīti /
parisaṃkhyātuṃ niyantumiti vadatā gaṇanīyartho 'nabhyupagamena parihṛtaḥ /
atha kimabhipretyāprastutameva bhāṣyakṛto idaṃ prastūyata ityata āha--evaṃ kileti /
na pramāṇaprayojanaṃ bhavitumarhantīti pramāṇasya bhūtārthatvādita bhāvaḥ /
tathā ca pramāṇadīnāṃ śakyājñānatve 'pi tadvyutpādakaṃ śāstramanārambhaṇīyameva, paramārthikaprayojanavirahāditi nigarvaḥ /
tatredamupatiṣṭhate nirākaraṇabhāṣyamiti śeṣaḥ /
sarvasādhāraṇanīlādivaidharmyeṇa hi kālpanikatvaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasya vyutpādayatā nīlādi paramārthikameva svīkartavyam /
children.translated_text: Resolving the contradiction of the fourfold group being of one nature, he says: 'kāryakāraṇābhyām' (by effect and cause). Now, even if the word 'artha' has the sense of 'purposeful,' there is no contradiction with having a different locus — [the matter] remains the same — therefore he says: 'candanādī' (sandalwood, etc.). By saying 'parisaṃkhyātum niyantum' (to enumerate, to restrict), the sense of 'what is to be counted' is resolved by not accepting [it]. Then, with what intention does the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> introduce this irrelevant matter? — therefore he says: 'evaṃ kila' (thus indeed). The meaning is: <s>pramāṇas</s> cannot be a purpose — because the <s>pramāṇa</s> deals with real things. And thus, even if <s>pramāṇas</s> and the like can be known, the <s>śāstra</s> that teaches them should not be undertaken at all, since it lacks ultimate purpose — this is the purport. And here this refuting <s>bhāṣya</s> presents itself — the completion. For by demonstrating the constructedness of <s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s> (causation) through the dissimilarity from universally common [things like] blue and the like, one who would teach [this] must accept blue and the like as absolutely real.

children.text:
tadapāramārthikatve tvabhimatasiddhireva na syāt /
na ca kāryakāraṇabhāvasyāpāramārthikatve nīlādi pāramārthikaṃ bhavitumarhati, nityatvaprasaṅgāt /
tasmād yo nīlādi paramārthikamicchati, tena kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pi paramārthika eva eṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who wishes blue and the like to be absolutely real must also accept <s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s> as absolutely real.

children.text: na cobhayamapi /
children.translated_text: Nor can both [be denied].

children.text: tathā ca tatrāpi tulyametat /
children.translated_text: And thus the same [argument] applies there too.

children.text: idaṃ tvavaśiṣyate--kathamekamanekaṃ parasparaviruddhaṃ kāryaṃ kuryāt? tatsvabhāvatvāditi yadi tadotpatterārabhya kuryādaviśeṣat tatrāha--nivedayiṣyate hīti //
children.translated_text: But this remains [to be addressed]: how can one [thing] produce many mutually contradictory effects? If [one says] 'because it is of that nature,' then from the moment of its arising it should produce [all effects] without distinction — to this he says: 'nivedayiṣyate hī' (for it will be explained).

If that [blue, etc.] is not absolutely real, then even the intended thesis would not be established. Nor can blue and the like be absolutely real when <s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s> (causation) is not absolutely real, because there would follow [their] permanence.

children.text:
na jātyā janmaprabhṛtisahakārinirapekṣatayetyarthaḥ /
jātideśeti /
svabhāvaniyāmikā jātiḥ /
avyavasthayeti sahakārivyavasthāvaicitryeṇetyarthaḥ /
pramāṇārthaḥ sukhaduḥkhalakṣaṇaḥ /
aniyataḥ candanāt sukhameva kaṇṭakād duḥkhameveti niyamarahitaḥ, aniyata hetukatvāt /
aniyatacandanādisahakārikāraṇakatvādityarthaḥ /
prāṇabhṛditi sahakārivaicitryasūcanāya /
ata evodāharaṇam--aniyatakālamiti /
yathā aniyatakāletyupalakṣaṇam, deśovasthāsahakāriṇāmapi aniyamo draṣṭavyaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, yathā keṣucit kāladeśāvasthāsahakāriṣu satsu meghāḥ salilamudvamanti, keṣucit tu satsu ta eva salilaṃ pibanti, tathā candanādayo 'pi keṣucit satsu sukhamupajanayanti keṣucicca duḥkhamiti /
viṣṭiḥ daṇḍākṛṣṭaḥ karmakaraḥ /
nanvarthavati ca pramāṇe pramātrādīnyarthavanti bhavanti jñāyanta
children.translated_text: The meaning is: not by <s>jāti</s> (class-nature), in the sense of not requiring auxiliary causes from birth onwards. 'By class and place' — <s>jāti</s> here is what determines the intrinsic nature. 'By irregularity' — the meaning is: by the diversity of the arrangement of auxiliary causes. 'The object of <s>pramāṇa</s>' — characterized by pleasure and pain — 'is indeterminate' — devoid of the restriction that from sandalwood there is only pleasure and from a thorn only pain — because of having indeterminate causes. The meaning is: because of having causes whose auxiliary [conditions] such as sandalwood and the like are indeterminate. '<s>Prāṇabhṛt</s>' (living being) is [mentioned] to indicate the diversity of auxiliary causes. For that very reason, the illustration: 'at indeterminate times' — 'just as at indeterminate times' is illustrative; the indeterminacy of place, condition, and auxiliary causes should also be understood. What is being said is this: just as clouds, when certain temporal, spatial, conditional, and auxiliary factors are present, pour forth water, yet when certain [other] such factors are present, those very [clouds] absorb water — so too sandalwood and the like, when certain [factors] are present, produce pleasure, and when certain [others are present], produce pain. '<s>Viṣṭi</s>' (forced labor) is a laborer compelled by authority. Now, what is intended is that when the <s>pramāṇa</s> is meaningful, then the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) and the like become meaningful — they are known,

children.text:
ityabhipretam, na tu jāyanta iti /
na caivamasti, pramityavyabhicāreṇaivetareṣāmavyabhicārāvadhāṇādityata āha--yadpīti /
children.translated_text: not that they are produced. And this is not the case, since the non-deviation of the others is ascertained through the non-deviation of valid cognition (<s>pramiti</s>) alone — therefore he says: 'Even though...'

children.text: na ca vācyam, vaidikī pratipattirarthāvyabhicāriṇī āptopadeśajapratipettitvāditi śakayata eveti /
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that Vedic cognition is non-deviating from objects because it is cognition arising from the instruction of an authoritative person — [for] this can indeed be [stated].

children.text: na hyāptopadeśo 'vyabhicāriṇīmevārthadhiyamādhatta ityanavadhārya śakyamidam /
children.translated_text: But without ascertaining that the instruction of an authoritative person produces only non-deviating cognition of objects, this [argument] is not possible.

children.text: na cāvyabhicāripratipattijanakatvādanyadeva pramāṇānāmarthavattvamityuktameveti /
children.translated_text: And it has already been said that the meaningfulness of <s>pramāṇas</s> is not something different from the fact that they produce non-deviating cognition.

children.text: tathāpi loke tāvadevamastīti cet? ata āha--adṛṣṭārtheti //
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'but in ordinary life at least it is so' — therefore he says: 'Of unseen purpose...'

children.text:
yadyapi tatsamavāyaḥ pramāsamavāyaḥ pramātṛtvamiti prakṛtopayogi syādeva, tathāpi vārttikakṛtā praśnopalakṣaṇābhyāṃ khātantryamupakrāntam--sāmānyanyāyena viśeṣo 'pi labhyata ityabhisandhāyātastathaivavyācaṣṭai--kārakāmidhāneneti /
prādhānyena dhātupratyayābhidhīyamānavyāpārasaṃbandha eva tatsamavāyaḥ /
prādhānyaṃ ca kārakāntarāttairaścīnyamātramabhipretam /
tena pacatītyādau sarvatrātiraścīnapākādivyāpāravato devadattādereva kartṛtvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati /
pācayatītyādau tu prayojyavyāpārapratītāvapi tasyānyatiraścīnatvāt na tadvataḥ kartṛtvam /
kiṃ nāma? prayojakasyaiva, tadvyāpārasyātiraścīnatvāt /
evaṃ tarhi,
children.translated_text: Although the inherence in that [<s>pramāṇa</s>], [i.e.,] the inherence in <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), which constitutes the knower-hood (<s>pramātṛtva</s>), would indeed be useful for the topic at hand — nevertheless, the <s>Vārttika</s>-author has introduced the full treatment through the question and its illustration — with the intention that 'the particular is also obtained through the general principle.' Therefore he explains it in just that way: 'By the designation of <s>kāraka</s> (factor of action).' The inherence in that [<s>pramāṇa</s>] is primarily nothing but the connection with the activity denoted by the verbal root and suffix. And what is meant by 'primarily' is merely being non-oblique relative to the other <s>kārakas</s>. Thus, in 'he cooks' and the like, the agent-hood of <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, who possess the non-oblique activity of cooking and so forth, is established everywhere. But in 'he causes to cook' and the like, even though there is cognition of the activity of the one who is caused to act, since that [activity] is oblique relative to [the activity of the causer], the agent-hood does not belong to the possessor of that [caused activity]. What then? It belongs to the instigator alone, since his activity is non-oblique. If so, then,

children.text: svavyāpāre hi kartṛtvaṃ sarvatraivāsti kārake /
children.translated_text: 'For agent-hood with respect to one's own activity exists everywhere in every <s>kāraka</s>' —

children.text: iti nyāyena karaṇādivyavahāravilopaprasaṅga ityata āha--prādhānyeneti /
children.translated_text: by this principle, there would be the absurd consequence of the obliteration of the conventional usage of instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) and the like — therefore he says: 'primarily.'

children.text: svavyāpārāpekṣayā na karaṇādivyavahāraḥ, kiṃ tu pradhānakriyāpekṣayetyabhiprāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: The intention is: the conventional usage of instrument and the like is not with respect to one's own activity, but rather with respect to the principal action.

children.text:
nanu ca kārakasādhyatvāviśeṣe 'pi (karaṇādivyavahāraḥ) pradhānakriyāpekṣayā ityetadeva kuta ityata āha-- avāntareti /
avāntareti /
asti hi kāñcit kriyāmuddeśya pravartamānānāṃ kārakāṇāmavāntaravyāpārayogaḥ /
, na tvavāntaravyāpārārthameva teṣāṃ pravṛttirityarthaḥ /
nanu na sarvo vyāpāraḥ pradhānakriyā vā puruṣamāśrayate, tat kathamāha--puruṣa itītyata āha--puruṣa iti prakṛtāpekṣam /
tadetad vaiyākaraṇānāṃ lakṣaṇam /
taccānupapannam, śabdaprayogamātrasyāvyavasthāpakatvāt /
vyavasthāhetośca lakṣaṇatvāt /
abhidhānayogyatālakṣaṇamiti cet--na, tasyā eva vicāryamāṇatvāt /
vivakṣāmātramiti cet--na, tasyā api nimittamantareṇāvyavasthiterityāśayavānāha--lakṣaṇāntaramiti /
puruṣa iti vartate /
tathā ca tatprayoktṛtvamityatra tasya prayokteti
children.translated_text: Now, even though there is no difference in being accomplished by <s>kārakas</s>, from where [comes] the [usage of] instrument and the like with respect to the principal action? — therefore he says: 'subsidiary...' 'Subsidiary' — for there is indeed, for <s>kārakas</s> that are engaged with reference to some action, a connection with subsidiary activity. But the engagement of those [<s>kārakas</s>] is not for the purpose of the subsidiary activity alone — that is the meaning. Now, not every activity, whether principal or otherwise, is dependent on a person — so how can he say 'person'? — therefore he says: 'Person [is used] with reference to the topic at hand.' This is the definition of the grammarians. And that is untenable, since mere verbal usage is not determinative. And because the determining factor has the character of a definition. If [one says] 'the definition is fitness for denotation' — no, because that itself is what is being examined. If [one says] 'it is merely the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>)' — no, because even that is indeterminate without a ground — with this intention he says: 'another definition.' 'Person' is carried over. And thus in 'the agent of that' — lest there be a doubt about the analysis [of the compound] that 'of that' means 'its agent,'

children.text:
vigrahaśaḍkā mā bhūdityāśāyavānāha---tasya cetanasyeti /
etena sa cāsau prayoktā ceti vā tasya cetanasya
children.translated_text: he says with the intention that there should be no such doubt: 'of that conscious being.'

children.text: prayoktṛtvaṃ dharma iti vā vigraha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, the analysis is either 'he who is that and also the agent' or 'the agent-hood of that conscious being is the property' — that is the meaning.

children.text: atra ca savrakāraṇānīti svetaraparasparavisadṛśānekakārakāmiprāyam /
children.translated_text: And here, 'together with all causes' means having the nature of many <s>kārakas</s> that are mutually dissimilar from each other.

children.text: tenādṛṣṭamanadhitiṣṭhato 'pi kulālasva kartṛtvamakṣatameveti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the agent-hood of the potter remains unimpaired even without being presided over by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit).

children.text:
etāvataiva lakṣaṇe parisamāpte itarāprayojyatvamityanena cetanaprayukti prati svātantryamitareṣāṃ vyavacchindatā parasparaprayojanakatvamapi vyavacchinnam /
cetanasyāpi tāni vyāpārayata eva kartṛtvamityuktam /
tathā ca yathā kāryaṃ kartradhīnaṃ tathā kārakāntarādhīnamityubhayavyāptāt kāryādekatarāpāye 'pyanyatarāpāya iti darśitam /
ato lakṣaṇasya nātivyāpakatvam /
acetaneṣu tu kartṛvyavahāraḥ kathamityavaśiṣyate tatrāha--acetanasya tviti /
svābhāvikaṃ mukhyam /
tattvaṃ hi pramāṇavyāpyatvaṃ pramāṇavyāpāraviṣayatvamiti vadataḥ karaṇavyāpāraviṣayaḥ karmeti karmalakṣaṇa saṃmatam /
tatra lakṣaṇe 'vāntaravyāpāro grāhyaḥ /
prakṛte ca pradhānavyāpāraḥ pramitilakṣaṇa iti vibhāgaḥ /
viniyojyateti /
anena vārttikasthasya viniyogasya viṣayaniṣṭhatvaṃ darśayatā yogyatāpi viṣayagataiva draṣṭavyetyapi darśitam /
children.translated_text: by showing that the application (<s>viniyoga</s>) stated in the <s>Vārttika</s> pertains to the object, it is also shown that fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) too should be understood as pertaining to the object.

children.text: tena viniyogāya yogyatā viṣayagataivetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning is that the fitness for application pertains to the object alone.

children.text: jñānaparaṃ caitat /
children.translated_text: And this pertains to cognition [specifically].

children.text: tenāyamarthaḥ viniyogo vārthagatastadyogyatājñānaṃ vā caturvargasya paryavasānamiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning is: the application, whether pertaining to the object, or the cognition of the fitness for it, culminates in the fourfold group [of knower, means, object, and result].

With the definition already complete by just this much, by [the addition of] 'not caused by another,' while excluding the independence of other [<s>kārakas</s>] with respect to the prompting by a conscious being, the mutual causation [among <s>kārakas</s>] is also excluded. It is stated that agent-hood belongs to the conscious being who sets those [<s>kārakas</s>] into operation. And thus, just as the effect is dependent on the agent, so it is dependent on the other <s>kārakas</s> — since the effect is pervaded by both, the removal of either entails the removal of the other. Therefore the definition does not over-extend. But the conventional usage of agent for non-conscious [entities] — how [is that explained]? — this remains. Regarding that he says: 'Of the non-conscious, however...' 'Natural' means primary. For the one who says that reality (<s>tattva</s>) is what is pervaded by <s>pramāṇa</s>, [meaning] what is the object of the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> — the object of the operation of the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is <s>karman</s> (object) — this definition of <s>karman</s> is accepted. In that definition, the subsidiary activity should be understood. And in the present context, the principal activity has the nature of valid cognition (<s>pramiti</s>) — this is the distinction. 'Is applied to' —

children.text:
pañceti /
rūpaṃ saṃjñā saṃskāro vedanā vijñānamiti /
tatra rūparasagandhasparśaśabdāḥ rūpaskandhaḥ /
savikalpakaṃ vijñānaṃ saṃjñāskandhaḥ /
samanantarapratyayaḥ saṃskāraskandhaḥ /
sukhaduḥkhe vedanāskandhaḥ /
nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ vijñānaskandhaḥ /
jīveti /
jīvaścetanaḥ /
taditaro 'jīvaḥ /
āstravantītyāstravāḥ /
srotāṃsīndriyāṇi /
srotobhiriva tairayaṃ jīvo dharmādharmābhyāmāpūryata ityarthaḥ /
saṃvaraṇaṃ saṃvaraḥ, jīvājīvaviṣayo 'bhedābhimānaḥ /
tena saṃvṛtohyayaṃ jīvo 'sarvajña iti /
children.translated_text: For this <s>jīva</s>, being covered over by that [restraint], is not omniscient.

children.text: nirjaraṇaṃ nirjaraḥ tapaścaraṇam, nigaḍakaṭakābhyāmivāyaṃ baddho 'svatanatro jīva ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirjarā</s>' (wearing away) is the wearing off — [i.e.,] the practice of austerity (<s>tapas</s>). The meaning is: this <s>jīva</s> is bound and unfree, as if by fetters and shackles.

children.text: mokṣaḥ sakalāvaraṇavigama ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mokṣa</s>' (liberation) means the removal of all coverings — that is the meaning.

children.text: sarvatra niyamo 'prāmāṇikaḥ //
children.translated_text: The restriction [to these categories] in every case is without valid basis.

'Five' — form, name (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Therein, form, taste, smell, touch, and sound constitute the form-aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>). Determinate cognition is the name-aggregate (<s>saṃjñāskandha</s>). The immediately preceding condition is the formation-aggregate (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>). Pleasure and pain are the feeling-aggregate (<s>vedanāskandha</s>). Indeterminate cognition is the consciousness-aggregate (<s>vijñānaskandha</s>). '<s>Jīva</s>' — the <s>jīva</s> is the conscious being. What is other than that is <s>ajīva</s> (non-living). '<s>Āsrava</s>' — those that have inflows. The 'streams' (<s>srotāṃsi</s>) are the sense-faculties. The meaning is: through those [streams], like through channels, this <s>jīva</s> is filled up by <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). '<s>Saṃvara</s>' (restraint) is the covering over, [i.e.,] the identification without distinction regarding the <s>jīva</s> and <s>ajīva</s>.

children.text:
nanu na vidhāyakapramāṇanivṛttimārgeṇāsattvamityata āha--taditi /
pramāṇaviṣayatvena sadasatorekatvamavilakṣaṇavyavahāraviṣayatvamabhimatameva, tato nirdalā śaḍketyata āha--sarvasāmarthyeti /
children.translated_text: Now, [one might object that] non-existence is not [established] through the method of the cessation of a prescriptive <s>pramāṇa</s> — therefore he says: 'that.' That existent and non-existent are the same insofar as being objects of <s>pramāṇa</s> — [and that this means they have] the same status as objects of undifferentiated conventional usage — is indeed accepted. Therefore, the objection is groundless — to this he says: 'of all capacity.'

children.text:
arthakriyāsāmarththaṃ hi sallakṣaṇam /
tacced bhavadabhimate abhāve 'pyasti so 'pi sadvyavahāraviśayaḥ prasakta iti
children.translated_text: For the definition of the existent is the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). If that [capacity] exists even in absence (<s>abhāva</s>) according to your view, then even that [absence] would absurdly become an object of the convention 'existent' —

children.text: ṭīkārthaḥ /
na ca vayamityādinā abhāvasya sāmārthyamaḍgīkṛtam, na tu sāmarthyena sadvyavahāraḥ, ananusaṃhitasāmarthyasyāpi sadvyavahāraviṣayatvāt /
children.translated_text: By 'nor do we' and so forth, the capacity of absence is accepted, but conventional usage as 'existent' [is not accepted merely] through capacity, since even something whose capacity is not attended to is an object of the convention 'existent.'

children.text: api tvastināstipratītiviṣayatvena /
children.translated_text: Rather, [it is] through being the object of the cognitions 'exists' and 'does not exist.'

children.text: na hyasti saṃbhavaḥ saditi vyavahniyate, na cāstipratyayaviṣaya iti /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that something is called 'existent' because it is a possibility, nor is it called 'existent' because it is the object of an 'exists'-cognition,

children.text: asaditi vā vyavahniyate na ca nāstipratyayaviṣayaḥ iti prakāraṇārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: nor is something called 'non-existent' while not being the object of a 'does-not-exist' cognition — that is the import of the passage.
this is the meaning of the sub-commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>).

children.text:
syādetat /
prameyavailakṣaṇyavat pramāṇavailakṣaṇyenāpi sākṣātkārādivat pratītibhedo ghaṭate /
tataḥ sadantara eveyaṃ nāstīti pratīti /
kadācid bhavedityāśaḍkyāha---saṃpratīti /
abādhite prasiddhatare vipratipattirna kāñcit kṣatimāvahatītyarthaḥ /
nanu niṣidhyatāṃ bhāvāntaram /
tathāpyabhāvidhau kimāyātam? na hi nīlaniṣadhe pītādividhiravaśyamityata āha--nīlapītau hīti /
nanu sarvaśaḍkānirākaraṇapaṭīyasi pratyakṣe 'pi pravṛtte kutastarkasyāvakārśaḥ? tataḥ kimatropapattyetyata āha--yadi kaściditi /
santyeva hi kecid vādino ye vipakṣadaṇḍamapaśyantaḥ pratyakṣaparikalitamapahnutya śaḍakāmutthāpayanti, tān sāṃkhyādīn prati ayaṃ prakāra ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For there are indeed certain disputants who, not seeing the penalty against the opposing side, deny what is ascertained by perception and raise doubts. This method is directed against them — the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and the like — that is the meaning.

children.text: pūrvavad vyākhyeyam /
children.translated_text: It should be explained as before.

children.text: tulyopalambhayogyatātarkāntarbhāvenetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: by subsuming [the argument] under the reasoning of equal fitness for apprehension (<s>tulyopalambhayogyatā</s>).

children.text: nanvabhāve tatpratyakṣatāyāṃ ca bahuvipratipattibījamastītyāha--sarva caitaditi //
children.translated_text: Now, regarding absence and its perceptibility, there are many seeds of disagreement — therefore he says: 'And all this...'

Now, just as there is diversity of <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge), so too through the diversity of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge), a difference in cognition is possible, just like [the difference between] direct perception and the like. Therefore, this cognition 'does not exist' is within the domain of the existent itself. Could it not sometimes [be otherwise]? — anticipating this, he says: 'At present.' The meaning is: when what is well-established and uncontradicted is [in play], disagreement does not cause any damage. Now, let another positive entity be denied. Even so, what follows for the establishment of absence? For it is not the case that by denying blue, yellow and the like are necessarily established — therefore he says: 'For blue and yellow...' Now, even when perception, which is most capable of removing all doubts, is operative, from where does reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) find scope? So what use is logical argument here? — therefore he says: 'If someone...'

children.text:
nanu yadyasadbhedāḥ prakṛtānupayoginaḥ, tadā anupayogādeva nocyanta ityucyatām /
athopayoginastadā avaśyaṃ vaktavyā eva /
pāratantryeṇa pratibhāsanāt nocyanta iti kkopayujyata ityata āha--niṣedhyeti /
pratipādanāya hi te vaktavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: For those [varieties] must be stated for the purpose of exposition.

children.text: tacca pratiyogyadhikaraṇapratipādanādevārthato bhūtamiti kiṃ tadarthaprayāsenetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [exposition] is already effectively accomplished by the exposition of the counterpositive and its locus — so what is the use of effort for that purpose? — that is the meaning.

children.text: tadidamuktaṃ gamyanta iti nāktā ityartha iti /
children.translated_text: This is what is meant by: 'they are understood' — the meaning is: 'they are not stated [explicitly].'

children.text: nanu yadyupāyapratipādanenaiva pratipāditā iti noktāḥ, tarhi prameyādayo 'pi pramāṇapratipādanenaiva pratipāditā iti kiṃ tatkathanenāpi? atha pratītā api prayojanaviśeṣādabhyarhitatayā pratipādyante, hanatāsadbhedā api upayuktāstathā kiṃ netyata āha--atha veti //
children.translated_text: Now, if [the varieties of absence] are not stated because they are already conveyed by the exposition of the means [of knowledge], then the <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) and the like too are already conveyed by the exposition of <s>pramāṇa</s> — so what is the use of stating them either? Or if, even though already understood, they are expounded because they merit [separate treatment] due to a specific purpose, then why not the varieties of the non-existent too, being useful? — therefore he says: 'Or alternatively...'

Now, if the varieties of the non-existent are irrelevant to the topic at hand, then let it simply be said that they are not discussed because of their irrelevance. But if they are relevant, then they must necessarily be stated. The fact that they are not stated because they appear only dependently — where is this applicable? — therefore he says: 'what is to be negated...'

children.text:
nanu bhāvaprapañcavadabhāvaprapañce 'pyuddiṣṭo veditavya iti pratijñāter'the caturvargānantarbhāvāditi heturbhāgāsiddho viruddhaścetyata āha-niḥśreyaseti /
tena niḥśreyasānapayogyabhāvaprapañcadhikaraṇatayā caturvargānantarbhāvo hetuḥ /
tadadhikāraṇatayā tathābhūta eva bhāvaprapañco dṛṣṭānto nocyata iti sādhyam /
niḥśreyasopayogī tūddiṣṭo veditavyaḥ,
children.translated_text: Now, [the objection is:] just as in the proliferation of positive entities, so too in the proliferation of absences, the meaning of the declaration 'what is enumerated is to be known' [should apply]. Since the fourfold group does not include [absences], the reason is partly unestablished and contradictory — therefore he says: 'of the highest good.' Therefore, the reason is the non-inclusion in the fourfold group due to the locus-hood of the proliferation of absences that are not conducive to the highest good. The example is: the proliferation of positive entities that is of such a nature [i.e., conducive to the highest good] due to being the locus of that [i.e., the highest good] — [and the conclusion is that] it is not stated. The thesis is: what is conducive to the highest good is enumerated and to be known,

children.text:
catuvargāntarbhāvāt /
upayuktabhāvaprapañcavaditi vārttikārtha ityarthaḥ /
ata evoddiṣṭo veditavya iti anupalabdhibādhitaṃ manyamāna uttaragranthamavatārayati--atheti /
kāraṇānupalabdhyā sarva evānupalabdhiprabhedā upalakṣitāḥ /
apavarga eva mardhābhiṣiktaḥ pradhānatayā rājakalpaḥ /
etadapyupalakṣaṇam /
artho 'pi śatruputrādyabhāvādiḥ, pravṛttirapyahiṃsādiḥ, pretyabhāvo 'pi pūrvaśarīraparityāgādiḥ,
children.translated_text: because of being included in the fourfold group. And the meaning of the <s>Vārttika</s> is: 'like the proliferation of useful positive entities.' For this very reason, considering the [objection] 'what is enumerated is to be known' to be contradicted by non-apprehension, he introduces the subsequent text: 'now...' By non-apprehension of the cause, all varieties of non-apprehension are indicated. Liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) alone is, as it were, crowned with eminence, being principal. And this too is illustrative. [There are also] objects such as the absence of enemies, sons, and the like; activities such as non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and the like; and afterlife-states such as the abandonment of the former body and the like.

children.text:
phalamapyutpannarogapradhvaṃsādyasadbheda iti mantavyam /
saṃśayasya jñānarūpatvādasadrūpatā na saṃbhavatīti tamullaḍghyātidiśati--evaṃ prayojaneti /
tathā hi sandhyāvandanaprāyaścittādāvahitanivṛttireva prayojanam /
dṛṣṭānto 'pi kaścidabhāvarūpo yathā suṣuptyavasthānamapavarge dṛṣṭāntayiṣyati /
siddhānto 'pi nairātmyādiḥ pareṣām /
asmākaṃ ca yathā bhābhāvastamaḥ [vai. sū. 5.2.19] ityevamādiḥ /
sarveṣāmapavargo duḥkhābhāva iti /
avayavatarkanirṇayavādajalpaviṇḍāstu sadbhedā eva /
hetvābhāsā dvividhāḥ /
yathā, anityaḥ śabdaḥ sattārahitatvāta, cākṣuṣatvādityevamādiḥ /
chalaṃ jātayaśca sadbhedā eva /
nigrahasthāneṣu vipratipattividhāḥ sadbhedāḥ /
apratipattividhā asadbhedāḥ /
tadidamuktam--evaṃ tatra tatrohanīyamiti /
nanu bhāṣye asadbhedakathanavārtāpi nāstītyata āha--atreti /
parasparaviruddhayorabhidhānānabhidhānayoḥ paramārthikatvaṃ na saṃbhavati /
tat kataradatra pāramārthikamityata āha--dvitīye tu kalpe pāramārthikaṃ iti /
sūtrasya saprapañca tātparyam--pramāṇata ityādiprapañcaḥ, sacca khalu ṣāḍaśadhā vyūḍhamupadekṣyata iti tātparyam /
children.translated_text: The import of the <s>sūtra</s> together with its elaboration — the elaboration [beginning with] "from <s>pramāṇa</s>" and so forth; and the import is that it will be taught as arranged in sixteen categories.

children.text: tasya tātparyamiti /
children.translated_text: "The import of that" — [this is the explanation].

children.text: tāsāṃ khalvāsāmityavatārabhāṣyasya, na tu sūtra pāṭhasya /
children.translated_text: "Of those indeed" — this is [the gloss] of the introductory <s>bhāṣya</s>, not of the <s>sūtra</s>-text itself.

children.text: avayavārthaṃ vyācikhyāsunetyanenaiva tātparyasya sphoritatvāt //
children.translated_text: Because the import has been made manifest by the very [statement] "wishing to explain the meaning of the components."

The result also should be understood as having non-real distinctions, such as the destruction of already-arisen disease and the like. Since doubt is of the nature of cognition, non-real form is not possible — overstepping that [objection], he directs: "Thus the purpose..." For indeed, in twilight worship, <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiatory rites) and the like, the cessation of what is harmful is the sole purpose. The illustration too is in some cases of the nature of absence — as, for example, the state of deep sleep will be cited as an illustration for <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).
