children.translated_text: The intention is: what is meant here by example-hood is merely being within the domain of the apprehension of connection, not being within the domain of the apprehension of a specific connection characterized by <s>vyāpti</s> (universal concomitance).

children.text: yattu tatpramāṇye tadviṣayagocarānumānābhiprāyeṇa dṛṣṭāntāpekṣā āgamasyāpyastīti kaiścid vyākhyātaṃ tat pūrvaṃ jñātaṃ cārthaṃ parasmā ācaṣṭa iti vadatā vārtikakṛtaiva apāstam /
children.translated_text: But what some have explained — that for scripture too there is dependence on an example, with the intention of an inference whose object is the object of that [scripture], for the purpose of establishing its authoritative status — that has been set aside by the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> himself by saying 'he communicates to another a meaning previously known.'

children.text: atastadupekṣitavāniti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, he [Udayana] has disregarded that [interpretation].

children.text:
atrārthāmyupagamayorguṇapradhānabhāvasya vivakṣātantratvādarthābhyupagamo 'bhyupagamyamāno vārthaḥ siddhāntaḥ /
tena sūtrabhāṣyavārttikaṭīkāsu mitho na virodhaḥ /
idamitthaṃbhūtaśabdayorviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyamāvabhramaṃ nivārayati--idamitīti /
na tu
children.translated_text: Here, since the principal-subsidiary relation of the thesis and the acceptance is a matter of intention, the acceptance that is being accepted [or] the thesis-meaning is the <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine). Therefore, there is no mutual contradiction among the <s>sūtra</s>, <s>bhāṣya</s>, <s>vārttika</s>, and <s>ṭīkā</s>. He prevents a confusion about the qualifier-qualificand relationship of the words 'idam' (this) and 'itthaṃbhūta' (of such a kind): 'idam iti' (by 'this'). But not

children.text:
puruṣaviśeṣe vyavasthāpayatīti /
vyavasthāśabdo na puruṣaviśeṣe abhyupagamaniyamamāha--kiṃ tarhyanabhyupagamasamuccayaṃ nirākurvan svarūpaniyamamityarthaḥ /
nanu vādādipravṛttyarthaṃ pratitantrasiddhānta evopayujyate, tat kimaparairityata āha--tatheti /
nanu yata eva sarvatantrasiddhānta na vipratipattiviṣayaḥ, ata eva na vādādipravṛttiheturityata āha--tathā
children.translated_text: as establishing [it] with reference to a specific person. The word 'establishment' (<s>vyavasthā</s>) does not denote a restriction of acceptance to a specific person — what then? It denotes a restriction of intrinsic nature, excluding the combination of non-acceptances — this is the meaning. Now, only the doctrine specific to a particular school (<s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s>) is useful for the purpose of engaging in debate and the like — then what is the point of the others? — therefore he says: 'tathā' (thus). Now, since the doctrine common to all schools (<s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s>) is not a subject of disagreement, for that very reason it is not a cause of engaging in debate and the like — therefore he says: 'tathā

children.text:
hīti /
yadyapi svarūpeṇa sarvatantrasiddhānto na vādādipravṛttyaṅgam, tathāpi pratitantrādisiddhāntotthāpanadvārā nyāyāśrayatayā copayujyeta ityarthaḥ /
etenaiva pratitantrasiddhāntaprayojanaṃ chalataḥ prakaṭīkṛtam /
kimāśrayaśrva nyāyaḥ syāt? asati sarvatantrasiddhānta iti śeṣaḥ /
adhikaraṇasiddhāntaprayojanamāha--tatheti /
sādhyasāmānyavyāptaṃ sādhānasāmānyamiti sādhanaviśeṣāt sādhyaviśeṣaḥ kathaṃ gamyeteti yojanā /
ayamarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the meaning:

children.text: adhikaraṇasiddhāntena hi phalena viṣayeṇa vā pakṣadharmatā phalavatī viṣayavatī vā syāt /
children.translated_text: For through the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> — either as the result or as the subject — the property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) would be fruitful or would have a subject.

children.text: tadabhāve tu sā niṣphalā nirviṣayā vā, tathā ca vyāptirapi sāmānyaviṣayā satī kevalā sāmānyamātramupanīya pakṣe kathaṃ vyavasthāpayet? avyavasthāpya ca kathaṃ kṛtārthā syāt? tathā cānumānamātram ucchidyeta /
children.translated_text: But in its absence, that [property] would be fruitless or without a subject; and thus even <s>vyāpti</s> (universal concomitance), being only about the general, would merely bring the general to the thesis-subject — how could it establish [anything specific]? And without establishing [it], how could it be effectual? And thus inference itself would be destroyed.

children.text: evaṃ ca kva nyāyaḥ? kva vā vādāyata iti? tasmādadhikaraṇasiddhānto 'pi pakṣadharmatāphalaviṣayatayā avaśyaṃ vyutpādanīyo yena vyāptirapi tatsahāyā satī phalavatī syāditi //
children.translated_text: And thus — where would <s>nyāya</s> be? Or where would debate be? Therefore, the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> too must necessarily be taught, as [providing] the fruit and subject of the property of the thesis-subject, so that <s>vyāpti</s> too, aided by it, would be fruitful.

hī' (for thus). Although the <s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s> in its own form is not a factor in engaging in debate and the like, nevertheless, through the door of raising doctrines specific to particular schools, it would be useful as a basis of <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning) — this is the meaning. By this very [explanation], the purpose of the <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> has been incidentally revealed. 'What would <s>nyāya</s> be based on?' — the completion being: 'in the absence of a <s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s>.' He states the purpose of the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> (doctrine pertaining to a topic): 'tathā' (thus). How can a specific <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) be understood from a specific <s>sādhana</s> (proof), when a general <s>sādhana</s> pervades only a general <s>sādhya</s>? — this is the construction.

children.text:
mukhyamartha gṛhītvā śaṅkate--nanviti /
bhaktyā ca vṛttyā pariharati--avayavā iveti /
bhaktimāha--yathā hīti, kriyodāharaṇaṃ--someneti, somapadasya karmanāmadheyatvāt /
dhātvarthamātravivakṣayā ca karakapadāt pṛthagamidhānam,
children.translated_text: Having taken the primary meaning, he raises a doubt: 'nanu' (now). And he resolves it through a secondary sense: 'avayavāḥ iva' (like the parts). He states the secondary sense: 'yathā hī' (for just as). The illustration of the action: 'somena' (with <s>Soma</s>), since the word '<s>Soma</s>' is the name of the ritual action (<s>karman</s>). And by intending only the meaning of the verbal root, the separate statement from the <s>kāraka</s> term [is explained],

children.text:
vastutastu somasyāpi kārakatvameva /
godohaneneti kārakodāharaṇam, apaḥ praṇayanasya vākyāntaraprāptatvāt /
prātipadikārthodāharaṇam--yasyeti vrātyaśabdasyārthavato 'dhātvapratyayarūpatvāt /
tathāpi na samūho vyutpādita ityata āha--tadaneneti /
children.translated_text: Even so, the aggregate has not been taught — therefore he says: 'tadanena' (by this).

children.text: nanu viśeṣapratyayahetavo 'vākyabhūtā api santīti anenābhiprāyeṇa pṛcchati--ka iti /
children.translated_text: Now, there are also [elements] that are not full sentences but are causes of the cognition of a specific [meaning] — with this intention he asks: 'kaḥ' (who/what?).

children.text: pratyayasya prādhānyaṃ nirākurvanneva pratyayapadopādānaprayojanamāha--na ca taditi /
children.translated_text: While refuting the primacy of the suffix, he states the purpose of mentioning the suffix: 'na ca tad' (and not that).

children.text: viśeṣaṇāsiddhiṃ parihārannāhapratītiśceti //
children.translated_text: Resolving the non-establishment of the qualifier, he says: 'pratītiśca' (and cognition).

but in reality <s>Soma</s> too has the status of a <s>kāraka</s> (factor of action). 'Godohanena' (by cow-milking) — this is an illustration of a <s>kāraka</s>, since the carrying of water is obtained from another sentence. The illustration of the nominal stem meaning: 'yasya' (whose) — since the word '<s>vrātya</s>' is meaningful but does not consist of a verbal root or suffix.

children.text:
athānubhava eva kasmānna bhavati? na hyantyapadaṃ nānubhūyata eva /
tathā sati smaryetāpi kathamityata āha--na hīti /
tathāpyevaṃbhūtasyāpi tadasya smṛtiranubhūtimantareṇa na syādityata āha--saṃbhavanti tviti /
astu tarhi tadanubhava evārthapratītyaṅgamityata āha--na caita iti /
tadanenānubhava evārthapratyāyanāṅgamiti nirastam /
anubhavasmṛtisamuccayaṃ nirākaroti--na ca pūrveti /
smṛtyunabhavayostu syāt sahabhāva ityanuṣañjanīyam /
etacca upāntyāntyavarṇānubhavāntarāle smṛtyabhyupagamena draṣṭavyam /
yadi tu varṇānāṃ nirantarotpādavatāṃ nirantarā evānubhavāstadā vinaśyadavinaśyadavasthayoḥ upāntyāntyānubhavayoreva sahabhāvaḥ śaṅganīyaḥ, nirākaraṇīyaścoktayuktyā /
children.translated_text: But if for phonemes that are produced without interruption, the experiences are also without interruption, then the simultaneity of the experience of the penultimate and the final [phonemes] — in the states of perishing and not-yet-perished — is to be suspected, and is to be refuted by the stated reasoning.

children.text: ato na pṛthagāśaḍkitaḥ ṭīkākṛtā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the author of the <s>Ṭīkā</s> has not separately raised this doubt.

children.text: kāraṇasamuccayavaśād viṣayāsamuccayavataḥ pratyayasya svarūpasamuccayaṃ parasvīkṛtaṃ śaṅkate--na ca pūrveti /
children.translated_text: He raises as a possible [opponent's] view the aggregation of the intrinsic nature of a cognition that has a non-aggregated object, through the aggregation of causes: 'na ca pūrva' (and not the prior).

children.text: nirākaroti--saṃbandheti //
children.translated_text: He refutes: 'saṃbandha' (connection).

Now, why should it not be experience alone [that generates sentence-meaning]? For the final phoneme is certainly experienced. If so, how would [the earlier phonemes] even be remembered? — therefore he says: 'na hī' (for not). Even so, [one may ask:] for something of this nature, the memory of it would not occur without experience — therefore he says: 'saṃbhavanti tu' (but they are possible). Then let that experience itself be a factor in the cognition of meaning — therefore he says: 'na ca etad' (and not this). By this, the [view that] experience alone is the factor in conveying meaning is refuted. He refutes the [view of an] aggregate of experience and memory: 'na ca pūrva' (and not the prior). But of memory and experience there could be simultaneity — this is to be connected. And this should be understood by accepting memory in the interval between the experience of the penultimate and the final phonemes.

children.text:
yadyapi sahakārilābhādaparaḥ saṃskārasyodbodho nāma nāsti, tathāpi na yaḥ kaścit pratyayaḥ tasya sahakārī, sarvadā sarvasaṃskārodvodhe sarvasmṛtiprasaṅgāt /
nāpi saḍketaviśeṣasmaraṇe padaikadeśavarṇānubhavastatsaṃskārasya sahakārī, tathā satyatiprasaṅgāt /
tasmāt padatvena pratisandhānameva samayasmṛtihetusaṃskārasya
children.translated_text: Although there is no awakening of a <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) apart from the obtaining of an auxiliary cause, nevertheless not just any cognition is its auxiliary cause — since if all <s>saṃskāras</s> were always awakened, there would follow the absurd consequence of all memories [arising at once]. Nor is the experience of the phonemes constituting a part of a word the auxiliary cause for remembering the specific convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) pertaining to that <s>saṃskāra</s> — since if so, there would be over-extension. Therefore, it is the integration [of phonemes] as a word (<s>padatva</s>) itself that is to be accepted as the auxiliary cause of the <s>saṃskāra</s> that causes the memory of the convention —

children.text:
sahakārītyupagantavyam /
tathā caikapraghaṭṭakenāpi vicitrajñānena viṣayīkṛto varṇāḥ khaṇḍaśaḥ padabhāvena pratisandheyāḥ,
children.translated_text: this must be accepted. And thus, the phonemes — even [though] made into objects by a single composite (<s>ekapraghaṭṭaka</s>) cognition of diverse [content] — are to be integrated piecemeal as words,

children.text:
arthasaṃbaddhatvena smartavyā iti kuto 'nubhavāvakārśaḥ ityarthaḥ /
prakriyā ta, antyavarṇānubhavasyotpādaḥ,
children.translated_text: and to be remembered as connected with meaning. So from where is the impairment of experience? — this is the meaning. The process is: the arising of the experience of the final phoneme,

children.text: tatsaṃskārapadatvapratisandhānayorūtpadyamānatetyekaḥ kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: and the arising of its <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) and the integration as a word — this is one moment.

children.text: atha tayorūtpādaḥ, sa eva padapratisandhānotpādātmā samayasaṃskārodbodhaḥ saṃbandhasmaraṇasyotpadyamānatā saṃskārodbodhād vicitrapratyayasya vinaśyattetyekaḥ kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then their arising — that very [process], consisting of the arising of word-integration, is the awakening of the convention-<s>saṃskāra</s>; the arising of the memory of connection; and from the awakening of the <s>saṃskāra</s>, the perishing of the composite cognition — this is one moment.

children.text: atha saṃbandhasmaraṇotpādaḥ vicitrapratyayasya vināśaḥ padatvānusaṃdhānasya vinaśyattetyekaḥ kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the arising of the memory of connection; the perishing of the composite cognition; and the perishing of the word-integration — this is one moment.

children.text: na caitadadṛṣṭaṃ kalpanamityāha--ata eveti //
children.translated_text: And this is not an unseen speculation — he says: 'ata eva' (for this very reason).

children.text:
nanvekapraghaṭṭakena vicitrapratyaya evānusaṃghānātmā bhaviṣyati, kariṣyati ca samayasmṛtiṃ tathāvidhām /
athāpi
children.translated_text: Now, the composite (<s>ekapraghaṭṭaka</s>) cognition of diverse [content] will itself take the form of integration and will produce the memory of convention of that kind. Or rather,

children.text:
pūrvasmṛtiraśeṣapadāvagāhinyekaiva svīkartavyā ityata āha--evaṃ ceti /
anubhūtaṃ hi pratisaṃdhīyate, na taṃ prathamata eva, tathā ca pūrvavarṇāṇāmunabhūtatvena padatvānusaṃdhānasaṃbhave 'pi antyavarṇasyānanubhūtatayā nāntyapadapratisaṃdhānasaṃbhavaḥ /
na cānubhavānusaṃdhānayorekakālatā, kāryakāraṇabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: And the simultaneity of experience and integration is not [possible], because of the cause-effect relation [between them].

children.text: tasmāt tadanantarameva padatvānusaṃdhānamiti suṣṭhūktaṃ, yadā padārthapratyāyane 'nubhavo na kāraṇamiti tadaupayikasmṛtyutpattau tu kāraṇameveti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is well stated that the word-integration occurs immediately after that [experience]. Thus, experience is not a cause in conveying the meaning of a word, but it is indeed a cause in the production of the relevant memory.

children.text: avadhāraṇādītyatrādiśabdena taṣāṃ smaraṇaṃ vivakṣitam /
children.translated_text: By the word 'ādi' (etc.) in 'ascertainment, etc.,' the memory of those [conventions] is intended.

children.text: prakaraṇādayastu yogyatāviśeṣatvāt tatraivāntarbhūtā iti tata eva vākyārthapratīterūpapatteḥ, anupapattau tvasiddhirlakṣaṇasya doṣa ityāśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: But context and the like, being specific types of fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>), are included in that very [fitness] — and thus the comprehension of sentence-meaning is accounted for. If it could not be accounted for, then the fault would lie with the definition — this is the intention.

the prior memory encompassing all words should be accepted as a single [cognition] — therefore he says: 'evaṃ ca' (and thus). For what is experienced is integrated, not [what is experienced] for the first time. And thus, although the integration of the prior phonemes as a word is possible due to their being experienced, the integration of the final phoneme [with the word] is not possible due to its not [yet] being experienced.

children.text:
nanu kramānubhūtānāmapyekasmṛtisamārohaḥ saṃbhavatyeva, kiṃ tu padāni krameṇāpi nānubhūtānītyata uktam--nirantareti, nirantarasmṛtibhirviṣayīkṛtāni tata ekasmṛtisaṅkalitānityarthaḥ /
nairantaryaṃ ca smṛtīnāṃ sannikarṣād boddhavyam /
nanvetāvatāpi asiddhameva lakṣaṇam /
na hyevaṃbhūtamapyantyapadaṃ viśeṣapratipattiheturityāśayavānāha--syādetaditi /
nanu pratyekaṃ vyabhicāre hi parasparānugrahaḥ syāt /
na ca padakadambakapratisaṃdhānavat tadarthasmṛtirapi tathāvidhāṃ vākyārthapratyayotpatti prati vyabhicaratītyata āha--etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
ayamāśayaḥ, na tāvat tadārthā eva vākyārthe pramāṇam, sarvadātatpratītiprasaṅgāt /
nāpi ta eva smṛtāḥ, prakārāntareṇāpi smṛtānāṃ tathābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
nāpi ta eva padaiḥ smāritāḥ, padānāṃ padārthasmaraṇamātropayoge pūrvavat pratītiprasaṅgāt /
vākyārthapratītyupayoge tu teṣāṃ kathaṃ na taddhetutvam /
tathāpi guṇapradhānabhāvavinagimanāyāṃ ko heturiti
children.translated_text: Now, the ascent into a single memory is indeed possible even for things experienced in sequence — but the words have not been experienced even in sequence — therefore it is said: 'without interruption' — the meaning is: [words] made the objects of uninterrupted memories, and from that, collected into a single memory. And the uninterruptedness of the memories should be understood from [their] proximity. Even with this much, the definition is still unestablished. For even a final word of such a nature is not the cause of the apprehension of the specific [sentential meaning] — with this intention he says: 'It may be that...' Now, where there is deviation in each [word] individually, there would be mutual assistance [among them]. And just as the recollection of word-meanings, like the connection of a cluster of words, deviates with respect to the generation of sentential cognition of such a kind — therefore he says: 'What is being said is this.' The intention is as follows: it is not the case that those word-meanings alone are the <s>pramāṇa</s> for the sentential meaning, since that would lead to the absurd consequence of constant apprehension of that [meaning]. Nor [is it the case that] those [word-meanings] merely as remembered [are the cause], since the absurd consequence would be that things remembered in other ways too would be of such a nature. Nor [is it the case that] those [word-meanings] merely as recalled by words [are the cause], since if words are useful merely for recalling word-meanings, the previous absurd consequence [of constant apprehension] would follow. But when they are useful for the apprehension of sentential meaning, how can they not be causes of that? Even so, what is the reason for determining the relation of subsidiary and principal?

children.text: cet? asādhāraṇakāraṇatvaṃ padānām /
children.translated_text: The uncommon causality of the words [is the reason].

children.text: tadarthānāṃ tu atītānāgatādirūpatayā kāraṇatvameva nāsti, kuto 'sādhāraṇatm? ata eva na smṛtisteṣāṃ vyāpāraḥ, kiṃ tu kāraṇībhūtānāṃ padānāmeva /
children.translated_text: But for the word-meanings, since they exist in the form of past, future, and the like, there is no causality at all — whence uncommon [causality]? For this very reason, memory is not their operation, but rather belongs only to the words that have become causes.

children.text: tathā ca vyāpārāvyabhicāramādāya nirvyāpārāvasthāyā vyabhicāravatāmakāraṇatvābhyupagamo bahuvyākulayatīti //
children.translated_text: And thus, accepting the non-causality of those [word-meanings] that have the deviation of the state of being without operation, while accepting the non-deviation of operation [of words] — creates much confusion.

children.text:
pratisandhīyamāna iti vārttikanirākaraṇīyamativyāpakatvaṃ darśayati--yadīti /
niṣpatterbhedaṃ darśayituṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Being connected' — he shows the over-extension to be refuted by the <s>Vārttika</s>: 'If...' To show the difference from accomplishment, again

children.text:
siddhirvyākhyānamanuvadati--vāstava iti /
na hi pratijñāvacanaṃ niśvāyakaṃ viśiṣṭasyeti śeṣaḥ /
hetuvacanādivaiyarthyāt
children.translated_text: he restates the explanation of 'real accomplishment': 'real...' The completion is: for the statement of the thesis is not determinative of the specific [conclusion]. Because of the pointlessness of the statement of the reason and so forth —

children.text:
vaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt /
sādhanasya nyāyaḥ pravṛttiprakāraḥ /
sa ca nānupalabdha ityādibhāṣye darśitaḥ /
tasyātipāto 'bhāva eva /
children.translated_text: the absurd consequence of pointlessness. The method (<s>nyāya</s>) of proof is the manner of procedure. And that is shown in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [beginning with] 'not unapprehended' and so forth. The transgression of that [method] is nothing but [its] absence.

children.text:
tameva vyutpādayet pradhānatayeti śeṣaḥ /
tasya ca nyāyaviṣeṣasya ātmādiviṣayasyetyarthaḥ /
alaukikopacāratvāt prayojanamāha--āgamopacārasyeti /
arthasaṃvādeneti karaṇe tṛtīyā /
āgamavirodhaśaṅgānivṛttiranugrahaḥ /
dṛḍhabhūmiśca saṃskāra āgamaikaviṣayatvāt /
saprayojanaśca bhavati niḥśreyasena prayojanena prayojanavāṃśca jñāto bhavatītyarthaḥ /
kutaḥ?
children.translated_text: The completion is: one should elucidate that [method of reasoning] itself as principal. And of that particular form of reasoning — the meaning is: pertaining to the self (<s>ātman</s>) and the like. Since it is a non-standard figurative usage, he states the purpose: 'of scriptural figurative usage.' 'By concordance with the object' — the instrumental is in the sense of means. The removal of the suspicion of contradiction with scripture is the assistance. And the firm ground is the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>), since it has scripture alone as its object. And it becomes purposeful — purposeful with the purpose of the highest good, and is known to be purposeful — that is the meaning. From where?

children.text: āgamārthajñānasyeti /
children.translated_text: From the cognition of the meaning of scripture.

children.text: nirūḍhatvāt prasiddhatvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because of being well-established, because of being well-known.

children.text: tat khalu hetuvacanamanumānapratipādakaṃ parāmṛśyamānaliṅgapratipādakaṃ yadi syāt, tadā viṣayatayānumānena parāmṛśyamānena liḍgenānugrahītavyam /
children.translated_text: If that statement of the reason, which presents inference, were to present the inferential mark as being reflectively considered, then it would have to be assisted by inference — [i.e.,] by the reflectively considered mark — as its object.

children.text: na ca tasya parāmṛśyamānaṃ liṅga viṣaya iti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: But the reflectively considered mark is not the object of that [statement of the reason] — this is the purport.

children.text:
nanu yadeva dṛśyamānaṃ liḍgaṃ hetuvacanasya viṣayaḥ, tadevānumitibhāvakamityata āha--na ca liṅgadarśanamātramiti /
dṛśyamānaliṅgamātramiti /
api tu saṃbandhasmṛtisahakārīti parāmṛśyamānaṃ liṅgamityarthaḥ /
tadidamuktam--tasmānna liṅgavacanamanumānapratipādakamiti /
dvitīyadaśanaviṣayaliḍgaṃ pratipādakaṃ na parāmṛśyamānaṃ liḍgaṃ pratipādakamityarthaḥ /
vyākhyānaṃ granthānurodhādasphuṭamityāśayavānāha--etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
evaṃ ca tatpratipādakasya tadviṣayapratipādakasyetyarthaḥ /
liṅgaparāmarśastāvadanumānam /
tasya ca
children.translated_text: Now, the very mark that is being observed is the object of the statement of the reason, and that very [mark] is productive of the inferential cognition — therefore he says: 'Not merely the observation of the mark...' The meaning is: 'merely the observed mark' — 'but rather [a mark] accompanied by the recollection of the relation' — that is what is meant by 'the reflectively considered mark.' This is what is said: 'Therefore, the statement of the mark is not what presents inference' — the meaning is: the mark as the object of the second observation is what presents [inference], not the reflectively considered mark. The explanation is unclear due to following the [order of the] text — with this intention he says: 'What is being said is this.' And thus, 'of that which presents that' means 'of that which presents what has that as its object' — that is the meaning. The reflective consideration of the mark (<s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s>) is, to begin with, inference. And of that,

children.text:
vyāptismṛtisahakāritānumitau, dvitīyāliṅgadarśanasyāpi vyāptismṛtisahakāritā parāmarśajñānajanana evetyubhayorapi saṃbandhasmṛtisahakāritāsāmyādanumānatvam /
tatastadviṣayaliṅgasyāpi, tatastadanugṛhītasya tadvacanasyāpītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: since the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) is an auxiliary in the inferential cognition, and since even the second observation of the mark has the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s> as an auxiliary in generating the cognition of reflective consideration — due to the similarity of both in having the recollection of the relation as an auxiliary, both have the character of inference. Therefore, [this applies] to the mark that is the object of that [second observation] too, and therefore also to the statement [of the reason] that is assisted by that [mark] — that is the meaning.

children.text: kimasyopacārasya phalamityata āha--evaṃ ceti //
children.translated_text: What is the fruit of this figurative usage? — therefore he says: 'And thus...'

children.text:
nanu pratyakṣaviṣayasya smṛtitaḥ punarūpadarśanāditi vaktavye kuto viparītamabhihitamityata āha--yatreti /
yadyapi pūrvapratyakṣaviṣayo dṛṣṭāntaḥ, tathāpyudāharaṇakāle tayāsmṛtyārūḍha eva vyāpriyata ityetāvatā tathaivoktamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, when it should be said that the object of a previous perception is [now] seen again from memory, why is the reverse stated? — therefore he says: 'Where...' Although the example pertains to the object of a previous perception, nevertheless, at the time of citation, it operates only as mounted on that memory — to this extent alone is it stated thus — that is the meaning.

children.text: na kevalaṃ pratyakṣeṇa sahaikaviṣayatvamupacāre bījam, api tu samānavyāpāratvamapītyāha--punarūpadarśanāt panuḥ smaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Not only having the same object as perception is the basis of the figurative usage, but also having the same operation — so he says: 'From seeing again, from remembering again.'

children.text: pratyakṣamapi hi vipratipatti paribhūya vyāptiviṣayatayā dṛṣṭāntaṃ smārayati--tadvacanamapīti /
children.translated_text: For even perception, overcoming disagreement, recalls the example as having <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) as its object — 'the statement [of the reason] too [does so].'

children.text: aparamapi bījamāha--mūlabhūteti //
children.translated_text: He states another basis: 'Being fundamental...'

children.text: nanu yathā śabdatadarthayorūpanaye vārtāpi nāsti, tat kathamāha---yathā tatheti? ata āha---upanayo hīti /
children.translated_text: Now, just as in the case of the application (<s>upanaya</s>) of verbal testimony and its meaning, there is not even a discussion [of it as a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>] — so how can he say 'just as, so too'? — therefore he says: 'For the application indeed...'

children.text: yadyapi nigamane 'pi pramāṇaviśeṣasamāveśo 'styeva, tathāpi jātyabhiprāyeṇāyaṃ vivakṣitaḥ, na ca tatra catuṣṭavijātīyaṃ pramāṇamastītyatastadvyākhyānāt pūrvameva paramatvopapādanāya samastapramāṇaviniveśanamāha---so 'yamiti //
children.translated_text: Although in the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) too there is indeed the inclusion of a particular <s>pramāṇa</s>, nevertheless this [particular point about application] is intended with reference to the generic [type of <s>pramāṇa</s>], and since no <s>pramāṇa</s> of a kind different from the four [recognized <s>pramāṇas</s>] exists therein — therefore, prior to explaining that, he introduces the inclusion of all <s>pramāṇas</s> [within the four] for the purpose of establishing [their] supremacy: 'This very...'

children.text:
mūlasamavāyābhāvādaupacārikaḥ samavāyo bhaviṣyatītyata uktam--pramāṇānāṃ veti /
adhyāropo viniveśanaṃ vā bhrāntirvā na saṃbhavatītyata āha--adhyāropa iti /
samārthya hīti /
dharmaḥ kāraṇatvalakṣaṇaḥ /
tadanena kiṃ punaḥ samarthyamiti pṛcchato 'bhisandhiḥ darśitaḥ /
uttarābhisandhimāha--iha tviti /
sāmarthyākāṅkṣayoḥ parasparavyāpterākāṅkṣaiva sāmarthyaśabdeneha vivakṣitetyarthaḥ /
tadevarūpayoḥ samavāyasāmarthyayoḥ pradarśanena phalaṃ darśayati--tadatreti /
prayojanābhede 'pyākāṅkṣāvirahitatvāt vākyaikavākyatvaṃ na bhavati /
yathā---
children.translated_text: Since there is no fundamental inherence [between the five members and the <s>pramāṇas</s>], the inherence will be figurative — therefore it is said: 'of <s>pramāṇas</s>...' Superimposition is inclusion, or error, which is not possible — therefore he says: 'superimposition...' 'Due to capacity' — the property characterized by causality. By this, the intention of the one who asks 'what further is the capacity?' is shown. He states the counter-intention: 'But here...' The meaning is: since the capacity and the expectancy mutually pervade each other, what is intended here by the word 'capacity' is just the expectancy. By the demonstration of both — inherence and capacity — which are of such a nature, he shows the fruit: 'There, in that case...' Even when there is no difference in purpose, sentence-unity does not obtain due to the absence of expectancy. For example:

children.text: bhago vāṃ vibhajatu, pūṣā vāṃ vibhajata, aryamā vāṃ vibhajatu ityādi /
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Bhaga</s> distribute to you, may <s>Pūṣan</s> distribute to you, may <s>Aryaman</s> distribute to you' — and so forth.

children.text: ata uktaṃ vibhajyamāneti /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is said: 'being distributed...'

children.text: ākāḍkṣāyāmapi prayojanānakatve vākyaikavākyatvaṃ na bhavati //
children.translated_text: Even when there is expectancy, if there is no unity of purpose, sentence-unity does not obtain.

children.text: yathā---
children.translated_text: For example:

children.text:
syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghutasya dhārayā suśevaṃ kalpayāmi ityādi /
ata uktamekaṃ prayojanamiti /
tadenena,
children.translated_text: 'I make a comfortable seat for you; with a stream of ghee I make [it] pleasant' — and so forth. Therefore it is said: 'a single purpose.' By this, then,

children.text: arthaikatvādekaṃ vākyaṃ sākāḍkṣaṃ cedvibhāge syāt
children.translated_text: 'A single sentence [is constituted] by unity of meaning; if [there is] expectancy, it would [also apply] in separation' —

children.text:
iti jaiminīya vākyaikavākyatālakṣaṇamabhimatam /
nanu yadi vipratipannaḥ vākyenaiva paraḥ pratibodhayituṃ śakyate, atha vākye tadarthe vā vipratipadyamānaḥ kenopāyena bodhanīyaḥ? vākyāntareṇa cedanavasthetyata āha--yadyapīti /
ananyathāsiddhapratyakṣāgamāgocarābhiprāyametadityarthaḥ /
vikalpaḥ anuvādaviśeṣaḥ /
tasya prayojanaṃ vidhiḥ pratiṣedho vā? atra cākṣepāvasare pratiṣadha eva, viśeṣapratipādakatvamiti vadatā tattvavyavasthāśrayatvaṃ vivṛtam, tatra tattvaṃ viśeṣaḥ /
tasya pratipattirvyavasthā /
children.translated_text: The apprehension of that [reality] is the determination (<s>vyavasthā</s>).

children.text: taddhetutvam āśrayatvam /
children.translated_text: Being the cause of that [determination] is the basis-character (<s>āśrayatva</s>).

children.text: tatra viśeṣaḥ ka ityata uktama--dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmoti /
children.translated_text: What is the specific therein? — therefore it is said: 'a property distinguished by a property.'

children.text: vākyāddhi sādhanadharmaviśiṣṭo dharmo sākṣāt pratīyate sādhyarūpadharmaviśiṣṭastu taddvāretyubhayamapi vivakṣitvā saṃmugdhamuktamiti //
children.translated_text: For from a sentence, the property qualified by the proving property (<s>sādhana</s>) is directly apprehended, while [the property] qualified by the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) [is apprehended] through that [proving property] — intending both, [the author] has stated it in a conflated manner.

the <s>Jaiminīya</s> definition of sentence and sentence-unity is accepted. Now, if one who disagrees can be made to understand by the sentence itself, but if he disagrees about the sentence or its meaning, by what means is he to be made to understand? If by another sentence, there would be infinite regress — therefore he says: 'Even if...' The meaning is: this is intended with reference to what is not the domain of perception and scripture, which are not otherwise established. '<s>Vikalpa</s>' (alternative) is a particular kind of restatement. Is its purpose a positive injunction or a prohibition? Here, at the juncture of objection, it is precisely a prohibition. By saying 'it presents the specific,' what is explained is its character of being the basis for the determination of reality. Therein, reality is the specific.

children.text: nanu pramāṇāntaratve 'pi tarkasya pramāṇapadena saṃgraha eva sāmānyena viśeṣasya saṃkalanāt, tat kimityāha--na
children.translated_text: Now, even if <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>, it should be subsumed under the term '<s>pramāṇa</s>' since the particular is subsumed by the general. So why does he say: 'not

children.text:
pramāṇāntaramiti? ata āha--pramāṇapadena hīti dṛṣṭo hi sāmānyaśabdenāpi kasyacidasaṃgrahaḥ kutaścit kāraṇādityabhisandhiḥ /
ata eva pramāṇāntaratvaśaḍkāyāṃ saṃgṛhītebhyo viśeṣebhyo 'nyatvamuktvā prameyaṃ dṛṣṭāntatvenopāttam /
aniśrvāyakatvāt /
svātantryeṇeti śeṣaḥ /
kiṃ tu pramāṇaviṣayavibhāgahetutayeti /
yasya
children.translated_text: a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>'? — therefore he says: 'For by the term <s>pramāṇa</s>...' The intention is: it is observed that even by a general term, something is sometimes not included, for some reason. For this very reason, when the suspicion of being a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> arises, having stated its difference from the included particulars, <s>prameya</s> (the object of knowledge) is cited as an example. Because it is not determinative [on its own] — the completion is: independently. But rather, because of being the cause of the distinction of the domain of <s>pramāṇa</s>. Of whichever

children.text:
pramāṇasyeyamitikartavyatā tadīyaviṣaye tadapekṣatvādityarthaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, tarko hi pramārūpaṃ vā pramāṇaṃ syāt liṅgadarśanavat, apramārūpaṃ vā indriyādivat /
na tāvadādyaḥ, tasyāhāryāroparūpatvāt /
ata eva na tatkaraṇasyāpi prāmāṇyamapramāphalatvāt /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, svaviṣayavyāpyaviṣaryaye hyasya prāmāṇyamāśāḍrikatam /
tena ca nāsya niyāmakaḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
asaṃbaddhasya gamakatve 'tiprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: If what is unrelated were indicative, there would be over-extension.

children.text: tadviparyayasya tu tena saha svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandho 'sti /
children.translated_text: But the opposite of that [i.e., the object of <s>tarka</s>] does have a natural relation with it.

children.text: tena tatsaṃvalitasya pravṛttestaditikartavyatātvameva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [<s>tarka</s>] combined with the opposite [i.e., the absurd consequence] has precisely the character of a requisite procedure for the activity [of the <s>pramāṇa</s>].

children.text: na hi viparyayāparyavasitaṃ kvacidapi kṛtārthaṃ prasaṅgamīkṣāmahe //
children.translated_text: For we never see a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) that does not culminate in the opposite [of the absurd consequence] as achieving its purpose anywhere.

<s>pramāṇa</s> this is the requisite procedure — [<s>tarka</s> pertains] to the domain of that [<s>pramāṇa</s>], because of depending on it — that is the meaning. What is being said is this: <s>tarka</s> is either a <s>pramāṇa</s> in the form of <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), like the observation of the mark, or a <s>pramāṇa</s> not in the form of <s>pramā</s>, like the sense-faculties and the like. Not the first, because it has the form of a deliberate superimposition (<s>āhāryāropa</s>). For that very reason, even its instrument does not have the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, since its result is not <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition). Nor the second, because its <s>prāmāṇya</s> (validity) is hoped for with respect to what is pervaded by its own object. And there is no determining relation of that [<s>tarka</s>] with that [pervaded object].

children.text:
nanvevaṃ tarhi pramāṇasyāpi kevalasya na kvacidapi kṛtārthatvam /
tathā ca sati prasaṅgatadviparyayapiṇḍa eva pramāṇyaṃ paryavasyet /
evametat, setikartavyatākasyaiva sarvatra karaṇatvāt /
itikartavyatātadvadbhāvakalpanāyāṃ tvayaṃ vibhāgaḥ /
tadidaṃ vakṣyati--tasya prasaṅgarūpatayā pāratantryeṇa svayamasādhākatvāditi /
prasaṃjanīyasya pramāṇaviruddhatvenāniṣṭatvamayuktatvam /
sādhanīyasya pramāṇāviruddhatveneṣṭatvaṃ yuktatvam, tenāyamartho vārttikasya, yadyevaṃ nābhaviṣyat tadaivaṃ yuktatvamahāsyat, idaṃ cāyuktatvamupādāsyatetyata āha--itikāreṇeti /
tataḥ
children.translated_text: Now, if so, then even the <s>pramāṇa</s> alone does not achieve its purpose anywhere. And if that is the case, validity would culminate in the aggregate of <s>prasaṅga</s> and its opposite alone. Just so — because it is the aggregate with its requisite procedure that is the instrument everywhere. But in the attribution of the status of requisite procedure to [<s>tarka</s>] or of possessing [that requisite procedure], this distinction [arises]. This is what he will say: 'Because of its having the form of <s>prasaṅga</s>, due to its dependence, and because it itself is not a prover.' The <s>prasajyamāna</s> (what is to be deduced) is undesirable and unreasonable because of contradicting the <s>pramāṇa</s>. The <s>sādhanīya</s> (what is to be established) is desirable and reasonable because of not contradicting the <s>pramāṇa</s>. Thus, the meaning of the <s>Vārttika</s> is: if this were not so, then this reasonableness would be lost, and this unreasonableness would be adopted — therefore he says: 'by the word <s>iti</s>.' From that,

children.text:
prasaṅgārūpavyutpādanasaya vārttikena avirodhaḥ /
bhāṣyaṃ tu prasaṃge sphuṭameva /
nanu bhavatīti pramāṇavyāpārāt prāgeva yadi niścitam, tadā tarkaḥ pramāṇameva syādityata āha-- saṃbhavatīti /
saṃbhāvanā cehāvirodhamātram, na tu saṃśayaḥ,
children.translated_text: the <s>Vārttika</s> is not contradicted by the elucidation of the non-<s>prasaṅga</s> form [of <s>tarka</s>]. The <s>Bhāṣya</s>, however, is quite clear regarding <s>prasaṅga</s>. Now, if 'it is so' [i.e., the conclusion] is already determined even prior to the operation of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, then <s>tarka</s> would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> itself — therefore he says: 'is possible.' And what is meant by 'possibility' here is merely non-contradiction, not doubt,

children.text:
ayuktāṃśasyāpi saṃśayāspadatvāt /
anujñā ceyameva yat pravartamānapramāṇānukūlatvenāvasthānam /
tadāha--etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
anujānan tadviruddhadharmavyudāsarūpeṇāvirodhayannityarthaḥ /
anugṛhṇāti savyāpārīkarotītyarthaḥ /
tadviṣayapramāṇānukūlyena tarkasyāpi tadviṣayatvamiti bhrāntimāśaḍkya nirākaroti--na ceti /
pāratantryeṇa viparyayaparatantratayetyarthaḥ /
āroparūpatāmupadarśamanneva svaviṣayadvārāpyasya prāmāṇyaṃ nirācaṣṭe--asti hīti /
na prasaḍgo heturna prasajyamāno
children.translated_text: because even the unreasonable aspect can be the locus of doubt. And this 'permission' is nothing but the standing in conformity with the operating <s>pramāṇa</s>. So he says: 'What is being said is this.' The meaning is: the one who permits, [also] makes compatible by the removal of the contrary property, [and thus] removes [the obstacle]. 'Assists' means 'makes operative' — that is the meaning. Anticipating the error that, because of the conformity of <s>tarka</s> with the <s>pramāṇa</s> that has that [object] as its domain, <s>tarka</s> too has that [object] as its domain, he refutes: 'Nor...' 'Due to dependence' means 'due to dependence on the opposite' — that is the meaning. While showing its nature as superimposition, he also denies its validity even through its own object: 'For indeed...' '<s>Prasaṅga</s> is not a reason, the reason that is to be deduced is not a mark' — the meaning is: because of being unestablished.

children.text:
heturliṅgamasiddhatvādityarthaḥ /
nanu na hi yadeva vidyate tadeva dṛśyata ityasti niyama ityata āha--tena saheti /
tasmāt nāstīti phaladvāreṇa tarkasyānugrāhyaṃ pramāṇaṃ darśitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is shown that the <s>pramāṇa</s> to be assisted by <s>tarka</s> is 'does not exist' — [i.e.,] through its fruit.

children.text: tenānujñāyamānaṃ pramāṇaṃ pravartate phalaṃ sādhayati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>pramāṇa</s>, being permitted [by <s>tarka</s>], operates and establishes the fruit.

children.text: phalamāha-kevalamevedamiti /
children.translated_text: He states the fruit: 'This alone indeed...'

children.text: kaivalyasvarūpavipratipattestad vivṛṇoti--neheti //
children.translated_text: He explains it due to disagreement about the nature of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation): 'Not here...'
Now, there is no rule that only what exists is perceived — therefore he says: 'together with that.'

children.text:
tadevamabhāvaviṣaye pratyakṣe 'pi tarkaṃ darśayatā anupalabdhiliṅgakānumānasya sādhyo 'bhāva iti saugatamatamapāstam /
anupalabdherapi niṣedharūpatayā anumānāntarasādhyatāyām anavasthānāt, asiddhāyāścāgamakatvāt, pratyakṣatastatsiddhau tvanumānānavakāśāt, vyavahārasyāpi vikalpānugatavyāpārāt pratyakṣata eva saddhitvāt /
anyathā vidhivyavahārārthamapyupalabdhiliṅgakamanumānamāstheyam /
evaṃ ca punarapyanavasthaiva /
na hi liṅgamapyavyavahniyamāṇamevānumitiṃ bhāvayet /
tasmād vidhivyavahāravanniṣedhavyavahāro 'pi pratyakṣasiddha eva /
vipratipannaṃ prati tu parīkṣakaistarkaḥ sahāyatvenopaneya iti ramaṇīyam /
āgamasahāyaṃ tarkamāha--evaṃ svargeti /
yajetetyatra samānapadopāttatvād bhāvyatvācca dhātvarthaḥ sādhyo bhavatu, bhavatu, vā puruṣārthatvāt svarga iti saṃśaye tarkasyāvatāraḥ /
yadi sādhyo dhātvarthaḥ syāt, tadopadeṣṭurāptatvaṃ vidheśceṣṭopāyatvaṃ vākyasya tadabhidhāyakatvaṃ prekṣāvatā ca pravṛttirna syāt /
asti caitat sarvaṃ pramāṇataḥ siddhamityarthaḥ /
anujñāyamānaṃ pramāṇamāha--samānapadeti /
children.translated_text: He states the <s>pramāṇa</s> that is being acknowledged: "Within the same expression..."

children.text: na hi yāgabhāvanāyāḥ svargaphalatve dhātvarthasyātatphalatve samānapadopāttattvabhāvyatvayoḥ kaścid vidodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For if the sacrifice-performance has heaven as its fruit, and the verbal meaning does not have that as its fruit, there is no conflict whatsoever between being taken up within the same expression and being something to be brought about.

children.text: tasmāt tadavirodhena svargaphalatvaṃ yuktam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having heaven as the fruit is consistent without conflicting with those [two properties].

children.text: dhātvarthasya ca sādhyatvaṃ viruddhatayā ayuktamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the to-be-accomplished nature of the verbal meaning is inconsistent as contradictory — that is the meaning.

Thus, by showing <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) even in the case of perception whose object is absence, the Buddhist view that absence is provable by inference based on the mark of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) has been set aside. For since non-apprehension itself, being of the nature of negation, would require proof by yet another inference, there would be an infinite regress; and because an unestablished [non-apprehension] cannot serve as a probative mark; and because when it is established through perception, there is no room for inference; and because even conventional practice, having its operation accompanied by conceptual construction, is established through perception alone. Otherwise, one would have to resort to inference based on the mark of apprehension even for positive conventional practice. And thus again there would be an infinite regress. For even the inferential mark, unless it is itself apprehended through conventional practice, would not generate an inferential cognition. Therefore, just like positive conventional practice, negative conventional practice too is established through perception alone. But for one who is in disagreement, examiners may employ <s>tarka</s> as an auxiliary — this is the pleasing [conclusion]. He states <s>tarka</s> that has scripture as its auxiliary: "Thus, heaven..." In [the injunction] "One should sacrifice," there is a doubt whether the verbal meaning is what is to be accomplished — because it is taken up within the same expression and because it is something to be brought about — or whether it is heaven, because it is the purpose of man. [It is at] this [point that] <s>tarka</s> enters. If the verbal meaning were what is to be accomplished, then the trustworthiness of the teacher, the injunction being a means to what is desired, the sentence being a statement of that [means], and the activity of a rational person — none of these would obtain. But all this is established through valid means of knowledge — that is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu pramāṇānugrahāya yuktatvāyuktatve vivecayati tarko na tu niścinoti iti kuto viśeṣādityata āha--na ceti /
kriyātipattiriti, kriyātipattiḥ pratyayopasthāpite ghaṭasattvadhātvarthasādhyatve eva kriyātipattiśabdena vivakṣite, na hyevaṃbhūtapratyayāviṣayo ghaṭo vā sādhyatayā dhātvartho vāstītyarthaḥ /
kimato yadyevamityata āha--yadāśrayeti /
yasminnāśraye tulyopalambhayogyatvena duḥkhatvena vā aniṣṭaprasaṃjakena hetunā upapannastarko yuktāyuktaviṣayaviścayasādhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, <s>tarka</s> discriminates consistency and inconsistency in aid of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, but does not determine [the matter] — whence the distinction? — therefore he says: "Nor..." "Overreach of action" — when the to-be-accomplished nature of the verbal meaning pertaining to the existence of the pot and so on is presented by the suffix [as the meaning], it is expressed by the word "overreach of action"; for there is no pot that falls outside the scope of such a suffix, nor is the verbal meaning to-be-accomplished in that way — that is the meaning. What of it, if this is so? — therefore he says: "That upon which it rests..." In that substratum upon which <s>tarka</s>, supported by a reason that is equally available for apprehension or is of the nature of undesirableness, is well-founded — [<s>tarka</s> as] a means for determining what is consistent and inconsistent —

children.text: bhaviṣyati sa eva nāstītyarthaḥ /
tadanena prasajyamānasyāśrayāsiddhisādhanāsiddhī dirśite, pūrvaṃ tu svarūpāsiddhirdarśitā /
children.translated_text: By this, the unestablished-substratum (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) and the unestablished-proof (<s>sādhanāsiddhi</s>) of what would follow have been shown; previously, [only] the unestablished-own-form (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>) was shown.

children.text: tasmādāropatvānna svaviṣaye pramāṇaṃ svaviṣayavyāpyaviparyaye niyāmakābhāvācca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, being a superimposition, [<s>tarka</s>] is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding its own object, and because there is no determining factor for the contradictory of what is pervaded by its own object.

children.text: niyatasaṃbaddhasvaviṣaye viparyayāpekṣitve tu pāratantryāt na pramāṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But if, regarding what is invariably connected with its own object, [<s>tarka</s>] were to depend on the contradictory, then due to dependence [on something else] it would not be a <s>pramāṇa</s> — that is the meaning.

children.text: tarhi kvāsyopayoga ityata āha--niśrayāya tviti //
children.translated_text: Then where is its use? — therefore he says: "But for determination..."
that very [substratum] does not exist — that is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu tarkapramāṇayorabhimataṃ bhedaṃ mīmāṃsāyā vedādabhedavādo virūṇaddhītyata āha--pramāṇeti /
atha yathāśruta eva
children.translated_text: Now, the accepted distinction between <s>tarka</s> and <s>pramāṇa</s> — the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> doctrine of non-difference of the Veda conflicts with it — therefore he says: "<s>Pramāṇa</s>..." Now, why does the meaning of the <s>vārttika</s> not stand as literally read?

children.text:
vārttikārthaḥ kāsmānna bhavatītyata āha--itikarttavyatātvaṃ cetyādinā /
nikāyaviśiṣṭābhiḥ rityasya vyākhyānasya
children.translated_text: — therefore he says with "The character of being a means-to-be-done" and so forth. Of the explanation [belonging to] a tradition distinguished by a [particular] school,

children.text: śarīrendriyāṇāṃ śukraśoṇitāderāhārādibhūtakāryatvāt, tatkāryatvācca buddhivedanayornimittāntare pramāṇaṃ nāstīti tātparyam /
children.translated_text: the import is: since the body and the sense-organs are effects of material causes such as semen, blood, food and the like, and since cognition and sensation are effects of those [bodily elements], there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for any other cause.

children.text: vicitranimittatve sādhye bhedavatvāditi hetuḥ svarūpābhiprāyeṇānaikāntikaḥ syāt svarūpabhedavatāmapi ghaṭādīnāmavicitranimittatvādataḥ prakārabhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe---vicitratvādityartha iti /
children.translated_text: When diversity of causes is to be proved, the reason "because of possessing distinctions" would be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) if intended in terms of own-form, since even pots and the like, which possess distinctions of own-form, do not have diverse causes. Therefore he explains it as intended in terms of mode: "The meaning is: because of diversity..."

children.text: vaicitryeṇotpādādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because of arising with diversity.

children.text:
nanu nimittavaicitryamātraprasādhane siddhasādhanam, na hi nimittaṃ kiścid vicitram astītyetāvataiva dharmādharmasiddhiḥ, dharmādharmalakṣaṇavicitranimittasādhanena tu nānvayo na vyatireka ityata āha--pramāṇamuktveti /
nimittasya vaicitrye janmano vaivitryagrasaṅgaḥ nimittasyāvaicitrye janmano 'vaicitryaprasaṅgaḥ /
yāgādīnāmeva nimittatve niranvayapradhvastāt kāryotpattiprasaṃgaḥ /
nimittasya nityatve kāryasya sadātanatvaprasaṃgaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the cause were permanent, there would follow the consequence of the effect being perpetual.

children.text: anekadravyatve 'bhyudayasādhāraṇatvaprasaṃgaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [the cause consisted of] multiple substances, there would follow the consequence of prosperity being common [to all].

children.text: sādhāraṇaikadravyatve 'pi eva doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if [the cause were] a common single substance, there would be the same fault.

children.text: emistarkaiḥ pakṣadharmatāmupajīvya pravṛttairanugṛhyamāṇaṃ sāmānyavyāptibalapravṛttaṃ vaicitryānumānaṃ viśeṣavirodhaṃ paribhūyābhimataṃ viśeṣaṃ sādhayatītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the inference of diversity, operating by the force of general pervasion and supported by these <s>tarkas</s> (reasonings) that proceed by establishing the property-of-the-thesis, overrides the specific contradiction and establishes the desired specific [conclusion].

Now, in merely establishing the diversity of the cause, it would be proving what is already proved. For the establishment of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> does not follow merely from the fact that some cause is diverse. But in proving a diverse cause of the nature of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, there would be neither positive nor negative concomitance — therefore he says: "Having stated the <s>pramāṇa</s>..." If the cause is diverse, there follows the diversity of birth; if the cause is not diverse, there follows the non-diversity of birth. If sacrifice and the like alone were the cause, there would follow the consequence of the production of effects from what has been completely annihilated without trace.

children.text: nanu jātyā kiṃ phalanirṇayo nāstyeva, yena kālaviśeṣaṃ pṛcchati kadā punarityato 'bhiprāyamāha--syādetaditi /
children.translated_text: Now, is it that the determination of the fruit does not exist at all according to the genus [of action], such that [the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>] asks about a particular time: "When then?" — therefore he states the intention: "This would be so..."

children.text: nanu nirṇayopādānaprayojane vaktavye nirṇītaprayojanasya tarkasya punarāvṛttau kiṃ tātparyamityata āha--saṃkalayyeti /
children.translated_text: Now, when the purpose of introducing determination is to be stated, what is the import of repeating <s>tarka</s> whose purpose has been determined? — therefore he says: "By collating..." The meaning is: the inseparability of the two is intended through collation.

children.text: saṃkalanayā ubhayoravinābhāvo vivakṣita ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the inseparability of both [<s>tarka</s> and <s>nirṇaya</s>] is what is intended.

children.text:
svasiddhāntānurūpaṃ sādhanaṃ dūpaṇaṃ cāhaturiti svādhyaparasādhyayoryathāsaṃkhyam /
nanu yadyapi sarvatra jalpe nirṇayāvasānatvameva nāsti kvacidanirṇaye 'pi puruṣāparādhataḥ kathāvicchedāt, tathāpi yatra nirṇayāvasānatvamasti, na tato jalpādanyatarādhikaraṇanirṇayāvasānatvena vādo vyavacchetuṃ śakyate /
na ca sarvavādavyāptiḥ, nirṇayasya vādaphalatvāt /
phalasya copāyāvyāpakatvādityata āha--vāde hīti /
nirṇayā vasānatā hi tadyogyatā abhipretā /
sā ca vivadamānayoḥ tattvabubhutsutayā tamuddhiśya pravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [fitness] is the activity of the two disputants directed toward [the goal], by virtue of their desire to know the truth.

children.text: tadidamuktam, tatvabubhutsorvādinorvāde 'dhikārāditi /
children.translated_text: This is what has been stated: "Because of the authority of the two debaters who desire to know the truth in debate."

children.text: tadayamarthaḥ, tattvanirṇayamuddhiśya tayoḥ sādhanadūṣaṇavacanasaṃdarbho vāda iti /
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: the composition of statements of proof and refutation by those two, directed toward the determination of truth, is <s>vāda</s> (debate).

children.text: evaṃ ca nāvyāptirna vā atiprasaṅgaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus there is neither under-extension nor over-extension.

"They state a proof conforming to their own <s>siddhānta</s> and a refutation" — [this applies] respectively to one's own thesis and the opponent's thesis. Now, although it is true that in every debate resolution through determination does not always occur — in some cases, even without determination, the discussion is broken off due to the fault of a person — nevertheless, where resolution through determination does obtain, debate (<s>vāda</s>) cannot be distinguished from <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) merely by being resolved through the determination of one side. Nor is there universal pervasion of all debate, since determination is the fruit of debate, and the fruit does not pervade the means — therefore he says: "For in debate..." For resolution through determination here means the fitness for that.

children.text:
jalpaḥ punaḥ kīdṛśa ityata āha--jalpe tviti /
puruṣaśaktītyuddeśyamāha /
tadayamarthaḥ, bhavatu nāma kvacita jalpato 'pi tattvanirṇayaḥ /
tathāpi nāsāvaddeśyo na ca śraddheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, that is neither the intended [purpose] nor to be relied upon.

children.text: svaśaktiparāśaktikhyāpanamātramuddeśyamiti /
children.translated_text: The intended [purpose] is merely the display of one's own power and [the exposure of] the other's weakness.

children.text: tasmādanyataranirṇayāvasānatveneti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, "by virtue of resolution through the determination of one side..."

children.text: nirṇayāvasānābhiprāyeṇetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: "with the intention of resolution through determination."

What then is <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) like? — therefore he says: "But in <s>jalpa</s>..." He states what is intended as the purpose: "The power of the person." The meaning of this is: let there indeed be determination of truth sometimes even for one engaged in <s>jalpa</s>.

children.text: nanu jalpavitaṇḍayorvādaviśeṣatve kathaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ parisaṃkhyāsamabhivyāhāraḥ, kathaṃ ca parasparaviruddhayoḥ sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvo 'pītyata āha--viśiṣyete iti /
children.translated_text: Now, if <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) are species of <s>vāda</s> (debate), how can there be the co-statement of a genus and its species in an enumeration, and how can there be a genus-species relation between mutually contradictory [items]? — therefore he says: "They are distinguished..."

children.text: aparamapi bhedahetumāha--vādāt jalpavitaṇḍayoriti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: He states yet another cause of distinction: the completion being "of <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> from <s>vāda</s>."

children.text: pūrvaṃ vādavyākhyānāvasare bhede heturuddeśyaviśeṣābhisandhiruktaḥ tadapekṣayā aparamapīti /
children.translated_text: Previously, on the occasion of explaining <s>vāda</s>, the cause of distinction stated was the specific intention of purpose; relative to that, [he says] "another also."

children.text: yau tau vādajalpayoḥ prayoktātau tāvekatrāvijigīṣayā anyatra vijigīṣayā viśeṣitau vādajalpau parasparato vyavacchindāte ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: those two [kinds of] practitioners — one in <s>vāda</s> and one in <s>jalpa</s> — being characterized in one case by non-desire-to-win and in the other by desire-to-win, <s>vāda</s> and <s>jalpa</s> are mutually distinguished.

children.text:
dūṣayitum ekadeśivyākhyānaṃ tanmatena vyācaṣṭe iti yojyam /
ubhayathāpyanaikāntikatvāditi /
yadyapi vyabhicārādarśane 'pi avinābhāvo na sidhyati pṛthagabhidhānasya puruṣecchādhīnatvāt, vāde codanīyatvasya cānudbhāvane tattvapratipattivyāghātahetutvaprayuktatvāt, tathāpi vyabhicārasya sphuṭatvāt sa eva darśitaḥ /
tasmād vāde codanīyā bhaviṣyantītyanena pṛthagabhidhānaprayojanamātraṃ pratipāditam /
hetutvaṃ punaravivarkṣitameva tārkikaṃmanyenaikadeśinā āropitāmityarthaḥ /
nanvevaṃrūpaprayojanalābho 'pi katham? na hi pṛthagabhidhānamātramatrapramāṇayituṃ śakyamityata āha---sāmānyeneti /
sāmānyo 'bhihitaṃ viśeṣato 'bhidadhatā sūtrakṛtā prayojanaviśeṣaḥ sūcitaḥ /
sa eva bhāṣyakṛtā darśita ityarthaḥ /
atha yadyetadeva vivakṣitamasya sūtrakṛtaḥ, tadā kimiti na kvacit śāstrapradeśe svayameva darśitavānityata āha--etāvāneveti /
atha bhāṣyakāreṇa kathamidamunnītamityata āha--tatreti /
kimevamapīti /
kimanena pratipāditena phalamityarthaḥ /
nanvagrevāde codanīyatvameva pratipādayati, iha tu vidyāprasthānabhedajñāpanārthatvaṃ varṇayati /
tat kuto na virodha ityata āha--vādajalpavitaṇḍā ityādi /
atraivārthe sūcakaṃ vārttikamāha--ata eveti /
ayamarthaḥ /
yadi vidyāśabdenāsya vādādayo na vivakṣitāḥ kathamagre vādavyāpāraṃ darśayitvā jalpavitaṇḍayoḥ sarvāṇyeva nigrahasthānāni vyāpāratvenāha? tad yadayameva brūte nūnamayamasyārtho vivakṣita iti /
tadayaṃ tātparyasaṃkṣapaṃḥ, na tāvadajñātasvarūpa vadajñātavyāpāraphalabhedā vādādayaścetanenādhiṣṭātuṃ śakyante /
na cānadhiṣṭhibhyaḥ phalasiddhiḥ /
tasmāt svarūpavad vyāpāraphalabheda apyamīṣāṃ pratipādanīyā bhavanti /
ata eva caturthe phalamapi darśayiṣyati
children.translated_text: It should be construed thus: in order to refute [the view], he explains the partial-view interpretation according to that doctrine. "Because of inconclusiveness in both ways" — although even when no deviation is observed, inseparable connection is not established, because the separate statement [of items] is dependent on the will of the person; and because in debate, the reason for [items] being censurable is precisely that their non-elicitation would cause obstruction to the apprehension of truth — nevertheless, since the deviation is manifest, that alone has been shown. Therefore, by "they will be censurable in debate," merely the purpose of separate statement has been conveyed. But the reason-hood was not at all intended — [it was] superimposed by an opponent who holds a partial view, thinking [it was the <s>tārkikas</s>' view] — that is the meaning. Now, how is even this gain of purpose [achieved]? For mere separate statement cannot be made authoritative here — therefore he says: "By the general..." The purpose-specific was indicated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> who states specifically what was stated generally. That same [purpose] was shown by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> — that is the meaning. Now, if this alone is what the <s>sūtrakāra</s> intended, then why did he not show it himself somewhere in the <s>śāstra</s>? — therefore he says: "Just this much..." Now, how was this brought out by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>? — therefore he says: "There..." "What even so?" — the meaning is: what is the fruit of what has been established by this? Now, earlier he establishes that they are censurable in debate; but here he describes [their purpose] as making known the distinction of branches of knowledge. Whence then is there no contradiction? — therefore he says: "<s>Vāda</s>, <s>jalpa</s>, <s>vitaṇḍā</s>..." and so forth. He states the <s>vārttika</s> that serves as an indicator of this very point: "For this very reason..." The meaning is this: if by the word "discipline" (<s>vidyā</s>) <s>vāda</s> and the like are not intended, then how is it that, having shown the operation of <s>vāda</s> further on, he states all the <s>nigrahasthānas</s> (points of defeat) as the operation of <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s>? Since this is precisely what he says, surely this is the intended meaning. Here then is the summary of the import: first, <s>vāda</s> and the like, whose own form, operation, and fruit-distinctions are unknown, cannot be presided over by this [discipline]. And without presiding [over them], there is no attainment of fruit. Therefore, like their own form, the distinctions of operation and fruit of these [<s>vāda</s> etc.] must also be taught. For this very reason, in the fourth [section] the <s>sūtrakāra</s> will also show the fruit —

children.text: sūtrakāraḥ //
children.translated_text: [this is what] the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> [intends].

children.text:
prayujyeran saṃbhāvyeranniti /
na tu teṣāmasti saṃbhavati prayoga iti /
nanu lakṣaṇena padārthasvarūpaṃ na vyavasthāpyate, api tu vyavasthitaṃ jñāpyate, tat kuto lakṣaṇatantrtvamityata āha--lakṣyata iti lakṣaṇamiti /
nanu yadi pṛthagabhidhānenaiva vāde codanīyatvaṃ pratipādyate, kathaṃ nyūnādhikāpasiddhāntānāṃ pṛthaganabhidhāne tatra codanīyatvapratipattiḥ? athānyathāpi teṣāṃ tad gamyata eva tadā hetvābhāseṣvapi sa eva prakāro 'sta, kṛtaṃ pṛthagabhidhānenetyata āha--hetvābhāsānāṃ ceti /
ayamāśayaḥ /
na hi hetvābhāsāḥ pṛthagabhihitā ityeva vāde codanīyatvaṃ teṣāṃ gamyate /
api tu vādasya tattvapratipitsukathātvāt, hetvābhāsānāṃ cānudbhāvane tattvapratipattivyāghātāt tattvabubhutsunā avaśyamudbhāvanīyāste /
anyathā vādo vādatvaṃ jahyāt /
hetvābhāsānāṃ cānudbhāvanaṃ tattvapratipattivyāghātakamiti /
ayameva ca nyāyo viśeṣataḥ pṛthagabhidhānena sūcitaḥ sūtrakāreṇa /
sa ca nyūnādiṣu
children.translated_text: "They would be employed" — [meaning] they would be possible. Not that their employment exists [independently]. Now, the definition does not establish the own-form of a category; rather, it makes known what is [already] established. Then whence the dependence on the definition? — therefore he says: "That by which [something] is defined is the definition." Now, if censurability in debate is conveyed by separate statement alone, how is there the apprehension of censurability there when the deficient, the excessive, and the contradictory-to-established-doctrine are not separately stated? And if their [censurability] is understood otherwise as well, then the same method applies to <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious marks) too — what need for separate statement? — therefore he says: "And of the <s>hetvābhāsas</s>..." The intention is this: it is not merely because the <s>hetvābhāsas</s> are separately stated that their censurability in debate is understood. Rather, because <s>vāda</s> is a discourse aimed at apprehending truth, and because the non-elicitation of <s>hetvābhāsas</s> would obstruct the apprehension of truth, they must necessarily be elicited by one who desires to know the truth. Otherwise, <s>vāda</s> would lose its character as <s>vāda</s>. And the non-elicitation of <s>hetvābhāsas</s> obstructs the apprehension of truth — this very principle has been specifically indicated by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> through separate statement. And this same principle applies to the deficient and the like

children.text:
samāna iti /
evaṃ ca vyavasthite vārtikakṛto 'pi praśno nāprāstāvika ityāha--tatra pṛcchatīti /
nanu yadi jalpavitaṇḍayostattvapratipādanārthamavatāraḥ kim apratibhādyudbhāvanena? atha na tadarthatvaṃ tayoḥ, kiṃ tadavatāreṇa? na cānyārthatve tayoretacchāstravyutpādyatvamityata āha--sāhaṅkāro hīti /
ahaṅkṛtasya tasya
children.translated_text: equally. And when it is established thus, even the question of the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> is not out of place — he says: "There he asks..." Now, if <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> are introduced for the purpose of teaching the truth, what [need] is there of eliciting non-response and the like? And if those two are not for that purpose, what [need] is there of their introduction? Nor, if they serve a different purpose, are they something to be taught in this <s>śāstra</s> — therefore he says: "For [the debater] with pride..." Of one who is proud,

children.text: tattvapratipatterayogādahaṅkāraśātanamevānayostattvapratipādanārthatvam, taccāpratibhādyudbhāvanaṃ vinā na syāditi tattvaṃ pratipipādayiṣatā kartavyamevedamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: since the apprehension of truth is impossible for him, the very shattering of [his] pride is the purpose-of-teaching-truth of these two [<s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s>]; and that would not be possible without eliciting non-response and the like — therefore one who wishes to teach the truth must indeed do this. That is the meaning.

children.text:
nanuc chalādīnāṃ parijñānaṃ na sākṣānniḥśreyasa upayujyate ātmādivat /
nāpi tadvyavasthānadvārā pramāṇavat /
nāpi nyāyāṅgatayā saṃśayādivat /
children.translated_text: Nor as a component of <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning), as do doubt and the like.

children.text: na ca parijñānameva phalam, apuruṣārthatvādityata āha--parijñānasya ca phalamuktamiti /
children.translated_text: Nor is the knowledge itself the result, since it serves no human purpose — to this he says: 'and the result of that knowledge has been stated.'

children.text: tattvapratipatyupāyabhūtakathātrayaparikaraśuddhidvārā tatparijñānaṃ niḥśreyasopayogītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: through the purification of the apparatus of the three kinds of discourse — which are means to the apprehension of truth — that knowledge [of quibble and the like] is conducive to the highest good.

children.text: svayaṃ ca sukaraḥ prayoga iti granthasya pratyakṣasiddhatvāt kimuktaṃ bhavatīti tatsvarūpapraśno 'saṃgata ityataḥ pūrayati--anena bhāṣyeṇeti //
children.translated_text: And 'the application is easy to do by oneself' — since the text is established through direct observation, what has been said? — the question about its nature would be incongruent — therefore he completes [the sense]: 'by this commentary.'

Now, the knowledge of <s>chala</s> (quibble) and the like does not directly serve the attainment of the highest good, as does [knowledge of] the self and the like. Nor does it serve through the determination [of truth], as does <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge).

children.text:
bhāṣye prayojanāntarābhidhānaṃ na sūtrakṛdabhihitaprayojanavirodhi, kiṃ tu tadanuguṇam evetyāśayavān sautraṃ prayojanamanuvadati--sūtrakāreṇeti /
anuguṇatvaṃ tu vyāptipradarśanena /
na hyasti saṃbhavaḥ, puruṣārthaścāpramāṇahetukaśceti /
children.translated_text: The statement of an additional purpose in the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) does not contradict the purpose stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>), but is in harmony with it — with this intention, he restates the purpose from the <s>sūtra</s>: 'by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>.' The harmony is shown through the demonstration of pervasion. For there is no possibility that something could be both a human purpose and not grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text:
tenāyamartho bhāṣyasya, yataḥ sarvaṃ prekṣāvatprayojanamānvīkṣikīvyutpādyapramāṇamūlam, ato niḥśreyasasya paramapuruṣārthasya tanmūlatāyāṃ viparyayaśaḍkaiva nāsti, atanmūlatve puruṣārthatvahāniprasaṃgāditi /
tadidamuktaṃ nāstyeva taditi /
nanu na
children.translated_text: Therefore this is the meaning of the <s>bhāṣya</s>: since every purposive action of a rational being is grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> as elucidated by <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (logic/philosophy), there is simply no room for the suspicion that the highest good, the supreme human purpose, is not grounded in that — since, if it were not so grounded, the absurd consequence would follow that it is not a human purpose. This is what was said: 'there simply is no such [possibility].' Now, not

children.text: tāvaditarāsu pramāṇavyavahāro nāstyeva, taditaravyavahārasyāpyucchedaprasaṃgāt, pramāṇavyavahāra sadbhāve tu kimānvīkṣikyā tatra prakāśayitavyam? tatpramāṇaireva prakāśitattvādityata āha--yadyapīti /
children.translated_text: even in the other [disciplines] is the practice of <s>pramāṇa</s> entirely absent, since there would follow the consequence of the destruction of other practices as well. But if the practice of <s>pramāṇa</s> exists [in them], what does <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> have to illuminate there? Since the truth has already been illuminated by those very <s>pramāṇas</s> — to this he says: 'although.'

children.text: vyutpāditena pramāṇādīnā tatra vyavahārastadvyutpattistvita eva, na tu tata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The practice [of <s>pramāṇa</s>] there is by means of <s>pramāṇas</s> and the like that have been elucidated [by <s>ānvīkṣikī</s>], but the elucidation of those [<s>pramāṇas</s>] is from this [<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>] alone, not from those [other disciplines] — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu praṇetṛśrotrapramāṇopajīvanamānvīkṣikyāmapi samānamato na vidyāntarād viśeṣa ityata āha--na tu pramāṇādīti /
pramāṇopajīvane samāne 'pi yathaitadvyutpādyamupajīvanti tāḥ, naivaṃ tadvyutpādyamiyamapītyarthaḥ /
nanu upajīvakatāsāmye 'pi parasparopajīvyopajīvakabhāvaḥ kva nāma dṛṣṭa ityata āha--yatheti /
pratyakṣādyapi hi svaprāmāṇyavyavasthitaye pramāṇāntaramapekṣate /
anumānamapi svotpattaye /
tathāpi pratyakṣādyevāpekṣyānumānaṃ svaviṣayu pravartate /
na tūpajīvakānumānamapekṣya pratyakṣādi, anumānāntaraṃ tu svaprāmāṇyavyutpādakamapekṣate /
tadapi na tadaiva, kiṃ tu prāgeva ityabhiprāyeṇa vyutpādyasajātīyāpekṣānirākaraṇāyoktam--na pratyakṣādiviṣayamapi tadānīmeveti /
pratyakṣādirūpo viṣayaḥ pratyakṣādiviṣaya iti /
vidyopakaraṇaṃ pramāṇādi /
tasya grahaṇaṃ pramāṇādigrakāśitamarthamitarā vidyāḥ pratipādyante iti vārttikena /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, vārttike pramāṇādigrahaṇaṃ bhāṣyoktavidyāprakāśakatvanirvāhāya /
na tu svātantryeṇa /
ato na virodhaḥ /
tadevaṃ svarūpeṇāpekṣāṃ darśayitvā viṣayagatā apekṣā bhāṣyakṛtā darśitā--upāya iti /
tadvārttikaṃ yojayituṃ vyācaṣṭa--saṃpratīti /
children.translated_text: Now, dependence on the <s>pramāṇas</s> of the founder, the disciple, and the authoritative source is common to <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> too — so there is no distinction from other disciplines — to this he says: 'but not the <s>pramāṇas</s> and the rest.' Although dependence [on <s>pramāṇas</s>] is common, those [other disciplines] depend on what is elucidated by this [<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>], but this [<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>] does not similarly depend on what is elucidated by them — this is the meaning. Now, even given the equality of mutual dependence, where has mutual dependence between what depends on and what is depended upon been seen? To this he says: 'just as.' For even <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the like require another <s>pramāṇa</s> for establishing their own validity. And inference too [requires perception] for its own arising. Nevertheless, inference operates in its own domain by depending on perception and the like. But perception and the like do not depend on inference, which depends on them [for its arising]. Rather, [perception] depends on another inference for establishing its own validity. But even that [inference] does not [operate] simultaneously, but rather beforehand — with this intention, to prevent the denial of dependence on things of the same class, it was said: 'not even what pertains to the domain of perception and the like at that very time.' 'The domain of perception and the like' means: the domain in the form of perception and the like. The instrument of a discipline is the <s>pramāṇa</s> and the like. Its 'grasping' [is expressed] by the <s>vārttika</s>: 'the other disciplines teach the object illuminated by the <s>pramāṇas</s> and the rest.' What is stated amounts to this: the inclusion of '<s>pramāṇas</s> and the rest' in the <s>vārttika</s> is for sustaining the meaning stated in the <s>bhāṣya</s> regarding the illuminating role of the discipline — not independently. Therefore there is no contradiction. Thus, having shown the dependence with respect to [<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>'s] own nature, the dependence with respect to the object was shown by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>: 'means.' To construe that <s>vārttika</s>, he explains: 'now.'

children.text: nanu vidyāntarāṇāṃ śabdātmakatayā pramāṇatvāt tasya ca svapratipādye 'napekṣatvāt, kiṃ tatrānvīkṣikī kariṣyatītyata āha--na hīti /
children.translated_text: Now, since the other disciplines are <s>pramāṇas</s> by virtue of being verbal in nature, and since a <s>pramāṇa</s> does not require [another] for what it teaches, what will <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> do there? To this he says: 'for not.'

children.text: pramāṇasya sataḥ svapratipādye pramāṇāntarāpekṣā nāsti, na tu svetikartavyatābhūtatarkāpekṣāpi /
children.translated_text: A <s>pramāṇa</s>, being such, does not require another <s>pramāṇa</s> for what it teaches — but it does not thereby not require <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) as a necessary auxiliary to itself.

children.text: sa cānvīkṣikīlabhya ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that [<s>tarka</s>] is obtained from <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text:
atha tarkamanapekṣamāṇasya kiṃ syādityata āha--mā bhūditi /
ādigrahaṇena
children.translated_text: Now, what would happen if one does not depend on <s>tarka</s>? To this he says: 'let it not be so.' By the word 'and so forth,'

children.text: yajamānaḥ prastaraḥ
children.translated_text: 'The sacrificer is the <s>prastara</s> (grass bundle)' [— an absurd literal reading] —

children.text:
ityādi grāhyam /
tarkaśca saṃśayamantareṇa nāvataratītyupasaṃhāre so 'pi darśitaḥ /
yadyapi satarkapramāṇapravṛttireva parīkṣā, tathāpīha gobalīvardanyāyena pramāṇasya svapadopāttatvāt prayojanajijñāsātarkā eva vivakṣitāḥ /
pramāṇasya nivaśaḥ pravattiḥ /
tasya dvāramavirodhaḥ /
arthatattvaṃ padārthatattvaṃ vākyārthatattvaṃ vā, avadhārya pramāṇāntarādarthavādādeva vā /
children.translated_text: and so forth should be understood. And since <s>tarka</s> does not arise without doubt, in the conclusion that too has been shown. Although the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> accompanied by <s>tarka</s> is itself examination (<s>parīkṣā</s>), nevertheless, here, by the maxim of the bull-and-ox, since <s>pramāṇa</s> has already been taken up by its own term, only the <s>tarkas</s> pertaining to the inquiry about purpose are intended. The operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> is unrestricted. The door to that is non-contradiction. The truth of things — either the truth of categories or the truth of sentence-meaning — is to be ascertained from another <s>pramāṇa</s>, or from <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) alone.

children.text: tatra trayī vidhiniṣedharūpā niveśanīyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, the three Vedas, having the form of injunction and prohibition, are to be installed — this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ ca daṇḍanītyāṃ yathā yamo rājā kubero vā rājatyādi, vārttāyāṃ māghe parikarṣitā bhūmiḥ suvarṇamayaṃ phalamādhatta ityādi tarkānapekṣayā viphalāyate /
children.translated_text: And thus, in the science of politics (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>), [statements] such as '<s>Yama</s> is king, or <s>Kubera</s> rules,' and so forth, and in economics (<s>vārttā</s>), [statements] such as 'land plowed in the month of <s>Māgha</s> yields golden fruit,' and so forth — these become fruitless without the examination of <s>tarka</s>.

children.text: tasmāt tatrāpi tadapekṣā astītyatidiśati--evamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even there the dependence on it [<s>tarka</s>] exists — he extends [the argument]: 'likewise.'

children.text: viṣayamiti śeṣa ityatrāpi vidheyatayā niṣedhyatayeti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The remainder at 'object' is: 'as what is to be enjoined or as what is to be prohibited.'

children.text:
idānīṃ vyāpāragatāmapekṣāmāha bhāṣyamatena--api ceti /
dravyasya yathā
children.translated_text: Now he states the dependence with respect to operation, according to the view of the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>: 'moreover.' Of a substance (<s>dravya</s>), for example:

children.text: dadhnā juhoti
children.translated_text: 'He offers with curd' —

children.text:
ityādi /
guṇasya yathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of a quality (<s>guṇa</s>), for example:

children.text: arūṇayā somaṃ krīṇāti
children.translated_text: 'He purchases <s>Soma</s> with a reddish-brown [cow]' —

children.text:
ityādi /
karmaṇo yathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of an action (<s>karman</s>), for example:

children.text: vrīhīnavahanti
children.translated_text: 'They thresh the rice' —

children.text:
ityādi /
daṇḍanītyāmapi yathā dravyasya
children.translated_text: and so forth. In the science of politics (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>) too, of a substance, for example:

children.text: svāmyamātya-
children.translated_text: 'The king, the minister —'

children.text:
ityādi /
guṇasya yathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of a quality, for example:

children.text: sāmabheda-
children.translated_text: 'Conciliation, division —'

children.text:
ityādi /
karmaṇo yathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of an action, for example:

children.text: śastraśikṣā gajavājivāhanam
children.translated_text: 'Training in weapons, riding elephants and horses' —

children.text:
ityādi /
vārttāyāmapi dravyasya yathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. In economics (<s>vārttā</s>) too, of a substance, for example:

children.text: yathartu bījaṃ saṃgṛhṇīyāt /
children.translated_text: 'One should collect seeds according to the season' —

children.text:
ityādi /
guṇasya yathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of a quality, for example:

children.text: bhūmiṃ plāvayecchoṣayet /
children.translated_text: 'One should flood the field or dry it' —

children.text:
ityādi /
karmaṇo yathā
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of an action, for example:

children.text: syānāntaraṃ ninīṣannanokahamabhimantrayet /
children.translated_text: 'Wishing to lead [the cattle] to the next pasture, one should consecrate the tree-stump' —

children.text:
ityādi /
viṣayaṃ darśayitvā saṃśayamāha--tatra kimiti /
saṃśayakāraṇaṃ ca vidhipadasamabhivyāhārastatpadasya /
vidhipadasamabhivyāhṛtasvapado hyadhikārī na vidhiviṣayaḥ /
tathābhūtameva cāgnihotraṃ tadviṣayaḥ /
ataḥ sādhye saṃśayaḥ kiṃ vidhipadasamabhivyāhṛtapadatvādagnihotrādivadvidhiviṣayo bhavatu svargo 'dhikārivad vā neti pūrvapakṣamādarśayanneva tatrāniṣṭaprasaṃgamāha--tatra yadīti /
na ca śyenādisādhyāyā hiṃsāyā vihitatvenārthatvameva bhavatu kā kṣatiriti vācyam /
vidhirhi pravartakaḥ svajñānena icchāmantarā kṛtvā prayatyanotpādakaṃ iti yāvat /
sa ca prayatno na sādhyaviṣayaḥ kartuṃ śakyate /
upayo hi prayatnaviṣayo na tu phalam /
tasmāt prayatnaviṣayatvāt sādhanetikartavyate eva vidhīyete na tu sādhyam, tadaviṣayatvāt /
na hi jñāpakatvamātraṃ vidhitvam, api tvicchāprayatnaviṣayajñāpakatvamiti /
tasmāt śyenādisādhyā hiṃsā anarthabhūtaivārthaḥ syād yadi vidhiviṣayaḥ syāditi sādhūktam /
siddhānte pramāṇamādarśayanneva sādhyapadasamabhivyāhārastarhi kvopayujyate ityāśaḍkāmapanayati--atha sādhyāṃśamiti /
