Here too, since the negation-prefix '<s>niḥ</s>' has the sense of the negation of the [preceding] word, and since the word '<s>svabhāva</s>' (intrinsic nature) refers to one or the other of existence and non-existence, the same absurd consequence [applies] as before.

children.text: pratītyagocaratvaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvamiti cet? atra tu svavacanavirodhaḥ, pratītyagocaraśca pratīyate ceti /
children.translated_text: If [one says] '<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>' means not being the object of cognition — here there is a self-contradiction: it is not the object of cognition and yet it is cognized.

children.text: yad yathā pratīyate tat tathā neti cet? atra na vipratipadyāmahe /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'what is cognized in a certain way is not [really] so' — here we do not disagree.

children.text: tasmāt ākārāsadanirvacanīyakhyātivādibhirapyanyathākhyātiravaśyābhyupagantavyet i //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the proponents of <s>ākārāsat</s> (non-existence of the form), <s>anirvacanīyakhyāti</s> (indescribable error), and other [theories of error] must necessarily accept <s>anyathākhyāti</s> (apprehension as other than what [something is]).

just as there is no positive injunction for both, so too there is no prohibition — because the injunction and prohibition [of each of two opposites] are inseparable from the injunction and prohibition of the mutual [injunction and prohibition]. In the second case, there is no damage. For even if a thousand non-ordinary objects are negated, neither the negation of the object of veridical cognition, nor the negation of its explanation, [follows].

children.text: nanu yadyathāsatprakāśate prapañco 'pi tarhi tathaivāstu jātyādikaṃ cetyata āha---yaḥ punariti /
asaccet? asatteyaiva prakāśeta, na pravṛttigocaraḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: If non-existent? Then it would appear as non-existent itself; it would not become the object of activity.

children.text: sattayā cet? nūnaṃ sādṛśyamapyapekṣyam /
children.translated_text: If [it appears] as existent? Then surely similarity must also be required.

children.text: na ca tadasti /
children.translated_text: And that [similarity] does not exist.

children.text: asadṛśasyāpi sattayā prakāśane cātiprasaṅga ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And if even what is dissimilar appears as [existent] through existence, there would be over-extension — that is the meaning.

Now, if what is non-existent appears [as existent], then let the empirical world (<s>prapañca</s>) also be [non-existent but appearing], and so too universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like — therefore he says: 'But he who...'

children.text:
saṃvidviruddham vicāryasaṃvidviruddham /
sarvasarvajñatāpattiratītānāgatābhijñatāpattiścetyapi draṣṭavyam /
pratibhāsamānaṃ yudallikhadvijñānaṃ jāyata ityarthaḥ /
autsargikakāryānukūlasahakāryabhiprāyeṇa śyāmākavījam udāhṛtam /
tatpratirodhikāraṇāntarasāhityābhiprāyeṇa kṛṭajabījamiti /
vivādadhyāsite vibhrame pravṛttikāraṇamagraho vā syāt, idamiti jñānaṃ vā, rajatamiti jñānasahitaṃ vā, bhedāgrahasahitaṃ vā ubhayamiti? tatrādye na tāvadityādi dūpaṇam /
dvitīye tu hanta bhoḥ ityādi /
tṛtīye tu nanu rajatavijñānam ityādi /
caturthe tu sāmyāpādane sati jñānadharmo vā agraho viśeṣaṇam, vastudharmo vā? ādye sāmyaṃ nāsti, ubhayajñānasyāgṛhītabhedasya bhrāntihetutvenānabhayupagamāt /
children.translated_text: In the fourth, when parity is produced: is the non-apprehension that serves as the qualifier a property of cognition, or a property of the object? In the first case, there is no parity, because it is not accepted that a cognition of both [aspects] in which the difference is not apprehended is the cause of error.

children.text: dvitīye tu viṣayadharmāṇāmajñātānāṃ pravṛttāvakiñcitkaratvam /
children.translated_text: In the second [alternative], however, the properties of the object, when unknown, are ineffective in generating activity.

children.text: jñaptau punarastyeva /
children.translated_text: But in cognition, they are indeed [effective].

children.text: tatra dṛṣṭāntamāha--maivaṃ jñānahetūnāmityādi //
children.translated_text: He gives an example for that: "Not so — of the causes of cognition" and so forth.

'Contradicted by awareness' means contradicted by discerning awareness. And the absurd consequence of omniscience of everything and the absurd consequence of knowledge of the past and future should also be understood. 'What appears' — the meaning is: a cognition arises that traces [the outline of the object]. The example of the <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) seed is given with the intention of an auxiliary cause favorable to the natural effect. And the example of the <s>kṛtaja</s> (cultivated) seed is with the intention of an association with another cause that obstructs that [natural effect]. In the case of an error that is disputed — is the cause of activity non-apprehension [of the difference], or the cognition 'this,' or [that cognition] combined with the cognition 'silver,' or both combined with the non-apprehension of difference? In the first [alternative], the refutation is: 'not, to begin with...' and so forth. In the second: 'well then, sir!' and so forth. In the third: 'but surely the cognition of silver...' and so forth.

children.text:
athavā dṛśyakāraṇasāmye 'pyadṛśyahetuviśeṣavaśād bhrāntisaṃbhavaḥ, kāryonneyatvāt sāmagryāḥ /
tadidamuktam--maivamityādi /
māmāpyevamiti cet---na, tasya kāraṇaviśeṣasya svātantryeṇāpravartakatvāt /
tadidamuktam--cetaneti /
jñānadvāreṇeti cet--na, tasya pavṛttinivṛttisādhāraṇyāt /
tadidamuktam--buddhipūrvakatve tviti /
ato na sāmyam /
tatsiddhamityādiprayogo vipratipannaṃ prati /
niyamena niścayeneti sāmānyajñānasya viśeṣapravartakatvavyudāsāvadyotanārtham /
na ca phalajñānenānaikāntikatvaṃ tasyāpravartakatvādeva /
tatsādhanajñānaṃ tu pravartakam /
tacca tadviṣayameveti /
kāryatvabodhastu pravartaka iti nirākariṣyate /
anavabhāsamānatvāditi hetupakṣe 'siddhatvaṃ siddhasādhanaṃ vā dūṣaṇam /
pratyakṣopavarṇane tu śuktikātvenānālambanatvamasmākamapyanumatam /
sitabhāsvaratayā tvanavabhāsamānatvamanubhavaviruddhamiti paramārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But its non-manifestation as something white and shining is contradicted by experience — this is the ultimate point.

children.text: doṣavattvāditi hetupakṣe 'naikāntikodbhāvanam dṛṣṭāntamātrodbhāvane tuvetrabījādiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Because of being defective" — in the thesis of [being] a reason, [this is] the raising of inconclusiveness; but in merely raising an illustration, [the example would be] a cane-stalk, a seed, and the like.

children.text: nedaṃ rajatamiti upalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: "This is not silver" is illustrative.

children.text: śuktiriyamityādyapi draṣṭavyam //
children.translated_text: "This is mother-of-pearl" and so forth should also be considered.

Alternatively, even when the visible causes are the same, error is possible due to a particular invisible cause, since the totality [of conditions] is to be inferred from the effect. This is what is said: "Not so" and so forth. If [one objects:] "Not so for me either" — no, because that particular cause does not independently generate activity. This is what is said: "A sentient being..." If [one objects:] "Through the medium of cognition" — no, because that [cognition] is common to both activity and cessation. This is what is said: "But when preceded by cognition..." Therefore there is no parity. The argument beginning with "therefore it is established" is directed toward one who is in disagreement. "With certainty" (<s>niyamena</s>) — [meaning] "with determination" — is for the purpose of illuminating the rejection of general cognition as a cause of specific activity. Nor is there inconclusiveness through knowledge of the fruit, because that [general knowledge] is itself non-productive of activity. But knowledge of the means to that [fruit] is productive of activity. And that [knowledge] pertains precisely to that object. The view that the mere awareness of being-an-effect is productive [of activity] will be refuted [later]. "Because of not being manifested" — in the thesis of [being] a reason, [this] is a flaw of either unestablishedness or proving-what-is-already-proved. But in describing perception, we too accept the non-apprehendability [of shell-silver] as mother-of-pearl.

children.text: anāśvāsastu yathārthatvājñānaṃ vā syāt, yathārthatvāyathārthatvasandeho vā? ādyaḥ prāmāṇyopāyakathanenaiva nirastaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, is the lack of confidence either ignorance of veridicality, or doubt about veridicality and non-veridicality? The first is already removed by the very statement of the means of validity.

children.text: dvitīyastu viśeṣopalabdhaiḥ prāgiṣyata evetyāha--yathā ceti //
children.translated_text: The second will be resolved by those who apprehend the distinguishing features — therefore he says: "Just as..."

children.text:
nanu kramavyatikramo 'nāditāṃ pratipādayitumuktaḥ /
anāditāpratipādanaṃ punaḥ kimarthamityata āha--anāditvācceti /
tasyāpi bādhyatvagrasaṅgāditi /
tathā ca sartyāgathyājñānayoraviśeṣaprasaṃga iti bhāvaḥ /
pūrvajñānasya mithyātvamādarśayat iti /
tadupadarśitaprakārāsahanatayā jāyamānamityarthaḥ /
tajjanitāṃ pravṛttiṃ vighaṭayaditi taducitavyapadeśābhiprāyam, viparītamabhiprāyaṃ kurvadityarthaḥ /
phalamasyāpaharatīti viṣayadārabhya phalaparyantamityarthaḥ /
ayameva viṣayāpahāro yattadviṣayādhikṣepasya svabhāvasya samutpādaḥ /
sa ca tatphalapravāhapratikṣepaparyanta iti samudāyārthaḥ /
parasparābhāvadharmiṇoriti /
yayārdharmiṇoryau dharmau
children.translated_text: Now, the transgression of order was stated to establish beginninglessness. But what is the purpose of establishing beginninglessness? — therefore he says: "Because of beginninglessness..." Because even that [beginningless cognition] would be subject to sublation. And thus there would follow the consequence of no distinction between cognition to be abandoned and cognition not to be abandoned — this is the purport. "Showing the falsity of the prior cognition" — [meaning] arising in a manner that cannot tolerate the mode shown by that [prior cognition] — that is the meaning. "Disrupting the activity generated by it" — with the intention of the designation appropriate to that; [meaning] "producing the opposite intention" — that is the meaning. "It takes away its fruit" — the meaning is: from the object up to the fruit. This very taking-away-of-the-object is the generation of its own nature, which is the negation of the object of that [prior cognition]. And that extends to the point of blocking the stream of fruit of that — this is the overall meaning. "Of two subjects possessing mutual absence" —

children.text:
parasparābhāvavantāvupalabdhau tayorityarthaḥ /
bādhyatve heturiti /
heturvyatirekaliṅgalakṣaṇamiti yāvat /
children.translated_text: the meaning is: of the two properties that possess mutual absence, which are apprehended in the two subjects. "The reason for sublatability" — the reason that has the form of a mark of negative concomitance — this is what is meant.

children.text: tattvaviṣayabuddhidhārāmiti dhyānam ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "A stream of cognitions having reality as their object" — the meaning is: meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>).

children.text: anugatamekaṃ svarūpaṃ samānāsamānajātīyavyacchedako dharmo lakṣaṇamiti yāvat //2 //
children.translated_text: One form that pervades [all instances], a property that distinguishes from both the same and different classes — that is a definition — this is what is meant.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
sarvatra tasya sulabhatvāditi /
svābhāvikaṃ tu śāstrasya traividhyaṃ nāstyeva tasya puruṣāyattatvādityapi draṣṭavyam /
prayojanasyeti /
avāntarasyetyarthaḥ /
catūrūpobhavatīti pratītiviṣaya iti śeṣaḥ /
arthaviparyayakīrtatena vyāghātāditi /
children.translated_text: "Because of the contradiction arising from the assertion of the opposite meaning."

children.text: pratyakṣapramāṇānuvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: [This is] a restatement of the <s>pramāṇa</s> of perception.

children.text: ato na sādhyāviśiṣṭatvaṃ vyadhikaraṇatvaṃ vā? avadyamāne śaśaviṣāṇādāvalakṣaṇam, vidyamāne tvanupayogini gaṅgāvālukādāvalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, is it not-different-from-the-<s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) or of a different substratum? When stated of what does not exist, it is a pseudo-definition like a hare's horn; when stated of what exists but is useless, it is a pseudo-definition like the sands of the Ganges.

children.text: ataḥ samānadharmadarśanāt asati nibhāge saṃśayaḥ, tannivṛttyartho vibhāgārambhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the observation of common properties, when distinction is not [yet] perceived, there is doubt; the undertaking of distinction is for the removal of that.

"Because of its easy availability everywhere" — but it should also be considered that the natural threefold nature of the <s>śāstra</s> does not exist at all, because it [the <s>śāstra</s>] depends on human effort. "Of the purpose" — the meaning is: of the intermediate [purpose]. "It has four forms" — the completion is: "as the object of cognition."

children.text: nanu sadanupayogisaṃśayānucchede kiṃ syāt? kathamanupayuktaṃ taditi jijñāsāyā anivṛttiḥ? api
children.translated_text: Now, if the doubt of what is useless is not cut off, what would happen? How would the non-cessation of the desire to know "how is that useless?"

children.text: cārthāpattyādīnāmupayogavatāmapi parairūdghuṣyamāṇānāmapi lakṣaṇākaraṇāt syāt sandehaḥ-- kiṃ lakṣaṇākaraṇādasanti, anupayogīni veti? tatraivāntarbhūtāni vā? atasttadapanuttaye vibhāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: Moreover, even of useful things like <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) and the like, which are proclaimed by others, since no definition is given, there would be doubt: "Do they not exist because no definition is given, or are they useless? Or are they included within those [already enumerated]?" Therefore, the division is for removing that [doubt].

children.text: tathā bauddhāpekṣayā mīmāṃsakānāmadhikapramāṇalakṣaṇābhidhānaṃ vinaiva pramāṇānām ādhikyāt /
sāṃkhyasya tu tadapekṣayaiva adhikapramāṇalakṣaṇābhidhānaṃ satyādhikye /
children.translated_text: But for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, relative to those [Buddhists], the statement of the definition of additional <s>pramāṇas</s> [is made] when the additional ones actually exist.

children.text: tad ihāpi sāṃkhyāpekṣayā adhikābhidhāne bhavati sandehaḥ, kiṃ satyādhikye athāsatīti? tadapanodanāya vibhāgavacanam /
children.translated_text: So here too, relative to <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, when additional [<s>pramāṇas</s>] are stated, there arises a doubt: is the addition real or not? The statement of division is for removing that.

children.text: ata evādhikyamāśaḍkya vibhāgaparīkṣāmavartayat sūtrakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, suspecting the addition, the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> set in motion the examination of division.

children.text: pūrvāparagranthasaṃgatiścātra sphuṭetyetadapi mantavyam //
children.translated_text: And it should be understood that the coherence of the preceding and succeeding texts is clear here.
Similarly, relative to the Buddhists, the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>' statement of the definition of additional <s>pramāṇas</s> is simply because of the actual existence of more <s>pramāṇas</s>.

children.text:
śakteranabhyupagame pramāṇābhāvo mūlam, asatpratipakṣebhyo dṛṣṭakāraṇebhya eva kāryotpattāvarthāpatteḥ kṣīṇatvāt /
pratipakṣatā ca mantrādīnāṃ sahakāriviraharūpatvāt /
tadvirahasya ca vyatirekamukhena sahakāritvāvadhāraṇāt /
trayo hi
children.translated_text: When the capacity [of certain things] is not accepted, the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> is the root [issue], because <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), [which infers] that effects arise only from observed causes against unestablished counter-arguments, is exhausted. And the counter-argument-hood of mantras and the like is because it is of the nature of the absence of an auxiliary cause. And the absence of that [auxiliary] is ascertained as auxiliary-cause-hood through the method of negative concomitance. For three

children.text:
bhāvā bhavanti kāryānukelāḥ, tatpratikūlāstadudāsīnāśca /
tatrānukūlā dahanādeḥ pavanādayaḥ /
tatpratikūlā api
children.translated_text: kinds of entities exist: those favorable to the effect, those opposed to it, and those indifferent to it. Among these, favorable to fire and the like are wind and the like. Opposed [to it] too

children.text:
dvividhāḥ svarūpataḥ sahakāritaśca /
svarūpato jalāvasekādayaḥ /
sahakārito mantrādiprayoktāraḥ /
te hi mantrādīn
children.translated_text: are of two kinds: by their own nature and through [their role as] auxiliaries. By own nature: pouring of water and the like. Through [role as] auxiliary: those who employ mantras and the like. For they,

children.text:
prayuñjānāstadvirahalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāriṇaṃ virundhanti /
udāsīnāstu tatraiva rāsabhādayaḥ /
tatrānukūlatvamanvayavyatirekaramyam /
pratikūlatvaṃ ca tadanvaye kāryavyatirekagamyam /
tacca tadviparyaryānvaye paryavasyati /
children.translated_text: in employing mantras and the like, obstruct the auxiliary cause characterized by the absence of those [mantras]. The indifferent ones are donkeys and the like in that very [context]. Among these, favorability is ascertained through positive and negative concomitance. Opposedness too is ascertained through the absence of the effect when that [opposed factor] is present — and this amounts to the presence of the opposite of that.

children.text: udāsīnatvaṃ ca vyabhicāragamyam /
children.translated_text: And indifference is ascertained through deviation (i.e., irregular co-occurrence).

children.text: evaṃ ca sati yatra yadā yasya yathānukūlatve pratikūlatve vā pramāṇamasti, tatra tadā tasya tathaiva svīkartavyam /
children.translated_text: And this being so, wherever, whenever, for whatever entity, and in whatever manner there is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for favorability or opposedness, there, then, for that entity, it should be accepted just so.

children.text: kimadhikasāmarthyakalpanayā? sarvaśca pareṣāṃ vimarśasaṃbhavo 'tīndriyasāmarthye 'pi samāna ityarthāpattim upekṣyānyadevātīndriyaśaktisvīkārabījamāśaḍkya vimṛśati--syādetaditi //
children.translated_text: What [need] is there for the supposition of additional capacity? And the possibility of all opponents' inquiry is the same even regarding supersensible capacity — setting aside <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), and suspecting some other ground for accepting supersensible power, he examines: "This would be so..."

children.text:
svarūpasya pratyakṣatve sākalyasya ca kāryaikavyaḍgyatve 'numeyamatīndriyaṃ sāmarthyam avaśiṣyata iti pūrvapakṣārthaḥ /
kāryasaṃbandhitāṃ kāryopalakṣitatāmityarthaḥ /
yadāha-- kāryopahitaṃ rūpamiti /
nanvanyakāryeṇopadhānaṃ tatkāryeṇaiva vā? ādye ahetureva hetuḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Now, is the qualification through another effect or through its own effect? In the first case, a non-cause would become a cause.

children.text: dvitīye tvitaretarāśrayatvam, tasya tatkāraṇatve siddhe sati tatkāryatvaṃ siddhaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: In the second case, there would be mutual dependence: its being a cause of that would be established only when its being an effect of that is established.

children.text: tatkāryatve sati ca tadupalakṣitaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ bhavedityata āha--idameva cāsya tadupadhānaṃ yat tatkāryotpādāt pūrvamavaśyaṃbhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when its being-an-effect is [established], causation as indicated by that would obtain — therefore he says: "This alone is its qualification by that — namely, the necessary existence prior to the production of that effect."

children.text: yudatpādāt pūrva yasyāvaśyaṃbhāvaḥ tat kāraṇamitarat kāryamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: that whose necessary existence is prior to the production of that [effect] is the cause; the other is the effect.

The own-form being perceptible, and the totality being inferable solely through the effect — what remains as the supersensible [element] to be inferred is the capacity. This is the meaning of the prior thesis. "Relatedness to the effect" means "being indicated by the effect" — that is the meaning. As is said: "The form qualified by the effect."

children.text:
nanvevaṃrūpaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ tajjātīyasya samāmanyato 'numīyeta prativyakti vā? na tāvat prativyakti, taduttarakāryābhāve 'pi kāsāñcid vināśadarśanāt /
tajjātīyasya tu prāgeva sāmānyato 'vadhāritam /
tadiha smaryata ityāśaḍkyāha--na ca tajjātīyasyeti /
yathā yo yo dhūmaḥ so 'gnimāniti sāmānyato 'vadhāraṇe 'pi eṣa dhūmo 'gnimāniti navādhāritam /
tathedamudakaṃ pipāsopaśamananimittamityanavadhṛtabhevāvadhāryata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: similarly, "this water is a cause of quenching thirst" is ascertained even though it was not previously ascertained — that is the meaning.

children.text: na ca kvacit kāryamakṛtvaiva vinaṣṭe vyabhicāraḥ, sati sahakārisākalye kuryāditi sādhyatvāt, tasya ca sahakāryasākalyaprayuktakāryābhāvavattvarūpasya tatrāpi bhāvāditi /
children.translated_text: Nor is there deviation when something is destroyed without having produced any effect, because what is to be proved is that it would produce [the effect] when the totality of auxiliary conditions is present; and that [property] — namely, possessing the absence of an effect caused by the totality of auxiliaries — exists even there.

children.text: tasmād yā nobhayaprayatnaprasavahetuḥ sopekṣābuddhiḥ tṛtīyeti viṣayabhedād buddhibhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the expectant cognition (<s>sāpekṣabuddhi</s>), which is the cause of the production of both [types of] effort but is not [itself] of [the same nature], is the third [type] — due to the difference of object, there is a difference of cognition.

children.text: sa ca sukhaheturduḥkhaheturataddhetuśceti trividha iti suvyaktamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that [object] is of three kinds: cause of pleasure, cause of pain, and cause of neither — this is quite clear. That is the meaning.

Now, would such causation be inferred generically of things of that class, or for each individual? Not for each individual, since even in the absence of a subsequent effect, destruction of some [things] is observed. But the generic [causation] of that class has already been ascertained previously. Suspecting that it is merely being recalled here, he says: "Nor of that class..." Just as, even when it has been ascertained generally that whatever is smoke possesses fire, [the particular judgment] "this smoke possesses fire" has not [yet] been ascertained —

children.text:
anumānapadaṃ vyutpādayatā bhāṣyakṛtā prasaṃgāt lakṣaṇamapyabhihitamiti ṭīkākṛd api smṛtyādivyavacchedyaṃ darśayati--tathā cetyādinā /
yato bhāṣye lakṣaṇamapyuktam, ato vārttike tadākṣepo nānuktopālambha ityāha--tadetadbhāṣyamanubhāṣyeti /
phalavataḥ pramāṇatvāt, tadviśeṣatvāccānumānasya nāphalatvaṃ yujyate /
kathañcit phalāntarasaṃbhave 'pyetasya pratyakṣaphalaṃ liṅgaparāmarśaḥ, suprasiddhamanumānamanena vyāpyata ityapi pūrvapakṣe draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Even if some other fruit is somehow possible, the perceptual fruit of this [inference] is the reflective consideration of the mark (<s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s>); well-known inference is pervaded by this — this too should be considered as part of the prior thesis.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati tatretyādinobhasamādhānasaṃgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: And this being so, the coherence of the two responses [beginning with] "there" and so forth [is clear].

children.text: samādhānāntaramāheti /
children.translated_text: "He states another response" — [this is the connection].

children.text: kasminnākṣepa ityata āha--pūrvoktamiti //
children.translated_text: In regard to which objection? — therefore he says: "The previously stated..."

The <s>ṭīkākṛt</s> (sub-commentator) also shows what is to be excluded by <s>smṛti</s> (memory) and the like — with "Thus" and so forth — since the definition was also incidentally stated by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> in the course of etymologizing the word "<s>anumāna</s>" (inference). Since the definition was also stated in the <s>bhāṣya</s>, the objection raised in the <s>vārttika</s> is not a reproach for what was left unsaid — he says: "Restating that very <s>bhāṣya</s>..." Since what has a result has the status of <s>pramāṇa</s>, and since inference is a specific form of that, fruitlessness of inference is not tenable.

children.text: nanu hānādiviṣayaṃ prāmāṇyamucyamānamanumānasya svagocaraṃ pratyevoktaṃ bhavati, hānādāveva tasya vyāpārānubandhāt /
children.translated_text: Now, the validity being stated with respect to [objects] to be abandoned and the like [as subject matter], this applies to inference only in regard to its own domain, since its operation is connected only with what is to be abandoned and the like.

children.text: ata āśaḍkaiveyamanupapannā kimatra samādhānenetyāśaḍkya vyāpārānubandhitayā hānādirasya gocaraḥ, pratīpatyanubandhitayā tu vahinajñānasya vahinareva viṣayaḥ, tadabhiprāyeṇa ca śaḍkāsamādhāne ityabhiprāyavānāha--yadpīti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this very objection is untenable — what need is there for a response? — suspecting this, [he explains that] by virtue of connection with operation, [objects] to be abandoned and the like are its domain, but by virtue of connection with cognition, the domain of fire-cognition is fire alone; and with that intention the objection and response [are formulated] — with this intention he says: "Although..."

children.text: vijñāne yat prakāśate yena vijñānaṃ nirūpyat ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: that which is manifested in cognition, by which cognition is characterized.

children.text: na ca svaviṣayādanyad viṣayāntaramasya saṃbhavati, atiprasaṃgāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: And no other object besides its own object is possible for this [cognition], since there would be over-extension — that is the purport.

children.text: pūrvapakṣiṇa iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The completion is: "of the prior-thesis proponent."

children.text: autpattika iti svabhāvāpratibaddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Innate" means not dependent on [its own] nature.

children.text: nanu heyādibuddhayaḥ kena viśeṣeṇa dvitīyānumānasya phalam, na tu dvitīyasya pratyakṣasyetyāha--parokṣārthāvagāhitayeti //
children.translated_text: Now, by what distinguishing feature are the cognitions of what-is-to-be-abandoned and the like the fruit of a second inference rather than of a second perception? — to this he says: "Because of apprehending remote objects."

children.text: nanu sāmīpyasya sādṛśyasya mānaṃ mitiḥ saṃjñāsaṃjñiparicchede pramāṇamityukte kuto vyāghātāvakāśa ityata
children.translated_text: Now, when it is said that the measure of proximity is similarity, and that the assessment [of the relation] of name and named is a <s>pramāṇa</s> in determining [the relation], whence is there scope for contradiction?

children.text: āha--anumānaśabdavadityādi //
children.translated_text: — therefore he says: "Like the word <s>anumāna</s>" and so forth.

children.text: nanu svaviṣayaparicchittau tāvat svarūpataḥ pramāṇam, vyāpāravataḥ kāraṇaviśeṣasya pramāṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: Now, in determining its own object, [<s>upamāna</s>] is at least a <s>pramāṇa</s> in its own form, since a particular cause possessing operation has <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood.

children.text: nāpi vākyārthapratipattirasyāḥ phalam, tadānīṃ tasyā vinaṣṭatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is the comprehension of the sentence-meaning its fruit, since at that time [the analogical cognition] has already ceased.

children.text: naca smṛtirūpāyā api śabdapravṛttestatphalatvam, anupayuktasamayānāmasmaryamāṇapadārthānāṃ śabdasmaraṇe 'pi tadabhāvādityata āha--yat khalu caitreti //
children.translated_text: Nor is the fruit of even the memory-based operation of the word its [<s>upamāna</s>'s] fruit, because for those whose conventions are not utilized and whose word-referents are not remembered, even the remembering of the word does not produce that [comprehension] — therefore he says: "What indeed, <s>Caitra</s>..."

children.text: nanu svaviṣayaparicchittau pradhānyamanumānāderapi, tat kutaḥ pratyakṣasya pradhānatvād iti ekadeśī vaktītyata āha--pratyakṣaparā hīti /
children.translated_text: Now, primacy in determining one's own object belongs to inference and the like too; then whence [comes the claim that] perception has primacy? The partial-view proponent says this — therefore he says: "For [they are] dependent on perception..."

children.text: prāyeṇa pratyakṣamātrapūrvakamiti sākṣāt, paraṃparayā tu sarvamevānumānaṃ tathetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: mostly preceded by perception alone — this is [the case] directly; but indirectly, all inference is likewise.

children.text: upamānaṃ tu pratyakṣapūrvakamapi śabdapūrvakameveti /
children.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> (analogy), however, though preceded by perception, is preceded by verbal testimony as well.

children.text: śabdapūrvakatve satyeva pratyakṣapūrvakatvaṃ tasya, kevalā tu pratyakṣapūrvakatā anumānamātra evetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: for <s>upamāna</s>, being preceded by perception obtains only when being preceded by verbal testimony obtains; but being preceded by perception alone [without verbal testimony] belongs to inference only.

children.text:
nanvevaṃ sati śabdānantaramupamānamabhidhīyatāmityata āha--smaraṇasahakāriteti /
yadyapi śabdasyapi pramāṇasya vākyarūpasya smṛtisthasya padārthasmṛti padārthasmṛtisahakṛtasyaiva vākyārthabodhakatvam, tathāpi na
children.translated_text: Now, if so, let <s>upamāna</s> be stated after verbal testimony — therefore he says: "Because of having memory as an auxiliary..." Although even verbal testimony as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, being in sentence form and residing in memory, has its capacity to convey sentence-meaning only when assisted by the memory of word-referents, nevertheless

children.text: kvacidapyanubhūyamānasya liḍgaṃ tvanubhūyamānamapi śabdasya viśeṣābhidhāne nyāyasiddhe 'pyekadeśyabhimataprayojanābhidhānaṃ
children.translated_text: the inferential mark, though not experienced anywhere, of a word — even though the statement of the particular is established by reasoning, the statement of purpose favored by the partialist

children.text: tadakauśalakhyāpanāya yadyapi prathamamekadeśimataṃ duṣyatvenābhimatameva, tathāpi dūṣaṇābhāsena ta tad duṣayituṃ śakyamiti śikṣayituṃ vārttikakṛtamanarañjayannevottaragranthamavatārayati--tadetadekadeśimatamiti /
pratyakṣaṃ pūrva prādhānyādityeke /
children.translated_text: 'Perception is first, due to its primacy' — so say some.

children.text: uktamupapādayituṃ mahāviṣayatvāccādau śabdopadeśa ityaparaścedyacañcuḥ /
children.translated_text: In order to substantiate what has been said, another clever person [argues]: 'Because verbal testimony has a vast scope, its instruction comes first.'

children.text: tatra mahāviṣayatvamanaikāntikāmiti śabdasya mahāviṣayatvāt ādyatvamāpādayatā pratyakṣasyānādyatvamicchatā anya eva dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, 'having a vast scope' is inconclusive — by the one who, claiming that verbal testimony has a vast scope and thus should be first, wishes perception not to be first — a different example should be cited.

children.text: tathā ca citrādau vipakṣabhūte pratyakṣa'pi gatatvena mahāviṣayatvamanaikāntikatvamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, since perception too is present in painting and other contrary instances, 'having a vast scope' is inconclusive — this is the meaning.

is to display his lack of skill. Although the partialist's view is initially regarded as faulty, nevertheless, in order to teach that it cannot be refuted by a mere semblance of refutation, he introduces the subsequent text, not gratifying the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>: 'This very view of the partialist...'

children.text:
tadetat prasaṅgāvasthāyām, svatantrasādhanapakṣe tu kālātyayāpadiṣṭatvam /
śabdacaramatāyāḥ pratyakṣaprāthamyasya ca pratyakṣasiddhatvādeva /
vyatirekipakṣe ca viruddhatvamityapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: This holds in the state of incidental application; on the view of independent proof, however, it would be 'set aside by lapse of time,' since the lastness of verbal testimony and the firstness of perception are both established by perception itself. And on the view of negative concomitance, it should be seen as contradictory.

children.text: mahāviṣayatveti /
children.translated_text: 'Having a vast scope' —

children.text: pūrvamupadiśyamānaṃ pramāṇaṃ dharmi, mahāviṣayatvāditi sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ pratyakṣaṃ vā śabdo veti saṃdehaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>pramāṇa</s> being taught first is the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); 'because of having a vast scope' is the common property; whether it is perception or verbal testimony is the doubt.

children.text: sāgharaṇatayā na heturiti bhāva iti /
children.translated_text: The sense is: since it is common [to both], it is not a valid reason.

children.text: prādhānyakhyāpanaṃ prayojanaṃ yadi prāthamyaṃ vinā na siddhyet tadānumānasyāpi prādhānyāt prāthamyaṃ syādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: If the disclosure of primacy as the purpose could not be established without priority [in enumeration], then inference too, being primary, would have priority — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanvasati ca saṃplave kā no hāniḥ? sati vā kiṃ bhevad yena bhāṣyakāro vicārayati smetyata āha--syādetaditi /
vyavasthitaviṣayatvāt pratyakṣasyānumānaviṣaye pravṛttistadā na syāta, yadyanumānamapi vyavasthitaviṣayaṃ bhavedityata āha---na cānumānaviṣaye sāmānyarūpa iti /
ato na punarūktam /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not redundant.

children.text: avyākhyāne kāraṇamiti kimiti na vyākhyātamiti śaṅgānivṛttikāraṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The reason for not explaining' means the reason for removing the doubt as to why it was not explained — this is the meaning.

children.text: sandigdhena hīti upadeśaprāmāṇye taddvāra vahnāvapyuttarakālamiti mantavyam, ato vahinaṃ pratyāhita utpāditaḥ pratyayo niścayo yasyetyanena na virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For one who is in doubt' — it should be understood that through the authority of instruction, subsequently regarding fire too [certainty arises]. Therefore there is no contradiction with the expression 'one in whom certainty regarding fire has been brought about and generated.'

children.text: abhyarhitatamaṃ manyata ityekadeśotkīrtanena pūrvoktasaṃplavopapādanaṃ smārayati //
children.translated_text: By mentioning one part, 'considers most worthy,' he reminds of the establishment of the previously stated confusion.

Now, if there is no confusion [of scope], what harm is there to us? And if there is, what benefit, that the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> examines this? To this he says: 'This may be so...' If perception, having a fixed scope, would not operate in the domain of inference — that would be so if inference too had a fixed scope — to this he says: 'And in the domain of inference, the general form...'

children.text: nanu ca niścavaphalatvāviśeṣe 'pi pratyakṣata eva ākākṣānivṛttiriti kuta etadityata āha--tāvadayamiti /
children.translated_text: Now, even though there is no difference in having determination as the result, why does the expectation cease only from perception? To this he says: 'To begin with, this...'

children.text: pratyakṣaphalasākṣātkārasyaivaṃsvabhāvatvādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Because the direct realization that is the result of perception has such a nature — this is the meaning.

children.text: nanvaḍgaṃ viśeṣaṇamityekor'thaḥ, tat kuto vyāpakatveneti vyākhyāyate? kutaśca pūrvācāryapradaśitaḥ panthāḥ parihnīyata ityata āha--tatta prakṛtānupayogitayeti /
children.translated_text: Now, 'accessory' and 'qualifier' have the same meaning — so why is it explained as a pervader? And why is the path shown by the earlier teachers abandoned? To this he says: 'That, due to irrelevance to the topic at hand...'

children.text: nirūpadhānalakṣaṇaṃ sākṣātkāraṇamākākṣānivartanayogyaṃ pratyakṣadharmo 'numānādiṣu nāsti, tena nānumānādiparicchinner'the ākākṣānivṛttiriti hi prakṛtam, na ca viśiṣṭārthagrāhakatvopadarśanenānumānādiṣu tadabhāvo darśitī bhavati /
children.translated_text: Direct apprehension, characterized by being without a limiting condition, capable of removing expectation, is a property of perception that does not exist in inference and the like. Therefore there is no cessation of expectation regarding the object determined by inference and the like — this is the topic. And by showing the apprehension of a qualified object, the absence of that [direct apprehension] in inference and the like is not demonstrated.

children.text: viśiṣṭārthagrāhakatve 'pi pratyakṣasya tabhdāvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because perception has that [direct apprehension] even when it apprehends a qualified object — this is the meaning.

children.text: vyavasthitānāṃ pratyekamekatvāditi dvitīyāsaṃsṛṣṭaviṣayatvādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Since each of the established [means of knowledge] has unity' means 'since [each] has a scope unmixed with the second' — this is the meaning.

children.text: // tātparyapariśuddhauprathamādhyāye
children.translated_text: In the <s>Tātparyapariśuddhi</s>, First Chapter,

children.text: trisūtrī samāptā //
children.translated_text: the three-<s>sūtra</s> section is completed.

children.text: // pramāṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: The section on <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge).

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification).

children.text:
pratyakṣādipramāṇaviśeṣalakṣaṇānāmiti svarūpakathanārtham /
lakṣaṇa hītyādi, arthākṣipteti ca
children.translated_text: For the purpose of stating the intrinsic nature of the definitions of specific means of valid knowledge such as perception. 'For definition' and so forth, and 'implied by the subject matter' —

children.text: prakṛtasvarūpasaṃgatikathanārtham /
lakṣaṇa hi jijñāsupratipādanāya, sā cānirjñātasāmānyasya viśeṣe nāsti /
children.translated_text: For definition is for the instruction of the inquirer, and the latter does not occur with respect to a particular when the universal is not known.

children.text: sāmānyajñānaṃ ca tallakṣaṇādhīnamatastallakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: And knowledge of the universal depends on the definition of that — therefore that definition [is given].

children.text: viśeṣavibhāgaṃ ca kṛtvā śiṣyasya jijñāsāmutthāpya viśeṣalakṣaṇāvatāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And having made the division of particulars, having aroused the student's desire to know, the introduction of the definition of the particular [follows].

children.text: tathā ca sāmānyalakṣaṇavibhāgoddeśajñānasya jijñāsadijananadvārā viśeṣalakṣaṇajñānaṃ prati hetutvāt tadgocarayorapi hetuhetumabhdāvaṃ vivakṣitvoktam--hetutveneti //
children.translated_text: And thus, since the knowledge of the universal definition, division, and enumeration is the cause of the knowledge of the particular definition through the door of generating the desire to know, with the intention of stating the causal relation between their respective objects too, it was said: 'As a cause...'
for the purpose of stating the connection with the topic at hand regarding the intrinsic nature.

children.text:
vyavacchedo nāsyāmidheya ityata āha--prayojanamiti samānajātīyamanumānādi pramāṇatvena, apratyakṣeṇa tu tadapi vijātīyameva /
ato nāsādhāraṇyaṃ lakṣaṇasya /
viśeṣakatvaṃ lakṣaṇadharmaḥ /
tatprayojanamityasaṃgatam /
ataḥ kārakāt phalabhūtāṃ kriyāṃ niṣkṛṣya darśayati--viśeṣakatvaṃ viśeṣa iti /
vipakṣavyāvṛttapratyakṣapratipādanam ityarthaḥ /
kaḥ punaranena lakṣaṇena pratipādayiṣyata ityata āha--yaḥ khalviti /
children.translated_text: Who then is to be instructed through this definition? To this he says: 'Whoever indeed...'

children.text: na ca sarve vyāmūḍhāḥ, yena pratipādyapratipādakavyavasthā na syāt /
children.translated_text: And not all are completely deluded, so that there would be no arrangement of instructor and instructed.

children.text: na ca sarvatra vyāmoho yenānavasthā syāt, na ca sarve vyāmohahetavo yenāpratipattiḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: And the delusion is not in all respects, so that there would be an infinite regress; and not all are causes of delusion, so that there would be total non-comprehension.

children.text: na ca sarvāpratipattiḥ, yenāśrayāsiddhiḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: And not all comprehension is absent, so that there would be the fault of an unestablished basis — this is the purport.

If one says that exclusion is not its designated purpose — to this he says: 'The purpose...' Inference and the like, being of the same type, are of the same type as <s>pramāṇa</s>; but from the standpoint of non-perception, even that is of a different type. Therefore the definition is not distinctive. 'Being a particularizer' is a property of the definition. 'That being the purpose' is inconsistent. Therefore, extracting the action as result from the instrument, he shows: 'The particularization is the particular...' The meaning is: the presentation of perception as distinguished from the contrary instances.

children.text:
nanu lakṣyamaprasiddhatvāt kathaṃ dharmi? prasiddhatve vā kiṃ lakṣaṇena? kiṃ cāsyābhidheyam, yadibhidadhat tatparaṃ syādityata āha--tasmāditi /
nanu lakṣaṇaṃ yadi prasiddhaṃ kiṃ vidheyam, tasyāprasiddhatvāt /
vidheyaṃ cet kathaṃ lakṣaṇam, tasyāprasiddhatvādityata āha--itastvavagatalakṣaṇa iti /
children.translated_text: And if what is to be predicated, how can it be a definition, since the definiendum is not well known? To this he says: 'But one whose definition is known...'

children.text: pratipādyāprasiddhatvād vidheyatvamagnihotrādivat, na tu pratipādakāprasiddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: What is to be predicated has the status of being predicable due to the non-familiarity of the object to be instructed, like <s>agnihotra</s> and the like — not, however, due to the non-familiarity of the means of instruction.

children.text: pratipādyaśca vidheḥ pratītyaiva lakṣaṇaṃ yāgamiva paścāt sādhyaṃ sādhayatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the object to be instructed, having been understood through the injunction itself, the definition, like a sacrifice, subsequently establishes what is to be proved — this is the meaning.

children.text: viśeṣyajñānaṃ savikalpakamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Knowledge of the qualified object is determinate cognition (<s>savikalpaka</s>) — this is the meaning.

Now, since the definiendum is not well known, how can it be the property-bearer? And if it is well known, what is the use of a definition? Moreover, what is to be predicated of it — if one predicates something, that would become the principal? To this he says: 'Therefore...' Now, if the definition is well known, what is to be predicated — since the definiendum is not well known?

children.text: nanvindriyārthasannikarṣaḥ pratyakṣakāraṇameva na bhavati, satyapi tasmin paramāṇvādiṣu indriyasaṃyuktavyavaghāyakasaṃyukteṣu ca ghaṭādiṣu tadanupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the contact of the sense-organ with the object is not even a cause of perception, since perception is untenable with respect to atoms and the like, and with respect to pots and the like that are in contact with what is connected to the sense-organ.

children.text: ato 'siddhamidaṃ lakṣaṇamityata āha--arthagrahaṇeneti //
children.translated_text: Therefore this definition is unestablished — to this he says: 'By the word "object"...'

children.text: nanu rūpatvādisāmānyaṃ nāstyeva, tat kimarthaṃ saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyābhyupagama ityata āha--na ceti //
children.translated_text: Now, universals such as color-ness (<s>rūpatva</s>) simply do not exist — so what is the point of positing contact through inherence in what is inherent in what is connected? To this he says: 'And not...'

children.text: nanu sādṛśyamarthāntaraṃ rocayamānānāmapi kuto vyāghātaḥ, na hi tadviparītamiha kiñcidabhyupetamityata āha--taṣāmiti //
children.translated_text: Now, even for those who prefer similarity as a distinct category, whence the inconsistency? For nothing contrary to that has been accepted here — to this he says: 'Of those...'

children.text:
nanvasannikṛṣṭasyaiva sannikṛṣṭāśrayasya vā grahaṇamagrahaṇameva vā bhaviṣyati, tat kuto vyāghāta ityata āha--itaratheti /
asannikṛṣṭasya hi grahaṇe indriyaprāpyakāritābhyupagamavyāghātaḥ /
sannikṛṣṭāśrayasya tu grahaṇe saṃyuktasamavāyābhyupagamavyāghātaḥ /
agrahaṇe ca tadabhyupagamavyāghātaḥ, pramāṇābhāvādityarthaḥ /
caturthasannikarṣānanubhavāt kutastadvyāghāta ityata āha--anubhūyante hīti /
children.translated_text: Since the fourth type of contact has not been experienced, whence its inconsistency? To this he says: 'For they are experienced...'

children.text: rūpatvādyanubhavasya caturthasannikarṣakāryatayā tamabhyupagamayaṃstadanabhyupagamaṃ vyāhantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: By presenting the experience of color-ness and the like as an effect of the fourth type of contact, he who accepts it contradicts the non-acceptance of it — this is the meaning.

children.text: upahitapratyayāyogāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of a conditioned cognition [without it].

children.text: tanmūlasya copahitavyapadeśasya tadabhāve 'nupapatterityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And because the conditioned designation that is based on it would be untenable in its absence — this is the meaning.

Now, what is not in contact will either be apprehended as residing in what is in contact, or it will simply not be apprehended — so whence the inconsistency? To this he says: 'Otherwise...' For if what is not in contact is apprehended, there is inconsistency with the acceptance that the sense-organ operates by reaching [its object]. If what resides in what is in contact is apprehended, there is inconsistency with the acceptance of contact through inherence in the connected. And if it is not apprehended, there is also inconsistency with that acceptance, due to the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text:
na ca rūpatvādisāmānyaviśeṣaviśiṣṭarūpādyupalabdhimantareṇa pramāṇamasti parasparavyāvṛtteṣu cakṣurādiṣu viśiṣṭopalabdhereva pramāṇatve parasparāśrayatvam /
na cāviśiṣṭopalabdhimātropanītamaviśiṣṭamindriyamātramupadhirviṣṭavyapadeśe rasādiṣvapi rūpādivyapadeśaprasaḍgād ityāśayavānāha--na cendriyāṇīti so 'yaṃ cākṣuṣatvādyupadhinibandhanatvamimānaḥ parasya rūpādivyapadeśābheda iti sa
children.translated_text: And without the apprehension of color and the like qualified by universals-and-particulars such as color-ness, there is no <s>pramāṇa</s>. And if only qualified apprehension in the mutually distinguished sense-organs such as the eye is the authority, there would be mutual dependence. And a mere unqualified sense-organ, brought about by mere unqualified apprehension, is not a condition in the conditioned designation — since there would follow the designation of color and the like even for taste and the like — with this intention he says: 'And not the sense-organs...' This reasoning, which holds that the conditions are grounded in [properties like] being visual and so forth, [entails] the non-differentiation of the other's designation of color and so forth —

children.text: evodāhṛtya nirākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: that very thing has been cited and refuted.

children.text: paramārthatastu nīlamadhurādivyapadeśābhede so 'pi nāsti /
children.translated_text: But in ultimate reality, when there is no differentiation of designations like 'blue' and 'sweet,' even that [reasoning] does not hold.

children.text: tāvatāpyasmākamabhimatalābha iti /
children.translated_text: 'Even by that much we obtain what we intend.'

children.text: śabdatvāsiddhau tu tātparyāṃ, tataḥ sādhāraṇavacasopasaṃharati--tasmāditi //
children.translated_text: But when the existence of sound-ness (<s>śabdatva</s>) is in question, [the point is made] in the <s>Tātparya</s> — therefore he summarizes with a general statement: 'Therefore...'

children.text: nanu nendriyaviśeṣaṇatayā kasyacid grahaṇamasti, anyaviśeṣaṇatayā tadgrahaṇe kimāyātamindriyasannikaṣasyetyata āha--viśeṣaṇabhāvena ceti /
children.translated_text: Now, no apprehension occurs with the sense-organ as a qualifier. If apprehension occurs with something else as a qualifier, what does sense-organ contact contribute? To this he says: 'And in the capacity of being a qualifier...'

children.text: na ca viśeṣaṇabhāvapadenobhayasaṃgrahe samavāyapadenāpi catuṣṭayasaṃgraho 'stviti vācyam, viśeṣaṇabhāvasya śuddhasya pratyakṣānaṅgasvena tadaṅgaprastāva viśiṣṭasya sulabhatvāt, samavāyasya śaphaddhasyāpi pratyakṣāṅgatvena prastutatayā tatpadasya tāvanmātrābhidhānenaiva paryavasitatvāditi //
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that if both are included by the term 'qualifier-relation,' then the four types of contact too should be included by the term '<s>samavāya</s>' (inherence). For the qualifier-relation in its pure form, being not an element of perception, when the discussion concerns elements of perception, is readily available in its qualified form; while <s>samavāya</s>, even in its pure form, being an element of perception, is relevant to the discussion, and its term is already exhausted by denoting just that much.

children.text: samavāye cābhāve ca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvāditi vārttikam /
children.translated_text: The <s>vārttika</s> is: 'And in the case of inherence and absence, due to the qualifier-qualified relation.'

children.text: taccānupapannam, samavāyasya tatpratyakṣatāyāśvāsiddhatvādityata āha--avayavetyādi //
children.translated_text: And that is untenable, since <s>samavāya</s> has not been established for its perception — to this he says: 'Parts and...' and so forth.

children.text:
nanvavayavaśvāvayavī cetyādyevāpalabhyate, na tu tayoḥ sambandho 'pītyata āha--nānyatheti /
evaṃbhūtā hi
children.translated_text: Now, only 'the part and the whole' and so forth are apprehended, but not their relation too — to this he says: 'Not otherwise...' For such

children.text: pratipattiḥ parasparāsambaddhebhyo vyāvartamānā parasparasambaddheṣu viśrāmyatīti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: a cognition, turning away from things that are mutually unrelated, comes to rest in things that are mutually related — this is the purport.

children.text: nanu sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ samānenādhikaraṇena sambandha iti paryāyau, tat kimanenoktam ityāśayavān pṛcchati--kiṃ
children.translated_text: Now, <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-referentiality) and relation with a common locus are synonymous — so what has been said by this? With this intention he asks: 'What

children.text:
punariti /
na hyatra kuṇḍamiva dravyamadhikaraṇatvena parispharati /
nāpi badarāṇīva śuklatvapaṭatve ādheyatvena, api tu ya eva śuklaḥ sa eva paṭa ityabhedenaiva pratītirityāśayavānāśaḍte--tādātmyamiti cediti /
buddheḥ paunarūktyaṃ pūrvāpekṣayā anyūnānatiriktārthatvam /
yadi hi guṇaguṇinorabheda eva syāt tadā tadvācakayorekārthatvāt tarūvṛkṣaśabdavat sahaprayogo na syāt /
paṭamānayetyukte yatmiñcit śuklmānayet, tasyaiva paṭatvāt /
apaṭaḥ paṭa itivadaśuklaḥ paṭa ityapi virudhyeti /
children.translated_text: 'Not-cloth is cloth' — like this, 'not-white is cloth' too would be contradictory.

children.text: andhasyāpi paṭo 'yamitivat śuklo 'yamityapi pratipattiḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Even a blind person's cognition 'this is cloth' would entail the cognition 'this is white.'

children.text: śuklāpratipattivad vā paṭapratipattirapi na syāt /
children.translated_text: Or, just as there is no cognition of whiteness, there would be no cognition of cloth-ness either.

children.text: mahārajanādisaṃyukte śuklatvavat paṭo 'pi tirohita iti na pratīyetetyevamāditarkasahāyaṃ pratyakṣameva paṭaśuklatvayorbhedamākalayatīti parihārārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: When connected with lac-dye and the like, just as whiteness is concealed, cloth too would not be cognized as concealed — and so forth. Perception itself, aided by reasoning of this kind, ascertains the difference between cloth and whiteness — this is for the purpose of the reply.

then...' For here the substance does not appear in the role of a locus, as a pot does. Nor does whiteness appear as contained like jujube fruits, or cloth-ness as contained. Rather, the cognition is simply one of identity: 'that which is white is itself the cloth' — with this intention he raises the doubt: 'If identity...' 'Redundancy of cognition' means having neither less nor more meaning than the preceding. For if there were absolute identity of quality and quality-bearer, then their designating words, having the same meaning, would not be used together, like the words <s>taru</s> and <s>vṛkṣa</s> [both meaning 'tree']. When one is asked to bring a cloth and brings something white, that would be correct, since that very thing is cloth.

children.text:
syādetat /
ekāntābhede hi sarvametad dūṣaṇam /
vayaṃ tvanekāntavādinaḥ /
tathā hi bhedamādāyāpaunarūktyam, abhedamādāya ca sāmānādhikaraṇyamityata āha--na caikaṃ vastviti /
bhedābhedayoḥ parasparavirodhādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because difference and non-difference are mutually contradictory — this is the meaning.

children.text: bhedo hi laukikaparīkṣakaprasiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For difference is well-known both to ordinary people and to critical inquirers.

children.text: abhede tu sāmānādhikaraṇyapratipattiḥ pramāṇamityāha paraḥ /
children.translated_text: But with regard to non-difference, co-referential cognition is the authority — so says the opponent.

children.text: sā cābhedaṃ nollikhatīti cintitamadhastādityato lokaprasiddhayorbhedābhedayorasaṃkīrṇatayā virodha eva, laukikabhedābhedātiriktastu bhedābhedanāmā samavāyo vā syāt, vājñmātraṃ vā, ubhayathāpi na no darśanahānirityāśayavānupasaṃharati--tasmāditi //
children.translated_text: And that [co-referential cognition] does not scratch [i.e., reach] non-difference — as has been considered above. Therefore, between difference and non-difference as commonly understood, there is indeed contradiction due to their unmixed nature. But a 'difference-cum-non-difference' beyond the commonly known difference and non-difference would either be <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) or a mere word — and in either case our view suffers no loss — with this intention he summarizes: 'Therefore...'

One might say: all this is a fault only if there is absolute non-difference. But we are proponents of non-absolutism. For taking difference, there is non-redundancy; and taking non-difference, there is co-referentiality — to this he says: 'And not a single entity...'

children.text: nanu yadyapi sāmānādhikaraṇyapratipattina tādātmyamullikhati, tathāpi bhedasambandhābhyāṃ vyāvartamānā abhedaṃ vā abhedasambandhaṃ vā sādhayet /
tathā hi prayogaḥ, paṭaśuklatve na bhinne sambaddhe, sāmānādhikaraṇyāt /
children.translated_text: The argument is thus: cloth-ness and whiteness are neither different nor related, because of co-referentiality.

children.text: ye punarbhinne sambaddhe na te samānādhikaraṇe yathā dadhikuṇḍe /
children.translated_text: Those that are different and related are not co-referential — like curd and the vessel.

children.text: na ca tatheme /
children.translated_text: And these are not like that.

children.text: tasmānna tathetyāśayavānāśaṅkate---sambandhe 'pīti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, they are not like that — with this intention, he raises the objection: 'even in the case of relation.'

Now, although the cognition of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) suggests identity, nevertheless, being excluded from difference and relation, it should establish either non-difference or the relation of non-difference.

children.text:
bhavedevam, yadi bhedasanbandhābhyāmasya vyatirekaḥ svābhāvikaḥ syāt /
kiṃ tu raktaḥ paṭaḥ, agnirmāṇavaka itivat śabdavṛttibhedopādhikaḥ /
śabdavṛttibhedastu saḍketopādhika ityāha---na śabdeti /
children.translated_text: And the difference in the function of words is conditional upon convention — he says: 'not by word.'

children.text: sāmānādhikaraṇyāditi /
children.translated_text: 'Because of co-referentiality' —

children.text: ca heturyathā bhedasambandhābhyāṃ vyāvartate tathā abhedasambandhābhyāmapītyasādhāraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: the reason, just as it is excluded from difference and relation, is likewise excluded from non-difference and the relation [of non-difference] — and hence it is inconclusive.

children.text: abhinnaṃ ca tatsambandhi ceti sādhyam, na caivaṃbhūtamubhayavādisaṃpratipannaṃ kiñcidasti yato vyāvṛtterasādhāraṇo hetuḥ syāditi cet na, ubhayavyavacchedaparyavasānasya manorathenāpyasiddheḥ //
children.translated_text: If one says: the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is 'non-different and related to it,' and nothing of this kind is accepted by both parties from which the exclusion of the inconclusive reason would obtain — no, because the culmination in the exclusion of both is not established even in imagination.

This would be so if the exclusion [of co-referentiality] from difference and relation were natural. But [the exclusion is] conditional upon the difference in the function of words — as in 'red cloth' or 'the fire is a boy' [i.e. the fire is young].

children.text: yo hyabhinnaḥ sa kathaṃ sambaddhaḥ, sambandhasya bhedādhiṣṭhānatvāt /
yaḥ sambaddhaḥ sa kathamabhinnaḥ, tenaiva tasyāsambandhāt /
children.translated_text: And how can what is related be non-different, since for that very reason [of being related] it is not non-different?

children.text: bhinno 'pīti cet? tathāpi bhedamādāyaiva sambandho na punarabhedamādāya /
children.translated_text: If one says 'even though different' — still, relation operates precisely by taking up difference, not by taking up non-difference.

children.text: tathā ca sambandho bhedenaiva vyāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus relation is pervaded by difference alone.

children.text: abhedastvasambandhenaiveti katham abhinne sambandhe iti pratijñā na vyāhatā? prakārabhedamādāyeti cet---na, tasyābhāvāt, na hi dravyasya guṇatvamapyasti, guṇasya vā dravyatvamapi, yenābhedaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: While non-difference is pervaded by non-relation alone — so how is the thesis 'non-different and related' not self-contradictory? If one says 'by taking up difference of mode' — no, because there is no such thing; for substance does not even have the nature of quality, nor does quality have the nature of substance, by virtue of which there would be non-difference.
For how can what is non-different be related, since relation has difference as its ground?

children.text:
uktaprakāreṇa ca bheda eva /
sattvenābheda iti cet? kimidaṃ sattvaṃ sattā vā, svarūpaṃ vā? svarūpaṃ tāvad
children.translated_text: And by the manner stated, there is difference alone. If one says 'non-difference by virtue of existence (<s>sattva</s>)' — what is this existence? Is it <s>sattā</s> (the universal 'being'), or the intrinsic nature? As for the intrinsic nature, to begin with,

children.text:
guṇo guṇa eva, dravyaṃ dravyameva /
sattā tu tābhyāmasādhāraṇābhyāṃ sādhāraṇī bhinnā kathamiva tayoḥ svabhāvaḥ? kenacidākāreṇa tatheti cet? na vaidravyaguṇakarmasādhāraṇādākārādasādhāraṇamākāraṃ sattāyāḥ paśyāmo yena sā tathā syāt /
evaṃ teṣāmapi dravyaguṇakarmaṇāṃ parasparāsaḍkīrṇāt rūpānna svabhāvāntaraṃ paśyāmaḥ pratīyamānarūpamevābhinnamityucyamāne sattā vā na syāt, tāni vā na syurityuktaprāyam /
tasmāt dravyaguṇayoḥ sattaiva
children.translated_text: a quality is just a quality, a substance is just a substance. And <s>sattā</s> (being), being common to those two that are distinctive, and being different [from them], how can it be their intrinsic nature? If one says 'in some respect it is so' — no, we do not see any form of <s>sattā</s> that is distinctive beyond the form common to substance, quality, and action, by virtue of which it could be so. Similarly, even of substance, quality, and action, beyond their mutually unmixed forms, we see no other intrinsic nature — and if one were to say that the very form being cognized is non-different, then either <s>sattā</s> would not exist, or those [categories] would not — this amounts to what has already been said.

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ svarūpaṃ svabhāvo dharmo viśeṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>sattā</s> (existence) alone is the common nature, intrinsic character, property, and qualifier of substance and quality — this is the meaning.

children.text: dravyatvaguṇayordravyameva svabhāvo dharmī viśeṣyamityarthaḥ viśeṣyasyaikasyaiva viśeṣaṇadvayadvārobhayaśabdabuddhiviṣayatvād guṇaguṇyādīnāmevābhedaṃ bhedābhedau vā pare menire iti yadyupanibandhenāha--śabdānāṃ tviti //
children.translated_text: Substance alone is the intrinsic nature, property-bearer, and qualified entity of substance-ness and quality — this is the meaning. Since the single qualified entity becomes the object of both words and cognitions through the two qualifiers, others have held that there is non-difference of quality and qualified, or both difference and non-difference — and since [the author] addresses this through reasoning, he says: 'but of words.'

children.text: nanvekāntabhinnānāṃ kālato deśato vā vivekakhyātirūpalabdhā /
children.translated_text: Now, for things that are absolutely different, a cognition of separation in terms of time or space has been obtained.

children.text: sā guṇaguṇibhyāṃ vyāvartamānā svavyāpyamaikāntikaṃ bhedamapi vyāvartayatīti ata āha--ayutasiddhyeti /
children.translated_text: That [cognition of separation], being excluded from quality and qualified, would also exclude absolute difference, which is pervaded by it — to this he says: 'by inseparable co-existence (<s>ayutasiddhi</s>).'

children.text: astyevāsau, na tu sphuṭataro nirluṭhitagarbhatayā /
children.translated_text: That [inseparable co-existence] does exist, but it is not more manifest, since its content has been worked out [i.e. subsumed into the relation].

children.text: na ca tannivṛttimātreṇa bhedanivṛttiḥ, lohadahanayorabhedaprasaḍgādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And mere absence of that [separability] does not entail absence of difference, since there would follow the absurd consequence of non-difference between iron and fire — this is the meaning.

children.text:
syādetat /
bhinnasaṃmbandhyanubhave 'pi kutaḥ sambandhānubhava ityata āha---na cāsāviti /
na hyagṛhyāmāṇe viśeṣaṇe viśiṣṭapratipattiḥ /
na ca buddhyā bodhyamanumīyate pratyakṣocchedaprasaḍgādityarthaḥ /
yo viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ sarvaḥ saṃndhāntarapūrvakaṃ iti vyāptirihaiva bhajyata iti pareṇāpi svīkaraṇīyameva /
na hyasau samavāyamabhāvaṃ vā abhyupagacchan viśeṣaṇatāmasya na svīkaroti /
anyathā samavāyābhāvaviśiṣṭapratītimeva na svīkuryāt /
kiṃ tu
children.translated_text: One might say: even granting the experience of different relata, whence the experience of relation? To this he says: 'and not that.' For there is no cognition of the qualified without grasping the qualifier. And one should not say that what is cognized is inferred [to have a relation], since there would follow the destruction of perception — this is the meaning. [The principle] 'every qualifier-qualified relation is preceded by another relation' — the invariable concomitance here is broken — and this must be accepted even by the opponent. For he, whether accepting <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) or <s>abhāva</s> (absence), does not deny the qualifier-status of this [relation]. Otherwise, he would not accept even the cognition qualified by <s>samavāya</s> or <s>abhāva</s>. But

children.text:
sambandhāntararahito viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ pratyakṣāḍgaṃ na bhavatīti kadācid brūyāt /
atastaṃ samānanyāyena nivārayati--tat
children.translated_text: one might say: the qualifier-qualified relation, without another relation, is not a component of perception — he might say this on some occasion. To that, he refutes by the same principle: 'then,

children.text: kimatreti /
children.translated_text: what here?'

children.text: yathā vinaiva sambandhāntareṇa tadviśiṣṭapratipattiḥ, tathā tasyā evaindriyakatvanāntarīyakaḥ sākṣātkāraḥ pratīyate, vipakṣe tvanavasthāprasaṅgalakṣaṇastarkaḥ samāna ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Just as the cognition of the qualified [occurs] without any further relation, so too the direct apprehension that is the necessary concomitant of its being sense-generated is cognized — and in the contrary case, the same reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) in the form of the consequence of infinite regress applies — this is the meaning.

children.text:
na ca guṇakarmasāmānyeṣvapi viśeṣaṇatvamātreṇaiva grahaṇamastu, kṛtaṃ samavāyādineti vācyam /
śabdasya svāśrayāviśeṣaṇasyāpi samavāyena grahaṇāt /
so 'pi tṛtīyo 'stviti cet---na, gandharasayoratathābhūtayorapi saṃyuktasamavāyena grahaṇāt /
so 'pi caturtho 'stviti cet---na, śabdarūpatvayorapi pratīyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: If one says 'let that too be a fourth' — no, because sound and form-ness too are cognized.

children.text: viśeṣaṇabhāvenaiveti cet---na, dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyānāṃ sambandhābhāve viśeṣaṇabhāvasyaivānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: If one says 'by the mere qualifier-relation' — no, because in the absence of a relation of substance, quality, action, and universal, the very qualifier-relation is untenable.

children.text: sambandhaśca prasādhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the relation [of inherence] has been established.

children.text: ato na samavāyābhāvavat pratyakṣabādhaḥ, nāpyanavasthā, sambandhāntaranirapekṣasambandha eva viśrānteḥ iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no perceptual sublation as in the case of the absence of <s>samavāya</s>, nor is there an infinite regress, since [the process] comes to rest in a relation that does not require a further relation.

Nor should one say: let the grasping of qualities, actions, and universals too be by the mere qualifier-status alone — what need is there for <s>samavāya</s> and the like? For even sound, which does not qualify its own locus, is grasped through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). If one says 'let that too be a third [relation]' — no, because odor and taste too, which are not of that nature [i.e. not qualifying their own locus], are grasped through contact-inherence (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>).

children.text: syādetat /
bhūtalameva ghaṭābhāvastacca saṃyogādeva pratīyate /
children.translated_text: The ground-surface itself is the absence of the pot, and that is cognized through contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>) alone.

children.text: ataḥ kiṃ tadarthena viśeṣaṇabhāvenetyata āha---na ceti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what need is there for qualifier-status for its sake? To this he says: 'and not.'

children.text: satyapi ghaṭādau bhūtarasya bhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the ground-surface exists even when the pot and the like are present.

children.text: bhūtalavyavahāravat ghaṭābhāvavyavahāraprasaḍgāditi śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The remainder is: there would follow the absurd consequence that, just as the practical usage 'ground-surface' [applies], so too the practical usage 'absence of the pot' [would apply even when the pot is present].
One might say:

children.text: na ca kevalyamiti /
children.translated_text: 'And not mere exclusiveness' —

children.text: kevalyaṃ hi bhūtaladharmo ghaṭādyavirodhī yudyucyeta na ghaṭādinā saha saṃbhavet, tathā ca sa doṣastadavastha eva, virodhī cet? sa tāvannobhayavādisiddhadravyādiṣvanyatamaḥ, teṣāṃ ghaṭena saha saṃbhavāt, abhāvavyavahārakāle 'pi ca keṣāñcidasaṃbhavāt, bhūtaladharmāṇāṃ ca teṣāṃ ghaṭaināvināśādanāvṛteśca /
children.translated_text: For exclusiveness, being a property of the ground-surface, if said to be non-opposed to the pot and the like — i.e. compatible with the pot — then the fault remains as before. If it is opposed? Then, to begin with, it is not any one of the [categories] substance, etc. that are accepted by both disputants, since those are compatible with the pot. And because even at the time of the practical usage 'absence,' some of them do not occur [there], and because those properties of the ground-surface are not destroyed by the pot and are not prevented [from arising]. And [that exclusiveness] is not destroyed or prevented [by the pot].

children.text: tadatiriktaṃ tu daśamaṃ dravyam, pañcaviśatitamo vā guṇaḥ, ṣaṣṭhaṃ vā karma, sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyā na saṃbhavantyeva, tasya dravyādyanyatamatvena tadavinābhāvidharmāpatteḥ /
children.translated_text: But something beyond those — a tenth substance, a twenty-fifth quality, or a sixth action — universals, particulars, and inherence simply cannot be [the answer], since, [that exclusiveness] being one or another of substance and the like, the property of being invariably concomitant with them would follow.

children.text: anāpattau vā tattvānupapatteḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, if it does not follow, its real existence would be untenable.

children.text:
sa khalvayaṃ saptamaḥ padārtho bhavet? tatrāpyasau bhāvaniṣedhākāro vā syāt, anyathā vā? na tāvadanyathā /
tathā sati avirodhitvaprasaṃgāt /
niṣedhākāro 'pi yadyanutpanno 'pi na nivartate, tadā ghaṭādivyavahāraḥ kadācidapi na syāt /
children.translated_text: If, having the form of negation, it does not cease even when unarisen, then the practical usage of the pot and the like would never occur.

children.text: utpanno vā yadi nivarteta, tadā vinaṣṭo 'pi ghaṭaḥ kadācidupalabhyeta /
children.translated_text: Or if, having arisen, it ceases, then even a destroyed pot would sometimes be perceived.

children.text: ataḥ padārthānāṃ saptamo niṣedharūpo 'nutpannapradhvaṃsī ca utpannavināśī ca bhūtalādidharmaḥ kaivalyamabhāva iti ekor'tha iti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>abhāva</s> (absence) is a seventh category among the categories, having the form of negation, non-arising-and-destruction [i.e. prior non-existence that is destroyed when the thing arises], and arising-and-destruction [i.e. destruction that arises when the thing ceases] — a property of the ground-surface and the like, [identical with] exclusiveness — these are synonymous.

children.text: tadidamuktam--na ghaṭābhāvādanyo ghaṭābhāva evetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is what was stated: 'There is no absence of the pot other than the absence of the pot' — this is the meaning.

Should this then be a seventh category? Even so, would it have the form of negation of existence, or otherwise? Not otherwise, to begin with — for if so, there would follow the consequence of its being non-opposed [to what it negates].

children.text: syādetat yadyapi jñeyarūpaṃ tattvāntaraṃ nāsti, tathāpi jñānarūpaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: One might say: although there is no further reality as an object of knowledge, there will be one as a form of knowledge.

children.text: viṣayaśca tasya dṛśye pratiyogini bhūtalamevetyata āha--na ceti, yathā bhūtalapakṣe ghaṭavatyapi prasaḍgo bhavati, tathā bhūtalajñānapakṣe ghaṭavabhdūtalajñāne 'pi prasaṅga ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And its object, when the counter-positive is visible, is the ground-surface alone — to this he says: 'and not.' Just as in the thesis of the ground-surface, there is the undesirable consequence [of asserting absence] even when the pot is present, so too in the thesis of the cognition of the ground-surface, there is the same consequence in the cognition of the ground-surface even when the pot is present — this is the meaning.

children.text: nanu dṛśye pratiyoginītyuktaṃ ghaṭavabhdūtalajñāne tu ghaṭo na dṛśyaḥ kiṃ tu dṛśyamāna ityata āha---nahīti /
na hi darśanānarhe dṛśyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: what is not worthy of being seen is not [merely] 'visible.'

children.text: darśanārhe hi ghaṭaḥ tatra yadi na nāsti tadā bhūtalavadakāmenāpyupalabhyetaiva, bhūtalamapi vā nopalabhyeta, tulyayogakṣematvāt /
children.translated_text: For if the pot, being worthy of being seen there, is not absent there, then it would be perceived even by one who does not wish to [perceive it], just like the ground-surface — or even the ground-surface would not be perceived, since they share the same status.

children.text: tasmād bhūtalopalabdhāvapi tadanupalambhastadabhāvamādāyaivopapadyata iti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the perception of the ground-surface, the non-apprehension of that [pot] is tenable only by accepting its absence.

children.text: yadyapyupalabhyābhāvamaḍgīkārayituṃ śakyate tarkagatyā paraḥ, tathāpi svavacanavirodhamapyapaśyantaṃ prati kiṃ tenāpītyāśayavānāha---dṛśye 'nupalabhyamāna iti //
children.translated_text: Although the opponent can be forced to accept absence by the method of reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) — even regarding what is perceptible — nevertheless, for one who does not see even the contradiction in his own words, what use is even that? — with this intention he says: 'when something visible is not perceived.'

Now, it was said 'when the counter-positive is visible,' but in the cognition of the ground-surface that has the pot [on it], the pot is not [merely] 'visible' (<s>dṛśya</s>, fit-to-be-seen) but rather 'being-seen' (<s>dṛśyamāna</s>) — to this he says: 'for not.'

children.text: anupalambho hyupalambhābhāvāka vā syāt, dṛśye smaryamāṇe bhūlopalambha eva vā, ghaṭopalambhe vā smaryamāṇe kevalātmopalambhaḥ? na tāvad dvitīyatṛtīyau, smaryamāṇe dṛśyamāne ghaṭe bhūtalopalambhe sati ghaṭavatyapi prasaṅgasya
children.translated_text: For non-apprehension would be either of the form of absence of apprehension, or — when the visible [counter-positive] is being remembered — a cognition of the ground-surface itself, or — when the apprehension of the pot is being remembered — a bare cognition of the self? Not the second and third — because when the pot is being remembered or being seen, and the apprehension of the ground-surface obtains, the undesirable consequence [of asserting absence] even when the pot is present

children.text: durnivāratvāt /
children.translated_text: is unavoidable.

children.text: tasmādupalambhābhāva evānupalambhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, non-apprehension is nothing but absence of apprehension.

children.text:
nanvnenaiva sarvavyavahāropapatto kimupalabhyābhāvenetyata āha--kimaparāddhamupalabhyābhāveneti /
tathā hi yathopalambhaniṣedhakāt pramāṇādupalambhābhāvasiddhistathopalabhyaniṣedhakāt pramāṇabalādevopalabhyābhāvasiddhirapi bhavati /
bhavati hi ghaṭaṃ nopalabhaitivat ghaṭo nāstīti pratītiḥ /
children.translated_text: For there arises the cognition 'the pot is absent' just as [there arises] 'I do not perceive the pot.'

children.text: na caikaviṣayatvamanayoḥ, nimīlitalocanasya hyupalambhābhāvaniścaya upalabhyābhāve ca sandeho jijñāsā ca kathañcid bhūtalaniścaye 'pi /
children.translated_text: And these two do not have the same object — for one who has closed his eyes has certainty about absence-of-apprehension, but doubt and desire-to-know about absence-of-the-perceptible, even when there is some certainty about the ground-surface.

children.text: na caitadekatraikadā saṃbhavatītyāśayavānupasaṃharati---tasmāditi /
children.translated_text: And these [certainty and doubt] are not possible with respect to the same thing at the same time — with this intention he concludes: 'therefore.'

children.text: asaditi sanniṣedha ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Is non-existent' means: is a proximate negation — this is the meaning.

Now, since all practical activity is accounted for by this alone, what need is there for the absence of the perceptible? To this he says: 'what fault has the absence of the perceptible committed?' For just as the establishment of absence-of-apprehension proceeds from a <s>pramāṇa</s> that negates apprehension, so too the establishment of absence-of-the-perceptible also proceeds from the force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that negates the perceptible.

children.text: sa ca dṛśyānupalabdharevāvagamyate, akṣavyāpārasyādhikaraṇagrahaṇopakṣīṇatvāditi kecit /
children.translated_text: And that [absence] is cognized only through non-apprehension of the visible, since the operation of the sense-organ is exhausted by the grasping of the locus — so say some.

children.text: tadanupapannam, andhasyāpi tvagindriyopanīte ghaṭādau rūpaviśeṣābhāvapratītiprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: That is untenable — because there would follow the absurd consequence that even a blind person would have the cognition of the absence of a specific color regarding a pot and the like presented by the tactile sense-organ.

children.text: asti hi tasyādhikaraṇasya grahaṇam, asti ca pratiyogismaraṇam, asti ca nīle śuklatvasya yogyasyābhāvo 'nupalabdhiśca //
children.translated_text: For there is grasping of the locus by that [blind person], there is recollection of the counter-positive, and there is the absence and non-apprehension of whiteness — which is something fit [to be perceived] — in [something] blue.

children.text: adhikaraṇagrāhakeṇendriyeṇa grāhyābhāvavādino 'pi samānametaditi cet---na, pratiyogigrāhakeṇendriyeṇa
children.translated_text: If one says: this is equally [a problem] for those who maintain that absence is grasped by the sense-organ that grasps the locus — no, because the essential position (<s>siddhāntamarma</s>) is that

children.text:
tadabhāvo gṛhyate bhāvāyattatvāt tasyeti siddhāntamarmatvāt /
mamāpi yadabhāvo 'nupalabdhyā bodhyaḥ tadgrāhakeṇendriyeṇādhikaraṇagrahaṇe sa gṛhyata iti siddhāntasāramiti cet---na, vāyau tvagindriyopanīte
children.translated_text: absence is grasped by the sense-organ that grasps the counter-positive, since [absence] has its being dependent on that [counter-positive]. If one says: 'for me too, the essential principle is that, when the locus is grasped by the sense-organ that grasps what is to be known as absent, then that [absence] is grasped' — no, because there would follow the consequence that the cognition of absence of color would not arise when wind is presented by the tactile sense-organ.

children.text: rūpābhāvapratītyanudayaprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: The consequence being that the cognition of absence of color would not arise.

children.text: na hi rūpagrāhakeṇa tatrādhikaraṇamupanītam /
children.translated_text: For in that case, the locus is not presented by the sense-organ that grasps color.

children.text: tatrāpi tāvaccakṣurindriyaṃ saṃbaddhamiti cet? evaṃ tarhi tasya nādhikaraṇagrahaṇe vyāpāraḥ, nāpi pratiyogismaraṇe rūpābhāvapratītyā ca niyamena apekṣata ityāyātam, ananyathāsiddhamaindriyakatvamabhāvasyetyanyathāsiddhatvapralāpaṃ gajanimīlanenāvadhīrya viddhavadāha---indriyavyāpāre sati tatpratyayāditi /
children.translated_text: If one says: 'even there, the visual sense-organ is connected' — then in that case, its operation is not in grasping the locus, nor in recollecting the counter-positive — and the conclusion reached is that [visual perception] is necessarily required for the cognition of the absence of color. The sensory nature of absence-cognition is not otherwise established — dismissing the babble of 'otherwise-establishment' by closing his eyes like an elephant, he speaks directly: 'when there is sensory operation, from that cognition.'

children.text: āntarālikameva vyāpāraṃ vyavadhāyakamiti bhrāntaṃ pratibodhayannāha---na ca pratiyogīti //
children.translated_text: Instructing the deluded one who [thinks] the very intervening operation is an obstruction, he says: 'and not the counter-positive.'

children.text:
pratiyogismaraṇamityatra vākchalavādinamutthāpya bodhayati---na ca śabdasmaraṇādīnāmiti /
