And the purpose of the explanation is the indication of another reason, and thus the argument [runs]: the cognition whose object is an entity such as form and the like is [a cognition] whose object is the word for form and the like, because it is invariably designated by that [word]; but what is not the object of something is not invariably designated by that — as form-cognition [is not invariably designated] by taste. The pervasion of cognition by the word does not exist even with the meaning of contact — how much less with the identity with the word? — therefore he says "as if" — just as an object,

children.text: parisphurati, tathā śabdo 'pītyarthaḥ /
śabdānuvyādhavadeva śabdasaṃbhinnaviṣayamevetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just like the pervasion by the word, [the cognition] has precisely a word-pervaded object — that is the meaning.

children.text: na cedamaprāmāṇikaṃ, yadavocat pramāṇamityādiśeṣau /
children.translated_text: And this is not without authority — the remainders being: "what was stated is the <s>pramāṇa</s>" and so forth.

children.text: śabdasyānubhavaḥ, saṃskāraḥ, smaraṇaṃ, samuccāraṇecchā, prayatnaḥ, sthānābhighātaḥ, śabdābhivyaktiriti svātmānyeva kramāvagamaḥ /
children.translated_text: The experience of the word, the residual impression, the recollection, the desire to utter, the effort, the impact on the place [of articulation], the manifestation of the word — the sequential understanding is within one's own self alone.

children.text: tadato bāle 'pi prathamataḥ śabdamuccārayati eṣa eva krama unnīyata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in a child who utters a word for the first time, this very sequence is inferred — that is the meaning.
though entered into cognition, shines forth as its object [as if it were within it], so too the word — that is the meaning.

children.text:
prathame pakṣe 'siddho hetuḥ aprasiddhaviśeṣaṇaśca pakṣaḥ śabdabrahmaṇa eva vājiviṣāṇāyamānatvāt /
dṛśyatvādṛśyatvalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedāpādakatvāt viparītapramāṇopapattiścetyapi draṣṭavyam /
dvitīye tu bhāgāsiddho heturityarthaḥ /
na hi aviśade 'pi bālamūkādiśabde pramāṇamasti /
na hi bhāvanā vā tajjanitā smṛtirvā pūrvānubhūtasya sattāyām idānīmanubhūyamānasaṃbhede vā pramāṇamasti /
children.translated_text: For neither the mental impression (<s>bhāvanā</s>) nor the memory generated by it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for the present existence of what was previously experienced, or for its being unseparated from what is presently being experienced.

children.text: tathā sati vinaṣṭo ghaṭaḥ smaryamāṇatvāt sanneva syāt /
children.translated_text: If it were so, a destroyed pot, being remembered, would still exist.

children.text: anubhūyamānaṃ na bhūtalaṃ ghaṭasaṃbhinnaṃ bhavedevaṃ cocchinnamaghaṭaṃ bhūtalamiti /
children.translated_text: And the ground-surface being experienced would be conjoined with the pot — and thus the ground-surface without the pot would be cut off.

children.text: tasmādabhyupetya viruddhadharmādhyāsavādo mantavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the doctrine of the superimposition of contradictory properties must be accepted as a concession.

In the first view, the reason is unestablished, and the thesis has an unestablished qualifier — since the <s>śabda-brahman</s> (word-<s>Brahman</s>) itself amounts to a hare's horn. It should also be noted that the superimposition of contradictory properties characterized by visibility and invisibility leads to difference, and there is evidence supporting the opposite [view]. In the second [view], however, the reason is partially unestablished — that is the meaning. For even in an unclear sound of a child, a mute person, and the like, there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> [for the presence of the full word].

children.text: nanu bālenānubhūyamānaṃ rūpaṃ tāvad viśadameva /
children.translated_text: Now, the form experienced by a child is at least vivid.

children.text: tataśca tadātmā rūpaśabdo 'pi kathamaviśadaḥ syāt, kathaṃ cāprāmāṇiko rūpasya prāmāṇikatvāt, kevalamavyutpanno 'pi śabdena vyavaharediti prasajyeta, tadasaṃbaddham /
children.translated_text: And from that, how could the word for form, being of its nature, be non-vivid? And how could it be without authority, given the authority of [the cognition of] form? The mere consequence that even an uneducated person would engage in verbal practice [would follow] — but that is irrelevant.

children.text: na hi śabdātmatāpratyayaṃ vyavahārāṅgam ācakṣmahe, kiṃ tu sambandhagrahaṇamityata āha--na ceti //
children.translated_text: For we do not declare the cognition of identity with the word to be a component of verbal practice; rather, [it is] the grasping of the conventional relation — therefore he says: "Nor..."

children.text:
ayamapyabhyupagamavāda eva /
śabdo hi vaktṛvaktrāvaruddhanabhobhāgāvacchinnatayā śrotreṇa pratīyate 'pratīyamāne 'pyarthe /
artho 'pi purovartitayā cakṣuṣā pratīyate 'navagate 'pi śabde /
children.translated_text: The object too is cognized by the eye as being in front, even when the word has not been learned.

children.text: tadayaṃ bālo yad rūpaṃ paśyati sa eva rūpaśabda iti loṣṭalaḍḍukadṛṣṭāntamanuharatīti /
children.translated_text: So this child, [who thinks] the form that he sees is the very word for form — he follows the example of a clod and a lump [being confused].

children.text: so 'yaṃ bhedapratyayo bhrānata iti yadi śaṅkate tatrāha--na ceti /
children.translated_text: If one suspects that this cognition of difference is erroneous, to that he says: "Nor..."

children.text: ayamapyabhyupagamavāda eva, na hyasti bhrāntatve 'sya pramāṇam //
children.translated_text: This too is only an argument by concession; for there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for its being erroneous.
This too is only an argument by concession. For the word is cognized by the ear as delimited by a portion of the ether enclosed by the speaker and the audience, even when the object is not cognized.

children.text:
syādetat, bālamūkādijñānānāṃ śabdasaṃbhedastāvat sāndehika evāstu, vyutpannānāṃ punaḥ savikalpā dhiyaḥ śabdasāmānādhikaraṇyena jāyamānāḥ śabdātmakatvamarthasya vyavasthāpayantu /
tathā sati bālamūkādivijñānānāṃ
children.translated_text: One might say: let the cognitions of children, mute persons, and the like be at least doubtful regarding [their] admixture with words; but the conceptual cognitions of the educated, arising through co-referentiality with the word, may establish the word-nature of the object. If so, the cognitions of children, mute persons, and the like,

children.text:
tadviṣayatvāt śabdasaṃbhinnaviṣayatvamarthataḥ siddhaṃ bhavatītyata āha--sāmānādhikaraṇyanirāsāyeti /
sāsnādimadrūpasyeti /
na tu gakārādirūpasyeti tātparyam /
ayaṃ śabdo gakārādyākāro na tu sāsnādyākāra iti tātparyam /
children.translated_text: This word has the form of the letter 'g' and the like, but not the form of dewlap and the like — that is the import.

children.text: nanu yo ḍittha iti ḍitthaśabdamevoccārayasi, na tvayaṃ ḍitthaśabda iti tameva niṣedhasi ceti kimidamityata āha--autsargikaṃ hīti /
children.translated_text: Now, when you utter the word "<s>Ḍittha</s>" [saying] "this is <s>Ḍittha</s>," you are uttering the word <s>Ḍittha</s> itself, and [at the same time] saying "this is not the word <s>Ḍittha</s>" — you are negating that very [word]. What is this? — therefore he says: "For by the general rule..."

children.text: arthaparatā hyasya svaparatāniṣedhenaivāvirodhataḥ siddhyatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: its reference to the object is established without contradiction precisely by the negation of self-reference.

children.text: tat kiṃ sarvatraivameva? netyata āha--kvacit punariti //
children.translated_text: Then is it always just so? No — therefore he says: "But sometimes..."

having that [same object] as their content, would be established implicitly as having a word-pervaded object — therefore he says: "For the refutation of co-referentiality..." "Of the form having dewlap and the like" — but not of the form having the letter 'g' and the like — that is the import.

children.text: yatra tarhi asaṃbhadena saṃketagrahe nityādipadāni santi, tatrāsaṃketitatvānna tāvadarthaparaḥ, svaparo 'pi yadi na syād vyarthaḥ prayogaḥ syādityata āha--yatrāpīti /
children.translated_text: Where, then, when the convention is grasped without admixture, words like "eternal" and the like exist — there, since no convention has been assigned, [the word] is first of all not object-referential; and if it were not self-referential either, the usage would be purposeless — therefore he says: "Even where..."

children.text: yathā hi gaurvāhīka ityatra gotvaṃ goguṇayogalakṣakatvena vāhikopādhirna tatsamavāyāt, tādātmyād vā, tathā hi ḍittho 'yamityatrāpi ḍitthaśabdo vācyatvopalakṣakatayā piṇḍopādhirna tu tatsamavāyāt tādātmyād veti /
children.translated_text: Just as in "the cow-possessing <s>Vāhīka</s>," cow-ness is a qualifier of <s>Vāhīka</s> through its capacity to indicate a connection with [qualities of] a cow — not through inherence in him, nor through identity — so too in "this is <s>Ḍittha</s>," the word <s>Ḍittha</s> is a qualifier of the individual through [its capacity as] an indicator of denotability — not through inherence or identity.

children.text: yathā cātra vāhīke gauriti pratyayābhāvaḥ pramāṇam, tathātrāpi vṛkṣaviśaiṣe ḍittho 'yamiti pratyayābhāvaḥ pramāṇamiti samudāyārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And just as the absence of the cognition "this <s>Vāhīka</s> is a cow" is the evidence [that the relation is not identity], so too the absence of the cognition "this particular tree is <s>Ḍittha</s>" is the evidence — this is the overall meaning.

children.text: nanu śabdapuraḥsaratvaniyamād vikalpasya tadupāyatā vā tadviṣayatvaṃ vā syāt, tatpuraḥsaratvaniyamasyātadupāyādatadviṣayatvānniyamato vyāvṛtteḥ tatra yadyarthavikalpastacchabdavipayastadā siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitam /
children.translated_text: Now, since conceptual cognition is invariably preceded by words, there would be either the means-relation [of the word] to it or its being the object [of that cognition] — because the invariable precedence of what is neither a means nor an object is excluded by restriction. Now, if the conceptual cognition of the object is [the same as] the conceptual cognition of the word, then what we desire is established.

children.text: athopāyastadā jñāto 'jñāto vā? ajñātatve nirvikalpakatvānupapattireva, tasmāt śabda upāyo bhavan jñāta eva vaktavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [the word is merely] a means, is it cognized or not? If not cognized, the very nature of being indeterminate would not be possible — therefore the word, if it is a means, must be said to be cognized.

children.text: na cāsannihite jñānamasti /
children.translated_text: And there is no cognition of what is not present.

children.text: tasmādarthatādātmyāt śabdasyārthasannidhānameva tatsannidhiḥ ityarthālocanameva tadālocanamityanicchatāpi svīkartavyamityata āha--yattviti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the identity of the word with the object, the very presence of the object is the presence of the word, and the very apprehension of the object is the apprehension of the word — even one who does not wish to must accept this — therefore he says: "But what..."

children.text:
na tāvat śabdaḥ pūrvaṃ niyamato bhavati vikalpasya /
kiṃ nāma? vyutpannasya śabdasmaraṇapuraḥsaratvaṃ niyamavad dṛṣṭam /
na caitāvataiva ghaṭajñānasya ghaṭaśabdaviṣayatvam /
tathā sati ghaṭābhāvajñānasyāpi ghaṭaviṣayatā syāt, tatsmaraṇapuraḥsaratvāt /
children.translated_text: If it were so, even the cognition of the absence of a pot would have the pot as its object, since it is preceded by the recollection of that [pot].

children.text: tasmād ghaṭe vikalpayitatavye anupāyo viṣayaśca ghaṭaśabdaḥ kimiti niyamataḥ smaryata ityavaśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when a concept of the pot is to be formed, the pot-word, being neither a means to it nor its object — why is it invariably recalled? — this remains [to be answered].

children.text: tatreyaṃ smaraṇaparipāṭī kathiteti /
children.translated_text: The sequence of recollection for that has been described thus.

children.text: śabdapuraḥsarā śabdasmaraṇapuraḥsarā ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Preceded by word" means "preceded by the recollection of the word" — that is the meaning.

To begin with, the word does not invariably precede conceptual cognition. What then? The precedence of word-recollection is observed as regular only for the educated person. And not by this alone is the cognition of the pot an object of the pot-word.

children.text: atraiva vṛddhasaṃmatimāha--yadāhuriti /
children.translated_text: He states the view of the elders (<s>vṛddhas</s>) on this very point: "As they say..."

children.text: pratisambandhipiṇḍadarśanasahakṛtastatsaṃskāraḥ smṛtiṃ janayati, dhūmānubhavasahakṛta iva mahānasasthadahanānubhavaprabhavaḥ saṃskāraḥ tatsmṛtim /
children.translated_text: The residual impression of that [word], aided by the perception of the corresponding individual, generates recollection — just as the residual impression arising from the experience of fire in a kitchen, aided by the experience of smoke, generates the recollection of that [fire].

children.text: na caitāvatā niyameva śabdasmaraṇapiṇḍavikalpayorūpāyopeyabhāvaḥ, śabdasya vā vikalpaviṣayatvaṃ sidhyati, yena tayostādātmyamāśaḍkyeta /
children.translated_text: And not by this alone is the means-end relation of word-recollection and individual-concept established as a rule, nor is the word's being an object of the concept established — such that one would suspect their identity.

children.text: tathā sati vahnismaraṇadhūmavikalpayorapi tathābhāvaḥ syāt, vahnerapi vā dhūmavikalpaviṣayatā bhavediti vārttikārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: If it were so, then there would be a similar relation between fire-recollection and smoke-concept, or fire too would be an object of the smoke-concept — this is the meaning of the <s>vārttika</s>.

children.text:
syādetat /
sarva eva vyavahāraḥ svārthaḥ parārtho vā vikalpasādhyo na tvālocanenāpi kaścidarthaḥ sādhayitavyo 'sti /
children.translated_text: One might say this: all practical activity whatsoever, whether for oneself or for others, is accomplished by conceptual cognition — but no purpose at all is to be accomplished by bare apprehension.

children.text: ato niṣprayojanamidaṃ kathamutpadyata ityata āha--tasmāditi /
na tāvat sarvasyaivotpattimataḥ prayojanaṃ piśitacakṣuṣaḥ sākṣātkurmaḥ /
children.translated_text: To begin with, we do not directly see the purpose of absolutely everything that arises, with our meat-eyes.

children.text: na ca prayojanāpratipattimātreṇa paṭutarapratyakṣaparikalitamapi kāryaṃ nānumanyāmahe /
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that merely from the non-apprehension of a purpose we do not infer even an effect that has been observed by a keener perception.

children.text: tadetat prayojanāpratipattilakṣaṇamalīkamuttaram /
children.translated_text: Hence this response characterized by non-apprehension of purpose is spurious.

children.text: tathāpi sphuṭaṃ savikalpakotpattirevāsya prayojanam iti sādarśiteti //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, the purpose of this [bare apprehension] is clearly the very generation of conceptual cognition — and this has been shown.
Therefore, since this [bare apprehension] is without purpose, how does it arise? — to this he says: "Therefore..."

children.text: nāmadheyasmaraṇāyeti /
children.translated_text: "For the recollection of the name" —

children.text: nāmāvacchinne vikalpe kartavye yato na viśiṣyate viśeṣeṇa na gṛhyate, ato vaidharmyasya yogyapramāṇabādhitatvāt tadarthajñānaṃ tādṛgeva bhavati tatsamānajātīyameva bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the meaning is: when a concept delimited by the name is to be formed, since [the object] is not differentiated — i.e. not grasped — by a distinguishing feature, because the dissimilarity is sublated by the appropriate <s>pramāṇa</s>, that cognition of the object is just of that kind — i.e. belongs to the same class as that [name-delimited concept].

children.text: ato bhāṣyapaunarūktyaṃ pariharato na sādhyāviśiṣṭo heturiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in removing the redundancy of the <s>bhāṣya</s>, the reason is not undifferentiated from the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved).

children.text: vyapadeśavyākhyayā bhāṣyakāreṇa sūcitaṃ hetuṃ sphuṭayati--nanviti /
children.translated_text: He makes explicit the reason indicated by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> through the explanation of designation: "Now..."

children.text: arthavyapadeśākāram arthavyapadeśaviṣayam /
children.translated_text: "Of the form of object-designation" means: having the object-designation as its content.

children.text: viṣayirūpajñānasya tāvadrūpaviṣayatobhayavādisiddhā /
children.translated_text: The cognition of the object that has such a form — its having that [form] as its object is accepted by both disputants.

children.text: tasya ca tadvyapadeśaviṣayatā tadā syāt yadi rūpatadvyapadeśayorabhedaḥ syādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And its having that designation as its object would be the case only if there were non-difference between the form and its designation — that is the meaning.

children.text:
anyenānyasya vyapadeśe atiprasaḍgo vyavahāravilopaśca vipralambhādityatra tannāmadheyatvādeva niyama iti sphuṭaṃ bhāṣya eva /
svarūpeṇaiva viṣayeṇaiva vā kimiti jñānaṃ na vyapadiśyata ityetad vivṛṇvan pariharati--arthākārameveti /
children.translated_text: In the designation of one thing by another, there would follow over-extension and the disruption of practical activity, due to deception — and on this point, the <s>bhāṣya</s> itself makes clear: "because of being its very name." Resolving the question of why cognition is not designated by its own form or by its object alone, he explains and resolves: "Having the form of the object alone..."

children.text:
ātmānaṃ prati tāvat svarūpeṇaiva jñānamajñānād vyavacchidyate, jñānāntarāt tu viṣayeṇāpītyetat ko nāma nābhyupaiti? parasya tu nityaparokṣaṃ parajñānam /
ata eva tadviṣayo 'pi tat kathaṃ svarūpaviṣayābhyāṃ paro bodhyatām? kathaṃ vā abodhito vyavaharatām? tasmāt tajjñānavācakena jñānamarthavācakena cāryamasau pratipādyaḥ /
na cājñātena
children.translated_text: With regard to oneself, cognition is distinguished from ignorance by its very intrinsic nature, and from another cognition by its object as well — who does not accept this? But for another person, the cognition of others is always beyond direct apprehension. For this very reason, even the object of that [cognition] — how can the other person be made to understand through both intrinsic nature and object? And how can one who has not been made to understand engage in practical activity? Therefore, that [cognition] must be communicated through a word denoting cognition and a word denoting the object. And one cannot understand the denoted through an unknown

children.text: vācakena vācyamadhigattumarhatītyavarjanīyatayā pratipādako vācakamuccārayati /
children.translated_text: denotant — therefore, the communicator, because it is unavoidable, utters the denotant.

children.text: nacaitāvatā arthaśabdayorabhedasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And this alone does not establish the non-difference of word and object.

children.text: na hi pramāṇavyatirekeṇa prameyamadhigantuṃ na śakyate ityetāvataiva tayorabhedaḥ syāditi tadidamuktam--anyathā aśakyatvāditi //
children.translated_text: For the mere fact that the knowable cannot be apprehended without a means of valid knowledge does not entail the non-difference of the two — this is what was stated: 'otherwise, because of impossibility.'

children.text: nanu kadācidarthajñānakāle 'pi śabdo vyāpriyata eva, yadā prayojakavṛddhāt prayojyavṛddhor'thamadhigacchatītya āha--pratīyamānatayā viṣayatayetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Now, sometimes even at the time of apprehending the object, the word does indeed operate — namely, when the learner (<s>prayojyavṛddha</s>) apprehends the object from the teacher (<s>prayojakavṛddha</s>) — to this he says: 'by being cognized' means: by being an object — this is the meaning.

children.text:
syādetat /
utkarṣāpakarṣādyanuvidhāyitvaṃ hetuḥ kīdṛgityata āha--tadaneneti /
na tāvat tāratamatvāderūtkarṣānmayūrāderiva gavāderapyutkarṣaḥ pratīyate /
na hi gośabde karṇajapite 'pabhraṣṭe vā aṇīyān gauḥ kṛśa upahatākṛtirvikṛto vā pratīyate, viparīte vā viparītaḥ /
children.translated_text: For when the word 'cow' is whispered in the ear or mispronounced, one does not cognize a smaller cow, an emaciated one, one of impaired form, or a deformed one — nor the opposite from the opposite [pronunciation].

children.text: nāpi sādhutvādibhedavato gośabdasya prāśastyamaprāśastyaṃ ca kiñcidasti /
children.translated_text: Nor does the word 'cow,' differentiated by correctness and so forth, have any excellence or deficiency.

children.text: nandābhadretyādimaṅgalasaṃjñāniveśasya tvarthamaṅgalyādivyabhicāraḥ sphuṭatara eva, abhadrādāvapi bhadrādivyapadeśāt /
children.translated_text: But as for the installation of auspicious names like <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Bhadrā</s> — the deviation from the auspiciousness of the object and so forth is quite clear, since even what is inauspicious is designated by auspicious names.

children.text: tasmād vyavahārotkarṣāpakarṣamātreṇa nobhadasiddhiratiprasaḍgādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, mere superiority and inferiority in practical usage does not establish non-difference [of word and object], because of over-extension — this is the meaning.

One might say: what kind of reason is 'conforming to superiority, inferiority, and the like'? To this he says: 'by this then.' To begin with, the superiority arising from gradation and the like — the superiority of the cow and the like, unlike the peacock and the like — is not cognized [through the word].

children.text: asyaiva sākṣādavyapadeśyapadāt pratīyamānasyaiva /
children.translated_text: Of that very [entity] which is directly cognized — from the word that cannot be designated [as the thing itself].

children.text: śabdānuvyādharahitatā śabdārthānuvyādharahitatopapattirityato 'sya nirākaraṇaṃ sūcitamiti pūrvoktena na virodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: The justification that the word's non-pervasion [of the object] establishes the non-pervasion of word-meaning [identity] — and therefore its refutation has been indicated — hence there is no contradiction with what was said before.

children.text: nanu vārttikatātparyavyākhyānamupakramya bhāṣyavyākhyā akāṇḍakūṣmāṇḍapatanavṛttāntamanuharatītyata āha--tadetabhdāṣyamiti /
tadetad vārttikaṃ vyākhyātumayamasmākaṃ bhāṣyavyākhyāpariśrama ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: this labor of commenting on the <s>bhāṣya</s> is for the purpose of explaining this very <s>vārttika</s>.

children.text: śabdo hi yatkāryo yatkāraṇaṃ yadgrāhyo yatpramāṇaṃ yadvirodhi yaddharmā yadrūpo yadviṣayaḥ, tadakāryastadakāraṇaṃ tadagrāhyastadapramāṇaṃ tadavirodhyataddharmātadrūpo 'tadviṣayor'thaḥ pratyakṣata evāvasīyate /
children.translated_text: For it is ascertained through direct perception itself that the object is: not the effect of that which the word is the effect of, not the cause of that which the word is the cause of, not graspable by that by which the word is graspable, not a <s>pramāṇa</s> of that which the word is a <s>pramāṇa</s> of, not opposed to that which the word is opposed to, not having the properties that the word has, not having the form that the word has, not having the object that the word has.

children.text: tadetadasyārthajñānasya viṣayabhedānuvidhāyitvaṃ śabdābhdedagrāhakatvam /
children.translated_text: This very conformity of the cognition of the object to the difference of the object — that is the [cognition's] quality of grasping the difference from the word.

children.text: yadi punareṣā pratītirbhedamullikhantyapyavadhīryate, tadoktadharmāṇāmavirodhe dharmiparivartenāpyupalambhāḥ syuḥ //
children.translated_text: But if this cognition, though suggesting difference, is disregarded, then even with a change of property-bearer, apprehensions [could be had] with non-opposition of the stated properties.
Now, having begun the explanation of the purport of the <s>vārttika</s>, [this] commentary-explanation emulates the manner of an untimely gourd falling — to this he says: 'this very <s>bhāṣya</s>.'

children.text:
tatrodāharaṇārthaṃ kāṃścidāha--cākṣuṣaṃ hīti /
cākṣuṣaṃ hi cakṣuṣaiva janyate, rūpa eva niyatam rūpeṇeva nirūpyate; na śabde pravartate, na śabdenaiva nirūpyata ityarthaḥ /
evamuttaratrāpi /
viṣayiviṣayāniyamaprasaḍgāmuktvā karmakaraṇāniyamaprasaṅgamāha--api ceti /
nanu śrotramevāsya kadācinnāstītyata āha--asti hīti /
kimatra pramāṇamata āha"--śabdajñānaṃ ceti /
nanu locanābhāve 'pyagrahaṇamupapadyata ityata āha--asti hīti /
kimatra pramāṇamata āha--rūpajñānaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: What is the evidence for this? To this he says: 'and the cognition of form.'

children.text: upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
children.translated_text: And this is merely illustrative.

children.text: arthasāmānyasya sarvendriyagrāhyatvāt śabdasāmānyamapi sarvendriyairgṛhyeta, śabdasāmānyasya vā śrotrendriyaikavedyatvāt arthasāmānyamapi śrotrendriyaikavedyaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Since the universal of objects (<s>arthasāmānya</s>) is graspable by all sense-organs, the universal of sound too would be grasped by all sense-organs — or, since the universal of sound is knowable by the auditory sense alone, the universal of objects too would be knowable by the auditory sense alone.

children.text: tathā cendriyāntarāṇāṃ vaiyarthyamityapi draṣṭavyamiti //
children.translated_text: And if so, the other sense-organs would be purposeless — this too should be considered.

For that purpose, he states some examples: 'visual [cognition], for...' For a visual cognition is generated only by the eye, is restricted to form alone, and is determined by form alone; it does not operate on sound, and is not determined by sound alone — this is the meaning. Likewise in what follows. Having stated the undesirable consequence of non-restriction between cognizer and cognized, he states the undesirable consequence of non-restriction of action and instrument: 'moreover.' Now, [one might say] it simply does not have an ear at that time — to this he says: 'it does have.' What is the evidence for this? To this he says: 'and the cognition of sound.' Now, even in the absence of eyes, non-grasping is tenable — to this he says: 'it does have.'

children.text:
itaretarābhāvavattāvyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgamāha--aśabda iti /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
anutpanno vinaṣṭo 'tyantāsannityatrāpyabhāvatraye vivakṣitaviparītamāpadyata iti mantavyam /
itaretarābhāvavyapadeśe virodhaprasaṅgamāha--abhāva iti /
atrāpyanutpādo vināśo 'tyantābhāva iti viruddhaṃ syāditi mantavyam /
iha hyarthaśabdenendriyagrāhya evābhipretor'yamāṇatayeti vyākhyānāt /
indriyasya ca grāhyaḥ sa eva yastajjanyajñānaviṣayaḥ /
tadamī cakṣurādisannikṛṣṭā apyanyaviṣayajñānāpekṣāyā
children.translated_text: He states the undesirable consequence of the absence of the practical usage of mutual absence: 'non-sound.' And this is merely illustrative. With respect to 'unarisen,' 'destroyed,' and 'absolutely non-existent' too, it should be understood that in the three types of absence, the opposite of what is intended would follow. He states the undesirable consequence of contradiction in the designation of mutual absence: 'absence.' Here too, it should be understood that in 'non-arising,' 'destruction,' and 'absolute absence,' what is contradictory would follow. For here, by the expression 'object-word,' what is intended is precisely what is graspable by the sense-organ. And what is graspable by a sense-organ is that very thing which is the object of the cognition generated by that [sense-organ]. And these [objects], even though in contact with the eye and other [sense-organs], from the standpoint of the requirement of cognition of another [object],

children.text:
atadarthā eva /
evaṃ cendriyagatijñāne kaḥ pratyakṣatāyāḥ prasaṅgaḥ?
children.translated_text: are not intended for that [other cognition]. And if so, what is the undesirable consequence for the cognition of sense-organ activity being perceptual?

children.text:
na hi tadapekṣayā dhaṭādayastadarthāḥ /
tasmādaprasakte 'pyarthaśabdasya padārthamātraparatvamabhyupagamya parihāre gatyantaraṃ vārttikakṛtā darśitam /
tacca duḥkhabodhamiti vyācaṣṭe--naitaditi /
children.translated_text: And that [resolution] is explained as being difficult to understand: 'not this.'

children.text: naitadindriyārthasannikarṣādupajāyate sattāmātravyavasthitāt /
children.translated_text: 'Not this' — it does not arise from mere sense-object contact that is established merely in existence.

children.text: indriyārthasannikarṣo hyajñāyamāna eva sattāmātravyavasthitaḥ pratyakṣe vivakṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For sense-object contact, even while being unknown [i.e. not cognized], being established merely in existence, is what is intended in [the definition of] perception.

children.text: anumāne tu liṅgasya jñāyamānatvameva vivakṣitam, na tu sattetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But in inference, what is intended is precisely the cognizedness of the inferential mark, not [its mere] existence — this is the meaning.

For with reference to that [sense-organ activity], pots and the like are not intended for that. Therefore, even though it is not relevant, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, accepting that the term 'object' (<s>artha</s>) refers merely to any category, has shown a different way of resolving [the difficulty].

children.text:
nanvanumāne 'pi liḍgāsattaiva ki na vivakṣitetyata āha--ata eveti /
tatsmaraṇamātrādeveti /
mātragrahaṇaṃ sattāmamipretya natvanumeyajñānaṃ prati kāraṇatāmamipretya, dhūmasyaiva jñāyamānasya tatkāraṇatvāt /
anyathā tatkālānanuvidhānaprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would follow the consequence of non-conformity to the time of that [inferential mark].

children.text: catra hi viṣayānapekṣaṃ jñānameva kāraṇaṃ tatra na viṣayakālānuvidhānam /
children.translated_text: For here, the cause is cognition alone, independent of the object — therefore there is no conformity to the time of the object.

children.text: yathā abhāvajñāne pratiyogijñānajanye pratiyoginaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in the cognition of absence, which is generated by the cognition of the counter-positive — [there is no temporal conformity] of the counter-positive.

children.text: api ca liḍgānapekṣasya liṅgajñānasya liḍgijñānajanakatve pramāṇādīnāṃ gatidvayavādo 'pi tatra tatra na syāt //
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the cognition of the inferential mark, independent of the mark [as existing], were to generate the cognition of the thing indicated by the mark, then the twofold classification of <s>pramāṇas</s> and the like would not apply in various cases.

Now, why is the mere existence of the inferential mark not intended in inference too? To this he says: 'for this very reason.' 'From the mere recollection of that.' The word 'mere' is intended to exclude [mere] existence, not to exclude the causality [of the recollection] for the knowledge of the inferable, since the smoke itself, when cognized, is the cause of that [inferential knowledge].

children.text:
tadayamarthaḥ /
indriyārthasannikarṣāt sattāmātravyavasthitādutpadyate jñānaṃ tatsādhakatamaṃ pratyakṣam /
liḍgāt tu
children.translated_text: This then is the meaning: cognition that arises from sense-object contact, established merely in existence, and that which is its most effective instrument — is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). But from an inferential mark

children.text: pañcarūpasampannādapi jñāyamānādevāsato 'pi yadutpadyate jñānaṃ tadanumānamiti //
children.translated_text: that is endowed with the five characteristics, even though existing, that which arises only when it is cognized — that is <s>anumāna</s> (inference).

children.text:
nanvindriyaviṣayeṣvityadhyāhārastarhi sūtre pūrveṣāṃ kiṃ mūlam ityata āha--imaṃ ceti /
na hyanumeyasyendriyeṇa sannikarṣāditi vadatā hyevamuktaṃ yasyendriyeṇa sannikarṣāt tajjñānamutpadyate nāsau tasya viṣayaḥ, yastu viṣayo na tasyendriyeṇa sannikarṣāt idaṃ jāyate /
tasmādindriyārthasannikarṣādupajātaṃ vijñānaṃ yadi tadarthaviṣayameva bhavati, tadā tatpratyakṣam /
na caitat sūtrāt labhyate /
tasmād vārttikakṛtā eva kṛto 'yamadhyāhāra iti keścid buddham /
sa
children.translated_text: Now, if 'with respect to sense-objects' must be supplied in the <s>sūtra</s>, then on what basis did the earlier [commentators establish this]? To this he says: 'and this.' For one who says 'the sense does not come into contact with the inferable' has said this: that from whose contact with the sense-organ the cognition of it arises — that is not its object; and what is its object — this [cognition] does not arise from the contact of that with the sense-organ. Therefore, if the cognition arising from sense-object contact pertains only to that object [with which the sense is in contact], then it is <s>pratyakṣa</s>. But this is not obtainable from the <s>sūtra</s> [alone]. Therefore, this supplementation was made by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> alone — so some have understood. But that

children.text: cāyamasaṅgato bodhaḥ, adhyāhārasyobhayathāpyanupapatteḥ, tadvyāvartyasyānyathaiva vyāvartitatvādaprasakteścatyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: understanding is incorrect — because the supplementation is untenable in either case, and because what it is meant to exclude has already been excluded otherwise, and because it is irrelevant — this is the meaning.

children.text: indriyārthasannikarṣādutpannasya hi jñānasya vyabhicārasaṃbhādavyabhicārīti viśeṣaṇaṃ yadyapi nānupapannam, tathāpyetadvyāvarttyasya sāmānyalakṣaṇenaiva vyāvṛttatvāt niṣprayojanamidam /
avaśyaṃ ca tadanuvartanīyam /
children.translated_text: And [the general definition] must necessarily be maintained [as applying here too].

children.text: na hi yata ityadhyāhṛtapadena karaṇamātraṃ parāmṛśyate tasyāprakṛtatvāt, kiṃ tu pramākaraṇam /
children.translated_text: For by the supplemented word 'from which' [<s>yataḥ</s>], it is not mere instrumentality that is referred to — since that is not the topic — but rather the instrumentality of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>).

children.text: tathā cāyamarthaḥ, indriyārthasannikarṣotpannaṃ jñānaṃ yataḥ pramāṇād bhavati tatpratyakṣam /
children.translated_text: And thus the meaning is: the cognition arising from sense-object contact that comes from a <s>pramāṇa</s> — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ ca vyabhicāriṇi kaḥ prasaṅga ityata āha--yadyapīti //
children.translated_text: And if so, what is the relevance to what is deviating? To this he says: 'although.'

For although the qualification 'non-deviating' (<s>avyabhicārin</s>), as a distinguisher of the cognition arising from sense-object contact from [cases of] possible deviation, is not untenable, nevertheless, since what it is meant to exclude [i.e. error] is already excluded by the general definition [of <s>pramāṇa</s>] alone, this [qualification] is purposeless.

children.text:
nanvavyabhicāripadakaraṇaṃ pramāṇapadānuvartanaṃ veti kaścid viśeṣa ityata āha--anyatheti /
avyabhicāripadaṃ pramāṇaparamityarthaḥ, pramāṇasyaivāvyabhicāritvāt /
yadyapi tatra tatpūrvakamiti lakṣaṇapadaparyālocanayaiva vyabhicārinirāsaḥ,
children.translated_text: Now, is there any difference between inserting the word 'non-deviating' and maintaining the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>'? To this he says: 'otherwise.' The meaning is: the word 'non-deviating' is tantamount to [the word] '<s>pramāṇa</s>,' since <s>pramāṇa</s> itself is non-deviating. Although the exclusion of what deviates is [already] achieved through the consideration of the definitional term 'preceded by that' (<s>tatpūrvaka</s>),

children.text:
na hyuktarūpe dve pratyakṣe pūrvaṃ yasya jñānasya tadvyabhicāriṇīmapi pramāṃ janayet /
ata eva tadarthaṃ tatra sāmānyalakṣaṇānuvartanamasārameva /
tathāpyevaṃbhūtapratyakṣadvayajanite saṃskāre nirṇaye ca anumānatvaprasaṅgastadavastha eva /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, the undesirable consequence that the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and the determinate cognition generated by two such perceptions would be inference remains as before.

children.text: tasmāt tannivṛttyarthaṃ pramāṇapadaṃ na kṛtaṃ cedavaśyamanuvartanīyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, if the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>' has not been included for preventing that [consequence], then [the general definition] must necessarily be maintained — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadyevaṃ kimavyabhicāripadaprayojanamityata āha--tathāpīti nopayujyate na ca śakyate parasparāśrayaprasaḍgādityapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: If so, what is the purpose of the word 'non-deviating'? To this he says: 'nevertheless.' It should also be noted that it is neither useful nor possible [to omit it], due to the undesirable consequence of mutual dependence.

children.text: tathāpi niyamo na sphuṭībhūta ityata āha--tatreti //
children.translated_text: Yet even so, the restriction has not become clear — to this he says: 'therein.'

for no two perceptions of the described type would first generate even a deviating cognition and then a valid one. For this very reason, the maintenance of the general definition there is pointless for that purpose.

children.text:
nanvanumānavadavyabhicārasiddhyā phalasiddhirna pratyakṣe yathā, tathā śabde 'pi /
tatastadavabodhanārtha tatrāpyavyabhicāripadāvatāraprasaṅga ityata āha--śabdādau tviti /
pratyakṣe phalāvyabhicāranirṇayenaivāvyabhicāraniścaya
children.translated_text: Now, just as in inference the result is established through the establishment of non-deviation, it is not so in perception — and likewise in verbal testimony too. Therefore, there would follow the consequence of introducing the word 'non-deviating' there too — to this he says: 'but in verbal testimony and the like.' The restriction is: the certainty of non-deviation is solely through the certainty of the result in the case of perception,

children.text:
iti niyamo nānyatretyarthaḥ /
avyabhicāripadopādānaṃ phalaviśeṣaṇatayeti śeṣaḥ /
ayaṃ ca niyamaḥ svarūpato 'pi phaladvāraiva pratyakṣamunnīyate, na tvanyatheti /
children.translated_text: And this restriction is: perception is ascertained from its intrinsic nature only through the result — not otherwise.

children.text: anumānādikaṃ tu pratītaṃ satphalāya kalpate, na tvanyatheti niyame sati syāditi /
children.translated_text: But inference and the like, once cognized, serve as [evidence for] a true result — and this would hold only when such a restriction exists.

children.text: ayamapyarthākṣiptatayā prāgeva darśito dvayīti /
children.translated_text: This too, as being implied by the meaning, was shown earlier as twofold.

children.text: aparamapyutpattijñaptibhyāṃ niyamadvayaṃ śliṣṭamāha--athaveti //
children.translated_text: He states yet another pair of restrictions, coherent with both origination and indication: 'or alternatively.'
not elsewhere — this is the meaning. The remainder is: the inclusion of the word 'non-deviating' is as a qualifier of the result.

children.text: kāraṇamutpādakaṃ pratyāyakaṃ ca ubhayaṃ sādhayati---na hīti /
children.translated_text: The cause — both as producer and as indicator — establishes both: 'for not.'

children.text: upādhiśaḍkānivṛttyarthaṃ tarkasahāyatvopavarṇanam //
children.translated_text: The description of being accompanied by <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) is for the purpose of removing the suspicion of adventitious conditions.

children.text:
āgamasyāpi ca vaktṛśrotṛgatatvena pratyakṣāpekṣā utpattau jñaptau ca cato 'taḥ saṃmugdhamāha--evamiti /
tathāpyayamarthaḥ kathamavyabhicāripadopādānamātrat labhyata ityata āha--na hīti /
tadayaṃ saṃkṣepaḥ /
children.translated_text: This then is the summary:

children.text: so 'yaṃ sūtrakārasyeha viśeṣataḥ prayatno jñāpayati yadetasminnavyabhicāriṇyanyatra vyabhicāraśaḍkaiva nāsti, ata ihaiva tadgrahāya viśeṣato yatitavyamiti /
children.translated_text: This special effort of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> here indicates that — since in this [perception] alone, which is non-deviating, there is simply no suspicion of deviation elsewhere — therefore, special effort must be made here alone for grasping that [non-deviation].

children.text: yadyapi jñāptipakṣe laukikavacasāṃ pravṛttisāmarthyādinā vyabhicārābhāvagrahaḥ, tathāpi pāralaukikāgamāvyabhicāraniścaya āptoktatvenaiva /
children.translated_text: Although, on the 'indication' interpretation, the non-deviation of ordinary statements is grasped through the capacity for practical activity and so forth, nevertheless, the certainty of the non-deviation of trans-mundane scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is solely through being spoken by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>).

children.text: tacca mūlabhūtapratyakṣaśuddhereveti //
children.translated_text: And that [trustworthiness] depends on the purity of the foundational perception.

And since <s>āgama</s> (scripture) too depends on perception through being in the speaker and the listener, both in origination and in indication — therefore, combining [all this], he says: 'thus.' Nevertheless, how is this meaning obtained merely from the inclusion of the word 'non-deviating'? To this he says: 'for not.'

children.text:
nanu bhāṣyavārttikāyoḥ kā gatiḥ? na hyayamarthastataḥ pratīyate /
kiṃ nāma? vyabhicārivyāvṛttimātramityata āha--tasmāt suṣṭhūktamiti /
sa evārthaḥ, kiṃ tu niyamyatayā, na tu vidheyatayetyāśayaḥ /
uccāvacamuccalata iti jalasādṛśya saṃkīrtanaṃ bhrāntibījatayā /
upaghātadoṣānnayanasyātapādinā /
etaduktaṃ bhavati /
upadarśitārthāprāpakatvaṃ vyabhicāraḥ /
na cārthena kaścidartha upadarśito yamaprāpayannartho vyabhicaret /
anyathārthopadarśanasvabhāvasya cotpattiḥ, na
children.translated_text: Now, what is the import of the <s>bhāṣya</s> and <s>vārttika</s>? For this meaning is not understood from them. What then? Merely the exclusion of what deviates — to this he says: 'therefore, well-said.' The meaning is the same, but [taken] as what is being restricted, not as what is being enjoined — this is the intention. The mention of similarity to water that rises and falls is as the seed of confusion. Due to the fault of impairment — of the eyes by sunlight and the like. What is stated amounts to this: deviation is the failure to lead to the object that has been presented. And no object has been presented by another object such that, by failing to lead to it, the object would deviate. And otherwise, the very origination of that which by nature presents the object — not

children.text:
cārthopadarśanasvabhāvo na cānyathotpannaḥ /
tasmādevaṃbhūto vyabhicāro jñānasyaiva na cārthasya /
tadidamuktam--pratyayo bhrānto jāyata iti /
vṛddhasaṃmatimāha--yathāhuriti /
andha iti yamyagdarśanopāyarahitatvamātraparam /
na paśyatītyapi samyagjñānābhāvamātropalakṣaṇaparam /
children.translated_text: 'Does not see' — this too is merely indicative of the absence of correct knowledge.

children.text: tena puruṣāparādhaḥ sa bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is the fault of the person.

children.text: atrādarśanaṃ viparītadarśanaṃ vetyaparādha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'fault' means either non-seeing or erroneous seeing — this is the meaning.

children.text: yathā hi sthāṇuradṛśyamānastathaiva puruṣatvenāpi daśyamāna iti tātparyam //
children.translated_text: For just as a post, when not seen, [is misidentified,] so too when seen as a person — this is the purport.

nor has the nature of showing the object, nor has it arisen in a different manner. Therefore, such deviation belongs only to cognition, not to the object. This is what is said: 'the cognition arises as erroneous.' He states the view approved by the elders: 'yathāhuḥ' (as they say). 'Blind' — this refers merely to the absence of means for correct vision.

children.text:
yadyani saṃśayo 'pi sāmānyalakṣaṇānuvṛttyaiva nirastastasyāpramāṇaphalatvāt, tathāpyavyabhicāripadaṃ niyamajñāpanārthamavaśyaṃ kartavyam /
tena ca vyabhicārivyudāsamukhenaiva niyamaḥ pradarśayitavyaḥ /
saṃśayo 'pi
children.translated_text: Although doubt too has been excluded by the very continuation of the general characteristic [of the definition of perception], since it too is a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> result, nevertheless the word '<s>avyabhicārin</s>' (non-deviating) must necessarily be included for the purpose of indicating the restriction. And by that [word], the restriction is to be demonstrated precisely by way of excluding what is deviating. And doubt too

children.text: vyabhicārijātīyaḥ, atastenaivāsya vyudāso yukta ityāśayavān āha--avyabhicāripadenaiveti //
children.translated_text: belongs to the class of what is deviating — therefore its exclusion by that very [word] is appropriate. With this intention he says: 'avyabhicāripadenaiva' (by the very word 'non-deviating').

children.text: nanu vyabhicāritvamevāsya katham? viparyājñānaṃ hi niścayākaram, ayaṃ tu na tathetyata āha--no khalviti /
children.translated_text: Now, how is it of the deviating class? For erroneous cognition has the form of a determinate judgment, but this [doubt] is not of that kind — therefore he says: 'no khalu' (surely not).

children.text: na hi niścayatvaṃ prayojakamatra, kiṃ tu visaṃvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is not determinacy that is the motivating factor here, but rather incongruence [with reality].

children.text: sa ca prāptyayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [incongruence] is the impossibility of attainment.

children.text: na ca prāptiyogo dvirūpasya vastunaḥ, kvacit kadācit kenacid aprāpterityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the impossibility of attainment [applies] to a thing that is of two forms — because of the non-attainment of some [aspect] somewhere at some time by someone — this is the meaning.

children.text: na ca vācyaṃ bhrānterabhrāntipratiyogitvādaniyatasya cārthasya kvacidapi
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that, since the object [of doubt], being indeterminate due to being the counterpositive of error, is not within

children.text:
pramāṇāgocaratvādasatkhyāteranabhyupagamācca sarvamidamasamañjasamiti /
no khalu dolāyamānaḥ sthāṇupuruṣavyatiriktaḥ
children.translated_text: the range of any <s>pramāṇa</s>, and since <s>asatkhyāti</s> (error of the non-existent) is not accepted — all this is incoherent. For surely, one who vacillates [does not perceive] some indeterminate object distinct from a post or a person

children.text: kaścidaniyato nāmārthaḥ parisphurati yatrāsamañjasaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: that would appear [to him], in which case there would be incoherence.

children.text:
nanu sthāṇupuruṣāvubhāvapi yadyāropitau tadobhayopamardātmanā bādhakena bhavitavyam /
athānyatadasyāropastadā aparasya pāramārthikatvāttatpratipatterabādhyatvameva syāt /
yathā yuktau rajatāṃśasya mithyātve śuklabhāsvaratvādiniścayasya satyatvam, tathā ca sthāṇvaṃśe niścayaḥ puruṣāṃśe tvekakoṭisanniveśavāneva vibhrama iti saṃśayo dattajalāñjaliḥ prasaktaḥ /
tasmād ubhayasmaraṇamātrātmako 'yamiti syāt /
na syāt, yatra tāvadubhayoranubhayātmake pāṣāṇastambhādau samāropastatrobhayopamardātmaka eva bādhaka iti kimatra vaktavyam? yatrāpyekatarāropastatrāpi nāparāṃśe niścayaḥ, parasparapratikṣepopasthitivyāhatyā aniścayātmakasyaiva jñānasyotpādāt /
yatra hi rajatatvārope 'pi śuklatvādau niścayastatrāropitānānopitayormitho virodhābhāvaḥ /
tasmādāropitānāropitatvāviśeṣe 'pi yatrāropitānāropitau parasparāviruddhau sa viparyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when there is no distinction between the superimposed and the non-superimposed, where the superimposed and the non-superimposed are non-contradictory to each other — that is error (<s>viparyaya</s>);

children.text: yatra tu parasparaviruddhau sa saṃśaya iti sarvamavadātam /
children.translated_text: but where they are mutually contradictory — that is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>). Thus everything is clear.

children.text: yadyevaṃ saṃśayo 'pi viparyayāntarbhūtastadapākaraṇenaivāpākṛtaśca /
children.translated_text: If so, doubt too, being subsumed under error, has been refuted by the very refutation of that [error].

children.text: kimarthaṃ tarhi vyavasāyātmakapadaṃ sūtrākāraścakāra? san vā sa udārārtho vyākhyātṛbhiḥ kimityupekṣitaḥ? tathābhūtor'vācīnaiḥ kathamunnīyata ityata āha--tasmāditi //
children.translated_text: For what purpose, then, did the author of the <s>sūtra</s> include the word '<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>' (of the nature of determination)? And if it has a significant meaning, why was it disregarded by the commentators? And how is it elicited by later [scholars] of such a character? — therefore he says: 'tasmāt' (therefore).

Now, if both the post and the person are superimposed, then the sublating cognition should have the nature of negating both. But if only one is superimposed, then the other, being real, [its cognition] should be unsublatable due to the veridicality of its cognition. Just as, in the doctrine [of error], when the silver-aspect is false, the determination of whiteness, luster, and the like is true — so too, the determination of the post-aspect is [true], while the person-aspect is merely a false superimposition of one alternative — and so doubt is a thing of the past. Therefore, one might think that [doubt] is merely an aggregate of memories of both. [But] this would not be the case. For where both are superimposed on something that is neither — such as a stone pillar and the like — there the sublating cognition is indeed of the nature of negating both — what is there to say about this? But where there is the superimposition of one [of the two], there too there is no certainty about the other aspect, because a cognition that is of the nature of non-certainty alone arises — due to the mutual obstruction of the presentation of mutual exclusion. For where, even when silver-nature is superimposed, there is certainty about whiteness and the like — there, there is no mutual contradiction between the superimposed and the non-superimposed.

children.text:
syādetaditi /
syāt tadavabodhārthaṃ, yadi tatpratyakṣaṃ syāt, na tvetadastītyarthaḥ /
hetumāha--abhilāpeti /
abhidhānākārasaṃsargayogyābhidheyākāraṃ hi tadityarthaḥ /
vipakṣād vyatirekamāha--na ceti /
abhidhānābhidheyasaṃsarge hi tadākārayoḥ saṃsarganiyamaḥ /
sa ca saṃyogasamavāyakāryakāraṇabhāvarūpastāvanna saṃbhavatītyāha--na hyarthe śabdāḥ santīti /
saṃyogena samavāyena kāryatayā veti śeṣaḥ /
tadātmāno veti /
children.translated_text: 'Nor are they of their nature' —

children.text: na hītyanuṣajyate /
children.translated_text: 'na hī' (for not) is to be carried over.

children.text: upapattimāha---tathā satīti /
children.translated_text: He states the justification: 'tathā sati' (this being so).

children.text: na ceti //
children.translated_text: 'Na ca' (and not).

'This might be so' — it might be for the purpose of its comprehension, if this [perception] were conceptual; but it is not — this is the meaning. He states the reason: 'abhilāpa' (verbal expression). For it [i.e., conceptual cognition] has the form of what is fit for the conjunction of designation-form and object — this is the meaning. He states the negative concomitance from the dissimilar: 'na ca' (and not). For in the conjunction of designation and designated, there is the rule of conjunction of their forms. And that [conjunction], in the form of contact, inherence, or cause-effect relation, is first of all not possible — he says: 'na hyarthe śabdāḥ santīti' (for words do not exist in the object). The completion is: through conjunction, inherence, or being an effect.

children.text: sa hi saṃvedanadharmo grāhyākārarūpo vā syāt? tannirapekṣagrāhakākārarūpo vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, arthāsaṃsparśī yataḥ, arthāsaṃsparśaścāsyātadvṛttitvādatadutpatteśceti pūrvaiva yuktirityāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For would that [connection with verbal expression] be a property of awareness, having the form of an apprehended aspect? Or would it have the form of an apprehending aspect that is independent of the object? The first is not [the case], since [the verbal expression] does not touch the object — and its not touching the object is because it neither inheres in the object nor arises from the object — this is the very reasoning stated earlier, the intention being:

children.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ, artheṣu tanniyojanāt /
children.translated_text: Nor the second, because of its assignment to objects.

children.text: aryamāneṣu bāhyeṣvartheṣveva tasyāmilāpasya niyojanāt /
children.translated_text: Because that verbal expression is assigned only to external objects that are being cognized.

children.text: niyogato bāhyasāmānādhikaraṇyena pratīterityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Because perception [occurs] necessarily in co-extension with the external — this is the meaning.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati saṃvedanākāro hi jñātṛtvādistatsāmānādhikaraṇyena pratīyate /
children.translated_text: What this says is: the awareness-aspect, namely knower-hood and the like, is cognized in co-extension with that [awareness].

children.text: abhilāpastu bāhyasanniyuktastatsāmānādhiraṇyenetyato na saṃvedanadharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: But verbal expression, being connected with the external, [is cognized] in co-extension with that [external object] — therefore it is not a property of awareness.

children.text: tasmād viṣayataḥ svarūpataśca yato 'sya nābhibhalāpasaṃsargayogyatāsambhavastasmādidamarthāt sarūpakādupajāyamānaṃ jñānaṃ vikalparūpamarthamevādarśayediti prasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the fitness for verbal-expression-conjunction does not arise either from the object or from the intrinsic nature [of the cognition] — there is the consequence that this cognition, arising from what is of the same form as the object, having the form of conceptual construction, would show only the object —

children.text: nāmilāpamarthasaṃsargitayeti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: not verbal expression in connection with the object — this is the completion.

children.text: syādetat /
children.translated_text: One might say this:

children.text: svakāraṇadupajātasya kāraṇamakāraṇaṃ vā kaścideva viṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some particular object is the domain of what has arisen from its own cause — whether it is a cause or a non-cause.

children.text: evaṃ cārthādupajātasyāpyaneko 'bhilāpo 'pyasya viṣayo yadi syāt ko doṣa ityata āha---na hīti /
children.translated_text: And thus, even for [a cognition] arising from the object, if multiple verbal expressions were its domain — what would be the fault? — therefore he says: 'na hī' (for not).

children.text: rūpāccakṣuṣo viṣayādupajāyamānaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ vijñānaṃ nayanāviṣayarasasahitamatad rūpamiti //
children.translated_text: A visual cognition arising from form, the object of the eye, does not [contain] taste that is not an object of the eye, [combined] with a non-form of that kind.

children.text:
etaduktaṃ bhavati /
sākāravādasiddhau tāvadanupaplutamākāramādadhadevārtho viṣayaḥ /
na ca śabdasaṃsargayogyatā
children.translated_text: What this says is: in the first place, on the thesis that cognition has form (<s>sākāravāda</s>), the object is that which imposes its uncorrupted form as the aspect. And the fitness for conjunction with words

children.text:
arthasyāsti yena tadākāraṃ jñānaṃ bhavet /
na cendriyavijñānaṃ śabdaḥ svatantra evākārādhāyako, vikalpakāle tadabhāvāt /
bhāve 'pi vā svatantraḥ pratibhāseta nārthasaṃsargitayetyuktam /
nirākārapakṣe 'pyātmānātmaprakāśanaśaktervijñānasya sa eva viṣayo yatrendriyaṃ
children.translated_text: does not belong to the object, by which the cognition would have that form. Nor is a word an independently form-imposing [cause] of sense-cognition, because of its absence at the time of conceptual construction. Or even if present, it would appear independently, not in connection with the object — thus it has been said. Even on the thesis that cognition is formless (<s>nirākāravāda</s>), the very domain of cognition — which has the power of self-illumination and other-illumination — is that in which the sense-organ

children.text: niyatasāmarthyam, anyathātiprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: has determinate capacity — otherwise there would be over-extension.

children.text: na ca cakṣurindriyāntaraviṣaye samartham /
children.translated_text: And the eye is not capable [of operating] in the domain of another sense-organ.

children.text: na ca cakṣurviṣayasyaiva śabdasaṃsargo 'stīti cintitamiti //
children.translated_text: And the conjunction with words does not exist for what is specifically the domain of the eye — this has been considered.

children.text: prasaṅgamuktvā viparyayārthamāha--tasmāditi /
children.translated_text: Having stated the consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>), he states the counter-positive: 'tasmāt' (therefore).

children.text: amilāpasaṃsargānapekṣamarthaṃ tatsaṃsargiṇamādarśayadadhyavasyad vikalpavāsanotthāpitaṃ nārthasāmarthyasamutthamiti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not depending on the conjunction with verbal expression, [a cognition] that shows the object as conjoined with that [verbal expression] and determines [it as such] — is produced by the arousal of conceptual impressions (<s>vikalpavāsanā</s>), not born from the power of the object — this is the purport.

children.text: viparyaye kiṃ bādhakamityata āha--aniyatārthagrāhi yataḥ, vikalpagatamarthākāraṃ pratyaniyāmakatvāt tasyetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: What is the sublating [argument] for the counter-positive? — therefore he says: 'because it apprehends an indeterminate object' — the meaning is: because [conceptual construction] does not determine the object-form present in conceptual construction.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati, yadi hi pratibhāsamānor'thopi vikalpasya janako bhavet, tadā tadākāraṃ niyamayet, na tu niyamayati, tadasannidhāvapi vikalpavāsanāvaśāt tasya tathāvidhākāropasthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: What this says is: if the appearing object were also the generator of conceptual construction, then it would determine its form. But it does not determine [it], because even in the absence of that [appearing object], through the force of the impressions of conceptual construction, [the cognition] presents a form of such a kind.

children.text: nanvindriyamasya janakamastu, na hi tasyākāraniyāmakatayā kārakatvamityata āha--mānasamiti /
children.translated_text: Now, let the sense-organ be its generator — for the sense-organ's causal status does not [depend on being] a determiner of [cognitive] form — therefore he says: 'mānasam' (mental).

children.text: manomātraprabhavamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: arising from the mind alone.

children.text: indriyamapi hi jñānajanakaṃ bhavadākāraniyāmakārthasannikarṣeṇaiva, na tu tannirapekṣam /
children.translated_text: For even the sense-organ, when generating cognition, [does so] only through the contact with an object that determines [cognitive] form — not independently of that.

children.text: na cāsya tathāvidhārthasannikarṣo 'stītyuktamiti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: And it has been said that [conceptual construction] does not have such object-contact — this is the purport.

children.text: nanu vivādādhyāsite vikalpe dṛśyatayaivārthākāraḥ parisphurati /
children.translated_text: Now, in the conceptual construction that is the subject of dispute, the object-form shines forth as if seen [directly].

children.text: na caivamubhayavādisiddhārthasannidhinipekṣavikalpeṣvaparokṣatayārthaḥ prakāśate, tadviśeṣo vikalpor'thasannidhisāpekṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that in conceptual constructions that depend on the presence of an object accepted by both parties, the object manifests with the character of directness; [rather,] the distinctive feature of conceptual construction [is that it] depends on the presence of the object.

children.text: tathā cārthasya tadākāraniyāmakatvāt tajjanakatvamanicchatāpyabhyupeyam /
children.translated_text: And thus, since the object determines the form of that [cognition], its being the generator must be accepted even by one who does not wish to.

children.text: anyathotprekṣāvyāpāratvād vikalpasya pravartakatvamapi na nirvahedityata āha--ātmīyamiti //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, because the operation of conceptual construction consists in imaginative projection, even its capacity to motivate activity would not be coherent — therefore he says: 'ātmīyam' (one's own).

children.text:
utprekṣā asadāropaṇaṃ yato bhavatyavaśyamato 'pyevamutprekṣāmaha iti vyāhāraḥ /
tiraskāro 'nadhyavasāyaḥ /
darśanaṃ sākṣātkaraṇam /
puraskāro bhedāgraho vā, taddhetuka āropo vā /
tatsiddhamiti /
prasaḍgādyupanibandhena /
yadi vivādādhyāsitā vikalpā arthasāmarthyalabdhajanmānaḥ, tadā na śabdakalpanānugatā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the conceptual constructions that are the subject of dispute have their origin in the power of the object, then they would not be accompanied by verbal construction — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadanugatatvamiti /
children.translated_text: 'Being accompanied by that' —

children.text: śabdakalpanānugatatvam /
children.translated_text: means being accompanied by verbal construction.

children.text: tasyopalabdhirabhilāpānugatatvaṃ nirākurvatī arthasāmarthyajatvaṃ virūṇaddhīti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The apprehension of that [verbal character] — while refuting accompaniment by verbal expression — also undermines [its] birth from the power of the object. This is the completion.

Imaginative projection (<s>utprekṣā</s>) is the superimposition of what is non-existent — that is what it necessarily involves, and hence the usage 'one imagines thus.' Disregard (<s>tiraskāra</s>) is non-determination. Direct seeing (<s>darśana</s>) is direct perception. Bringing forward (<s>puraskāra</s>) is either non-apprehension of difference, or the superimposition caused by that. 'This is established' — through the connection with the consequence and the like.

children.text:
asiddhaviruddhayorasambhavādiha sambhāvitatayā pūrvoktasmāraṇapuraḥsaraṃ sandigdhānaikāntikatvāśaḍkāmevāpanayati--na ceti /
artharūpamanukuryādartharūpasadṛśākāraṃ bhavedityarthaḥ /
tādātmyatadutpattibhyāmasaṃbaddharūpānukāre niyāmakābhāvāt sarvarūpānukāreṇa sarveṣāṃ sarvajñatāpattiḥ /
sadrūpānukāramātratvāt tadviṣayatāyā iti bhāvaḥ /
na hi tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ svarūpeṇopapujyate /
ki nāma? niyāmakatayā, tadatra saḍketa eva niyāmako yadi syāt ko doṣa ityāśayavānāśaṅkate--saḍketeti /
tadeva dṛṣṭaṃ sat smārayedetānniyameneti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: That very thing [i.e., the particular], having been seen, would cause the memory of these [individuals] with restriction — this is the completion.

children.text: kimetāvapītyata āha--tatraiva ceti /
children.translated_text: Even this much [is not sufficient]? — therefore he says: 'tatraiva ca' (and in that very domain).

children.text: anugatamanugamagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Continuous' (<s>anugata</s>) means the domain of continuity.

children.text: ata eva sāmānyaṃ deśakālānugatam, tatraiva saḍketasya sukaratvāditi bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the universal is continuous across space and time — because convention is easy in that very [domain] — this is the purport.

Since non-establishment and contradiction are not possible here, while they are suspected [by the opponent] — he dispels, preceded by the recollection of what was previously stated, the suspicion of doubtful inconclusiveness alone: 'na ca' (and not). 'It would imitate the object's form' means 'it would have a form similar to the object's form' — this is the meaning. Because in the absence of a determining factor for the imitation of a form unconnected [with the cognition] through identity or origination, there would follow the omniscience of all with respect to all forms, because the object-hood [of cognition] consists merely in the imitation of a similar form — this is the purport. For the connection characterized by identity or origination does not serve in its own form. What then? In its capacity as a determining factor. If here convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) alone were the determining factor, what would be the fault? — with this intention he raises the doubt: 'saṃketa' (convention).

children.text:
kimetāvatāpītyata āha--na ca tattat dṛṣṭaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ kiṃ tu svalakṣaṇaṃ darśanagocaraḥ /
sarūpakatvāditi śeṣaḥ /
sarūpakatvamevāsya kuta ityata āha--tadeva hīti /
children.translated_text: Whence even its being of the same form? — therefore he says: 'tadeva hī' (for that very thing).

children.text: paramārtho 'kṛtrimamanāropitaṃ rūpaṃ tenāstīti paramārthasat /
children.translated_text: <s>Paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality) is the uncreated, non-superimposed form — by which something exists is <s>paramārthasat</s> (ultimately real).

children.text: etadeva kuta ityata āha--vijñānasya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Even this — from where? — therefore he says: 'vijñānasya kāraṇam' (the cause of cognition).

children.text: vijñānasyeti prakṛtopayogāt kāraṇamarthakriyāsamarthaṃ yata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Of cognition' — because of its relevance to the present topic — 'cause' means 'capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>)' — this is the meaning.

Even with this much? — therefore he says: 'na ca tattat dṛṣṭam' — not that each of those has been directly seen; rather, the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is the domain of seeing. The completion is: 'because of being of the same form (<s>sarūpakatva</s>).'

children.text:
nanu sāmānyamapi kiṃ na darśanagocara ityata āha--na tu sāmānyamiti /
kutaḥ? sarvasāmarthyarahitaṃ hi tat /
sarvaḥ puruṣārtho heyopādeyarūpastasya sāmarthyaṃ śaktiḥ, tadrahitaṃ yasmāt tat /
na hi kiñcit puruṣaprayojanaṃ sāmānyasādhyamasti /
children.translated_text: For there is no human purpose whatsoever that can be achieved by a universal.

children.text: ator'thakriyāyāmaśaktatvāt na tat paramārthasat asattvānnatadvijñānajanakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, being incapable of causal efficacy, it is not ultimately real; and being not real, it is not a generator of cognition.

children.text: ajanakatvānna sarūpakam /
children.translated_text: And not being a generator, it is not of the same form [as reality].

children.text: asarūpakatvānna darśanagocara ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And not being of the same form, it is not within the domain of seeing — this is the meaning.

Now, is the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) too not within the domain of seeing? — therefore he says: 'na tu sāmānyam' (but not the universal). Why? For it is devoid of all capacity. All human purposes, having the form of the to-be-avoided and the to-be-adopted — their capacity, their power — it is devoid of that.

children.text:
nanu sāmānyasya tāvadarthakriyāvirahād darśanagocaratvaṃ mā bhūt, darśanagocarasyaiva tu vācyatāstu /
saḍketo 'pi tatra kenāpyupāyena bhaviṣyati /
tannirvicikitsameva tarhyarthakriyāsamarthavaspupratipādanābhiprāyavantaḥ prayojakavṛddhāḥ prayojyavṛddhāśca tathāvidhārthapratipattimantaḥ śābde vyavahāre upalabhyanta ityata āha--api ceti /
na hyaupṇyāt atirikto vahnirnāmāsti bauddharāddhānte /
na cobhayavādisaṃpratipattiviṣayaḥ pratītamauṣṇyaṃ śītāpanodanaṃ karotītyapi kadācit /
akurvaddhi sarvathā apratītaṃ na kuryādāropitaṃ vā /
na ca vahniśabdāt sarvathā vahnerapratītiḥ /
tasmāt
children.translated_text: Now, let the universal at least not be within the domain of seeing due to its lack of causal efficacy — but let that which is within the domain of seeing be expressible by words. And convention with respect to it will be achieved through some means. Without a doubt, then, the senior [teachers] who intend to convey things capable of causal efficacy — both those who motivate and those who are motivated — are observed in verbal practice as possessing the cognition of objects of such a kind — therefore he says: 'api ca' (moreover). For in the Buddhist doctrinal system, there is no fire apart from heat. Nor does perceived heat, which is a matter of agreement for both parties, ever produce the removal of cold. For if it did not [produce the removal of cold], then it would be either entirely unperceived or superimposed. And it is not the case that from the word 'fire,' fire is entirely unperceived. Therefore

children.text: śabdakalpanollikhitamavastveva vastvābhāsamityabhiprāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: the intention is: what is outlined by verbal construction is a mere non-entity that appears as an entity.

children.text:
jātyādīn paramārthikānabhyupetyāha--tanneti /
vivekena deśabhedenetyarthaḥ /
avacchedyāvacchedakabhāvena hi mitho yojanā viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ /
sa ca viviktadeśatāpratītyā vyāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that is pervaded by the cognition of occupying distinct spatial locations.

children.text: sā cāto nivarttamānā svavyāpyaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvamādāyaiva nivartate /
children.translated_text: And that [cognition of distinct locations], when ceasing, takes with it its own pervasion — [namely] the qualifier-qualified relation — as it ceases.

children.text: tataśca jātyādīnāṃ parasparamasambandhānna svatanatreṣu teṣu śabdo 'pi sukarasaḍketeḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, since universals and the like are mutually unrelated, verbal designation too is easy [to account for] when they are independent.

children.text: tathā ca na saṃsṛṣṭavedanamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, the meaning is: there is no cognition of [things] in association.

Without accepting universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like as ultimately real, he says: 'Therefore not...' 'By distinction' means by spatial difference — that is the meaning. For the mutual connection as delimited and delimiter is the qualifier-qualified relation (<s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s>).

children.text:
etena śabdasya vivekagrahasaṃbhave 'pi tadyojanā nirasto boddhavyā /
ekamasamuditam /
avibhāgamanaṃśam /
svalakṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: By this, even if verbal [cognition] can grasp distinction, its combination [with the object] should be understood as refuted. 'One' — not aggregated. 'Undivided' — without parts. '<s>Svalakṣaṇa</s>' (particular) —

children.text: trailokyavilakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: unique in the three worlds.

children.text: tathātatheti /
children.translated_text: 'In such-and-such a way' —

children.text: guṇakarmādisamuditatvena sādhāraṇatvena vikalpyate /
children.translated_text: is conceptualized as being associated with qualities, actions, and the like, [and] as being common.

children.text: na tu daśyata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But [it] is not perceived — that is the meaning.

children.text: api ca paramārthasadvastutrayavedane 'pi vivekeneti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Moreover, even in the cognition of three ultimately real entities, [the completion is:] 'through distinction.'

children.text:
nanu na hyekajñānaviṣayau samānakāle 'ḍgulyau na kāryakāraṇabhūte iti niyatapūrvāparatve 'pi te sarvajñaikavijñānagocarau na tatheti yuktaṃ vaktum /
yadyucyeta ko doṣaḥ? na hyupalabdhibhedābhedaprayukte kāraṇākaraṇatve /
kiṃ tarhi? yadanapekṣaṃ tat kāraṇam sāpekṣaṃ ca kāryamiti, tadatrāpi samānam /
ekajñānagocaratve 'pi yadavacchedakaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, it is not the case that two fingers that are objects of a single cognition at the same time are not in a cause-effect relation; even when the temporal sequence is fixed, they are the objects of a single cognition of the omniscient — so it is not proper to say 'not so.' If one were to say so, what fault [would there be]? For the [relations of] causality and non-causality are not brought about by the difference or non-difference of apprehension. What then? What is independent is the cause, and what is dependent is the effect — and the same [applies] here too. Even when they are objects of a single cognition, what delimits

children.text:
tadviśeṣaṇam, avacchedyaṃ ca viśeṣyamiti /
yattu naivaṃ na tat yathetyata āha--viśeṣaṇaṃ khalviti /
nānyatheti /
atiprasaḍgāditi śeṣaḥ /
tarhi upakāro 'pi kaścidastvityata āha--na caiketi /
kimiti na syādityata āha--tayoriti /
prasaḍgāditi śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The completion is: because of the absurd consequence.

children.text: svarūpataḥ paurvāparyaniyamaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The restriction of temporal priority and posteriority by intrinsic nature is the cause-effect relation.

children.text: jñāptitastu jñāpyajñāpakabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: But [the restriction] by cognition is the relation of what is made known and what makes known.

children.text: sa cāyamekajñānagocarayorekakālayośca dvirūpo 'pi niyato nāsti yasmādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the meaning is: this [relation], though twofold — [applying to things that are] objects of a single cognition and [to things] of a single time — is not definitively established anywhere.

is the qualifier, and what is delimited is the qualified. But that [the Buddhist view] is 'not so, not like that' — therefore he says: 'A qualifier indeed...' 'Not otherwise' — the completion is: because of over-extension. Then let there be some [other] kind of assistance — therefore he says: 'Nor a single...' Why should it not be [so]? — therefore he says: 'Of those two...'

children.text:
syādetat /
yadyapyuktasvarūpamupakāradvayaṃ na saṃbhavati tathāpyādhārādheyabhāvo bhavet, sa hi samānakālayoreva kuṇḍabadarayordṛṣṭaḥ /
kṣaṇabhaṅgastu tvayāpyupapādanīyo mayāpibhañjanīya ityata āha--api ceti /
children.translated_text: But momentary destruction is to be justified by you too, and to be refuted by me too — therefore he says: 'Moreover...'

children.text: yadyapi tīrthikaiḥ kuṇḍādhāvaśānna badarasyaiva apatanadharmakasyotpādaḥ svīkriyate sthaimaśraddhājaḍatvāt, tathāpi gatinivṛttilakṣaṇāṃ gurutvapratibandhakasaṃyogalakṣaṇāṃ vā sthitiṃ taddharmabhūtā vidadhadeva badarasya kuṇḍamādhāratayā abhyupetaṃ taiḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist philosophers) accept that it is not the mere origination of the berry — which by nature tends to fall — that occurs due to the support of the bowl, [this being] due to their dull-wittedness born of faith in permanence; nevertheless, the bowl is accepted by them as a support of the berry inasmuch as it produces a state — characterized by the cessation of motion, or characterized by a conjunction that obstructs gravity — that is a property of that [berry].

children.text: kiṃ cāto 'ta āha--tadvadihāpīti /
children.translated_text: What follows from that? — he says: 'Likewise here too...'

children.text: etāvatāpi kimityata āha--na ca śaktyantarairiti //
children.translated_text: Even this much — why? — therefore he says: 'Nor through other capacities...'

Now, even if the twofold assistance of the stated nature is not possible, there could be the relation of support and supported (<s>ādhārādheyabhāva</s>), for that is observed between a bowl and berries that exist at the same time.

children.text: yadyapi badaravajjātyādīnāṃ dharmasya kasyacidupajanāpāyarūpamupakāraṃ nābhyupagacchatyeva paraḥ, tathāpyabhyupagamavādo 'yaṃ saugatasyeti mantavyam //
children.translated_text: Although the opponent does not accept that universals and the like produce any assistance in the form of origination or destruction of any property [of the object], nevertheless this should be understood as an argument based on [the opponent's own] acceptance, [directed] against the Buddhist.

children.text: tathā ceti /
children.translated_text: 'And thus...'

children.text: sannityanena hi vikalpena sattvopakārasamartho viṣayīkṛtaḥ na ca tato 'nyaḥ kaścid dravyatvādyupakārasamartho 'sattvopakārasamartho 'sti, yatra dravyādivikalpāḥ sārthakāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: For by the alternative 'existent or permanent,' [only] what is capable of assisting existence has been made the object [of consideration]. And there is no other [entity] that is capable of assisting substance-hood and the like but not capable of assisting existence, with reference to which the conceptual constructions of substance and the like would be meaningful.

children.text: tasmādete dravyavatvādyupakārasamarther'the sattvopakārasamarthābhedini pravartamānāstadadhikaraṇamarthamaspṛśanto 'narthakāḥ prasaktā iti samudāyārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, these [conceptual constructions] — operating with respect to an object that is indistinguishable from what is capable of assisting substance-hood and the like, [which is itself] capable of assisting existence — without touching the object that is the locus of that [substance-hood] — are absurdly meaningless. This is the summary meaning.

children.text: bauddhasyātiparāmarśakuśalatāṃ codyasya cātitucchatāmālakṣyāsmākameva matilāghavaṃ saṃbhāvayiṣyatītyāśaḍkya tadgranthaṃ likhati--yadāheti /
children.translated_text: Suspecting that [the reader], noticing the excessive skill of the Buddhist in raising objections and the extreme triviality of the objection, would attribute superficiality of intellect to us [Naiyāyikas] — he records the [Buddhist's] text: 'What he says...'

children.text:
ayaṃ vārttikārthaḥ /
yasya darśane nānopādherapyarthasya dhīḥ vikalpadhīrgrāhikā bhedino viśiṣṭasya /
nānopādhyupakārāḍgaṃ yā śaktistadekātmanastasya /
sarvātmanā sarvaiḥ upādhibhirekasvabhāvasyaivopakāryasya viśeṣyasya grahe sati ko bhedo bhidyata iti bhedo viśiṣyata iti yāvat /
aniścitaḥ syāt? api tu sarvopādhimirviśiṣṭo niścita eva syādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Would it be undetermined? Rather, it would be determined as qualified by all qualifying conditions — that is the meaning.

children.text: emasyopādheḥ upakārakasvabhāve grāhye gṛhyamāṇe sati nopakārā upakārakāḥ svabhāvā upādhyantarāṇāṃ tato 'pare bhinna vidyante ye tasminnekopakārakasvabhāve dṛṣṭe 'pi na dṛṣṭāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: When the assisting nature — the nature to be grasped — of one qualifying condition is being grasped, the assisting natures — the natures — of the other qualifying conditions are not [seen as] different from that. [That is,] those others, which are different, which even when that one assisting nature is seen are not seen, do not exist.

children.text: kiṃ nāma? sa ervekasvabhāvaḥ sarveṣāmupakārakaḥ tatasadgrahe tadekopādhiviśiṣṭagrahe /
children.translated_text: What then? That very single nature is the assisting [nature] of all [qualifying conditions]. Therefore, in the grasp of that, in the grasp qualified by that single qualifying condition,

children.text: sakalagrahaḥ sakalopādhiviśiṣṭagrahaḥ prasakta ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: the complete grasp — the grasp qualified by all qualifying conditions — is entailed. That is the meaning.

This is the meaning of the <s>Vārttika</s>: In whose view, the cognition of an object with manifold qualifying conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) — [i.e.,] the conceptual cognition that grasps what is differentiated, what is qualified — [is such that:] the capacity that belongs to one who has the identity with all those [qualifying conditions] — that is, when the qualified, which is of a single nature with all qualifying conditions, is grasped in its entirety with all qualifying conditions — what difference is differentiated? — [the question is:] what distinguishing feature would be distinguished?

children.text:
nanu varaṃ vastusvabhāvavādamāsthāyānupakāryānupakārakayorapi viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaṃ spaṣṭadṛṣṭamupapādayituṃ śaktāḥ pare /
upādhupādhimabhdedāccāpaunarūktyam /
na punaḥ saugatāḥ sattvādīnāmupādhīnāṃ vastutvānabhyupagamāt /
evaṃ ca tvaccharāstvayyeva nipatitā ityata āha--asmākaṃ tviti /
