yacca gṛhṇanti sāmānyamātram, yaccādhyavasyanti santānam /
na manāgapi sāmānyenāpi rūpeṇa /
gāhante gocaranti /
tasyālīkatayā vastudharmatvābhāvādityarthaḥ /
tarhi kathamavisaṃvādakāḥ pravartakā vetyata āha--pāramparyeṇeti /
tataḥ kimityata āha--ata iti /
yatra viṣayādhīnā dhīḥ tatra
children.translated_text: Now, the opponents, taking their stand on the doctrine of the real nature of things, are capable of justifying the qualifier-qualified relation even between non-assisting and non-assisted [entities] — which is clearly observed. And there is no redundancy, due to the non-identity of qualifying condition and qualified. But the Buddhists [cannot do this], because they do not accept the reality of qualifying conditions such as existence and the like. And thus, this objection falls upon your [Buddhist] doctrine alone — therefore he says: 'For us, however...' What they [Buddhists] grasp is mere generality, and what they determine is [only] the continuum. Not even slightly in any general form. '[Conceptual constructions] range' — [means] they operate. Because of the unreality of that [generality], [it has] the absence of the property of being a real entity — that is the meaning. Then how are they [conceptual constructions] non-misleading and prompting [of activity]? — therefore he says: 'Indirectly...' What follows from that? — therefore he says: 'Therefore...' Where cognition depends on the object, there

children.text: tadāyattau viśeṣāviśeṣau, atra tu viparyayo viṣayasyaiva pratibhāsasattayā buddhyadhīnatvāt /
children.translated_text: the specific and the non-specific depend on that [object]. But here the reverse [holds]: because the object has existence only as an appearance, it depends on cognition.

children.text: tadiha vikalpasya viṣayo viśeṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, here the object of conceptual construction is the qualified.

children.text: tattadvadviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭatayāpi kiṃ bhinno 'bhinno vetyatra vikalpa eva sākṣī, na vicāra ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And as to whether [the qualified], as qualified by being possessed of this or that [property], is different or non-different — in this matter, conceptual construction itself is the witness, not analysis — that is the meaning.

children.text: nanu paramārthasannartho mā bhūdvikalpasya viṣayaḥ, janakastu bhaviṣyatītyata āha--api ceti /
children.translated_text: Now, let the ultimately real object not be the object of conceptual construction — but it will be its generator — therefore he says: 'Moreover...'

children.text: na vikalpikāmapīti /
children.translated_text: 'Not even conceptual' —

children.text: apirbhinnakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: the word '<s>api</s>' [here] has a disjunctive sequence.

children.text: artho vikalpasya na gocaro janako 'pi netyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the object is neither the domain of conceptual construction, nor even its generator.

children.text:
arthopayogaḥ sannikarṣaḥ /
na ca yadevetyādi /
nyāyāditi /
vācyamiti śeṣaḥ /
no khalviti /
smaraṇendriyayorekaviṣayasāmarthyābhāvāt na parasparāpekṣatvam /
tataśca sa evārthopayogī'viśiṣṭa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The usefulness of the object' is contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>). 'Nor is whatever...' and so forth. 'By the principle of...' — the completion is: 'it is to be stated.' 'Certainly not' — because memory and sense-organ lack the capacity for a single object, there is no mutual dependence between them. And thus, that very usefulness of the object is undifferentiated — that is the meaning.

children.text:
ekagocaratvamevānayoḥ kuto netyata āha--tadgocaratve ceti /
ananubhūtapūrvāṇāmapyarthānāṃ cakṣuṣorvyāpāramātreṇa
children.translated_text: Why should these two not have a common domain? — therefore he says: 'And if they had a common domain...' Even of objects not previously experienced, by the mere operation of the eyes,

children.text:
pūrvāvasthāsmaraṇaprasaṅga ityapi draṣṭavyam /
tena syāt /
tathā sati prasajyetetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the meaning is: in that case, it would absurdly follow.

children.text: akṣāpāye 'pi netradhīrityupalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Even when the eyes are destroyed, the visual cognition [would persist]' — this is illustrative.

children.text: vāsanābhāve smṛtidhīrityapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: 'Even in the absence of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), the memory-cognition [would persist]' — this too should be understood.

children.text: sahate pratīkṣata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Endures' means 'awaits' — that is the meaning.
the absurd consequence of the memory of previous states should also be understood. 'By that, it would be' —

children.text:
siddhāntamupakramate--atreti /
gaurayamityādervikalpasya tāvadabhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsavadarthasākṣātkāro 'pyanubhavasiddhaḥ /
asti cosyendriyārthānvayavyatirekānuvidhānam,
children.translated_text: He introduces the established conclusion: 'Here...' The direct apprehension of the object by conceptual construction [such as] 'this is a white [cow]' — endowed with an appearance fit for association with verbal expression — is also established by experience. And this [conceptual cognition] does conform to the presence and absence of sense-organs and objects.

children.text:
tadanyathāsiddham, tayorālocanamātra eva caritārthatvāditi cet? tat kimidānīmālocanasyāyaṃ mahimā vikalpopajananaṃ prati? tathā sati tasmānna kadācit apyālocanaṃ jāyeta /
vāsanāparipākavirahānna tatheti cet? sa khalu vāsanāparipāko yadi niyamādindriyārthamadhyamadhiśete kathaṃ na tadapekṣā kāryasya? kākatālīyaścet? sannidhisannihiteṣvapīndriyārtheṣu kadācid viśiṣṭād vāsanāparipākāt sākṣātkāravān vikalpa utpadyata /
na vai sākṣātkāvān vikalpaḥ kaścit, kiṃ tu nirvikalpakabhedāgrahāt tadvānivāvabhāsata iti cet--na, pramāṇābhāvāt /
na
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'that is otherwise established [i.e., explicable differently], because the sense-organs and objects have exhausted their role in mere initial perception (<s>ālocana</s>)' — then what, at present, is this greatness of initial perception with respect to the generation of conceptual construction? In that case, initial perception would never arise from that [sense-object contact]. If [one says] 'it is not so, due to the absence of the maturation of latent impressions' — is that maturation of latent impressions, by rule, dependent on the sense-organ and object as intermediary, or not? If so, how can the effect not depend on them? If it is accidental? Then even when sense-organs and objects are present, sometimes, due to a special maturation of latent impressions, a conceptual construction endowed with direct apprehension would arise. [If one says] 'No conceptual construction ever has direct apprehension; rather, due to the non-apprehension of the difference from <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate perception), it merely appears as having [direct apprehension]' — no, because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> [for this claim]. For

children.text:
hi vivādādhyāsitavikalpagato darśanavyāpāro 'yamaupādhika ityasti pratyakṣam /
nāpyanumānam /
darśanavyāpāratā kalpanāpoḍhatvena vyāptā, taccāto nivartamānaṃ tāmapi nivartayatīti cet--na, viparyayasyāpi vaktuṃ sukaratvāt /
tathāhi
children.translated_text: there is no perception [to the effect] that 'the operation of seeing that belongs to the disputed conceptual construction is adventitious.' Nor is there inference. If [one says] 'the operation of seeing is pervaded by freedom from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍhatva</s>), and that [freedom], ceasing [in the case of vikalpa], removes that [seeing] too' — no, because the reverse too is easy to state. Namely:

children.text: darśanavyāpāratvaṃ kalpanānugatatvena vyāptam /
tacca tadanugatatvamālocanānnivartamānaṃ svavyāpyaṃ darśanavyāpāratvamapi nivartayati /
children.translated_text: And that accompaniment by conceptual construction, ceasing with [the cessation of] initial perception, removes its own pervasion — [namely] the operation of seeing — as well.

children.text: tathā ca vikalpasānnidhyādaupādhiko darśanavyāpāro 'yamālocanamiti kiṃ na syāt? anubhavastūpādhiśaṅkayā tvayaivāsākṣīkṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, why should it not be [the case] that 'due to the proximity of conceptual construction, this initial perception is an adventitious operation of seeing'? But experience has been made a non-witness by you yourself, through the suspicion of an adventitious condition.

children.text: anāgate vikalpe kathamiva taddharmo nirvikalpake pratibhāseteti cet--na, kālabhedasyobhayatrāpi tulyatvāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'when the conceptual construction has not yet arisen, how can its property appear in <s>nirvikalpaka</s> [perception]?' — no, because the temporal difference is equal in both cases.

children.text: upādānopādeyabhāvaśca niyamahetuḥ samānaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the relation of material cause and effect is an equal ground for the restriction [in both cases].
The operation of seeing is pervaded by being accompanied by conceptual construction.

children.text:
nanūpādādharmā upādeyamanugacchanti /
na tūpādeyadharmā upādānamiti cet--na, vastuto 'vastudharmāṇāmapratisaṃkramāt /
ābhimānike tu pratisaṃkrame 'niyamaḥ /
upādānapratyayabalādupādeyapratyayastathotpadyata iti cet? hanta yadi sākṣātkāraḥ sākṣātkāravānutpadyate kathamasya tathātvamaupādhikam /
tāvanmātrādevendriyādinirapekṣādupajātamityetāvataiva tadaupādhikamityucyata iti cet--na, samanantarapratyayasākṣātkāramahimnā sākṣātkārotpattāvasākṣātkārānutpādaprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'it is called adventitious merely because it arises from that much alone — from the immediately preceding condition — without depending on sense-organs and the like' — no, because of the absurd consequence that direct perception would never arise [at all], due to the power of the immediately preceding condition, which is [itself] a direct perception, [always producing another direct perception].

children.text: na cāsākṣātkāriṇaḥ sākṣātkāraḥ kadācidupapadyeta /
children.translated_text: And non-direct-perception can never produce direct perception.

children.text: sahakāriviśeṣādevamapi syāditi cet? tarhi yādṛśi kārye yādṛganvayavyatirekānuvidhānaṃ dṛṣṭam, tādṛśasya tatra sahakāritvamāstheyam /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'it could be so due to a special auxiliary cause' — then, whatever conformity with the presence and absence [of causes] is observed in whatever effect, the auxiliary causality of that [type of cause] should be maintained for that [effect].

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ cobhayavādisaṃpratipannanirvikalpake sākṣātkāraṃ pratīndriyārthayoḥ sāmarthyam, na vikalpasya ityuktaprāyam //
children.translated_text: And what is observed, as accepted by both disputants, is the capacity of sense-organ and object with respect to the admittedly indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) direct perception — not [the capacity] of conceptual construction. This has been virtually stated [already].

Now, if [one says] 'the properties of the material cause follow the effect, but the properties of the effect do not follow the material cause' — no, because properties of a non-entity do not [actually] transfer to a [real] entity. And in the case of imagined transfer, there is no restriction. If [one says] 'due to the force of the material-cause cognition, the effect-cognition arises in the same way' — well then, if direct perception arises [from another] direct perception, how is its nature of being such adventitious?

children.text:
evaṃ tāvadarthaṃsākṣātkaraṇaṃ svābhāvikam /
tannāntarīyakatayā indriyārthasāmarthyasamutthatvamasya sthitam /
avisaṃvāditvamapyasyānopādhikam /
tathāhi, yadyasya pāramārthiko visaṃvādaḥ syāt, tadā pratīyamāno 'pyaupādhiko 'yamavisaṃvāda iti saṃbhāvyeta, sa ca deśakālākārakṛtastāvanna bhavati /
ananugatamevānugatatayā darśayatīti cet--na, asādhāraṇasya svalakṣaṇasya vikalpenāsaṃsparśāt /
saṃsparśe vā tajjanyatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
ajanakasyaiva tu vastusato viṣayatve pratyakṣatvamarthasāmarthyasamutthatvena vyāptamiti suptapralāpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, if there is contact, the absurd consequence is that it would be produced by that [svalakṣaṇa]. But the [claim] that 'when a really existent [entity] is the object without being the generator, perceptuality is pervaded by arising from the capacity of the object' — is mere babbling in sleep.

children.text: vikalpastāvat sādhāraṇaṃ svarūpamullikhanneva pravartayati /
children.translated_text: Conceptual construction, for its part, operates by tracing only the common form.

children.text: tacca sarvasāmarthyarahitam /
children.translated_text: And that [common form] is devoid of all causal efficacy.

children.text: na cārthakriyārthī tadasamarthaṃ dṛṣṭvā pravartate, tato 'samarthameva samāropitasāmarthyaṃ vikalpyate //
children.translated_text: And one who desires causal efficacy does not engage upon seeing that [common form] as lacking efficacy. Therefore, what is indeed lacking in efficacy is conceptualized with superimposed efficacy.

Thus, so far, the direct apprehension of the object [by conceptual construction] is natural. Consequently, the fact that it arises from the capacity of sense-organ and object is established, since it is inseparable from that. Its non-misleading nature too is not adventitious. For if it had a real discordance, then even the observed non-discordance would be suspected as adventitious — but that is not due to place, time, or form. If [one says] 'it shows what is not [actually] conforming as conforming' — no, because conceptual construction has no contact with the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular), which is uncommon.

children.text: tathā ca kathamasya viparītāroparūpasya saṃvādo nāmeti cet--na, yadi hi sāmarthyamevāropayet, asādhāraṇamevollikhet /
children.translated_text: And thus, how can there be concordance for something of the nature of erroneous superimposition? — if [this is objected] — no. For if it were to superimpose efficacy alone, it would trace only the uncommon [particular].

children.text: na hyanyadasādhāraṇādrūpāt samarthaṃ nāma tava darśane /
children.translated_text: For nothing other than the uncommon form is efficacious in your view.

children.text: tasmāt samarthamiva taddarśayati vikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, conceptual construction shows that [object] as if efficacious.

children.text: ivārthaśca na tatrāropyaḥ, vikalpārthasya samarthenāsādṛśatvāt //
children.translated_text: And the 'as-if'-ness should not be superimposed there, because the object of conceptual construction is dissimilar from what is [truly] efficacious.

children.text:
nanvasāmarthyavyāvṛttimātrameva sāmarthyaṃ na tu tattvāntaram, tasya ca na sādhāraṇarūpavirodhaḥ /
tathā caikātmyaprathanaṃ na viruddhamiti cet--na, avirodhe sati samāropānupapatteḥ /
na hi yad yatrāviruddhaṃ sat prathate tat tatrāropitaṃ nāma /
tasmād bhedāgrahāt pravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the activity [of conceptual cognition] is due to the non-apprehension of difference.

children.text: na ca sa eva visaṃvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that itself is not the discordance [with reality].

children.text: tathā ca satyālocanamapi visaṃvādi syāt, kalpanālocanayorbhedānullekhāt /
children.translated_text: And if so, even bare apprehension (<s>ālocana</s>) would be discordant, since neither [bare apprehension nor] conceptual cognition traces the difference [between concept and reality].

children.text: etena svapratibhāse 'narthe arthādhyavasāyena pravṛtteriti parāstam //
children.translated_text: By this, the [Buddhist] view that activity proceeds by determining an unreal [object] as a [real] object in what appears to itself is refuted.

Now, if one says: capacity is nothing but the exclusion of incapacity, and for that there is no contradiction with the common form; and thus the manifestation of identity is not contradictory — no, because in the absence of contradiction, superimposition would be untenable. For what manifests in something without being contradicted by it is not called superimposed upon it.

children.text:
anarthatvaṃ hi vikalpādabhedo vikalpyasya syāt, ālocanīyād bhedo vā? na tāvat kalpanāgocarasyālīkasya kalpanayā abhedaḥ saṃbhavati, yena bhedollikhanamāropaḥ syāt /
ālocanīyād bhede 'pi
children.translated_text: For what would the unreality [of the conceptual object] be — non-difference of the conceptualized from the concept, or difference from the directly apprehended? To begin with, non-difference of the unreal conceptual content from the concept is not possible, such that the tracing of difference [from it] would be superimposition. Even when there is difference from the directly apprehended,

children.text: nābhedapratheti nāropaḥ /
children.translated_text: non-difference is not manifested — therefore there is no superimposition.

children.text: svapratibhāse 'nartha iti vacanāt naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "In what appears to itself, an unreal [object]" — by this statement, this fault does not arise.

children.text: sa khalvākāro vikalpādabhinno 'pi bhinna āropyata iti cet? yadi tāvat vijñānanayamālambyaitaducyate, tadālocanasyāpyeṣaiva gatiriti tasyāpyāroparūpatvāt /
children.translated_text: If one says: that form, though non-different from the concept, is superimposed as different — if this is said from the standpoint of the doctrine of cognition [only], then the same applies to bare apprehension too, since it too would be of the nature of superimposition.

children.text: grāhyākāre 'prāmāṇyaṃ vikalpasyāpi svātmani ca saṃvedanatvādubhayorapi prāmāṇyameveti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Regarding the apprehended form, the concept too is invalid; and regarding its own self, both have validity through self-awareness — so there is no distinction whatsoever.

children.text:
atha bāhyamarthamadhikṛtya prastuteyaṃ kathā? tathāpi yādṛśākāro vikalpastādṛśākāra eva bāhyatayā pratibhāseta? na cāsau sādhāraṇākāraḥ samasti /
tato yedatat sādhāraṇaṃ rūpamābhāti tanna vikalpākāramabhiniviśate
children.translated_text: But if this discussion is conducted with reference to an external object? Even so, would the concept manifest as external in the very form in which it has its own form? But no such common form exists. Therefore, what appears as this common form does not conform to the form of the concept

children.text: iti bahirevāvatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: and thus remains external only.

children.text: bāhyatvavat sādhāraṇatvamapyasyāropyata iti cet--na, asādhāraṇyasya pāramārthikasya kvacidapyanupalabdherāropayitumaśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: If one says: just as externality, so too commonness is superimposed upon it — no, because the real uncommonness [of the particular], being never apprehended anywhere [as common], cannot be superimposed.

children.text: asadullekhe tvalīkālambanatvameva vikalpasyābhyupagataṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: If there is the tracing of what does not exist, then it is admitted that the concept has an unreal object only.

children.text: tatra cāropasaṃbhāvanaiva nāstītyuktam //
children.translated_text: And it has been said that in that case, there is simply no possibility of superimposition.

children.text:
pūrvāparayorvikalpākārayorabhedānusandhānameva sādhāraṇyamiti cet--na, ākāriṇāṃ bhedapratītāvākārāṇāmekatvena pratisandhātumaśakyatvāt, tayostādātmyāmyupagamāt /
vikalpasyātmāpyākāro bhinno bāhyatayāropitaḥ /
tato vikalpātmānāṃ bhedāvasāye 'pi nākārāṇāṃ bhedāvasāyaḥ /
tatastadekatayānusandhānamiti cet? hanta, yadyayamākāro vikalpātmā tatheti pratīyeta, kathaṃ bāhyatvenāropyeta? tādātmyāpratītistūbhayathāpi syāt, asvasaṃvedyatvād vikalpasya, svasaṃvedanatvena vā, tato bhinnātvāt tādātmyasya /
ādyaḥ tāvat saugatairanabhyupagamādeva duḥsthaḥ /
dvitīyastu sarvairevāvagataḥ /
avagataṃ na tu niścitamiti cet--na, niścayāniścayalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmasaṃsarṅgeṇa bhedāpatteḥ /
vyāvṛttyorbheda eva na tu vastunīti cet? atha keyaṃ vyāvṛttirnāma? na kiściditi cet? evamastu /
tathā ca nāropavārtāpi /
tato nāsyopadarśitārthavisaṃvādagandho 'pi /
asadarthaprakāśanameva visaṃvādanamiti cet? āstāṃ tāvadevat, yathāviṣayamātramatra vivakṣitam, prakṛtopayogāt /
evaṃ cāviparītārthatvāt prāmāṇyam /
pramāṇasya sataḥ sākṣātkāritvāt pratyakṣatvam /
asmadādipratyakṣatvācca indriyārthasāmarthyasamutthatvam /
children.translated_text: And because it is perceptual for beings like us, it arises from the capacity of the sense-organ and the object.

children.text: evaṃ sati sarva eva saugatenaprayujyamānāḥ kālātyayāpadiṣṭatayā pratipakṣahetavaḥ padamadhyāropayitumasamarthāḥ prāgeva vikalpasyāpratyakṣatāṃ sādhayitum /
children.translated_text: This being so, all the counter-arguments being urged by the Buddhist, being in the status of objections raised after the time has passed (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>), are unable to make even a step toward establishing the non-perceptuality of conceptual cognition — let alone proving it.

children.text: tathāpīdamavaśiṣyate, yadetāvatāpi na paramārthasad viṣayasya prāmāṇyaṃ sādhitam /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, this much remains — that even by all this, the validity regarding the object as ultimately real has not been established.

children.text: tatra cāvayorvivāda iti tatrāha--syādvirodha iti //
children.translated_text: And our dispute with [the Buddhist] is about that — therefore he says: "There would be contradiction..."

If one says: the identification of successive conceptual forms is itself the commonness — no, because when the bearers-of-form are cognized as different, their forms cannot be identified as one, since those two [form and bearer] are accepted as identical. [One might say:] the self of the concept, though another form, is superimposed as external; therefore even when the conceptual selves are determined as different, the forms are not determined as different; hence their identification as one. If so — well then! If this form, being the self of the concept, were cognized as such, how could it be superimposed as external? And the non-cognition of identity would obtain in either case: either because the concept is not self-aware, or because, if it is self-aware, the identity, being different from that [self-awareness], [is not cognized]. The first is untenable to begin with, since the Buddhists themselves do not accept it. The second is understood by all. [If one says:] it is apprehended but not ascertained — no, because the occurrence of contradictory properties characterized by ascertainment and non-ascertainment would entail difference. [If one says:] there is difference of the exclusions only, not of the reality — then what is this exclusion? [If one says:] nothing — very well then. And thus there is not even a whiff of superimposition. Therefore there is not even a trace of discordance with the object as shown. [If one says:] the very manifestation of a non-existent object is discordance — let that be for now; here, mere conformity-to-object is all that is intended, since it is relevant to the topic at hand. And thus, because of having a non-erroneous object, there is validity. And since a valid <s>pramāṇa</s>, being existent, makes [its object] directly known, there is perceptuality.

children.text: nanu paramārthasato 'bhilāpasaṃsargayogyatā aśakyavyutpādanaiva kṣaṇikatvāt jagata ityata uktam--sthemabhājamiti /
children.translated_text: Now, the fitness for connection with verbal expression (<s>abhilāpasaṃsargayogyatā</s>) of what is ultimately real is simply impossible to explain, because of the momentariness of the world — therefore it was said: "Of those that possess stability..."

children.text: nanu sthairyasiddhāvapi jātyādīnāṃ durūpapādatvāt kathaṃ paramārthasato 'bhilāpasaṃsargayogyatetyata uktam--jātyādimantam /
children.translated_text: Now, even if stability is established, since <s>jāti</s> (universals) and the like are difficult to establish, how can there be fitness for connection with verbal expression for what is ultimately real? — therefore it was said: "Possessing universals and the like..."

children.text: tathā ceti //
children.translated_text: "And thus..."

children.text: yadyapyuktarūpārthavyavasthāpane sati kālātyayāpadiṣṭo 'yaṃ prasaṅgahetuḥ, taddarśanecāpakṣadharmaḥ,na hyasti saṃbhavo vikalpasyārthasāmarthyasamutthatvaṃ niścitamaniścitaṃ ca tadarthasya paramārthasattvam, tathāpi paro 'pi tannirākaraṇasiddhyaiva pratyavasthito na rājājñayā nirākaraṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although this <s>prasaṅga</s> (consequential) argument is in the status of a time-barred objection when the reality of the stated nature of the object has been established, and although from the perspective of showing [the counter-argument], it is not a property of the thesis — for the possibility does not exist that the arising of the concept from the capacity of the object is ascertained and [at the same time] the ultimate reality of its object is not ascertained — nevertheless, the opponent too, having established himself precisely through the refutation of that [reality], is not to be refuted by royal decree.

children.text: tasmādāpātatastatsandehe sandigdhavipakṣavṛttitvamevāstvityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, at first blush, in the state of doubt about that, let there merely be the status of uncertain occurrence in the counter-example — that is the meaning.

children.text: etena viparyayo 'pi nirākṛto boddhavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the reversal [of the argument] too should be understood as refuted.

children.text: namu santu jātyādayaḥ paramārthabhūtāstathāpi yadi te 'pi piṇḍātmabhūtāḥ kathaṃ bhedena pratibhāsaren? tathā apratibhāsamānāśca kathaṃ viśeṣyatayā viśeṣyamavacchindyuḥ, anātmabhūtāścet kathaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyamaśnuvīrannityata āha--na ceti /
children.translated_text: Now, let universals and the like be ultimately real; still, if they too are of the nature of the individual, how would they appear as different? And, not appearing [as different], how would they, as qualifiers, delimit the qualificand? And if they are not of the nature [of the individual], how would they partake of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>)? — therefore he says: "Nor..."

children.text: tathāpi śabdo bhinnātmā atadvṛttiḥ kathamavacchedakaḥ syāt, yadi tadgatastadātmā vā na pratīyeta /
children.translated_text: Even so, the word, having a different nature and not residing in that [individual], how would it be a delimiter, if it were not cognized as residing in that [individual] or as being of its nature?

children.text: evameva tvavacchede 'tiprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: But precisely in this case, there would be an over-extension of delimitation.

children.text: avacchedapratītau tu bhrāntirityāśaṅkate--na ceti //
children.translated_text: And the cognition of delimitation would be erroneous — he raises this objection: "Nor..."

children.text: abhedakalpanamavacchedakalpanam /
children.translated_text: The supposition of non-difference is the supposition of delimitation.

children.text: tacca tadātmatayā tatsaṃsargitayā vā? uktametat iti na hi tadvṛttitayaiva tatsaṃsarga iti niyamaḥ, api tu taṭasthenāpi jñāneneva jñeyasya vācakena vācyasya na viruddha ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And is that [supposition] as identity or as connection? This has been addressed — for there is no rule that connection must be only through residence; rather, just as by a cognition that stands outside [the thing], of the knowable, so too by a word, of the denotable — there is no contradiction — that is the meaning.

children.text: nanu taṭastho 'pyayamavacchedako na sattāmātreṇa, api tu jñātaḥ /
na tu śabdajñāne tadānīṃ śravaṇasya vyāpāraḥ, viṣayasya viprayogāt /
children.translated_text: But at that time, the auditory sense has no operation in the cognition of the word, due to the separation from the object [of hearing].

children.text: savyāpāre cakṣuṣi manasastatra vyāsaḍgācca /
children.translated_text: And when the eye is operative [on the visible object], the mind too is engaged there.

children.text: tasmādyathā svpnāvasthāyāmindriyoparame 'pi pūrvasaṃskārapāṭavānmanasaivaikena avidyamānā apyarthā viṣayīkriyante, tathā aśabdavyāvṛttivikalpajanitavāsanāpaṭunā cakṣuṣaiva manasā vā śabdo 'pi viṣayīkriyata ityavidyamānaśabdālambanatvād bhrāntirevetyata āha--na ca śabdārthayoriti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as in the dream state, even when the sense-organs have ceased functioning, through the keenness of prior residual impressions, the mind alone — being one — makes even non-existent objects its content, so too, by the eye or the mind alone, made keen by the residual impression generated by the concept of word-exclusion, the word too is made into a content — and because this involves a non-existent word as content, it is nothing but error — therefore he says: "Nor of word and meaning..."

children.text: ekendriyagrāhyatetyatra prasaṅga iti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The completion is: "there is the undesirable consequence of being graspable by one sense-organ."
Now, even this one that stands outside is a delimiter not by mere existence, but [only when] cognized.

children.text:
ayamarthaḥ, yadi mano 'bhiprāyeṇaikendriyagrāhyatā prasajyate na kiñcidaniṣṭam, tasya sarvaviṣayatvāt /
atha
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: if single-sense-graspability follows with the mind in view, nothing undesirable results, since the mind has all things as its objects. But

children.text:
bāhyendriyamabhipretya, tatrāpi kiṃ nāma yojanātmake vikalpe, kiṃ vā jātyādiyojanātmake? tatra nāmno viśeṣaṇatvapakṣastāvadanabhyupagamenaiva parihṛtaḥ /
upalakṣaṇatvaṃ tu taṭasthasyaiveti pratipāditameva /
taccendriyāntaropanītasyapi nirvahatīti naindriyake vikalpe nāmasphuraṇamupayujyate /
children.translated_text: And that [indicatory function] is discharged even when [the word] is brought by another sense-organ — therefore the manifestation of the name is not needed in a sensory concept.

children.text: jātyādiyojanāyāṃ tu śabdasmaraṇasyāpi nāstyupayogaḥ, prāgeva tadgrahaṇasya, tasyānavacchedakatvāt /
children.translated_text: But in the joining of universals and the like, even the recollection of the word has no use, let alone the grasping of it, since [the word] is not a delimiter [of the universal].

children.text: kevalaṃ kimiti niyamataḥ smaryate śabda ityavaśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: Merely this remains: why is the word invariably recalled?

children.text: tatredamuktam--kiṃ tviti //
children.translated_text: To that, this has been said: "But..."

if it is with reference to an external sense-organ — then what [is intended]? Is it in a concept that involves naming, or in one that involves universals and the like? There, the view that the name is a qualifier is refuted simply by non-acceptance. And that it is an indicator standing outside has been established.

children.text:
tatkimidānīṃ śabdasmaraṇasya na kaścidastyupayoga ityata āha--indriyajavikalpotpādaṃ prati /
vyavahāraṃ prati
children.translated_text: Then does the recollection of the word have no use at all? — therefore he says: "With respect to the generation of a sensory concept." But with respect to practical activity,

children.text:
tvastyevopayoga ityarthaḥ /
saḍketasamayeti /
pūrvāvasthāsmaraṇagrahaṇayoranyataropalakṣaṇaparam /
śabdastu na niveśayatyātmānaṃ gṛhītaḥ smṛto 'pīti śeṣaḥ /
cakṣuṣāpi sa evāyaṃ dṛśyate, na tu pūrvahṛdayasthaḥ śabdo 'pītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the very same [object] is seen by the eye too — but not the word that was previously in the mind.

children.text: etadeva vyākhyāya ślokāntareṇa draḍhayati--ananena hītyādi /
children.translated_text: Having explained this very point, he confirms it with another verse: "For by this" and so forth.

children.text: na tu śabdaniveśanamapīti /
children.translated_text: But not even the installation of the word.

children.text: śabdarūpamapi viṣayamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: not even the word-form as an object.

there is indeed a use — that is the meaning. "Convention" (<s>saṃketa</s>) — this is intended as an indication of either of the two: recollection or grasping of the prior state. The completion is: but the word, even when grasped or recalled, does not install itself [in the concept].

children.text:
yadyapi saṃjñā hītyādi śloke sā taṭasthetyetāvadeva prakṛtopayogi, tathāpyanāgataṃ pratividhitsuravayavāntaraṃ vyācaṣṭe--nārthendriyeti /
arthasahitamindrayamarthendriyam /
yadyapi kṣaṇamaṅgapakṣe 'pi,
children.translated_text: Although in the verse beginning "For the convention" only the statement "it stands outside" is relevant to the topic at hand, nevertheless, wishing to anticipate what is to come, he explains another part: "Not by the object-sense..." "Object-sense" means the sense-organ together with the object. Although even in the thesis of momentariness,

children.text: pratyekamasamartheṣu yeṣu saṃbhāvyate guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "In things that are individually incapable, where a quality is conceived [as possible],

children.text: saṃhatau hetutā teṣām
children.translated_text: their causality is in the aggregate" —

children.text:
iti nyāyenātiśayaparamparotpādena pūrvāvasthāsmaraṇādisahakārimadhyamadhyāsīnaṃ yadevendriyaṃ tadeva vikalpajanakaṃ netaraditi nāsti kaścid virodhaḥ /
tathāpi vikalpasya sthiraviṣayatvāt kṣaṇikatvasvīkāre nirviṣayatvamāpādyeteti nisphalaḥ prayāsaḥ syāditi manyamānaḥ sthairyamālambyaiva pariharati--na ca janakatveti /
syādetaditi /
syādetatsahakāritvaṃ saṃskārasyendriyaṃ prati, yadyanayorviṣayabhedo na syādityarthaḥ /
tatkimiti /
children.translated_text: "Then why" —

children.text: indriyasaṃskārayoḥ parasparādhipatyaṃ viṣayabhedāt kīdṛśānna bhavati kiṃ pratipattyanubandhino, vyāpārānubandhino vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, tathāvidhaviṣayabhede 'pi gandhajñānacakṣuṣoḥ parasparādhipatyena rūpajñānotpattidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: From what kind of difference of object does the mutual dominance of sense-organ and residual impression not obtain? Is it [a difference] connected with the cognition, or connected with the operation? Not the first, to begin with — because even when there is such a difference of object, the generation of form-cognition is observed through the mutual dominance of smell-cognition and the eye.

children.text: dvitīyastvasiddhaḥ, tasya kāryeṇānuvidhīyamānatāmātronneyatvāt /
children.translated_text: The second, however, is unestablished — because that [operational object] is to be inferred merely from its conformity to the effect.

children.text: etaccomayamapyubhayavādisiddhamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And this much is accepted by both disputants — that is the meaning.

by this principle, through the successive generation of extraordinary [capacities], the very sense-organ that is situated amidst auxiliaries such as the recollection of the prior state is the generator of the concept — not any other [factor] — so there is no contradiction. Nevertheless, since the concept has a stable object, if momentariness were accepted, [the concept] would be rendered object-less — and thus the effort would be fruitless. Thinking thus, he refutes [the objection] by relying on stability alone: "Nor the generator-hood..." "This would be so" — the meaning is: this auxiliary-relation of the residual impression to the sense-organ would be the case if there were no difference of object between these two.

children.text:
nanu vyāpāranubandhitayā saṃskārasya yadi purovartī viṣayaḥ, tadā atītāvasthāsphuraṇaṃ na syādeva /
na hyanyaviṣayo vyāpāraḥ, anyatra kriyetyabhyupagamaḥ /
tasmādatītaviṣayatvāt kriyāyāḥ vyāpārānubandhitayāpi saṃskārasya sa eva viṣayaḥ, na tu purovartī /
evamindriyasyāpi yadyatītāvasthasyaiva vyāpāravato viṣayaḥ, tadā purovartiviṣayasphuraṇaṃ na syāt /
children.translated_text: Similarly, if the object of the sense-organ too, possessing operation, were only the past state, then the manifestation of a presently existing object would not occur.

children.text: tasmāt tasyāpi vyāpāravataḥ purovartyeva viṣaya iti vyāpārato 'pi kathamekaviṣayateti? samanantarapratyayastu pratipattito gandhaviṣayo 'pi vyāpārato rūpaviṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the object of that [sense-organ] too, possessing operation, is the presently existing one only — so how can there be one object even from the standpoint of operation? But the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), even though having smell as its object from the standpoint of cognition, has form as its object from the standpoint of operation.

children.text: rūpaviṣayavyāpārameva cakṣurapekṣate /
children.translated_text: And the eye requires precisely the operation pertaining to form as its object.

children.text: na hi cakṣuṣyapi sahakāriṇi gandhajñānād gamdhajñānam, api tu rūpajñānameveti //
children.translated_text: For even when the eye is an auxiliary, from the cognition of smell [there arises] not the cognition of smell [again], but precisely the cognition of form.

Now, if the object of the residual impression, by virtue of connection with operation, is the [presently] existing one, then the manifestation of a past state would simply not occur. For there is no accepted [principle] that the operation pertains to one object while the action is performed on another. Therefore, since the action pertains to a past object, the object of the residual impression too, by virtue of connection with operation, is that very [past object], not the presently existing one.

children.text:
naitatsādhīyaḥ, sahakārībhedādeva vyāpārabhedasyāpi niyamāt /
na hi cakṣurādisahakārivirahe 'pi gandhajñānasya rūpaviṣayavyāpāraniyamaḥ /
tathā sati gandhajñānād rasanādisahakāriṇo 'pi rūpajñānameva syāt, na rasādijñānam /
tasmāt kevalasya cakṣuṣo yadyapi rūpameva vyāpāraviṣayaḥ, tathāpi pūrvāvasthāsaṃskārasahakārimatastadvāneva purovartī vyāpāraviṣaya iti na kaścid virodhaḥ /
pūrvāvasthā cakṣuṣā asannikṛṣṭā kathaṃ tadvyāpāraviṣaya iti /
children.translated_text: The prior state, not being in contact with the eye, how can it be the operational object of that [eye]?

children.text: avaśiṣṭaṃ tu śaṅkate--nanvatīteti /
children.translated_text: He raises the remaining [objection]: "Now, the past..."

children.text: atra tatsaṃbandhameva tadvyāpāraviṣayatvaṃ syāt, saṃbandhasya tadvyāpakatvaṃ vā? ādyaṃ nirākāroti--tatkimiti /
children.translated_text: Here, would the connection with that [past state] itself be the operational object-hood of that, or would the connection pervade the operational object-hood? He refutes the first: "Then what..."

children.text: dvitīyaṃ śaṅkate--nanvasaṃbaddhamiti //
children.translated_text: He raises the second as an objection: "Now, what is unconnected..."

This is not correct — because the difference of operation is necessarily determined by the difference of auxiliaries alone. For in the absence of auxiliaries such as the eye, the cognition of smell does not have the rule of operation pertaining to form as its object. If it were so, then from the cognition of smell, even with the tongue and the like as auxiliaries, there would arise only the cognition of form, not the cognition of taste and the like. Therefore, although the operational object of the eye alone is form only, nevertheless, of [the eye] that possesses the residual impression of the prior state as its auxiliary, the presently existing [object] that possesses that [prior state] is the operational object — so there is no contradiction.

children.text: pradhānavyāpāraviṣayatā hyavāntaravyāpāraviṣayatayā vyāptā, sā cātītāvasthāto nivartamānā tāmapi nivartayati /
children.translated_text: For being the object of the principal operation is pervaded by being the object of the subsidiary operation, and that [principal operation], ceasing from the past state, removes the latter too.

children.text:
atha savikalpake janayitavye pūrvāvasthāsmaraṇamevāvāntaravyāpāro na tu viṣayasambandhaḥ, tadā lakṣaṇavirodho dūṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
mā bhūditi /
indriyāgocaraḥ indriyasannikarṣagocara ityarthaḥ /
na ceti /
ayamāśayaḥ, na tāvat sarvathaivātītāvasthā nendriyasannikṛṣṭa, saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatāyāḥ saṃbhavāt /
asyāpi saṃyuktasamavāyavat pratyakṣajñānotpādakatayā sannikarṣapadena saṃgrahāt /
yadyapi samavāyetarabhāvarūpadharmeṣu saṃbandhāntaragarbha eva viśeṣaṇaviśaṣyabhāvaḥ, tathāpi vidyamānadharmaviṣayaiva sā vyavasthitiriti na kaścit sūtravirodha iti yadyapi rahasyam, tathāpi atītāvasthāyāḥ saṃbandhānabhyupagame 'pi na kācillakṣaṇakṣatiḥ /
na hi yāvatpratyetavyagocara indriyasannikarṣa
children.translated_text: Now, if the subsidiary operation in generating determinate cognition (<s>savikalpaka</s>) is only the recollection of the prior state and not the sense-connection, then the fault is contradiction with the definition — this is the meaning. 'Let it not be so.' 'Within the range of the sense-organ' means 'within the range of sense-contact' — this is the meaning. 'And not...' The intention is: to begin with, the past state is not entirely outside the range of sense-contact, since the qualifier-status of what is connected is possible. And even this [qualifier-status] is included under the term 'contact,' like contact-inherence, by virtue of its capacity to produce perceptual cognition. Although the qualifier-qualified relation in properties that are of the nature of a relation other than inherence involves within it another relation, nevertheless that determination pertains only to an existing property — and thus there is no conflict with the <s>sūtra</s>. Although this is the esoteric point, nevertheless, even without accepting the relation of the past state, there is no damage to the definition. For the <s>sūtra</s> does not say: 'sense-contact extends to everything that is to be cognized.'

children.text: iti sūtram /
children.translated_text: — this is the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi? indriyārthasannikarṣajanitaṃ vijñānaṃ pratyakṣaphalam /
children.translated_text: What then? The cognition generated by sense-object contact is the result of perception.

children.text: tathāvidhaphalaviṣayor'thaḥ pratyakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The object that is the object of such a result is perceptual.

children.text: tathāvidhaphalasādhanaṃ pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇamiti //
children.translated_text: And the means of producing such a result is the perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge).

children.text:
syādetat /
kāryamekamadhikṛtyendriyasannikarṣasaṃskārayoḥ parasparasahakāritā, tadeva tvekamanayoḥ kuta ityāśayavān codayati--nanu pūrvāpareti /
sūcīkaṭāhanyāyena paścāduktamapi prathamaṃ vivṛṇoti--tathā hīti /
yadyapi tadityullekho na sarvavikalpavyāpī, tathāpi pratisandhānajñāne tāvadasti /
tasya ca prāmāṇyaṃ sthiravādibhiravaṣyābhyupetavyam /
anyathā sarvamālūnaviśīrṇamāpadyate /
pareṇāpi tadeva viśeṣato nirākartavyam /
children.translated_text: One might say: with respect to a single effect, sense-contact and latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) mutually assist each other — but why is that effect one and the same for both of them? — with this intention he raises the objection: 'Now, prior and subsequent...' By the needle-and-pan method, he first explains what was stated later: 'For thus...' Although the reference 'that' does not pervade all types of determinate cognition, nevertheless it at least obtains in recognition (<s>pratisandhānajñāna</s>). And the validity of that must necessarily be accepted by proponents of permanence. Otherwise, everything would collapse as if its roots were cut. Even the opponent must specifically refute just that.

children.text: tannirākaraṇenaiva hi jātyādyabhāve apratisandhānātmakasyāpi vikalpasya pratyākhyānamayatnasiddhamityabhisandhiḥ //
children.translated_text: For by the very refutation of that, when universals and the like do not exist, even the rejection of determinate cognition that does not involve recognition is effortlessly accomplished — this is the intention.

children.text:
nanu viruddhadharmasaṃsargo 'pi syāt, na ca bheda ityata āha--trailokyasyaikatvaprasaḍgāt /
tathā ca
children.translated_text: Now, there might be the co-presence of contradictory properties, but not difference — to this he says: 'Because there would follow the consequence of the entire triple world being one.' And thus

children.text:
bhedavyavahārasyākasmikatvaprasaṅga ityarthaḥ /
viṣayabhedaśceti /
yadyapi viṣayabhedavato 'pi sarvajñavijñānasyaikatvamakṣatameva, tathāpi kṣaṇikānekakālīna (?) nīlālambanatvamava yadi pratisandhānasya paro 'bhyupagacchet, na tasya kācidiṣṭasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the unity of the omniscient's cognition is unimpaired even when it has different objects, nevertheless, if the opponent were to accept that the momentary [cognition] having blue as its object at different times is what recognition [involves], none of his intended conclusions would follow.

children.text: nāpyasmākamidamaniṣṭaṃ kiṃ tu tadaparispharaṇameva vikalpe /
children.translated_text: Nor is this undesirable for us — but rather, the very non-manifestation of that [past object] in determinate cognition [is the issue].

children.text: tasmādāropitaikatvaviṣayatvamasya pāramārthikaikatvaviṣayatvaṃ vā? tatra prathamaṃ yadi paro 'bhyupagacchedanukūlayedevāsmān tasmāt nānāvasthāviśiṣṭapāramārthikaikaviṣayatayāstyekatvaṃ parābhiprāyagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, is this cognition one whose object is a superimposed unity, or one whose object is a real unity? In the first case, if the opponent accepts this, he would only favor us. Therefore, there is a unity that is the object of the opponent's intended meaning, consisting in having a single real object distinguished by multiple states.

children.text: tacca viṣayabhedāpādanenaiva nirasyata ityamisandhiḥ //
children.translated_text: And that is refuted by the very demonstration of difference of objects — this is the intention.
there would follow the consequence that the practical usage of difference is groundless — this is the meaning. 'And the difference of objects...'

children.text:
atrocyata iti /
yadyapi tadidamitijñānaṃ pūrvāvasthāyāmapyaparokṣameva /
na hi tadityullekhādeva parokṣatvam /
tathā sati śābdalaiḍgikavikalpānāṃ tadityullekhavirahiṇām aparokṣatvaprasaḍgāt /
nāpīdamāspadatvādeva sākṣātkāra iti bauddhasyābhyupagamo 'pasiddhāntaprasaḍgāt /
kiṃ tu sannihitaviṣayamasannihitaviṣayaṃ vā yadeva liḍgādinirapekṣeṇa indriyeṇa vijñānaṃ janyate, tadevāparokṣarūpaṃ samutpadyate /
anindriyajaṃ tu parokṣamiti vibhāgaḥ /
tatra parokṣamaparokṣaṃ vānubhūtāvasthāviśiṣṭaviṣayatayā tadityullikhyate /
sannihitaviṣayatayedamiti /
children.translated_text: 'This' is by virtue of having as its object something proximate.

children.text: so 'yaṃ viṣayakṛto viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is a distinction produced by the object.

children.text: tathāpyabhyupagamavāde 'pi na kaścid virodha iti pratibandigraha iti mantavyam /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, even on the view of acceptance [by the opponent], there is no contradiction — this should be understood as a provisional counter-argument.

children.text: tasmād viṣayabhedādavirodha iti tvayā samādhātavyamiti cet? nanvihāpīti //
children.translated_text: If one says: 'Therefore you should resolve this by [showing] non-contradiction due to difference of objects' — well, 'But here too...'

He says: 'Here it is said...' Although the cognition 'that is this' is direct even with respect to the prior state, for directness does not follow merely from the reference 'that.' If it did, there would follow the absurd consequence that verbal, inferential, and other determinate cognitions, which lack the reference 'that,' would be direct. Nor would the Buddhist's acceptance that directness follows merely from the word 'this' being applicable hold, since there would follow the consequence of a doctrinal error. Rather, whatever cognition is generated by the sense-organ, independent of inferential marks and the like, whether its object is proximate or non-proximate, arises in a direct form. But what is not sense-generated is indirect — this is the division. There, whether indirect or direct, a cognition is referred to as 'that' by virtue of having as its object something distinguished by a previously experienced state.

children.text: tat kimidānīṃ vikalpavikalpanīyayoryathā bhedastathaiva tadidantāspadayorapīti? nanvevaṃ sati dattaḥ svahasto bauddhānāmityata āha--sambandheti /
viśeṣaṇe uttaratrāpyevam, viśeṣyaṃ tvekameva /
children.translated_text: In the qualifier too, [the analysis applies] similarly even subsequently. But the qualified is one and the same.

children.text: tatra cāparokṣatvamevāsyetyāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And with respect to that, the intention is that its directness alone [is the point].

children.text: yo 'pīti /
children.translated_text: 'Even one who...'

children.text: atrāpinānādigdeśasambandhaḥ pratibandīkartavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here too, the counter-argument involving the relation with different directions and places must be made.

Then is it the case that, just as there is a difference between the determinate cognition and its object, so too between the bases of 'that' and 'this'? — but if so, we would give ourselves away to the Buddhists — to this he says: 'The relation...'

children.text:
nanu pratyabhijñānānnānākālasabaddhaikatvasiddhau parasparāvinābhāvabhaṅgaprasaṅgaḥ, tacca lūnapunarjātakadalīkāṇḍādau vyabhicāradarśanādapramāṇameva /
na ca kadalīkāṇḍapratyabhijñānataḥ padmarāgapratyabhijñānasya kañcid viśeṣamupalabhāmahe /
nanu nānādigdeśasaṃbaddhasyāpi tava kadācidekatvamupalabhyate, tat kathaṃ tasyāpyekatvaniścayaḥ? atha nānādigdeśasaṃsargaḥ svāśrayaṃ bhedayitvā na nivartata iti niḥsvabhāvatā vāpādayet, anaikāntiko vā syāt /
ato nāyaṃ viruddhaḥ /
siddhāstarhi saṃyogāvayavyādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then conjunction, the whole, and so forth are established.

children.text: tulyaṃ caitat kālabhede 'pi /
children.translated_text: And this applies equally in the case of temporal difference too.

children.text: tathā hi yadi pūrvāparakālasaṃbandho vastuni virudhyeta, vijñāne 'pi virudhyeta /
children.translated_text: For if the connection with earlier and later times were contradictory in an entity, it would be contradictory in cognition too.

children.text: tathā ca vijñānamapyekamatītavartamānaviṣayaṃ na syāt //
children.translated_text: And thus cognition too, being single, would not have past and present as its objects.

Now, if unity connected with different times is established through recognition, there would follow the consequence of breaking the invariable co-existence [of the momentary]. And that [recognition] is itself without <s>pramāṇa</s>, since deviation is observed in the case of a plantain stalk that has been cut and regrown. Nor do we perceive any difference between the recognition of a plantain stalk and the recognition of a ruby. Now, even for you, unity is sometimes perceived in something connected with different directions and places — so how is certainty of unity in that case possible? But if the connection with different directions and places, having differentiated its locus, does not cease, then either the thing would be reduced to having no intrinsic nature, or it would be inconclusive. Therefore, this [recognition across time] is not contradictory.

children.text:
evaṃ ca buddhīnāṃ niyatārthatayā pratisandhānagandho 'pi na syāt /
tathā ca mūlābhāvānnirīhaṃ jagajjāyeta /
sarvajñaśca dattajalāñjaliḥ prasaktaḥ /
atītavartamānaviṣayatve 'pi naikaṃ jñānamatītaṃ vartamānaṃ ca svīkriyata iti cet? atha kimidra ca vartamānatvam sattvaṃ sadantarasaṃbandho vā? evaṃ cātītatvamapi naṣṭatvaṃ naṣṭāntarasaṃbandho vā /
tatra sadantaranaṣṭāntarasaṃbandhaḥ pratisandhāne sarvajñavijñāne cāstyeva naṣṭānaṣṭaviṣayatvāt /
tadaviṣayatve
children.translated_text: And thus, since cognitions would have fixed objects, there would not be even a trace of recognition. And thus, from the absence of a foundation, the world would become inert. And the omniscient would be conceded to have no validity. Even if it is accepted that cognition has both past and present objects, a single cognition is not accepted as both past and present — if so, then what is 'presentness' here? Is it existence, or connection with another existing thing? And similarly, 'pastness' too: is it destructedness, or connection with another destroyed thing? Among these, the connection with another existing thing and another destroyed thing obtains in both recognition and omniscient cognition, since they have as objects both destroyed and non-destroyed things.

children.text:
pratisandhānatvasarvajñatvānupapatteḥ /
sattvanaṣṭatve parasparaṃ virudhyete, te caikatra pratisandhāne na sta iti cet? evaṃ tarhi padrāgamaṇirapyutpatterārabhya svāvayavavibhāgaparyantaṃ satsvarūpaḥ /
nāsya naṣṭatvasaṃsargaḥ /
sa eva tu satā kenacit saṃsṛṣṭaḥ kenacidasatā pratisandhānamiva sadasabhdyāṃ viṣayābhyāmiti /
tannāsti viruddhadharmasaṃsargaḥ /
tataḥ parimāṇabhedādayo viruddhadharmasaṃsargā vaktavyāḥ /
te yatra padmarāgādau na santi tatrautsargikamekatvameveti samaḥ samādhirityabhiprāyeṇa deśamantarbhāvyopasaṃharati--tasmāditi /
na cānyasya saṃbandhinaḥ kālasya bhedo viruddhadharmasaṃsargaḥ anyasya padmarāgamaṇerbhedaṃ nānātvam /
na cendriyeti /
yadi vikalpajātīyaṃ pratīndriyārthasannikarṣo na kāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Because without that being their object, recognition and omniscience would be untenable. If one says: existence and destructedness are mutually contradictory, and they are not [both] present in a single recognition — then the ruby gem too, from its origination until the separation of its parts, has an existing essential nature. It has no connection with destructedness. But that very thing, connected with something existing and something non-existing, is like recognition, which has as objects both existent and non-existent things. Therefore there is no co-presence of contradictory properties. Consequently, [only] contradictory properties such as difference in magnitude and so forth are to be stated. Where those do not exist, as in the ruby and so forth, the default position is unity alone — with this intention, subsuming place, he concludes: 'Therefore...' And the difference of time, which is something other [than the ruby], is not a co-presence of contradictory properties that would produce difference of the ruby, which is something else. 'And not the sense-organ...' If sense-object contact is not a cause of determinate cognition of the type of conceptual construction,

children.text: vyabhicārāditi parasyābhiprāyastadānujñaivottaram /
children.translated_text: because of deviation — this is the opponent's intention, and the concession itself is the reply.

children.text: na hi vayamapi vikalpamātraṃ prati tasya kāraṇatvaṃ brūmaḥ, kiṃ tu sākṣātkārivijñānaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: For even we do not assert that sense-object contact is a cause of mere determinate cognition, but rather of direct-apprehending cognition.

children.text: na cāsau indriyārthasannikarṣamantareṇāpi bhavatīti sāram /
children.translated_text: And the essential point is that the latter does not occur without sense-object contact.

children.text: nirvikalpakapratibandigrahastvimamarthaṃ sukhena grāhayitum //
children.translated_text: The counter-argument regarding indeterminate perception serves to make this point easily grasped.

children.text:
syādetat /
vikalpasyobhayathāsaṃbhave hi sāmānyavyabhicārādviśeṣamādāya kāryakāraṇatāvadhāraṇaṃ syāt /
na tu sākṣātkārādirasya viśeṣo 'sti, aupādhikatvāt tasyeti āśaḍkya nirākaroti---na ca vikalpagata iti /
vikalpagataḥ sākṣātkāralakṣaṇo dharmastāvadanubhūyata ityavivādam, tasyaupādhikatvaṃ na tāvadānubhavikamityāha---sarvā
children.translated_text: One might say: in the impossibility of determinate cognition belonging to either category, there would be ascertainment of the causal relation by taking the particular, because of deviation of the universal. But there is no particular of that [determinate cognition] such as direct-apprehending character, since that is adventitious — raising this doubt, he refutes: 'And not in determinate cognition...' That the property characterized as direct-apprehending character, present in determinate cognition, is indeed experienced — this is undisputed. That its adventitiousness is not experiential — he says: 'All

children.text:
eva hītyādi /
tasmād darśanavyāpārā vikalpā indriyārthasannikarṣajanmāna iti yojanā /
nāpyaupapattikam, upapatteḥ prāgeva nirākṛtatvādityāśayaḥ /
nanvindriyaviṣaya eva yadi śabdo 'pi pravarteta, so 'pi sākṣātkāriṇameva vikalpamādadhyāt, indriyamapicotprekṣāvyāpāriṇam, viṣayaviśeṣamantareṇa jñāne viśeṣābhāvāt /
tasmād śabdaikaviṣayatayā pravartamāno vikalpo nendriyaviśayaṃ spṛśati, tadasparśe ca na svābhāvikamasya sākṣātkāritvamityāśanayavānāśaḍkya nirākaroti---na ca śabdeti /
children.translated_text: indeed...' and so forth. Therefore, the connection is: determinate cognitions have the operation of seeing and are born of sense-object contact. Nor is it derivable through reasoning, since the reasoning has been refuted earlier — this is the intention. Now, if the word too operates on a sense-object, it too would produce only a direct-apprehending determinate cognition, and it would also make the sense-organ operate through conjecture, since without a specific object there is no specific feature in cognition. Therefore, a determinate cognition operating solely on a verbal object does not touch a sense-object, and when it does not touch that, its direct-apprehending character is not natural to it — raising this doubt, he refutes: 'And not the word...'

children.text:
ekatrārthe indriyaṃ kāraṇam anyatra tannirapekṣaḥ śabdādirityarthaḥ /
tucchatayopekṣaṇīyamapi śiṣyahitatayā dūṣayati---na ca vahnīti /
vahnijñānāduṣṇajñānādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From the cognition of fire, from the cognition of heat' — this is the meaning.

children.text: śītadravyāpagamaḥ, tadapagame vā tadanupalambhaḥ, taddhetukaduḥkhābhāvo vā śītāpanoda ityucyate, sa coṣṇadravyopagamasādhyo na tu tadupalambhasādhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The removal of cold substance, or in its removal the non-apprehension of it, or the absence of pain caused by it — is called the removal of cold. And that is accomplished by the approach of a hot substance, not by the mere apprehension of it.

children.text: anyathā sannipātamūḍhasya svedane 'pi doṣāpagamo na syāt, uṣṇadravyānupalambhāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, even the sweating treatment of one unconscious from fever (<s>sannipāta</s>) would not remove the humoral imbalance, due to the non-apprehension of the hot substance.

children.text: tuhinācalaguhāmadhyavartini ca sarvajñe vaḍavānalasākṣātkāravati tuhinācalavilayaḥ syādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And for an omniscient being dwelling in a cave of a snowy mountain who has direct realization of submarine fire, the dissolution of the snowy mountain would follow — this is the meaning.

In one object, the sense-organ is the cause; in another, the word and the like are independent of it — this is the meaning. He also refutes what should be dismissed as worthless, for the benefit of the student: 'And not fire...'

children.text: yasyāpītyādivārttikārthaṃ dūṣayati---na caikeneti /
children.translated_text: He refutes the meaning of the <s>vārttika</s> beginning with 'Of whichever too...': 'And not by a single...'

children.text: upādhayaḥ sattvādayastaiḥ viśiṣṭatvaṃ tairviśeṣaṇaiḥ sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Limiting conditions' are <s>sattva</s> (existence) and the like; 'being qualified by those' means relation with those qualifiers.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is this:

children.text: ekenaiva svabhāvena tāvadupakaroti sarvopādhīnāmiti paramārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The ultimate truth is that by a single essential nature it helps [produce cognition of] all limiting conditions.

children.text:
tatropakārakasyaikasvabhāvatayā upakārāṇāmavacchedānāmupakāryāṇāṃ copādhīnāṃ tadaikatvaṃ syāt, yadyupakārasvabhāvāntarbhūtatvaṃ teṣāmabhyupeyeta, na caivamātiṣṭhāmahe /
tvayāpyevameva samarthanīyaṃ kiṃ tvalīkaviṣayatayeti viśeṣaḥ /
sa eṣa nyāyo yadi paramārthasatyapi syāt, kīdṛśo doṣaḥ? na kevalaṃ kālpanike vyavahāre tavedaṃ samarthanamapi tu pāramārthike 'pītyāha---api ceti /
paramāṇusvabhāva iti ṣaṣṭhatatpuruṣaḥ /
paramāṇavo jñānasya svabhāva ityapi draṣṭavyam /
paramāṇusvabhāvatve jñānasyāpi nānātvaprasaḍgāt /
tathā caikekaparamāṇuniyame sthūlapratibhāso bhrānto 'pi na syāt /
jñānasvabhāvatve 'pi ca paramāṇunāmapyekatvaprasaḍgādamūrtatvādiprasaḍgācceti sa eva doṣa ityādyuttānaṃ dūṣaṇamutsṛjya anyamāha---teṣāṃ sarvān pratīti /
children.translated_text: And if atoms had the nature of cognition, there would follow the consequence of their being one, and of their being non-material and so forth — this being the same fault. Setting aside this obvious refutation, he states another: 'Of those, in all...'

children.text: paramāṇūnāmekajñānasvabhāvatve vā na te dvitīyena viditā syurityapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: If atoms had a single cognition as their nature, then they would not be known by a second [cognition] — this too should be considered.

children.text: yadyapi tādātmyābhāve 'pi jñānajñeyayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ saṃbandho viṣayaviṣayiniyamārthaṃ bauddhena svīkṛtastathāpi kāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi ko niyanteti tulyo 'nuyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the Buddhist accepts the causal relation between cognition and the knowable, even in the absence of identity, as a connection for the purpose of restricting the subject and its object, nevertheless, even in the causal relation, the question 'what restricts?' applies equally.

children.text: ataḥ svabhāvenaivottarayati---svabhāva eveti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, he answers through essential nature itself: 'The essential nature itself...'

In that case, since the helper has a single essential nature, the conditions that are its delimitations and the limiting conditions that are what is helped would all be one — if their being included in the essential nature of the help were accepted. But we do not maintain this. You too must vindicate it in just this way — the only difference being that [for you] the object is unreal. If this reasoning would hold even when the object is ultimately real, what fault would there be? This vindication of yours applies not only to conventional reality but to ultimate reality too — he says: 'Moreover...' '<s>Paramāṇu</s>-nature' is a genitive compound. It should also be read as 'atoms are the nature of cognition.' If cognition had the nature of atoms, there would follow the consequence of its being multiple. And then, since it would be restricted to individual atoms, even the erroneous appearance of gross objects would not occur.

children.text: bhāvābhāvayoḥ samavāyatadvatorviṣayaviṣayiṇośca vayamapi svabhāvenaiva parasparopahitaṃ sambandhamātiṣṭhāmahe /
children.translated_text: We too maintain, through essential nature itself, a mutual relation that is conditioned by each other — between positive entity and absence, between <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) and those [entities], and between subject and object.

children.text: dravyaguṇakarmajātitadvatāṃ yadyapi svabhāvenaivopādhyupādhimabhdāvaḥ, tathāpi sambandho 'pyanubhūyamāno vinā bādhakaṃ nopekṣituṃ yujyate /
children.translated_text: Although the relation of conditioner and conditioned (<s>upādhyupādhibhāva</s>) between substance, quality, action, universal, and their possessors is indeed by their very nature, nevertheless, the relation too, being experienced, cannot properly be disregarded without a sublating cognition.

children.text: yathā svabhāvike viṣayaviṣayībhāve kāryakāraṇabhāvastvayā nopekṣitaḥ, tasmādatiriktasambandhe kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanaṃ bādhakamavaśiṣyata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Just as you have not disregarded the causal relation in the case of the object-cognizer relation that is natural — therefore, for the additional relation [i.e. <s>samavāya</s>], the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) remains as the [only possible] sublating cognition — this is the meaning.

children.text:
na tāvadviśiṣṭavyavahāra eva nāsti, tasya spaṣṭatayā nihnotumaśakyatvāt tadabhāve sarvavyavahārābhāvaprasaḍgācca /
tasmādasmaduktaprakārerṣyayā prakārāntareṇāyamupapādanīyaḥ /
tatrāha---bhinnajñānāgocaratve 'pīti /
apiśabchaḥ codyābhāsatulyatāmātreṇa /
nanvasti vyavahāro na tu vāstavaḥ, sa ca
children.translated_text: To begin with, it is not the case that the qualified practical usage itself does not exist, since it cannot be denied due to its being evident, and since in its absence, all practical usage would be absent. Therefore, this [qualified usage] must be accounted for in a manner other than the one we have stated, out of hostility [to our position]. To that end, he says: 'even though not the object of distinct cognitions.' The particle 'even though' [indicates] that [the objection] is merely on par with a semblance of a rejoinder. Now, the practical usage exists but is not real, and that

children.text: yathākathañcidvāsanādvāreṇāpi nirvahet, yeṣāṃ tvayaṃ vāstavaḥ, tairarthadvāraivāsya nirvāhaścintanīya inyāśaṅkate--tābhayāmiti //
children.translated_text: could somehow be sustained even through the medium of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). But for those for whom it is real, they must account for its sustenance through the medium of the real object alone — he raises the objection: 'by both.'

children.text:
tvaduktameva vāsanādvāramupādāya yeti vāstava evāyaṃ vyavahāraḥ syāt, tadā kīdṛśo doṣa ityāśayavānāha--astu tāvaditi /
tathāpi vāstava evāyamityatra kiṃ pramāṇamityata āha---tathā satīti /
asyendriyārthasannikarṣajatve svābhāvikaṃ sākṣātkāritvameva pramāṇamityarthaḥ /
nirvikalpakopadhānaṃ kalpeta vināpramāṇamiti śeṣaḥ /
yadi hi svakāraṇabalena notpatteravicārakatvaṃ mānasasyāpyavicārakatvaprasaṅga
children.translated_text: Taking up the very medium of latent impression that you have stated — if by that the practical usage would indeed be real, then what kind of fault would there be? — with this intention he says: 'let it be so for the time being.' Even so, what is the evidence that this [practical usage] is indeed real? To this he says: 'that being the case.' When this [qualified cognition] is produced by sense-object contact, its natural quality of being a direct apprehension is itself the evidence — this is the meaning. The remainder is: the postulation of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate perception) as the basis would be imagined without evidence. For if non-erroneousness [were to be denied] merely because of arising from one's own causal conditions, then even the mental [cognition] would have the consequence of being non-erroneous.

children.text:
ityāśayavānā---hanteti /
manasaḥ sarvaviṣayatvaṃ na tāvad vyāpārānubandhitayā parasya vivakṣitam, indriyārthasannikarṣasyāpi saṃskārasahitasya tathābhāvavyavasthāpanāt /
tasmāt pratipattyanubandhitayā vā syāt, sarvavāsanādhāratayā vā? ādyaṃ dūṣayati--yadi pūrvakamiti /
asmākaṃ tu manaḥ sarvaviṣayakamapi na pratipattyanubandhitayā asarvaviṣayamapratipattirūpatvāt iti bhāvaḥ /
na ca sakalasaṃskārādhāratayetyāha--acetanatayā na vicārakam iti /
vicāraupayikasakalavāsanānādhāratvādityarthaḥ /
tvadabhipretasya ca manasaḥ sakalavāsanādhārakatvaṃ niṣetsyata ityanenābhiprāyeṇāha--tasmādātmaiveti /
sthitaṃ jñānaṃ jñānavāsanetyarthaḥ /
atra hetuḥ--sa hi bauddheti /
atra
children.translated_text: With this intention: 'alas' — the all-objectness of the mind is not intended by the opponent as due to the continuity of operation, since even sense-object contact accompanied by impressions has been established as being of such a nature. Therefore, would [the all-objectness] be due to the continuity of cognition, or due to being the substratum of all latent impressions? He refutes the first: 'if preceded by.' But for us, even though the mind is all-objective, it is not so due to the continuity of cognition — because it is not of the nature of non-cognition — this is the purport. Nor is it because of being the substratum of all impressions, he says: 'because of being insentient, it is not discriminative.' The meaning is: because it is not the substratum of all latent impressions that are useful for discrimination. And since it will be denied that the mind as you conceive it is the substratum of all latent impressions — with this intention he says: 'therefore the self alone.' 'Stable cognition' means cognition and its latent impressions — this is the meaning. The reason for this: 'for that Buddhist.' The

children.text: pramāṇam--gamyata iti /
children.translated_text: evidence: 'it is understood.'

children.text: ataḥ smaraṇe 'sya sāmarthyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it has the capacity for recollection.

children.text: co hetau //
children.translated_text: The <s>ca</s> indicates the reason.

children.text: nanu yadyevaṃbhūtacetanādhiṣṭhitamindriyam, tarhi nirvikalpakotpattikāla eva labdhasaskārasacivatayā vikalpameva janayedityata āha--sa khalviti /
children.translated_text: Now, if the sense-organ is presided over by such a conscious entity, then at the very time of the arising of indeterminate perception, having already acquired impressions, it should generate only determinate cognition — to this he says: 'that indeed.'

children.text: prāgālocya udbuddhasaṃskārasamupajātasmṛtisahāyaḥ paścād vikalpayatīti yojanā /
children.translated_text: The construction is: having first perceived [indeterminately], [the self], aided by memory arising from awakened impressions, subsequently determines [the object].

children.text: evaṃ tarhīndriyārthasannikarṣādālocanam, saṃskārodbodhaḥ, tataḥ smṛtiḥ, tatsahāyaśca vikalpayatīti na cakṣuṣaḥ kaścidupayoga ityata āha--cakṣuṣeti //
children.translated_text: If so, then: indeterminate perception arises from sense-object contact, [then] the awakening of impressions, from that memory, and aided by that [memory] determination occurs — so the eye has no role — to this he says: 'by the eye.'

children.text: nanvevaṃbhūtā sāmagrī militāpi yadi cakṣurvyāpāravirahe na vikalpikāṃ dhiyam upajanayet, tatastasyāpi kāraṇatvaṃ kalpyeta, natvetadastītyata āha--gaurayamiti /
children.translated_text: Now, even if such a causal aggregate is assembled, if without the operation of the eye it would not generate determinate cognition, then the causality of that [eye] too would be postulated — but this is not the case — to this he says: 'this is a bull.'

children.text: etena sākṣātkāraṃ prati tasyānvayavyātirekau sta iti darśitam /
children.translated_text: By this, the positive and negative concomitance of that [eye] with respect to direct apprehension have been shown.

children.text: etadevābhipretyottaraślokamāha--yathāheti /
children.translated_text: Intending this very point, he states the subsequent verse: 'as it is said.'

children.text: saha cetanayā vartata iti sacetanaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Functioning together with consciousness' — hence <s>sacetana</s> (endowed with consciousness).

children.text:
tathāpi ka upakāraḥ samarthita ityata āha--teneti /
jñāpyajñāpakabhāva ityupalakṣaṇam, kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pi na sarvatrāstīti draṣṭavyam /
kvacittu dravyaguṇakarmaṇām astīti nodāhṛtaḥ /
tadarthālocanānugataṃ smaraṇaṃ yayoste viśeṣaṇaviśeṣye tathokte tayoḥ /
atadadhikaraṇavyavacchedapratītijananameva viśeṣaṇena viśeṣyasyopakāra ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The very production of the cognition that excludes what is not the locus of that [qualifier] — that alone is the benefit that the qualifier confers upon the qualified — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadyapi svābhāviko viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo nopakāramapekṣata iti tatra tatra vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: Although the qualifier-qualified relation, being natural, does not require a benefit — as he will state in various places.

children.text: na copakāryopakārakabhāvo 'pyupakārāntaraprāptaḥ, tathā satyanavasthāpātāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is the benefited-benefactor relation itself obtained through a further benefit — for if so, there would be an infinite regress.

children.text: tathāpīha saṃbhavaprācuryeṇābhidhīyata iti mantavyam //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, it should be understood that it is stated here with the profusion of what is possible.

Even so, what benefit has been established? To this he says: 'by that.' 'The relation of indicator and indicated' — this is illustrative; the causal relation too does not exist everywhere — this should be understood. But in some cases, [the causal relation] does exist among substance, quality, and action — therefore it was not cited [as an example]. The two [sense-organ and self] that are described thus — as qualifier and qualified — are those whose recollection follows upon the perception of the object of that [qualifier].

children.text: nanu yadi svābhāvikamanayorviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatvam, prathamataḥ svabhāve gṛhyamāṇe kiṃ na gṛhītam, na ca svabhāvastadānīṃ na gṛhīta ityata āha--arthau hīti /
children.translated_text: Now, if the qualifier-qualified relation between them is natural, then when the nature [of the object] is grasped in the first instance, what has not been grasped? And the nature is not ungrasped at that time — to this he says: 'the two objects, for.'

children.text: na khalu rūpaparamāṇuṣu sparśādiparamāṇavo 'pi svabhāvataḥ sthitā ityetāvataiva pratītipathamavataranti /
children.translated_text: It is not the case that merely because the atoms of touch and the like are naturally established in the atoms of form, they thereby enter the path of cognition.

children.text: sāmagryabhāvānna tatheti cet? sa ihāpi samāna ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one says 'because of the absence of the causal aggregate, it is not so [perceived]' — the same applies here too — this is the meaning.

children.text: ata eva pramāṇaṃ kṛtsnavṛttīti matvā yadāpāditam, tadapi nāstītyata āha--teneti //
children.translated_text: For this very reason, what was concluded from the view that <s>pramāṇa</s> operates on the totality [of the object] — that too does not exist — to this he says: 'therefore.'

children.text:
svarūpābhiprāyeṇa kṛtsnavṛttitvaṃ pramāṇasyānumanyāmahe eva, svābhāvikasamastasambandhābhiprāyeṇa tu sarvajñetaradhiyāmaprāmāṇyamāpādayatīti upasaṃhāraṃ sthāne saṃkalayyāhā---savikalpakaṃ tviti /
paścādapi jāyamānamiti yojanā ālocanāditi śeṣaḥ /
tasmāt sarvaṃ tulyam /
kṣaṇabhaḍge paraṃ vivādo 'vaśiṣyata ityāśayavānāha---akramasyāpīti /
vivādādhyāsitā iti /
sākṣātkāriṇa ityarthaḥ /
tena taditaravyudāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: By that, the exclusion of what is other than that [is achieved].

children.text: sidvasādhyatāvyudāsārthaṃ svagocara iti /
children.translated_text: 'In its own domain' — for the purpose of excluding what is already established.

children.text: pītaḥ śaḍkha ityādinā vyabhicāranivṛttyartham avyabhicāritve satīti /
children.translated_text: 'The conch is yellow' and so forth — for the purpose of preventing deviation, 'when non-deviation obtains.'

children.text: atra ca kṛtaḥ prayatnaḥ //
children.translated_text: And in this regard, effort has been made [in the preceding discussion].

We do indeed accept the totality-operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> with respect to the intrinsic nature [of the object]; but with respect to all natural relations [being grasped simultaneously], that would lead to the invalidity of all cognitions other than the omniscient — and therefore, taking stock at the proper place, he says: 'but the determinate.' The construction is: 'even though arising afterwards' — the remainder is: 'after indeterminate perception.' Therefore everything is equal [between us]. Only in [the matter of] momentariness does the dispute remain — with this intention he says: 'even of the non-sequential.' 'Of those who are engaged in the dispute' — meaning: of the direct apprehenders.

children.text: na caitanmantavyamiti bhāṣyamiti indriyārthasannikarṣamantareṇāpi saṃśayotpattidarśanāt atatkāraṇatayā prasaṅga evāsya nāsti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>bhāṣya</s> saying 'and this should not be thought' — since doubt is observed to arise even without sense-object contact, there is simply no relevance [of the definition] to it, since [doubt] is not caused by that [sense-contact].

children.text: kuto 'nvācīyamāne 'pi vyudāsa iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Why then exclusion, when [doubt] is also included [in the definition]? — this is the prima facie view.

children.text: yadyapi na savaḥ saṃśayaḥ indriyārthasannikarṣajastathāpi sākṣātkāravānavaśya tajjanyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although not every doubt is produced by sense-object contact, nevertheless one that possesses direct apprehension is necessarily produced by it.

children.text: tasmād vyudāso 'nvācīyata iti prakāraṇārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore the exclusion is included — this is for the purpose of clarification.

children.text:
syādetadityādi /
mana eva kevalamindrayanirapekṣaṃ bahirvyāpriyamāṇaṃ sākṣātkārisaṃśayādi janayati, dṛṣṭo
children.translated_text: 'One might say' and so forth. The mind alone, independently of the [external] sense-organs, operating externally, generates direct apprehension, doubt, and so forth — for

children.text:
hyasyānuvyavasīyamānajñānaviśeṣaṇe ghaṭadau vyāpāraḥ, indriyavyāpāravigame 'pi saudāminīsaṃpātādau sakṛdupajātasyārthaniścayasya samandhakāre 'pyanuvyavasīyamānatvāt, tasya cānuvyavasāyasya sākṣātkārijātīyatvāt /
tasmāt aprasaṅga eva punarāpatita iti /
manasā hyanuvyavasīyamānajñānalakṣaṇaviśeṣyasannikṛṣṭena asannikṛśṭo ghaṭādiravacchedakatayā vyavasīyate /
cakṣuṣeva ghaṭasannikṛṣṭena prāgupalabdhā tadavasthā /
saṃśayajñānaṃ tu nordhvārthopalabdhiviṣayam, nāpi sthāṇupuruṣasmṛtiviṣayam, kiṃ tvanirdhāritasthāṇupuruṣatvordhvapadārthaviṣayam /
na ca tatsannikṛṣṭaṃ manaḥ /
bāhyena viśeṣyeṇāpyasannikṛṣṭaṃ manaḥ kathamiva jñānamutpādayet? utpādane
children.translated_text: its operation on objects like pots that are qualified by the cognition being retrospectively determined has been observed, and because, even when the operation of the [external] sense-organs has ceased, a determinate cognition of an object — such as a flash of lightning — that was generated in a single instant is retrospectively determined even in darkness, and because that retrospective determination is of the same class as direct apprehension. Therefore, the irrelevance [of the definition to doubt] has arisen again. For the mind, being in contact [with the object] by virtue of the retrospectively determined cognition that qualifies the object such as a pot, determines the pot and the like, even though not in direct contact, as the delimiting factor. Just as the visual sense-organ, being in contact with the pot, [determines] a previously perceived state of it. But the cognition of doubt does not have as its object the apprehension of what is higher [than the doubtful object], nor is it about the recollection of a post or person — rather, it is about the object that is higher, whose status as post or person has not been determined. And the mind is not in contact with that. How can the mind, not being in contact even with the external qualified entity, generate cognition? If it could,

children.text: vāndhabadhirāderapyutpādayet iti siddhāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: then even a blind or deaf person would generate [such cognition] — this is the established position.

children.text:
tatpūrvaṃ vyavasāyotpattau /
svaviṣayaprāptisampattaya iti śeṣaḥ /
tathā ca saṃśayajñānotpāde 'pīti sahakāritayeti śeṣaḥ /
avyāpakatvenetyādi codayati pārśvasthaḥ /
pariharati pūrvapakṣī /
