punaḥ pārśvasthasya śaḍkā mā bhūditi /
ata āheti /
pūrvapakṣī /
na ca sukhādau pramāṇāntaramasti /
pratyakṣaṃ vihāyeti śeṣaḥ /
saṃvedanatve hi teṣāṃ svasaṃvedanatā śaḍkāspadamapi syāditi śeṣaḥ /
nanvindriyasya vai sata iti vadato bhāṣyakṛto manasa indriyatvamiṣṭamevetyata āha---na ca taditi /
manasa indriyatvābhyupagamo vātsyāyanīye gautamīyasūtra viruddha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Preceded by that' — in the generation of the determinate cognition. The remainder is: 'as the fulfillment of reaching its own object.' And thus, even in the generation of the cognition of doubt — the remainder is: 'as an auxiliary.' 'Because of not pervading' and so forth — the bystander raises the objection. The prima facie proponent responds. Lest the bystander's doubt arise again: 'therefore he says' — the prima facie proponent [speaks]. And there is no other <s>pramāṇa</s> for pleasure and the like — the remainder is: 'besides perception.' For if they are objects of self-awareness, even self-awareness might be a matter of doubt — this is the remainder. Now, since the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says 'when the sense-organ exists,' the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> does indeed accept the mind as a sense-organ — to this he says: 'and not that.' The meaning is: the acceptance of the mind as a sense-organ is contrary to <s>Gautama</s>'s <s>sūtra</s> in the <s>Vātsyāyana</s> tradition.

children.text:
mā bhūd vibhāgaparamidaṃ sūtram, tathāpi sūtrākārasya mana indriyaṃ yadyabhimatamindriyaprakaraṇa eva lakṣayedityata āha---tatra ceti /
indriyatvena tatprakaraṇa evābhighāne prāpte yadanyatra karoti tenādhikamasya kiñcid rūpaṃ vijñeyamiti sūcayati, na tvindriyatvameva na sahata ityarthaḥ /
darśayiṣyati hi vātikakāra ityāgāmikā phakkikā bhramanirāsārthaṃ bhūtābhūteti /
śabdo 'tra duṣṭo, na tvabhiprāya iti /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
saguṇānāṃ cakṣurādīnāmindriyabhāvo, manastu na saguṇamindrayamityatrāpi yo viśeṣaguṇo yenendriyeṇa gṛhyate tajjātīyena guṇena saha vṛttiḥ saguṇatvam /
grāhyaviśeṣaguṇajātīyavirahaśca manasa iti yadyabhipretaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā tadaitadapi vaidharmyameva, kiṃ tvebhirakṣarairetadapyabhidhātuṃ na śakyate /
vibhaktivipariṇāmena tu bhāṣyaṃ sugamam /
children.translated_text: But with an alteration of the case-ending, the <s>bhāṣya</s> is easy [to understand].

children.text: tathā hi, indriyabhūtānāmeṣāṃ saguṇatvaṃ grāhyairguṇaiḥ saha saṃbandhaścakṣurādīnām /
children.translated_text: That is to say: the possession-of-qualities of these [sense-organs], which are in the nature of sense-organs — [and] the connection of the eye and the like with the graspable qualities —

children.text: manasastvindriyamūtasyaiva na saguṇatvam, na grāhyena guṇena saha saṃbandha iti /
children.translated_text: but of the mind, which is itself in the nature of a sense-organ, there is no possession-of-qualities, no connection with a graspable quality.

children.text: tasmādatrāpi śabdadoṣaḥ, na tvabhripāyadoṣa iti mantavyam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, here too the fault is in the expression, not in the intention — this should be understood.

Even if this <s>sūtra</s> is not specifically about the division [of sense-organs and mind], still, if the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> considered the mind a sense-organ, he would define it in the very section on sense-organs — to this he says: 'and therein.' When it was appropriate to treat it in the section on sense-organs by virtue of being a sense-organ, the fact that he treats it elsewhere indicates that something additional about its nature is to be understood — but it is not the case that he simply does not tolerate its being a sense-organ — this is the meaning. 'For the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> will show' — this [reference to a] future passage is for removing delusion: 'existing and non-existing.' The expression is flawed here, not the intention — and this is merely illustrative. As for the sense-organ status of the eye and the like, which possess qualities — the mind, however, is not a sense-organ possessing qualities. And here too, 'possessing qualities' means: co-occurring with a quality of the same type as the specific quality grasped by whichever sense-organ grasps it. And the mind's lack of a quality of the same type as the specific graspable quality — if this is what the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> intends, then this too is simply a dissimilarity. However, [the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>] cannot express this too in these words.

children.text:
nanvanabhimataniṣedhena matasunneṣyata iti śaṅkate---na ceti /
nirācaṣṭe--abhāvasyeti /
children.translated_text: Now, by denying what is not accepted, what is accepted will be established — he raises the doubt: 'and not.' He explains: 'of absence.'

children.text: yāvadanabhimataniṣedhenābhimatalābhe garīyo gauravamāpadyeta, tattanniṣedhyam anupanīya niṣedhasya pratipādayitumaśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: To the extent that acquiring what is accepted through the denial of what is not accepted would incur a greater complexity — that [what is not accepted] cannot be presented without presenting what is to be denied, since denial cannot be communicated without it.

children.text: viśeṣavidhau tu śeṣaniṣedho laghīyāniti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: But in a specific injunction, the denial of the remainder is simpler — this is the purport.

children.text: satrākāravacanasya vivādāspadatvāt kathaṃ tenaiva nirṇaya ityata āheti pūrayati bhāṣyakāra iti /
children.translated_text: Since the statement of the one who upholds form [of the sense-organ] is itself a matter of dispute, how can one determine [the matter] by that very [statement]? To this he says — the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> completes [the argument].

children.text: śābdetyanena śabdendriyasamāhārajamayamasāvaśva iti jñānaṃ vyavacchedyamabhimataṃ vārttikakṛta iti keṣāñcinmatamapanayati---na khalviti //
children.translated_text: The word '<s>śābda</s>' (verbal) — by this, the intention of the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> is that the cognition such as 'this is not a horse,' produced by the aggregate of sound and the sense-organ, is what is to be excluded — he sets aside the view of some: 'not indeed.'

children.text:
vācyatvena hi viśeṣaṇatayā gṛhītena niśeṣyaniṣṭhena bhavitvayamataḥ kevalavācyatvaprastāve 'pi tathaivodāhṛtam /
indriyavyatirekavyabhicārācca tadvyatireko na śaḍkitaḥ /
gṛhīte hyaśvatve tadasannikarṣe 'pi yo 'yaṃ piṇḍastvayā dṛṣṭo 'yamasāvaśva ityupadeśāt kevalādeva vācyatvapratītidarśanāt /
nasmādindriyasya saṃbandhisamarpaṇa eva vyāpāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the operation of the sense-organ is solely in presenting its associated [object].

children.text: evamuttaratrāpi tavyārthaḥ saḍketayiturabhiprāyaviśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise in the subsequent [discussion], the meaning of '<s>tavya</s>' is: the specific intention of the one establishing the convention.

children.text: yadyapi parābhiprāyastadupahito vārtho nendriyagocaraḥ, tathāpyabhyupagamyāśaṅkate---athāyamapīti /
children.translated_text: Although the intention of another or the object conditioned by it is not within the scope of the sense-organ, nevertheless, accepting that [for argument's sake], he raises the objection: 'now, even this.'

children.text: idamaindriyakamidam atīndriyamiti hi sākṣātkārāsākṣātkāronneyo 'yamarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: For the meaning 'this is sensory, this is supersensory' is to be inferred from the presence or absence of direct apprehension.

For what has been grasped as a denotation, in the role of a qualifier, pertains to the qualified — therefore, even when the occasion is merely of denotation, it has been exemplified in just that way. And deviation from the sense-organ is not suspected, because of the deviation of the exclusion of that [sense-organ]. For when horse-ness has been grasped, even without contact with that [horse], the instruction 'this thing that you see is not a horse' shows that the cognition of mere denotation arises from [verbal] designation alone.

children.text: tatra spaṣṭagrahaṇarūpatvāt sākṣātkārāparavyapadeśādaindriyakametaditi yuktaṃ syāt, na tvasākṣātkārādapi /
children.translated_text: Therein, by virtue of being of the nature of clear apprehension and by virtue of the alternative designation of 'direct apprehension' — it would be proper [to call it] sensory. But not from [what lacks] direct apprehension too.

children.text: tayośca ko 'tra manasā vedyata iti bhavāneva paribhāvayatu /
children.translated_text: And of these two, which one is cognized by the mind here — you yourself should consider.

children.text: tatra sākṣātkāritvapakṣe pratyakṣamevedamato na vyavacchedanīyam, asākṣātkāritvapakṣe ca nedam aindriyakamiti prathamapadeneva vyudastam /
children.translated_text: Therein, on the view that [determinate cognition] involves direct apprehension, it is perception itself — therefore this [type] need not be excluded. And on the view that it does not involve direct apprehension, 'this is not sense-generated' — it is already excluded by the very first term [of the definition].

children.text: nāvyapadeśyapadasyāvakāśa iti gāthāpāṭhasyārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: There is no scope for the term '<s>avyapadeśya</s>' (non-denotable) — this is the meaning of the verse-reading.

children.text: kimarthaṃ tarhyavyavadeśyapadam, kaścāsya vārttikasyārtha ityata āha---vyavasāyātmakapadena tviti /
children.translated_text: Then what is the purpose of the term '<s>avyapadeśya</s>,' and what is the meaning of this <s>Vārttika</s>? — therefore he says: 'But by the term <s>vyavasāyātmaka</s> (of the nature of determination)...'

children.text: ekapadaparigrahaṃ sphuṭaṃ manvāno 'pi dvipadaparigrahaṃ vyācaṣṭa---dvipadeti //
children.translated_text: Even while considering the inclusion by a single term as clear, he explains the inclusion by two terms: 'By two terms...'

children.text:
uttaraprabandhopayogaṃ darśayannāha--tadevamiti /
lakṣaṇamidamanumānam /
tacca tadābhāsād vivekena sugamaṃ bhavati /
sa ca tadābhāseṣu āviṣkṛteṣu bhavatītyāśayavataḥ ayamārambha ityarthaḥ /
tator'thādityatra hi pañcamyā hetutvamarthasya vijñānaṃ pratidarśitam /
tatparaśca evakāraḥ evaṃ saṃbadhyate--sa vyapadeśakor'tho hetureva yasya na punaraheturapi tadvijñānaṃ pratyakṣamiti /
children.translated_text: And the particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone) is connected thus: 'That designating object is the cause alone — [the cognition] whose [cause] is not also a non-cause — such cognition is perception.'

children.text: evaṃ cāyogavyavaccheda eva /
children.translated_text: And thus, there is only the exclusion of non-connection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>).

children.text: tathāpyanyayogavyavacchedo 'pi vārttikakṛtā nirākartavya iti vyākhyāyāmubhayaṃ darśitavān /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, [since] the exclusion of connection with another (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>) too was to be refuted by the <s>Vārttika</s>-author, he showed both in the explanation.

children.text: yadi tata eva tabhdavati, nārthāntarādityavyapadeśakādityato na virodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: If [cognition arises] from that [designator] alone and what possesses that [designator], and not from anything else — [this understanding of] '<s>avyapadeśaka</s>' (non-designating [cause]) — resolves the contradiction.

Showing the usefulness for the subsequent discourse, he says: 'Thus indeed...' This definition is of inference. And that becomes easily [distinguishable] through distinction from its semblance. And that [distinction from semblance] occurs when the semblances are revealed — this is the intention behind the commencement [of the discussion]. The meaning is: in 'from that object,' the ablative case shows the causality of the object with respect to cognition.

children.text:
nanvanumānaviśeṣastāvat kaścidavyapadeśakādevotpadyate /
tato na tasya vyudāsaḥ kṛta ityata āha--tator'thādityatra hīti /
pratyakṣajāteridaṃ lakṣaṇam /
tasyāśca pratiyoginyanumānādijātireva, tathā ca tasyā eva
children.translated_text: Now, a particular kind of inference arises from a non-designating [cause] alone. So its exclusion has not been accomplished — therefore he says: 'In the phrase \"from that object\"...' This definition belongs to the genus of perception. And its counter-class is the genus of inference and the like. And thus, the exclusion of that [counter-]

children.text: jātervyavacchedo vivakṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: genus alone is intended.

children.text: sa caitāvataiva siddha ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that is accomplished by just this much — that is the meaning.

children.text:
yatraiva yajjātīya eva /
tadayogastasya vyapadeśakasya hetutvenāyogastadapratyakṣamiti /
tena vyapadeśo hi tadupādhikaṃ nirūpaṇami vivakṣitam /
na ca jñānaṃ kartrā karaṇena vā nirūpyate, api tu karmaṇaivetyarthaḥ /
abhidhānāparyavasānāt śabdavyāpārāparyavasānāt /
tacchabdasya pūrvaprakrānta evārthe saḍketitatvāt, tadanabhidhāne 'vācakatvaprasaḍgāditi bhāvaḥ /
pūrvaprakrāntaśca vyapadeśaka eva /
sa cārtha eveti viśeṣyaḥ prāpyate, nāntarīyakatvādityarthaḥ /
naivaṃ vārttikamityata āha---abhyupetya tviti /
anumānādivyudāsārthaṃ hyayogavyavacchedaḥ /
sa
children.translated_text: 'Wherever' — of whatever genus alone. The non-connection of that — of that designator — as a cause: what lacks that is non-perceptual. Therefore, 'designation' (<s>vyapadeśa</s>) — the intended meaning is determination conditioned by that [designator]. And cognition is not determined by the agent or the instrument, but by the object alone — that is the meaning. 'Because the denotation does not extend' — because the operation of the word does not extend [to it]. Because the word is conventionally associated with the previously mentioned object alone; and in the non-denotation of that, there would be the absurd consequence of [the word] being non-expressive — this is the purport. And what was previously mentioned is precisely the designator. And that is the object — [thus] the qualified [entity] is reached, due to inseparability — that is the meaning. 'The <s>Vārttika</s> is not so' — therefore he says: 'But having accepted...' For the exclusion of non-connection is for the purpose of excluding inference and the like. And that

children.text: cānyayogavyavacchede 'pi sidhyatītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: is accomplished even in the exclusion of connection with another — that is the meaning.

children.text: nanvanyogavyavacchedo 'śakya eva, indriyāderavyapadeśakasyāpi tatkāraṇatvādata āha--anyavyavacchede 'pīti /
children.translated_text: Now, the exclusion of connection with another is simply impossible, since the sense-organ and the like, even though non-designating, are also causes of that [perception] — therefore he says: 'Even in the exclusion of another...'

children.text: indriyādayo hyavyapadeśakā api vyapadeśakādhipatyenaiva jñānajanakā ityavirodhitayā na te vyavacchedyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The sense-organs and the like, though non-designating, generate cognition only under the dominance of the designator — therefore, being non-contradictory, they are not to be excluded.

children.text: liḍgādayastu vyapadeśakādhipatyanirapekṣatayā tadvirodhina iti ta evānye vyavacchettavyā ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the like, being independent of the dominance of the designator, are contradictory to it — therefore it is they alone that are the 'others' to be excluded — that is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu sarvaṃ ca svaviṣayāditi vārttikamasaṅgatameva, smṛtyanumitibhrāntīnāṃ svaviṣayāpanutpatterata āha--yatsaṃvṛtitveneti /
nanu bhrāntijñānamapi na vyapadeśakam antareṇa bhavati, tat kutaścodyamatasmādapītyata āha--purovartīti /
atasmādapītyatra yadyapi na śrūyate, tathāpi vyapadeśakādapi na bhavatīti boddhavyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although 'even from what is not that' is not heard [in the text], nevertheless, the meaning to be understood is: '[perception] does not arise even from a designator [in the wrong sense].'

children.text: tadidamuktam--yena viśeṣarūpeṇa tasya vyapadiśyate na tatastabhdavatīti /
children.translated_text: This is what is said: 'By that specific form by which that [object] is designated — [cognition] that possesses that [specific form] does not [arise] from that [object].'

children.text: tasmād yattata eva bhavati tato bhavatyevetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning is: what arises from that alone, arises from that alone.

children.text: atataśca na tataścetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And what [arises] from what is not that — does not [arise] from that — that is the meaning.

Now, the <s>Vārttika</s> 'and all from its own object' is entirely incoherent, since memory, inference, and error do not arise from their own objects — therefore he says: 'What, in a concealed manner...' Now, even erroneous cognition does not occur without a designator — so from where is the objection 'even from what is not that [designator]'? — therefore he says: 'What is in front...'

children.text:
nanu vyapadeśakādanutpatterityavyapadeśakādutpatteriti vā codyamupakrābhyāśakte rajatāt notpadyata iti vākchalamātrāmityata āha--na hyatasmādāropitād rūpāditi /
ayamarthaḥ /
mithyājñānanirāso hyanyayogavyavacchedena vā, ayogavyavacchedena vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, anyayogavyavacchedasya tatrāpi bhāvāt /
tadā hi sa na syāt /
yadyavyapadeśakasyaiva, vaṇigvīthyāṃ svatantrasya rajatasya hetutvaṃ syāt /
na caitadasti /
tadidamuktam--na hyatasmādāropitāt tatrāsatastanmithyājñānaṃ bhavati /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, vyapadeśakasya hetutvādeva /
rajataṃ vyapadeśakaṃ na heturiti cet? kathaṃ punā rajataṃ vyapadeśakaṃ svātantryeṇa purovartyātmanā vā? na tāvadādyaḥ,
children.translated_text: Now, [the objection could be framed as] 'because it does not arise from a designator' or 'because it arises from a non-designator' — this is mere verbal quibbling — [like saying] 'it does not arise from silver' — therefore he says: 'For not from that — the superimposed form and so forth.' The meaning is this: is the exclusion of erroneous cognition through the exclusion of connection with another, or through the exclusion of non-connection? Not the first, because the exclusion of connection with another obtains there [in error] too. For in that case, it would not obtain — if the independent silver itself, in the marketplace, were the cause — but this is not the case. This is what is said: 'For erroneous cognition does not arise from that superimposed [silver], which does not exist there.' Nor the second, because the designator is indeed a cause.

children.text:
sāmānādhikaraṇyānupapatteḥ, svamithyātvaprasaḍgācca /
purovartyātmanā ca pratyantare tad bhavati vyapadeśakam /
sa ca purovartyātmā heturevetyayogavyavaccheda eva /
tadidamukam--āropitaṃ tu rajatamasya viṣayo dṛśyamānākāratayeti /
ayaṃ tvabhiprāyaḥ syāt, yādṛśākāreṇa vyapadeśakor'thaḥ tādṛśādutpannaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣamiti /
children.translated_text: But this might be the intended meaning: cognition that arises from the designating object with the very form by which it designates is perception.

children.text: na tvayaṃ lakṣaṇapadānāmarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But this is not the meaning of the words of the definition.

children.text: na cābhiprāyaviśuddhimātreṇa paraḥ pratipādayituṃ śakyate, pratyabhijñāsvasaṃvedanāvyāpakatvācca /
children.translated_text: And the opponent cannot be made to understand merely by the purity of intention, and because [the definition] does not pervade recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) and self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>).

children.text: etacca jaiminīye sphuṭībhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: And this will become clear in the <s>Jaiminīya</s> [context].

If [one says] 'silver is a designator [but] not a cause' — how is silver a designator? Independently, or in the form of what is in front? Not the first, because co-referentiality would be unjustified, and because its own falsity would follow. But in the form of what is in front, it is a designator in another cognition. And that 'what-is-in-front' form is indeed the cause — so this is just the exclusion of non-connection. This is what is said: 'But the superimposed silver is the object of this [error] in the form of the visible appearance.'

children.text:
tadetallakṣaṇamābhiprāyikamapyasmannaye kadācit saṃbhāvyeta, tvannate tu viruddhamasiddhaṃ cedamuktaṃ vārttikakṛtā /
tadetad vyutpādayati--yadyapyetaditi /
vyapadeśako hyartho vartamānatayā sarvatra pratyakṣasya viṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the designating object, as present, is the object of perception everywhere.

children.text: sa ceddheturevaivamatītaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: And if that were the cause alone, it would in this way be past.

children.text: tathā ca pratyakṣatve sādhye 'pratyakṣatvameva sidhyatīti bhavati viruddhatvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, when perceptuality is to be proved, non-perceptuality alone would be proved — thus there is the fault of contradiction (<s>viruddhatva</s>) — that is the meaning.

children.text: atha vartamāna eva vyapadeśakastadā samānakālatayā tator'thādityasiddhamāha--tatsamāneti //
children.translated_text: If the designator is present, then, since [cause and effect are] simultaneous, 'from that object' would be unestablished — he says: 'Simultaneous with that...'

This definition, even as intended [rather than literal], might sometimes be conceivable in our system, but in your [Buddhist] system it is contradictory and unestablished — this is said by the <s>Vārttika</s>-author. He explains this: 'Even though this...'

children.text: yattu kenacit pralapitam--aparokṣajñānāvabhāsitaiva vartamānateti, tat tucchamityupekṣitavān /
children.translated_text: Now, what someone has babbled — 'Presentness is nothing but what is manifested by a direct cognition' — that is dismissed as worthless.

children.text: tathā hyaparokṣaikasarvajñavijñānāvabhāsitayā sarveṣāmarthānāmekakālatvāt savyetaragoviṣāṇavat kāryakāraṇabhāvavārtaivocchidyeta /
children.translated_text: For if presentness were being manifested by a single direct omniscient cognition, then all objects would be simultaneous, and like a right-and-left horn of a cow, the very discourse of cause and effect would be severed.

children.text: pūrvoktaścānuyogastadavastha eveti //
children.translated_text: And the previously stated rejoinder remains in the same state.

children.text: bhinnakālaṃ kathaṃ grāhyam
children.translated_text: 'How can what belongs to different times be apprehended?' —

children.text: ityādinā kāryakāraṇabhāvaviśeṣa eva grāhyagrāhakabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: by this and so forth, the apprehender-apprehended relation is a particular case of the cause-effect relation.

children.text: sa ca bhinnakālayoreva bhavatīti svabhāṣayā samarthitaṃ pareṇa /
children.translated_text: And that obtains only between things of different times — thus it has been established by the opponent in his own words.

children.text: na ca vayaṃ bhinnakālayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaviśeṣam avajānīmahe; kiṃ tvatītasya vartamānatayāvabhāsanaṃ tasya vā satyatvam /
children.translated_text: And we do not disregard the particular cause-effect relation between things of different times. What [we disregard] is the appearing of the past as present, or the reality of that [appearing].

children.text: na ca tadanena samarthitamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that has not been established by him — that is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu jñānākārārpaṇakṣamamiti vadataiva samarthitametat /
anene hi na pratibhāsamānatayārtho grāhya iti vyavahniyate /
kiṃ nāma? ākārārpakatayeti darśitam /
ākāra eva tvavabhāsamamānatayā grāhyaḥ, sa ca jñānātmabhūtatayā vartamāna eveti na kaścid virodha ityata āha--anahaḍkāreti /
vijñānād bhinnasya nīlāderanubhavo
children.translated_text: Now, by saying 'capable of imparting its form to cognition,' this [point] has been established. For by this, it is shown that the object is not apprehended as 'appearing.' What then? It is shown [that it is apprehended] as 'imparting its form.' But the form itself is apprehended as appearing, and that, being of the nature of cognition, is present — so there is no contradiction — therefore he says: 'Without ego-sense...' The experience of blue and the like, which are different from consciousness —

children.text: yadi satyo, na jñānagatākāravedanam /
children.translated_text: if veridical, [then] it is not the cognition of a form belonging to cognition.

children.text: asatyaścenna pratayakṣaṃ pramāṇamiti seyamubhayataḥ pāśā rajjurityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And if non-veridical, then perception is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) — thus this is a rope that binds from both sides — that is the meaning.

children.text: api ca bhavatvākāravedanam, bhavatu vārthasyākārārpakatvaṃ vā , tathāpi
children.translated_text: Moreover, let there be the cognition of form; or let there be the capacity of the object to impart its form — nevertheless,

children.text: tator'thādvijñānaṃ pratyakṣam
children.translated_text: 'From that object, the cognition [that is] perception' —

children.text: ityasiddhaṃ lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: this definition is unestablished.

children.text: tathā hi pratibhāsamānasyaiva jñānaṃ vyapadiśyate, na tvapratibhāsamānasya /
children.translated_text: For cognition is designated with respect to what is appearing, not with respect to what is not appearing.

children.text: ākāraśca pratibhāsane na tu janako 'pyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the form [is relevant] in the appearing, but not the object as generator.

children.text: tasmād vyapadeśakona janakaḥ, janakaśca na vyapadeśaka iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the designator is not the generator, and the generator is not the designator.

children.text:
atra śaṅkate---na ceti /
pratibhāsamānākāradvārārtho vyapadeśako janakaścetyapi na cetyarthaḥ /
kutaḥ?
children.translated_text: Here he raises the objection: 'Nor...' The meaning of 'nor' is: nor [can one say] that the object is a designator and a generator through the medium of the appearing form. Why?

children.text: bhāktatvaprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the absurd consequence of [the word 'perception'] being figurative (<s>bhākta</s>).

children.text: kimato yadyevamityata āha---na ca gauṇamukhyeti /
children.translated_text: What [fault is there] if it were so? — therefore he says: 'Nor the figurative and the primary...'

children.text: yathā hyavinābhāvamantarbhāvyaiva gaḍgāśabdastīre, lakṣyamāṇaguṇayogamantarbhāvyasihaśabdo māṇavake vartate, na tathā dhūmapratyakṣamagnau siṃhapratyakṣaṃ māṇavake, pramāṇāntarocchedaprasaḍgādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' operates on the bank by incorporating [the relation of] inseparability, and the word 'lion' operates on a boy by incorporating the perceived connection of the quality — [the word 'perception'] does not [similarly] operate on fire as '<s>dhūmapratyakṣa</s>' (smoke-perception = perception of fire via smoke) or on a boy as '<s>siṃhapratyakṣa</s>' (lion-perception). The meaning is: because of the absurd consequence of eliminating other <s>pramāṇas</s>.

children.text: tadidamuktam--bhinnaprasthānatvāditi //
children.translated_text: This is what is said: 'Because of the different methods [of the various <s>pramāṇas</s>].'

children.text: etenaitadapi nirastam, yadāhuḥ--pratyakṣasiddhenākāreṇa artho 'numīyata iti phalataḥ pratyakṣor'tha iti /
children.translated_text: By this, the following too is refuted — what they say: 'The object is inferred through the form established by perception; therefore, the object is perceptual in its result.'

children.text: anumīyata iti kor'thaḥ? anumitau parisphuratīti, tacca bauddhanaye svapne 'pi durlabham, anumiterapi svākārālīkayorevānyatarasmin paryavasitatvāt /
children.translated_text: What is the meaning of 'is inferred'? 'It shines forth in the inference' — and this, in the Buddhist system, is hard to come by even in dreams, since even inference culminates in one or the other — either its own form or unreality.

children.text: yaśca sarvathaiva jñānāgocaraḥ sa vyavahniyata iti kutaḥ? tasmādākāravādapakṣebāhyor'tho heyaḥ, tadabhyupagame vā ākāravāda ityanenābhiprāyeṇāha--tasmānnirākāramiti //
children.translated_text: And that which is entirely beyond the reach of cognition — from where [comes the claim that] it is the object of conventional usage? Therefore, on the <s>ākāravāda</s> (representation-theory) position, the external object should be abandoned. Or if it is accepted, then the <s>ākāravāda</s> [should be abandoned] — with this intention he says: 'Therefore, formless...'

children.text:
śaṅkata iti /
na hi kiñcid vastubhūtaṃ vācyaṃ nāma saugatānāṃ samasti, lakṣaṇavākyena tu vyavahāramātraṃ prasādhyate, sa cātadvyāvṛttiniṣṭha ityarthaḥ /
jñānasya kalpanāpoḍhasya pratyakṣatayā vyutpādyamānasya kathaṃ sarver'thā pratyakṣatayā prasajyerannityata āha--na hīti /
dignāgasyātivyāpakatayā alakṣaṇam, kīrtestvavyāpakatayā vikalpapratyakṣānavarodhāt, tasya ca pratyakṣatayā vyutpādanāt, aniṣṭamātrasyātiprasañjakatvāditi siddhāntaḥ /
svadarśanasamādhitsayā vārttikamiti darśayituṃ codayati--nanu yadīti /
children.translated_text: In order to show that the <s>Vārttika</s> is for the purpose of vindicating his own view, he raises the objection: 'Now, if...'

children.text: sāmānyānvitam, abhidhīyata iti vārttikaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Connected with universal' — the completion of the <s>Vārttika</s> is: 'is denoted.'

children.text: manuṣyatvajātimānityartha iti /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: possessing the universal of humanness.

children.text: manuṣyaśabdasya brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇatvādijātimattayā avācyo 'pi manuṣyatvajātimattayā vācya evetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, though not denotable by the word 'human' insofar as he possesses the universal of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood and the like, is denotable [by it] insofar as he possesses the universal of humanness.

'He raises an objection' — for the Buddhists have nothing that is a real expressible entity. Rather, by the definitional statement, only conventional usage is established, and that is grounded in exclusion from what is not that (<s>atadvyāvṛtti</s>) — that is the meaning. How would all objects be entailed as perceptual when cognition, free from conceptual construction, is being explained as perception? — therefore he says: 'For...' The established conclusion is: <s>Dignāga</s>'s [definition] is a non-definition due to over-extension; <s>Dharmakīrti</s>'s is [a non-definition] due to under-extension, because it fails to include conceptual perception (<s>vikalpapratyakṣa</s>); and since that [conceptual perception] is [accepted as] explained as perception [by them], only what is undesired is entailed.

children.text: paunaruktyaṃ pariharannāha--athāścakarṇeti //
children.translated_text: Resolving the redundancy, he says: 'Now, regarding <s>Āścakarṇa</s>...'

children.text:
nanu vyatyaye 'pi satsaṃprayoga iti syāt, na tu tattacchabdasya prakṛtatayā viṣayaḥ kaścidastītyāha--buddhyeti /
yadyapi pratyakṣajñānamapyanena lakṣaṇena svātmani pratyakṣaṃ na syādeva, tathāpīndriyārthasannikarṣajanyatvamātraṃ tāvat tatrāpyastīti kadācit paro brūyādityata āha--anumānādīti /
etena tator'thādityasyābhiprāyaśeṣo dūṣitaḥ, pratyabhijñānasvasaṃvedanayoravyāpakatvāditi
children.translated_text: Now, even in the transposition, 'contact' would obtain; but the word in question does not have any specific object as its topic — he says: 'Of cognition...' Although even perceptual cognition would not be perceptual with respect to itself by this definition, nevertheless, since at least 'being produced by sense-object contact' does obtain even there, the opponent might at some point say so — therefore he says: 'Of inference and the like...' By this, the intended supplement of 'from that object' has been criticized, because of the non-pervasion of recognition and self-awareness.

children.text: atha tatpūrvakaṃ trividhamanumānaṃ pūrvavaccheṣavatsāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ca //1.1.5 //
children.translated_text: Now, preceded by that [perception], inference is threefold: <s>pūrvavat</s> (from prior [cause to effect]), <s>śeṣavat</s> (from remainder), and <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation). // 1.1.5 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
sūtraṃ paṭhati /
vyākhyātumiti śeṣaḥ /
sūtrāvatāramātramasahamānaṃ pratyāha---atreti /
sādharmyeṇa hi niyamavateti
children.translated_text: He reads the <s>sūtra</s>. The completion is: 'in order to explain.' Unable to tolerate even the mere introduction of the <s>sūtra</s>, he objects: 'Here...' 'For by similarity, with restriction' —

children.text:
śeṣaḥ /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
vaidharmyeṇetyapi draṣṭavyam /
aprāmāṇyavidhānaṃ prāmāṇyaniṣedha eva /
nāpratyakṣaṃ pramāṇamityanena hi viśeṣaniṣedhena kaṇṭhataḥ anumānaprāmāṇyaniṣedhor'thataḥ pratyakṣaprāmāṇyavidhiśca vivakṣitaḥ /
na caitadubhayamapi pramāṇam antareṇa sidhyati /
na cātra pratyakṣameva prabhavatīti cintitamādivākye /
nāpi śabdopamāne, svapratyaye tayoranavakāśāt, parapratyaye 'pi dharmyasiddheḥ /
siddhāvapi parasyāptatvāniścayāt /
tasmādatīndriyavidhiniṣedhayoranumānamanaḍgīkṛtyāśakyatvādaśakyāpahnavamanumānamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since without accepting inference it is impossible [to establish] the positive determination and negative determination of supersensible [objects], inference is impossible to deny — this is the meaning.

children.text: dṛṣṭasādharmyaṃ ca niyatamiti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And the observed similarity is invariable' — is the completion.

children.text: kathaṃ tenaiva tasyāprāmāṇyamiti vyāghātamātraṃ vivakṣitam? tenāyamarthaḥ---yadyanu mānamapramāṇam, kathaṃ tenaiva vidhiniṣedhasiddhiḥ? atha tena vidhiniṣedhasiddhiḥ, kathaṃ tasyāprāmāṇyamiti? kiṃ cānumānamanaḍgīkṛtya parapratyāyanāya śabdaprayogo 'pyayamaśakyaḥ---paravedanapratipatterava tadantareṇāśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: How can the very thing [i.e., inference] [be used to establish] the invalidity of that [inference]? — only the contradiction is intended. Therefore, the meaning is: if inference is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, how can positive and negative determination be established by it? But if positive and negative determination are established by it, how can it be invalid? Moreover, without accepting inference, even this very use of words for conveying [a thesis] to another is impossible — because the cognition of the other's understanding is itself impossible without it.

children.text: na cet parapratyāyanam, nūnamaunmattyamāviṣkaroti vakturityāha---api ceti //
children.translated_text: And if there is no conveying to the other, surely the speaker is displaying madness — he says: 'api ca' (moreover).

— is the completion. And this is merely indicative. It should also be read as [establishing] through dissimilarity. The statement of invalidity is indeed a denial of validity. For by 'perception is not a non-perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s>' — what is intended by this specific denial is explicitly the denial of the validity of inference, and implicitly the positive establishment of the validity of perception. And neither of these two is established without a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And it has been considered in the introductory statement that perception alone is not capable [of establishing] this. Nor verbal testimony or analogy — since in one's own cognition there is no scope for those two, and even in the cognition of another, the subject [to be proved] is unestablished. And even if [the subject were] established, [there remains] the non-certainty of the trustworthiness of the other [person].

children.text: sūtre vibhāgo 'pyastīti vyavacchidyāha--lakṣaṇasūtratātparyamāheti /
syādetadativyāpakamiti /
children.translated_text: 'This might be over-extensive' —

children.text: atrāvyāpakaṃ cetyapi draṣṭavyam, ata ubhayavyutpādanopasaṃhāravirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: and here it should also be read as 'under-extensive' — hence the contradiction in the summary-conclusion of both derivations.

children.text: vigrahatrayapradarśanaṃ vigrahatrayaṃ draṣṭavyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The display of the threefold analysis' means the threefold analysis should be understood — this is the meaning.

children.text: vyāptismṛtisahāyād dvitīyaliṅgadarśanādevānumitisiddheralaṃ tṛtīyaliṅgadarśanakalpanayeti yathāśrutabhāṣyānusāriṇaḥ tān risyati na ceti //
children.translated_text: Since inferential cognition is established from the second observation of the mark alone, aided by the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) — making the postulation of a third observation of the mark superfluous — he criticizes those who follow the <s>Bhāṣya</s> literally: 'na ca' (and not).
Indicating that there is also a division in the <s>sūtra</s>, he says: 'lakṣaṇasūtratātparyam āha' (he states the purport of the definitional sūtra).

children.text:
sa eṣa saṃskārodbodhamadhikamabhyupagacchato doṣa uktaḥ /
yastu sahakārilābhādanyo na kaścidudbodho nāmeti manyate, taṃ pratyāha--vinaśyadavasthasyeti /
na hi vyāptismaraṇamātrādanumitiḥ, nāpi liṅgadarśanamātrāt /
kiṃ tarhi?
children.translated_text: That fault has been stated for one who accepts additional awakening of latent impressions (<s>saṃskārodbodha</s>). But to one who holds that there is no awakening apart from the obtaining of an auxiliary cause, he responds: 'vinaśyadavasthasyā' (in the perishing state). For inferential cognition does not [arise] from the mere recollection of <s>vyāpti</s>, nor from the mere observation of the mark. What then?

children.text:
vyāptiviśiṣṭaliṅgadarśanāt /
na ca vyāptiviśiṣṭaṃ liṅgamekaikasyobhayasya vā gocaraḥ, kiṃ tu svatantramubhayamubhayasya /
na ca svatantrobhayajñāne 'pi viśiṣṭajñānaṃ bhavati /
tadidamuktam--parasparavārtānabhijñatayā svatantrasvasvaviṣayaparyavasitatayā /
mitho ghaṭanāyogo viśiṣṭapratyayayoga ityarthaḥ /
na ca svatantrametadubhayamekātmasamavāyamātreṇānumiti bhāvayiṣyatīti vācyam /
dvitīyaliṅgadarśanaṃ hi vasatugatyā liṅgaviṣayamityetāvataiva vyāptismṛteḥ sahakāriliṅgatvarūpollekhitayā vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, dūrād dhūmaviṣayavastutvajñānasyāpi prakārāntarāyātavyāptismṛtiṃ prati sahakāritvaprasaḍgāt /
dvitīyastu dvitīyaliṅgadarśane
children.translated_text: From the observation of the mark as qualified by <s>vyāpti</s>. And the mark qualified by <s>vyāpti</s> is not the domain of either one [cognition] individually or of both [separately]; rather, both independently are the domain of both [cognitions]. And even when there are two independent cognitions, a cognition of the qualified [whole] does not arise. This is what is said: 'due to being unaware of each other's content, due to being confined to their own respective objects independently — their mutual integration is impossible, [hence] the impossibility of a cognition of the qualified [whole].' Nor should one say that these two independent [cognitions] will produce inferential cognition merely through their inherence in the same <s>ātman</s>. For does the second observation of the mark [aid the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s>] merely by having the mark as its object, or by evoking the mark-character as the form of the auxiliary-cause? The first [option] is not [correct], because even the cognition of the mere thingness [of smoke] from afar would absurdly become an auxiliary cause for the recollection of <s>vyāpti</s> that has arrived through another route. But the second [option], in the second observation of the mark,

children.text: nāstyeva /
children.translated_text: simply does not exist.

children.text: tadidamuktam--vṛttyā salvayaṃ ghaṭayet, vyāpāreṇa na rūpato nobhayasamavāyitāmātreṇātiprasaḍgāditi //
children.translated_text: This is what is said: 'it should connect through its operation (<s>vṛtti</s>), inherently; through its function (<s>vyāpāra</s>), not through its form; not through mere co-inherence in both — because of over-extension.'

children.text:
tasmāt liṅgatvollekhi tṛtīyaṃ liṅgadarśanamāstheyamittyāha--tasmāditi /
iha tādātmyatadutpattisvarūpādiniścaye pratibandhaniścayastadā na syāt yadi te eva pratibandhaḥ, tābhyāṃ samānopāyo vā pratibandhaḥ, tayoreva vā pratibandhaparyavasānam, te eva vā pratibandhaniścayopāyaḥ /
tatropāyatvaṃ sahacārāvasāye vā, vyabhicāraśaḍkānirāse vā, vyabhicāraśaḍkāpyupādhidarśanād vā, upādhiśaṅkayā vā, bhūyo bhūyaḥ sahacaritayoḥ apyulabdhayoḥ kayościdarthayorvyabhicārānusandhānamātreṇa veti? tatra ca sahacārāvasāyaḥ tāvadindriyasannikarṣādhīnotpattiḥ tadutpattyaniścaye 'pi vahnidhūmayoḥ sidhyati, vyabhicāraśaḍkāpi darśanayogyopādhyadhīnā yogyānupalambhabādhādeva nirastā /
atīndriyāstu upādhayaḥ anyatra pramāṇaparidṛṣṭāḥ śaḍkitā api yathā nivartante, tathā vakṣyāmaḥ /
pramāṇapathānavatīrṇopādhiśaḍkā tu tadutpattiniścayamapyāskandatīti kathaṃ sā
children.translated_text: Therefore, a third observation of the mark that evokes the mark-character must be maintained — he says: 'tasmāt' (therefore). Here, if at the ascertainment of the intrinsic nature of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>) there were ascertainment of the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), then [the ascertainment of <s>pratibandha</s>] would not be [possible] if those themselves were the <s>pratibandha</s>, or if the <s>pratibandha</s> had the same means [of ascertainment] as those two, or if the <s>pratibandha</s> terminated in just those two, or if those very two were the means of ascertaining the <s>pratibandha</s>. Among those [options]: is the means-status [established] upon the ascertainment of co-presence, or upon the removal of the suspicion of deviation, or [the suspicion of deviation arises] from observing a <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition), or from the mere suspicion of a <s>upādhi</s>, or [is it established] merely by the investigation of deviation between two things that have been observed together again and again but have not been found [to deviate]? Among these: the ascertainment of co-presence — since its arising depends on sense-contact — is established for fire and smoke even when their origination is not certain. The suspicion of deviation too, being dependent on a perceivable <s>upādhi</s>, is removed by the very sublation of non-apprehension of what is fit [to be perceived]. But supersensible <s>upādhis</s> — those that are suspected even though observed elsewhere by a <s>pramāṇa</s> — how they are removed, we shall explain. But the suspicion of a <s>upādhi</s> that has never entered the domain of a <s>pramāṇa</s> overrides even the certainty of origination — so how is that [suspicion]

children.text:
tena nivartanīyetyāha--atrocyata iti /
sahacaritayorvyabhicāradarśanamātreṇa tu vyabhicāraśaḍkā kāryakāraṇayorapi samānā, tadutpattilakṣaṇaviśeṣasiddhau vipakṣe bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā śaḍgānivṛttiriti yadi, tadāsmākamapi svābhāvikasaṃbandhasiddhau vipakṣe bādhakapramāṇavṛttyaiva śaḍkānivṛttiriti samaḥ samādhiḥ /
viśeṣastu svābhāvikasaṃbandhasya vyāpakatvam, avyāpakatvaṃ tu tadutpattyāderityāha--api ceti /
tadidamuktam--sa ca yo vā sa veti /
na ca samānopāyatvādubhayoranyatarāniścaye nānyataraniścaya iti sāmpratam, pratibandhāniścaye 'pi hutāśabhasmanoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvāvadhāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is it correct [to say] that since the two [svābhāvika and tadutpatti] have the same means, the non-ascertainment of one entails the non-ascertainment of the other — because even when <s>pratibandha</s> is not ascertained, the cause-effect relation between fire-sacrifice ashes is ascertained.

children.text: kāryakāraṇabhāvāniścaye 'pi dhāmadhūmayoḥ pratibandhāvabodhāt /
children.translated_text: And even when the cause-effect relation is not ascertained, the <s>pratibandha</s> between fireplace and smoke is understood.

children.text: yadanatītameva vahnimanumimata ityāha--api ca kāryāditi /
children.translated_text: That which is inferred as fire that has not passed away — he says: 'api ca kāryāt' (moreover, from the effect).

children.text: tayoreva pratibandhaḥ paryavasyatīti pakṣaṃ nirācaṣṭe--api ca rasāditi //
children.translated_text: He rejects the position that '<s>pratibandha</s> terminates in just those two [identity and origination]': 'api ca rasāt' (moreover, from taste).

to be removed by it [i.e., by the certainty of origination]? — he says: 'atrocyata' (here it is said). But the suspicion of deviation merely from the observation of deviation between co-present [items] is equally applicable even to cause and effect. If the cessation of suspicion in the case of origination-type <s>pratibandha</s> is through the operation of a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> in the dissimilar [cases] — then for us too, upon the establishment of the natural connection (<s>svābhāvikasaṃbandha</s>), the cessation of suspicion is through the very operation of a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> in the dissimilar [cases] — thus the resolution is the same. The distinction, however, is that the natural connection is more pervasive, while origination and the like are less pervasive — he says: 'api ca' (moreover). This is what is said: 'sa ca yo vā sa vā' (and that [natural connection] is either this or that).

children.text:
yattu bhede sati vyāpyavyāpakābhāva eva kāryakāraṇabhāva eva kāryakāraṇabhāva iti vyudapādi prajñākareṇa tat pāpādapi pāpīyaḥ /
tathā hi niyāmakavirahe bhinnāyoravyabhicāraḥ śaḍkākalaḍkāḍkitatvāt duravadhāraṇa iti tāmapanetuṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'nenopanītaḥ, sa ced rūpa eva kathaṃ tanniścayenaivāvyabhicāraniścayaḥ?
children.translated_text: But what <s>Prajñākara</s> has put forth — that where there is difference, <s>vyāpya-vyāpaka</s> (pervaded-pervader) relation is itself the cause-effect relation — that is worse than bad. For thus: in the absence of a determining factor, the non-deviation of two different things is difficult to ascertain, being tainted by the stain of suspicion — and it is to remove that [suspicion] that the cause-effect relation was introduced by him. If that [cause-effect relation] is identical in form [with the pervaded-pervader relation], how can the certainty of the former bring about the certainty of the latter?

children.text:
na caitat kīrteranumataṃ yad rasena rūpānumāne 'nyathābhyupāyamāha--yadi ca sarvalokasiddhamativāhya svayaṅkṛtalakṣaṇairvyavahāraḥ, tadā bhede satītyetadapi parihīyatām /
avyabhicāramātraṃ tadutpattirityevāstu /
laghu caivaṃ sati lakṣaṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: And in that case, the definition would be simpler.

children.text: tadātmano 'pi etadastīti cet? astu śiśapāpi vṛkṣakāryam /
children.translated_text: If it is said that this [mere non-deviation] applies even to identity (<s>tādātmya</s>)? Then let <s>śiśapā</s> (rosewood) also be an effect of tree-hood.

children.text: kathaṃ tenaiva tatkartavyamiti cet? ko doṣaḥ? asiddhaṃ siddhena sādhyate, natu tadeva siddhamasiddhaṃ ceti cet? hantaivamanāgatamapi kathaṃ vyāpakatāmātreṇa kāraṇamasiddhatvāt? vartamānamapi kathaṃ vyāpyatāmātreṇa kāryaṃ siddhatvāt? evaṃ samānakāle 'pi kathamavinābhāvamātreṇa kāryakāraṇabhūte, asiddhāvasthāyāmubhayorapyasādhakatvāviśeṣāt, siddhāvasthāyāmubhayorapyasādhyatvāviśeṣāt? tasmāt pūrvakālabhāvaniyamaḥ kāraṇatvaṃ kaścādbhāvitāniyamaḥ kāryatvam /
children.translated_text: If it is said: 'How can that very thing establish itself?' — what fault? If it is said: 'The unestablished is established by the established, but the very same thing cannot be both established and unestablished' — well then, by the same token, how is what is future a cause merely through pervasion, since it is unestablished? And how is what is present an effect merely through being pervaded, since it is [already] established? Similarly, even when simultaneous, how is one a cause and the other an effect merely through non-separation, when in the unestablished state there is no difference in the non-capacity of both to establish, and in the established state there is no difference in the non-need-to-be-established of both? Therefore, the restriction of existing at a prior time is cause-hood, and the restriction of existing at a subsequent time is effect-hood.

children.text: avinābhāvastu niyamamātramityeva jyāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: But <s>avinābhāva</s> (non-separation) is simply a restriction — this is the better [view].

And this is not approved by <s>Dharmakīrti</s>. For regarding the inference of form from taste, he states an alternative means: 'If one bypasses what is established by all people and conducts discourse through self-made definitions, then even 'where there is difference' should be abandoned. Let mere non-deviation be called 'origination.''

children.text: api ca rasarūpayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaniścayo vahnidhūmayoriva pratyakṣānupalambhasādhyo vā syāt, kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhau puñjāt puñjāntarotpāttiriti nyāyena vā? ādyastāvat kṣaṇayoraśakya eva, tayoreva pratyakṣānārohāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, would the ascertainment of the cause-effect relation of taste and form be established through perception and non-apprehension, as [in the case] of fire and smoke? Or through the principle 'from one aggregate, another aggregate arises' upon the establishment of momentariness? The first, to begin with, is impossible for [individual] moments, since those very [moments] do not even rise to the level of perception.

children.text: tatra tasyāniścāyakatvāt, santānayorapi duravabodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since [perception] is not capable of ascertaining [the cause-effect relation] there, it is also difficult to understand even for continua.

children.text: na hi vahneriva rūpasya pūrvakālatāniyamaṃ dhūmasyeva rasasya praścādbhāvitāniyamaṃ laukikāḥ pratipadyante /
children.translated_text: For ordinary people do not understand the restriction of form to the prior time, like fire, and the restriction of taste to the subsequent time, like smoke.

children.text: kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhinyāyastu na laukika iti vastuto laukikānāṃ rasato rūpānumānaṃ na syādityāha---laukikānāṃ cedamiti //
children.translated_text: And the principle of momentariness is not [accepted by] ordinary people. So in reality, the inference of form from taste by ordinary people would not exist — he says: 'laukikānāṃ cedam' (this is of ordinary people).

children.text:
api ca ityanena te eva pratibandha iti nirastam /
tādātmyaṃ tu gamyagamakabhāve pratyuta viruddhamityāha--api ceti /
na hi tadeva karma niśceyam, kartṛ ca svaniścayena niścāyakaṃ ca, niścitāniścitayoḥ parasparavirodhādityarthaḥ /
bhavatvabhede 'pi gamyagamakabhāvaḥ, tathāpi na śiśapātvena vṛkṣatvānumānamanavasaradusthātvāt /
children.translated_text: Let there be the relation of what is to be known and what makes known even without difference; even so, there is no inference of tree-hood from <s>śiśapā</s>-hood (<s>śiśapātva</s>), because of the impossibility of the occasion for investigation.

children.text: na hyasti saṃbhavaḥ sāmānyamaniścitaṃ niścitastu viśeṣa ityāśaḍkya kenacit samarthitam utthāpya dūṣayati---yatviti /
children.translated_text: For there is no possibility that the universal is unascertained while the particular is ascertained — he raises this doubt, having attributed it to someone, refutes it: 'yat tu' (but what).

children.text: bhinnayoreva vyāvṛttyorgamyagamakabhāvaḥ kiṃ tvabhinnādhyavaseyasaṃbandhāt tayorapi tādātmyaṃ vyavahniyata iti /
children.translated_text: The exclusions (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) of precisely two different things have the relation of what is to be known and what makes known; but due to the relation with that which is determined as non-different, even the identity of those two is conventionally used.

children.text: sa yadyabhinnadevadattasaṃbandhāt, chatrakuṇḍalayorapyabhedaṃ vyavaharati ko vārayitā? kevalaṃ pramāṇaprayojanayorvyāvṛttirlaukikavirodhaścetyanenābhiprāyeṇopasaṃharati---tasmādita //
children.translated_text: If, due to the relation with a non-different <s>Devadatta</s>, one conventionally uses non-difference even of an umbrella and earrings — who would prevent that? Only the exclusion of <s>pramāṇa</s> and purpose, and the conflict with common usage [prevent it] — with this intention he concludes: 'tasmāt' (therefore).

'Moreover' — by this, [the position that] 'those very things are the <s>pratibandha</s>' is refuted. But identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), in the relation of what is to be known and what makes known, is rather contradictory — he says: 'api ca' (moreover). For the very same thing cannot be both what is to be ascertained and, through its own ascertainment, what ascertains — because the ascertained and the unascertained are mutually contradictory — this is the meaning.

children.text:
asyedaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇamityekaḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
svābhāvikaṃ saṃbandhamupasaṃhṛtya tasya svarūpamāha---tathā hīti /
svābhāviko nirūpādhirityarthaḥ /
yadyapi vyabhicārāvyabhicāravyāpte aupādhikatvānaupādhikatve, tābhyāṃ ca
children.translated_text: 'This is the effect of that, this the cause' — this is one connection. Having concluded the natural connection, he states its intrinsic nature: 'tathā hī' (for thus). '<s>Svābhāvika</s>' (natural) means unconditional (<s>nirupādhi</s>) — this is the meaning. Although the conditional and the unconditional are pervaded by deviation and non-deviation respectively, and by those two

children.text:
vyabhicārāvyabhicārāviti niyamaḥ /
tau hi na tāvannirnimittau sārvatrikatvaprasaḍgāt, niyataviṣayau copalabhyete /
nāpyanimittau /
sopādherapyavyabhicāre nirūpādherapi vyabhicāre aniyamaprasaḍgāt, , tathā sati kāryātmanorapi kāraṇātmavyabhicāraḥ prasajyeta /
tasmādupādhāvavaśyaṃ vyabhicāro 'nupādhau avaśyamavyabhicāraḥ /
vyabhicāre 'vaśyamupādhiravyabhicāre 'vaśyamupādhyabhāvaḥ /
tathāpi yatra sphuṭo vyabhicārastatra niṣphalamupādhyanusaraṇaṃ tadarthatvāt tasya /
asphuṭe tu vyabhicāre tasyopayogaḥ /
na tūpādhitadamāvasiddhaye vyabhicārāvyabhicāraparyeṣaṇamupayujyate /
children.translated_text: But the search for deviation and non-deviation is not useful for establishing the [presence or absence of a] <s>upādhi</s>.

children.text: vyabhicārādisiddhau satyāmupādhitadabhāvaparīkṣāyā niṣphalatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because, when deviation and the like are established, the examination of the <s>upādhi</s> and its absence is fruitless.

children.text: tasmādanyonyavyāptipradarśanamātraprayukto vyabhicāramudbhāvyāpyupādhimāha--yadā tviti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, motivated merely by the demonstration of mutual pervasion, he demonstrates the deviation and then states the <s>upādhi</s>: 'yadā tu' (but when).

children.text: yato na svābhāviko na nirūpādhikaḥ, tato na niyato nāvyabhicārītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Since [the connection] is not natural, not unconditional, therefore it is not invariable, not non-deviating — this is the meaning.

deviation and non-deviation [are respectively restricted] — this is the rule. For those two [conditional and unconditional connections] are not without a cause, because of the absurd consequence of universality, and they are observed to have restricted domains. Nor are they without a determining factor. For if the conditional also had non-deviation, and the unconditional also had deviation, there would follow the consequence of indeterminacy; and in that case, the absurd consequence would be that even identity-type [connections] would deviate from cause-type [connections]. Therefore, in the conditional, there is necessarily deviation; in the unconditional, there is necessarily non-deviation. Where there is deviation, there is necessarily a <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition); where there is non-deviation, there is necessarily the absence of a <s>upādhi</s>. Nevertheless, where the deviation is clear, the search for a <s>upādhi</s> is fruitless, since it [the search] is for the purpose of [establishing] that [deviation]. But when the deviation is unclear, the [search for a <s>upādhi</s>] is useful.

children.text:
atha dhūmādīnāmapi vahnyādibhiḥ kathaṃ svābhāvika ityata āha---svābhāvikastviti /
nanvasphuṭe vyabhicāre
children.translated_text: Now, how is the [connection] of smoke and the like with fire and the like also natural? — therefore he says: 'svābhāvikastu' (but the natural one). Now, when the deviation is unclear,

children.text: saphalamupādhyanusaraṇam /
children.translated_text: the search for a <s>upādhi</s> is fruitful.

children.text: tat kimatra nāsau sphuṭa ityata āha---kvacidvyabhicārasyādarśanāditi /
children.translated_text: Then why is the [deviation] not clear here? — therefore he says: 'kvacid vyabhicārasya adarśanāt' (because of the non-observation of deviation anywhere).

children.text: nanu kvacit kadācid vyabhicāro 'pi syādayogyatvācca na dṛśyetāpītyata āha---anupalabhyamānasyāpi kalpanānupatteḥ, anupalabhyamānavyabhicārakalpanādvārībhūtopādhyabhāvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, deviation might exist somewhere at some time, and due to unfitness [for observation] it might not be seen — therefore he says: 'anupalabhyamānasyāpi kalpanānupatteḥ' — because the postulation of unobserved deviation is untenable, [i.e.,] because of the absence of a <s>upādhi</s> that would serve as the door for the postulation of unobserved deviation — this is the meaning.

children.text: ato niyataḥ avyabhicārītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is invariable, non-deviating — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanūpādhyabhāve 'nupalabhyamānavyabhicārakalpanānavakāśaḥ, sa eva tūpādhyabhāvaḥ kutastya ityāśaṅkate---na ceti /
pariharati---avaśyamiti /
upādhirhi pramāṇapadavīmavatīrṇa eva vaktavyaḥ /
anyathā sarvaiḥ pramāṇaiḥ sarvadā sarvatra sarveṣāṃ jātyā kaścit anupalabhyamāno 'pi syādupādhiriti śaḍkā tadutpattāvapi brahmaṇāpyapanetumaśakyā /
nānāpramāṇagocarārthasākṣātkāravataḥ sarvajñasyāpi svabhāvata evānupalabhyaḥ kaścidartho bhavet, bhavecca sarvapramāṇāpoḍhamapi kadācidadvaitam, prakṛtipuruṣau vā, niḥsvabhāvatā vā jagataḥ, vedānāṃ vāprāmāṇyam /
tat kathaṃ caityavandanādāvapi bhikṣuḥ pravarteta? arthasandehāt pravṛttiriti cet? yatra pramāṇāni paribhūya śaḍkāpiśācī prasarati kutastatrārthasaṃbhāvanāpi? āstāṃ tāvat paralokapravṛttiḥ, ihalokapravṛttirapi na
children.translated_text: Now, in the absence of an <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition), there is no room for supposing an unperceived deviation; but whence comes the absence of the <s>upādhi</s>? — he raises the objection: "Nor..." He replies: "Necessarily..." For the <s>upādhi</s> must be stated only as having entered the path of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). Otherwise, there would always be the suspicion that among all things in all places for all people, something unperceived by all <s>pramāṇas</s> generically might be an <s>upādhi</s> — a suspicion that even <s>Brahmā</s> himself could not remove even at its arising. Even for an omniscient being who directly perceives objects within the range of various <s>pramāṇas</s>, something might by nature be imperceptible; and there might sometime be non-duality that is excluded by all <s>pramāṇas</s>, or <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, or the essencelessness of the world, or the invalidity of the Vedas. Then how would even a monk engage in worship at a <s>caitya</s> (Buddhist shrine) and the like? If [one says:] activity proceeds from doubt about the object — where the goblin of suspicion marches forth overriding all <s>pramāṇas</s>, how is there even the possibility of the object [being established]? Never mind activity regarding the other world — even activity regarding this world would not

children.text: syāt ityāha---antata iti //
children.translated_text: be possible — he says: "At least..."

children.text:
yadyapi viśiṣṭāhārānantaraṃ bhūyo bhūyaḥ puṣṭidhātusāmyādi daśyate, maraṇaṃ taṃ rogādyanantarameva, tathāpi āhāraviśeṣo maraṇasyaiva hetuḥ kadācid bhavet, kathamanyathānte tadantaramasyopalambhaḥ /
yattviyantaṃ kālaṃ na māritavān
children.translated_text: Although after specific food, nourishment, balance of bodily constituents, and the like are repeatedly observed, and death is observed only after disease and the like, nevertheless, specific food might at some point be the very cause of death — how else would there be perception of it just before death? As for the fact that it did not kill for this long —

children.text: tanmantrapratibaddhavahnivat, kenacit pratibaddhatvāt /
sa eva pratibandhakaḥ puṣṭyādiheturityapi saṃbhāvyeta /
children.translated_text: That very restraining factor might also be conceived as the cause of nourishment and the like.

children.text: rogādikameva ca puṣṭyādihetuḥ, tattu puṣṭyādikāle adṛśyatvādeva nāpalabhyate /
children.translated_text: And disease and the like themselves might be the cause of nourishment and the like; but at the time of nourishment and the like, they are not perceived simply because they are invisible.

children.text: na hi puṣṭyādikāraṇairdṛśyaireva bhavitavyamityapi kadācit syāt, yathā cāprāmāṇikopādhiśaḍkyā vyabhicāritvaśaṅkayā vā anumānanivṛttiḥ, tathāprāmāṇikānarthaśaṅkayaiva viśiṣṭāhārabhojanādinivṛttirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that the causes of nourishment and the like must be visible — this too might sometimes [be argued]. And just as through the suspicion of an unwarranted <s>upādhi</s> or the suspicion of deviation, there is the cessation of inference, so too through the very suspicion of unwarranted harm, there would be the cessation of eating specific food and the like — that is the meaning.

children.text: tasmādutprekṣitārthaniścayavat tacchaḍkāpi bandhyaiva, pramitasyaiva tu niścayavat śaḍkāpi samīhopayoginītyāha---tasmāditi //
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as the certainty of a fancied object is barren, so too the suspicion of it is barren; but the suspicion, like the certainty, of what is established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> alone is useful for activity — he says: "Therefore..."
that is like fire restrained by a mantra — because it was restrained by something.

children.text:
tadayaṃ saṃkṣepaḥ /
vyabhicāra eva pratibandhābhāvaḥ /
upādhereva vyabhicārāśaḍkā /
pramāṇaniścita evopādhitvena śaṅkanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is to be suspected as an <s>upādhi</s> must be ascertained by a <s>pramāṇa</s> alone.

children.text: sādhane sopādhiḥ sādhye nirūpādhireva upādhitvena niśceyaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is to be ascertained as an <s>upādhi</s> must be one that is present in the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) with an <s>upādhi</s>, and one that is without an <s>upādhi</s> in the thing to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).

children.text: ato 'nyaścānyathātveneti /
children.translated_text: "And anything else is [taken] as otherwise" — [this is the rule].

children.text: pramāṇaparidṛṣṭeṣveva kaścidupādhirbhaviṣyatītyata āha---prayatneneti //
children.translated_text: Now, some [<s>upādhi</s>] among the <s>pramāṇa</s>-discovered [entities] will indeed turn out to be an <s>upādhi</s> — therefore he says: "By effort..."
Here then is the summary: deviation itself is the absence of restriction. The suspicion of deviation pertains to the <s>upādhi</s> alone.

children.text:
ayaṃ prayatnārthaḥ /
pratyakṣopalabhyāstāvad yogyānupalabdhereva nirastāḥ /
pramāṇāntaraparidṛṣṭānāmapi vyāpakānāmupādhitve vahneḥ sārvatrikatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
avyāpakānamapi nityānām upādhitve bahneḥ sadānuvṛttiprasaṅgaḥ /
anityāstu trividhāḥ ubhayāvyabhicāriṇaḥ, ubhayavyabhicāriṇaḥ, anyatarāvyabhicāriṇaśceti /
tatra prathamadvitīyā upādhilakṣaṇābhāvādeva nopādhayaḥ /
anyatarāvyabhicāriṇaśca dvividhāḥ---dhūmamātrāvyabhicāriṇo vahnimātrāvyabhicāriṇaśceti /
pūrve lakṣaṇābhāvādeva nopādhayaḥ /
vahnimātrāvyabhicāriṇo 'pi dvividhāḥ, vyāpyamātrarūpā ubhayarūpāśceti /
pūrvavadeva pūrve /
ubhayarūpāstu sāmagrītaḥ /
nāpi pare vidyante /
children.translated_text: Nor do the latter exist.

children.text: sā ca na kvacidupādhiḥ, dhūmasya vahnineva tayāpi svabhāvasaṃbandhāt /
children.translated_text: And that [totality] is not an <s>upādhi</s> anywhere, because of the essential connection of smoke with fire and also with it [the totality].

children.text: vahnijananasāmagryāṃ vahnerapyantarbhāvācca /
children.translated_text: And because fire too is included within the fire-generating totality.

children.text: na ca kṛtakatvānuṣṇatvayoḥ saṃbandhe tejojātīyetaratvavadihāpi sādhyadharmajātīyetaratvamupādhiḥ, tasya pramāṇabādhaikamātraniyatatvāt //
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that, just as in the relation between being-made and being-non-hot, the <s>upādhi</s> is something other than the class of the <s>sādhya</s>-property [characterized as] being of that class — for that [type of <s>upādhi</s>] is restricted to being determinable only by the sublation of a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s>.

The meaning of "by effort" is this: those that are perceptible are ruled out by <s>yogyānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of what is fit to be apprehended) itself. And if those discovered by other <s>pramāṇas</s>, being pervaders, were <s>upādhis</s>, there would follow the consequence of fire being universal. And if permanent non-pervaders were <s>upādhis</s>, there would follow the consequence of fire being perpetually co-present [with them]. Non-permanent ones are of three kinds: those that do not deviate from either [<s>sādhana</s> or <s>sādhya</s>], those that deviate from both, and those that do not deviate from one of the two. Among these, the first two are not <s>upādhis</s> simply because the definition [of <s>upādhi</s>] is absent. Those that do not deviate from one are of two kinds: those that do not deviate from smoke only, and those that do not deviate from fire only. The former are not <s>upādhis</s> simply because the definition is absent. Those that do not deviate from fire only are also of two kinds: those that are merely of the form of the pervaded, and those of both forms. The former are [not <s>upādhis</s>] as before. But those of both forms [arise] from the totality [of conditions].

children.text: ata eva upādhimapaśyanto 'pi virodhipramāṇasadasadbhāvaniścayavyagratayā muhūrtam anumitau vilambāmahe /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, even when we do not perceive an <s>upādhi</s>, through being occupied with the ascertainment of the presence or absence of a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s>, we pause momentarily in inferring.

children.text: tadevaṃ sarvathopādhyanupalambhāt tadabhāvaniścayo yathā dhūmasaṃbandhe tathānyatrāpi draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, from the non-apprehension of an <s>upādhi</s> in every way, the ascertainment of its absence — as in the connection with smoke — should be seen similarly in other cases as well.

children.text: tarkaśca sarvaśaḍkānirākaraṇapaṭīyān vijayata iti //
children.translated_text: And <s>tarka</s> (reasoning), being most adept at removing all suspicions, prevails.

children.text:
nanu pramāṇasiddhe vastuni svabhāvo 'valambanam, na tu svabhāvāvalambanenaiva vastuvyavasthetyāśayavān pṛcchati---kena punariti /
prathamadarśanenaiva vahnidhūmayoḥ avyabhicāragrahaṇam, dvitīyādibhistu śaḍkāmātramapanīyata iti keṣāñcinmatamapanayanneva prakṛtaṃ prapañcayati---yadā tāvaditi /
atra caiṣa paramārthaḥ /
yo 'yamupādhimādāya yena saha saṃbadhyate sa nirūpādhyavasthāyāṃ tasyāgamako yathā vahnirdhūmasya /
sopādhyavasthāyāmapyupādheḥ, kevalasyaiva sāmarthye sa eva gamako na tūpahitaḥ /
yathāhārapariṇatibhedasyaiva gamakatve maitratanayatvam /
yatra tūpādhiḥ kevalo vyabhicārī tatra sopādhirapi gamaka eva /
children.translated_text: But where the <s>upādhi</s> by itself alone deviates, even the one accompanied by the <s>upādhi</s> is indeed an indicator.

children.text: yathārdrendhanavān vahnirdhūmasyeti /
children.translated_text: Just as fire possessed of wet fuel [is an indicator] of smoke.

children.text: tat kasya hetoḥ? viśiṣṭasya nirūpādhitvāditi bhūyodarśanamiti /
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because the qualified [entity] is free from <s>upādhi</s> — "therefore, repeated observation..."

children.text: tajjanitasaṃskārasahitamindriyamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the sense-organ together with the residual impression generated by that [repeated observation].

Now, for a thing established by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, its essential nature is the basis — but the thing is not established merely by relying on the essential nature. With this intention he asks: "By what then?" The view of some that already at the first observation itself the non-deviation between fire and smoke is grasped, and that by the second and subsequent [observations] only mere suspicion is removed — refuting this very [view], he elaborates on the topic at hand: "When, to begin with..." And the ultimate truth here is this: that which, together with the <s>upādhi</s>, is connected with [the <s>sādhya</s>], is — in the state free from the <s>upādhi</s> — an indicator of that [<s>sādhya</s>], just as fire is of smoke. Even in the state with the <s>upādhi</s>, when the <s>upādhi</s> has capacity by itself alone, that [entity] itself is the indicator — not the one accompanied [by the <s>upādhi</s>]. Just as, when the difference of transformation of food alone has the indicative capacity, being the son of <s>Maitra</s> [has no indicative role].

children.text:
agre caitadeva sphuṭīkṛtamityavirodhaḥ /
maṇibhedatattvavaditi /
yathā maṇiryairyairviśeṣaiḥ tattadvyavahāraviṣayo bhavati, dhārayituśca tattatphalabhedasaṃpādakaśconnīyate, te te sūkṣmā viśeṣāḥ parīkṣakairbhūyobhirdarśanairūnnīyante, tathātrāpīti /
tathā
children.translated_text: That this very point will be clarified later — therefore there is no contradiction. "As with the discrimination of gems" — just as a gem, through whatever particular features, becomes the subject of particular practical usages, and is inferred to produce particular fruit-differences for the wearer, those subtle particular features are discovered by expert examiners through repeated observations, so too here. For

children.text:
hi, prathamatastāvad bhūyodarśanaṃ kākatālīyanyāyavyudāsāya /
tataḥ sātatyordhvagatyādiviśeṣāvasāyāya /
tata upādhiśaḍkānirāśāya /
atra ca na vāraṃsakhyāniyame 'bhyupayogaḥ, mṛdumadhyādhimātrabuddhibhedena puṃsāṃ vicitraśaktitvāt /
na caivaṃ sati lakṣaṇaśāstravaiyarthyam, aniyatavāraviśiṣṭatattvasākṣātkārāvadhiyogābhyāsopadeśavadihāpi nirūpādhisaṃbandhabodhāvadhiniyamāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is there the purposelessness of the science of definitions in this case — because here too, just as in the instruction of practice of <s>yoga</s> whose limit is the direct realization of truth attained in an unrestricted number of times, there is a rule [governing] the limit of the understanding of unrestricted connection.

children.text: kāryakāraṇabhāvāvagame 'pyayameva mārgo, na tu pañcapratyakṣānupalambhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in ascertaining the causal relation, this very method [applies], and not the five perceptual non-apprehensions.

children.text: anyato 'nāgatasya tatrāsatastadanantaram upalambhe 'pi tato 'nyasmādanutpatteḥ bhāvamātreṇa niścetumaśakyatvāt ; kākatālīyanyāyenāpi saṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Because even when what was previously absent and non-existent there is perceived immediately after that [cause], since it might not have arisen from something other than that, it cannot be ascertained merely by existence; because accidental coincidence is also possible.

children.text: bhūyaḥpravṛttau tu yadi na vyabhicāropalambhaḥ, upādhyupalambho 'pi na syāt, dvayopagame tu tanniyataḥ saṃbandha iti //
children.translated_text: But when there is repeated engagement, if there is no perception of deviation, and no perception of an <s>upādhi</s> either, then when both are taken together, the connection is determined as invariable.

first, the repeated observation is for removing the accidental coincidence. Then, for the ascertainment of specific features such as continuity, upward motion, and the like. Then, for the dismissal of the suspicion of an <s>upādhi</s>. And here there is no restriction on the number of times, because of the varied capacities of people due to differences of dull, moderate, and sharp intelligence.

children.text:
syādetat /
dhūmādīnāṃ maitratanayatvādīnāṃ ca bhūyodarśanatvāviśeṣe 'pi kuto viśeṣādekasya gamakatvamaparasya natyata āha---na ceti /
yat tvatroktam, yathā hyanārdendhane vahnau na dhūma iti vahnestatsaṃbandhe tathāvidhamindhanamupādhiḥ /
tathā yadi maitrājjātasyāpi kasyacid vivakṣitāhārapariṇativiraheṇa śyāmatopālapsyata sa
children.translated_text: One might say: when there is no distinction in being repeatedly observed between smoke and the like on the one hand and being-the-son-of-<s>Maitra</s> and the like on the other, whence the distinction that one is an indicator and the other is not? — therefore he says: "Nor..." As for what was said here — just as when fire is without wet fuel there is no smoke, and thus such fuel is an <s>upādhi</s> in the connection of fire [with smoke], so too if, for someone born of <s>Maitra</s> as well, without the specific difference of food-transformation, dark complexion would be perceived — that

children.text: upādhirniraceṣyata //
children.translated_text: would be recognized as the <s>upādhi</s>.

children.text:
na tvetadasti /
tathā satyapi copādhivādo vyarthaḥ, vyabhicārādeva maitratanayasyāhetutvāditi /
children.translated_text: But this is not the case. And even if it were, the doctrine of <s>upādhi</s> would be useless — because being-the-son-of-<s>Maitra</s> would be a non-reason due to deviation alone.

children.text: tadidamanavadhāritopādhilakṣaṇasya sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānaṃ na kiñcideva //
children.translated_text: So this counter-argument of one who has not properly grasped the definition of <s>upādhi</s>, [made] through agreement and difference, amounts to nothing at all.

children.text:
tathā hi nopahitasya niścita eva sādhyavyabhicāraḥ, upādherlakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ nāma? sādhanāvyāpakatve sati sādhyavyāpakatvam /
tacca sādhyābhimatadhūmaśyāmatve prati vyāpakatvem ārdrendhanānnapānapariṇatibhedayoraviśiṣṭam, aviśiṣṭaṃ ca sādhanābhimatadahanamaitratanayatve prati tayoravyāpakatvam /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ, vahnerdhūmenevārdrendhanenāpi sākṣādeva vinābhāva upalabhyate /
maitratanayasya tu śyāmatvenevānnapānapariṇāmenāpyupādherevonnīyata iti /
nanu vajre lohalekhyatvaṃ prati pārthivatvahetoḥ ka upādhiḥ? praśithilāvayavatvam /
tarhi tannivṛttau paveriva sphaṭikādāvapi lohalekhyatvanivṛttiprasaṅgaḥ /
na khalu nibiḍāvayavatvena ubhayoḥ kaścid viśeṣaḥ /
na mṛdādibhyo nibiḍāvayavatve 'pi sphaṭikasya praśithilāvayavatvādeva /
na hyadbhyo medinī nibiḍeti na praśithilāvayavā /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ /
yathā yathā śaithilyāpakarṣastathā tathā lekhituḥ prayatnaprakarṣaḥ /
yadi tu śaithilyamaprayojakaṃ tadā mṛtkāṣṭhapāṣāṇādiṣu prayatnaprakarṣo 'pi viphalaḥ, pārthivatvasya sarvatrāviśeṣāt /
sphaṭike kathameṣā pratipattiriti cet? lohalekhyatvādeva /
lohalekhyatvapraśithilāvayavatvayoḥ samavyāptikatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the co-extensiveness of scratchability-by-iron and looseness-of-parts.

children.text: ata evānayorekatarapravṛttinivṛttyorevānyatarapravṛttinivṛttī, na tu pārthivatvapravṛttinivṛttyoreva lohalekhyatvapravṛttinivṛttī, vajre 'darśanāt ; jalādau darśanācca /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the occurrence and non-occurrence of one of the two [follow] from the occurrence and non-occurrence of the other — but the occurrence and non-occurrence of scratchability-by-iron do not follow from the occurrence and non-occurrence of earthiness, since it is not observed in diamond; and since it is observed in water and the like [which are not earthy].

children.text: vahnāvanuṣṇatvasādhanasya tu kṛtakatvasya tajjātīyetaratvalakṣaṇamupādhiḥ, sa ca bādhaikaniyataviṣaya iti nātiprasaṅga ityuktam /
children.translated_text: But for the reason "being-made" in [proving] "being-non-hot" of fire, the <s>upādhi</s> is defined as being-other-than-the-class-of-that [<s>sādhya</s>-property]; and that is restricted to being determinable only by sublation — therefore there is no over-extension. This has been stated.

children.text: tadetatsarvaṃ hṛdi nidhāyāha---ityādaya iti //
children.translated_text: Keeping all this in mind, he says: "And so forth..."

For here is the point: the deviation of the qualified [mark] from the <s>sādhya</s> is not at all certain. What then is the definition of <s>upādhi</s>? Pervading the <s>sādhya</s> while not pervading the <s>sādhana</s>. And that — the capacity to pervade the <s>sādhya</s>, namely smoke and dark complexion — is not distinguished between wet fuel and difference of food-and-drink transformation; and undistinguished is the non-pervasion by the two of the <s>sādhana</s>, namely fire and being-the-son-of-<s>Maitra</s>. But this distinction [exists]: the non-co-existence (<s>vinābhāva</s>) [of smoke] with wet fuel too — just as with fire — is perceived directly. But for being-the-son-of-<s>Maitra</s>, the non-co-existence with food-and-drink transformation — just as with dark complexion — is inferred even of the <s>upādhi</s> itself. Now, with respect to the reason "being-earthy" for "being-scratchable-by-iron" in a diamond, what is the <s>upādhi</s>? Looseness of parts. Then, when that is absent, as in crystal and the like [which are also earthy], there would follow the consequence of the absence of being-scratchable-by-iron — just as with a cloth. There is surely no distinction between the two in terms of compactness of parts. [The reply is:] no — even though crystal has compact parts, it has looseness of parts compared to clay and the like. For it is not the case that earth is not loose-parted compared to water, just because it is compact. But this distinction [exists]: as looseness decreases, the effort of the scratcher increases. But if looseness were non-productive, then even in clay, wood, stone, and the like, greater effort would be fruitless, since earthiness is the same everywhere. [If one asks:] how is this apprehension in crystal? — by its very scratchability by iron.

children.text: yadyapi dvitīyaliṅgadarśanasya smṛtyā saha vinaśyadavasthasyaiva parāmarśajanakatvaṃ kvacit, tathāpi yatra dṛṣṭamātra eva vahninivṛttau nivṛtto dhūmaḥ kālāntare jijñāsāvaśāt parāmṛśyate, tatra dvayorapi liṅgadarśanayoratītatvamityāśayavatoktam---yadyapītyādi //
children.translated_text: Although the second observation of the mark, in its perishing state together with memory, is in some cases the generator of reflective consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>), nevertheless, where smoke — observed only at [the time of] seeing [the first time] — ceases when fire ceases, and is later reflectively considered due to the desire to know, there both observations of the mark are past. With this intention it was said: "Although..." and so forth.

children.text:
yena ca parāmarśo neṣyate tena vākyasya caturtho 'vayava apanayo 'pi neṣitavyaḥ /
pakṣadharmatāpratipādanena tasyopayogaḥ parārthānumāne /
svārthānumāne tu sā dvitīyaliṅga darśanādevāvagateti kiṃ parāmarśeneti cet---na, pakṣadharmatā hi vyāptyā saha pratisaṃhitānumānopayoginī, tādṛśī copanayena pradarśyate, na tu dvitīyaliṅgadarśanena /
children.translated_text: And one who does not accept <s>parāmarśa</s> (reflective consideration) must also not accept the removal of the fourth member of the sentence [i.e. <s>upanaya</s>, application]. For the use of <s>upanaya</s> in inference-for-others is the establishment of the property-of-the-thesis. But in inference-for-oneself, that [property-of-the-thesis] is already understood from the second observation of the mark itself — so what is the use of <s>parāmarśa</s>? — if one objects: no, for the property-of-the-thesis, combined with the pervasion, is useful for inference when so conjoined; and such [combination] is shown by <s>upanaya</s>, not by the second observation of the mark.

children.text: tasya tu vyāptyanusandhānarahitaṃ pakṣadharmatāmātrameva gocaraḥ /
