na ca tadanumānopayogi /
children.translated_text: And that [bare property-of-the-thesis] is not useful for inference.

children.text: tasmādupanayārtho na dvitīyaliṅgadarśanaviṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the purpose of <s>upanaya</s> is not the object of the second observation of the mark.

children.text: tataḥ svārthānumāne yadyasti tasyopayogaḥ, nūnaṃ parāmarśo 'pi tṛtīyaḥ svīkartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hence, if there is a use for that [<s>upanaya</s>] in inference-for-oneself, then surely <s>parāmarśa</s> too, as a third [element], must be accepted.

children.text: nāsti cet, parārthānumāne 'pi liṅgaparāmarśaikārthaḥ upanayo 'pi nādaraṇīyaḥ, tulyaviṣayatvādityāśayavān saṃkalayyānayoḥ samānaviṣayatvamāha---saṃbandheti //
children.translated_text: If there is not [such a use], then even in inference-for-others, <s>upanaya</s>, being equivalent in meaning to the reflective consideration of the mark, should not be attended to, since it has the same content — with this intention, correlating the two, he states their having the same content: "The connection..."
For the domain of that [second observation] is merely the property-of-the-thesis without the connection of pervasion.

children.text: nanu vyāpārānubandhitayā viṣayatvam, viṣayatve ca vyāpārānubandha iti parasparāśrayatvam /
children.translated_text: Now, [one might object:] object-hood by virtue of connection with operation, and connection with operation by virtue of object-hood — this is mutual dependence.

children.text: atha vyāpārānubandhitayaiva viṣayatvam? tathāpyasaṃbaddhatvāviśeṣāt kathaṃ tasyaiva vyāpārānubandhitetyāśaḍkya pariharati--na cātiprasaṅga iti /
children.translated_text: Or is it that object-hood is simply by virtue of connection with operation? Even so, since there is no distinction in being unconnected, how is the connection with operation of that alone [and not others]? — raising this doubt, he replies: "Nor is there over-extension..."

children.text: na dhūmajñānasyāgniḥ svatantrasya vyāpāraviṣayo yenāsaṃbaddhatvāviśeṣādatiprasaṅgaḥ syāt, kiṃ tu jñeyaviśeṣaṇasya, tasya ca jñāyamānasya dhūmasyāgninā saha niyāmakaḥ svabhāvasaṃbandha eva, ato nātiprasaṅgaḥ ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Fire is not the object of the operation of the cognition of smoke independently, such that there would be an undesirable over-extension due to non-distinction from being unconnected. Rather, it is [the object] of the qualifier of the knowable. And for the smoke that is being known, the invariable connection with fire is the natural connection (<s>svabhāvasaṃbandha</s>) itself. Therefore there is no over-extension — this is the meaning.

children.text:
pūrvaṃ lakṣyapadārthapraśnāvasare anumīyate 'neneti kāraṇārtha ityuttaraṃ dattam /
idānīmanumitiḥ kasyāñcidavasthāyāmanumānaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavena veti vijñāsāpraśne bhāvaḥ karaṇaṃ vetyuttaram /
ato na virodho 'śataḥ, paunarūktyaṃ vā /
ataḥ ṭīkākṛd api vyāpāratvenāpramāṇyaṃ pūrvapakṣayitvā phalāntarahetutvena prāmāṇyaṃ samarthayati sma /
iha yadyapi vijñānapramāṇayoranyatarādhikāreṇa saṃskāranirṇayayorvyudāsaḥ, vijñānādhikāre hi tatpūrvakam anubhavakāraṇamanumānamiti sūtrasaṃbandhaḥ /
na caivaṃbhūtau saṃskāranirṇayaviśeṣau, tayoranubhavaṃ pratyahetutvāt /
pramāṇādhikāra'pi phalataḥ sa evārthaḥ, tatpūrvakaṃ pramākaraṇamanumānamiti sūtrasaṃbandhāt /
tathāpi vivakṣābhedāt vikalpenobhayamubhayatra saṃbhantsyata iti vivakṣitvā ekaikakaniṣṭhatayaikaikaṃ darśitamiti tathaiva vyākhyātavān /
vastutastu ubhayamubhayatra saṃbaddham iti nigarvaḥ /
vipakṣāvṛttiriti vārttike bahuvrīhisamāsasthito viśeṣaṇatayā vyatireko niṣkṛṣya svapradhānatayā tatpuruṣapadena pradarśito vipakṣāvṛttirvyatireka iti /
ato na vārttike hetusāmānādhikaraṇyavirodhaḥ /
vyatirekābhāvaṃ vyatirekanirūpaṇābhāvam ityarthaḥ /
ihāvastuno vidhiniṣedhavyavahāraviṣayatvaṃ laukikasamīhānurodhād vā,
children.translated_text: Previously, on the occasion of the question about the referent of the defined term, the answer was given in the sense of cause: 'that by which one infers.' Now, on the occasion of the question whether an inference (<s>anumiti</s>) at a certain stage can be a <s>pramāṇa</s> or not, the answer is: it is either the positive entity or the instrument. Therefore there is no real contradiction, nor redundancy. Therefore, even the <s>ṭīkā</s>-author, having presented the prior objection that it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> by virtue of being an operation, justified its being a <s>pramāṇa</s> by virtue of being a cause of another result. Here, although, by adopting one or the other of the two subjects — cognition and <s>pramāṇa</s> — latent impression and determination are excluded (for under the subject of cognition, the <s>sūtra</s>-connection is: 'inference is the means of experience preceded by that'; and latent impression and determination of such a kind are not [such means], since they are not causes of experience; and under the subject of <s>pramāṇa</s> too, the meaning is the same in terms of result, from the <s>sūtra</s>-connection: 'inference is the instrument of valid cognition preceded by that'), nevertheless, intending that by an alternative, both can be connected with both due to difference of purport, he showed each one as being the minimum in each, and thus explained it accordingly. But in reality, both are connected with both — this is [stated] without arrogance. The negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) in the <s>vārttika</s> 'absence in the counter-positive' is extracted as a qualifier in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, and displayed as a principal by means of the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> word: 'absence in the counter-positive is negative concomitance.' Therefore there is no contradiction with the co-referentiality of the reason in the <s>vārttika</s>. 'Absence of negative concomitance' means absence of the formulation of negative concomitance — this is the meaning. Here, the being-an-object-of-positive-and-negative-practical-usage of a non-entity is either in accordance with common worldly desire,

children.text: śuktirajatavadrajjusarpavacca pramāṇānurodhād, vā gandhaṃ prati pṛthivīvadudakavad vā, vacanamātrānurodhād vā pradhānavat śaśaviṣāṇavacca, mūḍhapraśnānurodhād vā dharmāntaraṃ prati pūrvavadeva svavacanavirodhabhayād veti //
children.translated_text: or in accordance with a <s>pramāṇa</s>, as nacre-silver or rope-snake; or as earth is to odor and water [is not], in accordance with a mere statement, as <s>pradhāna</s> or as a hare's horn; or in accordance with the question of one confused, as before with regard to another property — out of fear of self-contradiction.

children.text: tatra prathamastāvadavastunyasaṃbhavī, laukikapravṛttinivṛttyorvastumātraviṣayatvāt dvitīyādiṣveva ca paramparayā praviśatīti na
children.translated_text: Among these, the first is impossible with regard to a non-entity, since worldly activity and inactivity pertain only to real things, and it enters into the second and subsequent [alternatives] only indirectly — therefore it is not

children.text: pṛthak nirākriyate /
children.translated_text: separately refuted.

children.text: dvitīyanirākaraṇāya prāmāṇikaniṣedhavyavahārarītimāha---sadbhyāmiti /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of refuting the second, he states the method of negation-usage based on valid cognition: 'By the two existing...'

children.text: yadi tadviviktetarasvabhāvo 'bhāvo yadi comayathātiriktasvabhāvaḥ, ubhayathāpi niṣedhyaniṣedhādhikaraṇābhyāmeva nirūpyate, na tvekena satā niṣedhyena niṣedhādhikaraṇena vetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Whether absence is of a nature distinct from that [counter-positive], or whether it is of a nature not exceeding the locus — in either case, it is determined only by the two: the thing to be negated and the locus of negation; not by a single existing thing, either the thing to be negated or the locus of negation — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu sata eva kutaścit pramāṇapratītānnivartsyatītyata āha---pakṣādanyasyeti /
tadanenāsatyadhikaraṇe nivṛttinirūpaṇaṃ pratiṣiddham, nivṛttau tu mūkataivociteti hṛdayam /
nivṛttireva pratiṣiddheti /
bhrāntastu codayati---na nivartate cediti /
nirūpaṇam ādāyaiva pariharati---yasyeti /
yatra khalu bhāvaḥ sarvathaiva na nirūpitaḥ tadadhikaraṇatayā
children.translated_text: Now, an existing thing alone will be negated on the basis of some <s>pramāṇa</s> — to this he says: 'Of something other than the thesis...' By this, the determination of cessation with respect to a non-existent locus is prohibited; and regarding cessation [itself], silence alone is appropriate — this is the essence. 'Cessation itself is prohibited.' But the confused one objects: 'If it does not cease...' Taking the determination [itself], he replies: 'Of that which...' Where a positive entity has not been determined in any way whatsoever, it is seen that its absence is determined with respect to that [thing] as a locus, the entity having been perceived elsewhere — as with the horn perceived in a cow, [the absence of which is determined] in a hare.

children.text: tasyānyatropalabdhasyābhāvo nirūpyata iti dṛṣṭam, yathā gavi dṛṣṭasya śruṅgasya śaśe /
children.translated_text: — this is observed.

children.text: yatra tu śṛḍgābhāvo 'pi gaganakamalādau nirūpayituṃ na śakyate, tatra śṛṅgameva nirūpyata ityalaukikamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But where even the absence of a horn cannot be determined, as in a sky-lotus and the like — there the horn itself is determined — and that is non-ordinary — this is the meaning.

children.text: punarbhrāntaḥ śaṅkate--tat kimidānīmiti /
children.translated_text: The confused one again raises a doubt: 'Then what now...'

children.text: svavacanavirodhabhayamāśaṅkate--nanu ceti //
children.translated_text: He raises the fear of self-contradiction: 'But surely...'

children.text: taduktaṃ jñānaśriyā
children.translated_text: This was stated by <s>Jñānaśrī</s>:

children.text: dharmasya kasyacidavastuni mānasiddhā
children.translated_text: 'Is there or is there not a <s>pramāṇa</s>-established',

children.text: bādhāvidhivyavahṛtiḥ kimihāsti no vā /
children.translated_text: 'practical usage of sublation or injunction regarding some property in a non-entity?'

children.text: kkāpyasti cet kathamiyanti na ḍhūṣaṇāni
children.translated_text: 'If there is somewhere, how do these faults not accrue?'

children.text: nāstyeva cet svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'And if there is not at all, the proof of self-contradiction follows.'

children.text: iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text:
yadyapi svavacanavirodhabhiyāpi sarvathāvicārāsahor'thaḥ svīkartuṃ na śakyate, vacanād vicāro garīyāniti nyāyāt, anyathā vikalpaśabdau na vastugocarāviti svavacanavirodhādeva parihartavyam /
tathā hi svalakṣaṇasyāsādhāraṇyenāśakyasamayagocaratayā, śabdasya ca samayādhīnapravṛttikatayā vikalpasya ca tadekaviṣayatayā
children.translated_text: Although, even out of fear of self-contradiction, a matter that is entirely beyond examination cannot be accepted — since examination is weightier than mere statement, by the principle [that reason prevails over mere assertion] — otherwise, the objection that conceptual construction and words do not pertain to real things must be met by the fear of self-contradiction itself. For since the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is, by its uniqueness, unable to be the object of convention, and since words operate dependently on convention, and since conceptual construction has that alone as its object,

children.text: na tayorvastugocaratvamiti vicāre,
children.translated_text: neither of them pertains to real things — upon examination,

children.text: śabdasya kācidapi vastuni mānasiddhā
children.translated_text: 'Is there or is there not a <s>pramāṇa</s>-established'

children.text: bādhāvidhivyavahṛtiḥ kimāhāsti no vā /
children.translated_text: 'practical usage of sublation or injunction of a word with regard to anything real?'

children.text: astyeva cet kathamiyanti na dūṣaṇāni
children.translated_text: 'If there is, how do these faults not accrue?'

children.text: nāstyeva cet svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'And if there is not at all, the proof of self-contradiction follows.'

children.text: iti tulyā vibhīṣikā /
children.translated_text: — the same specter applies equally.

children.text: tathāpi tattvaṃ nirūpayan pariharati---na vai tattvata iti //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, investigating the truth, he replies: 'Not indeed in reality...'

children.text:
nanu yadi naikataraniṣedho vidhirvā tat kimubhayavidhiḥ niṣedho vā? tathā sati atitarā durghaṭamāpadyetetyata āha---no khalviti /
nanu sarvavyavahārābhājanamityapi niṣedhavyavahārabhājanatvenaiva nirvahet, anyathā punarapi svavacanapratirodha ityata āha---upayoge veti /
svavacanapratirodhabhayāddhi tadā niṣedhavyavahāragocaratvasvīkāraḥ syād
children.translated_text: Now, if there is neither negation nor assertion of either one, then is there assertion or negation of both? If so, an even greater impossibility would follow — to this he says: 'Not indeed...' Now, 'being unfit for all practical usage' would itself be resolved by being fit for the practical usage of negation — otherwise there would again be self-contradiction — to this he says: 'Or in the case of being useful...' For the acceptance that it is an object of the practical usage of negation would occur out of fear of self-contradiction,

children.text:
yadi tathā sati bhayaṃ nivarteta /
na tvetadasti /
no khalu sakalavyavahārābhājanaṃ ca tanniṣedhavyavahārabhājanaṃ ceti vacanaṃ
children.translated_text: if fear were to be removed thereby. But this is not the case. For the statement 'it is unfit for all practical usage and is fit for the practical usage of negation'

children.text:
parasparamavirodhi /
vidhivyavahāramātrābhiprāyeṇābhājanatvavyavahāre kuto virodha iti cet? hanta ! sakalavidhiniṣedhavyavahārābhājanatvena kiñcid vyavahniyate na vā? ubhayathāpi svavacanavirodhaḥ /
ubhayathāpyavastunaiva tena bhavitavyam, vastunaḥ sarvavyavahāravirahānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: In either case, that must be a non-entity, since a real entity's being devoid of all practical usage is untenable.

children.text: neti pakṣe sakalavidhiniṣedhavyavahārābhājanamityanenaiva vyavahāreṇa virodhāt, avyavahṛtasya niṣeddhumaśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: On the view that 'no [designation is made],' there is contradiction with this very usage: 'unfit for all assertion-and-negation-usage' — since what has not been designated cannot be negated.

children.text: vyavahniyata iti pakṣe tu viṣayasvarūpaparyālocanenaiva virodhāt /
children.translated_text: On the view that it is designated, there is contradiction by the very consideration of the nature of the subject.

children.text: na hi sarvavyavahārābhājanaṃ ca vyavahniyate ceti ca //
children.translated_text: For 'it is unfit for all practical usage and yet it is designated' — this is [self-contradictory].

is not mutually non-contradictory. If one says there is no contradiction in the usage of 'unfitness' with the intention of mere assertion-usage? Alas! Is something being designated by 'unfitness for all assertion-and-negation-usage' or not? In either case, there is self-contradiction.

children.text:
api ca yadyavastuno niṣedhavyavahāragocaratvam, vidhivyavahāraviṣayatāpi kiṃ na syāt? pramāṇābhāvasyobhayatrāpi tulyatvāt /
bandhyāsutasyāvaktṛtve 'cetanatvādikameva pramāṇam, vaktṛtve tu na kiñciditi---cet---na, tatrāpi sutatvasya vidyamānatvāt, na hi bandhyāyāḥ suto na sutaḥ /
tathā sati svavacanavirodhāt /
vacanamātrametanna tu paramārthataḥ suta evāsāviti cet? acetanasyāpyevaṃrūpatvāt, cetanādanyat
children.translated_text: Moreover, if a non-entity is the object of the practical usage of negation, why should it not also be the object of the practical usage of assertion? — since the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is equal in both cases. If one says: regarding the son of a barren woman, non-speakingness is established by the <s>pramāṇa</s> of being non-conscious and the like, but for speakingness there is no [<s>pramāṇa</s>] — no, because even there son-ness is present. For the son of a barren woman is not a non-son. For if so, there would be self-contradiction. If one says: 'This is merely a verbal expression, but not ultimately a son' — then even being non-conscious has the same form: what is other than consciousness

children.text:
svabhāvāntaram evācetanamityucyate /
caitanyanivṛttimātrameva vivakṣitamiha, tacca saṃbhavatyeveti cet---na tatrāpyasutatvanivṛttimātrasyaiva vivakṣitatvāt /
children.translated_text: is simply called 'non-conscious' as another essential nature. If one says: 'What is intended here is merely the cessation of consciousness, and that is quite possible' — no, because even there merely the cessation of non-son-ness is what is intended.

children.text: asutatvanivṛttimātrasya svarūpataḥ kṛtijñaptyorasāmarthye samarthamarthāntaramavaseyam anantarbhāvya kuto hetutvamiti
children.translated_text: If one says: 'How can the mere cessation of non-son-ness, being incapable of action and cognition in its own nature, be a reason, without subsuming it under a distinct meaningful entity?' —

children.text:
cet---na, acaitanye 'pyasya nyāyasya samānatvāt /
vyāvṛttirūpamapi ca tadeva gamakaṃ yadatasmādeva, yathā śiṃśapātvam /
bandhyāsutastvasutādiva ghaṭādeḥ, sutādapi devadattādeḥ vyāvartate, ato na heturiti cet? nanvacaitanyamapyasyaivaṃ rūpameva /
na hi bandhyāsutaścetanādiva devadattāderacetanādapi kāṣṭhāderna vyāvartate /
ato na heturiti /
vaktṛtvaṃ vastvekaniyato dharmaḥ sa kathamavastuni sādhyo virodhāditi cet? sa punarayaṃ virodhaḥ kutaḥ pramāṇāt siddhaḥ, kiṃ vaktṛtvaviviktasyāvastuno niyamenopalambhāt, āhosvit vastuviviktasya vaktṛtvasyānupālambhāditi? na tāvadavastu kenacit pramāṇenopalambhagocaraḥ /
tathātve vā nāvastu /
nāpyuttaraḥ samānatvāt /
na hyavaktṛtvamapi vastuviviktaṃ kasyacit pramāṇasya viṣayaḥ /
tadviviktavikalpanamātraṃ tāvadastīti cet?
children.translated_text: no, because the same reasoning applies equally to non-consciousness. And even what has the form of exclusion is indicative of precisely that from which [it excludes], just as rosewood-ness [indicates tree-ness]. If one says: 'But the son of a barren woman is excluded from both non-sons like pots and from sons like <s>Devadatta</s>, and therefore is not a reason' — well, non-consciousness too has precisely this form. For the son of a barren woman is excluded not only from conscious beings like <s>Devadatta</s> but also from non-conscious things like logs. Therefore it is not a reason. If one says: 'Speakingness is a property invariably restricted to real entities — how can it be proved of a non-entity, because of contradiction?' — then on what <s>pramāṇa</s> is this contradiction established? Is it from the invariable perception of non-entities as devoid of speakingness, or from the non-perception of speakingness devoid of a real entity? To begin with, a non-entity is not an object of perception by any <s>pramāṇa</s>. Or, if it were, it would not be a non-entity. Nor is the latter [alternative possible], for the same reason. For non-speakingness too, devoid of a real entity, is not the object of any <s>pramāṇa</s>. If one says: 'At least the mere conceptualization of it devoid [of a real entity] exists' —

children.text: tatsaṃsṛṣṭivikalpane 'pi ko vārāyitā?
children.translated_text: who would prevent even the conceptualization of its combination [with speakingness]?

children.text: nanu vaktṛtvaṃ vacanaṃ prati kartṛtvam, tat kathamavastuni, tasya sāmārthyavirahalakṣaṇatvāditi cet? athāvaktṛtvamapi kathaṃ tatra, tasya vacanetarakartṛtvalakṣaṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: Now, speakingness is the agency with respect to speech — how can that apply to a non-entity, since it is characterized by the absence of capacity? — if so, how does non-speakingness too apply there, since it is characterized by agency with respect to something other than speech?

children.text: sarvasāmarthyavirahe vacanasāmarthyaviraho na viruddha iti cet? atha sarvasāmarthyaviraho bandhyāsutasya kutaḥ pramāṇāt siddhaḥ? avastutvādeveti cet? nanvetadapi katham? sarvasāmarthyavirahādeveti cet? soyaṃ kevalairvacanairitastato nirdhanādhamarṇika iva sādhūn bhrāmayan parasparāśrayadoṣamapi na paśyati //
children.translated_text: If one says: 'In the absence of all capacity, the absence of the capacity for speech is not contradictory' — then from what <s>pramāṇa</s> is the absence of all capacity in the son of a barren woman established? If one says: 'From its very being a non-entity' — then how is even that [being a non-entity] established? If one says: 'From the very absence of all capacity' — this person, wandering about confusing honest people like a penniless debtor driven hither and thither by mere words alone, does not even see the fault of mutual dependence.

children.text:
kramayaugapadyavirahāditi cet na, tadvirahasiddhāvapi pramāṇānuyogasyānuvṛtteḥ /
sutatve ca parāmṛṣyamāṇe tadavinābhūtasakalavaktṛtvādidharmaprasaktau kutaḥ kramayaugapadyavirahasādhanasyāvakāśaḥ? kutastarāṃ cāvastusādhanasya? kutastamāṃ cāvaktṛtvādisādhanānām? tataśca pramāṇameva sīmā vyavahāraniyamasya, tadatikrame tvaniyama evetyanenābhiprāyeṇedamuktam /
upayoge vā niṣedhavyavahāropayoge vā /
na nirūpākhyo na vidhivyavahārāviṣayaḥ /
yasmin kiñcinniṣidhyate pramāṇena, tasmin kiñcid vidhīra'pīti niyamādityarthaḥ /
tatra praṣṭurūttare vaktavye na
children.translated_text: If one says: 'From the absence of succession and simultaneity' — no, because even when the absence of those is established, the demand for a <s>pramāṇa</s> continues. And when son-ness is being considered, since all properties inseparable from it — such as speakingness and the like — would follow, where is there scope for proving the absence of succession and simultaneity? Much less for proving non-entityness. And even much less for proving non-speakingness and the like. Therefore, the <s>pramāṇa</s> alone is the boundary of the restriction of practical usage; and when that is transgressed, there is simply no restriction — with this intention this was stated: 'Or when there is use' — or when there is use in the practical usage of negation. 'Not without a name' means 'not outside the scope of the practical usage of assertion.' The meaning is: there is a rule that in whatever something is negated by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, in that very thing something is also asserted. In that context, when one is obliged to give an answer to the questioner, it is not proper to say something contradictory or meaningless — with this intention he says: 'Of what then...'

children.text: viruddhamanarthakaṃ vā vaktumucitamityāśayavānāha---kasatarhīti /
children.translated_text: — this is the meaning.

children.text: uttaram---atheti /
children.translated_text: The answer: 'Now...'

children.text: anuttaraviṣaye ahṛdayairyadevottarīkriyate, tadeva viruddhamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Whatever the heartless ones answer regarding a subject about which no answer is possible — that itself is contradictory — this is the meaning.

children.text:
na ca kevalamatrottaradaḥ, praṣṭāpyahṛdaya eva /
na hyapratīte devadattādau sa kiṃ gaurakṛṣṇo veti vaiyātyaṃ vinā praśnaḥ /
tatrāpi yadyeko 'pratītaparamārthaviṣaya evottaraṃ dadāti na gaura iti, aparo 'pi kiṃ na dadyād gaura iti? na caivaṃ sati kācidarthasiddhiḥ, pramāṇābhāvavirodhayorūbhayatrāpi tulyatvāt /
tadidamuktam---ahṛdayavācāmiti /
nanvapratīte vyahārābhāva iti yuktam, kūrmaromādayastu pratīyanta eva /
children.translated_text: Now, regarding what is unestablished, the absence of practical usage is proper. But tortoise-hair and the like are indeed cognized.

children.text: na hyete vikalpāḥ kañcidarthabhedamanullikhanta evotpadyante /
children.translated_text: For these conceptualizations do not arise without tracing some real distinction.

children.text: na ca pramāṇāspadameva vyavahārāspadamityasti niyama ityata āha---na cātyanteti /
children.translated_text: And there is no rule that only what is the basis of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is the basis of practical usage — to this he says: 'And not absolutely...'

children.text: yadyapi sarvathāpratīte vyavahārābhāva iti vadato bauddhasyāpi svavacanavirodha eva, tathāpyayaṃ virodhaḥ prāgevodbhāvitaprāya ityenamupekṣya śaḍkāmātraṃ samarthitam //
children.translated_text: Although even for the Buddhist who says 'with regard to what is entirely uncognized, there is no practical usage,' there is self-contradiction, nevertheless, since this contradiction has been mostly brought out already, he sets it aside and develops only the doubt.

And not only is the answerer [heartless] here — the questioner too is heartless. For regarding an unestablished <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, there is no question 'Is he fair or dark?' except as a prank. Even there, if one person gives an answer about something whose ultimate nature is unestablished — 'He is not fair' — why would another not give the answer 'He is fair'? And if so, there is no determination of the matter, since the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> and contradiction are equal in both cases. This is what was stated: 'The words of the heartless...'

children.text: tathā hi śaśaviṣāṇamiti jñānamanyathākhyātiḥ syādasatkhyātirvā? na tāvadādyaste rocate, tathā sati kiñcidāropyaṃ kiñcidāropaviṣaya iti syāt /
tathā cāropaviṣayastatraivāstyāropaṇīyaṃ tvanyatreti jitaṃ naiyāyikaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, the locus of superimposition exists there itself, while what is to be superimposed exists elsewhere — and the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> have won.

children.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ, kāraṇānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor the second [option], because of the impossibility of a cause.

children.text: indriyasya jñānajanane svaviṣayādhipatyenaiva vyāpārāt, liṅgaśabdābhāsayorapyanyathākhyātijanakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Since the sense-organ operates in generating cognition solely through its dominion over its own object, and since even the inferential mark, the word, and false appearances generate cognition of the <s>anyathākhyāti</s> (misapprehension) type.

children.text: apahastitasvārthayoścāsatkhyātijanakatve śaśaviṣāṇaśabdāt kūrmaromādivikalpānāmapyutpattiprasaṅgaḥ, niyāmakābhāvāt //
children.translated_text: And if, when [the word and mark] are deprived of their own meaning, they generate <s>asatkhyāti</s> (cognition of the non-existent), then there would follow the consequence that from the word 'hare's horn,' conceptions of tortoise-hair and the like too would arise — since there would be no restricting factor.

For would the cognition 'hare's horn' be <s>anyathākhyāti</s> (error as mistaken identity) or <s>asatkhyāti</s> (error as cognition of the non-existent)? To begin with, the first is not agreeable to you, for in that case there would be something superimposed and something that is the locus of superimposition.

children.text:
sa hi saḍketo vā syāt, śabdasvābhāvyaṃ vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, saḍketaviṣayāpratīternirākṛtatvāt /
ata eva pratīteritaretarāśrayatvam /
padasaḍketabalena tu pravṛttau svārthāparityāgāt /
tathā cānanvitāḥ padārthā evānvitatayā parisphurantīti viparītakhyātirevāvartate /
svārthaparityāge tu punarapyaniyamaḥ, asāmayikārthapratyāyanāt /
śabdasvābhāvyāt tu niyame vyutpannavadavyutpannasyapi tathāvidhavikalpodayaprasaṅgaḥ /
vāsanāviśeṣāditi cet? athāsadullekhinaḥ pratyayasya vāsanaiva kāraṇamuta vāsanāpi? na tāvadādyaḥ, śaśaviṣāṇādipratyayānāṃ
children.translated_text: For that [restricting factor] would be either convention or the inherent nature of the word. Not the first, to begin with, since it has been refuted that there is cognition of the object of convention [for non-existent referents]. For this very reason, there is mutual dependence of the cognitions. But when activity proceeds by the force of word-convention, the word's own meaning is not abandoned. And thus, the word-meanings, which are unconnected [to each other], appear as if connected — and so <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (misapprehension of the reversed) alone recurs. But if the word's own meaning is abandoned, then again there is non-restriction, since non-conventional meanings would be conveyed. And if restriction is by the inherent nature of the word, then there would follow the consequence that even the uninstructed, like the instructed, would have such conceptions. If one says 'due to a specific latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>)' — then is the latent impression alone the cause of the cognition that suggests the non-existent, or is there something beyond the latent impression too? Not the first, to begin with, since there would follow the consequence that cognitions of hare's horn and the like would

children.text:
sadātanatvaprasaḍgāt /
kadācid vāsanāyāḥ, prabodhāt kadāciditi cet---na, prabodho 'pi sahakāryantaraṃ vā, atiśayaparamparāparipāko vā? ādye vāsanaiveti pakṣānupapatti /
dvitīyo 'pi yadārthāntarapratyāsattestadā pūrvavat /
svasantatimātrādhīnatve tu bāhyavādavyāghātaḥ, nīlādibuddhīnāmapi vāsanāparipākādeva utpādāt /
vāsanāpīti pakṣe tu
children.translated_text: exist at all times. If one says 'sometimes of the latent impression, due to awakening, sometimes not' — no: is the awakening a further auxiliary, or is it the ripening of the succession of intensifications? In the first case, the thesis 'the latent impression alone' is untenable. In the second case too, when [the ripening is] due to proximity of another thing, it is as before. But if it depends solely on its own continuum, there is a violation of the externalist position, since cognitions of blue and the like too would arise from the ripening of latent impressions alone. And on the view that [the cause is] the latent impression too,

children.text: tadanyo 'pi kaścaddheturvaktavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: some other cause beyond that must also be stated.

children.text: sa vicāryamāṇaḥ pūrvaṃ nyāyaṃ nātivartata iti //
children.translated_text: And when examined, that does not go beyond the previous reasoning.

children.text:
na ca śaśaviṣāṇādiśabdānāmasadarthaiḥ saha sambandhāvagamo 'pi /
tathā hi parabuddhīnāmanullekhāt tadviṣayasyāpyanullekha eva /
na cārthakriyāviśeṣo 'pyasti yato viṣayaviśeṣamunnīya tatra saḍketo gṛhyatām /
na ca
children.translated_text: Nor is there even an apprehension of the relation of words like 'hare's horn' with non-existent referents. For since the cognitions of others are not manifested [to us], the object of those [cognitions] too is simply not manifested. Nor is there any specific purposive activity from which, by inferring a specific object, the convention regarding it could be grasped. And not

children.text:
saḍketayitureva vacanāt tadavagamaḥ /
tadviṣayāṇāṃ vacanānāṃ sarveṣāmevāpratītaviṣayatvenāgṛhītasamayatayā apratipādakatvāt /
na ca śaśaviṣāṇaśabdamuccārayataḥ kaścidabhiprāyo vṛttaḥ, tadviṣayo 'sya vācya iti sugrahaḥ samaya iti vācyam /
na hyevamākāraḥ samayagrahaḥ /
gāṃ badhānetyukte apratītaśabdārthasya abhiprāyamātrapratītau samayagrahaprasaḍgāt /
na ca viśeṣāntaravinākṛtaḥ kalpanāmātraviṣayo 'sya vācya iti sāmpratam, ghaṭakūrmaromādīnāpi tadarthatvaprasaḍgāt /
na ca sarve pratipattāraḥ svavāsanayā asadarthaśabdasambandhapratipattibhāja iti sāmpratam /
parasparavārtānabhijñatayā aparārthatvaprasaḍgāt /
na hi svayaṅkṛtaṃ saḍketamagrāhayitvā paro vyavahārayituṃ śakyate /
na ca vyavahāropadeśāvantareṇa grāhayitumapi /
na ca gāṃ badhānetivat śaśaviṣāṇāpadārthe vṛddhavyavahāraḥ /
na cāyamasāvaśca itivadupadeśaḥ /
na ca yathā gaustathā gavaya iti vadupalakṣaṇātideśaḥ /
children.translated_text: And there is no extension through indication, like 'as a cow, so a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox).'

children.text: na ceha prabhinnakamalodare madhūni madhukaraḥ pibatītivat prasiddhapadasāmānādhikaraṇyam /
children.translated_text: And there is no co-referentiality with a well-known word, like 'in a broken open lotus, a bee drinks the honey.'

children.text: tadamūḥ śaśaviṣāṇādikalpanā nāsatkhyātirūpāḥ, tathātve kāraṇābhāvāt bhūkasvapnavadasāvyavahārikatvaprasaḍgācca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, these conceptions of hare's horn and the like are not of the <s>asatkhyāti</s> (cognition-of-the-non-existent) type — because if so, there would be absence of a cause, and because of the consequence of being non-empirical like the sky-flower or a dream.

children.text: tasmādanyathākhyātirūpā eveti naitadanurodhenāpyavastuno niṣedhavyavahāragocaratvamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, they are of the <s>anyathākhyāti</s> (misapprehension) type alone — and hence, even for accommodating this [theory], the non-existent is not an object of the practical usage of negation — this is the meaning.

is the apprehension of that [convention] from the statement of the one who established the convention alone — since all statements about such objects, having objects whose cognition has not been established, are non-communicative due to their conventions not being grasped. Nor should one say: the one who utters the word 'hare's horn' has some intention, and [therefore] 'what he means to denote is [such-and-such]' — [thus] the convention is easily grasped. For the grasping of convention is not of such a form — since, when one says 'bind the cow,' there would follow the consequence that one whose word-meaning has not been cognized would grasp the convention merely from apprehending the intention. Nor is it proper that [the convention is] 'his denotation is an object of mere imagination, unaccompanied by any further particular' — since there would follow the consequence that pot, tortoise-hair, and the like too would have that meaning. Nor is it proper that all apprehenders, by their own latent impressions, are recipients of the cognition of the relation of non-existent-referent words — since, due to not knowing each other's affairs, the consequence would be that [such words] would denote something else. For without making another aware of one's self-made convention, the other cannot engage in practical usage. And one cannot make [another] aware without the medium of practical usage and instruction. And there is no elder's practical usage regarding the non-entity 'hare's horn' as [there is with] 'bind the cow.' And there is no instruction like 'this is that' [for non-existent referents].

children.text:
bhavatu tathāpi nāsau siddhyupālambhayogītyāha---kalpitagocaraśceti /
tathā hi ko 'yaṃ vyatireko nāma? yadyato vyatiricyate tasya tatrābhāvo vā, tadabhāvasvabhāvatvaṃ vā? tatra na tāvat kramayaugapadyayoḥ śaśaviṣāṇe 'bhāvaḥ pramāṇagocaraḥ, vṛkṣarahitabhūbhṛtkaṭakavat kramayaugapadyarahitasya śaśaviṣāṇasya pramāṇāviṣayatvāt /
nāpi kramayaugapadyābhāvarūpatvaṃ śaśaviṣāṇasya prāmāṇikam, ghaṭābhāvavat śaśaviṣāṇasya pramāṇeṇa anupalambhāt /
children.translated_text: Even so, that [cognition] is not capable of being used for establishing or refuting — he says: 'and having a constructed object.' For what is this 'exclusion' (<s>vyatireka</s>)? Is it the absence of what is excluded in that from which it is excluded, or the nature of being the absence of that? Among these, to begin with, the absence in hare's horn of succession and simultaneity is not an object of <s>pramāṇa</s> — since hare's horn, being devoid of succession and simultaneity like a mountain-plateau devoid of trees, is not an object of <s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor is the nature of hare's horn as [consisting in] absence of succession-and-simultaneity established by <s>pramāṇa</s> — since hare's horn is not apprehended by <s>pramāṇa</s>, unlike the absence of a pot.

children.text:
ghaṭābhāvo 'pi na pramāṇagocara iti cet--na, tasya tadviviktetarasvabhāvasyāpi pramāṇata eva siddheḥ /
asiddhau vā tatrāpyavyavahāra eva /
ghaṭastāvat svābhāvavirahasvabhāvaḥ pramāṇasiddhaḥ tādrūpyeṇa kadācidapyanupalambhāt /
etāvataiva tadabhāvo 'pi ghaṭavirahasvabhāvaḥ siddha iti cet---na, ghaṭābhāvasya tadvirahasvabhāvatvānabhyupagamāt /
na cānyasya svabhāve pramāṇagocare tadanyo 'pi siddhaḥ syāt, atiprasaḍgāt /
evaṃbhūtāveva ghaṭatadabhāvau yadekasya paricchittirevāparasya vyavasthitiriti cet---na, ghaṭavad ghaṭābhāvasyāpi prāmāṇikatvānabhyupagame svabhāvavādānabhyupagamāt /
pramāṇasiddhe hi vastuni svabhāvavādālambanam /
na tu svabhāvavādālambanenaiva vastuparicchittiriti hi bhavatāmeva tatra tatra jayadundubhiḥ /
yaduktaṃ vārtikālaḍkāre,
children.translated_text: If one says 'the absence of a pot too is not an object of <s>pramāṇa</s>' — no, since that [absence], having the nature of what is distinct from that [pot], is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> alone. Or, if not established, then even there would be no practical usage. The pot, to begin with, having the nature of the absence of its own [non-being], is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> — since it is never apprehended as having such a form [as non-being]. If one says 'by this much, the absence [of the pot] too, having the nature of the absence of the pot, is established' — no, since we do not accept that the absence of the pot has the nature of the absence of that [pot]. And it is not the case that when the nature of one thing is an object of <s>pramāṇa</s>, another thing too is [thereby] established — because of over-extension. If one says 'the pot and its absence are such that the determination of one is itself the determination of the other' — no, because if we do not accept the <s>pramāṇa</s>-status of the absence of the pot, just as [we accept it for] the pot, then the doctrine of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvavāda</s>) is not accepted. For the doctrine of intrinsic nature rests on a real entity established by <s>pramāṇa</s>. But the determination of an entity is not made merely by relying on the doctrine of intrinsic nature — for that is precisely your victory-drum everywhere. As stated in the <s>Vārttikālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: yaktiñcidātmābhimataṃ vidhāya
children.translated_text: Having postulated whatever entity one wishes,

children.text: nirūttarastatra kṛtaḥ padeṇa /
children.translated_text: and having been silenced there by a word,

children.text: vastusvabhāvairiti vācayamitthaṃ
children.translated_text: [one says] 'by the intrinsic nature of things' — in this way,

children.text: tadottaraṃ syād vijayī samastaḥ //
children.translated_text: the reply to that would be: everyone is victorious!

children.text: tat kimidānīṃ svābhāvavirahasvabhāvo ghaṭaḥ pramāṇānaiva siddhaḥ? tava dṛṣṭyā evametat /
ghaṭo hi yādṛktādṛksvabhāvastāvat pramāṇapathamavatīrṇaḥ tasya yadi paramārthataḥ abhāvo 'pi kaścit syāt, paramārthataḥ so 'pi tadvirahasvabhāva iti tathaiva pramāṇāveditaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: For the pot, having entered the domain of <s>pramāṇa</s> with whatever nature it has — if, in ultimate reality, it had some absence too, that too, in ultimate reality, having the nature of the absence of that [pot], would have been made known by <s>pramāṇa</s> in just that way.

children.text: na caitadabhyupagamyate bhavatā /
children.translated_text: But this is not accepted by you.

children.text: tasmād ghaṭavat tadabhāvasyāpi prāmāṇikatvenaivānayoḥ parasparavirahalakṣaṇavyatirekasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as for the pot, so too for its absence — the establishment of their mutual exclusion, characterized by mutual absence, is by the <s>pramāṇa</s>-status of both.

children.text: aprāmāṇikatve vā anayorapi na tathābhāva iti śaśaviṣāṇādiṣvapīyameva gatiḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, in the case of both being non-established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, neither would have such a nature — and so for hare's horn and the like too, this very course [applies].
Then is the pot, whose nature is the absence of its own absence, not established by <s>pramāṇa</s> at all? From your point of view, it is indeed so.

children.text:
nanu kālpanikarūpasaṃpattirevāstvanumānāṅgamityata āha---tasyāḥ sarvatra sulabhatvādita /
dahanavattvādisādhane prameyatvādau śabdānityatvādisādhane cākṣuṣatvādau nityatvādisādhane kṛtakatvādāvityarthaḥ /
nanu pakṣasapakṣavipakṣāstāvad vastvavastubhedena dvirūpāḥ /
tatra ye kalpanopanītāḥ, tatra kālpanikā eva
children.translated_text: Now, let the fulfillment of the merely constructed form be a component of inference — to this he says: 'because of its being easily obtainable everywhere.' In proving the possession of fire and the like, [it is obtained] with respect to 'being knowable' and the like; in proving the impermanence of sound and the like, with respect to 'being visually perceptible' and the like; in proving permanence and the like, with respect to 'being produced' and the like — this is the meaning. Now, the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>), and the dissimilar case (<s>vipakṣa</s>), being of two kinds — real and unreal — among these, those that are brought about by construction, for them the merely constructed

children.text:
pakṣadharmatvānvayavyatirekāḥ /
pramāṇopanīteṣu tu prāmāṇikā eveti vibhāgaḥ /
tadiha kālpanikānniragneryadyapi prameyatvādervyāvṛttiḥ kālpanikī siddhā, tathāpi prāmāṇikāt jalahnadādeḥ prāmāṇikyevaiṣitavyā, sā ca na siddheti kutastasya hetutvam? evaṃ prāmāṇikāt śabde 'pi pakṣīkṛte prāmāṇika eva hetusadbhāvo /
vaktavyaḥ na cāsau cākṣuṣatvasyāstīti so 'pi kathaṃ hetuḥ? evaṃ kṛtakatvasyāpi vastvekaniyatasya dharmasya vāstava evānvayo vaktavyaḥ /
vastuno vipakṣācca vāstava eva vyatireko vaktavyaḥ /
na ca tasya tau staḥ /
tat kathamasāvapi heturiti /
? pralapitametat /
na hi niyāmakamantareṇa saṃpadaṃ prati kalpanā tvarate, vipadaṃ prati tu vilambata iti śakyaṃ vaktum /
tathā ca niragnikamapi kūrmaroma sadhūmamiti kalpanāmātreṇa vipakṣavṛttitvād dhūmo nāgni gamayet /
vāstavyāṃ rūpasaṃpattau kimamena kālpanikadoṣeṇeti cet? tarhi vāstavyāmasaṃpattau kiṃ kālpanikyā tayeti samānam /
virodhāvirodhau viśeṣa iti cet? kuta etat? ubhayorekatra vastvavastutvādanyatrāvastuvaditi cet? tat kiṃ kālpaniko 'pi
children.translated_text: property-of-the-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>), positive concomitance, and negative concomitance [are established]. But for those brought about by <s>pramāṇa</s>, [these must be] established by <s>pramāṇa</s> alone — this is the division. Thus here, although the exclusion of 'being knowable' and the like from fireless constructed [entities] is established as merely constructed, nevertheless, from a <s>pramāṇa</s>-established [entity] like a lake, the [exclusion] must be sought as <s>pramāṇa</s>-established — and that is not established. So how can that be a reason? Likewise, even when sound is proposed as the subject, only the <s>pramāṇa</s>-established presence of the reason must be stated. And since 'being visually perceptible' does not have such [presence], how is that too a reason? Likewise, for 'being produced' too — whose positive concomitance, being a property restricted to real entities, must be stated as real. And its negative concomitance from the dissimilar case of a real [entity] must be stated as real. And it does not have these two. So how is that also a reason? This is mere babble. For in the absence of a restricting factor, one cannot say that construction hastens toward fulfillment but delays toward non-fulfillment. And thus, merely by constructing that even the fireless tortoise-hair is smoky, smoke would not indicate fire — because of occurring in the contrary case merely by construction. If one says 'of what use is this constructive fault when the real form-fulfillment [is established]?' — then equally, of what use is the constructive [fulfillment] when the real non-fulfillment [is established]? If one says 'opposition and non-opposition are the distinction' — whence is this? If one says 'because of both [real and unreal] being present in one [place] for the entity, while for the non-entity it is like the non-entity' — then is the constructed

children.text: dhūmo vastubhūto yena kūrmaromṇastena saha virodhaḥ syāt?
children.translated_text: smoke too an entity, such that it could be in opposition with tortoise-hair?

children.text: kvacid vastubhūta iti cet? nirdhūmatvamapi kvacid vastubhūtamiti tenāpi virodha eva /
children.translated_text: If one says 'in some cases it is an entity' — then the absence of smoke too is in some cases an entity — so there is opposition even from that.

children.text: tasmād yathā kālpanikī vipattirna doṣāya, tathā kālpanikī saṃpattirapi na guṇāyeti tasyāśca sarvatra sulabhatvāditi ṭīkārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as constructed non-fulfillment is not a fault, so too constructed fulfillment is not a virtue — and since that [constructed fulfillment] is easily obtainable everywhere — this is the meaning of the <s>ṭīkā</s>.

children.text: etaccābhyupetyoktam---vastutastu na na nirūpākhyaṃ kasyacid vyavahārasya bhājanamiti //
children.translated_text: And this was stated by way of accepting [the opponent's position]: in reality, however, what is devoid of any form whatsoever is simply not the object of any practical usage.

children.text: nanu yadyāvayorakuśalatayā svavacanavirodhaḥ, atha praṣṭuḥ kimuttaraṃ vaktavyamityavaśiṣṭamupasaṃharan pariharati---tasmāditi /
children.translated_text: Now, whether it is our incapacity that leads to self-contradiction, or what answer should be given to the questioner — concluding what remains, he resolves: 'therefore.'

children.text: yatra vacane sarvathaiva virodhasatatrāvacanameva śreya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: where the statement is contradictory in every way, silence is better than speaking.

children.text: etena mūkatāhetuvikalpāḥ parihṛtā boddhavyā iti //
children.translated_text: By this, the various alternatives for the reason of becoming mute are to be understood as having been resolved.

children.text:
nanvekarūpamavikalamidaṃ kathaṃ gamakam? gamakatve vā vyatirekavikalavad rūpāntaravikalamapi tathā kiṃ na syādaviśeṣādityāśaḍkyāha---na caitāvateti /
rūpāntaravaikalyavanna vyatirekavaikalyamavinābhāvakṣatimāvahatītyarthaḥ /
evaṃ tarhi satyapi vipakṣe vyatireko na paryeṣaṇīya ityata āha---vipakṣasambhave tviti /
children.translated_text: If so, then even when the dissimilar case exists, negative concomitance need not be sought — to this he says: 'but when the dissimilar case is possible.'

children.text: vipakṣe sati tatra vṛttiśaḍkā, tatastannivṛttyarthaṃ tadupayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the dissimilar case exists, the suspicion of occurrence there [arises] — therefore, for removing that [suspicion], the use of that [negative concomitance] is needed.

children.text: vipakṣābhāve tu śaḍkaiva nāsti, yathoktaṃ prāk /
children.translated_text: But in the absence of the dissimilar case, there is simply no suspicion — as was stated before.

children.text: na hi tāyābhyavaharaṇe 'pyasamarthasya mumūrṣoḥ śaṣkulībhakṣaṇaṃ śaṅkate cetana ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a sensible person does not suspect that one who is dying and unable even to swallow gruel is eating sweetmeats — this is the meaning.

Now, how is this, which is of a single form and without deficiency, an indicator? And if it is an indicator, why would it not equally be [deficient] in another form, like [it is undeficient] in the exclusion — since there is no distinction? — anticipating this, he says: 'and not merely this much.' The meaning is: unlike the deficiency of another form, the deficiency of negative concomitance does not impair the invariable concomitance.

children.text: svamate tviti /
children.translated_text: 'But on our own view' —

children.text: asya tu kālpaniko 'pi vipakṣaḥ pareṇābhidhātuṃ na śakyate, abhidhāne sapakṣatvāpatteḥ asapakṣatve 'nabhidhānaprasaḍgāt, tataścābhidheyatve sādhye yaḥ kaściddheturūpādīyate, tasya kiṃ vipakṣe vṛttiravṛttirveti praśne anenottarakovidena kiṃ vaktavyam? mūkībhūya tiṣṭhāsostu na kaścit pratimalla iti svayamevollapitamanena /
children.translated_text: On this [view], even a constructed dissimilar case cannot be stated by the opponent — since, if stated, the consequence would be that it becomes a similar case; and if it is not a similar case, the consequence would be that it cannot be stated. And so, whatever reason is adduced in proving the stateability [of the dissimilar case], regarding that reason — the question whether it occurs in the dissimilar case or not — what should be said by this [opponent] who is skilled in replies? Having become mute, let him stand — there is no rival at all — this was itself babbled by him.

children.text: na tvevaṃbhūto 'hetureva doṣābhāvāt, arūcimātrasya sarvatra sulabhatvāditi bhāgāsiddhinirākāraṇāya vyāptyeti vadataḥ //
children.translated_text: But such [a reason] is not simply a non-reason, because there is no fault — since mere distaste is easily obtainable everywhere. This is said by one who, to refute the non-establishment of a part, speaks of 'pervasion.'

children.text:
pūrvavadityatiśāyane matupo vidhānam /
atiśayaśca vyāptirevetyāśayaḥ /
tadidam uktaṃ ṭīkākṛtā---asti gandhavatvasya sādhyaṃ na tu vyāptyeti /
nanu sādhyasajātīye śeṣaśabdasya na kācid vṛttirityata āha---sādhyasyopayuktatvāditi /
paunarūktyabhramamapākaroti---padāni vibhajyeti /
na mantarbhāvya vyākhyāne sāmānyatodṛṣṭapadamevaṃ yojanīyam, uktaviśeṣarahitatvena vipakṣa eva sāmānya ityucyate /
tatrādṛṣṭam /
saptamyāstasiḥ /
yogyadarśananivṛttyā ca dṛśyanivṛttirvivakṣitā, tena vipakṣe asadityarthaḥ /
ataḥ siddhavat
children.translated_text: 'More than before' — the <s>matup</s> suffix is employed in the sense of surpassing. And the surpassing is in pervasion itself — this is the intention. This is what was stated by the <s>ṭīkā</s>-author: 'the possession of odor — the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) exists, but not the pervasion.' Now, the word 'remainder' has no application in what is of the same type as the <s>sādhya</s> — to this he says: 'because the <s>sādhya</s> is useful.' He removes the confusion of redundancy: 'dividing the words.' [The word 'general'] within the subsumption interpretation is not to be construed thus with the term '<s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s>' — since, being devoid of the stated specification, the universal is said to be precisely in the dissimilar case. Therein, 'unseen.' The <s>-tas</s> suffix is the ablative of the locative. And by the cessation of seeing what is fit [to be seen], the cessation of the visible is intended — hence the meaning is: 'non-existent in the dissimilar case.' Therefore, as if established,

children.text: trirūpasaṃpattimabhyupetya rūpadvayasaṃpade cakāramavatārayati---tathā ceti //
children.translated_text: having accepted the fulfillment of the three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>), he introduces the <s>ca</s>-particle for the fulfillment of two characteristics: 'and thus.'

children.text: tadevaṃ tatpūrvakamityanena liṅgaparāmarśo 'numānamiti lakṣaṇārthe vyākhyāte, atha kiṃ liṅkam, katividhaṃ veti jijñāsāyāṃ trividhamityavacchedena vyākhyāya, kiṃ lakṣaṇam iti jijñāsāyāṃ pūrvavadityādyekavākyatayā vyākhyānena parāmarśaviṣayaḥ saṃjñito vibhakto lakṣitaśca /
viṣayaviṣayiṇorabhedavivakṣayā ca sāmānādhikaraṇyamiti mantavyam /
children.translated_text: And the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) [of mark and inference] should be understood as intended through the non-distinction between the object and its possessor.

children.text: evam anyānyapīti /
children.translated_text: "Likewise others too" —

children.text: tadyathā, manojñamattakāśinīsaṃdarśanena saṃsārirāgānumānam, śatrudarśanena krodhānumānam, viṣayabhogena sukhānumānam, rogādinā duḥkhānumānam, avikalendriyasya yogyaviṣayāvadhānena jñānānumānam, śraddhāvatāṃ yathāvidhi yāgādyanuṣṭhānena dharmānumānam, niṣiddhācaraṇenādharmānumānam, paṭvabhyāsādarapratyayaiḥ saṃskārānumānam, mithyāpratyayena bhaviṣyatsaṃsārapravāhānumānamityadhyātmam /
children.translated_text: For example: inference of the worldly being's attachment (<s>rāga</s>) from seeing a beautiful intoxicated woman; inference of anger from seeing an enemy; inference of pleasure from the enjoyment of objects; inference of pain from disease and the like; inference of cognition from the attentive observation of a fit object by one with unimpaired sense-organs; inference of <s>dharma</s> (merit) from the proper performance of sacrifice and the like by the faithful; inference of <s>adharma</s> (demerit) from prohibited conduct; inference of residual impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) from the evidences of acuity, practice, and care; inference of the future stream of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) from false cognition — these are in the internal domain.

children.text: bāhye ca jvalantaṃ tṛṇarāśimupalabhya bhaviṣyadbhasmānumānam, tathāvidhavṛṣṭyā bhaviṣyannadīpūrādijñānam, prakārāntarāvagatena vāyunā tvarāvatā vṛkṣādisaṃkṣobhānumānamityādi neyam //
children.translated_text: And in the external domain: inference of future ashes from perceiving a burning pile of straw; knowledge of future river-floods from rainfall of such a kind; inference of the shaking of trees and the like from wind apprehended through another means and moving swiftly — and so on. This should be extended.

Thus, when the definition in its meaning has been explained by "preceded by that" — namely, that reflective consideration of the mark (<s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s>) is inference — then, in the inquiry "What is the mark, and how many kinds are there?", having explained with the distinction "threefold," and in the inquiry "What is the definition?", having explained as a single syntactic unit with "as before" and so forth — the object of reflective consideration has been named, classified, and defined.

children.text:
duravabodhamiti /
sāmānyatodṛṣṭasvarūpasyaivāvivecanādityarthaḥ /
udāharaṇadvāreṇa tadvivecanaṃ
children.translated_text: "Difficult to understand" — the meaning is: because the nature of <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (inference from general observation) has not been discriminated. Its discrimination through examples

children.text:
bhaviṣyatītyāha---śeṣavadudāharaṇānatargataṃ ceti /
śeṣavallakṣaṇayoge 'pi tadudāharaṇāntaravailakṣaṇyenedameva sāmānyatodṛṣṭapadārthe bhaviṣyatītyata āhā---na caitāvateti /
na tāvadaśvakarṇādiśabdavadayaṃ sūryavrajyānumāne vartate, anyatrāpi vṛddhaprayogāt /
nāpi sūtrakārasyaiva paribhāṣeyam, niṣprayojanatvāt /
tasmādudāharaṇavailakṣaṇyamātravivakṣayedamucyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is said with the intention of indicating merely the distinctness of examples.

children.text: tathā cātiprasaṅga ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus there would follow over-extension — that is the meaning.

children.text: tasmād bhāṣyakāravyākhyānaviruddhodāharaṇamātrākhyānamarocayamānaḥ sāmānyatodṛṣṭapadaṃ vyākhyāyānyathodāharaṇamāheti yojanā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, not finding it agreeable to simply relate examples that are inconsistent with the explanation of the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>, the interpretation is: he explains the term <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> [differently] and then states the examples otherwise.

children.text: kṣayavṛddhipratyayāviṣayatve satīti spaṣṭārtham, prāḍmukhopalabhyatve parivṛttya tatpratyayaviṣayatvāditi paryālocanayaivāvināśasya prāptatvāt //
children.translated_text: "When it is not the object of the cognition of waxing and waning" — this is clear in meaning; because non-destruction has already been obtained through the very consideration that when [the sun] is perceived going in the forward direction, upon turning back, it becomes the object of that [waxing-waning] cognition.

will follow — he says: "And included within the remainder and examples." Even when the definition of <s>śeṣavat</s> (inference from the remainder) applies, by the distinctness of its examples from the latter, this alone will serve as the referent of the term <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> — therefore he says: "Nor is this much..." To begin with, this [term] does not apply only to the inference of the sun's motion, like the word <s>aśvakarṇa</s> ("horse-ear," a proper name); because learned people use it elsewhere too. Nor is this a restrictive convention of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> alone, since it would be purposeless.

children.text:
na hyupalabdhavināśe upalabdhaṃ pratyabhijñāyate bhrāntāvapyanupalabdhamevopalabdhatayeti /
prāḍmukhopalabhyatve cetyasya ṭīkayā sphoritasya prāḍmukhopalabdhasya prāḍmukhenānupalambhe satītyarthaḥ /
narāntarasya tatsamānadeśasthasyeti mantavyam /
anyathā mārtaṇḍamaṇḍalasyāpi lokāntaravartipuruṣāpekṣayā prāḍmukhopalabhyatā durvāretyasiddhaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ syāt /
tadetat narapadena sūcitam /
children.translated_text: For when something whose destruction has been perceived is recognized [later], even in an erroneous [recognition], what was not perceived is taken as having been perceived. And the meaning of "when perceived going in the forward direction" as elucidated by the <s>ṭīkā</s> is: when what was perceived going forward is not perceived going forward. It should be understood [that this refers to] another person located in the same place. Otherwise, the forward-perception of the solar disk too, relative to a person in another world, would be inevitable — and the qualifier would be unestablished. This is indicated by the word "person."

children.text: tadabhimukhadeśasaṃbandhāditi śiṣyahitatayā vyabhicāraupayikapādaviharaṇajñāpanāya /
children.translated_text: "Because of connection with a place facing it" — for the benefit of the student, to indicate the knowledge of the pattern of stepping that is useful for [demonstrating] deviation.

children.text: na hi yathātathā pādavihāraṇamātramasya hetoḥ kṣatimāvahatīti /
children.translated_text: For not just any stepping-pattern is sufficient to damage this reason.

children.text: satyavināśe iti ca draṣṭavyam sati draṣṭavyatva iti veti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The completion is: "And when there is real destruction" should be understood as: "when there is [the property of] being-worthy-of-being-seen."

children.text:
iha yadyapi diśaḥ pratyakṣatve sādhye 'ḍgulyā nirdeśo vyadhikaraṇaḥ, tarūnagarādiṣu evāḍgulyā vyapadeśāt /
diśaḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ tvaḍgulīvyapadeśasya na tadadhikaraṇatāsādhanamanyathāsiddhatvāt /
tathāpi yasyāṃ diśi ete taravaḥ sā prācīti tarvādibhedena apyaḍgulyā vyapadeśo 'stīti na vyadhikaraṇatvamāhatyābhidhātuṃ śakyata ityanenābhiprāyeṇa anyathāsiddhimeva vārtikārthamāha---anyathāsiddhatayeti /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat, calantīṃ patākāmupalabhyāyaṃ vāyurvātīti aḍagulīnirdeśasyācākṣuṣe vāyāvapi gatatvena vyabhicārasya api saṃbhavāt /
rūpeṇa sparśānumānamityādāvādigrahaṇena rasena rūpānumānam, gandhena rasānumānamityādi /
vṛkṣādarśane sandehe vā na śiśapādarśana niścayo vā tato 'navasaraparāhatamevānumānam /
vṛkṣaśabdaprayogalakṣaṇavyavahārānumānaṃ tu na svārtham, aviditasamayenāśakyatvāt ; viditasamayasya ca vyarthatvāt /
paro 'pi yadi vyutpanno, yadi viditaśabdapravṛttinimittaḥ,
children.translated_text: Here, although when the perceptibility of directions is to be proved, pointing with a finger is [in a] different substratum, since pointing with a finger [occurs] precisely with respect to trees, cities, and the like — nevertheless, the co-referentiality of the direction with the finger-pointing is not established as having that as its substratum, since it is otherwise-explained. Even so, since there is finger-pointing based on the distinction of trees and the like too — "the direction in which these trees are, that is the east" — over-extension cannot be definitively stated. With this intention he states the <s>vārttika</s>-meaning as being precisely the otherwise-establishment: "As otherwise-established..." And this is illustrative — because even from perceiving a moving flag and [saying] "this wind is blowing," since deviation is possible even in the finger-pointing with respect to the non-visual wind through the inference of motion. In "the inference of touch from form" and so forth, the word "and so forth" [includes]: inference of form from taste, inference of taste from smell, and the like. When a tree is not seen or when there is doubt, there is no seeing or certainty of <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood) — therefore inference is excluded by the absence of scope. But the inference of practical usage characterized by the employment of the word "tree" is not for oneself, since it is impossible for one who does not know the convention; and for one who knows the convention, it is purposeless. If the other [person] too is educated, and knows the grounds of word-usage,

children.text:
tadā svayameva vyavaharet /
viparītastu śiśapātvamapi na pratīyāt /
avyutpannaścet, samayamagrāhayitvā vyavahārayitumaśakya eva /
na cāyaṃ samayagrahaprakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And this is not the method of teaching convention.

children.text: tathā sati śiśapātvādayaṃ vṛkṣo vyavahartavyaḥ iti śiśapātvameva vṛkṣaśabdapravṛttinimittamākalayet /
children.translated_text: If it were so, then from "because of being rosewood, this tree is to be used practically," one would understand rosewood-ness itself as the ground of the usage of the word "tree."

children.text: na ca śiśapātvādayaṃ vṛkṣaśabdapravṛttinimittavāniti vākyārthaḥ, viditatannimittaṃ prati vyarthatvāt ; viparītaṃ pratyapraddhiviśeṣaṇatvaprasaḍgāt, sāmānyopakrame samayagrahānupapatteḥ ; puruṣecchāmātrādhīnatvācaca samayasya pakṣadharmatayā niyantumaśakyatvāt ; aviditasamayaṃ prati cānvayopakramasyāyuktatvādityata āha---śruteneti /
children.translated_text: And the sentence-meaning is not "this thing, because of being rosewood, possesses the ground of usage of the word tree" — because it would be purposeless for one who already knows that ground; because there would follow the consequence of the qualifier being unestablished for one of the opposite [type], since it is impossible to learn a convention by the method of starting with the particular; because the convention, being dependent on the mere will of the person, cannot be restricted as a property of the thesis; and because the method of starting with the positive concomitance is improper for one who does not know the convention — therefore he says: "By what is heard..."

children.text: tadanena ye cānye sādhyasamānakālāḥ, te sarve sāmānyatodṛṣṭānumānasaṃgrāhyatvena upalakṣitā iti //
children.translated_text: By this, all [inferences] whose results are simultaneous with what is to be proved are indicated as being classifiable under <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference.

then he would engage in practice by himself. But one of the opposite [disposition] would not cognize even rosewood-ness. And if he is uneducated, he simply cannot be made to engage in practice without being taught the convention.

children.text:
svamatena vyākhyānāntaram, na tu tātparyāntaramityarthaḥ, pūrvaṃ sādhyaṃ tadyasya vyāptyetyanenaikatātparyatvāt /
anenaivābhiprāyeṇāha---atrāpi yathāsaṃbhavamiti /
nānantarbhāvacakāranirapekṣate cāsmin vyākhyāne pūrvasmād viśeṣaḥ /
sāmānyena kāryaṃ vā kāraṇaṃ vā anubhayātmakaṃ vā avinābhāvitayā dṛṣṭaṃ niścitaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭameva ca yojanā /
children.translated_text: A different explanation according to his own view, but not a different import — that is the meaning; because both have a single import, as [shown] previously by "the <s>sādhya</s> — that whose pervasion" [statement]. With this very intention he says: "Here too, as applicable." The distinction from the earlier [explanation] in this interpretation is not dependent on the "and" particle of inclusion. The construal is: what is seen — i.e. determined — to have inseparable concomitance as generally a cause, or an effect, or neither, is <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s>.

children.text: tadidamuktam---asandigdhatāmāheti /
children.translated_text: This is what was stated: "He states the non-doubtfulness."

children.text: tatra tatpūrvakamiti /
children.translated_text: "In that case, preceded by that" —

children.text: svarūpavipratipattinivṛttiḥ svalakṣaṇasāmarthyena nyūnādhikasaṃkhyatvāśaḍkānivṛttiḥ prathamaṃ tātparyam /
children.translated_text: The first import is: the removal of disagreement about the own-form, and the removal of the suspicion of an excessive or deficient number by the power of the own-definition.

children.text: niyamajñāpane tvaśakyalakṣaṇatvaśaḍkānivṛttistātparyamiti na paunarūktyamiti vṛttavartiṣyamāṇānukīrtana phalam //
children.translated_text: But in indicating the rule, the import is the removal of the suspicion of being impossible-to-define — and thus there is no redundancy. This is the purpose of the recitation of what has been stated and what is to be stated.

children.text: yadyapi pratipannaṃ pratyanumānasya na saṃśayaviparyayanivṛttirajñātajñānaṃ vopayogaḥ, tathāpyadhyavasitābhyanujñānaṃ vastubalāyātamapekṣite viṣaye 'nupekṣaṇīyameveti tasyāpyanumānapratipādyeṣu gaṇanā /
children.translated_text: Although for what is already understood, inference does not have the use of removing doubt and error, or of knowing the unknown, nevertheless, the endorsing-acknowledgment of what has been determined — arising from the force of reality regarding the required subject — is not to be disregarded. Therefore the enumeration of that [endorsement] too among the things to be demonstrated by inference.

children.text: tenādivākye pratipannaḥ pratipādayiteti pratipanna eva pratipādayitā, na tu pratipannaḥ pratipādayitaiveti boddhavyam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the opening sentence "the understood is to be demonstrated," it should be understood that what is understood is itself the demonstrator — not that what is understood is only the demonstrator.

children.text:
punaḥ paunarūktyaparihārārthaṃ vṛttavartiṣyamāṇe anukīrtayati---pūrvaṃ siddhavaditi /
sākṣātkṛtyanumityoḥ kriyayostulyatā viṣayagatā draṣṭavyā /
tenāyamarthaḥ /
vyāptigrāhakapramāṇayogyo dharmo yatrānumīyate tat pūrvavadanumānam /
tadayogyastu yatra tat sāmānyatodṛṣṭamiti /
dhūmatvaikārthasamavāyibhiriti /
satātparyaṃ viśeṣaṇam /
na hi saṃtatamūrdhvagamanamātreṇāgniranumātuṃ śakyate, dhūlīpaṭalādau vyabhicārāt /
ekadravyatvādityasya sapakṣe rūpādāvanvayasya
children.translated_text: Again, for the purpose of avoiding redundancy, he recites what has been stated and what is to be stated: "Previously, as established..." The equality of the two actions — direct realization and inference — should be seen as pertaining to the object. The meaning is thus: where a property is inferred in [a subject] that is fit for the <s>pramāṇa</s> that grasps the pervasion, that is <s>pūrvavat</s> (inference from what precedes) inference. But where it is not fit for that, that is <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference. "With those sharing a single-meaning co-inherence with smoke-ness" — [this is] a qualifier with import. For fire cannot be inferred merely from continuous upward motion, because of deviation in dust-clouds and the like. Of "being-a-single-substance" — since its positive concomitance with form and the like in the co-present instances

children.text:
spaṣṭatvāt vipakṣavyatireka evoktaḥ /
dvividhameva hīti /
na tvatrānvayābhidhānamātreṇa kevalavyatirekiśaḍkā kartavyā /
samānajātīyārambhakatvaṃ śabdasya asiddhamataḥ sādhayati---kāryatvāditi /
children.translated_text: Since the origination of sound from things of the same class is not established for [the opponent], he proves it: "Because of being an effect..."

children.text: kāryatvaṃ punarasyānupalabdhikāraṇabhāve sati anupalabdhasyopalabhyamānatvād vā pratyakṣād veti /
children.translated_text: Is the effecthood of this [sound established] from perception — by virtue of being perceived as arising when the condition of non-perception is present? Or [some other way]?

children.text: sarvatropalabdhiprasaḍgādityasya viparyayeṇa hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Because there would follow the consequence of being perceived everywhere" — the reason [is stated] by the converse of this.

children.text: prayogastvevam---avyāpyavṛttiḥ śabdaḥ, āśrayāprāptāvapi kvacidanupalabhyamānatve sati kvacidupalabhyamānatvāt saṃyogavaditi //
children.translated_text: The argument is thus: sound has a non-pervading occurrence; because, while not being perceived when there is no contact with the substratum, it is perceived somewhere [when there is contact] — like conjunction.

is obvious, only the negative concomitance in the counter-example is stated. "For it is only twofold" — but one should not suspect that this is a purely negative inference merely from the statement of the positive concomitance alone.

children.text: yadyapi caitāvanmātreṇa guṇatvaṃ sidhyati, tathāpi bhāṣyakārīyo heturūpekṣitaḥ syādityato 'vyāpakatāmātraṃ prasādhyaiva prakṛte lagayati---karṇeti /
atrāpi prayogaḥ, śabdo vīcītaraṅganyāyena karṇaśaṣkulīmantamākāśadeśamāsādayati, prakārāntarāsaṃbhave satyupalabhyamānatvāditi vyatirekī /
children.translated_text: Here too the argument [is]: sound reaches the region of ether up to and including the conch of the ear by the method of ripples and waves, since it is perceived when no other method is possible — [this is] a negative [inference].

children.text: udāharaṇārthaṃ vivecayati---idaṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: He discriminates for the purpose of illustrating: "But this..."

children.text: sadādyabhedaḥ sattāyogaḥ, anityatvam, kāraṇavattvam, sāmānyaviśeṣavattvamiti /
children.translated_text: Non-difference from existence and the like means connection with existence, non-eternality, having causes, possessing universals and particulars.

children.text: sādhyadharmiṇyasmadādibhiḥ kadācit pratyakṣeṇānupalambhādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because the <s>sādhya</s>-property is sometimes not perceived by us and the like through perception in the <s>sādhya</s>-subject.

Although by this much alone, quality-hood is established, nevertheless, lest the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>\s reason be disregarded, he proves only the non-pervasion and applies it to the topic at hand: "The ear..."

children.text:
ābhiprāyiko hyarthaḥ pakṣadharmatāyā viṣayaḥ /
sa evābhiprāyeṇa vyāpyate, yena vinā pratijñātor'tho nopapadyate /
ubhayathā saṃbhāvanāyākekataratra bādhakopapattāvanyataraḥ pramāṇāntaragocaraḥ, tatra vidhāyakapramāṇābhāve kevalavyatirekiṇo 'vatāraḥ /
tathā hi
children.translated_text: For the intended meaning is the domain of the property-of-the-thesis. That alone, by intention, is pervaded — [the property] without which the meaning of the thesis is untenable. When there is the possibility in both ways, and when a sublating [argument] is available for one, the other is within the scope of another <s>pramāṇa</s>. When there is no positive-establishing <s>pramāṇa</s> there, the purely negative inference (<s>kevalavyatirekin</s>) enters. For here,

children.text:
kṣityādikaṃ sakartṛkaṃ kāryatvādityatra sarvajñatvamantareṇa kṣityādīnāṃ kartṛtvameva nopapadyate, paramāṇvadṛṣṭādīnāmajñāne tadadhiṣṭhānānupapatteḥ /
tadadhiṣṭhāne vā asarvajñatvānupapatteḥ /
tasmāt sarvajñatvamantareṇa pratijñātārthānupapattau tadabhiprāyavyāptam /
ābhiprāyikatvācca pakṣadharmatāgocaraḥ /
icchādayaḥ paratantrā guṇatvādityatra punarātmā nābhiprāyavyāptaḥ /
na hīcchādīnāṃ kṣityādipāratantryamasaṃbhāvit, api tu mānasapratyakṣavedyatvādibhaḥ bādhitam /
dhūmagatanīlatveneva dhūmasyāpālālatvam /
children.translated_text: Just as the non-straw-ness of smoke [is established] by the blue-ness belonging to smoke [and not to straw].

children.text: tasmādubhayathāpi saṃbhavādātmā naivābhiprāyavyāptaḥ, tadavyāptatvācca na pakṣadharmatā tamaṅkamāropayitumarhati, api tvicchāsaṃbaddhaparamātramādāyaiva nivartate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the possibility obtains in both ways, the self is not at all pervaded by intention; and since it is not pervaded by that, the property-of-the-thesis cannot elevate it to its lap, but stops merely by taking what is connected with desire and the like.

children.text: etaduttarakālaṃ kṣityādau bādhite tadanyāsiddhau vidhāyakapramāṇābhāvānniṣedhamukhena vyatirekī pravartate /
children.translated_text: At a subsequent time, when earth and the like are sublated [as candidates], and when what is other than those is unestablished, due to the absence of a positive-establishing <s>pramāṇa</s>, the negative inference proceeds through the method of negation.

children.text: tamimaṃ viśeṣaṃ hṛdi nidhāyoktam---bādhakairapanīte dravyāṣṭakaguṇatva iti //
children.translated_text: Keeping this distinction in mind, it was said: "When the eight-substance-and-quality-hood is removed by sublating [arguments]..."

in [the inference] "the earth and the like have a maker, because of being effects" — without omniscience, the very maker-hood of the earth and the like is untenable, because atoms, <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), and the like, when unknown, cannot be superintended by anyone. Or because, in superintending those, non-omniscience is untenable. Therefore, without omniscience, since the meaning of the thesis is untenable, it is pervaded by that intention. And because it is intentional, it is the domain of the property-of-the-thesis. But in "desires and the like are dependent on another, because of being qualities" — the self is not pervaded by intention. For the dependence of desires and the like on earth and the like is not inconceivable; rather, it is sublated by the perceptibility by mental perception and the like.

children.text:
nanu sāmānyatodṛṣṭād yadrūpaṃ siddham, na tat kevalavyatirekiṇā sādhyam /
yādṛśaṃ ca tena sādhyam, tādṛśaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, what is established as being of such a form through <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference cannot be proved by a purely negative inference. And what is proved by that [purely negative inference] is of a form that

children.text: na kvacit siddham /
tathā cāprasiddhaviśeṣaṇaḥ pakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus the thesis has an unestablished qualifier.

children.text: na ca tathābhūte sandeho 'pi kāraṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: And regarding such a thing, there is not even doubt, due to the absence of a cause [for doubt].

children.text: samānāsamānadharmavipratipattīnāmanupalabdhacarāviṣayatvādityata āha---yadyapi cāyamiti /
children.translated_text: Because the [three causes of doubt —] disagreement about common properties, uncommon properties, and conflicting views — do not have what is beyond apprehension as their domain — therefore he says: "Although this too..."

children.text: svarūpeṇa asādhāraṇarūpeṇetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: in its own form, i.e. in its unique form.
has never been established.

children.text:
na hi vākyārthasayāpūrvatayā padārthānāṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo vihanyate /
tathā sati, anvayinopyanutthānamiti pralīnamanumānena /
na ca dravyāṣṭakātiriktādipadārthā evāpūrve, yenāprasiddhaviśeṣaṇatā syāt pakṣasya /
na caivaṃ sati śaśaśṛṅgadhanurdharādāvapi prasaṅgaḥ, tatrāpi tadārthamātrāprasiddheḥ sarvatra sulabhatvāditi vācyam /
sāmānyatodṛṣṭapūrvakatvaniyamasīmāyāḥ durlaḍghyatvāt /
anyathā sāmānyato 'pyasiddhaḥ kathaṃ niṣpramāṇakaśabdasāmarthyamātramāśritya parāmṛśyeta /
aparāmṛṣṭaśca kathaṃ pramāṇavyavahāramavatārayet /
tadidam uktam---adūraviprakarṣeṇa parāmṛṣṭa iti /
viśeṣasiddheḥ sāmānyasidbhiradūraviprakarṣaḥ, tadasiddhistu tadviparyaya
children.translated_text: For the qualifier-qualificand relation of the categories is not vitiated by the novelty of the sentence-meaning. If that were the case, even the positive concomitant would not be raised — [and thus] the inference would be dissolved. And it is not the case that only the categories beyond the eight substances are novel, such that the thesis would have an unestablished qualifier. Nor, this being the case, is there the consequence [of the argument applying] even to the horn of a hare, the bearer of the bow [Śiva], and the like — because even there the non-establishment of the mere referent [of the word] is easily available everywhere — this objection should not be made, because of the difficult-to-transgress boundary of the restriction that what is prior [must be ascertained] through inference from the general. Otherwise, how could even what is generally unestablished be reflectively considered while relying merely on the power of a word without a <s>pramāṇa</s>? And if not reflectively considered, how could it enter into the practice of <s>pramāṇa</s>? This is what is said: 'reflectively considered through non-remote proximity.' The non-remoteness of proximity is the establishment of the general from the establishment of the specific; remoteness of proximity is the opposite of that —

children.text: ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ ca saṃśayo 'pyatra vādivipratipattereva sugamaḥ, icchādīnāmubhayavādisiddhe sāmānyato 'dhikaraṇe dravyāṣṭakātiriktānatirekakoṭyorūbhābhyāṃ samutthāpanāt /
athavā pratyekotthitaḥ saṃśayaḥ samudāye viśrāmyatīti nyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or rather, doubt raised in individual [cases] comes to rest in the aggregate — this is the principle.

children.text: tathā hi guṇatvaṃ pṛthivyāśrite gandhādau, tadatiriktāśrite snehādau ca dṛṣṭam, icchādiṣu ca dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: For thus, property-hood (<s>guṇatva</s>) is observed in odor and the like that reside in earth, and in viscosity and the like that reside in what is beyond that [i.e., beyond earth]; and it is also seen in desire and the like.

children.text: tat kimicchādayaḥ pṛthivyāśritā, uta tadatiriktāśritā ityanenākāreṇa sarvadravyeṣu bhavan sandehaḥ samānadharmadarśanādeva dravyāṣṭakatadatiriktakoṭyoreva paryavasito bhavati /
children.translated_text: So are desire and the like resident in earth, or resident in what is beyond that? — by this form [of doubt], the doubt that exists in all substances comes to rest in precisely the two alternatives of the eight substances and what is beyond them, through the very observation of common properties.

children.text: tadidamuktam---dharmiṇi cetyādi //
children.translated_text: This is what is said: 'dharmiṇi ca' (and in the subject), etc.

And thus, even doubt here is easily obtained from the disagreement of the disputants alone — since it is raised from both alternatives — the alternative of there being, and the alternative of there not being [categories] beyond the eight substances — in a locus agreed upon by both parties through the general [inference], such as desire and the like.

children.text:
vibhāgavacanādevetyādibhāṣyavakravyākhyāyāḥ śaḍkāpoṣaṇe tātparyam /
nanu sadasatī tattvamityatra sadasacchabdābhyāṃ bhāvābhāvāvuktau /
tadiha vartamānāvartamānārthatvavyākhyānaṃ tadviruddhamapi kuta upādīya ityata āha---pratyakṣaṃ hīti /
atha tathaiva kiṃ na syādityata āha---yadyapīti /
na viśeṣaṇtvaṃ svātantryeṇa svātantryābhidhānenetyarthaḥ /
āho nyāyopyastītyasyākṣarārthena naḥ saṃbandhānupapatteḥ, tātparyārthenasaṃbandhamāha---na sandeha
children.translated_text: The purport of the oblique explanation of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [beginning with] 'vibhāgavacanāt' (from the statement of division) and so forth is to support the doubt. Now, in 'the real and the unreal constitute reality,' by the words 'sat' (existent) and 'asat' (non-existent), positive entity and absence are denoted. Then the explanation here as 'having the meaning of present and non-present' is contradictory — from where is it adopted? — therefore he says: 'pratyakṣaṃ hī' (for perception). Now, why should it not be just so [i.e., existent and non-existent]? — therefore he says: 'yadyapī' (although). The meaning is: not as a qualifier independently, not through independent statement. Since the literal meaning of 'āho nyāyo 'pyasti' (or is there also a method?) does not have a connection with us, he states the connection through the purport-meaning: 'na sandeha',

children.text: iti /
nyāyābhāvena hi tarkasya niścayāparyāptau sandehastadavastha ityāśaḍkitam, atastanniṣedha evottaraṃ yuktamiti /
children.translated_text: For the doubt is raised [by asking]: in the absence of a <s>nyāya</s> (method of reasoning), when <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) is insufficient for certainty, the doubt remains as it was — hence the negation of that [doubt] alone is the appropriate answer.
