children.text: astyeva nyāyaḥ, sandehavirodhiniścayasamartho yata iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is indeed a <s>nyāya</s>, capable of producing certainty that opposes doubt — this is the completion.

children.text: nimittatvaṃ yadi viṣayatvaṃ tannātmani dṛṣṭānte /
children.translated_text: If 'being a cause' (<s>nimittatva</s>) means being the object — that is not [seen] in the <s>ātman</s>, the example.

children.text: athopādānatvam, na tatsādhye samavāya ityata āha---nimittatvaṃ kāraṇatvamiti //
children.translated_text: But if [it means] being the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) — then <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) does not exist in what is to be proved — therefore he says: 'nimittatvaṃ kāraṇatvam' (being a cause means being a causal factor).
'iti' (not doubt).

children.text:
nanu vyāpakatvaṃ paramamahatparimāṇayogaḥ, sarvasaṃyogisamānadeśatā vā /
tadubhayamapi samavāye na saṃbhavatītyata
children.translated_text: Now, <s>vyāpakatva</s> (pervasiveness) is either connection with a supremely great magnitude, or co-extensiveness with everything conjoined. Neither of these is possible for <s>samavāya</s> — therefore

children.text:
āha---satyupalabdhīti /
upalabhyatetyucyamāne ghaṭāderapi vyāpakatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
ata uktaṃ sarvatreti /
deśasyāvacchedakatāmātreṇa saptamyā nirdeśo vane sihanāda itivat /
tathāpyasiddhaṃ lakṣaṇam, na hyātmādayaḥ sarvatropalabhyante ityata uktam---satyupalabdhikāraṇa iti /
tathāpi viṣayasyāpyupalabdhikāraṇatvād yatra yatra ghaṭādiparamāṇvantāḥ svopalabdhisāmagrīsahitāḥ, tatra tatropalabhyanta eveti taireva vyabhicāra ityata uktam---antareti /
etacca dravyarūpakāraṇāntarābhiprāyeṇa draṣṭavyam /
anyathā yatra ghaṭādayo na santi, tatra tato 'nyasya tadupalabdhikāraṇasya tadindriyasaṃyogasyābhāvādeva teṣāmanupalambhaḥ, tatsadbhāve tu sarvatropalambha eva ityetadapyāśaḍkyeta /
tathāpi paramāṇvādiguṇaireva yāvaddravyabhāvibhirāśrayādhīnanirūpaṇairvyabhicāraḥ, tannivṛttyarthamanekasaṃbandhitve satīti draṣṭavyam /
etacca sarvatretyanena ṭīkākṛtā sūcitam /
children.translated_text: And this was indicated by the author of the <s>Ṭīkā</s> through [the word] 'everywhere.'

children.text: yadyapi ca sarvatrāstitvaṃ vyāpakatvam, tathāpi lakṣaṇamantareṇa tad duravabodhamiti tadevoktamiti /
children.translated_text: And although pervasiveness is existence everywhere, nevertheless, without a definition that is difficult to understand — hence that very [definition] is stated.

children.text: nyāyetikartavyatābhūtaṃ tarkaṃ pṛcchati /
children.translated_text: He asks about <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) that serves as a requisite procedure for the <s>nyāya</s> (method).

children.text: kartrā avyāpāryamāṇasya karaṇasya svayaṃ vyāpārāyogādityāśayavāniti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: The purport is: since an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) that is not operated upon by an agent is unable to operate on its own.

he says: 'satyupalabdhī' (when apprehension [exists]). If it were said 'is apprehended,' there would be the absurd consequence of pervasiveness even of pots and the like. Hence it is said 'everywhere.' The locative case is merely in the sense of delimiting place, as in 'the roar of a lion in the forest.' Even so, the definition is unestablished, for the <s>ātman</s> and the like are not apprehended everywhere — hence it is said: 'satyupalabdhikāraṇa' (when the cause of apprehension [exists]). Even so, since objects too have causes of apprehension, wherever atoms of pots and the like, up to [the most minute], are accompanied by the totality of conditions for their own apprehension, there they are indeed apprehended — and so the deviation [occurs] through those very [atoms] — hence it is said: 'antara' (different). And this should be understood with the intention of a different cause of the substance-type. Otherwise, where pots and the like do not exist, [one might suspect that] the non-apprehension of those is simply due to the absence of their apprehension-cause — namely, the conjunction with their sense-organ — and if that [conjunction] were present, they would be apprehended everywhere. Even so, the deviation [occurs] through the qualities of atoms and the like, which exist wherever the substance exists and whose determination depends on the substratum — and to prevent that, 'when there are multiple connections' should be understood.

children.text: athoktamanavasthānaprasaṅgamavatārayituṃ kimityanādhāratvaprasaṅga ucyate, yāvatā svatantra evāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ kiṃ
children.translated_text: Now, what is said in order to introduce the consequence of infinite regress — why is the consequence of there being no substratum stated, since that consequence itself is independent? Why

children.text:
na syāt? na hi kāryasyānādhāratvamasyeṣṭamevetyata āha---syādetaditi /
paścāt turyā saṃyukta iti śeṣaḥ /

na hyutpanno 'pyasaṃyukta eva turyā prathamekṣaṇe paṭa iti kasyacinniścayaḥ, atha ca pramāṇabalādiṣṭa evāyamarthaḥ, tathotpanne 'pi prathame kṣaṇe tantuṣvasamaveta eveṣyata iti pādau prasārya tiṣṭhato nedamuttaramityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For no one has the certainty that 'at the first glance, cloth that has arisen is simply not conjoined with the fourth [substance, i.e., the loom].' Yet this very meaning is established by the force of <s>pramāṇa</s>. Similarly, even when [cloth] has arisen, at the first moment, being accepted as not inherent in the threads [is unacceptable] — this answer is not for one who stretches out his legs [i.e., is stubbornly entrenched] — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasmādanavasthāprasaḍgāvatāraṇāyaivedamuktamityāha---samavāyaścetīti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this was stated merely for the purpose of introducing the consequence of infinite regress — he says: 'samavāyaśca' (and inherence).

children.text: yadyapyupādhikathanenaiva vṛttimattvasya prāptidharmatvaṃ nirākṛtam, tathāpi prāptitvasyānaikāntikatvasūcanāya punarapyanavasthāprasaṅgamavatārayati---atheti /
children.translated_text: Although the property of contact (<s>prāpti</s>) being a <s>vṛttimat</s> (something that has occurrence) has been refuted by the very statement of the limiting condition, nevertheless, to indicate the inconclusiveness of contact-hood, he introduces the consequence of infinite regress once more: 'atha' (now).

children.text: anavasthābhiyā avaśyamantataḥ kācit prāptiśca na ca vṛttimatīti svīkartavyam, tataśca tathaiva prāptimattvamanaikāntikamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Out of fear of infinite regress, at least some contact must be accepted that does not itself have occurrence — and thus, contact-hood (<s>prāptimattva</s>) is inconclusive — this is the meaning.

should it not [simply stand]? For it is not the case that the absence of a substratum for the effect is what is desired — therefore he says: 'syādetat' (this might be so). The completion is: 'later, conjoined with the fourth [substance].'

children.text: athānavasthāsvīkāre ko doṣa ityāśaḍkya nirākaroti---nanviyamiti /
children.translated_text: Now, what is the fault in accepting infinite regress? — suspecting this, he refutes: 'nanu iyam' (now this).

children.text: anāditāyāṃ hyaḍkurotpādānuguṇasamayasaṃbhavinā bījena janite 'ḍkureṇa janite bīje vartamānaṃ bījatvaṃ tasyāḍkurapūrvakatāmavagamayatīti yujyate, avikalasya hetoḥ pramāṇasya vidyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: For in a beginningless [series], the seed that is produced at a time suited to the production of a sprout generates a sprout, and in the seed generated by the sprout, the seed-hood that is present enables the understanding of the sprout's having been preceded [by a seed] — this is justified, because the reason, namely the <s>pramāṇa</s>, is present in its complete form.

children.text: idaṃprathamatāyāṃ tu kāryotpādānuguṇasamaye bhaviṣyatpravāhasyāsattvāt prathamasyānutpāde tadāśrayasya hetostasminnasatyāśrayāsiddhatayā sarvasyāgamakatve pramāṇābhāva ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But if [the series is] first-ever, since a future stream does not exist at a time suited to the production of the effect, and since the first [member] would not arise without it, and since the reason that depends on it [as its substratum] would have the fault of an unestablished substratum — [then] in the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> for all that follows, everything becomes unsupported — this is the meaning.

children.text:
abhyupetakaṇādāptatvasya śāstravirodhaścetyādi /
kāryamakṛtakasaṃbandhavaditi pratijñāyāṃ ghaṭāderbhūtalādināpyakṛtaka eva saṃbandhaḥ syāt, sa cāniṣṭa iti pratijñāṃ viśinaṣṭi---svopādāneneti /
svasamavāyinetyarthaḥ /
kāryamiti ca samavetamātropalakṣaṇaparam, anyathā jātyādiṣu vipakṣeṣu saṃbhave hetorvirodhaḥ syāt /
athavā pratijñā yathāśrutaiva, ādhāravattvādityatrādhāraśabdena nāśrayamātraṃ vivakṣitam, kiṃ tvadhikaraṇaṃ kārakam /
children.translated_text: 'The accepted trustworthiness of <s>Kaṇāda</s> and the contradiction with scripture,' etc. In the thesis 'an effect has an uncreated connection with its own material cause,' even pots and the like would have an uncreated connection with the earth-element and the like. Since that is undesired, he qualifies the thesis: 'svopādānena' (with its own material cause). The meaning is: 'with what is co-inherent with it.' And 'effect' is merely indicative of what is co-inherent; otherwise, if the reason applied to counter-examples like universals and the like, there would be contradiction. Or rather, the thesis is to be taken literally; and in 'ādhāravattvāt' (because of having a substratum), by the word 'ādhāra' (substratum), not mere locus is intended, but rather the <s>adhikaraṇa</s>-<s>kāraka</s> (the locative factor of action).

children.text:
tenādhikaraṇakārakavattvād ityarthaḥ /
na ca vācyam---kārakavattvamātreṇaiva paryāptau kimadhikaraṇagrahaṇeneti, pradhvaṃsena virodhaprasaḍgāt /
na kāryasya kāryaḥ saṃbandha ityarthaḥ /
mithaḥ saṃbadhyete /
ādhāryādhārabhāvenāvatiṣṭhete ityarthaḥ /
so 'pi samavāye nāsti samavāyāntarābhāvādityarthaḥ /
sannapyasau na kāryamādhāravat karoti, svasamavāyenaiva tasyādhāravattvāt, tadabhāve tvekārthasamavāyo 'pi na syādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though it [samavāya] exists, it does not make the effect possess a substratum by its own inherence, since the substratum-hood of that [effect] is precisely through its own <s>samavāya</s>; and in its absence, even co-inherence in the same substratum would not exist — this is the meaning.

children.text: sahotpāde kāryamanādhāraṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: If [effect and substratum] arise simultaneously, the effect would be without a substratum.

children.text: sarvadeti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Always' is to be supplied.

children.text: samavāyikāraṇābhāve 'samavāyikāraṇaśaḍkāpi nāsti, tatpratyāsannasvabhāvatvāt tasyetyabhiprāyavatā tadupekṣya nimittamātrādutpattirāśaḍkya nirākṛtā //
children.translated_text: In the absence of an <s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s> (non-inherent cause), there is not even the suspicion of a non-inherent cause — because of its having a nature proximate to that [inherent cause]. With this intention, setting that aside, the [theory of] arising from a mere efficient cause alone was suspected and refuted.

Hence the meaning is: because of having the <s>adhikaraṇa</s>-<s>kāraka</s>. And one should not say: 'when mere possession of a <s>kāraka</s> suffices, what is the need for specifying <s>adhikaraṇa</s>?' — because there would be the consequence of contradiction with destruction (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>). The meaning is: the connection of the effect is not itself an effect. 'They mutually connect' — the meaning is: they stand in the relation of supported and support. 'Even that [relation] does not exist in <s>samavāya</s>' — the meaning is: because of the absence of a second <s>samavāya</s>.

children.text:
nanu vidhīyamānaniṣidhyamānavyatirekeṇa jagati na svatantro nāma /
tat kathaṃ dharmatraividhyamityata āha---atra ceti /
vidhīyamāno vartamāna ityarthaḥ /
pratiṣidhyamānaḥ avartamāna ityarthaḥ /
tatra ye vartamānāḥ, teṣāṃ kaścit paratantro vṛttimānityarthaḥ /
kaścit svatantro vṛttirahita ityarthaḥ /
pratiṣidhyamānāstu paratantrā na santi, asattvādeva iti /
tadevaṃ vidhīyamānaḥ svatantro vidhīyamānaḥ paratantraḥ pratiṣidhyamānaḥ svatantraśceti tisro vidhā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, apart from what is positively enjoined and what is negated, there is nothing independent in the world. Then how is there a threefold classification of <s>dharma</s> (property)? — therefore he says: 'atra ca' (and here). 'What is being positively enjoined' means 'what is present' — this is the meaning. 'What is being negated' means 'what is absent' — this is the meaning. Among those, of those that are present, some are dependent, [i.e.,] having occurrence — this is the meaning. And some are independent, [i.e.,] without occurrence — this is the meaning. But what is negated, [i.e.,] what is dependent [on a positive entity], does not exist — simply because of its non-existence. Thus, the three kinds are: what is positively enjoined and independent; what is positively enjoined and dependent; and what is negated and independent — this is the meaning.

children.text:
tadevamavartamāno gharmaḥ pratiṣidhyamānatayaiva vyavahriyate, na cāsau pratyakṣaviṣayaḥ, kiṃ tvanumānaviṣaya iti darśitam /
taccānupapannamiti śaḍkāvārttikārtham āha---nanviti /
asannityuddeśyam /
tenāyamarthaḥ, asannavartamāno na kevalaṃ pratiṣedhavyavahāraviṣayaḥ, kiṃ tu vidhīyamāno 'pi, vidhivyavahāraviṣayo 'pi /
evamasau na kevalam anumānaviṣayaḥ, pratyakṣaśca /
kvacit pratyakṣaviṣayaścetyarthaḥ /
kketyata āha---yatheti /
kathamasau vidhīyamāna ityata āha---jāyamāna iti /
kathamasau pratyakṣaviṣaya ityata āha---visphāriteti /
kathamasāvavartamāna ityata āha---na cāsāviti /
children.translated_text: How is it not present? — therefore he says: 'na cāsau' (and it is not that).

children.text: asattayā sattayā vānabhyupagamāditi sattāyā jāyamānatayā virodhāt, asattayā vidhiviṣayatayeti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because it is not accepted either as non-existent or as existent — because of the contradiction of being-born with existence, and because of the contradiction of the usage of positive injunction with non-existence — this is the purport.

children.text: kathaṃ nābhyupagamyate na hi sattāsattābhyāmanyaḥ prakāro 'stītyata āha---niṣedhaviṣayatayā tviti /
children.translated_text: How is it not accepted? For there is no other mode besides existence and non-existence — therefore he says: 'niṣedhaviṣayatayā tu' (but by virtue of being the object of negation).

children.text: vidhīyamānatāpakṣe hi jāyamānatābhyupagame ubhayathāpi virodho, na tu pratiṣidhyamānatāpakṣe 'pītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: For in the position that it is positively enjoined, upon accepting that it is being-born, there is contradiction in both ways; but not in the position that it is being negated — this is the meaning.

Thus, heat that is not present is conventionally used only as what is negated, and it is not an object of perception, but rather an object of inference — this has been shown. And this is untenable — he states the purport of the objecting <s>Vārttika</s>: 'nanu' (now). 'The non-existent' is the subject. By this, the meaning is: the non-existent — what is not present — is not merely the object of the usage of negation, but also positively enjoined, also the object of the usage of positive injunction. Likewise, it is not merely the object of inference, but also of perception — the object of perception in some cases — this is the meaning. Where? — therefore he says: 'yathā' (as). How is it positively enjoined? — therefore he says: 'jāyamāna' (being born). How is it the object of perception? — therefore he says: 'visphārita' (manifested).

children.text:
tasmāt jāyamāne ghaṭe na vidhāyakapratyakṣapravṛttiḥ, virodhāt /
niṣedhakaṃ taṃ pratyakṣaṃ pravartamānamapi tanniṣedhameva gocarayet, na tu niṣedhyaṃ ghaṭam /
tataḥ siddho viṣayabheda iti sāram /
upapādanīya iti satkāryavādamapanīya /
apare tviti /
children.translated_text: 'Others, however' —

children.text: arthātirekamātram /
children.translated_text: [this is] merely a surplus of meaning.

children.text: arthapadātirekamātram /
children.translated_text: [this is] merely a surplus of the word 'artha.'

children.text: evamuttaratrāpi //
children.translated_text: Similarly in what follows.

Therefore, in the case of a pot that is being born, there is no operation of a perception that positively establishes — because of contradiction. A perception operating as negating would make known only that negation, not the pot as the thing negated. From this, the established conclusion is: the distinction of object [between positive and negative perception]. This is the essence. 'Is to be demonstrated' — having set aside the <s>satkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine that the effect pre-exists in the cause).

children.text:
nanu kenaitaduktam, yadubhayapadavyabhicāra eva viśeṣaṇasamāso bhavatītyata āha---viśeṣaṇamiti /
nanu tathāpyubhayorapi pṛthivīdravyaśabdayorūbhayavācitvāt kathaṃ viśeṣapratipattirityata āha---na ceti /
na hi bhavati pṛthivītvaṃ dravyatvamityupalakṣaṇam /
pṛthivītvaṃ dravyam, dravyatvaṃ ca pṛthivītyapi na bhavatītyapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: 'Earth-hood is substance, and substance-hood is earth' — this too does not hold. This should also be observed.

children.text: na ca nāntarīyakārthaśabdayorapīyameva gatirastviti vācyam, aniyamaprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: And one should not say that even for words denoting inseparable things, this very analysis holds — because there would follow the consequence of non-restriction.

children.text: nāntarīyakatvārthayorapi sāmānādhikaraṇyādarthatvanāntarīkayorapīti /
children.translated_text: For even inseparability and purposefulness, being co-referential, would entail that purposefulness and inseparability [are identical].

children.text: tatastadvyavacchedārthaṃ punarapi prayatnāntaramāstheyam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for distinguishing that [inseparability from purposefulness], yet another effort must be maintained.

Now, who has said that the qualifying compound occurs only when there is deviation from both terms? — therefore he says: 'viśeṣaṇam' (qualifier). Now, even so, since both the words 'earth' and 'substance' denote both [earth and substance], how is specific understanding [obtained]? — therefore he says: 'na ca' (and not). For it is not the case that 'earth-hood is substance-hood' — this is [established through the] indicative marker.

children.text:
tasmādanekārthatve 'pi viśeṣapara evāyaṃ nāntarīyakaśabda ityakāmenāpyabhyupeyam /
tathā ca pūrvadūṣaṇānivṛttiriti /
nanu aniyataprasareṇāsati nāstīti sahiteneṣṭalābho yadyapi tathāpi sarvathā sapakṣāvṛttirasādhāraṇo 'pi nivartayitavyaḥ, na hi pakṣavyāpako vipakṣe ca nāstyevaitāvataiva tasya nirākaraṇam, tasyāpyevaṃbhūtatvāt /
tasmāt tattulye sadbhāva iti kartavyamevetyāśaḍkyāha---prasaktamapratiṣiddhamanumatameveti /
prasaktasya pratiṣedhādupādāne tadviparītasya hānamarthāyātamityarthaḥ /
na cāsaṃbhavo 'pi prasakto, yenāniṣedhāt
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though [the word] has multiple meanings, it must be accepted even by one unwilling that this word 'antarīyaka' is directed toward a specific meaning. And thus the earlier objections are not averted. Now, even if the desired result is obtained by [the combination] 'when the indeterminate extension is absent, [the property] is absent,' nevertheless, the complete absence from the <s>sapakṣa</s> (positive instance), even of the uncommon [reason], must be removed; for it is not the case that merely by the fact that [the reason] pervades the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) and is absent in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (counter-instance), its refutation [is achieved], since that [uncommon reason] too is of such a nature. Therefore, anticipating the objection that one must still [show] 'presence in what is similar to that' — he says: 'what is applicable and not prohibited is accepted.'

children.text:
tasyāpyupādāne tadviparītahānaṃ saṃbhāvyeta /
prathame pade saṃbhavasya vidheyatvena ivāsaṃbhavasya niṣedhyatvenānupādānāditi /
samuccīyamānetyādi vaicitryeṇa hi nipātasaṃbandhe vākyabhedaprasaṅgaḥ, athaikavākyatvamicchannavaicitryeṇaiva nipātasaṃbandhamicchedityarthaḥ /
etadevānūdyamānasamuccayamāśaḍkyamānaḥ sphuṭayati---na ceti /
uditaṃ hyanūdyate, natvanuditam na cobhayatvaviśiṣṭaṃ havirūditam /
kiṃ tu havirmātram /
tathā cānuvādapakṣe ubhayatvamavivakṣitam /
ubhayatvavivakṣāyāṃ tu nāyamanuvādaḥ, kiṃ tu vāda eva /
tathā ca vākyabhedaḥ /
evaṃ dārṣṭāntike 'pi yadi sādhyāyogavyacchedaviśiṣṭo heturūditaḥ, yuktamidānīṃ yattathāsāvanūdyate, na tvetadasti /
hetumātraṃ tvaviśiṣṭamuddiṣṭam /
viśiṣṭasya tu tasyāyameva prathamo vādāvatāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And of that qualified [reason], this itself is the very first occasion of [fresh] statement.

children.text: tadyadi yasyetyayamanuvādo, nūnamanumeye sadbhāva evetyavivakṣitaṃ viśeṣaṇam, vivakṣite tasminnanenaiva vākyena viśiṣṭo vādaḥ kartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, if 'of which' is a restatement, then surely the qualification 'presence precisely in the <s>anumeya</s> (inferendum)' is unintended; if that [qualification] is intended, then by this very sentence the qualified statement must be made,

children.text: paścādidamevāvṛttyānuvāda iti vākyabheda ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: and afterward, the repetition of this very [sentence] would be a restatement — thus there would be splitting of the sentence — this is the meaning.

children.text: so 'yaṃ prayatnāntarīyasthānaśabdasyārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the meaning of the word '<s>sthāna</s>' (place) [in the expression] '<s>prayatnāntarīya</s>' (requiring no additional effort). //

When that [applicable thing] too is included, the exclusion of its opposite would be expected. Because in the first clause, just as possibility is the thing to be predicated, so impossibility is not included as something to be negated — this is [the meaning]. 'When being combined...' etc. — for with varied connection of particles, there would be the consequence of splitting the sentence; but if one desires single-sentence unity, one should accept the connection of particles without variation — this is the meaning. Anticipating [the objection regarding] this very aggregate being restated, he clarifies: 'and not...' For what has been stated is restated, not what has not been stated. And [what was stated as] qualified by duality is not the <s>havis</s> (oblation) that was stated, but merely the <s>havis</s> [unqualified]. And thus, in the restatement view, duality is not intended. But if duality is intended, then this is not a restatement but a [fresh] statement itself. And thus there would be splitting of the sentence. Likewise in the analogous case — if the reason qualified by exclusion of connection with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) has been stated, then it would be proper that it be restated as such; but this is not the case. Rather, the reason alone, unqualified, has been propounded.

children.text: nanu yadyanūdyamānamaśakyaṃ viśeṣṭum, athārtirapi kathaṃ haviṣā viśeṣyata ityata āha---atra hi yadyapīti /
ananyagatikatvāt prāptena haviṣā viśeṣaṇamārteḥ /
children.translated_text: The qualification of <s>ārti</s> (affliction) is by the <s>havis</s> (oblation), which is obtained through there being no other recourse.

children.text: ubhayatvasya tu na pūrvaprāptatvam, nāpi tadantareṇārtiraśakyapratipattiḥ, sādhyāyomavyavacchedaḥ api hetorīdṛśa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But duality is neither previously established, nor is <s>ārti</s> (affliction) impossible to understand without it — [meaning:] the exclusion of connection with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is also such a [qualification] of the reason — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadyevamubhayavacanaṃ kimarthamityata āha---pratīyamānamapi ubhayatvamavivakṣitam /
children.translated_text: If so, then for what purpose is the statement of duality? — to this he says: 'even though understood, the duality is unintended' —

children.text: viśeṣaṇatayeti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'as a qualifier' — this is to be supplied. //
Now, if what is being restated cannot be qualified, then how is <s>ārti</s> (affliction) qualified by the <s>havis</s> (oblation)? — to this he says: 'here, although...'

children.text: ayaṃ vākyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the meaning of the sentence.

children.text: ārtiviśeṣaṇatayā havistāvadupādātavyam, tasya cājyapuroḍāśādyanekarūpatvādubhayatvamapyastīti prāyikatayā tadapyupāttam /
children.translated_text: The <s>havis</s> (oblation) must be included as a qualifier of <s>ārti</s> (affliction), and since that [oblation] has multiple forms such as <s>ājya</s> (ghee), <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) and others, duality too exists [in it], and so that [duality] too is included incidentally.

children.text: tenedaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati, ekamanekaṃ vā haviryasyārtimārcchedityādi /
children.translated_text: Thereby this is established: whether one or many oblations may relieve the affliction — and so on.

children.text: ubhayatvavivakṣāpakṣe tu naikaikahavirārtau prāyaścittavidhiḥ syāditi doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: But in the view that intends duality, there would be the defect that there is no injunction of expiatory rite for affliction from each single oblation. //

children.text:
na caivamastviti vācyam, vākyabhedaprasaṅgasya tādavasthyāditi /
na cānumeye sadbhāva eva, tattulya eva sadbhāva iti vākyadvayamevedamubhayavidhāyakamastu, ko doṣa iti vācyam, trirūpasaṃpannasya heturūpasyaikasyārthasyālābhaprasaḍgāt /
vākyabhede hyavaśyamarthabheda iti nyāyāt /
śaṅkate---atheti /
children.translated_text: And it should not be said 'let it be so,' because the consequence of splitting the sentence remains unchanged. Nor should it be said 'let these two sentences — presence precisely in the <s>anumeya</s> (inferendum), and presence precisely in what is similar to that — serve as enjoining both [aspects]; what is the fault?' — because there would be the consequence of failing to obtain the single meaning of the form of the reason possessing the three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>). For according to the principle that splitting of the sentence necessarily entails splitting of meaning — he raises the objection: 'but if...'

children.text: avāntaravākyabhede 'pi mahāvākyasyaikatvāt, vivakṣitaikārthapratilambha iti śaḍkārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even though there is splitting of subordinate sentences, since the great sentence is one, the intended single meaning is obtained — this is the purport of the objection. //

children.text:
atra naiyāyikasamādhānamāśaḍkya bauddhaḥ svabhāṣayā nirākaroti---na ceti /
yadyapi tattulya evetyanyayogavyavacchedasya vipakṣamātraviṣayatvaṃ tadā syād yadi viṣayāntarasaṃkocaḥ syāt, sa ca tadekavākyatayeti parasparāśrayadoṣaḥ /

anyathobhayorapi tattulyānyatvāviśeṣe vipakṣayogasya vyavacchedo na tvanumeyayogasyeti kutaḥ? vihitatvāt tasyeti cet? ata eva virodhādekavākyatvāsaṅgatirityucyate, yasmāt tadekavākyatāyāmeva satyāṃ vipakṣamātraviṣayatvamasya vaktuṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, when there is no distinction between 'similar to that' and 'other than that' for both, [one might ask:] why is it the connection with the <s>vipakṣa</s> (counter-instance) that is excluded and not the connection with the <s>anumeya</s> (inferendum)? If [you say:] because that [connection with the inferendum] has been enjoined — precisely therefore, because of the contradiction, the coherence of single-sentence unity is undermined — it is said: since only when the single-sentence unity holds can the scope of this [statement] be restricted to the <s>vipakṣa</s> alone,

children.text: sāpi tasmin satyeveti durūttaradoṣāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: and that [single-sentence unity] too holds only when this [restriction] holds — the fault of an unanswerable difficulty arises.

children.text: tathāpi bauddhanaye śābddhaṃ vyavahāramāśritya samuccaya eva na nirvahet, kṛtamanayā virodhe sūkṣmekṣikayetyāśayavānāha---anyāpoheti /
children.translated_text: Even so, from the standpoint of the Buddhist doctrine, relying on verbal convention, the aggregation itself would not be sustained; [thinking] 'enough of this subtle examination of the contradiction' — with this intent he says: '<s>anyāpoha</s>' (exclusion of the other).

children.text: so 'yaṃ sādhāraṇo 'pi nyāyo 'prastutatvabhiyā viśeṣaniṣṭhatayāvatārita iti //5 //
children.translated_text: This very principle, though general, has been introduced as applying to a specific [topic] out of concern for irrelevance. // 5 //

Here, anticipating the <s>Naiyāyika</s>'s resolution, the <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist) refutes it in his own language: 'and not...' Even though the exclusion in 'precisely in what is similar to that' would have the <s>vipakṣa</s> (counter-instance) alone as its scope — that would be so only if there were restriction to another domain, and that [restriction] is by virtue of being in one sentence with it — thus there is the fault of mutual dependence.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
yathoddeśaṃ ca lakṣaṇāditi bhāvapadam /
lakṣaṇamāha ityanayormadhye itiḥ pūraṇīyaḥ /
atrāpītyapiśabdaḥ pratyakṣalakṣaṇopakṣayā /
nanu sādhyate 'neneti sādhanamityevāstu, saṃbhavati cāyamartho jñānasya karaṇatāyām, tasya prasiddhasādharmyasamutthatvādityata āha---tadetaditi /
na sāmānyātiriktaṃ sādṛśyam, anāśritasyānyāśrayatve dravyatvaprasaḍgāt, ananyāśritasyāpyayutasiddhobhayavyaḍgyatve samavāyatvaprasaḍgāt, gogavayādiyutasiddhaniṣṭhābhivyaktyanupapatteśca /
yutasiddhābhivyaḍgyatve 'bhāvatvaprasaḍgāt, ayutasiddhāvayavyavayavādiniṣṭhābhivyaktyanupapatteśca /
nityasyānekāśrayatve jātitvaprasaḍgāt ekāśrayatve tasya nāśe anāśrayasyāvasthānānupapatteḥ nityatve pramāṇābhāvaprasaḍgācca /
sāmānyaṃ hyekāśrayanāśe 'pi āśrayāntare tādrūpyeṇaiva
children.translated_text: 'And the definition in the order of enumeration' — this is a statement of fact. Between 'states the definition' and [the preceding], the word 'iti' should be supplied. The word 'api' (also) here is with reference to the definition of perception. Now, let [the meaning be] '<s>sādhana</s>' (means) in the sense of 'that by which [something] is established' — and this meaning is possible when cognition has instrumentality, since that [cognition] arises from well-known similarity — to this he says: 'that very...' Similarity is not something distinct from the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>); for if what is not based [in a substrate] were to have another substrate, there would be the consequence of its being a substance (<s>dravya</s>); and if what is not based in another were to be manifested through inseparable inherence in both [relata], there would be the consequence of its being <s>samavāya</s> (inherence); and because the manifestation through inseparably-connected [entities] such as cow and <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is impossible. If manifested through separably connected [entities], there would be the consequence of its being an absence (<s>abhāva</s>); and because manifestation through inseparably-connected wholes-and-parts is impossible. If eternal and residing in multiple substrates, there would be the consequence of its being a universal (<s>jāti</s>); if in a single substrate, upon the destruction of that [substrate], the impossibility of something without a substrate continuing to exist; and because there would be the consequence of lack of a means of knowledge for its eternality. For the universal, even upon the destruction of one substrate,

children.text:
pratyabhijñānāt nityamiti vyavasthāpyate /
idaṃ tu na tatheti kathaṃ nityamiti jñātavyam?
children.translated_text: is established as eternal because it is recognized in another substrate in exactly the same form. But this [similarity] is not like that — so how can it be known as eternal?

children.text:
pratyutānityaikāśrayatvādevānityatvamevānumīyate, nityaikavṛttitve tu svarūpasato viśeṣatvaprasaṃgāt /
sattāsato guṇatvāpatteḥ /
anityeṣu ca sadṛśavyavahārahānaprasaḍgāt, anityasya tvanekāśrayatve guṇavato dravyatvaprasaḍgāt ; nirguṇatve guṇatvaprasaḍgāt /
ekāśrayatve saṃyogavibhāgayoranapekṣakāraṇasya karmatvaprasaḍgāt /
tadviparītasya tu guṇatvaprasaḍgāt /
guṇeṣu ca karmasu ca sādṛśyavyavahāro na syāt, teṣāṃ samavāyikāraṇatvābhāvenānityadharmāyogāt /
āśrayasādṛśyena tadvyavahāropapattau visadṛśāśrayāṇāṃ guṇakarmaṇāṃ tadvyavahārānupapatteḥ, kāraṇatrayavicārānupapatteścetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the usage [of similarity] is justified through the similarity of the substrates, then for qualities and actions whose substrates are dissimilar, that usage would be unjustified — and [also because of] the impossibility of investigating the three types of causes — this is the meaning.

children.text: sādharmyaprasiddhirapi draṣṭavyeti /
children.translated_text: 'The establishment of similarity [through perception] should also be considered' — [he says].

children.text: sūtre sā ca karmadhārayasamāśrayeṇa /
children.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s>, that [establishment] is through a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional) compound.

children.text: ityāptavākyāditi vākyādārabhyaṃ pratyakṣaparyanteneti hṛdayam //
children.translated_text: 'From the reliable statement' — beginning from 'statement' and ending with 'perception' — this is the purport. //

On the contrary, from being resident in a single non-eternal [substrate], non-eternality alone is inferred; for if it were eternally resident in a single [substrate], there would be the consequence of its being a <s>viśeṣa</s> (ultimate differentiator) of an existent entity. There would be the consequence of being a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) for what lacks real existence. And among non-eternal [entities], the usage of similarity would be lost; but for a non-eternal [entity] residing in multiple substrates, if it possesses qualities, there would be the consequence of its being a substance (<s>dravya</s>); if devoid of qualities, there would be the consequence of its being a quality (<s>guṇa</s>). If in a single substrate, there would be the consequence of its being a <s>karma</s> (action), [since it would be] a cause requiring no reference to conjunction and disjunction. And of the opposite of that, there would be the consequence of its being a quality. And in qualities and actions, the usage of similarity would not apply, since they, lacking the status of inherent cause, are incapable of possessing non-eternal properties.

children.text:
prajñāpanīyasya gavayaśabdavācyatayeti vadatā atideśavākyasyākṛtasamayasaṃjñāsamabhivyāhāro darśitaḥ /
tathāpi karaṇavyutpattyā sādhanapadavyākhyānasya parityāge na kācidupapattirdarśitā, prajñāpanapadasyāpi karaṇavyutpattisaṃbhavādata
children.translated_text: By saying that [the wild ox] to be made known is denoted by the word '<s>gavaya</s>,' [the author] has shown the co-expression of the analogical statement with a convention-establishing designation. Even so, no justification has been shown for abandoning the explanation of the word '<s>sādhana</s>' (means) through instrumental derivation, since the word '<s>prajñāpana</s>' (making known) also admits instrumental derivation — therefore

children.text:
āha--piṇḍasya hīti /
pratyakṣāt sādṛśyāt prajānan tena prajñāpyata iti vadan sādṛśyasyaiva prajñāyamānasya kāraṇatvamabhipraiti /
tathā ca tena saha sādhyasādhanapadasya vyadhikaraṇatvādanyasya ca karaṇasyābhāvāt sādhyasādhanapadamanarthakamāpadyeta, yadi bhāvasādhanaṃ na syāt /
na ca tajjñānamevāstu karaṇamiti vācyam, avāntaravyāpāravirahiṇaḥ karaṇatvāyogāt /
asamīcīne 'pi sādṛśyajñāne tathābhāvaprasaḍgācca /
tadapi hi sādṛśyajñānameva /
pramāṇānuvṛttyā tannivṛttirityapi na vācyam, vṛttaireva padaiḥ samīhitasiddhāvanuvṛtteranavakāśāt /
sāpi hi granthavaicitryamāpādayantī padāntaravṛttireva /
children.translated_text: That [continuity] too, bringing about variety in the text, is merely the usage of different words.

children.text: tathāpi prajñānaṃ prasiddhipadārthona tu prajñāpanamityata āha---ityetadarthe /
children.translated_text: Even so, [one might say] '<s>prajñāna</s>' (cognition) is the established meaning, not '<s>prajñāpana</s>' (making known) — to this he says: 'for this purpose...'

children.text: pramāṇasya vyāpāro 'vyavadhānena phaloparaktā prātisvikī kriyā /
children.translated_text: The operation of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is an unmediated activity that is colored by the result and is specific [to each means].

children.text: jñāyamānasya sādṛśyasya karaṇatvamāviṣkartuṃ tasyānyatra acaritārthaḥ phalānuguṇo vyāpāro darśita iti tātparyār'thaḥ //
children.translated_text: In order to reveal the instrumentality of the similarity being cognized, its operation — purposeful and consonant with the result, not employed elsewhere — has been shown — this is the purport. //

he says: 'for of the individual...' One who cognizes through the similarity perceived directly, and says 'he is made known by that' — intends the causality of similarity itself, which is the thing being cognized. And thus, since the means-result expression is in a different grammatical case from that [similarity], and since there is no other instrument, the means-result expression would become meaningless unless it were a <s>bhāvasādhana</s> (action-noun). Nor should it be said 'let the cognition itself be the instrument,' because instrumentality is impossible without an intermediate operation. And because even in the case of incorrect similarity-cognition, the same [result] would follow — for that too is indeed similarity-cognition. Nor should it be said 'its cessation is through the continuity of valid cognition,' because when the words themselves in their [established] usage accomplish the desired [meaning], there is no scope for [additional] continuity.

children.text:
tatreti /
tātparyārthākṣarārthayoḥ /
lakṣyapadaṃ hi lakṣaṇavyavasthāpakaṃ na bhavati parasparāśrayatvamagatirveti doṣāt /
nanu upasthāpakamapītyāśayavānāśaḍkya dvitīyapadopādānatātparyamāha--yadyapīti /
nanvevaṃ sati prathamaivāstu, na ceyamaśokavanikā, tasyāḥ prathamatvādeva prathamaṃ buddhāvupanipātāt /
na sādhyasādhanapadena phalavācinā sāmānādhikaraṇyānupapatteḥ /
astu tarhi tadapi karaṇasādhanam /
evaṃ yata ityadhyāhārakaṣṭasṛṣṭirapi na syāt /
children.translated_text: In that case, the difficulty of supplying 'because' (<s>yataḥ</s>) by ellipsis would also not arise.

children.text: satyamevaitat, kintu phalābhāvenaiva hetunopamānasya prāmāṇyamapanīyate pareṇa /
children.translated_text: This is indeed true; however, precisely by the reason of the absence of a result, the validity of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) is taken away by the opponent.

children.text: tasmāt tadavabodhāya niṣkṛṣya phalamasya darśanīyamiti tathaiva sūcitavān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in order to make that [validity] understood, the result of this [means of knowledge] must be extracted and shown separately — and thus he has indicated it accordingly.

children.text: etaccāgre sphuṭamiti neha ṭīkākṛtā darśitam //
children.translated_text: And since this becomes clear later, the commentator (<s>ṭīkākṛt</s>) has not shown it here. //

'Therein' — of the purport and the literal meaning. For the object to be defined does not establish the definition — because of the fault that there would be mutual dependence and [logical] failure. Now, anticipating [the thought] 'but it serves as an indicator' — he states the purport of including the second term: 'although...' Now, if so, let it [simply] be the first [definition]; 'and this is not the <s>Aśokavanikā</s>' — because of its being first, it first falls upon the intellect. [But] because of the impossibility of co-referentiality with the means-result expression that denotes the fruit — [this is not feasible]. Then let that too be an instrument-means.

children.text: bhāṣyavārttikayoḥ virodhamāśaḍkyāha---vārtikakāreṇeti, tṛtīyāsamāsa ityupalakṣaṇam arthasiddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Anticipating a contradiction between the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and the <s>Vārttika</s>, he says: 'by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>...' — 'a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound with the third case-ending' is an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>); it should be seen that

children.text:
karmadhārayasamāso 'pi na nirasta iti draṣṭavyam, aviruddhatvāt /
prasiddhaṃ sādharmyaṃ yasyeti bahuvrīhāvapi karmadhārayārthasya praviṣṭatvāt /
evaṃ prasiddhena sādharmyamityatra tṛtīyātatpuruṣasya praveśād virodhāntaramāśaḍkyāha---bhāṣyakāreṇa hīti /
nāyamartho bhāṣyākṣarebhyaḥ śrūyata ityata āha---ākṣipreti /
praścānniṣkṛṣyābhidhānaṃ kṛtam, samayapratipatteḥ phalasya /
tadāha---samākhyeti /
tathāpi kimāyātaṃ vārttikavirodhasyetyata
children.translated_text: the <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional) compound too, being implied, is not excluded — because of non-contradiction. Since even in the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> 'that whose similarity is well-known,' the meaning of the <s>karmadhāraya</s> has entered. Thus, anticipating another contradiction in [the expression] 'through well-known similarity' where a third-case <s>tatpuruṣa</s> enters — he says: 'for by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>...' The objection that this meaning is not heard from the words of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — to this he says: 'by implication...' The extraction and statement was made from [what follows] afterward, since the result is the apprehension of the convention. To this he says: 'the designation...' Even so, what follows regarding the contradiction with the <s>Vārttika</s>? — to this

children.text: āha---etadeveti /
children.translated_text: he says: 'this very...'

children.text: pratipadyatāmayamityādiśaḍkottarārtha sūtroktaṃ karoti---prasiddhasādharmyādityatreti //
children.translated_text: 'Let him accept this' — and so on: he formulates what is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> for the purpose of answering the doubt. [He says:] 'in [the expression] from well-known similarity...' //

children.text:
atropamānasya phale vipratipadyamānān prati sāśaḍkaṃ jarannaiyāyikajayanta prabhṛtīnāṃ parihāramāha--yadyapīti /
saṃjñākarma saṃjñākaraṇam /
mānāntaraṃ śabdo vā śabdārtho vā liṅgabhūtaḥ /
tatra liṅgapakṣe, upalakṣitaḥ pratipāditaḥ /
śabdādavagatena gosādṛśyena pratipādyamānaḥ piṇḍa samānāsamānajātīyebhyo vyavacchinnaḥ śakyamavaganatumiti saṃbandhaḥ /
śabdapakṣe, tu gosādṛśyenopalakṣito viśiṣṭaḥ śabdādavagamyamānaḥ piṇḍaḥ samānāsamānajātīyebhyo vyavacchinnaḥ śakyo 'vagantum, guṇakarmādivat sādṛśyasyāpi samānasamānajītīyavyavacchedakatvāditi sugamam /
gosadṛśo gavayaśabdavācya iti tāvadastu /
atha gosadṛśa eva ka ityāśaḍkānivartanāsāmarthyamateḥ pariplavaḥ /
enamevārthaṃ kaścidityādinā darśitavān /
children.translated_text: This very point has been shown by someone through [the words] 'someone...' and so on.

children.text: tatreti /
children.translated_text: Therein —

children.text: tarhi viśiṣṭaiva pratipattirvākyādastu ityata āha---na ceti /
children.translated_text: Then let the qualified cognition arise from the sentence alone — to this he says: 'And not...'

children.text: pratyakṣamātrād bhaviṣyatītyata āha---na ceti //
children.translated_text: It will arise from perception alone — to this he says: 'And not...'

Here, with respect to those who disagree about the result of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy), he states with [raising] doubts the resolution of the old <s>Naiyāyikas</s> such as <s>Jayanta</s> and others: 'although...' '<s>Saṃjñākarma</s>' means the act of naming. '<s>Mānāntara</s>' (another means of knowledge) is a word or a word-meaning that serves as a mark (<s>liṅga</s>). In the view that it is a mark: 'indicated' means 'established.' The individual (<s>piṇḍa</s>), being established through the similarity with a cow known from verbal testimony, can be discriminated from things both of the same and of different classes — this is the connection. In the view that it is a word: the individual, indicated — i.e., qualified — by similarity with a cow, being understood from verbal testimony, can be discriminated from things both of the same and of different classes — [this is] easily [understood], since similarity, like quality and action, also serves to discriminate from things of the same and different classes. Let it be granted that [the wild ox] is 'similar to a cow and denoted by the word gavaya.' But then, [when one asks] 'which one exactly is similar to a cow?' — the inability [of this doctrine] to remove the doubt shows the vacillation of the position.

children.text:
etena vākyapratyakṣasamāhāro 'pi nirastaḥ /
sa hi pramāṇasamāhāro vā syāt, phalasamāhāro vā? ādye 'pi pramāṇatve sati samāhāraḥ, samāhṛtayorvā prāmāṇyamiti? na tāvat prathamaḥ, phalānekatve sati samāhārānupapatteḥ,
children.translated_text: By this, the combination of sentence and perception is also refuted. For would that be a combination of <s>pramāṇas</s> or a combination of results? In the first case too, is the combination when they are [already] <s>pramāṇas</s>, or does their being <s>pramāṇas</s> arise from the combination? Not the first, because when the result is multiple, a combination is untenable,

children.text:
tasyaikaphalaṃ prati parasparādhipatyarūpatvāt /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, vākyapratyakṣayorbhinnakālatvāt /
vākyatadarthayoḥ smṛtidvāropanītāvapi gavayapiṇḍasaṃbaddhenāpīndriyādinā tadgatasādṛśyānupanaye samayaparicchedāsiddheḥ /
phalasamāhāre tu tadantarbhāve 'numānaśabdayorapi pratyakṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
tat kiṃ tatphalasya tatpramāṇabahirbhāva eva, antarbhāve vā kiyatī sīmā? tattadasādhāraṇendriyādisāhityam /
asti tarhi sādṛśyādijñānakāle 'pi vistāritasya cakṣuṣo vyāpāraḥ? na, tasmin sati
children.translated_text: since the combination takes the form of mutual dominance with respect to a single result. Nor the second, since the sentence and perception occur at different times. Even when the sentence, its meaning, and the subject are brought together through the door of memory, if similarity pertaining to the individual connected with the <s>gavaya</s> is not conveyed through the sense-organ and the like, the determination of the convention is not established. But in the case of a combination of results, if that [result of analogy] is included within [perception and sentence], there would follow the consequence that inference and verbal testimony too would be perception.

children.text: tasyānupayogāt /
upalabdhagosādṛśyaviśiṣṭagavayapiṇḍasya vākyasmṛtimataḥ kālāntare 'pyanusandhānabalāt samayaparicchedopapattiriti /
children.translated_text: One who possesses the memory of the sentence, regarding a <s>gavaya</s> individual qualified by the perceived similarity to a cow, even at a later time can determine the convention by the force of connecting the two — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadetat jarannaiyāyikamatamāskandati---nanviti /
children.translated_text: He challenges the view of the older <s>Naiyāyikas</s>: 'But...'

children.text: pūrve hi yathā gaustathetyeva vākyaṃ gavayapadenāpratītasamayenāpi prayogamātropayoginā sahitaṃ saṃbandhapratipattihetuḥ, pratisaṃbandhinastu śabdād vopalakṣaṇād vopasthāpanamityāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: For the earlier [Naiyāyikas] hold that the sentence 'like a cow' (<s>yathā gaus tathā</s>) itself, combined with the <s>gavaya</s> word whose convention is not yet understood — being useful merely for the application [of the word] — is the cause of the cognition of the relation. But the presentation of the correlative is either from the word or from an indicatory mark — so they say.

children.text: ādhunikāstu pratisaṃbandhyupasthitiḥ pūrvavadeva, samayaparicchedastu prayogānumānādityāhuḥ //
children.translated_text: The more recent [Naiyāyikas], however, say: the presentation of the correlative is as before, but the determination of the convention is from the inference of application.
because of its being useless in that case.

children.text: avācakaprayogasya vākyānaṅgatayeti tadvirahiṇaśca saṃbandhyupalakṣaṇaparyavasānāditi manyamānā etadeva
children.translated_text: Considering that the application of a non-denotative [word], not being a component of the sentence, and [the view of] one who lacks it ending in the indicatory mark of the correlative —

children.text:
prayogamāropya darśayanti---yo hīti /
etenaiva pariplavo nirastaḥ /
yadi hi saṃbandho viditaḥ, kaḥ pariplavārthaḥ? atha na vidita iti tatrākāḍkṣānuvṛtterevamucyata iti cet--tadapyayuktam /
children.translated_text: For if the relation is known, what is the purpose of the doubt? But if it is not known, and one says 'Thus it is said because the expectation continues there' — that too is untenable.

children.text: na hi viśeṣaniṣṭhaḥ samayaḥ, tathā satyaśakyagrahatvāt, api tu kiñcit nimittīkṛtya deśakālādiviśeṣavinākṛtavyaktimātraniṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the convention does not pertain to a particular [individual], since if so, it would be impossible to grasp. Rather, it pertains to a mere individual stripped of specific distinctions of place, time, and the like, on the basis of some ground.

children.text: tadeva nimittaṃ nāvagatamiti cet? avagatireva tarhi saṃndhasya saṃbandhino 'navagamāditi kiṃ pariplutaṃ pramātuḥ? na caiṣa paramārthaḥ, sādṛśyaviśiṣṭapiṇḍopakṣepe nimittasyāpyupakṣepāt /
children.translated_text: If one says: 'That very ground has not been understood' — then the understanding is simply of the relation, and from the non-understanding of the correlative, what is it that confuses the knower? Nor is this the ultimate truth, because when the individual qualified by similarity is presented, the ground too is presented.

children.text: anyathā piṇḍopakṣepe 'pi nimittānupakṣepe manodharmādiśabdānāṃ jātiśabdatvaṃ na syāt, avācakatvameva vā syāt, tajjātīyānāṃ nityaparokṣatvāditi //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, even when the individual is presented but the ground is not, words like <s>manodharma</s> and the like would not be class-words, or they would simply be non-denotative — since things of that class are always imperceptible.
they display this very argument by setting it up: 'For whoever...' By this very argument, the doubt [about the convention] is also removed.

children.text:
atrocyate abhinavanaiyāyikaiḥ, pañcadhā hi vācyavācakabhāvavyavasthā /
nimittopalakṣaṇarahite śṛṅgagrāhikayā caitramaitravat /
nirnimitte 'ntarbhūtopalakṣaṇe nirvacanikayā pācakādiśabdavat /
nirnimitta eva taṭasthopalakṣaṇe paribhāṣaṇikayā ākāśādiśabdavat /
sanimitte taṭasthopalakṣaṇa evaṃprakārikayā pṛthivyādivat /
viśeṣavannimitte nimittasaṃḍkocanikayā svargādivaditi /
tatra prathamadvitīyayorasaṃbhāvitatvādiha viditavṛttāntatayā tṛtīyaṃ prakāraṃ nirasya pañcamaścaturthamupayātīti caturthaṃ vyavasthāpayati---na tāvaditi /
aviditagavayaśabdavṛttāntasya tu yad bhaviṣyati, tadanantarameva vakṣyati /
tadidamuktamiti /
paramārtho vastugatiḥ /
tataśca tathābhūta eva piṇḍe saṃbandho grāhyo,
children.translated_text: Here the more recent <s>Naiyāyikas</s> say: the arrangement of denotation and denotative capacity is fivefold. Without ground or indicatory mark, it is horn-grasping — like <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Maitra</s> [proper names]. Without ground but with an included indicatory mark, it is etymological — like the words <s>pācaka</s> (cook) and the like. Without ground, with an external indicatory mark, it is conventional — like the words <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the like. With ground and external indicatory mark, it is of-such-a-type — like <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth) and the like. With a ground possessing a particular, it is by narrowing the ground — like <s>svarga</s> (heaven) and the like. Of these, since the first and second are inapplicable here, and since the knower of the background [already knows], rejecting the third type, the fifth having approached the fourth, he establishes the fourth: 'Not to begin with...' But what will happen for one who does not know the background of the <s>gavaya</s> word — that he will state immediately after. This is what was stated. 'The ultimate truth' means the real state of affairs. And therefore the relation is to be grasped precisely in such an individual,

children.text: na tu sādṛśyopalakṣaṇopanīte piṇḍamātra ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: not in the mere individual brought about through the indicatory mark of similarity — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu nimittamapyavagatamityata āha---na ceti /
na ca gosādṛśyenopalakṣyata iti upalakṣaṇamanumāpanam, smāraṇaṃ vā /
ubhayamapyadṛṣṭasaṃbandhe 'nupapannam /
smaraṇamātrāpekṣayā daṇḍapuruṣodāharaṇam /
etāvadeva ca syāt /
yaduta
children.translated_text: Now, even the ground has been understood — to this he says: 'And not...' And the fact that it is indicated by similarity to a cow is [the question of whether this] indicatory mark [provides] inference or memory. Both are untenable when the relation is not [previously] seen. The example of the man-with-a-staff is in respect of the requirement of mere memory alone. And this much alone would follow: namely,

children.text:
gavayaśabdo vā gavayatvaṃ gamayet, yathā gauḥ tathā gavaya iti /
śabdārtho vānumāpayet avyabhicārapakṣe /
vyabhicārapakṣe tu smārayediti /
nanu sādṛśyameva jātibhedamanantarbhāvya pratyetuṃ na śakyam, tasya bhinnapradhānasāmānyavyaktiguṇāvayavakarmasāmānyabāhulyarūpatvāt /
tasmāt sādṛśayathātathādiśabdā eva tasya pratyāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, words like 'similarity,' 'such-as,' and the like are the conveyors of that.

children.text: kevalaṃ prasiddhāprasiddhasandeho 'vāśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: Only the doubt between familiar and unfamiliar [classes] remains.

children.text: tatra hastitvādikaṃ gośabdena nirastam /
children.translated_text: There, elephant-ness and the like are excluded by the word 'cow.'

children.text: mahiṣatvādikaṃ tu anucitaviṣayatayā, anyathopamānasvīkāre 'pyapratīkārāt //
children.translated_text: But buffalo-ness and the like — since [the analogy] has an unsuitable object, even upon accepting analogy, there is no remedy.

the <s>gavaya</s> word would convey <s>gavaya</s>-ness, [as understood from] 'as a cow, so a <s>gavaya</s>.' Or the meaning of the word would be inferred — on the view of non-deviation. On the view of deviation, however, it would merely remind. Now, similarity cannot be cognized without including a difference of class, since similarity has the form of abundance of commonalities in universal, particular, substance, quality, part, and action belonging to different principal categories.

children.text:
tadayaṃ gosadṛśa ityasyārthaḥ /
goto bhinnajātīyaḥ, tadgataguṇāvayavādisāmānyabāhulyavāniti /
naitadapi sādhīyaḥ, darpaṇa iva candraḥ, candra iva mukham mukhamivāravindam, ado 'ravindamivedamaravindamiti caturdhā sādṛśyagatau bhinnapradhānasāmānyaniyamāyogena tadanantarbhāvyaiva sādṛśyapratipattyupapatteḥ /
kvacid dṛṣṭamiha smaryeta tāvaditi cet? smaryatāṃ tāvadatrāvagatam, na tviha tadavagatamiti brūmaḥ /
tasmād gosāmānyenopalakṣyamāṇaḥ piṇḍaḥ kiṃ tadvāneva gavayaśabdasya vācyo bhavatu? pacikriyayopalakṣyamāṇaḥ karteva pācakaśabdasya, āhosvit taṭasthameva gosādṛśyam, tadupalakṣita eva piṇḍa ākāśavat tasya vācyo bhavet? kiṃ vopalakṣaṇaṃ vihāya gandhāpalakṣitapṛthivītvajātimāniva gosādṛśyopalakṣitajātiviśeṣavāneva piṇḍo 'sya vācyo bhaviṣyatītaraniyatakoṭisaṃśayatiraskāreṇa koṭitrayāvalambī sandeha eva jarannaiyāyikairūpaplutaḥ saṃbandhapariccheda ityucyate, etāsvavaśyamanyatamā koṭirgavayapadārtho bhaviṣyatīti nirdhāraṇasaṃbhāvanāṃ hṛdi nidhāya /
aitena manodharmādipratibandigrahaḥ pratyuktaḥ /
tatrāpyanumānenonnīyamānānāṃ manovyaktīnāṃ samānaguṇatayā samānārthakriyākāritayā
children.translated_text: This then is the meaning of 'similar to a cow': of a different class from a cow, possessing an abundance of commonalities in quality, part, and the like pertaining to it. Even this is not more reliable, because in the fourfold cognition of similarity — 'the moon is like a mirror,' 'the face is like the moon,' 'the face is like a lotus,' 'that lotus is like this lotus' — there is no invariable restriction to principal categories of different kinds, and therefore similarity can be cognized without including them. If one says: 'What was seen somewhere would at least be remembered here' — let it be remembered then, but we say: it has been understood here, not that it has been understood there. Therefore, the individual indicated by the universal of cow — is it this very individual that is the denotatum of the <s>gavaya</s> word, possessing that [universal]? — like the agent indicated by the cooking-action is the denotatum of the word <s>pācaka</s>. Or is the cow-similarity merely external, and the individual indicated by it, like space, is its denotatum? Or, leaving aside the indicatory mark, will the individual possessing the specific class indicated by cow-similarity, like earth indicated by odor-possession, be its denotatum? — this three-pronged doubt, obscuring the definite alternatives, is what the older <s>Naiyāyikas</s> call the determination of the relation as confused. It is held in the heart that necessarily one of these alternatives will be the denotatum of the <s>gavaya</s> word. By this, the counter-argument regarding <s>manodharma</s> and the like is also answered. Even there, of mental instances inferred by inference, possessing the same qualities, causing the same purposive action,

children.text: samānajātīyatvānumānāt /
children.translated_text: from the inference of their being of the same class.

children.text: sāmānyānavagatau tu tatrāpyaśakya eva samayagrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: But without the universal being known, even there the grasp of the convention is impossible.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vā na tasya pravṛttinimittamiti //
children.translated_text: Or the universal is not the ground of its application.

children.text:
tadidamuktam--sarvathānupalabdheriti /
yadyapi gavayatvāvagame 'pi saṃjñāsaṃjñisaṃbandhānavagame tatra prayujyamānatvāditi heturasiddha eva /
na hyasati vṛttyantare tadviṣayatayā prayogaḥ saṅgatimavijñāya jñātuṃ śakayate, prāgeva pramāṇāntarāt tadavagame tu kimanumānena sādhanīyam? ata eva pratyakṣe 'pi gavaye anumānamanavakāśameva /
tathāpi saṃbandhyavagame gavayapadasamabhivyāhṛtaṃ vākyameva saṃbandhaṃ bodhayiṣyati /
avācakasyāpi ca samabhivyāhāra upayokṣyate upamānapakṣa iva /
tadapi hyatideśavākyaṃ
children.translated_text: This is what was stated: 'Because of non-apprehension in every way...' Although, even when <s>gavaya</s>-ness is known, since the relation of name and named is not known, the reason 'because it is being used there' is unestablished. For without another usage, it is not possible to know the usage with respect to that object without knowing the convention. Much less when it is known from another <s>pramāṇa</s> — and then what is to be proved by inference? For this very reason, even when there is a perceptible <s>gavaya</s>, inference has no scope. Nevertheless, when the correlative is not known, the sentence combined with the <s>gavaya</s> word itself will convey the relation. And the co-occurrence of even a non-denotative [word] will be useful, just as in the analogy view. For that too is an extension-sentence

children.text: vākyameveti matvā tannirāsārthaṃ saṃbandhina evāpratipattirūpapāditā //
children.translated_text: — thinking it is merely a sentence, in order to refute it, the non-cognition of the correlative itself has been established.

children.text:
ata evāha---kuto vākyād veti /
ata eva vākyasya vyāptiparatāpi nirākṛtā, saṃbandhino 'navagamāt /
na ca vyatireke tātparyam, saṃketayiturabhiprāyopādhikatvāt, satpratipakṣatvācceti /
yadyapi vinigamanāyāṃ hetvabhāve 'pi nopamānasya kācit kṣatiḥ, ubhayorapi vācyatve saṃbandhasya tadānīmavadhāraṇāt, tathāpi vastugati vivecayati---tathāpi
children.translated_text: For this very reason he says: 'How from a sentence...' For this very reason, the sentence's having invariable concomitance as its purport is also refuted, due to the non-understanding of the correlative. Nor is the purport the negative concomitance, because it is conditional on the intention of the one who establishes the convention, and because it has a valid counter-argument. Although in the determination, even without a reason, analogy suffers no harm — since, when both are denotata, the relation is ascertained at that time — nevertheless, he discriminates the real state of affairs: 'Even so,

children.text:
kim ityādi tadanujānāti ityantaṃ karabhavṛttāntam /
pariharati---sādhyarmyagrahaṇaṃ ceti /
upalakṣaṇapadaprayogaścāvāntarabhedasaṃsūcanāya teneyaṃ sūtragatiḥ /
prasiddhasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanamupamānam /
children.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> (analogy) is the means of proving what is to be proved through similarity with what is well known.

children.text: sa ca prasiddho dharmaḥ samānaḥ pratiyogitayā tadupakṣipto 'samānaśceti /
children.translated_text: And that well-known property, being common, presents as its correlative what is uncommon as well.

children.text: bahuvrīhipakṣe tu prasiddhadharmaṇa iti /
children.translated_text: On the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> reading: 'of what has a well-known property.'

children.text: śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
children.translated_text: The rest is as before.

what...' and so forth up to 'he concedes that' — the account of the young camel. He replies: 'And the grasp of the similarity with the probandum...' And the use of the word 'indicatory mark' is to hint at the internal distinction. Thus this is the purport of the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text:
jaranmīmāṃsakamataṃ gosādṛśyaṃ gavayasthaṃ pratyakṣameveti vadatā nirastam /
śābaramatamāśaḍkya nirācaṣṭe--gosthāmiti /
jātyantaravarti jātyantarasyeti prāyovādaḥ /
tathāpi gavayavyaktyavacchinnasya na govyaktyavacchedo 'vagataḥ, tatropamānamavatariṣyatītyata āha--tasmād yatheti /
dṛṣṭānte tātparyam /
children.translated_text: The purport is in the illustrative example.

children.text: prayogastvityādi /
children.translated_text: 'But the argument...' and so forth.

children.text: akṛtasamayasaṃjñāsamānādhikaraṇavākyārthopadhānaṃ pramāṇavailakṣaṇyamiha draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: What is to be seen here as the distinctiveness of the <s>pramāṇa</s> is: the presentation of the meaning of the sentence co-referential with the name whose convention has not been made.

children.text: viṣayasvarūpavailakṣaṇyayorasiddhatvādati //6 //
children.translated_text: Because the distinctiveness of the nature of the object has not been established.

The view of the older <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, who say that the cow-similarity residing in the <s>gavaya</s> is perceived directly, is refuted. He raises and explains the <s>Śābara</s> view: 'Cow-form...' 'A universal of a different class residing in [what belongs to] another class' — this is stated in an approximate sense. Even so, the delimitation of the <s>gavaya</s> individual as delimited by the cow-individual is not known — analogy will be introduced for that — to this he says: 'Therefore, just as...'

children.text: // pariśuddhi //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification).

children.text:
iha śabde trividhā vipratipattiḥ---prāmāṇyato, bhedato, lakṣaṇataśceti /
tatra prathamaḥ kalpo vacanavirodhādeva nirastaḥ, tatprāmāṇyamanabhyupagamya vivakṣitārthasya pratipādayitumaśakyatvāt ; pratipādane vā tata eva tatprāmāṇyasiddheriti /
bhedastu parīkṣāparvaṇi nirūpaṇīyaḥ, leśatastvihāpi /
vyāvartakadharmayogādeva bhedavyavahāro 'pi /
children.translated_text: The practical usage of distinctness too arises from the possession of distinguishing properties.

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ ca tathā /
children.translated_text: And the definition likewise.

children.text: tataḥ tadeva vivecanīyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that alone is to be discriminated.

children.text: tatra vipratipadyamānaṃ prati tu parīkṣāvatāra ityāśayavān siddhavat saṅgatibhāṣyaṃ vyākhyāya lakṣaṇamavatārayati---atheti //
children.translated_text: But the introduction to examination is directed toward one who disagrees — with this intention, having explained the <s>bhāṣya</s> on connection as if established, he introduces the definition: 'Now...'

Here, regarding verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), there is a threefold disagreement: regarding its validity, regarding its distinctness [from other <s>pramāṇas</s>], and regarding its definition. Among these, the first alternative is refuted by self-contradiction alone — since without accepting its validity, the intended meaning cannot be communicated; or, if communicated, its validity is established from that very fact. The distinctness, however, is to be examined at the stage of examination, though to some extent here too.

children.text:
tatra samayabalena samyakparokṣānubhavasādhanaṃ śabda iti eke /
iha cādyena padenānumānam, dvitīyena śabdābhāsaḥ, tṛtīyena savikalpakapratyakṣam, caturthena padārthasmaraṇam, pañcamena kartṛkarmaṇī nirasyete /
apare tu
children.translated_text: There, some say: verbal testimony is that which, by the force of convention, is the means of correct indirect experience. Here, by the first word [convention], inference is excluded; by the second, pseudo-verbal testimony is excluded; by the third, determinate perception is excluded; by the fourth, the recollection of word-meanings is excluded; by the fifth, the agent and the object are excluded. But others,

children.text: ceṣṭāyāmapi gatametadityativyāpakaṃ mattvā śabdatvasamavāye satītyāhuḥ //
children.translated_text: considering that this applies even to gesture, and thus is over-extensive, say: 'when there is inherence of sound-ness.'

children.text:
atra prācayānāmayamāśayaḥ /
yadi ceṣṭā na prāmāṇam, aprasaṅga eva tasyāḥ, kiṃ śabdatvasamavāye satītyanena nirvartanīyam? pramāṇaṃ cet tasyāḥ pratyakṣādyanantarbhāve pañcamapramāṇābhyupagamaprasaṅgaḥ /
tasmāt śabda eva ceṣṭāyāḥ praveśaḥ samayabalapravṛtteḥ /
śabda eva tu śabdavyavahāro laukikaḥ prāyikatvāt, cākṣuṣe jñānadarśanavyavahāravaditi /
te 'pi sthūladṛśvānaḥ /
ceṣṭā hyabhiprāyasthaśabdasmaraṇamātropayoginī lipivat /
śabda eva tu ceṣṭotpāditasmaraṇasamārūḍhaḥ pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: But it is the word itself, mounted upon the memory produced by the gesture, that is the <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: arthena ca smṛtyutpādanāt śabdaviṣayam evāsyāḥ prāmāṇyam, pramāṇaphalasya pramāṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: And since the memory is generated by the [word-]meaning, its validity pertains to the domain of the word alone, since the result of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is itself a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: na ca smṛtirasyāḥ avāntaravyāpāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And memory is not a subsidiary operation of this [gesture].

children.text: yadi ceṣṭopadhānamantareṇāvagato 'pi śabdo nārthaṃ gamayedevamapi saṃbhavet, na caitadasti //
children.translated_text: If even a word understood without the intermediary of gesture does not convey the meaning — then this [gesture being a pramana] might be tenable. But this is not the case.

Here the intention of the earlier [Naiyāyikas] is as follows. If gesture is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, it is simply irrelevant — what is to be accomplished by 'when there is inherence of sound-ness'? If it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, and is not included under perception and the like, there would follow the consequence of accepting a fifth <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, gesture enters into verbal testimony alone, since its operation is by the force of convention. But the common usage of 'verbal testimony' applies to verbal sound alone — since it is predominant, just as the common usage of 'cognition' and 'seeing' applies to the visual. They too are coarse-sighted. For gesture is useful merely for reminding of the word present in the mind, like script.

children.text:
nanvevaṃ sati ceṣṭayā eḍamūkavyavahārānupapattiḥ, na hyasau tataḥ śabdasmṛtimān, agṛhītasamayatvāditi cet? ---ata eva taṃ prati samayabalena śabdavadarthe 'pi ceṣṭāyāḥ kuṇṭhatvameva /
vyavahārastu anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ niyataviṣayāvinābhāvagrahe pravṛttinimittaupayikaḥ, abhiprāyānumānādeva eḍamūkasya, karituragayoḥ
children.translated_text: Now, if so, then practical usage through gestures by mutes and deaf-mutes would be unjustified, for such a person does not have the recollection of words from gestures, due to not having learned the conventions — if [this is objected] — for this very reason, the incapacity of gesture with respect to meaning, like words, is established through the force of convention for such a person. Practical usage, however — when, through agreement in presence and absence, the invariable concomitance with a specific object is grasped — is useful as a ground for activity, [and arises] for the mute through the inference of intention alone, just as for a horse or elephant

children.text: kaśāḍkuśābhighātādiva /
children.translated_text: through the blow of a whip or goad.

children.text: atha kṛtasamayāpi ceṣṭaiva kiṃ na syāt, avinābhāvābhāvāt? smārayatu vā padārthān, tathāpi na pramāṇam //
children.translated_text: Now, why should even gesture for which the convention has been made not [be a <s>pramāṇa</s>], since there is no invariable concomitance [between gesture and meaning]? Or let it recall word-meanings — even so, it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text:
dvividhā hi sā samayapramārabhedāt---kṛtyanvayinī, jñaptyanvayinī ca /
tatra kṛtyanvayinī prayojakābhiprāyaṃ smārayantī pravartayati, na tu kiñcit pramāṇayati śaḍkhadhvanivat /
ato 'pramāṇameva /
jñaptyanvayinī tu kārakeṣu pratipadikārthapradhānā, kriyāsu vartamānārthapradhānā /
tathā ca gauraśvaḥ puruṣa ityādipadairiva svatantreṣu padārtheṣu smāriteṣu parasparānvayayogaḥ /
padaikadeśavibhaktiviśeṣavat ceṣṭaikadeśaviśeṣāt prakaraṇādiviśeṣād vā kārakādismṛtiniyama iti cet---ceṣṭaikadeśaviśeṣābhāvāt /
na hyatītānāgatavartamānapākādipratipādakaṃ ceṣṭaikadeśaviśeṣaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
prakaraṇādayastu viṣayaviśeṣe śabdān niyamayanti, na tu kārakakālaviśeṣeṣu pravartayanti /
tathātve vā gauraśvaḥ puruṣo hastītyādāvapi karmatvādīnyunnīya vivakṣitārthāvasāyaḥ syāt /
na hi ceṣṭākalāpe prakaraṇādayaḥ
children.translated_text: For gesture is of two kinds, due to the difference between action-based and knowledge-based conventions: action-accompanying and cognition-accompanying. Of these, the action-accompanying [gesture], by recalling the intention of the instigator, prompts [action], but does not validate anything — like the sound of a conch-shell. Therefore it is simply not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. The cognition-accompanying [gesture], however, is primarily about the meaning of the nominal stem in the case of factors of action (<s>kārakas</s>), and primarily about the meaning of the present [tense] in the case of actions. And thus, just as when independent word-meanings are recalled through words like 'cow,' 'horse,' 'person,' their mutual syntactic connection [is established]. If [one says] 'just as there is restriction of the recollection of <s>kāraka</s> and the like through a specific part of a gesture, from a specific part of the gesture, like a specific inflectional ending in a word-part, or from a specific contextual feature' — [the reply is:] because there is no specific part of a gesture [that does this]. For we do not see a specific part of a gesture that communicates past, future, present cooking and the like. And context and the like restrict words to a specific object, but they do not cause them to operate with respect to specific <s>kāraka</s> and temporal features. Or if they did, then even in 'cow, horse, person, elephant,' by inferring the object-case and the like, the ascertainment of the intended meaning would follow. For in the collection of gestures, context and the like

children.text: kārakaviśeṣādīnākṣeptumalam, na tu padakadambka ityasti niyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: are not capable of extracting specific <s>kāraka</s> features — but it is not the case that only the collection of words [can do this] — there is no such restriction.

children.text: tathā ca kālasaṃkhyākārakaviśeṣapratipādakavibhaktisamabhivyāhāravaiyarthyaprasaṅgaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, the absurd consequence would be the pointlessness of the co-utterance of inflectional endings that convey specific tense, number, and <s>kāraka</s> features.

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi tato vyavahāraviśeṣāḥ? saṃśayapratibhayoranyatarasmād viśeṣānupalambhe vidūravartini samānadharmiṇi sthāṇvarthina iveti /
children.translated_text: How then [are there] specific practical usages from [gestures]? From one or the other of doubt and intuitive flash — when the specific [meaning] is not apprehended — in the case of a similar instance at a distance, like one who desires a post — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasmādubhayathāpi ceṣṭā na pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in both ways, gesture is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: ataḥ kasya caturṣu praveśāpraveśau cintanīyau? etacca saṃbhāvitaprāmāṇyam aitihyādyantarbhāvayatā ceṣṭāpabhraṃśalipidhvanipadaikadeśān sāvyavahārikānapyakīrtayatā sūtrakṛtā sūcitamapi mandamatayo na gṛhṇantīti tadanukampayā lakṣaṇaṃ vyācakṣāṇa eva kiñcidudbhāvayati //
children.translated_text: Therefore, whose inclusion in or exclusion from the four [<s>pramāṇas</s>] is to be considered? Even this, [namely] the inclusion of what has plausible <s>pramāṇa</s>-status — such as tradition (<s>aitihya</s>) and the like — [within the four], while not mentioning gesture, corrupt texts, script, phonemes, and word-parts as having conventional status — [all this] was indicated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> himself, but dull-witted persons do not grasp it. Therefore, out of compassion for them, while explaining the definition, he brings out something [more].

children.text:
vākyajñānaṃ tadarthajñānaṃ veti /
ākāḍkṣāyogyatāsattimatpadakadambakaṃ vākyam /
tasya jñānaṃ jñānamānaṃ tadityarthaḥ /
yathāśrutamuttaratra /
kiṃ tu tatrāpi vākyameva pradhānam, asādhāraṇatvādindriyādivat /
sannidhitāratamyavivecane tu sarvasminnayaṃ nyāyaḥ /
hānādibuddhiḥ parāmarśalakṣaṇā, itarasyā anumānaphalatvāt /
tadanena nirākāḍkṣāyogyānāsannāni padāni nirasyātā ceṣṭādayo 'pi nirastā bhavantīti vijātīyavyudāsaḥ /
svārthadvārakaṃ cākāḍkṣādikamiti saṃgatigrahapadapratisandhānatadarthasmaraṇayogyatādyanusandhānaprakaraṇādikamuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: And [the fact that] expectancy and the like operate through [the medium of] one's own meaning — [this shows that] syntactic connection, word-connection, recollection of their meanings, fitness-investigation, context, and the like have been stated.

children.text: anenaivābhiprāyeṇoktam---padārthasmṛtyādayastviti /
children.translated_text: With precisely this intention it is said: 'But the recollection of word-meanings and the like...'

children.text: tadanena pratyakṣādeḥ samānajātīyasya vyudāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, the exclusion of what is of the same kind — from perception and the like — [is accomplished].

children.text: anāptavacasāṃ cāptagrahaṇena nirākaraṇamiti sāmānyalakṣaṇalābhaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the refutation of the words of non-authoritative persons through the mention of 'authoritative' — [thus] the general definition is obtained.

'The cognition of a sentence, or the cognition of its meaning' — a collection of words possessing expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>), and contiguity (<s>sannidhi</s>) is a sentence. The cognition thereof — [i.e.,] the <s>pramāṇa</s> is the cognition — that is the meaning of 'that.' As literally stated, [this applies] subsequently [in the text]. But therein too, the sentence itself is primary, due to being the uncommon [cause], like the sense-organ and the like. In the discernment of the degree of proximity, however, this principle applies throughout. The cognition of what is to be abandoned and the like has the nature of reflective consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>), since the other [i.e., the cognition of sentence-meaning] is the result of inference. By this, having rejected words that lack expectancy, fitness, and contiguity, gestures and the like too are rejected — this is the exclusion of what is of a different kind.

children.text: nanu nāyamupadeśaśabdasyārtho yathāśruti cāvyāpakatā siddhārthāsaṃgrahādivadityata āha---yadyapīti /
children.translated_text: Now, this is not the meaning of the word '<s>upadeśa</s>' (instruction), and as literally [taken] there is under-extension, since it fails to include established truths and the like — therefore he says: 'Even though...'

children.text: na kevalaṃ bhūtārthāsaṃgrahaḥ sādhyārthamapi na kiñcit saṃgṛhṇātītyāha---yadyapi ceti /
children.translated_text: Not only does it fail to include established truths — it does not include anything having the status of what is to be proved either — he says: 'And even though...'

children.text: nanu pravartakatvena vidherājñādhyeṣaṇayoḥ ko viśeṣaḥ, yenānayorūpadeśapadenāsaṃgraha ityatastābhyāṃ vidhervaidharmyaṃ pratipādya tayorapi tato vaidharmyamuktam---te hīti /
children.translated_text: Now, what is the difference between injunction on the one hand, and command and request on the other, in terms of prompting [action], such that these [latter two] are not included under the term '<s>upadeśa</s>'? — Therefore, having shown the dissimilarity of injunction from those two, the dissimilarity of those two from that [injunction] is also stated: 'For they...'

children.text: tat kimājñādhyeṣaṇāsaṃgrahe 'pi prayatnaḥ kartavyaḥ? netyāha---tathāpīti //
children.translated_text: Then, should effort be made even for the non-inclusion of command and request? He says 'no': 'Nevertheless...'

children.text:
ayamāśayaḥ /
yadyapi lakṣaṇayā te api saṃgrahītuṃ śakyete parasthāne prayoktṛpadaṃ prakṣipya, tathāpi nāstyasmākaṃ tadasaṃgrahe 'pi kācit prayojanakṣatiḥ, svargāpavargopāyaviṣayasya śabdaviśeṣasya lakṣaṇārambhāt śāstrasya tadadhikāreṇa pravṛtteḥ /
sāmānyalakṣaṇe tvakṛte viśeṣalakṣaṇānavatāra ityataḥ prathamaṃ tathaiva vyākhyātam /
vakṣyati ca
children.translated_text: The intention is this: although those two could also be included through secondary usage by inserting the term 'agent' in the place of 'another [person],' nevertheless, even if they are not included, there is no loss of purpose for us — because the definition-effort is for a specific kind of verbal [testimony] pertaining to the means to heaven and liberation, and because the <s>śāstra</s> proceeds under the jurisdiction of that. But without the general definition being made, the specific definition cannot be introduced — therefore, it was first explained in just that way. And he will say

children.text:
dignāganirākaraṇaprastāve /
parapadamapahāya prayojanavānityeva vākyārthapratipattiḥ phalamiti ca lākṣaṇikapadaprayogasya cāyamevopayogo yadubhayalakṣaṇalābhaḥ /
prayojanamarthagatamasādhāraṇaṃ grāhyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The purpose pertains to the object, is uncommon, and is to be grasped.

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ tu śabdasya svārthapratipādakatvam /
children.translated_text: But what is common is the word's capacity to convey its own meaning.

children.text: tacca parasyaiva /
children.translated_text: And that belongs to the 'other [person]' alone.

children.text: tataḥ tadapekṣayā pareti viśeṣaṇamanarthakaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: Therefore, with reference to that [common purpose], the qualifier 'another [person]' would be meaningless.

in the context of refuting <s>Dignāga</s>. Having removed the word 'another [person],' the sentential meaning-apprehension that 'it is purposeful' is the fruit — and this alone is the use of employing the term with secondary meaning, namely the obtaining of both definitions.

children.text:
nanu yadi upaniṣadaḥ prayojanavatyaḥ, nūnaṃ kañcidarthaṃ pratipādayantyaḥ kvacit paraṃ pravartayeyuḥ pravṛttyaḍkitatvāt prayojanasadbhāvasya /
na cet paraṃ pravartayeyuḥ kathaṃ paraprayojanavattyaḥ pravṛttivirahāḍkitatvāt prayojanābhāvasyetyata āha---yadyapīti /
na kvacidityādau sākṣāditi śeṣaḥ /
