buddharṣabhādīnāmanāptatve kārako heturmāyāmohanimittatvam /
jñāpakastu pramāṇāviruddhasarvadharmakṣaṇikanairātmyādivacanam /
yathāśrutaṃ bhāṣyamavyāpakaṃ manvāna āha---sudṛḍheneti /
children.translated_text: Considering the <s>Bhāṣya</s> as literally stated to be under-extending, he says: 'By a firmly-established...'

children.text: sudṛḍhaṃ parito nirastavibhramāśaṅkam pramāṇaṃ pramā /
children.translated_text: 'Firmly-established' — a <s>pramāṇa</s> that is free from the suspicion of error on all sides is a <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition).

children.text: tathāvadhāritā viṣayīkṛtā iti /
children.translated_text: 'Thus ascertained' means 'made the object [of cognition].'

children.text: neyaṃ nityānityavyāptimabhisandhāya //
children.translated_text: This is not with the intention of the pervasion between permanent and impermanent.

Now, if the <s>Upaniṣads</s> are purposeful, they must, by conveying some meaning, prompt someone to act — because the existence of purpose is marked by activity. And if they do not prompt another to act, how are they purposeful for another — because the absence of purpose is marked by the absence of activity — therefore he says: 'Even though...' In 'not anywhere' and so forth, the completion is: 'directly.' Regarding the non-authoritativeness of <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, and the like: the producing cause is [their] being the basis of deception and delusion. And the indicating [cause] is [their] statements such as 'all <s>dharmas</s> are momentary,' 'non-self,' and the like, which are contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text:
nanu kāraṇamadhitiṣṭhata eveśvarasyāpi kartṛtvam /
tathā ca sthānakaraṇādīnāmanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ varṇanipatti prati sāmarthyāvagamāt, tadadhiṣṭhānaśūnyatayā tasya nāgamakartṛtvaṃ bhavet /
na ca śarīramantareṇa tasya
children.translated_text: Now, even <s>Īśvara</s>'s (God's) agent-hood [in authoring scripture] is [exercised] only while presiding over [material] causes. And thus, since the capacity of the articulatory organs — tongue, palate, and the like — for producing phonemes is understood through agreement in presence and absence, his authorship of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) would not obtain, due to the absence of the presiding over those [articulatory organs]. And without a body, there is no possibility of his [having]

children.text: sthānakaraṇādisaṃbhavaḥ, teṣāṃ tālvādivivṛtādirūpatvādityāśayavānāśaṅkate---tathāpīti /
children.translated_text: articulatory organs, tongue-opening, and the like — since these are of the form of palatal opening and the like — with this intention he raises the objection: 'Nevertheless...'

children.text: bhāṣyamuttarayati---ata āha upadeṣṭeti //
children.translated_text: He answers the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'Therefore he says: the instructor...'

children.text: na vayamasya bhagavataḥ kāryaviśeṣeṇānuvihitabhāvābhāvatayopakaraṇaṃ śarīraṃ nirākurmaḥ, tryaṇukādiniṣpattaye dvyaṇukādivaccharīrānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyikāryaniṣpattaye tadupagrahasyāpīṣyamāṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: We do not deny a body for this Blessed One — as an instrument, whose existence and non-existence conform to specific effects — since, for the production of triads of atoms and the like, the acceptance of his taking up [a body] for the production of effects conforming to the presence and absence [of conditions], like dyads of atoms and the like, is also desired.

children.text: api tvāyatanatayā kartṛtvanirvāhakatayā vyāpakatayā ca tat tasya neṣyate bhogābhāvāt, kartṛtvasya nityatvāt, kāryasya kartrā nirūpādhisaṃbandhāt, śarīrasyavyabhicārāccetyabhiprāyavato vivaraṇam---sthānakaraṇeti /
children.translated_text: But that [body] is not accepted for him as a locus [of the self], as what accomplishes agent-hood, as what pervades [him], or as [his] body — because of the absence of enjoyment, because of the permanence of agent-hood, because of the unconditional relation of the effect with the agent, and because of the non-deviation of the body — the explanation with this intention: 'articulatory organs...'

children.text: tadevaṃ rūpa āptaḥ kutaḥ pramāṇāt niścetavyaḥ, paracittavṛttīnāmapratyakṣatvāt? kāyavāgvyāpārayośca buddhipūrvakam, anyathāpi saṃbhavādityāśaḍkya mlecchā api hītyādinā bhāṣyatātparyaṃ bruvāṇaḥ tanniścayopāyamapi leśato darśayati---hetudarśanaśūnyā iti //
children.translated_text: Thus, from what <s>pramāṇa</s> is an authoritative person (<s>āpta</s>) of such a form to be ascertained, since the mental states of others are not perceptible? And since both bodily and verbal activity could be preceded by cognition, since it is possible otherwise too — anticipating this doubt, while stating the purport of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [beginning with] 'Even <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians)...,' he also indicates in brief the means for ascertaining that: 'Devoid of the perception of a motive...'

children.text:
ayamāśayaḥ /
dvividho hi puruṣo 'sarvajñaḥ sarvajñaśceti /
tatra pūrvasya tāvat sattvaprasādhakādeva pramāṇād rāgadveṣamohavirahasiddhāvanāptatvaṃ nirastam /
uttarasyāpi jñānecchāprayatnasthānakaraṇapāṭavāni tāvadupadeśamātreṇaiva niścīyanta iti
children.translated_text: The intention is this: a person is of two kinds — non-omniscient and omniscient. Of the former, to begin with, from the very <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes his existence (<s>sattva</s>), upon establishing the absence of passion, aversion, and delusion, non-authoritativeness is removed. And of the latter too, knowledge, desire, effort, and the skill of articulatory organs are ascertained even through mere instruction alone —

children.text:
tatra sarveṣāmavivāda eva /
jñānaṃ tu yathārthamayathārthaṃ vā syāt /
icchāpi pratipipādayiṣā vipralipsā vā syāditi sandeho 'vaśiṣyate /
tatrāpyabhyāsadaśāpanne 'yamartho 'syeti sāmānyato niścaye bhavatyeva tajjñānasya yathārthatvaniścayaḥ, yathābhyāsadaśāpannamidamaraṇyamamīṣāṃ mlecchānāmataḥ asminnete mārgāmārgavibhāgajñā iti pānthānāmevaṃ niścayaḥ /
vipralipsā ca hetudarśanena vyāptā hetau sati syāt /

sa ca dvirūpaḥ, svopakāraḥ paropakāro vā? tatra tāvat pāntheṣu vimārgeṇa pratiṣṭhamāneṣu mlecchādīnāṃ na kaścit svopakāraḥ, svasya gṛhītatvāt śarīramātrasya ca karaṇīyāntarābhāvāt, bhāve vā aparityāgāt /
children.translated_text: And that [motive] is of two kinds: self-benefit and benefit to another. Of these, to begin with, there is no self-benefit for the barbarians and the like when travelers are stranded on the wrong path — because they themselves are already established [in the forest], and because the mere body has no other task [to perform], or because even if there were, [the body's resources] would not be abandoned.

children.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ, na hyanunmattā anapakāriṇamapakurvate /
children.translated_text: Nor the second, for those who are not insane do not harm one who has not harmed [them].

children.text: nāpi parāpakāramātraṃ puruṣārthaḥ tathā sati sarvaḥ sarvamapakuryādityevaṃ vipralipsāpi nivāryate /
children.translated_text: Nor is mere harm to another a human goal — otherwise, everyone would harm everyone. Thus, even the desire to deceive is precluded.

children.text: anabhyāsadaśāpannaviṣaye tu pravṛttisāmarthyāt pramāṇāntarasaṃvādād vā mohavipralipsayornivṛttiriti //
children.translated_text: And in a domain that has not reached the stage of repeated practice, the removal of delusion and the desire to deceive [is established] through the capacity to generate [correct] activity, or through concordance with other <s>pramāṇas</s>.

therein, there is no dispute among all [parties]. But the question remains whether his knowledge is veridical or non-veridical, and whether his desire is a desire to communicate or a desire to deceive. Therein too, when the subject has reached the stage of repeated practice — when the general ascertainment 'this is the meaning of this' [has been made] — there indeed arises the ascertainment of the veridicality of his knowledge, just as when [the matter] has reached the stage of repeated practice — 'this is a forest of these barbarians; from this, they are knowledgeable about the distinction between paths and non-paths' — thus arises the ascertainment of travelers. And the desire to deceive is pervaded by the perception of a motive — [it] would exist when there is a motive.

children.text:
mlecchā apyāptā bhavanti yataḥ pratītigocarāḥ, tataḥ kaḥ sandeho mahādhiyām āryāṇāṃ ca tattvāvadhāraṇa iti apiśabdārthaḥ /
etena yad yena rūpeṇa na niścitam, na tat tena vyavahriyate, yathā rathyāpuruṣaḥ sarvajñatvena, na pratīyate cābhimataḥ puruṣa āptatveneti vyāpakānupalabdherasiddhatvamuktam /
pareṣām avyāpakamāptalakṣaṇam, yathāśrutasyāryamlecchayoḥ abhāvāt /
viśeṣaṇāntaraprakṣepe tvasmallakṣaṇābhyupagama ityarthaḥ /
viparyastasyāyaṃ praśnaḥ, viparyāsaśca pramāṇābhāsamūlaḥ /
children.translated_text: This question belongs to one who is confused, and the confusion is rooted in pseudo-<s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: atastamāha---astīti /
children.translated_text: Therefore he states that: 'There is...'

children.text: bhāgāsiddhatāmāśaḍkyāha---atra yāvatīti /
children.translated_text: Anticipating the partial unestablishedness [of the reason], he says: 'To the extent that here...'

children.text: nanu paraprayogamadūṣayitvā svātantryeṇa prayogāntaropādānaṃ prakaraṇasamājātiḥ, satpratipakṣatayā cet svargādīnāṃ pratyakṣatvaṃ kutaḥ setsyatītyata āha---yogaje tviti //
children.translated_text: Now, without refuting the opponent's formulation, taking up another formulation independently constitutes the fallacy of context-shifting (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>); and if [the opponent's reason] has a counter-proof — from where will the perceptuality of heaven and the like be established? — therefore he says: 'But in <s>yogaja</s> (yoga-born [perception])...'

Since even barbarians are authoritative persons because they are the objects of cognition — therefore, what doubt [can there be] about the ascertainment of reality by the great-minded noble ones (<s>āryas</s>)? — this is the meaning of the word '<s>api</s>' (even). By this, the following is stated as unestablished due to non-apprehension of the pervader: 'What is not ascertained in a certain form is not used in that form — just as a person on the street [is not used] as omniscient; and the person in question is not cognized as authoritative.' The opponents' definition of the authoritative person is under-extending, because of the [non-applicability] of the literal [definition] to both <s>āryas</s> and barbarians. But if another qualifier is inserted, then it becomes an acceptance of our definition — that is the meaning.

children.text: hetvabhāve phalābhāvāt pramāṇe 'sati na pramā,
children.translated_text: 'In the absence of a cause, there is absence of the effect; in the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is no valid cognition;

children.text: cakṣurādyukta viṣayaṃ paratantraṃ bahirmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: the external mind, dependent [on sense-organs], is conjoined with the objects of the eye and the like.' //

children.text: iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasmādāpātatastāvat satpratipakṣā evaite hetava ityata āha---asmākaṃ tu sabhyañca iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, at first sight, these reasons have counter-proofs — therefore he says: 'But for us, and [what is] fit for an assembly...'

children.text:
ayamāśayaḥ, dṛśyate hi tāvad bahirandriyoparame 'pyasannihitadeśakālārthasākṣātkāraḥ svapne /
na ca vācyaṃ smṛtirevāsau paṭīyasīti /
na hi smaraṇānubhavavibhāge api sākṣī praṣṭavyaḥ /
kiṃ tarhi? idaṃ smarāmīdamanubhavāmīti pratītyā svasākṣiko 'yam arthaḥ /
na cāropitaṃ tatrānubhavatvam--abādhānāt, smṛtitvānullekhanāt anupalabdhasya svaśiraścchedāderavabhāsanācca /
smṛtiviparyāso 'sāviti cet? yadi smṛtiviṣaye viparyāsa ityarthaḥ, tadānumanyāmahe /
atha smṛtāvevāyamanubhavatvaviparyāsa ityarthaḥ, tadā prāgeva nirastaḥ /
children.translated_text: But if the meaning is that this is an error of taking [mere] memory as experience, then that has been refuted already.

children.text: na ca saṃbhavatyapi, na hyanyenākāreṇa vyavasāyaviṣayībhūto 'yamartho 'nyena jñānāvacchedakatayānuvyavasīyate /
children.translated_text: Nor is it possible [that memory be taken as experience], for what has become the object of determination (<s>vyavasāya</s>) with one form is not reflectively apprehended (<s>anuvyavasīyate</s>) as delimited by cognition of another [form].

children.text: tathā ca sa ghaṭa ityutpannāyāṃ smṛtau bhrāmyatastaṃ ghaṭamanubhavāmīti syāt, na tvimaṃ ghaṭam, na hyayaṃ ghaṭa iti smṛterākāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, when the memory 'that was a pot' has arisen, one who is deluded would think 'I am experiencing that pot' — but not 'this pot'; for the form of memory is not 'this is a pot.'

children.text: tasmādanubhava evāsau svīkartavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, that [yogic cognition] must be accepted as experience itself.

The intention is this: for we do observe the direct realization of objects not present in place and time even when the external sense-organs have ceased, in dreams. Nor should one say that [dream-cognition] is merely a vivid memory. For even in the distinction between memory and experience, one should not ask for a further witness. What then? 'I remember this, I experience this' — this matter is self-witnessed through such cognitions. And the character of being an experience is not superimposed there — because of non-sublation, because memory-character is not traced [in it], and because of the appearance of things not [previously] apprehended, such as the cutting of one's own head and the like. If [one says] 'that is an error of memory' — if the meaning is that there is error in the object of memory, we agree.

children.text:
asti ca svapnānubhavasyāpi kasyacit satyatvam, saṃvādāt /
tacca kākatālīyamapi na nirhetukam, sarvasvapnajñānānāmapi tathātvaprasaḍgāt /
hetuścātra dharma eva /
sa ca karmajavad yogajo 'pi yogavidheravaseyaḥ, karmayogavidhyostulyogakṣematvāt /
children.translated_text: And that, like what arises from <s>karma</s>, is to be understood as arising from <s>yoga</s> too, through the injunction of <s>yoga</s> — since the status of <s>karma</s> and the injunction of <s>yoga</s> is equal.

children.text: tasmād yogināmanubhavo dharmajatvāt pramā, sākṣātkāripramātvāt pratyakṣaphalam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the experience of <s>yogins</s>, because it arises from <s>dharma</s>, is valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>); and because of being a valid cognition of the directly-apprehending type, it has perception as its result.

children.text: dharmājanakabhāvanāprabhavastu na prameti vibhāga iti /
children.translated_text: But what arises from meditation that does not generate <s>dharma</s> is not valid cognition — this is the distinction.

children.text: tatsāmagrīrahitatvādityasiddho heturiti sūktam //
children.translated_text: The reason 'because of lacking that causal aggregate' is unestablished — this has been well stated.

And there is some truth even in the experience of dreams, because of correspondence [with reality]. And even if accidental, that [correspondence] is not without a cause — for if it were, there would follow the consequence that all dream-cognitions would be equally [true or false]. And the cause here is <s>dharma</s> (merit) alone.

children.text: asmākaṃ tu sabhyañca iti bahavaśceti anvācaye cakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: But for us, the <s>ca</s>-particle in 'and among the assembly' and 'and many' is in the sense of inclusion.

children.text: yadyapi cāsmākaṃ paramasarvajñasiddhāvavāntarasarvajñe na sidhyatyapi na kācit prakṛtahāniḥ, tathāpi tatsadbhāve api pramāṇasadbhāvāt so 'pi nopekṣāmarhatīti //
children.translated_text: And although, for us, when the supreme omniscient is established, even if the intermediate omniscient is not established, there is no loss to the topic at hand, nevertheless, since there is evidence for the existence of even that [intermediate omniscient], he too should not be disregarded.

children.text:
iha dignāgena bhāvasādhanatvakarmasādhanatvābhyāmupadeśapadaṃ vikalpya dūṣitam karaṇasādhanatvapakṣastvasmadamito 'pi kuta upekṣita ityata āha---anyasmādanyasyeti /
arthena hi sākṣāt pratibandhaḥ pratyakṣasyaiva, paramparāpratibandho 'numānasya /
tadasya śābdasya vijñānasya sākṣādarthapratibandhe pratyakṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ, paramparāpratibandhe tvanumānatvāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, if this verbal cognition were directly connected with the object, there would follow the consequence of its being perception; but if indirectly connected, the consequence of its being inference.

children.text: apratibandhe tvaprāmāṇyameva ityasaṃbhava eva karaṇavyutpattipakṣasyeti manyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if not connected at all, it would simply not be a valid means of knowledge — thus the causation-interpretation of <s>karaṇa</s>-derivation is simply impossible — this is what he thinks, this is the meaning.

children.text: atra bhāvavyutpattipakṣe āptatvaniścayaḥ śabdaphalam, taddvārā vākyārthaniścayo vā /
children.translated_text: Here, on the existence-derivation interpretation, the certainty of the speaker's trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) is the result of verbal testimony, or alternatively, the certainty of the sentence-meaning through that.

children.text: nanvāptatvena niścitānāṃ kimaparamavisaṃvāditvamavaśiṣyate, yanniśceyamityata āha---upadeṣṭadṛṣṭṭṭaṇāmityartha iti //
children.translated_text: Now, once the trustworthiness of the [speakers] has been ascertained, what further non-deceptiveness remains to be ascertained? To this he says: the meaning is 'of those seen by the teacher.'

Here, <s>Dignāga</s> has analyzed the term 'instruction' (<s>upadeśa</s>) into 'being an instrument of bringing into existence' and 'being an instrument of action,' and has refuted [both]. But the alternative of 'being an instrument of causation' has been neglected even by our own side — why? To this he says: 'of one from another.' For perception alone has a direct connection with the object; inference has an indirect connection.

children.text:
arthasya sākṣātkāraḥ pratyakṣatvamiti varṇayojanā /
tenāyamarthaḥ /
āptopadeśaḥ tasminnevāpte niścayaṃ kurvan
children.translated_text: The direct apprehension of the object — that is perceptuality. This is the construction of the words. Therefore this is the meaning: the instruction of a trustworthy person, generating certainty regarding that very trustworthy person,

children.text:
śabdaḥ pramāṇam, atha vā āpte niścayaṃ kṛtvā tatsahāyo vākyārthaniścayaṃ janayannityubhayaṃ dūṣayatītyāha--imamiti /
anumānātkarūṇābhyāsahetudarśanaśūnyatvādeḥ karmasādhanatvapakṣamutthāpayati--dvitīyamiti /
atrāpyupadarśitārthaprāptiniścayaḥ, taddvārā arthatathātvaniścayo vā śabdasya phalam /
tatra prathamaṃ darśayati---yasmāditi /
dvitīyaṃ darśiyati---evaṃ ceti /
upadiśyamānor'thaḥ prāptaḥ, prāptatvena niścito yasmāditi vā /
tathātvena niścita iti vā sūtrayojanā, ubhayamapi
children.translated_text: is a <s>pramāṇa</s> as verbal testimony; or, having generated certainty regarding the trustworthy person, generating certainty of sentence-meaning with that [certainty] as an aid — he refutes both: 'this.' He raises the action-derivation interpretation from inference through observing the absence of causes such as practice of compassion: 'the second.' Here too, the result of verbal testimony is either the certainty of the attainment of the indicated meaning, or through that, the certainty of the truth of the meaning. Of these, he shows the first: 'because.' He shows the second: 'and thus.' The construction of the <s>sūtra</s> is either: 'the indicated meaning has been attained, because it is ascertained as attained' — or: 'ascertained as being in that state.' He refutes both,

children.text: dūṣayatītyāha---dūṣayatīti //
children.translated_text: he says: 'he refutes.'

children.text: nanvarthaprāptyā arthatathātvaṃ niścīyamānaṃ liṅgabhūtayaiva niścīyate /
children.translated_text: Now, the truth of the meaning, being ascertained through the attainment of the meaning, is ascertained by that very [attainment] which is the inferential mark.

children.text: tat kathamāha pratyekṣeṇetyata āha---āptyā hīti /
children.translated_text: Then how does he say 'by perception'? To this he says: 'for by attainment.'

children.text: āptiniścaye 'pi śabdasya vyāpāro nāstīti darśayitumarthatathātvaniścayo 'pi pratyakṣeṇetyuktam, mūlabhūtatvāt tasyetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: In order to show that even in the ascertainment of trustworthiness, verbal testimony has no function, even the ascertainment of the truth of the meaning is said to be 'by perception' — since that [perception] is foundational, this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu śabdopalabdhasyārthasya kvacidanumānemāpi pratipattirastītyata uktam--prāyeṇeti /
atra cobhayorapi pakṣayorāptoktatvapravṛttisāmarthyahetupradhānayoḥ śabdasya prāmāṇyaniścayaḥ phalamiti śaḍkitumucitamapi na śaḍkitam, prāmāṇyaniścayāvinābhūtatvāt arthaniścayatattathātvaniścayayoḥ, tasya tayorevāntarbhūtatvāditi manyamāneneti /
tamimamiti /
children.translated_text: 'that very' —

children.text: nāptatvasahāyo nāptatvaniścayasahāya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: not aided by trustworthiness, not aided by the certainty of trustworthiness.

children.text: prāptyā /
children.translated_text: Through attainment.

children.text: prāptiniścayenetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: through the certainty of attainment.

Now, even of the meaning learned from words, there is sometimes understanding through inference too — to this it was said: 'mostly.' And here, for both alternatives — where the certainty of the validity of verbal testimony is the result, principally through the trustworthy-speaker's utterance and the capacity for activity as reasons — it would have been appropriate to doubt [this], but no doubt was raised — since the certainty of the object and its truth are invariably accompanied by the certainty of validity, and since the latter is subsumed under the former — thinking thus,

children.text:
nanvanabhyupagatebhyaḥ pakṣebhyo na kañcidabhyupagatasya viśeṣaṃ paśyāma ityata āha---etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
nāptatvahetukaṃ nāptatvaniścayahetukam /
avisaṃvāditvam avisaṃvāditvaniścayaḥ /
anena sūtreṇāgamārthatayā āgamaphalatayā pratipādyate /
nāpyarthatathātvamarthatathātvaniścaya iti neyam /
upalakṣaṇatayā ca vidhādvayamudāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: And two modes have been illustrated by way of indication.

children.text: yathā tu pūrvapakṣe vyākhyātam, tathātrāpi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: And as it was explained in the prima facie view, so too it should be understood here.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi phalamasyetyata āha--kiṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: What then is the result of this? To this he says: 'but what.'

children.text: anenollekhenānuvyavasāyena ya pratipattirviṣayīkriyate setyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the cognition that is objectified by this tracing, by this retrospective determination.

Now, we do not see any distinction of what is accepted from the unaccepted alternatives — to this he says: 'this is what is stated.' Not caused by trustworthiness, not caused by the certainty of trustworthiness. Non-deceptiveness — the certainty of non-deceptiveness. By this <s>sūtra</s>, it is taught as the meaning and as the result of <s>āgama</s> (scripture). And this should not be construed as: 'not the truth of the meaning, not the certainty of the truth of the meaning.'

children.text:
yadyevaṃ tarhi kkāptoktatvaniścaya upayujyata ityata āha---āptatvaṃ ceti /
āptoktatvaṃ cetyarthaḥ /
nanu prāmāṇyamarthāvyabhicāraḥ /
sa khalu kathamarthamapratyāyya pratyāyayituṃ śakyet? tataśca punarāptoktatvenārthaniścaya āyāta ityata āha---na ca yata iti /
prameyamiti svātantryeṇeti śeṣaḥ /
avacchedakatayā tu tasyāpi sphuraṇamiṣyata eva,
children.translated_text: If so, then where is the certainty of trustworthy-utterance useful? To this he says: 'and trustworthiness.' The meaning is: 'and trustworthy-utterance.' Now, validity means non-deviation from the object. How can that be made known without first making the object known? And so the ascertainment of the object through trustworthy-utterance has come again — to this he says: 'and not because.' 'As knowable' — the remainder is: 'independently.' But as a delimiting factor, its appearance too is accepted,

children.text: manasaiva /
children.translated_text: by the mind alone.

children.text: ghaṭasyetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: of the pot.

children.text:
tadayaṃ saṃkṣepaḥ /
bhūtārthopadeśakatvaṃ hi prāmāṇyam /
tadeva prameyamanupadarśayataḥ śabdasya na syāt /
children.translated_text: A word that does not present the very object to be known would not have that [validity].

children.text: tathānāptoktatvenāpi hetunā kiṃ niścīyeta? tathā ca kasyāvacchedakatayā artho 'pi parisphuret? tasmād yathā sattāmātrāvasthitairaduṣṭairindriyaiḥ pratyakṣaṃ janyate, jātāduṣṭatvaistu pramāṇatayā niścīyate, tathā sattāmātrāvasthitenāptena pramāṇaṃ śabdo janyate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, by the reason 'not being uttered by a trustworthy person' either, what would be ascertained? And so, as a delimiting factor of what, would the object too become manifest? Therefore, just as perception is generated by non-defective sense-organs established merely in existence, and is ascertained as a <s>pramāṇa</s> through the ascertainment of the non-defectiveness of its birth, so too verbal testimony as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is generated by a trustworthy person established merely in existence.

children.text: jñātāptatvena tūpadeṣṭrā tathātvena niścīyata iti pratyakṣavat svaviṣaye vyavastheti jñānamātramanumāpayet /
children.translated_text: But by the instructor whose trustworthiness has been ascertained, it is ascertained as having that nature — and thus, like perception, being settled in its own domain, it should indicate merely cognition.

children.text: avyutpannamiva vyutpannamapīti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The remainder is: even the learned, just like the unlearned.
This then is the summary: the validity [of verbal testimony] is the capacity to instruct about real things.

children.text:
ayamāśayaḥ /
asti tāvad vākyādarthaviśeṣāvasāya ityavivādam /
na cāyaṃ laiḍgikaḥ, vacanamātrasyānaikāntikatvāt, āptoktatvasya prāgevāsiddheḥ /
na ca vacanasya liṅgatvapakṣe sādhyamapyasti /
tathā hi, na tāvat tādātmyatatprāptī saṃbhavataḥ /
nāpi tadutpattiḥ, āptavacasāmapyatītānāgatagocarāṇāṃ paramparayāpyarthādanutpatteḥ /
tasmādarthajñāpakatvameva śabdānāmarthavattvam /
na ca tadevānumeyam, tasya svātantryeṇa bhavadbhiranabhyupagamāt /
abhyupagame vā vivādavicchedāt /
na ca liṅgasya svātmano laiḍgikajñānajanakatvamevānumeyam, tasya liḍgāntaraviṣayatvāt /
children.translated_text: And the very capacity of the inferential mark to generate inferential cognition from its own nature is not what is to be inferred — since that belongs to the domain of another inferential mark.

children.text: tasmād vacanamātraliṅgapakṣe yad vacanaṃ tad buddhipūrvakamityudāharaṇīyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, on the view that mere utterance is the inferential mark, what is to be cited as an example is: 'whatever is an utterance is preceded by cognition.'

children.text: buddhistu kiñcidullikhantī jāyata iti svabhāvādevollekhyamātrapratilambhaḥ, na tu tatrāpi bhūtābhūtavibhāgo, na tu tarāṃ prakāravibhāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: But cognition, arising as it does while suggesting something, [arises] from its very nature — and thus there is obtainment of the mere object of suggestion. But even therein there is no distinction of true and false, much less a distinction of mode.

children.text: tasmāt jñānamātramanumāpayediti sūktam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it should indicate merely cognition — this has been well stated.

This is the intention: to begin with, it is undisputed that from a sentence there is a determination of a specific meaning. And this is not inferential — since mere utterance is inconclusive, and since trustworthy-utterance is previously unestablished. Nor, on the view that utterance is an inferential mark, is there even a <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). For, to begin with, neither identity nor attainment [of the object by the word] is possible. Nor is the production of that [object] — since even the words of trustworthy persons, whose scope includes the past and the future, do not produce the object, even indirectly. Therefore, the meaningfulness of words is their very capacity to indicate the object. And that very [meaningfulness] is not what is to be inferred — since it is not accepted by you as existing independently. Or if accepted, the dispute is settled.

children.text:
kimato yadyevamityata āha---tathā ceti /
vyavahārānubhavābhyāṃ vyavasthāpitāpi nānurodhitā syāt /
vyutpattiprayāsavaiyarthyaprasaṅgaścetyarthaḥ /
nanu jñānaviśeṣādevārthaviśeṣaḥ setsyatītyata āha---na ceti /
jñānenārthaḥ sādhayitavyaḥ /
tasya ca na kaścid viśeṣor'thāhitākārādilakṣaṇaḥ samasti /
children.translated_text: And there is no specific feature of that [cognition] — characterized by the form imposed by the object and the like — that would obtain.

children.text: sākāratve 'pyatītānāgatādigocarasya tasyārthādanutpatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if [cognition] has form, that [cognition], which pertains to past and future objects and the like, is not produced from the object.

children.text: tasmādullekhyatayārtha eva viśeṣo vaktavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the specific feature must be stated as being in the very object, as what is suggested.

children.text: sa cet jñānasiddhāvantarbhūtaḥ kimaparaṃ tena sādhanīyam? na cedantarbhūtaḥ punarapyaviśiṣṭameva jñānamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: If that is subsumed in the establishment of cognition, what more is to be established by it? If not subsumed, then the cognition is undifferentiated as before — this is the meaning.

What follows from this? To this he says: 'and thus.' Even what has been established by both practical usage and experience would not be accommodated. And there would follow the consequence of the fruitlessness of the labor of linguistic derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>) — this is the meaning. Now, from a specific cognition alone, a specific object will be established — to this he says: 'and not.' The object is to be established through cognition.

children.text:
syādetat /
tajjñānasiddhyarnbhata evārtho 'vacchedakatayā sidhyatu /
yadyapi vacanamātramarthaviśeṣollekhi
children.translated_text: One might say: let the object be established as a delimiting factor in the very course of establishing that cognition. Although mere utterance, [while] suggesting a specific object,

children.text:
jñānapūrvakatāṃ vyabhicarati, tathāpi yaḥ padakadambakaviśeṣo yatpadārthajātaṃ smārayati, sa tatsaṃsargajñānapūrvaka ityasti niyamaḥ /
evaṃ ca samayagrahasyāpyupayoga iti cet---na, gauraśvaḥ puruṣa ityādipadakambakena vyabhicārāt /
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvenāvasthitau na vyabhicaratīti cet? so 'yaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo na tāvat svarūpataḥ, padānāṃ parasparaṃ svātantryāt /
nāpyarthataḥ, tasyānavagamāt /
avagame vā kastato 'paraḥ padārthānāṃ saṃsargo, yo jñānāvacchedakatayā anumātumiṣṭaḥ? ākāṅkṣādimattve satīti viśeṣaṇānna vyabhicāra iti cet? atha keyamākāṅkṣā? na tāvadavinābhāvaḥ svarūpator'thataśca, tasyā abhāve 'pi
children.translated_text: deviates from being preceded by cognition, nevertheless, a specific cluster of words that causes the recollection of a specific set of word-meanings — that is preceded by the cognition of their connection — there is a restriction. And thus, the grasping of convention too has its use — if so, no: because of deviation by the word-cluster 'cow, horse, man,' and the like. If one says 'it does not deviate when established in the relation of qualifier and qualified' — this qualifier-qualified relation, to begin with, is not by the intrinsic nature [of the words], since words are mutually independent. Nor from the meaning, since that has not been apprehended. Or, if apprehended, what further connection of word-meanings is there beyond that, which is desired to be inferred as a delimiting factor of cognition? If one says 'no deviation when syntactic expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) and the like obtain' — what then is this expectancy? It is not, to begin with, invariable co-occurrence, either intrinsically or from the meaning — since even in its absence,

children.text: vākyārthapratipatteḥ /
children.translated_text: the apprehension of sentence-meaning [occurs].

children.text: bhāve 'pyapratīteḥ, vākyārthapratipādanena vināparyavasānamākāṅkṣeti cet? evaṃ tarhi vākyārthaviśeṣapratipādakaṃ yat padakadambakam, tat tatsmāritārthasaṃsargajñānapūrvakamiti prayogārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And even in its presence, non-apprehension [occurs]. If one says 'expectancy means [the state of] not terminating without the communication of sentence-meaning' — then the meaning of the argument is: a cluster of words that communicates a specific sentence-meaning is preceded by the cognition of the connection of the meanings recalled by it.

children.text: tathā ca prāgeva sādhyaviśeṣasiddhaye hetuviśeṣasiddhimicchatā vākyādeva vākyārthaviśeṣapratyaya eṣitavya ityupasaṃharannāha---tasmāditi //
children.translated_text: And thus, since one who wishes to establish a specific reason for establishing a specific <s>sādhya</s> must seek the specific cognition of sentence-meaning from the sentence itself — concluding, he says: 'therefore.'

children.text:
syādetat /
tathāpyasaṃbaddhasya prakāśakatve 'tiprasaṅga ityata āha---na ceti nanu na hi saṃbandha ityeva gamako 'tiprasaḍgāt api tvavinābhāva eva /
sa ca śabdasyārthena nāstītyata āha---na cāvineti /
yat tvatroktam, cakṣurapi rūpakāryatvādeva rūpaṃ prakāśayatīti, tadayuktam /
yadi hi tatkṛtatvādeva tad gamayet, rūpamiva rasādīnapi gamayet /
avanābhāvajñānaṃ vā apekṣeta /
na hyavinābhāvasyaiṣa mahimā yadayaṃ sattāmātreṇaiva gamayati /
tathātve vā dhūmādapi cakṣuṣa iva sattāmātrāvasthitādevāgniḥ pratīyeta /
api ca jñānasamasamayo vārthaḥ prakāśate, anantarasamayo vā /
tasmācca na cakṣuṣo janma, svakāraṇādevāyamasya svabhāvabhedalābho yadanātmānamapyakāraṇamapi kāraṇatvāviśeṣe 'pi vā rūpamevājñātameva satprakāśayatīti rūpolabdhilakṣaṇakāryadarśanabalenaiva tadvyavasthāpyate /
tasyāśakyāpahnavatvāditi cet? tarhi yasya yatra pratibandho nāsti, na tasya tatra prāmāṇyam, yathā dahane 'pratibaddhasya rāsabhasyeti vyāpakānupalabdhistvayaivānaikāntikī kṛtā /
kimasmābhiratra vaktavyam? kiṃnibandhanastarhi pramāṇavyavahāraḥ śabde, yannibandhanaścakṣurādiṣu /
tatraiva kiṃ nibandhana iti cet? idaṃ mahāpāṇḍityaṃ yat siddhamātṛkāyāmapyadyāpi sandehaḥ /
bhūtārthānubhavajanananibandhano hi pramāṇavyavahāraḥ sarvatreti bālo 'pyāha /
tabdalenaiva śabdasyāpi tadanuguṇaḥ sa
children.translated_text: One might say: even so, if what is unconnected can illuminate, there is over-extension — to this he says: 'and not.' Now, it is not the case that connection alone is the indicator — because of over-extension. Rather, invariable co-occurrence alone [is the indicator]. And that does not exist between the word and the object — to this he says: 'and not invariable co-occurrence.' As for what was stated here — that even the eye illuminates form only because it is an effect of form — that is incorrect. For if it indicated [form] merely because it is produced by that, it would indicate taste and the like just as [it indicates] form. Or it would require the cognition of the invariable co-occurrence. For the greatness of invariable co-occurrence is not such that it indicates [something] merely by its existence. Or if so, then from smoke too, just like from the eye established merely in existence, fire would be cognized. Moreover, does the object become manifest simultaneously with, or immediately after, the cognition? From that [cognition], the eye is not born — this acquiring of a specific nature distinct from itself is its own nature, arising from its own causes — that even what is not itself and even what is not a cause, or even when there is no distinction of being a cause, illuminates form alone, even unrecognized form — this is established by the force of observing the effect in the form of the apprehension of form. If one says 'because that cannot be denied' — then, for that which has no connection to something somewhere, there is no <s>pramāṇa</s>-status there — like the donkey which is unconnected to fire — thus the <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader) was itself made inconclusive by you. What should we say here? On what basis, then, is the practice of <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding verbal testimony — the same basis on which it is regarding the eye and the like? If one asks: what is that basis there [for the eye]? — this is great scholarship indeed, that even in the established matrix there is still doubt today! For the practice of <s>pramāṇa</s> is everywhere based on the capacity to generate veridical experience — even a child says this. And by just that measure, that harmonious

children.text: svabhāvabhedaḥ svakāraṇādāyāto vyavasthāpyate /
children.translated_text: specific nature of verbal testimony too, having come from its own cause, is established.

children.text: yataḥ tattatsaḍketopadhānasūtramarthaṃ pratipādayatīti, tathāpi samayasya puruṣāyattatvāt kimayaṃ sāṃvyavahārikasaḍketāneva śabdān prayuḍkte? kiṃ vā svayamidānīmarthabhedeṣu saḍketyeti sandeho na nivartata iti cet---na, ubhayathāpyasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Since the <s>sūtra</s> teaching the assignment of conventions for those various [things] conveys the meaning — even so, since convention depends on human effort, the doubt is not removed: does he employ words with their conventional designations, or does he now assign conventions to the divisions of meaning himself? — if so: no, because both are impossible.

children.text: yadyasau pratipādakaḥ kathaṃ svahṛdayaguhānikṣiptasamayāneva śabdānuccārayet? jānātyeva hyayaṃ nāviditasamayā ete pratipādakā iti //
children.translated_text: If he is a teacher, how could he utter words with conventions deposited in the cave of his own heart? For he surely knows: "these [words] do not convey [meaning] to those who do not know the convention."

children.text: atha vipralambhakaḥ, tathāpi samayāntarakaraṇe ka upayogaḥ, prasiddhasamayaireva vipralambhasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: And if he is a deceiver, even so, what use is creating another convention, since deception is possible with well-known conventions themselves?

children.text: yatrāpi hi guptasamayairvyavahāraḥ, tatrāpi na pratipādyaṃ prati samayo gopyaḥ, api tvaviśvastān pratīti hṛti nighāyāha---tasamāditi //7 //
children.translated_text: Even where there is dealing with secret conventions, the convention is not to be kept secret from the addressee, but from those who are not trusted — keeping this in mind, he says: "Therefore..."

children.text: na dvividho dṛṣṭādṛṣṭārthatvāt //1.1.8 //
children.translated_text: "[Verbal testimony] is not twofold, because of having both seen and unseen objects" // 1.1.8 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: svacchāḥ svabhāvaśucayo 'tiśayena gurvyo
children.translated_text: Clear, naturally pure, exceedingly weighty,

children.text: durbandhadurdharadurāgrahadurvibhāvyāḥ /
children.translated_text: difficult to bind, difficult to hold, difficult to grasp, difficult to comprehend —

children.text: ṭīkāgiro viśadapāradavipruṣo vā
children.translated_text: the words of the <s>ṭīkā</s> — or are they drops of refined mercury?

children.text: yeṣāṃ vaśe nanu vaśe jagadeva teṣām //8 //
children.translated_text: Those in whose power [they are], in their power indeed is the world.

children.text: // pramāṇanibandhaḥ samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: // The treatise on <s>pramāṇa</s> is complete //

children.text: // iti pramāṇalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> //

children.text: // prameyaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // The section on <s>prameya</s> (the knowable) //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
nanu yadi prameyameva mumukṣuṇā pratipitsitam, tadullaḍghya kimiti prathamataḥ pramāṇamamihitamityata āha---tacceti /
tarhi uktāni pramāṇānīdānīṃ parīkṣayantāṃ kiṃ prameyalakṣaṇenetyata āha---lakṣaṇaṃ ceti /
tarhi prameyalakṣaṇamevāmidhīyatām /
kiṃ
children.translated_text: Now, if it is <s>prameya</s> (the knowable) itself that is desired to be known by one who seeks liberation, why was <s>pramāṇa</s> treated first, passing over that? — therefore he says: "That and..." Then let the stated <s>pramāṇas</s> be examined now — what is the need for the definition of <s>prameya</s>? — therefore he says: "And the definition..." Then let the definition of <s>prameya</s> alone be stated — what is the need for

children.text:
pratyakṣādilakṣaṇenetyata āha---na ceti /
nanu pramāṇaṃ tāvat prathamata eva vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: the definition of perception and the like? — therefore he says: "Nor..." Now, <s>pramāṇa</s> should be stated first of all.

children.text:
taditarasya tadadhīnatvāditi prāgeva saṃgamitametat /
idānīṃ tu pañcadaśasu prathamaṃ kimabhidhīyatāmiti jijñāsā /
abhidhīyamānasaṃgatiparyālocane ca saṃśayādīnāmanupayogādanabhidhānameva prasaktam, kutaḥ pūrvāparabhāvaspardhetyata āha---aparīkṣitaṃ ceti /
etena saṃśayādīnāmupayogaṃ darśayatā vaktavyatā darśitā /
etasmād viśeṣāt pramāṇaprakaraṇāt
children.translated_text: This was already connected earlier — that the other [categories] depend on it. But now the inquiry is: among the fifteen [remaining categories], which should be stated first? And since, upon reflecting on the relevance of what is stated, doubt and the like are not useful, their non-statement itself is warranted — whence then the competition of priority? — therefore he says: "And without examination..." By this, showing the usefulness of doubt and the like, the necessity of stating [them] has been shown. From this distinguishing feature, the <s>prameya</s> section has priority over the <s>pramāṇa</s> section

children.text:
apakarṣaḥ saṃśayādiprakaraṇebhyaśca utkarṣaḥ prameyaprakaraṇasyeti samudāyārthaḥ /
ārabhyatāṃ tahi prameyalakṣaṇam, kimantargaḍunā vibhāgenetyata āha---tadiheti /
prameyanāntarīkatvaṃ prameyālambnaphalatvam /
kiṃ tadarthajātamiti bhāṣyakārīyaḥ praśnaḥ śliṣṭaḥ, ki lakṣaṇaṃ katividhaṃ ceti /
asminnarthe vibhāgavat sāmānyalakṣaṇamantareṇāpi viśeṣalakṣaṇānavatārāt /
tatra dvitīye---sūtrapāṭhe nottaram /
prathame tu śabdavyākhyāneneti bhāṣyagatiḥ /
tadatra dvitīyapraśnārtho vibhāgoddeśasūtramavatārayitumityanena darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The purpose of the second question — namely, the division-enumeration <s>sūtra</s> — is shown to be the occasion for introduction by this.

children.text: prathamastu viśiṣṭaṃ prameyamadyāpi na sidhyatīti tadarthaṃ praśna ityanena /
children.translated_text: But the first [question is shown as]: the qualified <s>prameya</s> has not yet been established — so the question is for that purpose — by this.

children.text: tatra vārttikakāreṇa tuśabdasūcitaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ gṛhītvā vibhāganiṣṭhaḥ praśna ityanena /
children.translated_text: There, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, having taken the general definition indicated by the word "but," asks a question culminating in division — [this is shown] by this.

children.text: tatra vārttikakāreṇa tuśabdasūcitaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ gṛhītvā vibhāganiṣṭhaḥ praśnaḥ kṛta ityāha---sa ca viśeṣa iti //
children.translated_text: There, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, having taken the general definition indicated by the word "but," has asked a question culminating in division — he says: "And that is the specific..."

and inferiority to the sections on doubt and the like — this is the overall meaning. Then let the definition of <s>prameya</s> be commenced — what is the use of the intervening division? — therefore he says: "Now here..." "Being immediately connected with <s>prameya</s>" means having <s>prameya</s> as the object of the result. "What is that class of things?" — the question of the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> is apt — [meaning] "what is the definition, and how many kinds?" In this matter, without a general definition even with the division, the specific definitions cannot be introduced. Among these, to the second [question] — the <s>sūtra</s> text gives no answer. But to the first, the <s>bhāṣya</s> proceeds by explaining the word itself.

children.text:
nanvayameva ca sūtrārtha iti vibhāga evāsya sūtrāsyārtha iti gamyate /
tathā ca na vivakṣitaviśeṣalābhaḥ sūtrāt, evaṃ ca prameyamātravibhāgo 'narthako 'satyaścetyata āha---yeṣāmiti /
children.translated_text: Now, since "this very [division] is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>" — [the objection is:] the division alone is the meaning of this <s>sūtra</s>. And thus, the desired specific [<s>prameya</s>] is not obtained from the <s>sūtra</s>; and thus, the mere division of <s>prameya</s> in general would be purposeless and false — therefore he says: "Of which..."

children.text:
prakṛtopayogiprameyaviśeṣalakṣaṇakroḍīkṛtānāmeva vibhāgo 'sya sūtrasyārtha iti vārttikārtha ityarthaḥ /
yeṣāmityādinā yathāsaṃkhyaṃ lakṣaṇadvayam /
naśca tattvapadena saṃbandhaḥ /
sākṣāditi ca pūraṇīyam /
children.translated_text: And "directly" should be supplied.

children.text: apavargo mithyājñānanivṛttiḥ, tadāditvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Apavarga</s> (liberation) is the cessation of false cognition, since it begins with that.

children.text: saṃsāro rāgadveṣau, tadekadeśatvāditi /
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is attachment and aversion, since it is a part of that.

children.text: paramāṇūnāmityupalakṣaṇam, tenāśarīrānindriyā tadartharūpāṇāṃ dvyaṇukādīnāṃ tadguṇakarmaṇāmapīti //
children.translated_text: "Of atoms" is illustrative — therefore it also includes bodiless [entities], sense-organs, and the forms that serve their purposes, as well as dyads and the like, and the qualities and actions of those.

The meaning is: the division of those [<s>prameyas</s>] whose specific definitions relevant to the topic have been embraced is the meaning of this <s>sūtra</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>vārttika</s>. By "of which" and so forth, the twofold definition in due order. And the connection is not with the word "<s>tattva</s>" (reality).

children.text: nanu yadā digādayo 'bhihitā evārthata iti samādhānam, tadā tadabhidhāne ka upayoga ityapi samarthanīyamityata āha---kauśalamātramiti //9 //
children.translated_text: Now, when the resolution is that direction and the like have indeed been implicitly stated, what is the use of explicitly stating them? — this too needs to be justified — therefore he says: "Mere skill..."

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
nanu pratyakṣamapyātmani pramāṇameva, ahamiti vikalpasya parairapīṣṭatvāt /
na cāyamavastukaḥ saṃdigdhavastuko vā, aśābdatvādapratikṣepācca /
na cāyaṃ laiḍgikaḥ, ananusaṃhitaliṅgasyāpi svapratyayāt /
nāpi smṛtiriyam, ananubhūte smaraṇāyogāt /
anādivāsanāvaśādanādirayamavastuko vikalpa ityapi na yuktam, nīlādivikalpeṣvapyevaṃ vaktuṃ sukaratvāt /
kādācitkatvena tatra vastukalpanamihāpi samānam /
arthakriyāsthiteḥ sūtraprāmāṇyasiddhervastusthitirityapi na yuktam, arthakriyāsthitiniścayasyāpi vāsanāmādāyopaplāvayituṃ śakyatvāt /
ata eva pramāṇāntarapravṛtterityapi gatam /
tasmād vāsanāvādamātraṃ vihāya āgantukamapi kiñcit kāraṇaṃ vācyam /
taccāptānāptaśabdau vā liṅgatadābhāse vā pratyakṣatadābhāse vā? tatra yathā prathamamadhyamaprakārābhāvāt nīlavikalpaśyaramaṃ kalpamālambate, tathāhamitti vikalpo 'pi /
tatrāyam,
children.translated_text: Now, perception too is indeed a <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding the self, since the conceptual cognition "I" is accepted even by opponents. And this is not devoid of an object or of doubtful objecthood, because it is non-verbal and because it is not contradicted. And this is not inferential, because the self-cognition arises even for one who has not connected an inferential mark. Nor is this a memory, because remembering what has not been experienced is impossible. And it is not proper to say that this is a beginningless objectless conceptual cognition due to beginningless latent impressions, since it is easy to say the same regarding concepts of blue and the like. The supposition of an object based on occasional occurrence is the same here too. And it is also not proper to say that the existence of reality is established from the validity of the <s>sūtra</s> through the establishment of purposive action, since even the certainty of the establishment of purposive action can be overwhelmed by taking latent impressions [as the cause]. For this very reason, [the argument] "from the operation of other <s>pramāṇas</s>" too is gone. Therefore, setting aside the mere doctrine of latent impressions, some adventitious cause must be stated. And is that the words of trustworthy or untrustworthy persons, or an inferential mark or its semblance, or perception or its semblance? Among these, just as the concept of blue, due to the absence of the first and middle types, finally resorts to the last type, so too the "I" concept. And therein,

children.text: pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvitve sākṣādeva savastukaḥ /
children.translated_text: when it is immediately posterior to perception, it has a real object directly.

children.text: tadābhāse tu mūle 'sya pāramparyāt savastutā //
children.translated_text: But when the root [perception] is a semblance, its having a real object is indirect.

children.text:
iti /
na ca bāhyapratyakṣanivṛttāveva nirmūlatvam, buddhivikalpasyāpi nirmūlatvaprasaḍgāt /
tatra svasaṃvedanaṃ mūlam, ihāpi mānasamiti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ /
tatkathamātmani pratyakṣapratiṣedhakaṃ bhāṣyamityata āha---ahamiti /
children.translated_text: — thus. And it is not the case that rootlessness [occurs] only upon the cessation of external perception, since there would follow the consequence of even the concept of cognition being rootless. There, self-awareness is the root; here too, mental [perception] is the root — so there is no distinction. Then how is the <s>bhāṣya</s> a denial of perception regarding the self? — therefore he says: "The [cognition] 'I'..."

children.text:
yadyapi savastuko 'yaṃ tathāpi śarīrapratyayasāmānādhikaraṇyāt tadvastuka evāyamityapi syāt /
ato na tadatirikte vastuni pramāṇayituṃ śakyate tāvad yāvad dehādibhyo bhinna ātmā pramāṇāntareṇa na sādhyata ityarthaḥ /
tadidamuktam---drāgiti /
children.translated_text: This is what was stated: "Quickly..."

children.text: ghaṭādijñānavaditi vyatirekidṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: "As with the cognition of a pot and the like" — this is the illustration through negative concomitance.

children.text: yathā hi ghaṭādijñānaṃ śarīrādipratyayavaiyadhikaraṇyāt
children.translated_text: For just as the cognition of a pot and the like, due to its being in a different substratum from the cognition of the body and the like,

children.text: tadatirikte vastuni drāgevapramāṇayitu śakyate, tathā nedamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: can quickly serve as a <s>pramāṇa</s> for a reality different from that [body], not so this ["I" cognition] — that is the meaning.

Although this ["I" cognition] has a real object, nevertheless, due to its co-referentiality with the cognition of the body, it might have precisely that [body] as its object. Therefore, it cannot serve as a <s>pramāṇa</s> for a reality different from that [body], so long as the self, different from the body and the like, is not established by another <s>pramāṇa</s> — that is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu yadi nāma na drāgeva, vicārakrameṇa tu pramāṇayiṣyate /
tathā hi,
nirūpādhiśarīrabuddhitatsamudāyālambanatvena ahaṃ pratyayasyātiprasaḍgāt svasaṃbandhini śarīrādāvayamahaṃpratyaya iti vācyam /
children.translated_text: Now, even if not quickly, it will be made a <s>pramāṇa</s> through the course of investigation. For thus: since the "I" cognition would over-extend to the body-cognition, the cognition that is free from the body, and their aggregate, the "I" cognition should be said to pertain to the body and the like, which are connected with oneself.

children.text:
tatrātmavyatirekeṇa kaḥ svārtha iti cintanīyam /
ananyatvaṃ svatvaṃ sarvabhāvānām /
tathā ca yadā tenaiva tadanubhūyate tadā pratyetuḥ pratyetavyādananyatvādahamiti syāt /
ata eva ghaṭādayo na kadācidapyananyānubhavitṛkā iti na kadācidapyahamāspadamiti cet? evaṃ tarhi tvanmate 'pyayamahamiti pratyayaḥ śarīrādāvāroparūpa eva, tataḥ pratyeturanyatvāt /
buddhau mukhya iti cet---na, tasyāḥ kriyātvenānubhūyamānāyā bhinnasya tatkarturahaṃ chinadmītivadahaṃ jānāmītyanubhavāt nīlādipratyetavyākāravat pratipattrākāro 'pi pratīterevāyamātmā tathā bhāsata iti cet? tarhi pratyetavyākārasamānayogakṣematvena pratipatrākārasyāpi siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitam /
astu svopādānamātramiti cet---na, tatpratibhāsane tadgatārthākārasyāpi pratibhāsaprasaḍgāt /
ākāramantareṇākāriṇo 'navabhāsanāt /
pravṛttivijñānasaṃtānādanya evāyaṃ buddhisaṃtānaḥ pratipattā, yamālayavijñānamācakṣata iti cet? evaṃ tarhi pravṛttivijñānopādānamanādinidhanaḥ siddho 'dhikaḥ pratipattā /
sa kiṃ saṃtanyamānajñānarūpaḥ, tadviparītarūpo veti cintā pariśiṣyate /
tasyāśca raṅgabhūmiḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgabhaṅga ityata āha---pareti /
dṛḍhataraṃ viśeṣaniṣṭham /
smṛtyā saha pūrvāparapratyayayorekaviṣayatvamūkajñānagocaratvam /
pūrvānubhūtitatkāryasmṛtitatkāryānubhūtīnāmekenānuvyavasāyena
children.translated_text: There, what is "self" apart from the <s>ātman</s>? — this is to be considered. "Self-ness" is the non-otherness of all entities. And thus, when that very thing experiences by itself, due to the non-otherness of the experiencer from the experienced, [the cognition] "I" would arise. For this very reason, pots and the like are never experienced as non-other, and therefore are never the locus of "I" — if one says so? Then in your view too, this "I" cognition regarding the body and the like is of the nature of superimposition, since the experiencer is different from that [body]. [If one says:] it is primary in cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) — no, because cognition, being experienced as an action, of its different agent the experience is "I cut" — just so, "I know" — therefore, just as the form of the object-to-be-experienced, like blue, is of the experience itself, so too the form of the experiencer is also of the experience itself — this self appears thus — if one says so? Then, by sharing the same status as the form of the experienced object, the form of the experiencer too establishes what we desire [namely, the self]. [If one says:] let it be merely what is self-originated — no, because if that were to appear, even the object-form residing in it would appear. Because without a form, the form-bearer cannot appear. [If one says:] this experiencer is another stream of cognition, different from the operational-cognition stream — whom they call <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) — then in that case, an additional experiencer has been established, beginningless and endless, as the substratum of operational cognition. Is he of the nature of the connected stream of cognitions, or of a nature opposite to that? — this inquiry remains. And the arena of that [inquiry] is the refutation of momentariness — therefore he says: "Of the opponent..." More firmly, [the arguments are] directed to the specific [points]. The single-objecthood of prior and subsequent cognitions along with memory, and [that this is] within the domain of the cognition of a mute person. Of prior experience, the memory that is its effect, and the experience that is the effect of that memory — by a single reflective apprehension (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>),

children.text:
etena pratisaṃdhānaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ vā syāt, kāryakāraṇaviśeṣayorekasaṃtānaniyamo vā? ādye tattvataḥ pratyabhijñānamasiddham, abhimānato viruddham, aviśiṣṭamanaikāntikam /
dvitīye 'pi virodha eveti nirastam /
tadāha---tadaneneti /
tadatra pratisaṃdhāne kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ pareṇopanyastaḥ kimupādhitayā vipakṣavyāvṛttisaṃdehamudbhāvayitum? atha svadarśane pratisandhānavyavasthāṃ pratipādayitum? pratisandhānasya tu kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanameva bādhanamityāśayaḥ /
tatra pratyabhijñānaṃ pratisandhānamiti gṛhītvopādhilakṣaṇamapaninīṣān kāryakāraṇabhāvapratisandhānayoḥ paraspareṇa vyāpti khaṇḍayati---na hi yatreti /
punaḥ bauddhaḥ /
na hi kāryakāraṇabhāvamātraṃ pratisandhānanibandhanamācakṣmahe /
kiṃ tarhi? sādṛśyaviśiṣṭamiti śaṅkate---vastuta iti /
tadidamuktam, sabhāgeṣu iti /
etadvyatirekavyabhicāreṇa dūṣayati---tanneti /
viśiṣṭo 'pi kāryakāraṇabhāvo na pratisandhānaṃ prati prayojako yatastannivṛttāvapi nedaṃ nivartata ityarthaḥ /
na ca sādṛśyamātramevāstu tannibandhanamiti sāmpratam, bhedagrahe tasyāpi vyabhicārāt /
tadagrahapakṣastu vācya iti tamupekṣyāsmadabhipretaṃ pratisandhānamādāya śaṅkate---pūrvāpareti /
yatra kartari pratisandhānaṃ tatrāvaśyaṃ pratisandhayānāṃ buddhīnāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is recognition in the agent, there necessarily the cognitions that are recognized have a causal relation.

children.text: yatra caiṣa evabhūtaḥ, tatrāvaśyaṃ kartṛpratisandhānamiti na vyabhicaratītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And where there is precisely this causal relation that has arisen, there necessarily there is recognition of the agent — thus it does not deviate. That is the meaning.

children.text: dūṣayati---hanteti /
children.translated_text: He refutes: "Well then..."

children.text: nairātmyasākṣātkārasātmībhāva iti sarvajñopalakṣaṇaparam //
children.translated_text: "Becoming identified with the direct realization of non-self" — this is intended as an illustration for the omniscient.

would this be recognition or recollection — or would there be a rule restricting the specific cause and effect to a single continuum? In the first case, recognition in reality is unestablished; as mere identification, it is contradictory; if the distinction is not made, it is inconclusive. In the second case too, it is refuted as being contradictory. He says: "By this..." Now, the opponent has adduced the causal relation with respect to recognition — is this as an <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition), to raise doubt about the exclusion from the counter-example? Or to establish the arrangement of recognition in his own doctrine? But the intention is that the proof of momentariness is itself the sublation of recognition. There, taking recognition as identification, one who wishes to remove the definition of <s>upādhi</s> breaks the mutual pervasion of the causal relation and recognition: "For not wherever..." The Buddhist again [objects]: "We do not declare the mere causal relation as the ground of recognition. What then? [The causal relation] qualified by similarity" — he raises this objection: "In reality..." This is what was stated: "In those of the same class." He refutes this by the deviation in the negative concomitance: "Not that..." Even the qualified causal relation is not productive of recognition — because even when that [qualified causal relation] ceases, this [recognition] does not cease — that is the meaning. Nor is it proper that mere similarity alone should be its ground, because even that deviates when difference is apprehended. But the view of non-apprehension of difference is [merely] verbal — setting it aside, taking recognition as we intend it, he raises the objection: "Prior and subsequent..."

children.text:
tadayamarthaḥ, sarvajñastāvadubhayavādyavivādaviṣayaḥ /
sa kimātmanaḥ pūrvāparapratyayānekakartṛkatayā pratisaṃdhatte na vā? ādye tatpratisandhānādeva pratisandhāturekatvaṃ siddham /
jñānānāṃ bhedasya dhiyāmasthairyasya sarvaireva pratīteḥ /
pratisandhātuḥ kṣaṇikatāyāḥ sarvajñenāpyapratīteḥ /
atha na pratisandhatte, na tarhi kāryakāraṇabhāvanibandhanaṃ kartaryapi pratisandhānam /
na hyasti saṃbhavo yadanvaye 'pi yasyānanvayastat tāvanmātranibandhanamiti /
saiva ca ityādi sotprāsam /
vyartha iti /
svanibandhanānuvṛttau sattvadṛṣṭerdurapahnavatvāt /
avaśyaṃ ca tasya pratisaṃdhānena bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: And he must necessarily have recognition.

children.text: kathamanyathopadiśet? avaśyaṃ copadeṣṭā svīkartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, how would he instruct? And an instructor must necessarily be accepted.

children.text: yadi pāralaukiker'the vipralambhakā eva vaktāra iti niścayaḥ, saṃbhāvanayāpi prekṣāvanto na pravarteran /
children.translated_text: If one is certain that speakers regarding other-worldly matters are nothing but deceivers, then discerning persons would not act even on the basis of mere possibility.

children.text: tasmādubhayathāpi pratisandhāturekatvaṃ siddham //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in either case, the unity of the recognizer is established.

The meaning is this: the omniscient is, to begin with, an undisputed subject for both parties. Does he recognize his own cognitions as having a single agent through the earlier and later cognitions, or not? In the first case, from that very recognition the unity of the recognizer is established. Since the difference of cognitions and the instability of intellects are cognized by everyone. Since the momentariness of the recognizer is not cognized even by the omniscient. But if he does not recognize, then even recognition grounded in the causal relation does not exist regarding the agent. For it is not possible that what does not obtain even when [its condition] obtains could have that alone as its ground. And 'that very...' and so forth is said with derision. 'Purposeless' — because the persistence of existence-perception with respect to its own ground is impossible to deny.

children.text:
atra śaṅkate---athāsadapīti /
tataśca na kāṣakāraṇabhāvo na tasya nibandhanam avyabhicārāt /
nāpyanupadeśaprasaṅgaḥ, tannibandhanasya pratisandhānasya bhāvāt /
nāpi doṣāvakāśaḥ, svarasavāhinastasya taddhetutvāt /
asya tvāhāryatvādityarthaḥ /
śaṅkate---na ceti /
so 'yaṃ kāryakāraṇābhāve satyeva draṣṭavyaḥ /
upadeśastu pūrvapratisandhānabalopanītakarūṇābhyāsaprakarṣādeva virodhapratisandhānabalena suptasyeva prabodha iti śaḍkārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here he raises an objection: 'Even if non-existent...' And therefore there is no causal relation, nor is that [unity] its ground — because of non-deviation. Nor is there the consequence of non-teaching, since recognition, which is grounded in that, exists. Nor is there scope for the fault, since recognition, flowing naturally, has that [causal relation] as its cause. But this [recognition of the opponent] is artificial — this is the meaning. He raises an objection: 'And not...' This is to be seen as being precisely when there is no causal relation. And the teaching, through the force of previous recognition arousing the intensification of the practice of compassion, is — by the force of contrary recognition — like the awakening of a sleeping person — this is the purport of the objection.

children.text:
uttaram---pravṛttīti /
na ca sphaṭikavad viṣayoparāgaparihāreṇa buddhiṣu bhedagraha iti yuktam, sphaṭikavadupādhiparihāreṇa buddhīnāṃ pratyetumaśakyatvāt /
tathābhāve buddhimātreṇa bhedāgrahe pārthivatayā vṛkṣāt kāṣṭhaṃ kāṣṭhādaḍgāraḥ, tato bhasmādibhedena na gṛhyeta /
gṛhyate ca /
tasmānnimittavyāvṛttau pratisandhānaṃ na syāt, bhavad vā nimittāntaramākṣipatītyarthaḥ /
na copadeśaḥ pratisandhānamantareṇa samarthitaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: And teaching would not be justified without recognition.

children.text: sa hi vivakṣāyoniḥ /
children.translated_text: For that [teaching] has its source in the desire to speak.

children.text: sā ca saḍketitaśabdasmaraṇādiyoniḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [desire to speak] has its source in the memory of conventionally established words and the like.

children.text: tadeva ca pratisandhānam //
children.translated_text: And that itself is recognition.

The answer: 'Activity...' And it is not proper [to say] that the grasping of difference in cognitions is by removing the coloring of the object, like a crystal. Because cognitions cannot be cognized by removing the limiting conditions like a crystal. If, in the absence of such [removal], difference is not grasped by mere cognition — then, just as a tree produces charcoal by its earthy nature, and charcoal [produces] ash, the difference of tree from charcoal and from ash would not be grasped. But it is grasped. Therefore, when the occasion [for difference] ceases, there would be no recognition; or, if there is [recognition], it would entail a different occasion — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanvālayavijñānabhedāgrahāt pratisandhānaṃ bhaviṣyatītyata āha---ālayeti /
sa hyālayasantāno 'hamāspadaṃ pravṛttivijñānādanya eva syāt, tadantaḥpātikādācitkānekāhaṃpratyayarupo vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, na hyahamahamikayā parasparasvatantrasantānadvayamanubhūyate /
satyapi vā parasparamanupādānānupādeyabhāvānna parasparapratyākalitārthānusandhānabandhaḥ /
tathātve vā caitramaitrādiṣvapi prasaṅgaḥ /
ubhayorvā ubhayopādānatve ekamapyanekāśritamiti kimaparāddhamavayavisaṃyogādibhiḥ? na
children.translated_text: Now, recognition will arise from the non-grasping of difference in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) — to this he says: '<s>Ālaya</s>...' For would that <s>ālaya</s> continuum, which is the basis of 'I,' be something other than the active consciousnesses, or would it be an occasional, multiple I-cognition belonging within them? Not the first, because two mutually independent continuums are not experienced in the form of 'I, I.' Or even if [two exist], because of their not being in the relation of material cause and product to each other, there is no binding of the investigation of meaning mutually recognized by each other. Or if such [a relation obtained], there would follow the same consequence in <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Maitra</s> and the like. Or if both were material causes of both, what harm would one more [entity] do, being multi-based? — what [harm] is done by the disjunction of parts and the like? Nor

children.text: cālayavijñānopāttaṃ pravṛttivijñānaṃ na kiñcidupādatta ityapi yuktam /
tathā sati nimittatāmapi na yāyāt, upādānatvavyāptatvānnimittatāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: In that case, it would not even attain the status of an occasional cause, since the status of occasional cause is pervaded by the status of material cause.

children.text: evaṃ ca yadi jñānāntaramupādadīta, tadā apūrvānantasantānapravṛttiprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, if it were to take up another cognition, there would follow the consequence of the arising of a new infinite continuum.

children.text: tasmānnālayasantāna ānubhaviko na caupapattika ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>ālaya</s> continuum is neither experienced nor derivable through reasoning — this is the meaning.

children.text: dvitīye tvāha---ahamiti //
children.translated_text: In the second [alternative] he says: 'I...'
is it proper that the active consciousness taken up by the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> does not take up anything.

children.text:
ayamāśayaḥ /
asya hi bhedāgrahaḥ svarūpato vā syāt, viṣayato vā? svarūpato 'pi pūrvāhamiti pratyayamātrād vā, pravṛttivijñānebhyo 'pi vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, ahamityajñāsiṣam, ahamiti jānāmi, ahamiti jñāsyāmītyatītatvādipratīterbhedaniścayamantareṇānupapatteḥ /
kathañcid bhedāgrahe 'pi tadarthasyaiva pratisandhānamucitam, na pravṛttivijñānānām /
na ca tebhyo 'pi bhedāgraha iti coktameva /
nāpi viṣayataḥ /
sa hi svākāro vā syāt,
children.translated_text: The intention is as follows. The non-grasping of difference in this [ālaya] — would it be with respect to its essential nature or with respect to its object? With respect to essential nature too — would it be merely from the preceding I-cognition, or from the active consciousnesses as well? Not the first, because the cognitions 'I knew,' 'I know,' 'I will know' — involving the cognition of pastness and so forth — are untenable without the determination of difference. Even if somehow there is non-grasping of difference, the recognition of that very object [of the I-cognitions] would be appropriate, not of the active consciousnesses. And that there is no non-grasping of difference from those too — this has already been stated. Nor with respect to the object. For that [object] would be either its own form,

children.text:
vastvantarameva vā, alīkaṃ vā? nādyaḥ, prāgdūṣaṇenaiva gatatvāt /
na hyanena svākāraḥ svātmano bhedenāropitaḥ, api tu svātmaviṣaya eva darśitaḥ /
tasya ca bhedo niścita iti /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, svayamanabhyupagamāt /
nāpi tṛtīyaḥ, ahamiti vikalpasya savastukatāyāḥ prāgeva prasādhanāt /
avastukatve 'pi na tatra prakṛtopayogibhedāgrahasaṃbhavaḥ /
sa hi vidyamāna eva bhedo na gṛhyate, avidyamāna eva vā, āropito vā, āropitāsattvo vā? na tāvadādyaḥ, alīkasya ajñāyamānabhedasampattāvanalīkatvaprasaḍgāt /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, pāramārthikasya bhedābhāvasya pāramārthikābhedaparyavasāyitvāt /
na ca paramārthata eva nānāvikalpollikhitamalīkamekātmakam anātmakatvāt /
tathātve vā kva bhedāgrahasyopayogaḥ, ekatvādevaikatvenānusandhānāt? nāpi tṛtīyaḥ, virodhaparāhatatvāt /
yadi hi tatra bhedāropaḥ, kathaṃ tadagrahaḥ? tadagrahe vā kathaṃ bhedāropaḥ? na ca bhedārope 'bhedāropasyāpyavakāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: For if difference is superimposed there, how is there non-grasping of it? Or if there is non-grasping of it, how is there superimposition of difference? And when difference is superimposed, there is no scope for the superimposition of non-difference either.

children.text: nāpi caturthaḥ, ātmāśrayaprasaṃgāt, pāramārthikabhedaprasaḍgācca /
children.translated_text: Nor the fourth, because of the consequence of self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>) and the consequence of ultimate difference.

children.text: ghaṭapaṭayoryo bhedaḥ pāramārthikaḥ, śaśaviṣāṇanaraviṣāṇayorvā yo bhedaḥ kālpanikaḥ, sa iha na gṛhyate ityabhedānusaṃdhānamiti cet---na, anyaviṣayabhedāgrahe anyatrābhedārope 'tiprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: If one says: 'The difference between a pot and a cloth is ultimate; or the difference between a hare's horn and a human horn is imaginary — that [imaginary difference] is not grasped here, and hence recognition of non-difference' — no, because there would follow the over-extension that non-grasping of difference in one object [would lead to] superimposition of non-difference in another.

children.text: catuṣkoṭivinirmuktavyapadeśyabhedāgrahe tvabhedārope trailokyaikatāropaprasaṅgaḥ //
children.translated_text: And in the case of non-grasping of a designable difference free from the fourfold alternatives, there would follow the superimposition of the unity of the triple world.

or some other entity, or something unreal. Not the first, since it has already been disposed of by the earlier refutation. For one has not superimposed one's own form as different from one's own self — rather, one has shown it to be precisely the object of one's own self. And the difference of that is determined. Nor the second, since [the opponent] himself does not accept it. Nor the third, since the reality of the conceptual construction 'I' has already been established. Even on the view of its unreality, the non-grasping of difference that is useful for the topic at hand is not possible there. For [the non-grasping would mean that] either existing difference is not grasped, or non-existing difference [is assumed], or difference is superimposed, or the existence of superimposed [difference] is [assumed]. Not the first, since if an unreal thing possessed the full complement of ungrasped difference, it would follow that it is not unreal. Nor the second, since the ultimate absence of difference would terminate in ultimate non-difference. And what is ultimately one — manifoldly traced by various conceptualizations — is not non-self, because of being unreal. Or, if it were, where is the use of non-grasping of difference, since from unity itself there would be recognition as one? Nor the third, since it is defeated by contradiction.

children.text: tatra bhedagraho 'pyastīti cet? tarhi yathābhūto bhedaḥ tatra gṛhyate, tadagrahe evābhedāropa ityeva sādhu /
na caitadalīkaviṣayatvapakṣe saṃbhavatīti sthiravastugocaratvam eva sattvabuddherjyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this is not possible on the view that [recognition] has an unreal object — therefore, having a stable real entity as its object is indeed preferable for the cognition of existence.

children.text: kṣaṇabhaṅgastu niṣetsyata iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: But momentary destruction will be refuted — this is the purport.

children.text: tadidamuktarūpaṃ pratisandhānaṃ nimittavattayā vyāptaṃ nirnimittatve niyamānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: This recognition of the described form is pervaded by having a cause, because without a cause there would be no regularity.

children.text: taccānekakartṛtve nāstīti vyāpakānupalabdhyā vipakṣānnivartamānaṃ nimittavatyekakartṛkatve viśrāmyatīti pratibandhasiddhiḥ ityanenābhiprāyeṇopasaṃharati---tasmāditi //
children.translated_text: And that [recognition] does not exist when there are multiple agents — thus, by the non-apprehension of the pervader, [recognition,] turning away from the counter-instance, comes to rest in having a single agent, which possesses a cause — thus the invariable connection is established. With this intention he concludes: 'Therefore...'

If one says: 'There is grasping of difference there too' — then it is proper that whatever difference exists there is grasped, and the superimposition of non-difference occurs precisely in the non-grasping of it.

children.text:
tadetatsarvaṃ buddhīnāmupādānopādeyabhāvamabhyupetyoktam /
vastutastu tatraivāyaṃ vivādaḥ /
tathā hi vyavahitakālā api pratyayā yadyekakartṛkāḥ, kva buddhīnāmupādānopādeyabhāvaḥ? sa cet, kva teṣāmekakartṛkatā? sā hyekopādānataiva /
na caikajātīyatve sati tadutpattiḥ evopādānopādeyabhāvaḥ /
śiṣyo pādhyāyabuddhyorapi tathābhāvaprasaṅgat /
bhedāgrahe satītyapi na yuktam, samastopādhisvīkāraparihāreṇa śiṣyācāryabuddhyorapi bhedāgrahāt /
sopādhibhedagrahasya prakṛte 'pi bhāvāt /
śarīrabhedāgrahasya janmāntareṇavyabhivacārāt /
anupalabdhapitṛkeṇa bālena cāti prasaḍgāt /
ghaṭakapālakṣaṇayoratathābhāvaprasaḍgācc /
ekādhāratāniyama ityapi na yuktam, tasya vāstavasya kṣaṇikapakṣe viṣayasamayānāṃ kṣaṇānāmabhāvāt kālpanikasya tvatiprasaṃjakatvāt /
asti hi sarveṣāmabhimāno yatraiva ghaṭe
children.translated_text: All this has been said on the assumption that cognitions are in the relation of material cause and product. But in reality, the dispute is precisely about that. For if cognitions separated in time have a single agent, where is the relation of material cause and product among cognitions? And if that [relation] exists, where is their having a single agent? For that [single agency] is just single material-cause-ness. And it is not the case that when things are of the same class, the origination of one from another is material-cause-product relation — for there would follow the same consequence between the cognitions of a student and a teacher. And [the restriction] 'when there is non-grasping of difference' is also not proper, since there is non-grasping of difference between the cognitions of a student and a teacher too, by accepting and setting aside the totality of limiting conditions. And the grasping of difference with limiting conditions exists even in the topic at hand. And the non-grasping of bodily difference is deviated by [the case of] another birth. And there would be over-extension even with a child whose parents are not known. And there would follow the absurd consequence that pot and potsherd would not be in that relation. And the restriction to a single substratum is also not proper — since in the momentariness view, moments that are the objects of real convention do not exist for the real [substratum]; and the imaginary one is over-extensive. For everyone has the conviction: wherever there is odor in a pot,

children.text:
gandhaḥ tatraiva rūparasasparśā iti, yatraiva śarīraṃ tatraiva jñānamiti /
etena cābhrāntasamataikāvasāyaḥ prakṛtivikriye /
tato
children.translated_text: there too are form, taste, and touch; wherever there is a body, there too is cognition. And by this, the investigation [terminates in] the non-erroneous consensus on <s>prakṛti</s> (primary cause) and <s>vikṛti</s> (modification). Therefore

children.text:
hetuphalasyopādānopādeyalakṣaṇamiti nirastam /
kāṣṭhasya tu prakṛtervikṛtiraḍgāra iti kuto niścitaṃ bhavatā? yāvatā vahnerevāsau vikāraḥ kiṃ na syāt, vahnisaṃbandhe kāṣṭhādeva tadutpatteriti cet---na, kāṣṭhasaṃbandhe vahnereva tadutpattirityevaṃ kiṃ na syāt? pārthivaṃ pārthivopādānakameveti niścayāditi cet? kuta etat? sabhāgeṣu kṣaṇeṣu tathā darśanāditi cet? tadapi kutaḥ? abhrāntasamataikāvasāyāditi cet---na, nīlaparamāṇuṣu parasparapratyāsanneṣu nirantaraṃ
children.translated_text: the view that the cause-effect relation has the character of material-cause-product is refuted. But how have you determined that charcoal is the modification of the primary cause wood? For it could well be a modification of fire, since in conjunction with fire it is produced from wood alone — if so, no, because in conjunction with wood too, it is produced from fire alone — [so how would you determine?] If one says: 'From the certainty that what is earthy has an earthy material cause' — whence is this? If one says: 'From observation in the case of homogeneous moments' — whence even that? If one says: 'From the non-erroneous consensus' — no, because when blue atoms are mutually proximate, being known without interval,

children.text:
jñāyamāneṣu parasparopādānatvaprasaṃgāt /
asti hi teṣāṃ tadutpattau satyāṃ mamatā ābhimānikaikatvāvasāyaśca /
pāramārthikastu na kvacidapi /
astu piṇḍitānāṃ rūparasaparamāṇūnāṃ sarveṣā sarvopādānatvamityapi na yuktam, anekavṛtteḥ ekasya svayamanabhyupagamāt, saprasidhānāṃ samānadeśatvābhāvācca /
etena bhrāntasaṃmataikāvasāya iti pāṭhāntaramapāstam, laukikānāṃ bhrāntasaṃmatestatrāpi tulyatvāt /
parīkṣakāṇāṃ tu prakṛte 'pyasattvāt /
tasmāt kāryakāraṇabhāvamātramavaśiṣyate /
sa ca nopādhiratiprasaṃgāt /
kiñcideva svakāraṇasāmagrīvaśādutpadyate jñānaṃ yat kāṃścideva kāraṇasāntānikān pratyayān pratyavekṣate nānyat /
nāparānityetadapyasādhīyaḥ, niyāmakamantareṇa śiṣyasyāpyupādhyāyacittapratyavekṣakajñānotpādaprasaḍgāt /
tatra teṣāmanabhisaṃskārakatvāt naivamiti cet? kāraṇatvajñānatvāviśeṣe 'pyetadeva kutaḥ? vicitrā hi kāraṇānāṃ śaktiḥ /
tat
children.translated_text: there would follow the consequence of their being mutual material causes. For when they have originated together, there is a sense of 'mine' and a conviction of conventional unity. But ultimate [unity] does not exist anywhere. If one says: 'Let there be the material-cause-ness of all aggregated form-and-taste atoms for all' — that too is not proper, since the [Buddhist] himself does not accept a single entity having multiple substrata, and since entities with equal status do not have co-spatiality. By this, the alternative reading 'non-erroneous consensus of the confused' is also set aside, since common people's consensus, even if confused, is equally present there too. And the consensus of critical inquirers does not exist even in the topic at hand. Therefore, only the mere causal relation remains. And that is not a limiting condition, because of over-extension. Only certain cognitions arise by the force of their own causal complex and retrospectively examine only certain causal-continuum cognitions, not others.
