If one says: 'And not others' — even this is not more reliable, because without a determinant, there would follow the consequence that even a student's cognition would retrospectively examine the teacher's mind. If one says: 'Because those [other cognitions] have not conditioned it, it is not so' — whence is this, when there is no distinction in being a cause and being a cognition? For the capacities of causes are various. Then

children.text:
kimatinirbandhena? yatra yathā kāryaṃ dṛśyate tatra tathā kalpyata iti cet? tat kimidānīṃ kiṃbhūtasya kutra sāmarthyamityanuyogo 'nuttara eva /
evaṃ tarhi sarvatra jñāpakajanakeṣvanāśvasāt nirīhaṃ jagat jāyeta /
kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanabādhitatvāt pratisandhānahetorevaṃ kalpyata iti cet? athānenaitat kiṃ na bādhayate? tasya nirdeṣatvāditi cet? asya tarhi doṣāntaraṃ vacanīyam /
agṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatvādastūbhayoḥ satpratipakṣatvamiti cet? nanvidamapi te vyasanaṃ nivartayiṣyāmo mā tvariṣṭā
children.translated_text: why insist excessively? If one says: 'Where a certain effect is seen in a certain way, there it is postulated in that way' — then what now? The question 'Of what kind does something have capacity where?' is simply unanswerable. In that case, from the lack of confidence everywhere in the indicators of causes, the world would become inert. If one says: 'Because the ground for recognition is subverted by the proofs of momentary destruction, it is postulated thus' — then why does it [the proof of momentary destruction] not subvert this [postulation] too? If one says: 'Because it [recognition] has no proof' — then some other fault should be stated against it [recognition]. If one says: 'Since the distinguishing feature is not grasped, let there be the condition of having a valid counter-argument for both' — well, we shall also remove this misfortune of yours — do not be hasty!

children.text: ityupasaṃhāraśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: — this is the remainder of the conclusion.

children.text:
yadi hi sarvajñasya cetaso 'smadādicittamālambanapratyayatvenodāhniyate vaisadṛśyād daṇḍaghaṭavanna pratisaṃdhatta ityapi pariharedata uktam---yogicittamapīti /
tasyāpi yogicittena pratisandhānaṃ syāditi viparyayo hetuviparyāsasyāpi saṃbhavāt /
tasyāpi yogicittena pratisandhānaṃ syāditi viparyayo hetuviparyāsasyāpi saṃbhavāt /
sahārthe vā tṛtītā /
ihānubhavo vā kālāntarabhāvinīṃ smṛtiṃ janayati, jajjanito vā saṃskāraḥ? so 'pyatīndriyo 'dhyakṣasiddho vā? atīndriyo 'pi tatkālasthāyī, saṃtanyamāno vā? adhyakṣāsiddho 'pi taduttarabuddhidhārārūpo vā, tadanyo vā, tadviśeṣo vā? viśeṣo 'pyanubhavaprasavatvamātraṃ vā, anubhavitṛsantānavaijātyaṃ ceti? tatra prathamaṃ dūṣayati---na hyajāteti /
adhyakṣasiddhastu taduttarabuddhidhārārūpāt, anyastāvadanupalabdhibādhitaḥ, tairanabhyupagataśca /
anubhavaprabhavatāmātralakṣaṇastu viśeṣo 'viśeṣa eva /
na hi karmakarakaropanītam eva bījaṃ kṣitimāsādyaḍkuraṃ kurute /
na tu tathābhūtamapi pramādapatitam, tathā nīlādyanubhavasantānaḥ pītādyanubhavena vopanīyatām,
children.translated_text: For if the mind of the omniscient were cited as the supporting condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>) of our minds and the like, then [it could be said that] due to transparency, like a glass vessel, it does not connect [with impurity] — even this could be answered — it was said: 'the yogic mind too.' Of that too, connection through the yogic mind would follow — thus the reversal, since the reversal of the reason is also possible. Or [the particle] is in the sense of 'together with.' Or [the question is:] does the experience here generate memory that arises at a later time, or does the <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) generated [by it do so]? That [<s>saṃskāra</s>] too — is it supersensible or directly established? Even if supersensible — does it endure at a later time, or is it a continuum? Even if directly established — is it of the form of the stream of cognitions subsequent to it, or different from it, or a special feature of it? And if a special feature — is it merely the capacity to produce experience, or the homogeneity with the experiencer's continuum? Therein, he refutes the first: 'For not unborn...' But [if] directly established, [it is] of the form of the stream of cognitions subsequent to it — [an entity] different [from those cognitions] is, to begin with, contradicted by non-apprehension, and is not accepted by them [the Buddhists] either. And a special feature characterized merely by being produced from experience is no special feature at all. For it is not the case that only a seed brought by the action of a farmer, having reached the soil, produces a sprout,

children.text:
nīlādyanubhavenaiva veti na kaścit svarūpakṛto viśeṣaḥ /
evaṃ cānanubhūte 'pi smaraṇaprasaḍgo na cānubhūte 'pīti vaijātyaṃ tu viśeṣo bhavet /
yathā kṣīrāvasekādamlatvaṃ parihṛtya mādhuryamādāyānuvartamānāmalakī kālāntare api phale mādhuryamunmīlayati, lākṣārasāvasekād dhavalatāṃ parihṛtya raktatāmupādāyānuvartamānaṃ kārpāsabījaṃ kusumeṣu raktatām, na caivaṃ prakṛte saṃbhavati /
javākusumādyupadhānāt tadrūpatāṃ parihṛtya dhavalimānamupādāyaiva saṃtanyamānasya sphaṭikasyeva jñānasyāpi viṣayoparāgaṃ parihṛtya cidrūpatāmātramupādāyānuvṛtteḥ /
sarvākāratvameva sarvavijñānānāṃ kiṃ tu kaścidākāra ḥ
children.translated_text: but not one that has fallen accidentally in the same state. Similarly, let the continuum of blue-experience be brought about by yellow-experience, or by blue-experience itself — there is no intrinsic difference. And thus, there would be the unwanted consequence of remembering even what has not been experienced; and not [remembering] even what has been experienced — therefore, homogeneity with [the experiencer's continuum] would be the [required] special feature. Just as an <s>āmalakī</s> (gooseberry) tree, having been watered with milk, discarding sourness and taking on sweetness as it continues, unfolds sweetness in its fruit even at a later time; just as a cotton seed, having been watered with lac-dye, discarding whiteness and taking on redness as it continues, [produces] redness in the flowers — but this is not possible in the present case. For just as crystal, having been placed near <s>javā</s>-flowers (hibiscus) and the like, discarding the color-tinge and taking on only its transparent nature as it continues — so too of cognition, which continues taking on only its consciousness-nature while discarding the object-coloring. [If one says] 'all cognitions have all forms, but a certain form

children.text:
sphuṭaḥ, anye tvapaṭava iti tu svadarśanaśraddhā, yato viruddhadharmādhyāsādapi na bhīḥ /
nirākārapakṣe 'pi yāvānartho buddherviṣayastatra sphuṭaiva sā /
yatra tvasphuṭā nāsau tasyā viṣayaḥ /
tathātve vā viṣayetaravyavasthā na syāt /
tasmādatīndriyaḥ saṃskāraḥ pariśiṣyate /
sa cet kālāntarasthāyī, nūnaṃ tadupādānamapi tathaiva sthāyi /
na hyupādānanivṛttāvapi upādeyamavatiṣṭhata ityāśayavānāha---iti pūrvotpanna iti /
saṃtanyamāna evātīndriyaḥ saṃskāro bhaviṣyatītyāśayavānāśaṅkate---punaḥ para ityādi /
pṛthaksaṃskārasantāno hi na tāvat parābhyupeto nāpyupapannaḥ, ālayasya prāgeva pratiṣedhāt /
tato 'pyadhikatve tatraiva smṛtyādiphalaprasaḍgāt /
tasmāt pravṛttisantāne phalānavakāśāt anyatra saṃskāre 'nyatra phale 'tiprasaḍgāt /
tasmād pravṛttisantāne phalānavakāśāt anyatra saṃskāre 'nyatra phale 'tiprasaḍgāt /
tasmād pravṛttisantāne phalānavakāśāt anyatra saṃskāre 'nyatra
children.translated_text: is vivid, while others are faint' — this is [mere] faith in one's own doctrine, since even the superimposition of contradictory properties causes no fear [to you]. Even on the formless (<s>nirākāra</s>) view, to whatever extent an object is the object of cognition, to that extent [cognition] is vivid with respect to it. But where it is not vivid, that is not its object. Or if it were [its object even when cognition is not vivid], there would be no distinction between object and non-object. Therefore, the supersensible <s>saṃskāra</s> remains [as the only option]. If that endures at a later time, surely its material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) too must endure in the same way. For even when the material cause has ceased, the product does not remain standing — with this intention he says: 'thus what was previously arisen...' Intending to object that the supersensible <s>saṃskāra</s> might be a continuum, he raises the doubt: 'again, the other...' and so forth. For a separate <s>saṃskāra</s>-continuum is, to begin with, not accepted by the opponents, nor is it tenable — since <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) has already been refuted. And if [one posits something] over and above that, the unwanted consequence of memory and the like [bearing] fruit in that [continuum] alone [follows]. Therefore, since there is no room for the fruit in the active continuum, [and since] if the <s>saṃskāra</s> is in one [continuum] and the fruit in another, there would be over-extension — therefore, since there is no room for the fruit in the active continuum, [and since] if the <s>saṃskāra</s> is in one [continuum] and the fruit in another, there would be over-extension —

children.text: phale 'tiprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: therefore, since there is no room for the fruit in the active continuum, [and since] if the <s>saṃskāra</s> is in one [continuum] and the fruit in another, there would be over-extension —

children.text: tasmād yatrānubhavastatra saṃskāraḥ, yatra ca sa tatra smṛtyādiphalamiti paramupapadyate //
children.translated_text: therefore, it is most tenable that where the experience is, there the <s>saṃskāra</s> is, and where that [<s>saṃskāra</s>] is, there the fruit of memory and the like [arises].

children.text:
evaṃ ca kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanaṃ pratirodhakamavaśiṣyate /
tatrāha---upapādayiṣyate hīti /
etena yo yaḥ saṃskāraḥ kvacit santāna āhitaḥ, sa tatraiva phaladānayogyo nānyatretyādi nirastam, atiriktasya saṃskārasyāśrayāsiddhatvāt, viśeṣalakṣaṇasya ca svarūpāsiddhatvāt, aviśiṣṭottarakāryapravāhalakṣaṇasya ca viruddhatvāditi /
anityatvasya hetorviśeṣavyāvartakatvotkīrtanaṃ guṇatvasiddhyupayogāt /
ata eva netaretarāśrayatvaśaṅkā,
children.translated_text: And thus, the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) necessarily becomes an obstacle. Thereupon he says: 'it will be demonstrated indeed.' By this, the following is refuted: 'whatever <s>saṃskāra</s> is deposited in a certain continuum, that is capable of bearing fruit in that [continuum] alone, and not elsewhere' — and so forth — because the additional <s>saṃskāra</s> has an unestablished locus, because the specific characterization is intrinsically unestablished, and because the characterization as an undifferentiated subsequent causal stream is contradictory. The mention of impermanence as the reason's capacity to distinguish the specific [feature serves] the purpose of establishing <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-nature). For this very reason there is no suspicion of mutual dependence,

children.text: anityatvena pāratantryaṃ sādhayitvā tena guṇatvaprasādhānāt /
guṇatvaṃ tu yadarthaṃ sādhitam, tat tatsādhakenaiva sādhitamiti vaiyarthyamavaśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: But <s>guṇatva</s> — for whose sake it was established — that is [already] established by its own proof — thus pointlessness necessarily follows.

children.text: tadupasaṃharati---tasmāditi /
children.translated_text: He sums this up: 'therefore...'

children.text: nanu yadi vaiyarthyamasya hṛdi nihitameva vārttikakṛtā, tat kimathamamumeva hetumupanyastavānityata āha, tadapi pūrvamūktam, na tu prasādhitam /
children.translated_text: Now, if the pointlessness of this was already placed in the heart of the <s>Vārttika</s>-author himself, then for what purpose did he present this very reason? — to this he says: that too was stated earlier, but not [yet] demonstrated.

children.text: na cāsiddhaṃ sādhanaṃ nāmeti kṛtvā iti garbhaśoṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that an unestablished [reason] is not a proof — taking it thus — this is the implied reproach.
since, having established dependence [on substance] through impermanence, <s>guṇatva</s> (quality-nature) is then established through that.

children.text:
ayamarthaḥ /
yathā anityatvaṃ dravyapāratantryāvinābhūtam, tathā guṇatvamapi /
yathā ca tadicchadiṣu, tathā guṇatvamapīti /
na tāvadanayoḥ sādhanatvaṃ prati kaścid viśeṣaḥ /
kevalamanumānakālābhāvo vivakṣitaḥ /
so 'pi nāsti, ekahetusiddhe 'pi hetvantarajijñāsuṃ prati bhāvāt /
ananusaṃhitānityatvamapi tallakṣaṇayogana guṇatvavyavahāriṇaṃ prati ca /
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: just as impermanence is inseparable from dependence on substance, so too is <s>guṇatva</s>. And just as [impermanence obtains] in desire and the like, so too does <s>guṇatva</s>. To begin with, there is no difference between the two with respect to being a proof. The only [objection] intended is the absence of an occasion for inference. But even that does not [hold], since it exists for one who seeks another reason even when [the conclusion] has been established by one reason. And even for one who uses the term '<s>guṇatva</s>' with respect to impermanence that is not [yet] connected [with the notion of guṇatva], through the applicability of the definition of that [<s>guṇatva</s>].

children.text:
dṛśyate hīcchādīnāṃ sāmānyavatāmacalanātmakānāṃ guṇāntarāyogaḥ /
atra vipratipattau tvanityatvāderūpanyāsaḥ /
tadayamaperarthaḥ /
anityatvena pāratantryamapi sādhayati, tatsādhakaṃ guṇatvamapīti /
children.translated_text: Through impermanence he also establishes dependence [on substance], [and] <s>guṇatva</s> too, which proves that.

children.text: uttaraprabandhopayogamāha---na caitaditi /
children.translated_text: He states the usefulness for the subsequent discourse: 'and this is not...'

children.text: dravyapāratantryeṇa viśeṣiteneti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The remainder is: 'qualified by dependence on substance.'

children.text: tadetad viśeṣaṇaṃ kutaḥ siddhamityata āha---yadyapīti //
children.translated_text: Whence is this qualification established? — to this he says: 'even though...'

For it is observed that desire and the like, which are general [properties], of a non-moving nature, do not co-occur with other <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). In the case of disagreement on this point, however, the presentation of [reasons such as] impermanence and the like [is made]. This then is the fuller meaning.

children.text:
ayamāśayaḥ /
pratyakṣagrahaṇayogyāstāvadasyāvayavāḥ pratyakṣānupalambhenaiva nirastāḥ /
atīndriyeṣvanumānaṃ pramāṇam, tacca dvividhaṃ samavyāptikamasamavyāptikaṃ ceti /
tatra yadyapi dvitīyasya nivṛttau na sādhyanivṛttiḥ, tathāpi prathamasya nivṛttāvavaśyaṃ nivarteta /
tathā hi, kvacidupalabhyamānasparśavattayā duvyasyārambhakatvaṃ kalpyeta /
ārambhake sati ca tat kāryadravyaṃ sāvayavaṃ vyavasthāpyeta, vāyuvat /
na ceha kvacidupalabhyamānasparśavattāstīti nārambhasaṃbhavaḥ, tadabhāve na sāvayavatvamākāśavat /
tadidamuktam---tadavayavakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāveneti /
na tāvadaṇviti /
vyāpakamityarthaḥ, viśeṣaniṣadhasya śeṣābhyanujñāviṣayatvāt /
kuta itya āha---tatra tatreti /
tathā satyeva hīcchādīnāṃ sārvatrikatvamupapadyate yata ityarthaḥ /
tadupapādayati--kvaciditi /
anyatarat śarīrādi /
kvacit svabhāvataḥ kāryadravyotpatterārabhya tatkaraṇasaṃyogādeḥ /
atha gatereva kiṃ na taṃ tamāpnotītyata āha---gatikalpanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt /
gatikalpanāpramāṇaṃ hi mūrtiḥ /
tayā aparidṛśyamānāpi gatiḥ kalpyate manasi paramāṇuṣu ca /
tadabhāvaścātmani /
children.translated_text: And its absence [obtains] in the <s>ātman</s> (self).

children.text: tathā hi, na paramāṇvāśrayā icchādayaḥ, anityatve satyasmadādipratyakṣatvāt, śabdavat /
children.translated_text: Thus: desire and the like do not have <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) as their substratum; because, being impermanent, they are perceptible to us and the like — like sound.

children.text: niravayavadravyāśritatvaṃ ca sādhayatā sāvayāśritatvaṃ prāgeva nirastam /
children.translated_text: And by one who establishes that [they] inhere in a partless substance, their inherence in a composite [substance] has already been refuted a fortiori.

children.text: ato 'mūrtatvānna gatisaṃbhavo mūrtergatyā samavyāptikatvāditi pūrvavanneyam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of incorporeality, there is no possibility of motion — since corporeality has co-extensive pervasion with motion — this [argument] should be understood as before.

The intention is this: to begin with, its parts that are fit for perceptual apprehension have been refuted by the very non-apprehension in perception. For supersensible [entities], inference is the <s>pramāṇa</s>, and that is of two kinds: with co-extensive pervasion and without co-extensive pervasion. Therein, although from the absence of the second [kind], there is no absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), nevertheless, from the absence of the first, [the <s>sādhya</s>] must certainly be absent. Thus: the capacity to initiate [a composite] substance might be postulated from the tangibility that is observed somewhere. And when there is an initiator, that product-substance would be established as composite, like <s>vāyu</s> (wind). But here there is no tangibility observed anywhere — therefore there is no possibility of initiation; in its absence, there is no compositeness, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space). This is what was said: 'because of the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> for postulating its parts.' 'Not even an atom' — the meaning is: the pervader; since the remainder of what negates the specific [pervader] is in the domain of [the general] permission. Whence? — to this he says: 'there, there.' The meaning is: only in such a case is the universal presence of desire and the like tenable — because. He demonstrates that: 'somewhere...' 'One or the other' — body and the like. Somewhere, naturally, from the beginning of the production of the product-substance, through the conjunction with its <s>karaṇa</s> (instrumental cause) and the like. Now, why should motion itself not reach that? — to this he says: 'because of the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> for postulating motion.' For the <s>pramāṇa</s> for postulating motion is corporeality (<s>mūrti</s>). Even motion that is not [directly] perceived is postulated in the mind and in <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) through that [corporeality].

children.text: nanu naitadekamapi vārttikasthamityata āha---tadetadādigrahaṇeti /
children.translated_text: Now, not even one of these [arguments] is found in the <s>Vārttika</s> — to this he says: 'this and the like are grasped by...'

children.text: nanu tathāpi kimanayā kaṣṭasṛṣṭyā, yāvatā guṇatvamanyathāpyamīṣāṃ sādhayituṃ śakyam? tathā hi icchādayo guṇā anityatve satyekendriyagrāhyajātimattvāt, rūpādivadityādinā ityata āha---tadanayeti //10 //
children.translated_text: Now, even so, what is the use of this tortuous line of reasoning, since <s>guṇatva</s> can be established for these [properties] by other means? Thus: desire and the like are <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), because, being impermanent, they possess a <s>jāti</s> (universal) apprehensible by a single sense-faculty — like color and the like — and so forth — to this he says: 'by this method...'

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Pariśuddhi</s>.

children.text:
yasya kṛte 'pavargo mṛgyate sa tāvallakṣitaḥ /
athedānī puruṣasyāpekṣitatamatvāt apavargo lakṣayitumucitaḥ /
tat kimantarāle śarīrādilakṣaṇamityata āha---ātmānamityādi /
apavargasyābhāvarūpatvāt pratiyogyadhīnanirūpaṇatayā duḥkhādapakarṣaḥ /
tasyāpi hetvadhīnotpattikatayā taddheturūpebhya indriyādibhyo 'pakarṣaḥ /
teṣāmapi śarīramāśritya tathābhāvāt śarīrādapakarṣa iti saṃgatisaṃkṣepaḥ /
sākṣāt śarīramāśrityeti /
children.translated_text: The senses directly depend on the body.

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ manasaḥ aṃśator'thādeḥ paramparayā tu śarīrāśritatvam /
children.translated_text: The senses, the mind, and parts of the objects — [these] depend on the body indirectly.

children.text: buddherdeṣāṇāmarthādyaṃśasya ca /
children.translated_text: And of cognition, of those [senses], and of the part that is the object.

children.text: asminnevārthe bhāṣyam ityāha---tadavatārāyeti //
children.translated_text: He says that the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is on this very topic: 'for the introduction of that...'

That for whose sake <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) is sought has been defined. Now, since <s>apavarga</s> is most desired by a person, it is appropriate to define it. Then why is the definition of body and the like in the interval? — to this he says: 'the self...' and so forth. Since <s>apavarga</s> has the nature of absence, by virtue of its characterization being dependent on its counter-correlate, it is the cessation of suffering and the like. And that too, by virtue of its arising being dependent on its causes, is the cessation from the causes in the form of the senses and the like. And since those too are so [i.e., arise] only in dependence on the body, the cessation from body and the like — this is the summary of the connection.

children.text:
atra hi ceṣṭāyāḥ śarīrāvyabhicārapakṣe arthendriyasamuccayo 'nupapannaḥ, sambhave vyabhicāre ca viśeṣaṇasyārthavattvāt /
samuccayapakṣe vyabhicāradarśinaḥ kathaṃ ceṣṭāśraya iti praśno 'nupapannaḥ, pratyekavyabhicāre satyeva hi samuccayasambhavāt /
ato vikalpaṃ gṛhītvā bhāṣyamutthāpayati---atreti /
yadyapi ceṣṭā kāyavyāpārastathāpi tasyaiva lakṣyatvāditaretarāśrayabhiyā vyāpāramātraṃ vaktavyamityāha---ceṣṭā vyāpāra iti /
prayuktasya iti satātparyaṃ padam /
ato vyācaṣṭe---prayuktasyotpāditaprayatnasyeti /
tena kāraṇadvārā ceṣṭānirūktiḥ /
prayatnavadātmasaṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇāntyāvayavikriyā ceṣṭā /
phaladvārā tu hitāhitaprāptiparihāraphaleti /
tadidamubhayaṃ vivakṣatoktam---api tu viśiṣṭo vyāpāra iti /
tena phaladvāranirūktau vyabhicārodāharaṇam /
dārūyantrādikāraṇadvāranirūktau tu prāṇākhyo vāyuḥ /
manaḥkaracaraṇādayastu antyāvayavipadenaiva nirastāḥ /
tatrobhayavyabhicāramudbhāvayan dārūyantrādītyahā /
dvayamapi pariharati---mūrtāntareti /
atra ca sparśavaddravyaparimāṇaṃ mūrtiriti paralakṣaṇābhiprāyeṇa mūrtiśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ /
tena ca sparśavaddravyāntarāprayoge satītyarthaḥ /
prayogaśca kriyaupayiko guṇaḥ /
sa ca dārūyantrādau nodanādiḥ /
prāṇe tu prayatnaḥ /
tena yadyapi śarīrasya prayojakaṃ mano 'styeva, tathāpi na tat sparśavat /
yadyapi ca śarīreṇāpi tatra prayatyate, tathāpi na tat tato 'nyat /
tadidam anyaragrahaṇaphalam /
ato nāsiddhaṃ viśeṣaṇamiti /
etacca yathāśrutaṃ bhāṣyavārttikānurodhena viśeṣaṇam /
āgāmivārttikaparyālocanāyāṃ tu ceṣṭāśabda evāyamevambhūter'thaviśeṣe vartata iti na nyūnaṃ sūtramāśaṅkanīyam /
children.translated_text: For here, on the view that <s>ceṣṭā</s> (bodily activity) is invariably [confined to] the body, the aggregation of objects and senses is untenable; and [this aggregation with the body] is purposeful as a qualifier both when [the invariable relation] is possible and when deviation [from it] is [possible]. On the aggregation view, for one who sees deviation, the question 'how is [the body] the locus of activity?' is untenable — for aggregation is possible precisely when there is individual deviation. Therefore, taking up the disjunction, he raises the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [question]: 'here...' Although <s>ceṣṭā</s> is bodily action (<s>kāyavyāpāra</s>), nevertheless, since it is what is to be defined, to avoid mutual dependence, only 'action' should be stated — so he says: '<s>ceṣṭā</s> is action.' 'Of one who is impelled' — this is the completing word. Therefore, he expounds: 'of one who is impelled, i.e., in whom effort has been produced.' Thereby, the definition of <s>ceṣṭā</s> is through the instrumental cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>). The action of the ultimate parts [of the body], having the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) of conjunction with the self possessing effort, is <s>ceṣṭā</s>. But through the result, [the definition is:] having the fruit of attaining and avoiding what is beneficial and harmful. This both-fold [definition] is stated with intention: 'but rather, a specific action.' Thereby, in the definition through result, [the instance of] deviation is cited. But in the definition through the instrumental cause, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital air), which is called <s>vāyu</s> (wind), [is cited as deviation]. Mental activity, bodily movement, and the like, however, are excluded by the very term 'of the ultimate parts.' Therein, bringing out the deviation from both, he says: 'wooden automaton and the like.' He resolves both: 'a different corporeal [entity]...' And here, the word '<s>mūrti</s>' is used with the intention of the opponent's definition, as 'corporeality is the measure of a tangible substance.' And thereby, the meaning is: when there is no employment of another tangible substance. And 'employment' is a quality useful for action — and that in wooden automata and the like is pushing and the like. But in <s>prāṇa</s>, it is effort. Therefore, although the mind exists as the instigator of the body, nevertheless, it is not tangible. And although effort is exerted even through the body [toward those ends], nevertheless, that [effort] is not different from it [the self]. This is the fruit of grasping 'different.' Therefore, the qualifier is not unestablished. And this is a qualifier as literally read, in accordance with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Vārttika</s>. But upon examination of the forthcoming <s>Vārttika</s>, the word '<s>ceṣṭā</s>' itself applies to an object-particular of such a nature — therefore, the <s>sūtra</s> should not be suspected of being deficient.

children.text: pāṣāṇetyādi /
children.translated_text: 'By <s>Pāṣāṇḍa</s>...' and so forth.

children.text: na ca tasyāpi prāṇitvenocchvāsaniḥśvāsānumānāt nayanodarādyavayavasaṃkocavikāśalakṣaṇā ceṣṭāstīti vācyam, ucchvāsaniḥśvāsāvakāśābhāvāt antyāvayavino niṣkriyatvācca /
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that even of that [<s>prāṇa</s>], because it is <s>prāṇa</s>, since it is inferred from inhalation and exhalation, there is bodily activity characterized by the contraction and expansion of parts such as the eyes, belly, and the like — because there is no room for inhalation and exhalation [in the case of the automaton], and because the ultimate parts are actionless.

children.text: api ca mṛtaśarīrāvyāptiparihārāya yogyataiva śaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, fitness alone is the recourse for avoiding the over-extension to dead bodies.

children.text: na codāharaṇamādaraṇīyamiti //
children.translated_text: Nor should the example be regarded [as authoritative] — thus [ends the discussion]. //

children.text:
nanu yadyapīndriyāṇi śarīre na samavayanti, tathāpi saṃyujyante /
tāvataiva āśrayārtha upapanna ityato vārttikakārasya bhāvamāviṣkaroti---saṃyogitayā tviti /
yadyapi golakasyābhidhāte 'pi cakṣurūpahanyate tadanugrahe cānugṛhyate, tathāpi viśeṣānupādānāt sarvendriyābhiprāyametad draṣṭavyam /
na hi golakamātrasyopadhāte 'nugrahe vā tvagādīnyupahanyante anugṛhyante vā /
children.translated_text: Now, even though the sense-organs do not inhere in the body, they are nevertheless conjoined [with it]. Since that alone suffices to establish the purpose of being a substratum — therefore he reveals the intention of the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>: 'by way of conjunction...' Although when the eyeball is damaged, the eye is impaired, and when it is supported, [the eye] is supported, nevertheless, since no specific [organ] is mentioned, this should be understood as referring to all the sense-organs. For it is not the case that by mere damage to or support of the eyeball alone, the skin and other [sense-organs] are impaired or supported.

children.text:
yathā jarāyauvanādinā śarīropaghātānugrahābhyāṃ sarvāṇi vikalāyante paṭūni vā sampadyanta iti /
tadetad bhāṣyavārttikakārābhyāmevānugṛhyante upahanyanta iti bahuvacanaprayogeṇa spaṣṭaṃ darśitamityupekṣitavān /
na svarūpeṇa śarīram āśrayanta iti /
avyāptyativyāptī vihāyeti śeṣaḥ /
nanu sukhādyupalabdhihetutvamarthānāṃ kāryopahitaṃ rūpam, na tu tadeva kāryamityata āha---prayojanaṃ tadadhikāreṇa tatra pravṛtteriti /
tadayaṃ lakṣaṇārthaḥ /
yadavacchinne ātmani arthā bhogaṃ janayanti taccharīram /
tena nātmanā vyabhicāraḥ /
na
children.translated_text: Just as through old age, youth, and the like — through damage to and support of the body — all [sense-organs] become impaired or become sharp. This very point has been clearly shown by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> and the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> through the use of the plural in 'are supported' and 'are impaired,' and therefore [the author] has set it aside. '[The sense-organs] do not rest in the body by their own nature' — setting aside under-extension and over-extension — this is the remainder. Now, the capacity of objects to be causes of the apprehension of pleasure and the like is a form superimposed by the effect, and not the effect itself — to this he says: 'the purpose is that [the soul] engages there through the governance of that.' This then is the meaning of the definition: that in which the self, being delimited, objects produce experience — that is the body. Therefore there is no deviation with respect to the self,

children.text:
hyātmātmanaivāvacchidyate /
nāpi manasā, tasya śarīrānavacchedena pravṛtterabhāvāt /
nāpīndriyaiḥ, tadavacchedena tatra bhogotpattau bahirapi bhogaprasaṅgaditi /
tadetat tasya bhogadhiṣṭhānamiti vadatā bhāṣyakṛtā eva prāk darśitaṃ sphuṭamiti
children.translated_text: for the self is not delimited by itself. Nor by the mind, since in the absence of the mind's delimitation by the body, there would be no engagement [of the mind]. Nor by the sense-organs, since if experience arose there through their delimitation, there would be the absurd consequence of experience even externally. This very point — that [the body] is the seat of experience — has been clearly shown earlier by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> who said 'the instrument of experience';

children.text:
neha vitanyate /
codayatīti /
arthagatiṃ samarthya śabdagatāviti śeṣaḥ /
ceṣṭādayaḥ sāmānyaśabdā iti vārttike bahuvacanaṃ dṛṣṭāntabrahmaṇādiśabdāntarbhāvena /
āśrayaśabdāvṛttibhedavivakṣayā vetyato mandāśaṅkatvādupekṣitam /
aśeṣabrāhmaṇabhojanasyāśakyatvādityanupapattivarṇanaṃ sampātāyātamasya pakṣasyāgre varṇanīyatvāt /
ata eva tadupekṣya prakṛtopayuktaṃ vivṛṇoti---viśeṣeṇeti /
bubhukṣitatvādinā sannidhīyamānamityanena sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Being proximate by virtue of being hungry and the like' — with this [phrase] the connection [is established].

children.text: atrānayoḥ prakaraṇādītyādipadasaṃgṛhītayormadhya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, of these two — [the word] 'etc.' in 'from context and so forth' includes [the term] 'intermediate' — that is the meaning.

children.text: pramāṇāsambhavo 'nupapattirbādha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The impossibility of a means of valid knowledge is an absurdity, a contradiction — that is the meaning.

children.text: yasyāpi pramāṇena śarīratvaṃ bādhitaṃ bhavati, tatrāpi vyāpāraśrayatvaṃ gatamiti //
children.translated_text: Even for that whose status as body has been refuted by a means of valid knowledge, the status of being a substratum of activity is [still] obtained — thus [ends the section]. //

it is not elaborated upon here. 'He raises an objection' — having considered the meaning of the matter, [he turns] to the verbal expression — this is the remainder. 'Effort and the like are general terms' — in the <s>Vārttika</s>, the plural is by inclusion of the words for examples such as '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' and the like. Or, with the intention of distinguishing the occurrences of the word '<s>āśraya</s>' (substratum) — therefore, since this doubt is feeble, it has been set aside. The description of impossibility — that the feeding of all <s>brāhmaṇas</s> without exception is impossible — has been passed over since this position, arrived at incidentally, is to be examined later. For that very reason, setting that aside, he explains what is relevant to the topic at hand: 'specifically...'

children.text:
atha samavāyābhiprāyeṇeti /
atra hīndriyāśraya iti ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣo bahuvrīhirvā /
tatra samavāyābhiprāyeṇobhayaṃ dūṣayati---tathāpīti /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
śarīrasyendriyeṣvityapi draṣṭavyam /
prathamapakṣe mūrtānāṃ samānadeśatāprasaḍgāt, ekasya dravyasya anārambhakatvāt, pṛthivyā abādidravyānārambhakatvācca /
dvitīyapakṣe tu vijātīyānām anārambhakatvāt /
śrotramanasordravyānārambhakatvādityarthaḥ /
indriyaviśeṣaṃ gṛhṇāti---ghrāṇasyeti /
śliṣṭaṃ vākyam /
atrāyamanuyogaḥ /
śarīrāvayavāntareṇa ghrāṇasya samavāyo vā saṃyogo vā? prathame 'pi dvayī gatiḥ, ghrāṇasya vā śarīrāvayave samavāyaḥ, tasya vā ghrāṇa iti /
tadetadanuyogadvayamabhipretyāha---na tasyeti /
śarīrāvayavasamavāyikāraṇatvena śarīre 'samavāyāt /
na hi kāraṇaṃ kāryakārye samavaitītyarthaḥ iti ṣaṣṭhatatpuruṣapakṣe /
bahuvrīhipakṣe 'pi śarīrasyāsamavāyāt /
na hi kāraṇakāraṇe kāryaṃ samavaitītyarthaḥ /
ghrāṇasya śarīrāvayave samavāya iti tu na sambhavatyeva, mūrtayorekāśrayatvānupapatterityatra ṭīkā sphuṭā /
saṃyogapakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti---atha tadādhāramiti /
tatra saṃyuktamityarthaḥ /
atrāpi dvayīgatiḥ, ārambhakatayā anārambhakatayā vā /
tatra prathamaṃ dūṣayati---tathāpīti /
ārabhyamāṇaṃ hi dravyamaindriyakairevāvayavairārabhyate yathā ghaṭaḥ /
atīndriyaireva vā yathā dvyaṇukādikam /
na tu miśrairiti vyāptiḥ, tāmupobdalayitumapratyakṣatvaprasaṅga uktaḥ /
anārambhe tu saṃyogidravyamātra syāt keśādivat /
tathā ca na tatra śarīrasamavāyasambhava iti kimanena śaḍkitenāpītyupekṣitavān /
etena śarīrasamavetametaditi nirastam, atīndriyadravyasyaindriyakeṇānārambhāt, ekadravyasya ca dravyasyābhāvāt /
alpaparimāṇasya mahatānārambhāt /
śarīravyāpakatve ca tasya sarvatra gandhopalabdhiprasaḍgāt /
api ceti /
yadyarthaśabdo rūpādimātravacanaḥ, tadaivaṃ dūṣaṇam /
yadā tvindriyaviṣayavacanaḥ, tadā vāyavīyaśarīrāvyāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: But when [the word '<s>artha</s>'] refers to the object of the sense-organ, then there is the under-extension with respect to the aerial body.

children.text: yoginastadapi tatheti yadi tadendriyaparamāṇubhireva vyabhicāraḥ, teṣāmapi tathābhāvāditi /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>yogin</s>'s [body] is also like that' — if [one objects that] even the atoms of the sense-organs [of the aerial body] constitute a counter-example, [the reply is:] because those too are of the same nature.

children.text: tadetatsarvaṃ śabdagatimupekṣya carcitam /
children.translated_text: All this has been discussed setting aside the verbal interpretation.

children.text: paramārthatastu yadi dvandvānantaraṃ bahuvrīhiḥ ka liṅgasaṅgatirarthasaṅgatiśca? atha prathamata eva bahuvrīhiḥ kkaikapadyamiti? //11 //
children.translated_text: But in ultimate truth, if a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound] follows immediately after a <s>dvandva</s>, what is the consistency of gender and consistency of meaning? If, on the other hand, it is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> from the very start, then how is there a single compound? // 11 //

Now, with the intention of [discussing] inherence — [he says:] 'here, the compound <s>indriyāśraya</s> (substratum of the sense-organ) is either a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> or a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>. In that case, with the intention of inherence, he refutes both [interpretations]: 'even so...' And this is an indication — 'of the body in the sense-organs' should also be understood. In the first alternative, because of the absurd consequence of co-location of corporeal [substances]; because one substance cannot be the cause [of another single substance]; and because earth cannot be the cause of non-earth substances. In the second alternative, because heterogeneous [substances] cannot be causes. The meaning is: because the ear and the mind cannot be causes of [other] substances. He specifies which sense-organ [is at issue]: 'of the olfactory organ...' The passage is compressed. Here is the inquiry: is the relation of the olfactory organ to another part of the body one of inherence or conjunction? In the first case too, there are two possibilities: either the olfactory organ inheres in the body-part, or the body-part inheres in the olfactory organ. Intending these two lines of inquiry, he says: 'not of that...' Because [the olfactory organ], being the inherent cause of the body-part, does not inhere in the body. For a cause does not inhere in the effect of [its own] effect — that is the meaning, on the genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> interpretation. On the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> interpretation too, [it does not inhere] in the body. For an effect does not inhere in the cause of [its own] cause — that is the meaning. As for the olfactory organ inhering in the body-part — that is simply not possible, since it is impossible for two corporeal [substances] to share a single substratum — here the <s>Ṭīkā</s> is clear. He takes up the conjunction alternative: 'now, that which supports it...' There the meaning is: conjoined. Here too there are two possibilities: either as a cause [of the body] or as a non-cause. Of these, he refutes the first: 'even so...' For a substance that is being produced is produced either by entirely perceptible parts alone, as in the case of a pot, or by entirely imperceptible [parts] alone, as in the case of dyads and the like. But not by mixed [parts] — this is the invariable rule; to undermine it, the absurd consequence of imperceptibility has been stated. In the case of non-causation, it would merely be a substance conjoined [with the body], like hair and the like. And in that case, since inherence in the body would not be possible — [the objection is:] what is even the point of raising this doubt? — therefore he has set it aside. By this, [the view that] this [olfactory organ] is inherent in the body is also refuted, since an imperceptible substance is not produced by perceptible [parts], and since a substance [produced] from a single substance does not exist, and since a substance of small magnitude cannot produce one of large [magnitude]. And if [the olfactory organ] were pervading the body, there would be the absurd consequence of perceiving smell everywhere. 'Moreover...' — if the word '<s>artha</s>' (object) refers only to color and the like, then this is the refutation.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
indriyasyeti /
kenacidupādhinā śarīrādīnāmeva phalatvamiti svabhāvikarūpapratītyadhīnatvāccaupādhikarūpapratīteḥ tebhyaḥ phalasyāpakarṣaḥ /
śarīrādīnāmeva dharmaḥ pretyabhāvo dharminirūpaṇādhīnatvācca dharmasya tebhyaḥ pretyabhāvasyāpakarṣaḥ /
arthādīnāṃ doṣāntānāṃ śarīramāśritya duḥkhahetutvāviśeṣe 'pi paramparayā śarīrāśriyatvādindriyāṇāṃ tu sākṣāt tathābhāvādebhyasteṣāmapakarṣaḥ /
manasastvevaṃrūpatve satyapi bāhyendriyavaidharmyajñāpanārthatvāt buddhikramānumeyatvācca buddheḥ sakāśādapakarṣaḥ /
tadidamuktam---upanāyakatveneti /
sākṣāccharīramāśritya pratiniyataviṣayādyupanayadvārā duḥkhahetutvenetyarthaḥ /
śarīrasaṃyuktaṃ saditi śeṣaḥ /
ato nobhayāvadhāraṇe bhāgāsiddhamasiddhaṃ veti doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the determination of both [alternatives], the fault of part-wise unestablishedness or [total] unestablishedness does not [arise].

children.text: sarpamaṇipradīpādīnāṃ tu saṃskārapadenaiva nirāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: The [objection from] serpent, gem, lamp, and the like is refuted by the very word '<s>saṃskāra</s>' (preparatory refinement).

children.text: etāvāṃstu viśeṣo yadañjanādīnāmindriyasaṃskārakatvam /
children.translated_text: But this much is the distinction: that collyrium and the like serve as refiners of the sense-organ,

children.text: pradīpādīnāṃ tu viṣayasaṃskārakatvamiti //
children.translated_text: while lamp and the like serve as refiners of the object. //

'Of the sense-organ...' Since [even] with some adventitious condition, it is the body and the like alone that are the fruits — and since the cognition of adventitious form depends on the cognition of intrinsic form — therefore [there is] the subordination of the fruit to those [body etc.]. The property of the body and the like alone is [their] cessation after death — and since a property depends on the determination of the property-bearer — therefore [there is] the subordination of cessation after death to those [body etc.]. Although <s>artha</s> (objects) and the other causes of suffering are equally causes of suffering by depending on the body, nevertheless, since the sense-organs depend on the body only indirectly while being directly [causes of suffering] — therefore [there is] the subordination of those [objects etc.] to these [sense-organs]. But as for the mind — although it is of such a nature — since [the purpose is] to indicate its difference from the external sense-organs, and since [the mind] is inferable through the sequence of cognitions — therefore [there is] its subordination to the intellect. This is what has been stated: 'by way of being an intermediary' — meaning: by directly depending on the body and through the intermediary of presenting the specific object, [the sense-organs] are causes of suffering. 'Being conjoined with the body' — this is the remainder.

children.text:
nanu bhāṣyakṛd āha---bhogasādhanānīti, tatkathametat tena sūcitamityata āha---sākṣāditi /
yadyapi bhujyeta
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> said 'instruments of experience' — how then is this indicated by him? — to this he says: 'directly...' Although 'that which is experienced' —

children.text: iti bhogau sukhaduḥkhe iti sākṣādeva bhogasādhanatvaṃ sarveṣāṃ sambhavati, tathāpi bhogo buddhiriti tatra tatra bhāṣyadarśanāt tadanusāreṇa vyācaṣṭe---pāramparyeṇa ceti //
children.translated_text: pleasure and pain are experience — and thus it is possible for all [categories] to be directly instruments of experience, nevertheless, since the <s>Bhāṣya</s> shows in various places that 'experience is cognition,' he explains in accordance with that: 'and indirectly...' //

children.text:
yathā ca sāmānyalakṣaṇamantareṇa na viśeṣalakṣaṇāvasaraḥ, tathā vibhāgamantareṇāpīti so 'pi vaktavyaḥ syāt /
tadetadevaṃlakṣaṇakamindriyaṃ bāhyamābhyantaraṃ cetīndriprakaraṇāt mano 'nyatra nayatā sūtrakṛtā eva sūcitam /
children.translated_text: And just as without the general definition there is no occasion for the specific definition, so too without the division [there is no occasion] — therefore that too should be stated. This very point — that the sense-organ having such a definition is external and internal — has been indicated by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> himself, who leads the mind elsewhere from the section on sense-organs.

children.text:
bāhyamapi pañcadheti /
gandharasarūpasparśaśabdā iti pratiniyatārthavibhāgaṃ kurvatā sūtrakṛtā eva darśitam /
yadi hyaparamapi bāhyam indriyaṃ syāt, kathaṃ pañcaiva pratiniyatā viṣayā iti tadeva vyavacchedyaṃ darśayanneva manāk smārayati,
children.translated_text: And that the external [sense-organs] are five-fold — by distinguishing the objects as smell, taste, color, touch, and sound, the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> himself has shown the division of specifically assigned objects. For if there were yet another external sense-organ, how could there be exactly five specifically assigned objects? Thus, showing the very thing to be excluded, he gently reminds:

children.text:
rasanādi pratiniyataviṣayam, mana ādi sarvaviṣayamiti ca /
ādigrahaṇena ātmaśarīre /
na tvātmādiprameyoddeśasūtre sāmānyenendriyamātramuddiṣṭam /
iha tu ghrāṇetyādyucyate /
tat kathaṃ tato na viśeṣa ityata āha---pramāṇādyudyeśeneti /
uddeśaviśeṣeṇa /
children.translated_text: by the specific enumeration.

children.text: atha vibhāgasūtratve 'pi lakṣaṇasūtraṃ kiṃ na syāt? na hyanayoḥ kaścid virodha ityata āha---lakṣaṇaṃ hīti /
children.translated_text: Now, even if it is a <s>sūtra</s> of division, why should it not be a <s>sūtra</s> of definition? For there is no conflict between the two — to this he says: 'for the definition...'

children.text: jñātaṃ coddiśyate vidhiviṣayatayā anūdyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is [already] known is enumerated — [meaning:] it is restated as the subject of an injunction — that is the meaning.

children.text: ajñātaṃ ca vidhīyate jñāpyata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And what is unknown is prescribed — [meaning:] it is made known — that is the meaning. //

the gustatory organ and the like have specifically assigned objects, while the mind and the like [apprehend] all objects. By the word 'etc.' [are meant] the self and the body. But in the <s>sūtra</s> listing the objects of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), only the sense-organ in general has been listed. Here, however, 'olfactory' and so forth are mentioned. How then is there no specific [distinction] from that? — to this he says: 'by the enumeration of the means of valid knowledge and the like,'

children.text:
parārthānumāne virodhamuktvā svārthānumāne 'pyāha---nāpi lakṣyalakṣaṇatve iti /
lakṣyasya pakṣarūpatayā sādhyatvāt, lakṣaṇasya ca liṅgarūpatayā siddhatvādityarthaḥ /
tathāpi kathamebhya eva padebhyo vivakṣitobhayalābha ityata āha---atra ceti /
kvacit kvacit sāmānyaviśeṣa iti /
jātirūpe sādharmyarūpe cetyarthaḥ /
tena śrotrapadamapyavayavārthaṃ nimittīkṛtya nabhaso viśiṣṭādṛṣṭopagṛhītakarṇaśaṣkulyavacchinnatve vartata iti /
tarhi yoga evāstvityata āha---avayavārthayoge 'pīti /
tathāpyubhayābhidhāyakatvāviśeṣe kathaṃ lakṣya--lakṣaṇapadavyavasthetyata āha---tathā ceti /
nanu kevalenāvayavārthena lakṣaṇe ativyāptiḥ, ghrāṇatvādisahitena tu itaretarāśrayatvamityata āha---na ceti /
sāmānyalakṣaṇayuktasyeti /
yāvatā vyabhicāro nivartate tāvadupalakṣaṇaparam, na tu samuccitaṃ padaṃ nirūcyate tvakpadaṃ tvanavayavaṃ vṛddhikṣayavaddravyasahajāvaraṇamātre vartata ityabhiprāyavatā bhāṣyakṛtā lakṣaṇaṃ tadbījaṃ ca darśitam /
tathāpi na prakṛtasiddhiḥ /
na hyevamapi lakṣya-lakṣaṇavyavasthā sidhyatītyata āha---nirvacanagrahaṇeneti /
kriyātvāditi kāryatvād ityarthaḥ /
saṃyogādhāratvāditi grāhyasya mṛgamadādigandhasya tatrāsamavāyāt mṛgamadādīnāṃ svāvayavasamavāyena samavetasamavāyābhāvāt /
svātantryeṇa grahe viśeṣaṇatvābhāvat aprāptasya cāgrahaṇāt /
itarasannikarṣatrayasya saṃyogagarbhatvāt saṃyogaḥ siddha evetyupakramaḥ /
atha ko niyamārthaḥ? kiṃ yajjātīyaṃ yadindriyaṃ tattajjātīyasyaiva guṇaviśeṣaṃ gṛhṇāti? atha yajjātīyaṃ yadindriyaṃ tajjātīyasya tenaiva guṇaviśeṣo gṛhyate ityata āha---na caivamiti /
yadyapi prathamamapyavadhāraṇaṃ ghrāṇaśravasoḥ saṃbhavati, tathāpi rasanādiṣu vyabhicārāt tadupekṣyottaraṃ grahītavyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having stated the contradiction in inference for the sake of others, he also states [it] in inference for one's own sake: 'nor in the case of the <s>lakṣya</s>-<s>lakṣaṇa</s> relationship...' Since the <s>lakṣya</s> (definiendum), being of the nature of the thesis, is what is to be established; and the <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (definition), being of the nature of the inferential mark, is already established — that is the meaning. 'Even so, how is the intended dual [purpose] obtained from these very words?' — to this he says: 'and here...' 'In some [cases] the general, in some the particular' — meaning: of the form of genus, and of the form of similarity. Therefore, the word '<s>śrotra</s>' (ear), taking the meaning of its component parts as the occasion, refers to the specific [organ] delimited by the ear-cavity, appropriated by a distinctive unseen force (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) from ether. 'Then let it just be etymological derivation' — to this he says: 'even in the derivation of the component meanings...' Even so, in the absence of a distinction [that would make one word] denote both [the general and the particular] — how is the assignment of the <s>lakṣya</s>-word and the <s>lakṣaṇa</s>-word [established]? — to this he says: 'and thus...' Now, with the component meaning alone as the definition, there is over-extension; but with [the component meaning] combined with olfactoriness (<s>ghrāṇatva</s>) and the like, there is mutual dependence — to this he says: 'and not...' 'Possessing the general definition' — to the extent that deviation is prevented, [the additional qualifier] serves as an indicator, but the word is not etymologically analyzed as a compound; the word '<s>tvak</s>' (skin), being non-compositional, refers to the mere covering inherent in the substance that is subject to growth and decay — with this intention, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> has shown the definition and its basis. 'Even so, the present thesis is not established' — for even thus, the assignment of <s>lakṣya</s> and <s>lakṣaṇa</s> is not established — to this he says: 'by the inclusion of the etymological explanation...' 'Because of being an action' means: because of being an effect — that is the meaning. 'Because of being the substratum of conjunction' — since the object to be grasped, namely the smell of musk and the like, does not inhere there [in the nose]; and since musk and the like, through inherence in their own parts, [have] no supervenient inherence [with the nose]; and since in independent grasping, there would be no status as a qualifier and what is not obtained cannot be grasped; and since the remaining three types of connection are embedded in conjunction — conjunction is established — this is the introduction. Now, what is the meaning of the restriction? Is it that whichever type of sense-organ [it is], it grasps only the specific quality of that same type? Or that whichever type of sense-organ [it is], the specific quality of that type is grasped by that [organ] alone? — to this he says: 'and not thus...' Although the first restriction too is possible for the olfactory and auditory organs, nevertheless, since there is deviation in the case of the gustatory organ and the like, that [first option] should be set aside and the latter [option] should be adopted — that is the meaning.

children.text:
tathāpi bhūtebhya iti sūtrapadasya kiṃ tātparyam ityata āha---anena khalviti /
yadyapi viśeṣasiddhireva śeṣaṃ niṣedhati, tathāpi viparyaye bādhakaṃ vaktavyamityata āha---nirākaraṇahetumāheti /
na tvekaprakṛtikatvamāha sāṃkhyo na tvekasvābhāvyamindriyāṇāmityata āha---śliṣṭaṃ padamiti /
ekaḥ pākyaḥ /
sarvasādhāraṇa iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Common to all' — this is the remainder.

children.text: evamuttaratrāpi /
children.translated_text: Likewise in what follows.

children.text: stokabhṛyasvaniḥśeṣatvena iti, prārabdhapākāpekṣayā /
children.translated_text: [The meaning is:] by virtue of the complete exhaustion of a small amount of merit — relative to the ripening already commenced.

children.text: tathā ca lakṣyahāniriti---na hyasti saṃbhavo nirhetuko vyavahāra iti bhāvaḥ //12 //
children.translated_text: And thus, the definition fails to apply — the meaning is: for there is no possibility of causeless usage. //12//

Even so, what is the purport of the <s>sūtra</s>-word 'from the elements' (<s>bhūtebhyaḥ</s>)? — to this he says: 'by this indeed...' Although the establishment of the specific [nature of each sense-organ] alone negates the rest, nevertheless, a refuting reason must be stated for the contrary [position] — to this he says: 'he states the reason for the refutation...' The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> does not say that [all sense-organs] have a single material cause — nor [does he say] that the sense-organs have a single nature — to this he says: 'it is a compressed expression...' '<s>Ekaḥ</s>' (one) [means:] one transformable [substance].

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> //

children.text: indriyaprakṛtitvaṃ bāhyendriyaprakṛtitvamiti //13 //
children.translated_text: The property of being the nature of sense-organs means the property of being the nature of external sense-organs. //13//

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> //

children.text:
pravṛtterdeṣāpakarṣe manasa pravṛttyapakarṣe vakṣyate /
buddhermano 'pakarṣe coktam /
viṣayanirūpaṇīyatvāccarthebhyo buddhedapakarṣaḥ /
tator'thalakṣaṇameva kramaprāptamityāha---kramaprāptamiti /
sūtre vibhāgabhāgasyāpi vidyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because in the <s>sūtra</s>, even the portion on division is present.

children.text: śliṣṭaṃ tu śabdārthamāha---yeṣāmiti /
children.translated_text: But he states the closely connected meaning of the words: 'of those.'

children.text: yeṣām uktalakṣaṇayogasta hame vibhajyanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that have the fitness of the stated definition — those are being classified — this is the meaning.

children.text: yeṣāṃ mithyājñānaviṣayīkṛtānāṃ nimittānuvyañjanasaṃjñāviṣayīkṛtānāṃ saṃsārahetutvaṃ ta hame lakṣyanta ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Those that have been made objects of false cognition, that have been made objects of the cognitions of marks (<s>nimitta</s>), secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), and designations (<s>saṃjñā</s>) — their being causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) — those are being defined — this is the meaning.

The withdrawal from activity is the withdrawal of the mind from defects of activity; the withdrawal of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) will be stated in the context of the withdrawal of the mind. And it has been said: because it is to be determined in terms of its objects, the withdrawal of <s>buddhi</s> from objects [follows]. Since what comes next in sequence is the definition of objects — he says: 'what comes in sequence.'

children.text:
tatra cādye pade vibhāgapare /
tatastadarthā iti lakṣaṇapadaṃ cet, lakṣyapadaṃ nāsti /
lakṣyapadaṃ cet, lakṣaṇaṃ nāsti ityata
children.translated_text: Now, in the first word [of the compound], which pertains to division — then, if the word 'definition' serves the purpose of that, there is no word for 'what is defined'; and if it is a word for 'what is defined,' there is no 'definition' — therefore

children.text:
āha---atra ceti /
arthānimittānuvyañjanasaṃjñāviṣayatayā saṃsārahetava ityarthaḥ /
ke te? ya indriyāṇāmarthā viṣayā ityarthaḥ /
āgāmino vārttikasya bhāṣyeṇa virodhaṃ parijihīrṣurāha---na ṣaṣṭhīti /
ghrāṇādayaḥ śabdā iti śeṣaḥ /
vyadhikaraṇabahuvrīhau na kevalaṃ lakṣaṇābhāvaḥ prayojanābhāvaścetyāha---na ceti /
children.translated_text: In a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound with different case-relations, not only is there absence of definition but also absence of purpose — he says: 'and not.'

children.text: tadarthā iti lakṣaṇamavyāpakaṃ syāditi /
children.translated_text: 'Having those as their purpose' — the definition would be non-pervasive — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadi vāyvādayaḥ paramārthator'thā iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The remainder is: if wind and the like are ultimately 'objects.'

children.text: ādigrahaṇena vāyvādisaṃgrahe lakṣaṇavibhāgayorvyāghāta ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: If wind and the like are included by the word 'and so forth,' there is contradiction between the definition and the division — this is the meaning.

he says: 'and here.' By virtue of being objects of the cognitions of marks, secondary marks, and designations of objects, they are causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the meaning. Which are they? Those that are the objects — the sense-objects — of the sense-organs — this is the meaning. Wishing to remove the contradiction of the forthcoming <s>Vārttika</s> with the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, he says: 'not in the genitive.' The remainder is: the words 'nose' and the like.

children.text:
eteṣāṃ cetyādi /
tadyathā, dantauṣṭhamityanurāgaḥ /
asthimāṃsamiti vairāgyam /
śyāmeti harṣaḥ /
pākajamidaṃ māṃsapārthivarūpamiti mādhyastham /
mukhāmoda iti pramodaḥ /
aupādhiko 'yamasya, sahajastu pūtiriti vaimukhyam /
aho
children.translated_text: 'Of these' and so forth. For instance: 'teeth and lips' — attachment. 'Bones and flesh' — dispassion. 'Dark-complexioned' — delight. 'This is a product of digestion, a form consisting of flesh and belonging to earth' — equanimity. 'Fragrance of the mouth' — joy. 'This [fragrance] of his is adventitious, while the natural [odor] is foul' — aversion. 'Ah,

children.text:
madhuramidam etanmukhāvarjitaṃ tāmbulamiti pravṛttiḥ /
ucchiṣṭamidamiti nivṛttiḥ /
preyasīsparśa ityutsavaḥ /
pārthivadravyamātrasparśa iti na kiñcit /
bahukeśītyanurāgaḥ /
majjadhātumalā hame bahavaḥ śmaśāne tarāviva śarīre saṃyuktā ityudvegaḥ /
pīnastanītyānandaḥ /
sphiḍnirviśeṣau palalapiṇḍāvityalaṃpratyayaḥ /
mṛtaśarīrādacetanāt pṛthagiyamiti harṣaḥ /
cetanādātmanaḥ pṛthagiyaṃ sahajaśavabhūtācetanādapṛthagbhāvastu bhrānta ityaratiḥ /
divyamālyābharaṇavasanavatīti prītiḥ /
pārthivaṃ pārthivena saṃyuktamiti viratiḥ /
hasatīti harṣaḥ /
asthimāṃsavibhāga iti viṣādaḥ /
mama priyā parāparā veti harṣaviṣādau /
śarīrāpekṣayā parāparabhāvo na madapekṣayeti na kiñcit /
nṛtyamiti ratiḥ /
satpratyayāsatpratyayakarmasantāno māyāśarīra iveti viratiḥ /
gamyajātīyeti strīti cotsāhaḥ /
tvaḍmāṃsaśoṇitasnāyvasthimajjaśukramūtrapurīṣasamudāyo 'yaṃ caṇḍālīsādhāraṇa ityalaṃbuddhiḥ /
vakrabhrūḥ ṛjuromarājī gabhīranābhirūnnatapayodharā pṛthunitambā kṛśamadhyeti snehaḥ /
annapānapariṇatiriyaṃ bhedomāṃsādyapacayāpacayasaṃsthānabhedavatī
children.translated_text: how sweet this is — a betel without this [impure] mouth' — engagement. 'This is defiled [by contact with the mouth]' — disengagement. 'The touch of a beloved' — festivity. 'The touch of mere earthly substance' — indifference. 'Rich-haired' — attraction. 'These hairs are impurities of the marrow-tissue, many of them attached to the body as to a tree in a cremation ground' — agitation. 'Full-breasted' — delight. 'The buttocks, no different from lumps of flesh' — the conviction of 'enough.' 'She is separate from a dead body, which is unconscious' — joy. 'She is separate from the conscious <s>ātman</s>, but her non-separation from the naturally corpse-like, unconscious [body] is an error' — disgust. 'Wearing divine garlands, ornaments, and garments' — affection. 'Earth conjoined with earth' — dispassion. 'She laughs' — joy. 'A partition of bones and flesh' — despondency. 'My beloved is inferior or superior' — joy and despondency. 'The inferiority-superiority is relative to the body, not to me' — indifference. 'She dances' — attachment. 'A continuum of actions producing true and false cognitions, like a body made of illusion' — detachment. 'She belongs to the class of those to be approached' — 'she is a woman' — enthusiasm. 'This is an aggregate of skin, flesh, blood, sinew, bone, marrow, semen, urine, and feces, common to a <s>caṇḍālī</s>' — the conviction of 'enough.' 'Curved eyebrows, straight line of body-hair, deep navel, upraised breasts, broad hips, slender waist' — affection. 'This is the transformation of food and drink, subject to differences of separation and decay of flesh and the like,

children.text: acirasthāyinīti nirveda iti nimattasaṃjñayā saha aśubhasaṃjñeti /
children.translated_text: not long-lasting' — disenchantment. Thus, together with the cognition of marks (<s>nimitta-saṃjñā</s>), [this constitutes] the cognition of unattractiveness (<s>aśubha-saṃjñā</s>).

children.text: anuvyañjanasaṃjñayāpi saha draṣṭavyeti //
children.translated_text: It should be seen together with the cognition of secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana-saṃjñā</s>) as well.

children.text:
asti tāvadiha darśanasparśanābhyāmekārthānusandhānam /
tadidamekaikaviṣayaṃ vā, samudāyaviṣayaṃ vā,
children.translated_text: Now, to begin with, there is here an investigation of a single object through sight and touch. Is this [investigation] directed at each individual [quality], or at the aggregate,

children.text: tadatiriktavastuviṣayaṃ vā, vastvanurodhākāraviṣayaṃ vā, atīkaviṣayaṃ veti?
children.translated_text: or at a thing beyond that [aggregate], or at a form that conforms to the thing, or at something unreal?

children.text: na tāvadādyaḥ, na hi bhavati yadeva rūpaṃ sa eva sparśa iti /
children.translated_text: Not the first, to begin with — for it is not the case that the very form [that is seen] is that very touch [that is felt].

children.text: na ca rūpaṃ dvīndriyagrāhyam, andhasyāpi nīlapītādiprayatyayaprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is form apprehensible by two sense-organs — because there would follow the consequence that even a blind person would have the cognition of blue, yellow, and the like.

children.text: na caikameva vastu kāraṇabhedādanyathā prathata iti yuktam, anātmakatvaprasaḍgāt, bhedābhedavyavasthānupapatteśca //
children.translated_text: Nor is it correct that one and the same thing appears differently due to difference of causes — because of the consequence of lacking intrinsic nature, and because of the impossibility of establishing [something as both] different and non-different.

children.text:
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, sa hyekadeśatayā vā, ekakālatayā vā, ekakāryatayā vā, ekakāraṇatayā veti /
na tāvadupādānalakṣaṇaikadeśasaṃbhavaḥ, tayoḥ pratiniyatopādānāt /
saṃbhave vā tadeva dravyamiti paryavasitaṃ vivādena /
nāpyadhikaraṇībhūtabhūtalādyādhāratayā tatsaṃbhavaḥ /
tathā hi cakṣuṣopalabhyamāne bhūtale rūpaviśeṣe ghaṭo 'pi cakṣuṣaivopalabhyamāno rūpaviśeṣastadādhāra iti śakyate niścetum, tayoradharottarabhāvena ekajñānasaṃsargitvāt /
tadadhikaraṇāḥ sparśādayo 'pīti tu kasya pramāṇasya viṣayaḥ? na hi sparśādayaścākṣuṣe cetasi cakāsati, tvaco 'yaṃ vyāpāra ityapi na yuktam, tayāpi bhūtale ghaṭasparśayorevādhārādheyabhāvapratīteḥ /
na ca samudāyayorevādhārādheyabhāvānubhavaḥ, parasparāśrayaprasaḍgāt ekādhāratayā samudāyānusandhānam, tadanusandhāne caikādhāratānubhava iti /
anavasthāprasaḍgācca, bhūlatasyāpi hi samudāyatvaṃ kiṅkṛtamityanuyogānivṛtteḥ /
ata eva naikakālatayāpi, tayorekakālatāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt /
bhāve vā rāsabhakarabhayorapyekakālatayā samudāyatvaprasaḍgāt /
bhedāgrahastvatrāsaṃbhāvita eva /
ata eva naikakāryatayāpi upadeyalakṣaṇasyaikasya kāryasyābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, not by virtue of having one effect either — because of the absence of a single effect characterized as what is to be sought.

children.text: ata evaikodakāraṇakriyetyādyapi na yuktam, rūpādyatiriktasyodakasyānabhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, 'because of having a single material-cause activity' and the like too is not correct — because water as something beyond form and the like is not accepted.

children.text: ekaikasyānekāhāryatve pramāṇābhāvāt, samudāyasya cāsiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: Because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for each individual [quality] being obtainable from many [sources], and because the aggregate is unestablished.

children.text: ata eva naikakāraṇatayāpi, nimittamantareṇa samudāyavyavahāre 'tiprasaḍgāt //
children.translated_text: For this very reason, not by virtue of having one cause either — because without a determining factor, the usage of 'aggregate' would be over-extended.

Nor the second [option, namely the aggregate]. For that would be either by virtue of being a part [of a common whole], or by virtue of simultaneity, or by virtue of having one effect, or by virtue of having one cause. Not, to begin with, is there the possibility of being a part in the sense of a material cause, since those two [form and touch] have fixed respective material causes. Or if it were possible, then the dispute comes down to: 'that itself is the substance.' Nor is their aggregation possible by virtue of being a substratum such as the ground and the like that serves as a locus. For thus: a pot too, being a specific form apprehended by the eye on a ground apprehended by the eye, can be ascertained as a substratum of that [ground], since both stand in the relation of lower and upper and enter into a single cognition. But that touch and the like are based on that [ground] — what <s>pramāṇa</s> has this as its object? For touch and the like do not shine forth in a visual cognition — nor is it correct [to say] 'this is the operation of the tactile [sense],' since even by that [tactile sense], only the substratum-superstratum relation of the ground and the touch of the pot is cognized. Nor is there an experience of the substratum-superstratum relation of the aggregates themselves — because of the consequence of mutual dependence: the investigation of the aggregate depends on a single substratum, and the experience of a single substratum depends on the investigation of the aggregate. And because of the consequence of infinite regress — for even the question 'what makes the ground an aggregate?' cannot be stopped. For this very reason, not by virtue of simultaneity either — because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for the simultaneity of those two. Or if there were, there would follow the consequence of aggregation of a donkey and a camel too by virtue of simultaneity. And the non-apprehension of difference here is simply inconceivable.

children.text: tṛtīye tu na vivādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Regarding the third [option, a thing beyond the aggregate], there is no dispute.

children.text:
nāpi caturthaḥ /
sa hi vijñānanayamāśritya vā syāt, dvicandrādivad visaṃvādād vā, sthairyavadbādhakād veti? ādye rūpādiṣu kaḥ pakṣapātaḥ? prāpterarthakriyāsthiteśca na dvitīyo 'pi /
te dve api rūpādīnāmeveti cet? na teṣāṃ kiṃ tu tasyaivetyeva kiṃ na syāt? bādhakāditi cet? sa yadi kramayaugapadyavirodhaḥ, kṣaṇikaṃ tāvadastu /
raktāraktādivirodhaścet? paramāṇurūpaṃ tāvadastu /
saṃbandhābhāva iti cet? asaṃbaddhaṃ tāvadastu /
kathaṃ tadvat pratīyeteti cet? taiḥ saha tathotpādāditi parihāro 'stu, bhavatāmeva yathā śarīraṃ cetanāvaditi /
rūpādibhireva samastārthakriyāsiddheḥ kiṃ tadatiriktavastukalpanayeti cet---na, tāvanmātreṇaiva samastārthakriyāsiddheḥ kiṃ rūpādikalpanayetyasyāpi vācāṭavacaso 'vakāśaprasaḍgāt /
pratīyamānatvāditi cet?
children.translated_text: Nor the fourth [option]. For would that be based on the idealist position (<s>vijñānavāda</s>), or because of being contradicted like double-moon [perception] and the like, or because of a sublating [cognition] like [the cognition of] stability? In the first case, what partiality is there regarding form and the like? Due to attainment and the persistence of causal efficacy, nor the second either. 'Those two also belong to form and the like' — if so said: why should it not be that they belong not to those but to that [substance] alone? 'Because of a sublating cognition' — if so: if that is the contradiction of succession and simultaneity, let the momentary [nature] be [accepted] for the time being. If it is the contradiction of colored and uncolored and the like — let the atomic form be [accepted] for the time being. 'Because of the absence of relation' — if so: let it be unrelated for the time being. 'How then would it be cognized as such?' — if so: let the answer be 'because of arising together with them in that manner' — just as you [accept that] the body [appears] as if conscious. Because all causal efficacy is accomplished by form and the like alone — what is the need for postulating a thing beyond them? — if so said: no, because the same flippant speech would apply equally: 'since all causal efficacy is accomplished by just that much alone, what is the need for postulating form and the like?' 'Because it is cognized' — if so said:

children.text: tulyam //
children.translated_text: the same [applies].

children.text:
etenaivālīkaviṣayatā nirastā /
abhedasādhanāni pramāṇāni bādhakamiti tu cintyata ityāśayavān paryanuyogārthamāha---svasaṃvedaneneti /
atra para āha anākalitasamaya iti śeṣaḥ /
anurañjanādikayā tviti /
atadrūpasya svarūpasaṃkrāntiḥ anurañjanam /
yathā nīladravyasamparkād dhavalo 'pi nīlo mahārajanasaṃparkādrakta iti /
children.translated_text: By this very [argument], the position that [the object] is unreal has been refuted. 'But the <s>pramāṇas</s> that establish non-difference are the sublating cognition' — this, however, needs to be considered — with this intention, for the purpose of cross-examination, he says: 'by self-awareness.' Here the opponent says — the remainder is: 'one who has not understood the convention.' 'By coloring and the like' — the transfer of one's own nature to what is not of that nature is coloring. Just as a white thing becomes blue through contact with a blue substance, or red through contact with red dye.

children.text:
atra nīlādayo dravyavyapadeśaṃ vihāya rūpavyapadeśameva labhante, nīlarūpaḥ paṭo raktarūpaḥ paṭa iti /
ādiśabdena gandhādīnāṃ vāsanādikāḥ vāsanādikāḥ kriyāḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ /
śabdagatidūṣaṇametaditi vibhāvayannirākaraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Here, blue and the like, abandoning the designation of substance, receive only the designation of form — 'a cloth of blue form,' 'a cloth of red form.' By the word 'and so forth,' the activities of scenting and the like of odor and the like are included. Showing that this is an objection to the argument's formulation,

children.text:
vivṛṇoti---tathārthasyeti /
arthagatirapi tridhā /
utpādamātraṃ vā, trailokyavilakṣaṇotpādo vā, sabhāgasantānabhedotpādo veti /
tatra dvayaṃ dūṣayatītyāha---dūṣaṇāntaramiti /
tṛtīyamutthāpayatītyāha---śaṅkata iti /
dṛṣṭisṛṣṭiviṣaye hi kasmiścid ghaṭa iti vyavahāraḥ /
sa cedanayā vacobhaḍgyātiriktaḥ samarthitaḥ, siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitamityāha---anyatva iti /
ananyatve vyarthābhidhānamiti /
tathā sati hi rūpaparamāṇavaḥ sparśaparamāṇavaścetyeva /
te ca kathamapyutpadyantām, na kadācidapi dvīndriyagrāhyāḥ /
samudāyaśca durūpapādaḥ /
tathā ca dṛṣṭisṛṣṭiviṣayo naikaḥ samarthitaḥ syāt /
ato niṣprayojanamuttarābhidhānamityarthaḥ /
śaṅkata ityādi /
yadyapi kṣaṇikaparamāṇurūpe dravye na kaścid vicāravirodhaḥ, tathāpi sthirāvayavyabhiprāyeṇa śaḍkā /
so 'pi hyasmākaṃ prasādhya iti /
ata evāha---ekānekavicārāsahatvāditi /
children.translated_text: For this very reason he says: 'because of inability to withstand the analysis of one and many.'

children.text: asanta iti upalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Non-existent' is merely indicative.

children.text: bāhyānanurodhijñānākārarūpā ityapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: It should also be seen as: 'having the form of a cognition-aspect that does not conform to the external.'

children.text: bījamiti //
children.translated_text: 'The seed.'

he elaborates the refutation: 'of the object thus.' The meaning of 'object' too is threefold: either mere origination, or origination distinct from the three worlds, or origination as a division of a homogeneous continuum. Of those, he refutes two — he says: 'another refutation.' He raises the third — he says: 'he doubts.' For in the domain of the doctrine of perception-creation, there is the usage 'pot' with respect to something. If that is established as something beyond [what is given in] this formulation of words — then our desired [conclusion] is established — he says: 'otherness.' If there is no otherness, the statement is purposeless — this is the meaning. For in that case, [there would be] just atoms of form and atoms of touch — nothing more. And let those originate somehow, [but] they are never apprehensible by two sense-organs. And the aggregate is hard to establish. And thus, not even one object of the doctrine of perception-creation would be established. Therefore the subsequent statement is purposeless — this is the meaning. 'He doubts' and so forth. Although in a substance that is momentary and atomic, there is no conflict from analysis, nevertheless the doubt is with the intention of a stable whole. For that too is to be established by us.

children.text:
atra prayogaḥ, ye ghaṭādipratyayā na satyāḥ, ta evambhūtasamyakpratyayapūrvakā mithyāpratyayatvāt, taimirikakeśapratyayavaditi /
atra copādhimudbhāvayati---yastviti /
yadyapi hi ādimānanādiriti vibhāgo 'nupapanna eva /
tathā hi keyamanāditā? kimevaṃrūpamithyājñānapravāhāvicchedaḥ, kiṃ vā pūrvamapyevaṃbhūtasya vibhramasya kadāpi
children.translated_text: Here the argument is: those cognitions of pots and the like that are not real — those are preceded by a veridical cognition of such a kind — because of being false cognitions — like the cognition of hair by one afflicted with an eye-disease (<s>timira</s>). And here he raises the condition (<s>upādhi</s>): 'but what.' For indeed, the division 'the first cognition has no beginning' is simply untenable. For thus — what is this beginninglessness? Is it the non-interruption of a stream of false cognition of such a kind, or is it that even previously, such an error

children.text:
bhāvaḥ? na tāvadādyo 'sambhavāt /
dvitīye tu taimirikakeśajñānamapyanādyeva /
anādau saṃsāre viplutasya keśajñānasyābhūtacaratvānupapatteḥ /
tathā cānāditā nopādhiḥ /
tasyāṃ satyāmapi keśajñānasya satyajñānanimittāpekṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: had existed at some time? Not the first, to begin with — because of impossibility. But in the second case, even the cognition of hair by one with an eye-disease would be beginningless. Since in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, the impossibility of the hair-cognition of one with disturbed [vision] never having occurred is untenable. And thus, beginninglessness is not a condition (<s>upādhi</s>). Even if it were present, because the hair-cognition also requires a cause in the form of a veridical cognition.

children.text:
na ca viparyaye bādhakābhāvād vibhramaśca syāt /
satyapratyayānanukārī ceti śaṅkayā bhavitavyamiti vācyam /
ananyathāsiddhānvayavyatirekānuvidhānasiddhakāraṇabhāvaparihāre mithyāpratyayānāmākasmikatvaprasaḍgāt /
satyapratyayānanukāre ghaṭādipratyayānāmapravartakatvaprasaḍgācca /
tathā hi mithyāpratyayā apyābhimānika pākṣikaṃ vā prāmāṇyamupādāyaiva pravartayeyaḥ /
vibhramatvaniścaye tvapravṛtteḥ /
na ca pramāṇānanukāre prāmāṇyābhimānasaṃśayaḥ /
na ca pramāṇabhedāgrahamātreṇa tattvābhimānasaṃbhavaḥ, visadṛśārthagocaratve tasyābhāvāt /
sadṛśārthagocaratve tu satyapratyayānukāro 'kāmenāpi svīkartavya iti /
tathāpi ghaṭādipratyayānāṃ satyatve kiṃ nibandhanā bauddhasyerṣyeti jijñāsuṃ pratibubodhayiṣurāhetyāha---taṃ pratīti /
avayavina iti dravyamātropalakṣaṇaparam /
yadyasmāditi vārttikam yattadorvyatyāsena sugamamevetyupekṣitavān /
vyaktyabhiprāyeṇānaikāntikatve dahanāyogolakamudāharaṇam /
vārttikoktaṃ tu vyāghātasphoraṇāya /
jātyabhiprāyeṇa buddhitadviṣayāvudāhāryau /
asti hi viṣayāgrahe buddhijātīyāgraho na cābhedobāhyasthitau satyāṃ guṇaguṇivādārambhāt /
dvividhāṇuḥ śabdātmako 'śabdātmakaśca /
tatrānantaro 'ṣṭadravyaka iti /
kavaḍīkārāhāraparyantāḥ kāmadhātavaḥ /
dhyānāhārā rūpadhātavaḥ /
ānandāhārā arūpadhātava iti vibhāgaḥ /
sā hīti /
yatastvayaivoktam,
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that in the case of error, due to the absence of a sublator, there would be delusion, and [one should] suspect 'it does not conform to veridical cognition.' For if the causal status established through agreement and difference, which cannot be otherwise accounted for, is set aside, there would follow the consequence that erroneous cognitions would be causeless. And there would follow the consequence that cognitions of pot and the like would not motivate action, since they would not conform to veridical cognition. For even erroneous cognitions motivate action only by presupposing presumed or provisional validity. But when error is ascertained, there is no activity. And when there is non-conformity with <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is no presumption or doubt of validity. Nor is a conviction of reality possible merely from the non-grasping of the distinction of <s>pramāṇas</s>, since that [conviction] is absent when the objects are dissimilar. But when the objects are similar, conformity with veridical cognition must be accepted even unwillingly. Even so, as to what grounds the Buddhist's envy regarding the reality of pot-cognitions and the like — intending to enlighten the inquirer, he speaks thus, he says: 'Toward that...' 'Of the possessor of parts' — this is intended as an indication of substance in general. The <s>vārttika</s> 'if, because' — that was set aside as easily understood by transposing the two [clauses]. As an illustration of inconclusiveness with reference to individuals, the fire-pot is the example. But what is stated in the <s>vārttika</s> is for revealing the self-contradiction. With reference to universals, cognition and its object are to be cited as examples. For when the object is not grasped, there is non-grasping of the class of cognition too; and given the external existence of non-difference, there would be no need for the distinction of quality and quality-bearer. Atoms are of two kinds: those constituted by sound and those not constituted by sound. Among these, the immediately following [atom] belongs to the eight substances. Those up to the stage of morseled food are beings of the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). Those sustained by meditation are beings of the form-realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>). Those sustained by bliss are beings of the formless realm (<s>arūpadhātu</s>) — this is the division. 'For that...' — because it was stated by you yourself,

children.text: pararūpaṃ svarūpeṇa dhiyā saṃvriyate yayā /
children.translated_text: by which the other-form is concealed by one's own form through cognition,

children.text: ekārthapratibhāsinyā tāmāhuḥ saṃvṛtiṃ kila //
children.translated_text: that which appears as having a single object — they call it <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional reality) indeed.

children.text:
ityarthaḥ /
udbhāvanaprakārasaṃkalanārthaṃ pūrvoktaikadeśaṃ smārayitvā paramatamavatārayati---tadevamiti /
tadatrānaikāntikatvena hetvābhāso nigrahasthānam /
tadabhyupetaprāmāṇyāgamavyāghātenāpasiddhāntaḥ /
tacchabdaparyālocanayā niṣprayojanatvenāpārthakam, pratijñāpadayorvyāghātena virodha iti /
children.translated_text: — this is the meaning. Having recalled a part of what was previously stated for the purpose of collecting the modes of demonstration, he introduces the opponent's view: 'That very thing, thus...' Therein, the inconclusive reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) constitutes a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>). The contradiction with the validity of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) accepted by the opponent himself constitutes a <s>prasiddhānta</s> (counter-established conclusion). Through the examination of words in that [argument], the purposelessness constitutes meaninglessness (<s>apārthaka</s>); through the contradiction between the thesis and the statement, there is <s>virodha</s> (contradiction).

children.text:
ānuśāsanikaṃ vacanabhedamādāya virodha udbhāvitaḥ /
tato na pāribhāṣikeṇa vyabhicāraśaḍkāsamānārthānāṃ prakṛtīnāmiti prakṛte 'bhyupagamavādaḥ /
utpannataddhitāyāḥ prakṛteradhikārthatvāt, spārthikasya pratyayasya nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt /
nanvāpa ityapi toyagatāmeva bahutvasaṃkhyāmācaṣṭām, ko doṣa ityata āha---ityekasyāmapīti /
yadyupanibandhena yadi toyaparamāṇāvapyāpa iti śiṣṭaprayogastadaivaṃ neyam /
vastutastu yathaikavacanāttoyamanuśāsanabalādasādhustathaikasaṃkhyāvacchinne pāthasyapīti na kaścid virodhaḥ /
dārā ityatra tveṣaiva yuktirityarthaḥ /
krandata ityanādare ṣaṣṭhī /
bhavata iti pūraṇīyam /
children.translated_text: A contradiction was demonstrated by taking a grammatical distinction of statement. Therefore, it should not [be objected] that through the technical [sense], the roots — which have the same meaning as the suspicion of deviation — [pose a problem] in the topic at hand, [since] this is an argument by acceptance. Because the root with the secondary suffix added has additional meaning, and because the suffix in the sense of possession will be refuted. Now, 'waters' (<s>āpaḥ</s>) also designates the plural number with reference to water alone — what is the fault? — to this he says: 'Even in a single one...' If through convention, if even regarding a single water-atom the learned usage 'waters' (<s>āpaḥ</s>) [obtains], then it should be interpreted thus. But in reality, just as from the singular 'water' (<s>toyam</s>), by the force of grammatical teaching, the usage is not faulty, so too even regarding what is delimited by the singular number, for 'water' (<s>pāthas</s>) — there is no contradiction at all. But in the case of 'wife' (<s>dāra</s>), this very reasoning [applies] — that is the meaning. In '<s>krandataḥ</s>' ('of the weeping one'), the genitive is in the sense of disregard. '<s>Bhavataḥ</s>' ('of you') should be supplied.
