children.text: ṣaṇṇagarītyādiṣu tu sugamameva, samāhāre samāsānuśāsanāt /
children.translated_text: But in cases like 'six-citied' (<s>ṣaṇṇagarī</s>) and the like, it is easily understood, because of the grammatical teaching of compounds in the collective sense.

children.text: sa ca samāhriyamāṇārthātirikta evābhyupagamyate 'smābhiḥ //
children.translated_text: And that [collective entity] is accepted by us as indeed different from the meanings of the components being collected.

children.text: yadi yathālokavyavahāramādriyase, kimiti savikalpakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ pariharasi? kutaśca na śabdādīni pramāṇāni
children.translated_text: If you defer to worldly practical usage, why do you reject determinate perception (<s>savikalpaka pratyakṣa</s>)? And why do you not accept verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) and the like as <s>pramāṇas</s>

children.text:
pṛthagevābhyupagacchasītyāha---anyatheti /
vārttikoktodāharaṇānurodhenāhnīkaṃ pratyāha---na ca nīlasyeti /
vastutastu pītaśaḍkhavibhrame ayam api na pītasyaiva śaḍkhasyotpādamicchati, puruṣāntareṇāpi tathopalambhaprasaḍgāt /
tato
children.translated_text: independently? — he says: 'Otherwise...' In accordance with the example stated in the <s>vārttika</s>, he responds to the day's [objection]: 'And not of the blue...' But in reality, in the delusion of the yellow conch, [the opponent] too does not intend the production of the yellow alone in the conch, since even another person would perceive it thus. Therefore,

children.text:
dhavalimni pratīte 'pi tadāśrayaṃ śaḍkhadravyamabhipretyetyeva /
toyaviraha ityādi /
na caitad vaidharmyamātram, upaṣṭambhakasyāvinirbhāgenaivāvasthānaniyamāt /
yathā hemni pārthivo bhāgaḥ /
taile payasi sarpiṣi ca pāthasīyaḥ /
na ca saṃyogimātraṃ yūṣe jalam /
tadasaṃyoge yūṣatvanivṛtteriti tairvyapadeśaḥ /
tairviśeṣaṇaistasya vyavacchedyasya vyavacchedaḥ /
sa cātrānubhaviko vivakṣitaḥ /
sa hyevaṃ pravartate, candano 'yaṃ surabhiḥ, tiktaḥ, śuklaḥ, śītaḥ iti /
tādātmyabhramanirāsārthaṃ tu śabdo vyapadeśakatayopāttaḥ, candanasya śuklaṃ rūpamityādi /
etaccāgambhīramiti matvā yathāśrutamevopādāya tātparyamahā---asti hīti /
na kevalaṃ hetusvarūpālocanena pratijñālocanenāpi candanasyopālambhābhyupagamo 'vasīyate parasya /
na hyanupalabdhasyaiva rūpādyabhedaṃ sādhayati /
tathā satyaprasiddhaviśeṣyaḥ pakṣaḥ syāt /
svātantryeṇa vā sattve sādhye āśrayāsiddho heturiti tṛtīye vyutpādanīyamiti ihopekṣitavāniti /
ekāntato vyapadeśaṃ vyāvartayitumiti prayogāntarasūcanāya /
tathā hi, ayaṃ cakṣurgocaraḥ candano rasādibhyo bhidyate, tadanupalambhe 'pyetasyopalabhyamānatvāt /
yadyasminnanupalabhyamāne 'pyupalabhyate tat tato bhidyate, yathā rūpādibhyaḥ śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is perceived even when something [else] is not perceived, that differs from that [other], just as sound [differs] from form and the like.

children.text: tathā cāyaṃ candanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And so this sandalwood [differs thus].

children.text: tasmāt tatheti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is so.

children.text: spamātrāttu vyavacchedaḥ sandigdhaḥ tatra vyapadeśo heturiti //
children.translated_text: But from mere designation, the delimitation is doubtful — there, designation is the reason.

even when whiteness is perceived, it is with reference to the conch-substance that is its substratum — just so. 'Absence of water...' and so forth. And this is not merely a point of dissimilarity, because of the rule that what supports [a quality] remains inseparably present. Just as the earthy component in gold. The watery component in oil, milk, and ghee. And it is not mere conjunction that [constitutes] water in broth — because upon its non-conjunction, broth-ness would cease — this is their account. By those qualifiers, the delimitation of what is to be delimited. And that [delimitation] here is intended as experiential. For it operates thus: 'this is sandalwood — fragrant, bitter, white, cool.' But to remove the error of identity, the word is employed in a descriptive capacity, like 'the white color of sandalwood' and so forth. And considering this to be not profound, he takes it as stated and states the purport: 'For indeed...' Not only by examining the nature of the reason, but by examining the thesis too, the opponent's acceptance of the censure of sandalwood is ascertained. For one does not establish non-difference from form and the like of what has not even been perceived. In that case, the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) would have an unestablished qualifier. Or, if existence were independently the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), the reason would have an unestablished substratum — [this] should have been explained in the third [section], but was set aside here. 'To exclude designation absolutely' — [this is] for suggesting an alternative proof. Namely: this sandalwood, being an object of vision, differs from taste and the like, because even when those are not perceived, this is perceived.

children.text:
prayogāntaramāheti /
vailakṣaṇyasya hetorvyaktyapekṣayānaikāntikatvāt, jātyapekṣayā asiddhatvāt, viṣayavailakṣaṇyasya ca sādhyatvāt /
tadāhitākāralakṣaṇasyānabhyupagamādityāśayavāniti śeṣaḥ /
atra ca hetutayā vyāpti pradhānīkṛtya ṣaṣṭhyanto heturūktaḥ /
pañcamyantaśca sādhyaḥ /
parvato 'yamagnimān /
kasmāt? dhūmavattvāt /
kiṃ kāraṇam? dhūmavato 'gnimattvāditivat /
granthagauravabhiyā tu yathāśrutaṃ vyācaṣṭe---ghaṭapratyayasyeti /
viṣayo ghaṭa eva /
nimittaṃ ghaṭatvam /
taddhi nimittīkṛtya ghaṭapratyayo ghaṭe vartate /
ghaṭapratyayastvanubhavaḥ smaraṇaṃ ca /
tadiyaṃ prayogapariśuddhiḥ /
ghaṭādiṣvekādipratyayā uktanimittavyatiriktapravṛttinimittādhīnajanmānaḥ, uktanimittam antareṇāpi jāyamānatvāt /
teṣveva ghaṭādiṣu nīlādiṣu nīlādipratyayavaditi /
atra yadi ghaṭamanatareṇāpi jāyamānatvādityetāvanmātraṃ kriyeta tadaikaghaṭaparityāge ghaṭāntare jāyamānaghaṭapratyayena vyabhicāraḥ, tathābhūtasyāpi nimittāntarānapekṣatvāt /
tannimittam antareṇetyetāvanmātre tu ghaṭanirvikalpakena vyabhicāraḥ, tasya tannimittanirapekṣasyāpi nimittāntarānapekṣaṇāt /
tatpratyayamantareṇetyetāvanmātre 'pi tenaiva vyabhicāraḥ /
prathamadvitīyapadopādāne 'pi tatsmaraṇānuvyavasāyavibhramairvyabhicāraḥ /
tatpratyayaviṣayanimittavyatirekeṇāpi teṣāṃ janma /
na ca pravṛttinimittāntarāpekṣā /
dvitīyatṛtīyayorapi nirvikalpakena vyabhicāraḥ /
prathamatṛtīyayorapi ghaṭāntarapratyayena vyabhicāra iti samastopādānam /
ato yannyūnaṃ tatpūrayati---bhāja ityatrāpīti /
tadetadghaṭādi pratyayavailakṣaṇyamekādipratyayānāmiti /
sthāṇurdravyamityevaṃ sādhu /
na ca jātisaṃkaraḥ, tatra khadirajāterabhāsāt /
tadguṇayogāt tu tadvyavahāro māṇavake siṃhavyavahāravat tadavayavārabdhatvāt tadīyatāvyavahāraḥ kṣīrasya dadhīvivat /
sarpeṇāntyāvayavinā ekenānārambhāt tadavayavānāṃ kāryāvaṣṭabdhatvāt sarpakuṇḍalakaṃ saṃsthānameva sphuṭam /
pratimāyā iti /
śarīralakṣaṇābhāvāt na tatra mukhyaḥ śarīraśabdaḥ, tadekārthasamavesaṃsthāne aupacārika iha prayujyate, tatsādṛśyāt /
rāhoḥ śira ityatra tu saṃsthāne śiraḥ śabdopacāramātram /
children.translated_text: But in '<s>Rāhu's</s> head,' it is merely a figurative usage of the word 'head' for the configuration.

children.text: suvarṇāsyāḍgurīyakamityatra jātisaṅkaprasaḍgāt saṃsthānamevāḍgurīyakam, rajatāderapyaḍgurīyakadarśanāditi sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: In 'a gold ring,' because of the consequence of intermixture of universals, ring-ness is just the configuration — since rings of silver and the like are also observed — this is clear.

children.text: śilāputrakasyetyatroktayukti smārayannāha---evamiti /
children.translated_text: In the case of 'stone child' — recalling the reasoning already stated, he says: 'Thus...'

children.text: vyatirekopadeśaviveko yadi syāt tadā buddhiśarīrābhyāmevānaikāntikaṃ syādata āha---atādātmyeti //14 //
children.translated_text: If there were a distinction in the teaching of negative concomitance, then it would be inconclusive through cognition and body alone — to this he says: 'Non-identity...'

He states an alternative proof — because of the inconclusiveness of the reason 'dissimilarity' with reference to individuals, because of its unestablished-ness with reference to universals, and because the dissimilarity of objects is itself the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). The intention is that [the opponent] does not accept it as characterized by the form imposed by that [object] — this is the remainder. And here, the reason is stated with a genitive ending, giving prominence to pervasion as the reason. And the <s>sādhya</s> is stated with an ablative ending. 'This mountain possesses fire. Why? Because of possessing smoke. For what reason? Because what possesses smoke possesses fire' — just so. But fearing verbosity, he explains it as stated: 'Of the pot-cognition...' The object is the pot itself. The ground (<s>nimitta</s>) is pot-ness. For it is by taking pot-ness as the ground that the pot-cognition pertains to the pot. But pot-cognition includes both experience and memory. This then is the purification of the proof: cognitions of unity and the like regarding pots and the like are dependent for their origination on a ground of activity different from the stated ground, because they arise even without the stated ground. In those very pots and the like, [they arise] like the blue-cognition in blue things and the like. Here, if only 'because of arising even without the pot' were stated, there would be deviation by the pot-cognition arising in another pot when one pot is abandoned, since even what is of such a nature is independent of another ground. And if only 'without that ground' were stated, there would be deviation by the indeterminate perception of the pot, since even though independent of that ground, it is also independent of another ground. And if only 'without that cognition' were stated, there would be deviation by that very [indeterminate perception]. Even when the first and second terms are included, there would be deviation by the memory, reflective apprehension, and error regarding that [pot]. For the origination of those is independent of the ground of the cognition's object. And the dependence on another ground of activity [does not hold]. Even of the second and third [terms], there would be deviation by the indeterminate perception. Even of the first and third, there would be deviation by the cognition of another pot — hence all [terms] must be included. Therefore, what is deficient, he supplies: 'In the case of the bowl too...' This then is the dissimilarity of pot-cognitions and the like from cognitions of unity and the like. '<s>Sthāṇu</s> is a substance' — this is correct. And there is no intermixture of universals, because the <s>khadira</s> universal does not appear there. But because of connection with its qualities, the designation is like the designation 'lion' for a boy — because of being constituted by its parts, the designation of belonging to it, like curds from milk. Since the final part, the serpent, does not constitute [the whole], the coiled shape of the serpent is clearly just a configuration, because the parts of the serpent are sustained by the [prior] product. 'Of the image...' — because the defining characteristics of a body are absent there, the primary word 'body' does not apply; because it has a configuration co-extensive with that [body], the figurative [usage] is employed here, because of similarity to that.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
arthakathanapūrvakaṃ saṅgativārttikamavatārayati---ātmādīnāmiti /
kāraṇatve 'pi manaso 'pakarṣe tūktam /
children.translated_text: Having stated the meaning first, he introduces the <s>vārttika</s> on connection: 'Of the self and the like...' Although the mind is [accepted as] a cause, its inferiority has been stated.

children.text:
sarvajanīnenāpi samayena gośabdavad yadyarthāntare 'pyete pravarteran tadā ko virodha ityata āha---tatra sarvajanīnaḥ śaknotīti /
svābhidheyadvāreṇeti śeṣaḥ /
tenāyamarthaḥ /
eteṣāṃ śabdānāṃ vyavahriyamāṇānāṃ yadekaṃ pravṛttinimittaṃ
children.translated_text: Even by universal convention, if these [words] like the word 'cow' were to apply to other objects too, what would be the contradiction? — to this he says: 'There, universal convention is capable...' The remainder is: 'through the medium of its own denotatum.' Therefore this is the meaning: of these words being used, that one ground of activity

children.text:
tadyogād itarebhyo buddhirbhidyata iti /
tadidamuktaṃ sūtrakṛtā---ityanarthāntaramiti /
tenaitannirastam /
gṛhītasamayairebhirbṛddhiḥ samānāsamānajātoyebhyo vyāvartanīyā /
tathābhūtāyāṃ ca tasyāmeteṣāṃ samayo grāhya ityanyonyāśrayatvam /
vyavahāre tu sādhye
children.translated_text: — by connection with which, cognition differs from others — thus. This is what was stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras): 'Thus it is not a different matter.' By this, the following is refuted: by those who have grasped convention, cognition must be distinguished from those of the same and different universals. And when such [cognition obtains], the convention of these [words] is to be grasped — thus there is mutual dependence. But when practical usage is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum),

children.text:
ātmāśrayatvamiti /
tarhi buddhirjñānamityevāstu kimanekaśabdoccāraṇenetyāśaḍkya paramatamapākartṛm ityāha---bhāṣyakāra eveti sphuṭamiti---upapattisārthyāditi bhāṣyāvayayavaṃ vyācaṣṭe---paryāyeti /
tatropapattipadārthaḥ paryāyaśabdābhidhānamityanene vyākhyātaḥ /
śeṣeṇa sāmarthyapadārthaḥ /
tenāyamarthaḥ, paryāyaśabdābhidhānalakṣaṇāyā upapatteḥ sāmarthyam anekārthatvapratiṣedhākṣepakatvam /
tasmāditi /
children.translated_text: there is self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>). 'Then let cognition, knowledge — just this much suffice; what is the need for uttering multiple words?' — anticipating this, in order to set aside the opponent's view, he says: 'The <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) himself...' — this is clear. '...from the force of reasoning and capacity' — he explains the passage of the <s>bhāṣya</s>: 'Synonyms...' There, the meaning of the word 'reasoning' (<s>upapatti</s>) is explained by 'designation by synonyms.' By the remainder, the meaning of the word 'capacity' (<s>sāmarthya</s>) [is explained]. Therefore this is the meaning: the capacity of the reasoning characterized by designation through synonyms is [its power of] negating multiplicity of meaning. 'Therefore...'

children.text:
tadetannirākāraṇaṃ sūcitam /
yadupapattisādhyaṃ tāṃ pṛcchati vārttikakāraḥ---kā punarūpapattiratreti /
nirvikalpakavyāpārāṇīndriyāṇi /
savikalpakavyāpāraṃ manaḥ /
adhikārābhimānavyāpāro 'haṅkāraḥ /
kṛtyadhyavasāyavyāpārā buddhiḥ /
nirvyāpāra eva kalpitabuddhivyāpāraḥ puruṣa iti /
tenāyamarthaḥ, akāraṇam akāryaśca puruṣaḥ /
ādikāraṇaṃ prakṛtiḥ /
ādikāryaṃ buddhiḥ /
tato 'haṅkārādisarga iti /
puruṣaḥ kūṭasthacaitanyarūpaḥ /
itaradacetanamiti sākhyāḥ /
tatra buddhiraṃśatrayavatī, puruṣoparāgo viṣayoparāgo vyāpārāveśaścetyaṃśāḥ /
bhavati hi mayedaṃ kartavyamiti /
mayeti hi cetanoparāgo darpaṇasyeva mukhoparāgo bhedāgrahādatāttvikaḥ /
idamiti viṣayoparāgaḥ indriyapraṇālikayā pariṇātibhedo darpaṇasyeva malasaṃbandhaḥ pāramārthikaḥ /
tadubhayāyatto vyāpārāveśo 'pīti /
tatraivaṃrūpavyāpāralakṣaṇā buddhiḥ /
viṣayoparālakṣaṇaṃ jñānam /
tena saha yaḥ puruṣoparāgasyātāttvikasya saṃbandho darpaṇapratibimbitasya mukhasyeva tadgatamalinimnā sopalabdhiriti teṣāṃ rahasyam /
tadutthāpayati---buddhiḥ kileti /
sā ca na tāvad buddheḥ, tasyā acaitanyāditi /
yadyapyacetana eva bhrāmyatīti sāṃkhyābhyupagamo yathāhuḥ,
children.translated_text: This refutation has been indicated. The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> asks for the justification that is to be proved by reasoning: "What then is the justification here?" The sense-organs have the operation of indeterminate cognition. The mind has the operation of determinate cognition. The ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) has the operation of the presumption of authority. The intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) has the operation of determining what is to be done. The <s>Puruṣa</s> has no operation at all — [his] operation in the intellect is merely imagined. The meaning of this is: <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither a cause nor an effect. <s>Prakṛti</s> is the first cause. <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is the first effect. Then the creation of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and the rest. <s>Puruṣa</s> is of the nature of immutable consciousness. Everything else is non-conscious — thus say the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>. There, the intellect possesses three aspects: the coloring by <s>Puruṣa</s>, the coloring by the object, and the infusion of operation — these are the aspects. For there is [the experience]: "I should do this." "I" — this is the coloring by the conscious [<s>Puruṣa</s>], like the coloring of a mirror by a face — unreal due to non-apprehension of difference. "This" — this is the coloring by the object, a modification through the channel of the sense-organs, like the connection of a mirror with impurity — real. The infusion of operation too is dependent on both of those. Among these, the intellect is characterized by operation of such a form. Knowledge is characterized by the coloring by the object. The connection of the unreal coloring by <s>Puruṣa</s> with that [knowledge] — like the [connection of] the reflected face in a mirror with the impurity therein — is apprehension. This is the secret of those [<s>Sāṃkhyas</s>]. He raises this: "The intellect, it is claimed..." And that [apprehension] is not of the intellect, to begin with, since it is non-conscious. Although the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position is that it is the non-conscious alone that is deluded, as they say:

children.text: yogaścittavṛttinirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Yoga</s> is the cessation of the modifications of the mind,"

children.text: iti, tāstu
children.translated_text: — and those [modifications] are:

children.text: pramāṇasaṃśayaviparyayasvapnasmṛtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "valid cognition, doubt, error, sleep, and memory,"

children.text:
iti, tathāpi vyāptyā pratyavasthānam /
yatra hi cetanācetanayorasaṃsargāgrahe saṃsargabhramaḥ, tādātmyabhramo vā, tatra cetanasyaiva, yathā darpaṇacaitrayoḥ śarīraśarīriṇorvā /
na hi tatra darpaṇasya śarīrasya vā bhrama iti /
api ca buddhirātmānaṃ cetayamānā bhrāmyet, puruṣeṇa vā cetyamānā /
nobhayamapi prāguktayuktereva /
children.translated_text: Neither alternative [is tenable], by the very reasoning previously stated.

children.text: na ca svataḥ parato vā aprakāśamānaiva buddhirbhrāmyatīti yuktam /
children.translated_text: And it is not reasonable that the intellect, not being illuminated either by itself or by another, could be deluded.

children.text: na hyadṛśyamāna eva darpaṇaḥ timire maitrasannidhānamātreṇa tatpratibimbamudgrāhayati /
children.translated_text: For a mirror that is not being seen, in darkness, does not generate a reflection merely by the proximity of <s>Maitra</s>.

children.text: tasmādubhayathāpi buddheḥ sahajaṃ caitanyamāpannamityupasaṃhāravyājenāha---tasmāt kṛpaṇeti //15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in both cases, the intellect has acquired innate consciousness — he says, under the guise of a conclusion: "Therefore, pitiable..."

— nevertheless, the counter-argument [is made] through pervasion. For where, in the non-apprehension of the contact of the conscious and the non-conscious, there is a delusion of contact or a delusion of identity — there [the delusion belongs to] the conscious alone, as with a mirror and <s>Caitra</s>, or with a body and the embodied. For there, it is not the mirror or the body that is deluded. Moreover, the intellect would be deluded either when it makes itself conscious, or when made conscious by <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: vaidharmyādindriyaprakaraṇādapasāritasya buddhikramonneyatayā pravṛttihetutayā ca tayoḥ madhyer'thādavasaro manasa ityāha---kramapraptamiti //
children.translated_text: Having been moved away from the sense-organ section by dissimilarity, and since [the mind] is to be inferred through the sequence of cognitions and serves as a cause of activity, there is occasion for it between those two [sense-organs and objects] — he says [this is] by implication.

children.text:
yasmādityādivārttikaṃ vākyabhedena sūtrakāroktasvoktahetupapādakabhāṣyavyākhyānamityāha---anindriyeti /
yadyapi nimittāntaramityanenaivākāśo 'pi vyavacchidyate, avyāpītyanenaiva vā, sahakārītyanenaivātmādi, upādānātiriktasyaiva sahakāritvaprasiddheḥ, tathāpi yathāvivakṣaṃ gobalīvardanyāyena vyavasthā /
indriyaṃ pradhānīkṛtya vā ātmani sahakārivāda iti /
nanu mano vibhu sarvadā sparśarahitadravyatvāt, viśeṣaguṇaśūnyadravyatvāt, nityatve satyanārambhakadravyatvāt, jñānasamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogādhāratvāt ityādeḥ /
tatkathamucyate---avyāpīti /
naitadevaṃ, saveṣāmeṣāmāpātataḥ svarūpāsiddhatvāt /
tathā hi yadā sukhādyupalabdhīnāṃ kriyātvena karaṇatayā mano 'numitam, tadā na dravyatvasiddhiḥ, adravyasyāpi karaṇatvāt /
athāsāmeva sākṣātkāritayā indriyatayā tadanumātavyam, tathāpi śarīravayavasyopādhitvam, tadā tāvanmātre vṛttilābhaḥ /
taddoṣe ca vṛttinirodhaḥ śrotravat prasajyeta /
tataḥ śarīramātramupādhirabhidheyaḥ /
tathā ca tadavacchedena vṛttilābhe śirasi me vedanā, pāde me sukhamityādyavyāpyavṛttitvapratītivirodhaḥ /
asamavāyikāraṇānurodhena vibhukāryāṇāṃ deśaniyamāt /
śarīratadavayavāvayavaparamāṇuparyantopādhikalpanāyāṃ ca kalpanāgauravaprasaṅgaḥ, niyamānupapattiśceti /
tato 'nyavaikaṃ sūkṣmamatīndriyam upādhitvena kalpanīyam /
tathāpi tasyaivendriyatve svābhāvike adhikakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt dharmigrāhakapramāṇabādhaḥ /
atha jñānakrameṇendriyasahakāritayā tadanumānaṃ tadā sutarāmeva prāguktadoṣaḥ /
yadi tu manaso vaibhave 'pi adṛṣṭavaśāt krama upapadyate, tadā manaso 'siddherāśrayāsiddhireva vaibhavahetūnāmiti /
atha yatrādṛṣṭasya dṛṣṭakāraṇopahāreṇopayogaḥ, tatra tatpūrṇatāyāṃ kāryamutpadyata eva, anyathā antyatantusaṃyogebhyo 'pi kadācitpaṭo na jāyeta /
jāto 'pi vā kadācinnirguṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>vārttika</s> beginning with "since" is an explanation of the <s>bhāṣya</s> that substantiates the reasons stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> and by himself [the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>], through separate statements — he says: "Not a sense-organ..." Although from the instrumental cause alone

children.text:
syāt /
balavatā kulālena dṛḍhadaṇḍanunnamapi cakraṃ na bhrāmyet /
yatra tu dṛṣṭānusaṃhāreṇa adṛṣṭasya vyāpāraḥ tatra tadveguṇyāt kāryānudayo yathā paramāṇukarmaṇāḥ /
tadihāpi yadi viṣayendriyātmasamavadhānam eva jñānahetuḥ, tatsadbhāve sadaiva kāryaṃ syāt /
na hyetadatiriktamapyadṛṣṭasyopaharaṇīyamasti /
na ca sadaiva jñānodayaḥ /
tato 'tiriktamapekṣaṇīyamasti /
tacca yadyapi sarvāṇyevendriyāṇi vyāpnoti, tathāpi karaṇadharmatvena kriyākramaḥ saṃgacchate /
akalpite tu tasmin nāyaṃ nyāyaḥ, pratipatturakaraṇatvāt cakṣurādīnāmanekatvāt /
tasmādantaḥkaraṇamastīti cet? nanvevamapi yugapajjñānāni mā bhuvan /
yugapajjñānaṃ tu kena vāryate? bhavatyeva samūhālambanamekaṃ jñānamiti cet---na, ekendriyagrāhyeṣviva nānendriyagrāhyeṣvapi prasaḍgāt /
teṣvapi bhavatyeveti cet---na, vyāsaṅgakāle jñānakrameṇa vivādaviṣaye kramānumānāt /
bubhutsāviśeṣeṇa vyāsaḍge kriyākrama iti cet---naivam, na hyeṣa bubhutsāyā mahimā, yadabubhutsite viṣaye jñānasāmagryāṃ satyāmapi na jñānamapi tu tatra saṃskāraviśeṣādhāyakaḥ pratyayaḥ syāt /
yadi tvabubhutsite sāmagrīmeva sā nirūndhyāt /
tathā ca ghaṭāyonmīlitaṃ cakṣuḥ paṭaṃ na darśayet /
tasmād bubhutsāpīndriyāntarādākṛṣya bubhutsitārthagrāhiṇīndriye mano niveśayantī yugapat jñānānutpattāvupayujyate, na tu svarūpata iti yuktamutpaśyāmaḥ /
tasmāt suṣṭhūktam---avyāpīti /
gandhādikriyānyatve satīti vārttikaṃ yathāśrutaṃ dravyakarmādijñānenānaikāntikamato vyācaṣṭe---cakṣurādibhya iti /
nanu smṛtyādiṣu saṃskārādayaḥ /
santi /
tato naite karaṇāntarakalpanāyāṃ prabhavantītyata āha---atra ceti /
indriyajanmānaḥ śarīrasaṃyuktadravyarūpakaraṇajanmāna ityarthaḥ /
nanvindriyatvenaiva mano 'pi janakaṃ smṛtyādīnāṃ tathātve sākṣātkāritvaprasaḍgāditi /
athetyādivārttike pratibhāsamānavyadhikaraṇatāmupādāya codyam /
ekadeśisamādhānaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: it would follow. A wheel pressed up even by a strong potter with a firm stick would not revolve. But where, through the connection of observed [causes], there is the operation of the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), there that [unseen]

children.text: vyāptirvyadhikaraṇayoraśakyagraheti vastugatimupādāya samādhānaṃ sphuṭamityāha---sautramiti //16 //
children.translated_text: the pervasion of two things in different substrata being impossible to grasp — taking the real state of affairs, the resolution is clear — he says: "In accordance with the <s>sūtra</s>..."

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: pretyabhāvādutkarṣe sati pravṛttermano 'pakarṣe hetumāha---manaso 'pīti //
children.translated_text: Since there is superiority in [the category of] after-life existence (<s>pretyabhāva</s>), he states a reason for the inferiority [of the section on] activity with respect to the mind: "Of the mind too..."

children.text:
pravṛtteḥ vikalpasamuccayāmyāmavyāpakatayā nedaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇam /
na ca tadantareṇa viśeṣalakṣaṇāvakāśa ityāśaḍkya sūtravākyaṃ bhinatti---ārambhaḥ pravṛttiḥ /
janmahetuḥ sthirātmaviśeṣaguṇajanakaḥ prayatna ārambhaḥ /
na caivaṃ dayādyavyāptiḥ /
tatrāpi tadarthaṃ prayatnasya vidyamānatvāt /
yadi tvayatamānasyaivecchāmātraṃ jñānamātraṃ dveṣamātraṃ vā pravṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: Since activity does not pervade the combination or accumulation of conceptual cognitions, this is not the general definition. And lest one suspect that without that [general definition], there is no scope for the specific definition — he raises the doubt and the <s>sūtra</s>...

children.text:
syāt, pravartamānaṃ prati prayojakatvamamīṣāṃ nivarteta /
tataścottarasūtravyāghāta iti /
atra yadyapi vāgityādiyathāśrutaviśeṣalakṣaṇāvasare dayādyasaṃgraha iti vuddhipadaṃ mano 'bhiprāyeṇa vyākhyātaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā, tathāpi viśiṣṭadevatādyanucintanādyasaṃgraha ityata āha---sa ca dvividheti /
jñātuṃ jñāpayituṃ vā prayatnaḥ ubhayathāpi jñānahetuḥ, tena vāggocaro 'pi prayatnaḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ /
kartuṃ kārayituṃ vā prayatnaḥ ubhayathāpi kriyāhetuḥ /
tena steyahiṃsādau ajñānādigocaro 'pi prayatnaḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ /
etena yat siddhaṃ tadāha---tatreti /
tadarthaṃ prayatno jñānaṃ janayan jñāpakahetuviṣayo bhavatīti jñāpakaikadeśena vācopalakṣayatā svasamavetajñānamātraheturityapi bhramo nirastaḥ /
kāyanimitteti kāyo nimittaṃ viṣayatayā yasyāḥ sā tathoktā /
children.translated_text: "Body-occasioned" — that which has the body as its occasion, i.e. as its object, is so called.

children.text: dānasteyādyartha yaḥ khalu prayatnaḥ sa kāyaviṣayo bhavati /
children.translated_text: The effort that has the purpose of giving, stealing, and the like — that has the body as its object.

children.text: evaṃ manonimittaṃ dayādrohādyarthaṃ yaḥ khalu prayatnaḥ, sa manoviṣayo bhavatīti neyam /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the effort that has the purpose of compassion, hostility, and the like, and that is mind-occasioned — that has the mind as its object. This should be extended.

children.text: anyathā nāstyevāsau puruṣavyāpāro yatra kāyamanasī na nimittamiti //17 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there is simply no human activity where the body and mind are not the occasion.

it would follow that the motivating capacity of these [factors] with respect to one who is already active would cease. And therefore there would be a contradiction with the subsequent <s>sūtra</s>. Here, although the literal reading of "speech" and the like

children.text: pravarttanālakṣaṇā doṣāḥ //18 //
children.translated_text: "Defects (<s>doṣas</s>) are characterized by impelling [to activity]" // [Sūtra] 18 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
pretyabhāvādutkarṣe sati doṣāṇāṃ pravṛttyapakarṣe hetumāha---prayojyeti /
puruṣaṃ pravartayataḥ utkarūpaprayatnayoginaṃ kuruta ityarthaḥ /
ānantaryādanayorabhidhānam moho 'pi pravartayatīti draṣṭavyam /
mohaikārthasamavāyo mohasaṃskāraikārthasamavavāyaḥ /
mohāntareṇa vā /
etadevāha---tāvaddhi ayamiti /
tasyārtha iti /
bhāṣyasya iti bhāva iti codakasya /
atra ca samavāyo yadyapi na vyāpāraḥ tathāpi mohādeḥ pravartakasya svāśrayasamavetarāgadveṣamohajananāvāntaravyāpārasya pravartakatvamityadūraviprakarṣeṇa sambandhasambandhinoretad draṣṭavyam /
tena phalagocarau moharāgau mohadvaiṣau vā tatsādhanaviṣayau moharāgau mohadveṣau vā janayantau
children.translated_text: Since there is superiority in [the category of] after-life existence, he states a reason for the inferiority of the <s>doṣas</s> with respect to activity: "By the impelled..." [The <s>doṣas</s>] impel the person — the one who possesses the effort of the form of superiority —

children.text: puruṣaṃ pravartayataḥ /
children.translated_text: they impel the person.

children.text: tataḥ phalaviṣayā rāgadveṣamohāḥ pravartakāḥ, sādhanaviṣayāstu tadekārthasamavāyinaḥ pravartanā iti vastugatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, attachment, aversion, and delusion directed toward the fruit are the impellers; but those directed toward the means, being co-inherent with them in a single purpose, are the impelling [conditions] — this is the real state of affairs.

children.text: vyāpāro 'pi ca kāryānuguṇa iti kṛtvā rāgādayaḥ pravartayanti pravṛttihetutvād doṣā ityucyatante //18 //
children.translated_text: And the operation too is in accordance with the effect — and therefore attachment and the like impel, and because of being causes of activity, they are called <s>doṣas</s> (defects).

children.text: punarūtpattiḥ pretyabhāvaḥ //19 //
children.translated_text: "Re-birth (<s>punarutpatti</s>) is after-life existence (<s>pretyabhāva</s>)" // [Sūtra] 19 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: śarīrādīnāṃ doṣaparyantānāṃ parityāgapūrvakaḥ prāptilakṣaṇo dharmaḥ pretyabhāva iti tadanantaramevāsyāvasara ityāha---uddeśakrameti //
children.translated_text: The property characterized as attainment — preceded by the relinquishment of body and the like up to the faults — is <s>pretyabhāva</s> (post-mortem existence). And its proper place is immediately after that — he says: 'In the order of enumeration...'

children.text:
nanu pūrvaśarīrādiparityāgāditi sūtre nāstyeva /
na cotpattimātraṃ pretyabhāvaḥ, ekasminnapi janmani tathāvyavahāraprasaḍgāt /
na ca punaḥśabdasyāyamarthaḥ, tasyābhyāsamātrārthatvāt /
ata uktaṃ vārttikakṛtā punariti /
tad vyācaṣṭe---punarityabhyāsamāheti /
abhyāsaṃ vadanneva nāntarīyakatayā pūrvaśarīradiparityāgaṃ pratipādayatītyarthaḥ /
tathāpi kiṃ vakrokteḥ prayojanamityata āha---tathā ceti /
nanu dvitīyasūtre duḥkhādīnāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāva saṃsāra ityuktam, iha tu punarūtpattiriti, tat kuto na virodha ityāśayavato vārttikakṛta ākṣepaḥ, kaḥ punariti /
duḥkhāndīnāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāve sati pūrvadehādiparityāgādanyadehādiprāptilakṣaṇaḥ pretyabhāvaḥ /
tatasteṣāṃ tathābhūtapravāhavicchede pretyabhāvāparanāmā saṃsāro vicchidyeta iti tulyapravṛttinimittatvāt sa eva tatra saṃsāra uktaityayo na virodha ityāśayavataḥ parihāro duḥkhādīnāmiti /
tadetatsmaraṇamātreṇa, vyācaṣṭai, tadetadvārttikajātamiti /
children.translated_text: He explains that this is generated from the <s>vārttika</s> by mere recollection: 'This very <s>vārttika</s>-born [discussion]...'

children.text: seyamuktarūpā punarūtpattiryadyacetanasya manasaḥ saṃsāraḥ kimiti nivartanīyaḥ? athātmanastadāśakyanivṛttiḥ, muktasyāpi saṃsāridehādiparityāgāt tadīyāparadehādiprāptisaṃbhavādityāśayavatā vārttikakṛtā śaḍkitam---so 'yamiti /
children.translated_text: If this re-origination of the described form is the <s>saṃsāra</s> of the non-conscious mind, why should it be stopped? But if it is of the <s>ātman</s> (self), then its cessation is impossible, since even for the liberated one, there is the possibility of attaining another body and the like belonging to the <s>saṃsārin</s> after relinquishing that body — with this intention the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> raises the doubt: 'This...'

children.text: neyaṃ bhogenaviśeṣitā punarūtpattiḥ saṃsāra ityāśayavatā parihṛtam---yadīti /
children.translated_text: With the intention that this re-origination not qualified by experience is not <s>saṃsāra</s>, it is replied: 'If...'

children.text: tatrāsphuṭaṃ padaṃ sphuṭayati---kriyāmiti //19 //
children.translated_text: He clarifies the unclear word therein: 'Action...'

Now, 'from the relinquishment of the prior body and the like' is not in the <s>sūtra</s> at all. And mere origination is not <s>pretyabhāva</s>, since there would follow such usage even within a single birth. Nor is this the meaning of the word <s>punar</s> (again), since it means mere repetition. Therefore the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> said '<s>punar</s> means...' He explains this: '<s>Punar</s> means repetition...' The meaning is: in stating repetition, he incidentally conveys the relinquishment of the prior body and the like. Even so, what is the purpose of the indirect expression? To this he says: 'And thus...' Now, in the second <s>sūtra</s>, it was said that the causal relation of suffering and the like is <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), but here it is 're-origination' — so how is there no contradiction? — with this intention the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> raises the objection: 'What then...' When there is a causal relation among sufferings and the like, <s>pretyabhāva</s> is characterized by the relinquishment of the prior body and the like and the attainment of another body and the like. Therefore, when their continuity of that nature is cut, <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is another name for <s>pretyabhāva</s>, is cut — since they have the same ground of application, that very thing was called <s>saṃsāra</s> there. Therefore there is no contradiction — with this intention, the reply is: 'Of suffering and the like...'

children.text: pravṛttidoṣajanitor'thaḥ phalam //20 //
children.translated_text: The object that generates activity and faults is the result (<s>phala</s>).

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification).

children.text: śaḍkāmapanayanneva saṅgati karoti---yadyapīti /
children.translated_text: While removing the doubt itself, he establishes the connection: 'Although...'

children.text: sāmānyena jñātā hi viśiṣṭatayā jñātuṃ śakyante /
children.translated_text: For what is known in general can be known in particular.

children.text: tataḥ sāmānyarūpeṇa lakṣitānāṃ viśiṣṭalakṣaṇāvasaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is occasion for the particular definition of those that have been defined in general form.

children.text: ubhayoścākārayornirvedopayogādubhayopādānamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And since both forms are useful for dispassion (<s>nirveda</s>), both are adopted — this is the meaning.

children.text:
atra ca sūtre padadvayamatiriktam /
tatra prathamopayogamāha---atra ceti /
yadyapi svarūpato 'pi pravṛtteḥ kāryabhūtau dharmādharmau prati doṣāṇāmatiśayenopayogo, vakṣyati ca, doṣatuṣāvanaddhā hi karmataṇḍulā ityādi, tathāpi pravṛttiphale doṣāṇāmupayogo darśanīyaḥ sūtre prakṛtatvāt /
na ca dharmādharmayoḥ phalavyavahāraḥ /
tato vyāpāradvāramupādāyopayogamāha---api tviti /
tadeva dvāraṃ sphorayati---doṣasalileti /
ato dharmādharmaśrutyā na lakṣaṇābhramaḥ kartavyaḥ /
svarūpatastu pravṛtti prati doṣāṇāṃ sahakāritvaṃ sūtrakāra eva caturthe vakṣyatīti /
tat kiṃ nirdeṣasya sukhaduḥkhe na sta ityupāttakarmapracayasya tādavasthyamadattaphalasyaiva vā vināśa ityata āha---na cāstīti /
na brūmo nirdeṣasya upabhoga eva nāsti /
children.translated_text: we do not say that there is simply no experience of what is being indicated.

children.text: api tu yādṛśaḥ saṃsārahetustādṛśo nāsti /
children.translated_text: But rather, such as is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, such [experience] does not exist.

children.text: doṣāntarajanako hi tādṛśa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For such [experience] generates other faults — this is the meaning.

children.text: arthapadasyopayomāha---sūtra iti //20 //
children.translated_text: He states the use of the word <s>artha</s> (object): 'In the <s>sūtra</s>...'
And in this <s>sūtra</s>, two words are additional. Of these, he states the use of the first: 'And here...' Although even from the standpoint of essential nature too,

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification).

children.text: mukhyaṃ duḥkhamadhikṛtya saṅgatiruktā /
children.translated_text: The connection has been stated with respect to primary suffering.

children.text: gauṇābhiprāyeṇāha---nānukta iti //
children.translated_text: With the intention of the secondary [sense], he says: 'Nor is it unstated...'

children.text:
nanu lakṣaṇaśabdo yadi svarūpavacanaḥ syāt, gauṇaduḥkhāvyāptiḥ syāt āvṛttau vākyabhedaḥ /
tata ekavākyatvaṃ rocayannayamāha---atra ceti /
evaṃ cāsiddhiḥ /
tāṃ pariharati---saiva hīti /
mukhyā svarūpato, gauṇī vidheyaduḥkhopādhinibandhanā /
na caivamitaretarāśrayaprasaṅgaḥ /
duḥkhatayā tadviṣayatvaṃ tathātve ca duḥkhatvamiti lokasuprasiddhena bādhanābuddhiviṣayatvena heyatāyāḥ prasādhanāt /
yo hi duḥkhaṃ taddhetuṃ vā śarīrādi tadanuṣaktaṃ vā sukhaṃ jānāno 'pi sukhatṛṣṇāpariplutamatirna hātumicchati, taṃ pratyucyate śarīrādiduḥkhāntaṃ duḥkhaṃ heyamityarthaḥ, bādhanālakṣaṇatvāt, yattu na heyaṃ na tadevam, yathātmasvarūpāpavargāviti /
vaśī jitāvidyaḥ /
yadyapi rāgābhāvo vairāgyaṃ tathāpi suṣuptyādau tasya bhāve mokṣānupayuktatayā ātyantiko vivakṣitaḥ /
sa ca
children.translated_text: Now, if the word 'definition' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) means 'essential nature,' there would be non-extension to secondary suffering; and with repetition there would be a different sentence. Therefore, a single sentence

children.text:
kāraṇayogyatānivṛttyā sidhyati /
tataḥ saiva darśitā /
upanateṣvapi viṣayeṣvaudāsīnyaṃ kiṃ tadupekṣābuddhiḥ prabalatattvasākṣātkārasamunmūlitaniravaśeṣamavidyāsaṃskāre heyopādeyapakṣavyavacchedavatī buddhirityarthaḥ /
śarīrādiṣu uktaḥ uktarūpa eva grāhya ityarthaḥ /
nanvabhāvaphalatvaṃ dharmasya duḥkhābhāvasukhavādino nāniṣṭam /
nāpīdamadṛṣṭamityata
children.translated_text: is established by the cessation of fitness for being a cause. Therefore, that alone has been shown. Even with respect to objects that have presented themselves, what is disregard? Is it neglect of those?

children.text:
āha---yadyapīti /
yathā ca kālotkarṣaḥ sukhasyāgamikaḥ, tathā svarūpotkarṣo 'pyānubhavika āgamikaśceti draṣṭavyam /
na cāndhakāravat pratiyogyutkarṣādutkarṣopapattiriti vācyam /
dharmaphalaṃ hi duḥkhābhāvo bhavan pradhvaṃso vaktavyaḥ, prāgabhāvāderasādhyatvāt /
tasya ca kālenānavaccheda eva /
na ca tajjātīyāvadhisadbhāvaniyamo 'ndhakāravadeva /
na hi brahmalokopabhogānantaramevāvaśyaṃ duḥkhena bhavitavyamityasti niyāmakam /
yathā ca viśiṣṭaśālisūpādinā kulmāṣapiṇḍikayā codarapūraṇe kṛte duḥkhanivṛttistulyā, tathendrabrāhmapadayorapīti na kaścit svarūpato viśeṣaḥ syāt, api ca svargārthī yāgādikaṃ kṛtvā kadācillabdhavṛtteradharmānnarakaduḥkhamanubhūya svargamanubhavati /
kadācit tu manuṣyadehapātānantarameva ityaniyamaḥ /
so 'yaṃ na syāt, duḥkhapradhvaṃsaphalatvād dharmasya /
na cānutpannasya pradhvaṃsaḥ tasmād dharmaṃ caritvā avaśyamakāmayamāno 'pi prathamatastāvannarakādiduḥkhamanubhavet /
tatastadabhāvamiti kṛtaṃ dharmeṇa,
children.translated_text: He says: 'Although...' Just as the temporal remoteness of pleasure is future [and hence a reason for dispassion], so too its essential inferiority is both experiential and future.

children.text: prakṣālanāddhi paṅkasya dūrādasparśanaṃ varam /
children.translated_text: 'Rather than washing mud, it is better to avoid touching it from afar'

children.text: iti nyāyāt //21 //
children.translated_text: — by this maxim.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification).

children.text: śarīrādiṣu pratiyogiṣu lakṣiteṣu tannivṛttirūpasyāpavargasya lakṣaṇāvasara ityāha---krameti //
children.translated_text: When the counter-positives — body and the like — have been defined, there is occasion for the definition of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), which has the form of the cessation of those — he says: 'In sequence...'

children.text:
yadyapi mano na jāyate, tathāpi karmopagrahamantareṇa tasyākiñcitkaratvāt sa eva tasya janmeti jāyamānāḥ sarva ityuktam /
atra ca pratiyogināṃ śarīrādīnāmādhyātmikatvāt tatpradhvaṃso 'pyādhyātmika eva /
tadviśiṣṭasya jīvanmuktyuttarakāle duḥkhasyātyanatābhāvo mokṣa iti nākāśādigatena duḥkhasyātyantābhāvena vyabhicāraḥ /
pariṇāmo hi pūrvadharminivṛttau dharmyantarotpādo vā syāt, vaināśikānāmiva /
pūrvadharmanivṛttau dharmāntarotpādo vā syāt sāṃkhyānāmiva /
tadetat takṣadvayaṃ vikalpayati---sarvātmanā veti /
pūrvasminniti /
āstāṃ tāvatkauṭasthyaṃ pariṇāminityatāpi na syādityarthaḥ /
ekadeśeti /
yadi dharmadharmiṇorekāntenābhedo yadi vā bhedābhedaḥ, ubhayathāpi na kūṭasthānityatā /
ekāntabhedena tu katham
children.translated_text: Although the mind is not born, nevertheless, since without the support of <s>karma</s> it is ineffective, that [karmic support] alone is its birth. Being born

children.text: brahmaivedaṃ sarvamiti
children.translated_text: 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>'

children.text:
śrutivacanamādriyata ityarthaḥ /
sāvayavatvāditi sāṃśatvāt /
svātmībhūtopajanāpāyadharmavattvāditi yāvat /
ghaṭādivaditi /
yathā ghaṭādayo brahmadharmā anityāḥ, tathā tadabhinnasvabhāvaṃ brahmāpyanityaṃ syādityarthaḥ /
na ca vācyaṃ pariṇāminityameva brahmāsatu /
anekāntavādasya nirākṛtatvāt /
satkāryavādasya nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt /
na caikāntabhinna evāyaṃ brahmadharmaprapañco 'stu iti vācyam, vyaktād vyaktasya niṣpattiḥ pratyakṣapramāṇyādityupādānādicintāyāḥ kariṣyamāṇatvāt, paramāṇūnāṃ nityatāvyavasthāpanācca /
tatkāryatāmātratve tu siddhasādhanāditi /
nityamityādi bhāṣyaṃ na yathāśrutaṃ paramatotthāpanamityata āha---asyārtha iti /
ityartha iti /
pareṣāmabhimata iti /
ātmā nityasukhavān kāraṇāntarāṇi parityajyāśrīyate tattajjātīyanityaguṇavat, yathā varṇātkena śadenāśrīyamāṇamākāśaṃ nityaśabdavaditi mīmāṃsānaye /
satkāryanaye tu, ātmā nityasukhavān /
tenāśrīyamāṇatvāt /
yadyenāśrīyate tattena nityena tadvat, yathā paṭena tantava ityutthāpya dūṣayatītyāha---atra ceti /
anaikāntikatāṃ draḍhayitumatiprasaḍgo 'vatāritaḥ /
nanu sukhatatsaṃvedanena brahmayaṇo bhinno brahma cānuditānastamitarūpaṃ śuddhabuddhasvabhāvaṃ svata eva siddham /
kastatra pramāṇapraśnāvakāśaḥ? sarveṣāmeva pramāṇānāmanubhava eva sīmā /
kutaścābhivyaktyādicintā? muktasaṃsārāvasthayoraviśeṣaśca prasañjito 'pi nāniṣṭa ityata āha---ayamabhisandhiriti /
viṣayasukhasaṃvedane evātmā tadatirikto vā? ādyaṃ dūṣayati---sukhamiti /
uktopapatti smārayitvā aparāmāha---na hīti /
children.translated_text: having reminded of the previously stated reasoning, he states another: 'For not...'

children.text: nanu sukhasaṃvedanayorūdayavyayau na tāttvikau /
children.translated_text: Now, the arising and passing away of pleasure and consciousness are not real.

children.text: na ca kalpito virūddhadharmādhyāso bhedahetuḥ sphaṭikasyāpi javātāpicchādisannidhānāpāditārūṇimanīlimādinā bhedaprasaḍgādityāśaḍkya pariharati---na cātmaiveti /
children.translated_text: And a falsely imagined superimposition of contradictory properties is not a cause of difference — for even a crystal, when in the proximity of a <s>javā</s> flower or lac, acquires redness or blueness,

children.text: na hyasti saṃbhavaḥ sphaṭikaḥ svarūpeṇa pūrvāparakālaikatayā sphuranneva nīlīdivyāvṛttātmā nīlādyātmanāropyata iti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: for it is not possible that the crystal, appearing by its own nature in unity across earlier and later times, is of the nature of blue and the like, having excluded its nature of being different from blue and the like.

— this <s>śruti</s> statement is respected — this is the meaning. 'Because of having parts' means because of having components. 'Because of possessing the property of origination and destruction of what has become part of itself' — what

children.text: syādetat, svasaṃvedanamātmasvabhāvamapyanādyavidyāvaśādanātmatayā sphurat tattadviṣayoparāgeṇa bhinnamiva sphuratyātmanyekatayā pratisandhīyamāne 'pi yathā gaganasaviturekatvenānubhūyamānasyāpi pratibimbamambuni taraḍgabhedādityata
children.translated_text: One might say: self-awareness, even though of the nature of the Self, due to beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), appears as non-Self, and through the coloring of various objects, appears as different —

children.text:
āha---na caitadasatīti /
ayamarthaḥ, na tāvat sa eva tasminneva tadānīmeva bhrānto 'bhrāntaśceti saṃbhavati /
tasmādavidyāyā durghaṭatvaṃ nāmālaḍkāra eveti pādaprasārikayā pratyavastheyam /
seyaṃ bhedajñāne bādhakamālambya syāt /
tacca nāstīti vakṣyāmaḥ /
pratibimbe tu suvyakta eva bhrama iti /
dvitīyaṃ dūṣayati---na cāgantuketi /
nanvātmani nityaṃ caitanyamiti ka evamāha? ki tvātmaiva nityacaitanyasvabhāva ityata āha---na cātmaiveti /
na ca sukhenāhamasvāpsamityastyeva smaraṇamiti vācyam /
ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmīti tadajñāsiṣamitivat sukhenāhaṃ svapimīti tadajñāsiṣamityevamapi smaraṇaprasaḍgāt, tarhi kimidaṃ sukhamahamasvāpsamiti duḥkhābhāvānumānamātraṃ supto 'haṃ na kiñcidajñāsiṣamiti jñānābhāvānumānavat /
atha kena liḍgena smaraṇārhāsamaraṇena /
ko dharmī? ātmā anubhūyamānaḥ smaryamāṇo vā pratyabhijñāyamānaḥ /
tathāpi suṣuptāvasthā yā
children.translated_text: He says: 'and this is not unreal.' The meaning is this: to begin with, it is not possible that the very same [person], in the very same [locus], at the very same time, is both deluded and non-deluded. Therefore, the difficult-to-accomplish nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is merely an ornament [of speech] — this should be countered by one who stretches out his legs [i.e., is stubbornly entrenched]. This [argument] would depend on taking recourse to a sublating cognition regarding the cognition of difference. And that does not exist — we shall say so. But in the case of a reflection, the error is perfectly evident. He refutes the second [alternative]: 'nor adventitious.' Now, who says that consciousness is eternally in the <s>ātman</s>? Rather, the <s>ātman</s> itself is of the nature of eternal consciousness — therefore he says: 'nor is the <s>ātman</s> itself.' Nor should one say: 'there is indeed the memory, I slept with happiness.' For just as there is a memory 'I knew the pot — I had known that,' so too there would follow the consequence of the memory 'I sleep with happiness — I had known that.' Then what is this 'I slept with happiness'? It is merely an inference of the absence of suffering, just like 'I slept, I did not know anything' is an inference of the absence of cognition. Now, by what inferential mark? By the non-remembering of what is worthy of being remembered. What is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>)? The <s>ātman</s>, as being experienced, or as being remembered, or as being recognized. Even so, the state of deep sleep, which

children.text:
nānubhūtā ata eva na smṛtā, kathamiva tacchabdena parāmṛśyata iti cet---na, pūrvāparāvasthayorekatvapratyabhijñānena madhyāvasthāyā api sāmānyenopanayanāt /
yathā prāgupalabdhaḥ paścādupalabhyamāno ghaṭo madhyāvasthāyāṃ nāyaṃ jñāta iti jñānābhāvaviśiṣṭo 'numīyata iti na kiñcidanupapannam, stāmātmano jñānasukhe bhinne na tu mithastathā ca sukhātmakaṃ jñānamātmani jñānāntareṇa yadi nānubhūyata /
evametat, svayamapi na prakāśata iti tvasiddhamityata āha---sukhaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: this is so; but [the claim] that it does not manifest even by itself is unestablished — therefore he says: 'and happiness.'

children.text: tadevamātmani sukhaṃ nityaṃ bhinnaṃ bhinnanaiva jñānena prakāśyamānamāstheyam tatra bhāṣyavārtike ityāha---tadevamiti /
children.translated_text: Thus, happiness in the <s>ātman</s>, being eternal, being distinct, being illuminated only by a distinct cognition — this is what should be maintained. Regarding that, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Vārttika</s> [say] — he says: 'thus indeed.'

children.text: nanu vaiṣayikasukhajñāne kartavye sukhātiriktaṃ kimātmamanaḥsaṃyogo 'pekṣate, yena tatrāpi viṣayamātrāpekṣāyāṃ manasaiva rūpādyupalabdhiprasaḍgo na syāt, atha bahirmanaḥsāpekṣaṃ nanvantariti parihāraḥ, sa ihāpīti /
children.translated_text: Now, when the cognition of objective happiness is to be produced, what does the contact of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> (mind) require beyond happiness itself? — such that even there, when only the object is required, there would not follow the consequence that form and the like would be apprehended by the mind alone. But if [the cognition of] the external requires the mind — the reply 'but the internal' [applies]. And the same [reply applies] here too.

children.text: ato vārttikaṃ sphorayati---saṃsārāvasthāyāmiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore he elucidates the <s>Vārttika</s>: 'in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence).'

was not experienced and for that very reason not remembered — how can it be referred to by that word [i.e., 'deep sleep']? — if so objected: no, because through the recognition of identity between the prior and subsequent states, even the intermediate state is brought in by way of generalization. Just as a pot perceived earlier and perceived again later — in the intermediate state, 'this was not known' — is inferred as qualified by the absence of cognition — so nothing is untenable. Let cognition and happiness in the <s>ātman</s> be distinct from each other, but not mutually so. And thus, if cognition whose nature is happiness is not experienced in the <s>ātman</s> by another cognition —

children.text:
āpāditaprayāsavaiyarthyaparihāraṃ parasya vārttikakṛto hṛdisthaṃ sphuṭīkaroti siddhāntavārttikaṃ saṃgamayitum---nanu tvanmata iti /
yathā hi śāstreṇa pravartamānaḥ pravartayitvayaḥ, tathā sa eva śakyasādhane /
na ca nityaṃ śakyam /
taddhi na nirvartyaṃ nityatvāt /
nāpi vikāryamapariṇāmitvāt /
nāpi prāpyam /
na hi tasya saṃbandhalakṣaṇā prāptirapratisaṃkramatvāt nāpi tādātmyalakṣaṇā, tasyāḥ prāgeva siddhyasiddhyorūbhayathāpi aśakyatvāt /
nāpi jñānalakṣaṇā, nityānityavikalpena tasyā apyapāsitatvāt /
nāpi viṣayatvalakṣaṇā, anatirekāt /
tathātve cotpannatayā vināśe punarasaṃbandhāt /
ṣaṭpadārthātirekasyāsiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the non-establishment of [anything] beyond the six categories.

children.text: bhāvatve 'vaśyaṃ tadantarbhāvāt /
children.translated_text: If it is a positive entity, it must necessarily be included within those [six categories].

children.text: abhāvatve pratiyogyanupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: If it is an absence, its counter-positive is untenable.

children.text: nāpi saṃskāryaṃ tat, anādheyatvātiśayatvāditi //
children.translated_text: Nor is that [eternal happiness] something to be refined (<s>saṃskārya</s>), because of having no additional excellence that can be conferred.

He clarifies the opponent's objection, which is in the heart of the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, in order to reconcile the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>Vārttika</s> — by removing the futility of the effort that was undertaken: 'now, according to your view.' For just as one who is impelled by scripture [can act only] where the goal is achievable, so too that very [person] can [act only] with respect to what is achievable. And what is eternal is not achievable. For it is not producible, because of its eternality. Nor modifiable, because of its being immutable. Nor attainable. For contact-type attainment of it [is impossible] because of its non-transference. Nor identity-type [attainment], because that [identity], whether already accomplished or not accomplished before, is in either case unachievable. Nor cognition-type [attainment], because that too has been set aside by the division of eternal and non-eternal. Nor object-type [attainment], because of non-difference [from what already exists]. And even if it were so, upon its arising, it would again be unconnected when destroyed.

children.text:
tasmāt nityaṃ sukhamaśakyatvāt na prayojanam /
prayojanaṃ tu duḥkhābhāvaḥ, tasya nirvartyatvāditi vastugatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, eternal happiness, being unachievable, is not the purpose [of scripture]. But the purpose is the absence of suffering, because that is producible — this is the actual state of affairs.

children.text:
atrāhuḥ---nanu sasādhanaṃ duḥkhamapi na pāramārthikamasti /
tataḥ kasyābhāvaḥ śakyaḥ /
yathāvidyopadarśanaṃ tu pravṛttiḥ sukhe 'pi samāneti, tatrāha---dharmādharmāviti /
tadidaṃ pūrvoktaṃ hṛdi nidhāyoktam---śakyau bhogena kṣetumiti /
na kevalamiyaṃ nityasukhadṛṣṭirmokṣānupayoginī, pratyuta virodhinītyāha---anyathā tviti /
tasmānmanāgapyasyā avakāśo na dātavyaḥ paraiḥ, apitvavidyānivṛttimātre prayatitavyaṃ śakyatvāt, avirūddhatvāccetyarthaḥ /
tasmādupapannānavadyavādinaḥ parameśvarasyopadeśo nāśakyaprayojano na viparītaprayojano na viparītaprayojano vā bhavitumarhatīti bhāktatvamevānandaśrutīnāṃ nyāyyamityāha---tasmāditi /
nityaṃ sukhaṃ bhavatyasti /
yadyapi kiñcinnārabhate nopādatte tathāpi nimittatayā kiñcitkurvan san bhaviṣyatīti cet? naivam, ṭīkārthānavabodhāt /
nimittatā hi upādānatayāvyāptā /
anyathā rūpāderapyanupādānasyāpi kiñcitpratinimittatāmupagamya nivṛttau sarvasantānanivṛttiprasaḍgāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, because even of form and the like, which are not material causes, upon accepting some efficient-cause-ness and then its cessation, there would follow the consequence of the cessation of all continua.

children.text: evamastviti cet? atra ṭīkayottaraṃ, tadevamasmadabhipretāpavargalakṣaṇe saṃpratipannāvapi lābhahānyoradhikavādinau nirastau, saṃkhyādayastu naivamiti notthāpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Let it be so' — if so said: to this the answer is in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>. Thus, even when agreement has been reached on the definition of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) as intended by us, those who hold excessive views regarding gain and loss have been refuted. But the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and others are not so [refuted], hence they were not raised [as opponents].

children.text: te hi prakāre paraṃ vivadante /
children.translated_text: For they dispute only about the mode [of liberation].

children.text: sa ca tatra tatra cintanīyaḥ //22 //
children.translated_text: And that is to be considered in the respective [contexts]. //22//

Here they say: now, suffering too, together with its means, does not ultimately exist. Then whose absence is achievable? But just as [on the Advaita view] activity, like the appearance presented by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), is equally [present] with respect to happiness — to this he says: '<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.' This has been said with the earlier [argument] in mind: 'they are capable of being exhausted through experience.' Not only is this view of eternal happiness useless for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), but rather it is contradictory — he says: 'otherwise, however.' Therefore, not even the slightest scope should be given to this [view] by others; rather, one should strive merely for the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, because it is achievable and because it is non-contradictory — this is the meaning. Therefore, the instruction of the supreme lord, who is a speaker of what is blameless, cannot be either of unachievable purpose or of contradictory purpose — hence the secondary (figurative) interpretation alone of the <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) <s>śrutis</s> (scriptures) is proper — he says: 'therefore.' Eternal happiness exists. Although it does not produce or take up anything, nevertheless, might it do something as an efficient cause and thus be [relevant] in the future? — if so: not so, because of not understanding the meaning of the <s>Ṭīkā</s>. For being an efficient cause is not pervaded by being a material cause.

children.text: // iti pramayalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the section on the definition of the objects of valid cognition (<s>prameya</s>). //

children.text: // nyāyapūrvāḍgalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // The section on the definition of the preliminaries of the <s>nyāya</s> (method of reasoning). //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> //

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ pramāṇādhīnatvāt prameyasya tu bubhutsitatamatvāt tābhyāṃ saṃśayādīnāmapakarṣaḥ /
sāṅgepāṅge ca nyāye vyutpādye pūrvāṅgatayā prakaraṇāntarebhyaḥ saṃśayādiprakāraṇasyotkarṣaḥ /
tatrāpi sandigdhe prayojanādicintā /
na ca prayojanamanusandhāya saṃśaya iti saṃśayasya prāthamyamevaṃlakṣaṇakrame 'pi nyāyaḥ /
uddeśyalakṣaṇayorekavākyatvādityabhisandhinā bhāṣyam ityāha---saṃśayeti /
children.translated_text: Since all [objects of valid cognition] are dependent on <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), and since <s>prameya</s> (object of valid cognition) is the most desired to be known, by those two [reasons] there is the withdrawal of doubt and the like from them. And in the <s>nyāya</s> that is to be taught with its limbs and sub-limbs, there is the elevation of the section on doubt and the like, by virtue of being a preliminary. And even within that, when the [subject] is in doubt, the consideration of purpose and the like [follows]. And it is not the case that doubt [arises] upon considering the purpose — therefore the primacy of doubt even in this order of definition is proper, because of the unity of sentence between what is to be enumerated and [its] definition — with this intention [is] the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — he says: 'doubt.'

children.text: ata eva dvitīya pāṭhaṃ vyācaṣṭe---kvaciditi //
children.translated_text: For this very reason he explains the second reading: 'in some [readings].'

children.text:
nanu saṃśayasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ cedidam, vimarśaḥ saṃśaya ityetāvadevāstu /
viśeṣalakṣaṇāni cet?nākṛte sāmānyalakṣaṇe teṣāmavasaraḥ /
vimarśasaṃśayapadayoścānyatarat anarthakamityata āha---atra ceti /
lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇavākyam /
vimarśa ityanena ca viṣayataḥ svarūpataśca sāmānyalakṣaṇadvayaṃ sūcitam /
tatra prathamamāha---ekasminniti /
virodhicaturarthāvamarśa iti tu parisaṃkhyānamanarthakam /
sthāṇurvā puruṣo vetyatra dravyādeḥ anantasyāvamarśāt /
prādhānyena cet? dvayasyaiva /
na hyayaṃ niṣedhaḥ pradhāna iti /
dvitīyamāha---kiṃsviditi /
kimityupakrame /
sviditi pakṣāntare /
tena kimidamavam utasvidevamityarthaḥ /
anuvartanīyamāvartanīyamarthānurodhāt /
saṃśayapadasannidhaśca vimarśapadaṃ vivakṣitamarthamāheti tatsahitamevoktavāniti parasparaniṣedhavadubhayavidhipradhāna ekaḥ /
parasparavidhimadubhayaniṣedhapradhāno 'paraḥ /
parasparaviraharūpavidhiniṣedhapradhāno 'nya iti yathāsaṃkhyaṃ viśiṣṭaḥ saṃśayo lakṣya ityāha---atra viśiṣṭa iti /
lakṣyapadaṃ lakṣyapadārtha iti /
guṇagataṃ saṃśayo lakṣya ityāha---atra viśiṣṭa iti /
lakṣyapadaṃ lakṣyapadārtha iti /
guṇagataṃ sādṛśyamavāntarasāmānyaviśeṣa eva /
yatastulyārohapariṇāhāvimāviti pratyayo bhavati, tameva vyaktikāraṇamukhena darśayati---saṃkhyāparimāṇeti /
mahattvadīrghatvasāmānyadharmayoga iti /
mahattvadīrghatvasāmānyamātradharmayoga ityarthaḥ /
iha vārtikakāreṇa samānadharmopapatterityādau sattāmātreṇa saṃśayāhetutayā upalabdheraśrutyā ca pūrvapakṣayitvā samādhānatrayamabhihitaṃ tadvivecayati---yadyapīti /
prathame 'nupapattiśabdaḥ sattāvācakaḥ tatparaśca /
upalabdhistu viśeṣāpekṣa ityanenākṣipyate /
dvitīye tūpapattiśabdo 'yamanekārtho 'pīhopalabdhivācaka upāttaḥ /
tṛtīye tu sattāvacana eva lakṣaṇayopalabdhipara iti /
tatra viśeṣāpekṣa iti padaṃ tadā sāmānyajñānamākṣipet, yadi viśeṣajñānaṃ niṣedhet /
na tvetadastītyata āha---viśeṣeti /
vākyasāmarthyādanvayayogyatāsāmarthyāt /
yadyapi viśeṣāpekṣaśabdaḥ sākṣād viśeṣopalabdhi na niṣedhati, tathāpi lakṣaṇayā tatparaḥ /
sā ca mukhye bādhakāt, vivakṣite saṃbandhāt avācakopādāne prayojanātt pravartate /
tatra mukhye bādhakamāha---na ceti /
prayojanānuyogaparihārāya laukikalakṣaṇātvaṃ sūcayan dṛṣṭāntapūrvakaṃ saṃbandhamāha---yatheti /
yathā hi gaḍgātīrayoḥ saṃyogamantarbhāvyāvinābhāvastathā agṛhyamāṇasmaraṇabubhutsayorekaviṣayatayā saṃśayamantarākṛtvā paurvāparyaniyamenāvinābhāva eva saṃbandha ityarthaḥ,saukaryaviśeṣāt /
tatprayojanamapyabhidhātuṃ śakyate /
viśeṣamapekṣata iti hi viśeṣāpekṣaḥ saṃśaya uktaḥ /
tathā ca viśeṣe jijñāsājanaka ityukte phalamasya darśitaṃ bhavati /
tadidamuktam---tasyāḥ saṃśaye sati bhāvāditi /
etena phaladvārakamapi sāmānyalakṣaṇamanugantavyam /
dvitīye tu vinigamanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvaścodyam /
tadutthāpya vārttikeṇottarayati---syādetaditi /
tṛtīye prayojanābhāścodyam, tad vārttikamukhenaiva pariharati---na ceyamalaukikī lakṣaṇetyādi yena prayojanamanurudhyeteti śeṣaḥ /
nanu kṛtakatvaṃ paricchedasya hetuḥ, na vyavacchedasyetyata āha---api tvanityatvasyeti /
nanu tathāpi vivakṣitatajjātīyavṛttitve satyanyavṛttireva dharmaḥ samānaśabdavācya iti kuto niyama ityata āha---samāno hīti /
atrottaraparasya yāvannāvatārastāvat parihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the resolution of the one that is directed toward the answer is [valid] as long as it has not descended [to the topic]; until then, the resolution [holds].

children.text: tasmistvavatīrṇe prasaktireva nāsti /
children.translated_text: But once it has descended [to the topic], there is simply no applicability [of the objection].

children.text: yadi hi samāno dharmo vyavacchedaheturiti kutaḥ sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvaḥ, tasyaiva tadabhāvarūpatvāt /
children.translated_text: For if the common property is the cause of exclusion, whence is the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes or sublates? — because that [common property] itself is of the nature of the absence of that [determination].

children.text: sa cet kathamasau vyavacchedahetuḥ? na copalabdhyādipadaṃ taditarasya sādhakabādhakatvaṃ pratikṣipati //
children.translated_text: If so, how is it the cause of exclusion? Nor does the word 'perception' and the like reject the establishing or sublating status of the other.

Now, if this is the general definition of doubt, then 'deliberation is doubt' — this much alone should suffice. And if [these are] specific definitions — without making the general definition, there is no occasion for them. And one of the two words 'deliberation' and 'doubt' is meaningless — therefore he says: 'and here.' 'Definition' means the definitional sentence. And by the word 'deliberation,' a twofold general definition in terms of the object and in terms of its own nature is indicated. Of those, he states the first: 'in one.' But 'deliberation of two or four meanings' as an exhaustive enumeration is purposeless — because in 'is it a post or a person?' there is deliberation about an infinite [number of things] such as substance and the like. If [limited] by predominance — then of just two. For this negation is not the predominant [element]. He states the second: 'what indeed.' 'What' in the opening. 'Indeed' in the alternative. Hence the meaning is: 'Is this thus, or indeed thus?' What is to be continued must be repeated as required by the meaning. And the word 'deliberation,' being proximate to the word 'doubt,' conveys the intended meaning — thus it was stated together with that. [The doubt is] one in which the predominant element is the positive assertion of both, as in mutual negation. Another in which the predominant element is the negation of both, as in mutual assertion. Yet another in which the predominant element is the positive assertion and negation in the form of mutual exclusion — thus, according to the enumeration, the specific [types of] doubt are what is defined — he says: 'here the specific.' The word 'what is defined' [means] the referent of the word 'what is defined.' Similarity pertaining to qualities is simply a subordinate universal-particular. The cognition 'these two have equal extent and magnitude' — that very [cognition] he shows by way of the cause of the individual [instance]: 'number, dimension.' The meaning is: the conjunction of merely the common properties of greatness and length. Here, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, having made the prima facie view that mere existence is not a cause of doubt because of the non-hearing of 'from the obtaining of common properties' and the like, has stated three resolutions — he analyzes those: 'although.' In the first, the word 'obtaining' is a word for 'existence' and is directed toward that. But 'perception' requires a specific [property] — by this it is objected. In the second, however, this word 'obtaining,' though polysemous, is here taken as meaning 'perception.' In the third, however, [it is] a word for 'existence' [but] directed toward 'perception' by secondary signification. Now, the expression 'requiring a specific' would object to general cognition only if it negated specific cognition. But this is not so — therefore he says: 'the specific.' By the force of syntactic connection, by the force of the fitness for construal. Although the word 'requiring a specific' does not directly negate specific perception, nevertheless it is directed toward that by secondary signification. And that [secondary signification] operates because of an obstacle in the primary [meaning], because of a connection with what is intended, and because of a purpose in employing a non-denotative [expression]. Of those, he states the obstacle in the primary [meaning]: 'and not.' Indicating the non-technicality of the definition by way of suggesting a common-usage definition, he states the connection with a preceding example: 'just as.' Just as between the Ganges and the bank, subsuming conjunction [under a broader relation], there is invariable co-existence — so too, between non-apprehension and the desire to know what is remembered, by virtue of having a single object, subsuming doubt within [the broader relation], the invariable co-existence in fixed sequence alone is the connection — this is the meaning, because of a specific ease. The purpose of that can also be stated. For it is said: 'doubt, requiring a specific, [is called] doubt.' And thus, when it is said 'generating the desire to know about the specific,' the result of this is shown. This is what is said: 'because of [its] existence when doubt exists.' By this, the general definition through result should also be followed. In the second [resolution], however, the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> for determining [which specific quality obtains] is the objection. Having raised that, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> answers: 'this might be so.' In the third, the absence of purpose is the objection — he removes that through the very formulation of the <s>Vārttika</s>: 'and this is not an extraordinary definition' and so forth — the remainder is: 'by which purpose would be respected.' Now, being-produced is a cause of determination, not of exclusion — therefore he says: 'moreover, of non-eternality.' Now, even so, when there is occurrence in things of the intended type, only occurrence in other things is the property expressible by the same word — whence the restriction? — therefore he says: 'for the common.'

children.text:
nanu tasyeti viśeṣalakṣaṇamastīti, tasmāt tasminnasatyapi na vaktavyasyāvakāśa iti darśayitumiyaṃ yuktirukteti /
paunaruktyaṃ pariharannāha---vimarśapurvakamiti /
pūrvaṃ hi karaṇākaraṇayorguṇadoṣau na cintitau, idānīṃ tau cintyete ityapaunaruktyam /
ata eva prāgāha---yojayatīti /
idānīmāha---avadhārayatīti /
yathā saptame rasa iti /
tathā hi saptamo rasaḥ saṃśayajñāne dharmitayā viṣayaḥ syād, dharmatayā vā? na kadācilloka evaṃ sandigdhe yadayaṃ saptamo rasaḥ sthāṇurvā puruṣo veti, dravyaṃ vā guṇo veti /
nāpyevaṃ sandigdhe ayamupalabhyamānaḥ padārthaḥ saptamo vā raso daśamaṃ vā dravyamiti? saptamo rasaḥ kimasti nāsti veti sandeho bhavatyeveti cet na, ananubhūte smaraṇābhāvāt /
asmṛtasya ca saṃśayāviṣayatvāt /
naudoleti /
sadṛśadarśane 'pyasmaraṇaṃ tu paṭvabhyāsādarapratyayābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: But the non-recollection even upon seeing something similar is due to the absence of the conditions of acuity, practice, and care.

children.text: yathā hi tathāvidhapratyayajanyaḥ saṃskāraḥ, tathā tadudbodhyo 'pīti /
children.translated_text: For just as the residual impression is generated by such a cognition, so too it requires such [conditions] for its awakening.

children.text: dve dvitveneti /
children.translated_text: "Two by two-ness" —

children.text: samuditayorānantarya vivakṣitamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the immediate succession of the two taken together is what is intended.

Now, since it has a specific definition beginning with "of that," therefore, even when that [general definition] does not hold, there is no scope for what needs to be said — this reasoning is to show [that].

children.text: anekadharmapadaṃ lakṣaṇayā asādhāraṇaṃ dharmamāha---tatraikadeśivyākhyādūṣaṇavyājane mukhye bādhakamāha
children.translated_text: The word "many-propertied" (<s>anekadharma</s>) states, through secondary usage, the uncommon property: "There, under the pretext of refuting the partial-view interpretation, [he states] the sublating [argument] against the primary [meaning]" —

children.text:
vārttikakṛt ityata āha---aneketi na sarvatra dravyādau saṃyogajatvamato viśeṣayati---kāryadravya ityādi /
ato mukhye
children.translated_text: the <s>Vārttikakṛt</s> [states it] — therefore he says: "Many-propertied" — not everywhere in substance and the like is there origination from conjunction; therefore he specifies: "In the effect-substance..."

children.text:
bādhakaṃ dṛṣṭavā jaghanyāṃ vṛttim ālambya bhāṣyakṛtā sūtraṃ vyākhyātamiti darśayanniva vārttikam avatārayati---bhāṣyakṛdvyākhyayeti /
punaḥ pṛcchati /
yadi lākṣaṇikamidaṃ padaṃ kaḥ saṃbandha ityāśayavāniti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen the sublating [argument], he shows that the <s>bhāṣyakṛt</s> explained the <s>sūtra</s> by resorting to the secondary meaning, as it were, introducing the <s>vārttika</s> —

children.text:
avadhyavadhimadbhāvaḥ saṃbandhaḥ iti saṃkalayya vārttikārthamāha---etaduktaṃ bhavatīti dharmapadasāmānādhikaraṇyena viśeṣaśabdasya bhāvasādhanatvaṃ nivartayatītyāha---etaduktaṃ bhavatīti dharmapadasāmānādhikaraṇyena viśeṣaśabdasya bhāvasādhanatvaṃ nivartayatītyāha---adhyāhṛteti /
yadyevamalagnakaṃ tarhi bhāṣyaṃ tasyānekasyetyata āha---saṃbandhasāmānyeti /
bījāntaraṃ saṃbandhāntaram /
pūrvaṃ hi vibhāgajatvādinā svāśraya eva śabdastadviparītebhyo vyāvartata ityuktam /
children.translated_text: For previously it was said that sound, by origination from disjunction and the like, is distinguished from those that are the opposite only in its own substratum.

children.text: idānīṃ tu svāśrayācchabdāntara eveti na nivartyata ityabhisandhiḥ /
children.translated_text: But now the intention is: it is not excluded from a different sound in its own substratum.

children.text: ato nivartyanivartakabhāvaḥ saṃbandho bhavatīti bījāntaramiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the relation of what is to be excluded and the excluder is a connection — this is the seed of [another argument].

children.text: tasyānekasya dharmo nivartakatayā yaḥ sa evāneka ityucyate iti vyākhyātamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: it has been explained that the property of that manifold [entity], which is such by virtue of being the excluder, is itself called "manifold."

correlating the meaning of the <s>vārttika</s> by [the principle] "the relation is the state of having a limit and what is limited," he says: "This amounts to saying..." — the co-referentiality of the word "property" [is explained].

children.text:
nanvevaṃ sati kiṃ lakṣaṇayā yāvatā mukhya evānekaśabdo 'stu /
tathā hi pūrvam anekasya dharmo 'nekadharmaḥ sākṣāt samavāyādivṛttyā cet samānapadenaiva gatārtha iti matvā dūṣitaḥ /
nivartakatayā tvanekasya saṃbhavatyevetyata āha---na tvatreti /
children.translated_text: but as the excluder, the manifold is indeed possible — therefore he says: "But not here..."

children.text: kutaḥ? darśayiṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: Why? — "He will show."

children.text: yadi saṃbandhivacana evānekaśabdaḥ syānna dharmaśabdena samānādhikaraṇaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: If the word "manifold" were merely a relational term, it would not be co-referential with the word "property."

children.text: tathā ca bahuvrīheralābhe dharmī na labhyetetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, without obtaining a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound), the property-bearer would not be obtained — that is the meaning.
Now, if so, what need is there for secondary usage? Let the word "manifold" (<s>aneka</s>) be used in its primary sense. For previously, the property of the manifold is the manifold property —

children.text:
evaṃ bhāṣyānugataṃ vārttikamupasaṃhṛtya svatantraṃ vārttikamutthāpya lakṣaṇānurodhena tāvad vyācaṣṭe---prakāreti /
ekamekajātīyam /
aneka naikajātīyaṃ, bhinnajātīyam ityarthaḥ /
tena viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayorviśiṣṭabuddhihetutvenābhedamupacarya viśaiṣyavacano 'yam anekaśabdo viśeṣaṇe dharme prayuktaḥ ityāśayavānāha---bhedābhedapratyayaheturityartha iti /
ata evopasaṃhāre vakṣyati---tatpratyayaheturupacāreṇāneka iti /
taditarebhya iti /
dravyaguṇakarmabhyo na tu śabdetarebhya eva, tadvyatirekasya saṃśayaṃ pratyanupayogāt /
imamevārtha vārttikena saṃvadati---tadidamāheti /
yadyapyasādhāraṇe dharme vivakṣite ekapratyayaheturiti mandaprayojanam, tathā pyasādhāraṇāt saṃśayo bhavan tajjātīyatāyāmeva paryavasyati /
children.translated_text: although when an uncommon property is intended, the [qualification] "the cause of a single cognition" has little purpose, nevertheless, since doubt [can arise] even from the uncommon [property]

children.text: na tu tadvyaktitāyām tajjātoyā api hi vidharmāṇo dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: but not in its instances — for even those of a different class are seen as having the same [uncommon] property.

children.text: na tu ta evetyetat sūcayitumanekavyaktiniṣṭhatā darśitā /
children.translated_text: But not those alone — to indicate this, the residence in multiple instances has been shown.

children.text: ata ekavacanaṃ samarthayati---jātyeti //
children.translated_text: Therefore he justifies the singular number: "By the universal..."
Having thus concluded the <s>vārttika</s> that follows the <s>bhāṣya</s>, he raises the independent <s>vārttika</s> and explains it first in accordance with the definition —

children.text:
idānīmudāharaṇānurodhena vyācaṣṭe---sadādiriti /
atreti vyākhyāne, anurūpam udāharaṇamāhetyarthaḥ /
udāharaṇaparatāṃ sphuṭayitumasādhāraṇāvasare sādhāraṇamapi sadādi kimityupanyastamiti śaṅkāṃ nivārayati---dravyatvādikoṭīti /
sat sattāvat /
anityaṃ pradhvaṃsayoti /
dravyavat samavāyikāraṇatayā dravyamasyāsti /
children.translated_text: Having substance, in the sense of [having] substance as its inherence-cause.

children.text: kāryaṃ prāgabhāvavat /
children.translated_text: An effect — like prior non-existence.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ nimittetaratayāpi sāmānyāviśeṣavat avāntarasāmānyavaditi /
children.translated_text: A cause — by being an instrumental cause as well — like universals and <s>viśeṣas</s> (ultimate particularities), like intermediate universals.

children.text: yattadavocāma, parasparavidhimadubhayaniṣedhapradhānaḥ saṃśayo lakṣyo dvitīyalakṣaṇa iti, tat siddhāntaprasaṅgena niṣedhamupakramya vidhiparyavasānena darśayati---dravyakarmabhyāṃ vyāvartamānaḥ kiṃ guṇa ityādi //
children.translated_text: What we said — that the doubt whose defining target is primarily the negation of both [alternatives] possessing mutual injunction is the second definition — that is established.
Now he explains in accordance with the examples: "Existence and the like..." "Here" — in the explanation — the meaning is: he states an appropriate example.

children.text:
nanu codyamevaitadanupapannam /
na hi vibhāgaje vibhāge pramāṇamasti /
yaugapadyenaiva vibhāgasahasrasyāpi samānadeśasya jāyamānatvādityata āha---ayamamisandhiriti /
yadyapi vaṃśadalayorvibhāgānantaraṃ saṃyoganāśaḥ, tato dravyanāśaḥ, tato dravyanāśaviśiṣṭaṃ kālaṃ svatantraṃ vā avayavamapekṣya dalayorvartamāno vibhāga ākāśādideśād vibhāgaṃ karotīti vaiśeṣikāḥ, tathāpyaprakṛtatvāt saṃyoganāśadravyanāśakramo nopanyastaḥ /
prakṛtasya hi karmaṇo vibhāgadvayajanakatvaṃ krameṇa vā syād, yaugapadyena vā /
na tāvadādyaḥ, karmaṇo vibhāgārambhe 'napekṣayā avilambakāritvaniścayāt /
apekṣāyāṃ vā, ādyamapi vibhāgam anantarameva na kuryāt /
uttarasaṃyoge kartavye pūrvasaṃyogapradhvaṃsāpekṣeti vilambaḥ /
āgantukabhāvamabhisandhāya tu nairapekṣyamuktam /
na dvitīyaḥ, yadā ākāśādideśād vibhāgaṃ karoti karma ta tadāvayavāntarāditi sthitiriti vaiśeṣikāḥ /
tadetad yathāśrutamubhayamapyanupapannam /
ādye vibhāge hi kartavye karmaṇo nirapekṣatvāt sa eva kālaḥ /
dvitīye tu kartavye prathamānantarakāla eva nairapekṣyam /
children.translated_text: but in the second [disjunction] that is to be produced, there is independence precisely at the time immediately after the first.

children.text: ato na kālātipāta ityevamapyupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no delay — this too is tenable.

children.text: yadetyādisthitistu vikasatkamalakuḍmaleṣveva bhagnepyato 'syārthamāha---avayavakriyā hīti /
children.translated_text: The position beginning with "that" applies only to blooming lotus buds — even when [something is] broken, he states the meaning of "from that": "For the action of the parts..."

children.text: kāryaikāryeti---pratyāsattisūcanam //
children.translated_text: "Effect and non-effect" — this is an indication of proximity.
Now, even this objection is untenable. For there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for disjunction arising from disjunction. Even thousands of disjunctions [arising] simultaneously

children.text:
nanu bhavatvevaṃ tāvaduktavyāpteranavadhāraṇam, tathāpi yā kriyā dravyānārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvinaṃ vibhāgamārabhate, nāsau dravyārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvinamapi /
tathātve vā yataḥ kutaścit karmaṇo yugapadubhayavibhāgopapattau calatyevāvayave sarvadravyanāśaprasaṅgaḥ, na caivam /
tasmād yadanārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvijanakaṃ tannārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvijanakaṃ karmeti
children.translated_text: Now, let there be, for the time being, the non-ascertainment of the stated pervasion. Even so, the action that is the counterpart of conjunction that does not produce substance —

children.text:
siddhe viparyayo 'pi siddha iti tatrāha---kriyāvailakṣaraṇyātviti /
ayamarthaḥ /
vibhāgasya tāvadvailakṣaraṇyamavaśyamabhyupetavyam, anyathā niyamānupapatteḥ /
tadanurodhāt karmaṇo 'pi jātikṛtaṃ sahakārikṛtaṃ vā vailakṣaṇyamavaśyaṃ svīkartavyam /
tadetasya vailakṣaṇyam ārambhakānārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvivibhāgadvayajanakatayā ekatra, anyatra tvanārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvivibhāgamātrajanakatayā paryavasyati, āhosvidārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvivibhāgamātrajanakatayaikatra, anyatra tvanārambhakasaṃyogamātrapratidvandvivibhāgajanakatayeti na niyantuṃ śakyate /
anārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvinamapi vibhāgaṃ
children.translated_text: when the established [view] is proven, the reverse too is proven — therefore he says regarding that: "Because of the distinctiveness of action..." The meaning is this: to begin with, [regarding] disjunction —

children.text: kariṣyati, ko virodhaḥ? yathānārambhakottarasaṃyogajanakatve satyeva kutaścit viśeṣādārambhakottarasaṃyogajanakatvamapi karmaṇaḥ, anyathā tatrāpyanayaiva diśā kāraṇamātrasaṃyogapūrvakāḥ kāraṇākāraṇasaṃyogāḥ kalpanīyāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: what contradiction is there in its also generating subsequent conjunction that does produce [substance]? Just as, while having the capacity to generate subsequent conjunction that is non-productive, from some specific [feature] it also generates subsequent conjunction that is productive —

children.text: yathā ca tatra krame pramāṇaṃ nāsti tathehāpīti /
children.translated_text: and just as there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for sequence there, so too here.

children.text: yadekāntavibhāgamekamavayavadvayamātravartinam, anyā tu vibhāgadvayamavayavadvayavartinamavayavānavayavavartinaṃ ceti /
