children.translated_text: One [action] is a disjunction in one direction, residing only in a pair of parts; another [action] is a pair of disjunctions, residing in a pair of parts [and their] parts —

children.text: yathā caitadvailakṣṇyaṃ tathā varamevamasatu yadekānārambhakasaṃyogapratidvandvinamanyā tu ārambhakānārambhakapratidvandvinaṃ janayatītyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: and just as this distinctiveness [holds], so too it is better that in this case, one [action] is the counterpart of conjunction that does not produce substance, while another is the counterpart of productive [conjunction] —

children.text:
tasmāt kāraṇamātravibhāgapūrvake kāraṇākāraṇavibhāge pramāṇaṃ nāstīti nābhyupagamyata ityetāvanmātravyaktīkaraṇaphalo 'yamanamyupagama ityāha---tasmāditi /
kāraṇākāraṇavibhāgapūrvakastu kāryākāryavibhāgaḥ prāmāṇika ityabhyupagamyata ityāha---yastviti /
kāryaikārthasamavāyastarumadhikṛtya kvacit pāṭhaḥ /
kāryakāraṇaikārthasamavāyaḥ /
so 'ṅgulīmadhikṛtyeti /
sa iti /
asādhāraṇībhūtanimittajātīyāsamavāyikāraṇajanya iti pratijñārthaḥ ādyaśabdatvāditi hetvarthaḥ /
yadyapi vibhāgāpekṣavibhāgāsamavāyikāraṇam asādhāraṇaṃ śabde tadeva vaktumucitam, tathāpi kāraṇamātravibhāgajavibhāgamabhyupetyoktaṃ vārttikakṛteti tathaivāha---tadevamiti, etadapi vyabhicārya samarthayati---tadapīti /
yadyapyevamapi vibhāgajatvāditi heturadoṣa eva, na hi vibhāgād dravyasya janma saṃbhavati,
children.translated_text: therefore, there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for a disjunction of cause-and-non-cause preceded by the disjunction of mere causes — this much alone is not accepted.

children.text:
kamaṇo vā /
sa hi dravyānārambhakasamaveto 'kāraṇameva, ārambhakasamavetastu saṃyoganāśadvārā vināśaka eva, karmaṇo 'pi kāraṇaṃ vibhāgo bhavanna tāvadādyasya tasminnasati vibhāgasyaivānupapatteḥ /
taduttarasyāpi pūrvakarmanivṛttau janma /
yadā tu tannivṛttiruttarasaṃyogāt, tadā vibhāgasyāpīti kathamuttarakarmajanma vibhāgāt? tasmādasandigdhavyāptikaṃ vibhāgajatvaṃ śabdasya guṇatve pramāṇameva /
children.translated_text: But when the cessation of that [conjunction] is from subsequent conjunction, then even from disjunction [there would be generation] — so how [is there] the birth of subsequent action from disjunction? Therefore, when [the matter is] not established,

children.text: na ca tadavāntaraviśeṣamādāyāsādhāraṇyaṃ doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: nor is uncommonness a fault by taking [only] that sub-particular.

children.text: tathā sati dhūmo 'pyagamakaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: If it were so, even smoke would be a non-indicator [of fire].

children.text: tathāpi bhāṣyoktodāharaṇavyutpādanamātramidamiti mantavyam //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, this should be understood as merely the elucidation of the example stated in the <s>bhāṣya</s>.

[whether it is] of an action, or [of another kind]. For that [action], being co-inherent with what does not produce substance, is a non-cause only; but being co-inherent with what does produce [substance], it is a cause of destruction through the destruction of conjunction.

children.text:
nanu tulyajātīyeṣvityādivivakṣitaviparītāpādikeyaṃ yuktirityata āha---yadyapīti /
pūrvaiva yuktiriyaṃ bhāṣyakāragauravāduktetyarthaḥ /
pūrvasmāraṇena prakārāntaratvaṃ sphuṭayan vārttikamavatārayati---pūrvamiti /
samāno hi dharmaḥ pakṣe vartamānaḥ sapakṣavipakṣadharmābhyāmekajātīyaḥ, tadrūpapratiṣedhaścāyamaneka iti /
tathā ca pakṣe vartamānasya sapakṣavipakṣadharmābhyāṃ vijātīyatvamuktaṃ bhavati /
yaśca pakṣagaḥ sapakṣavipakṣadharmābhyāṃ vijātīyo dharmaḥ, so 'sādhāraṇa eveti bhavatyabhidheyāvinābhūtatvāt lakṣaṇāviṣayaḥ /
tadidamuktam---lakṣaṇayaiveti /
children.translated_text: This is what was stated: 'By indirect indication alone...'

children.text: vārttikaṃ yojayati---samāneti /
children.translated_text: He construes the <s>vārttika</s>: 'Common...'

children.text: samānaśabdena pratiyogitayā buddhāvasamāne 'pyusthāpite saṃśayakāraṇatve ca tasya pramāṇasiddhe tasmin vaktavye yadanekapadamupādatte sūtrakārastena jānīmo nūnamayamevārtho 'nayā vacobhaṅgyā anena darśita iti yojanārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the word 'common' (<s>samāna</s>), even what is uncommon in cognition is set up as a counter-correlate; and when its being a cause of doubt is established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, and that is what is to be stated — the fact that the <s>sūtrakāra</s> employs multiple words — from this we understand that surely this very meaning is shown by this turn of phrase — this is the purpose of the construal.

children.text: etena sarveṣūktaprakāreṣu sūtrakārasya saṃpratipattirdarśitā bhavati //
children.translated_text: By this, the <s>sūtrakāra's</s> agreement with all the modes explained has been shown.

Now, this reasoning — 'among those of the same class' and so forth — leads to the opposite of what is intended — to this he says: 'Although...' This reasoning is the very same as before, stated [again] out of deference to the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> — that is the meaning. Making clear its being a different mode through the recollection of the earlier [argument], he introduces the <s>vārttika</s>: 'The earlier...' For a common property present in the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), being of the same class as the properties of the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and the dissimilar case (<s>vipakṣa</s>), and the negation of its form being multiple — thus, what is stated is the heterogeneity of the property present in the subject from the properties of the similar and dissimilar cases. And the property present in the subject that is heterogeneous from the properties of the similar and dissimilar cases is simply uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) — and thus, since it is invariably accompanied by what is to be expressed, it falls outside the scope of indirect indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).

children.text:
pṛtchatītyādinā lakṣaṇaprakārāṇāṃ prayojanaṃ darśitamityanugantavyam /
pratyabhijñānaṃ tāvadvyaktiviṣayakaṃ nāstyeva gakārādāviti dvitīye vyutpādanīyam /
yadāpyasti tadāpyasya viṣayaḥ kiṃ vyaktirutajātiriti viṣayataḥ sandihyate /
yadāpi vyaktirevāsya viṣayaḥ, tadāpi pramāṇamapramāṇaṃ veti sandeha ityabhiprāyavān saṃmugdhamāha
children.translated_text: It should be understood that by 'he asks' and so forth, the purpose of the modes of definition has been shown. To begin with, recognition pertaining to the individual does not exist at all in the case of the letter <s>ga</s> and the like — this should be explained in the second [section]. Even when it does exist, there is doubt regarding its object: is its object the individual or the universal? Even when the individual alone is its object, there is doubt whether it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> or not — with this intention, he speaks confusedly:

children.text:
sādṛśyenāpi saṃbhavati, svayaṃ sandigdhaṃ saditi /
yadyapi gavādivyaktaya iva gotvādyupadhānā iti jātimātrapadārthavādī na svīkarotyeva, tathāpi svasiddhāntadārḍhyena paro 'pyevamaṅgīkārayitavyaḥ /
anyathābhidheyasyāvinābhāvapratītireva kathaṃ vyaktibhiḥ? tadabhāve ca kathaṃ lakṣaṇāpīti? kathaṃ netyādi /
na ca vācyaṃ śabdasya tathābhāvasandehe 'pi ghaṭādau niścitatvena vyāptigraho yadi syāt ko doṣa iti /
sarvopasaṃhāreṇa hi vyāptiniścaye yatkṛtakaṃ tadavaśyamanityamiti kṛtakatvaṃ śabde niścayameva kuryāt /
satpratipakṣatayā śabde sādhyasiddhiṃ na karoti /
apratihatatayā tu buddhyādau karotīti cet---na, pratipakṣasādhane vyāptisaddūṣayati satyapi sādhyasiddheravirodhāt /
children.translated_text: 'It is possible even through similarity, and is itself doubtful as existent.' Although the proponent of universals alone as the meaning of words does not at all accept that individuals like cows and the like are underlain by cow-ness and the like, nevertheless, the opponent too must be brought to accept this by the firmness of one's own doctrine. Otherwise, how would the cognition of the invariable accompaniment of what is to be expressed occur through individuals? And in its absence, how would there be even indirect indication? 'How not...' and so forth. Nor should one say: 'Even when there is doubt about its being so for sound, if the pervasion is grasped with certainty regarding pots and the like, what is the fault?' For when pervasion is ascertained through complete enumeration — 'whatever is produced is necessarily impermanent' — the producedness would generate certainty in sound itself. [If one says:] because of having a counter-reason (<s>satpratipakṣa</s>), it does not bring about the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> in sound, but because of being unimpeded, it does so in cognition and the like — no, because even when the <s>sādhya</s> is established, there is no inconsistency with the genuine vitiating of the pervasion in proving the counter-reason.

children.text: virodhe 'duṣṭādapi na sādhyasiddhiriti sarvānumānocchadaprasaṅgaḥ /
imaṃ cārthamanantarameva vakṣyate /
children.translated_text: And this very point will be stated immediately after.

children.text: vyāptidoṣe tu sarvopasaṃhārābhāvāt kathaṃ tadbalena buddhyādau sādhyasiddhiriti sandigdhatattvaṃ śabdaṃ vihāya vyāptiriti cet? evaṃ tarhi śabdādanyatve sati kṛtakatvāditi vācyam /
children.translated_text: If one says: 'When there is a defect of pervasion, since there is no complete enumeration, how can there be establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> in cognition and the like by its force? Setting aside sound whose nature is doubtful, let pervasion [be established]' — then one should state: 'being produced, while being other than sound.'

children.text: tathā ca yadi daivāt śabdo 'pyanitya eva vastutaḥ, tadā asamarthaviśeṣaṇatvāpattiriti sandigdhāsamarthaviśeṣaṇatvamiti /
children.translated_text: And thus, if by chance sound too is actually impermanent, then there would be the consequence of a qualifier that is incapable [of restriction] — hence there is [the fault of] doubtful incapable qualifier.

children.text: tasmāt sūṣṭhūktaṃ sandigdhe nityānityabhāve śabde kṛtakatvaṃ gatamiti nānityatvena svabhāvataḥ pratibaddhamiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it was well stated: when the permanent or impermanent nature of sound is doubtful, producedness has been cognized [in it] — hence it is not bound by its own nature to impermanence.
If there were inconsistency, then even from an unvitiated [reason], there would be no establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> — and there would follow the consequence of the destruction of all inference.

children.text:
pratyayabhedabheditvaṃ kāraṇatīvratvāditāratamyena tīvratīvratarāditvaṃ pratyekaṃ satpratipakṣatvam ityekaikasyānvayato vyatirekato vobhayakoṭyanupanāyakatayā na saṃśayahetutvam /
nāpi niścayahetutvamasatpratipakṣatvarūpavaikalyādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The differentiation by difference of cognitions, the hierarchy of intensity such as intense, more intense, and the like due to the intensity of causes and the like, and the counter-reason for each — since each one individually, by positive concomitance or by negative concomitance, cannot bring about both alternatives, it is not a cause of doubt. Nor is it a cause of certainty, because of the deficiency in the form of not having a counter-reason — that is the meaning.

children.text:
militayostvasādhāraṇatvamiti /
tathā ca tenaiva rūpeṇa saṃśayakāraṇatvaṃ nānyathetyarthaḥ /
anunāsikatvādayo hi sāmānyaviśeṣāḥ pratyakṣā bhavantaḥ pratyakṣavyaktivṛttaya eva bhavitumarhanti /
na cānyendriyeṇa vyaktiranyena jātirupalabdhigocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that the individual is perceived by one sense-organ while the universal is perceived by another.

children.text: tathā cānunāsikatvādisāmānyāśrayabhūtāyā eva vyakteḥ śrāvaṇatve 'pyanityatvamubhayavādisiddham /
children.translated_text: And thus, even when the auditory nature of the individual that is the substratum of the universals nasality and the like [is accepted], its impermanence is accepted by both parties.

children.text: kevalaṃ sa vyaktirākāśāśrayā vā, anyāśrayā veti vipratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text: The only disagreement is whether that individual has space (<s>ākāśa</s>) as its substratum or something else.

children.text: seyamāstāṃ tāvat //
children.translated_text: Let that be set aside for now.

But when combined, there is uncommonness. And thus, only in that very form is there the status of being a cause of doubt, not otherwise — that is the meaning. For nasality and the like, being common and specific properties that are perceptible, must be properties residing in perceptible individuals alone.

children.text: nanu tathāpi naiyāyikānāṃ mate śabdāśrayā evānunāsikatvādayo dharmā, na ca pakṣeṇaitra vyabhicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, even so, in the view of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, nasality and the like are properties of sound alone, and there is no deviation in the subject.

children.text: na, avarṇātmakenāpi taddharmaśālinānaikāntikatopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: No, because inconclusiveness is established even by [an entity] whose nature is the vowel <s>a</s> that possesses that property.

children.text: tasyāpi pakṣatvamiti cet---na, taddarśane 'naikāntiko 'yamiti virodhamukhenāpyudbhāvanāt, vastutaḥ śabdadharmatve ca kālātyayāpadeśadoṣāt /
children.translated_text: If one says 'that too is the subject' — no, because upon observing that, the demonstration takes the form of contradiction too, [saying] 'this is inconclusive'; and in reality, if it were a property of sound, there would be the fault of <s>kālātyayāpadeśa</s> (belated statement).

children.text: aprayojakāśca rūpādayo nityāścakṣurādyekaikendriyagrāhyatvāt rūpatvādivadityanena samānayogapekṣamatvāditi //
children.translated_text: And form and the like are irrelevant, because of being permanent and graspable by a single sense-organ such as the eye and the like — just as form-ness and the like, by requiring the same co-occurring factors, [the suffix] <s>-matvādi</s>.

children.text:
vipratipatterityādi /
asya ca lakṣībhūtasya saṃśayasya parasparaviraharūpavidhiniṣedhaprādhānyāt /
astyātmā nāstyātmetyudāharaṇaṃ tu bhāṣyakṛtaiva darśitaṃ sphuṭamiti na prapañcitaṃ vārtikaṭīkākārābhyām /
udāharaṇamātraṃ caitat /
na nvidameva ādaraṇīyam /
ātmano 'nupalabdhacaratve smṛtyanārūḍhasya saṃśayānāspadatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because when the self's nature has not been perceived, being unascended to memory, it cannot be a locus of doubt.

children.text: upalabdhacaratve vā sarvathāpahnavāyogāt /
children.translated_text: Or when its nature has been perceived, because denial in every way is impossible.

children.text: etacca tṛtīye prapañcanīyamitīhopekṣitam, śabdo nitya ityeke /
children.translated_text: And this is to be elaborated in the third [section], hence it is set aside here. But 'sound is eternal — say some;

children.text: netyapare ityādi tūdāhāraṇīyam //
children.translated_text: not so — say others' and the like should be cited as illustrations.

'Because of divergence of views' and so forth. And this doubt, which is the target, is primarily of the form of affirmation and negation consisting of mutual exclusion. But the illustration 'the self exists, the self does not exist' was shown clearly by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> himself, and so was not elaborated by the <s>vārttika</s> and <s>ṭīkā</s> authors. And this is merely an illustration — this alone need not be insisted upon.

children.text:
kāraṇabhedeneti /
lakṣaṇabhedarūpeṇa trividham, vidhipradhānaṃ niṣedhapradhānaṃ niṣedhavidhipradhānamiti /
na cānabhyāsadaśāpanna iti /
anabhyāsadaśāpannopalabdhau hi pramāṇottarabhāvāniścaye buddhitvasāmānyopalabdheḥ satyatvāsatyatvasaṃdeha iti yadyabhimatam, prathamapadenaiva gatametat /
tatastaddvāraker'the saṃdeha iha vivakṣita iti yadi, so 'pi svarūpato deśakālataḥ prakārato vati? ādyastāvadvirodhādevāsaṃgataḥ /
na hīdamidaṃ na veti saṃbhavati /
nidrādyupaplavābhāvaniścayena tadekakāraṇakoṭivyudāsāt dvitīyo 'pi nirastaḥ /
upaplavasaṃdehe tvādhyātmika eva saṃśayaḥ /
tṛtīye tvāha---na nāgo vā nago veti /
children.translated_text: Regarding the third, he says: 'Is it a serpent or a mountain?'

children.text: evamayogyeti /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, unfit...'

children.text: etāvāṃstu viśeṣo yat sthāṇurvā puruṣo vetyatropalabdhyanupalabdhī anutpādādevāvyavasthite /
children.translated_text: But the distinction is this: in 'a post or a person,' perception and non-perception are unsettled simply because they have not arisen.

children.text: prakṛte tūdāharaṇe jātameva jalajñānamaprāmāṇyaśaṅkayā na vyavasthitamiti //
children.translated_text: But in the illustration at hand, the water-cognition has already arisen but is not settled due to the suspicion of its not being a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

'By difference of cause...' By way of difference of definition, there is a threefold [classification]: primarily affirmation, primarily negation, and primarily both negation and affirmation. 'And not having reached the stage of non-habituation...' For if [one holds] that upon perceiving what has reached the stage of non-habituation, when the <s>pramāṇa</s>-posterior nature is uncertain, because of the perception of the universal 'cognition-ness,' there is doubt about its being true or false — if that is intended, this is already conveyed by the first term alone. If then [one says] that through that medium, doubt about the object is intended here — is that [doubt] about its essential nature, or about its place and time, or about its mode? The first, to begin with, is untenable because of self-contradiction. For 'this is this and not this' is not possible. The second too is removed by the certainty of the absence of impediments such as sleep and the like, since thereby one alternative of the cause is eliminated. But when there is doubt about impediment, the doubt is merely subjective.

children.text:
evamayogyeti /
yadi viśeṣasmṛtisahitāyā ayogyānupalabdheḥ dharmiṇamanantarbhāvya saṃśayaḥ syāt sa tāvannātyantānupalabdhakoṭyullekhī, tatra smṛterabhāvāt /
nāpyupalabdhakoṭyullekhī /
children.translated_text: Nor would it trace the alternative of perception.

children.text: na hi bhavati paramāṇurasti naveti astyeva yataḥ /
children.translated_text: For the [doubt] 'does the atom exist or not?' does not [arise as] 'it certainly exists, because...'

children.text: iheti cet? tarhi deśakālādiviśeṣaṃ dharmiṇamupādāyopapadyate /
children.translated_text: If one says 'here [it does]' — then it is possible by taking a locus of doubt qualified by a specific place, time, and the like.

children.text: tathā ca sa upalabdhaḥ sannanvayato vyatirekato vipratipattito vā viśeṣau smārayet, na svarūpata iti pūrvānupraveśa ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, that [locus], being perceived, would recall the specific features through positive concomitance, negative concomitance, or divergence of views — not through its own essential nature — and this falls under the previous [classification] — that is the meaning.

'Thus, unfit...' If doubt, without subsuming the locus of doubt under unfit non-perception accompanied by the recollection of a specific feature, were to arise — that, to begin with, would not trace the alternative of complete non-perception, since memory is absent there.

children.text:
tadidamuktam---na saṃśayo vinā samānadharmādidarśanamiti /
sāmagrībhedena bhede traividhyaṃ viṣayakṛtamiti /
api
children.translated_text: This is what was stated: 'There is no doubt without the observation of a common property and the like.' The threefold [classification] by difference of causal complex is made with respect to the object. Moreover,

children.text: tvanekavidhaḥ, pratyekaṃ kāraṇānāṃ viṣayavyavasthāṃ pratyahetutvādityarthaḥ //23 //
children.translated_text: it is of many kinds, since each cause individually is not a cause with respect to the determination of the object — that is the meaning.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
pūrvāṅgatvāviśeṣe 'pi saṃśaye sati prayojanānusaṃdhānāt tataḥ prayojanasyāpakarṣa ityuktamṛ /
prayojanamanusaṃvāya
children.translated_text: Even though there is no distinction in being a prior component, when doubt exists, because of the investigation of purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), from that there is the inferiority of purpose — thus it was stated. Having investigated the purpose,

children.text: ca tatsādhanībhūtanyāyamanusandhitsato dṛṣṭāntānusaraṇamiti dṛṣṭāntādasyotkarṣa uddeśe /
children.translated_text: and for one who wishes to investigate the method (<s>nyāya</s>) that is the means to that [purpose], there is the following of the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) — thus from the example, its superiority in the enumeration.

children.text: saiva saṃgatirihāpīti āha---uddeśeti //
children.translated_text: That very connection [applies] here too — he says: 'Enumeration...'

children.text:
arthaśabdasya lakṣaṇe 'kiñcitkaratvādādhikyaṃ manvānastātparyamāha---atreti /
arthapadaṃ bhāṣyakāreṇa anūdyāpi na vivṛtamityata āha---sasādhanāviti /
nanvevaṃ satyuttarabhāṣyavirodhaḥ, tadāptihānopāyamanutiṣṭhatītyatra tacchabdenārthasya parāmarśāt /
sukhaduḥkhāptihānopāyamiti ca prakṛtasaṃgaterityata āha---na ceti /
atra ca ṭīkāyāṃ yadyapi tathāpīti tadacatuṣṭayamadhyāharanti /
lokyata ityādi /
tathā ca prāmāṇikatvādeva prayojanaṃ na vaktavyamiti vākyārthaḥ /
nanvevaṃ sati pramāṇamapi na vyutpādyam /
children.translated_text: Now, if so, <s>pramāṇa</s> too need not be explained.

children.text: tacca tvayā vyutpāditamityata āha---na ca pramāṇamīdṛśamiti /
children.translated_text: And that [pramāṇa] has been explained by you — to this he says: 'And <s>pramāṇa</s> is not of this kind.'

children.text: yathā ceti /
children.translated_text: 'And as...'

children.text: tathā ca pramāṇopapannaṃ na vācyamiti vadataḥ svacaritāvirodha ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, the meaning is: for one who says 'what is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> need not be stated,' there is no contradiction with his own conduct.

Considering that the word <s>artha</s> (object/meaning), because of doing something [additional] in the definition, conveys something more, he states the purport: 'Here...' The word <s>artha</s>, even though mentioned by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>, was not explained — to this he says: 'Together with the means...' Now, if so, there would be contradiction with the subsequent <s>bhāṣya</s>, since in 'he follows the means of attaining and avoiding that,' the word 'that' refers back to the object (<s>artha</s>). And since the contextual connection is 'the means of attaining and avoiding pleasure and pain' — to this he says: 'And not...' And here, in the <s>ṭīkā</s>, although 'even so' — they supply those four [items]. 'It is commonly known...' and so forth. And thus, because of being established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, the purpose need not be stated — this is the meaning of the sentence.

children.text:
kathamasaya prayuktau sādhanatvaṃ sato 'sato vā? asato 'pi svajñānadvārā vyāpārāntareṇa vā? kva ca prayojayati, svātmanyeva vā svasādhane vā? kathaṃ ca vyāpakaṃ svarūpeṇa, karmavidyādvārā veti parīkṣāsādhyamityarthaḥ /
na brūmaḥ prayojanaṃ nyāyasya aṅgamupakārakam, kiṃ tu prayojanavān nyāyastadgatācintāṅgīkarotīti /
yāvad vākyaṃ na samāpyate tāvadeva /
nanu cintāpi nāṅgam /
na hi nyāyānnirṇayaścānirṇayaśca /
na ca nirṇayādanyat prayojanaṃ nyāyasya /
tasmāt kimanena cintiteneti śaṅkāmapanetumāha---mukhyamityādi /
gauṇaṃ prayojanaṃ mukhyasyaiva prayojanasya kṛte upādīyate /
mukhyamapi yadyanyopakārārthamupādīyeta,
children.translated_text: How does purpose, when employed, have the status of being a means — of what exists or of what does not exist? Even of what does not exist, through the medium of its own cognition, or through another operation? And where does it motivate — in itself alone, or in its own means? And how is the pervader — through its own nature, or through the medium of <s>karma</s> and knowledge? — this is to be determined through examination — that is the meaning. We do not say that purpose is a component of <s>nyāya</s> in the sense of being a subsidiary; rather, the <s>nyāya</s> that possesses purpose accepts the investigation directed toward that [purpose] as a component. Only until the sentence is not completed. Now, investigation too is not a component. For from <s>nyāya</s>, there is both determination and non-determination. And <s>nyāya</s> has no purpose other than determination. Therefore, 'what is the use of this investigation?' — to remove this doubt, he says: 'Primary...' and so forth. The secondary purpose is adopted for the sake of the primary purpose itself. Even the primary, if it were adopted for the benefit of another,

children.text:
mukhyatāmeva jahyāt /
etadeva hi mukhyasya mukhyatvam, yadananyārthatayā puruṣāpekṣitatvam /
na ca nirṇaya evamityarthaḥ /
vākyaśeṣamāha---prayojanavāṃstviti /
mukhyaprayojanavāneva nyāyo gauṇaprayojananirṇayakāraṇatayopādeyo yataḥ, atastadgatāṃ mukhyaprayojanagatāṃ cintāmabhisandhānamaṅgīkaroti aṅgatayā apekṣate /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, yadyapi na prayojanaṃ nyāyasyāṅgaṃ sādhyatvāt, tathāpi tadabhisandhānamaṅgam tadantareṇa nyāyasyāpravṛtteḥ /
niṣphalasyāpi ca svayaṃ phalavanyāyapravartakatayā tatsannidheḥ /
yathā svargasya yāgānaṅgasyāpi abhisandhānaṃ svayamaphalamapi yāgapravṛttiṃ prati kāraṇatayā saṃnidhīyamānamaṅgamiti /
etadevopasaṃhāravyājenāha---tasmāditi /
children.translated_text: He states this very thing in the guise of a conclusion: 'Therefore...'

children.text: anye tu, kiṃ tu mukhyamityavacchidya vyācakṣate, pradhānamuddeśyamiti yāvaditi /
children.translated_text: Others, however, cutting off at 'But the primary,' explain: '[What is] primary [means] the chief, the intended — to that extent.'

children.text: tadāpyevamevottaratra neyamiti /
children.translated_text: Even on that [interpretation], it should be interpreted in just this way in what follows.

children.text: akṣarārthastu vārttikasya ya khalu niṣprayojanā cintā prayojanābhisandhānaśūnyaḥ saṃśayo nāsau nyāyasya pravartaka iti sphuṭatvānnoktaḥ //14 //
children.translated_text: But the literal meaning of the <s>vārttika</s> — that investigation devoid of purpose, i.e. doubt devoid of the intention toward purpose, does not motivate <s>nyāya</s> — was not stated because of its being clear.

would lose its very primary-ness. For this is precisely the primary-ness of the primary: that it is desired by a person as being not-for-another's-sake. And determination is not of this kind — that is the meaning. He states the remainder of the sentence: 'But that which has purpose...' Since the <s>nyāya</s> that possesses the primary purpose is to be adopted as a cause of the determination of the secondary purpose, therefore it accepts — i.e., requires as a component — the investigation directed toward the primary purpose. This is what is stated: although purpose is not a component of <s>nyāya</s> because it is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be established), nevertheless the intention directed toward it is a component, because without it <s>nyāya</s> would not proceed. And even when [the investigation] is itself fruitless, because of its proximity to <s>nyāya</s> that is fruitful and that motivates [activity], [it is a component]. Just as the intention directed toward heaven — which is not a component of sacrifice — even though itself fruitless, is a component because it is present as a cause for the undertaking of sacrifice.

children.text: laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ yasminnarthe buddhisābhyaṃ sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ //15 //
children.translated_text: That in which both ordinary and examining persons have consensus of cognition — that is the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>). // [Sūtra] 15 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text: saṃśaye prayojane ca sati kva punaretat sādhyasambaddhaṃ sādhanamupalabheya, yadupādāyaitatsādhayeyamiti jijñāsākramānurodhena prayojanānantaraṃ dṛṣṭāntasyoddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: When there is doubt and purpose, [the question arises:] 'where then shall I find this proof connected to the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), by means of which I may establish this?' — in accordance with the order of inquiry, the enumeration of the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) comes after the purpose.

children.text: saiva cātrāpi saṃgatirityāha---krameti //
children.translated_text: And the same connection [applies] here too — he says: 'in order...'

children.text:
na ca sāmānyalakṣaṇamantareṇa viśeṣalakṣaṇāvatāra iti tatsūcakaṃ sūtraṃ tathaiva vyācaṣṭe---sādhyasādharmyāditi /
atrānvayavyatirekavati prakāradvaye 'pi sādhyasādhanayoravinābhāvasiddhireva phalaṃ pratīyate /
tathā cāvinābhāvaviṣayatayā aryyate yaḥ, sor'tho dṛṣṭānta iti sāmānyalakṣaṇalābhaḥ /
viśeṣe tu ṭīkā sphuṭaiva /
nanvevaṃrūpor'tha iti kuta etadityata āha---udāharaṇeti /
kṣīranīravadavivecitāni sāṃvyavahārikāṇi pramāṇāni nisargaḥ /
tadbhāvo naisargikaḥ /
khalitailavad vivecitāni durnirūpārthagocarāṇi pramāṇāni vinayaḥ /
sa eva vainayikaḥ /
tamāha---śāstreti /
sārūpyavyutpattyartha iti vārttike sārūpyagrahaṇamavinābhāvamātropalakṣaṇaparamityabhisaṃdhāyāha---dṛṣṭāntasya prayojanamāheti /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vārttika</s>, 'similarity' (<s>sārūpya</s>) — intending that it is ultimately indicative of mere invariable concomitance — he says: 'he states the purpose of the example...'

children.text: na khalviti /
children.translated_text: 'Not indeed...'

children.text: api tu vastusthita eva jñāpyata iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: But rather, what is established in reality is [merely] made known — this is the remainder.

children.text: tadetacchalena sāmānyalakṣaṇamāviṣkṛtam //25 //
children.translated_text: This very [point] has been brought out by way of a ruse, as the general definition.

And since without the general definition there is no introduction of the specific definition, he explains the <s>sūtra</s> that indicates that in exactly that way: 'from the similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>...' Here, in both modes — that involving positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) — the establishment of the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> is understood to be the result. And thus, the object that is cognized as having invariable concomitance as its subject-matter — that object is the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) — this is the obtaining of the general definition. As for the specific [definition], the sub-commentary is clear enough. Now, whence [is it known that the] object is of such a form? — to this he says: 'example...' <s>Pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) that are mixed together like milk and water, undiscriminated and conventional, are the natural state (<s>nisarga</s>). The condition of that is 'natural' (<s>naisargika</s>). <s>Pramāṇas</s> discriminated like oil pressed from sesame, pertaining to objects difficult to ascertain, constitute discipline (<s>vinaya</s>). That very [discipline] is 'disciplinary' (<s>vainayika</s>). He states that: 'by the <s>śāstra</s>...'

children.text: // iti nyāyapūrvāṅgalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the definition of the preliminary components of <s>Nyāya</s>.

children.text: // nyāyāśrayasiddhāntalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: The section on the definition of <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), which is the basis of <s>Nyāya</s>.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
evaṃ nyāyapūrvāṅgaprakaraṇaṃ samarthya parikalitasāmarthyaṃ sādhanaṃ yatropaneyaṃ sa siddhāntāparanāmā nyāyasyāśrayo 'vasaraprāptatvāducyata iti /
atha siddhānta iti bhāṣyaṃ sphuṭārtham /
sūtramapaṭhitvā vyākhyānaṃ tu kuta ityata āha---atreti /
bhāṣyakārasya rītiriyam, svapratibhayā svatantrasūtravivaraṇaṃ bhāṣyamiti lakṣaṇāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus examined the section on the preliminary components of <s>Nyāya</s>, the proof whose capacity has been ascertained — that to which [the proof] is to be applied — namely <s>siddhānta</s>, which is another name for the basis of <s>Nyāya</s>, is discussed because its occasion has arrived. 'Now, <s>siddhānta</s>...' — the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is clear in meaning. But whence the explanation without having read the <s>sūtra</s>? — to this he says: 'here...' This is the method of the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> — [the <s>Bhāṣya</s>] is, by definition, an independent exposition of the <s>sūtra</s> through one's own insight — this is the purport.

children.text: saṃsthitiritthambhāvavyavastheti bhāṣyaṃ dṛṣṭvā idamiti sāmānyābhyupagame siddhāntabhramaḥ syāt, ato vyācaṣṭe, bhāṣye ceti //
children.translated_text: Seeing the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [statement] that '<s>saṃsthiti</s> (establishment) is the determination of such-and-such a state' — there would be the error that this is merely a general acceptance of <s>siddhānta</s> — therefore he explains, 'and in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>...'

children.text: arthābhyupagamo 'bhyupagato vārthaḥ siddhāntaḥ, viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaṃ prati kāmacārāditi ca prathama sūtra evoktam, ato na granthacatuṣṭayasyāpi mitho virodhaḥ //26 //
children.translated_text: An accepted meaning, or a meaning that has been accepted, is <s>siddhānta</s> — and it was stated already in the first <s>sūtra</s> that there is freedom regarding the qualifier-qualified relation — therefore there is no mutual contradiction even among the four texts.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: nanu yadi tantraṃ pramāṇamabhimatam, kathaṃ vyatirekamāha---yo 'tho na śāstrita ityata āha---aśāstrito 'prāmāṇika iti /
children.translated_text: Now, if <s>tantra</s> (a system) is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, how does he state the exclusion: 'that meaning which is not [established] by the <s>śāstra</s>'? — to this he says: 'what is not [established] by the <s>śāstra</s> is not authoritative (<s>aprāmāṇika</s>).'

children.text: nanvevaṃ bauddhasiddhāntā na siddhāntāḥ syuraprāmāṇikatvāt, tathā ya vyatikrame 'pi teṣāṃ nāpasiddhānto bhavedityata āha--ābhimānikaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: Now, if so, Buddhist <s>siddhāntas</s> would not be <s>siddhāntas</s>, since they are non-authoritative; similarly, even their violation would not constitute <s>apasiddhānta</s> (counter-doctrine) — to this he says: 'and the notional (<s>ābhimānika</s>) [siddhānta]...'

children.text: etaccāgrato vārttikakāra eva tatpratyayādabhyupagama iti vadan sphuṭīkariṣyatīti //27 //
children.translated_text: And this — the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> himself will clarify ahead by saying 'acceptance based on the cognition of that' —

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
nanu sadṛśatantrāsiddho 'ṣyarthaḥ kvacidabhyupagamyamānaḥ siddhānto yathā prābhākare niyogo vākyārthaḥ, nyāye upamānaṃ pramāṇamityata āha---samānaśabda ekaparyāyaḥ /
yathā taruvṛkṣaśabdau samānārthāviti /
tathāpyanekasambandhāpekṣayā ekamapi
children.translated_text: Now, this meaning, which is unestablished in a similar system (<s>sadṛśatantra</s>), yet accepted somewhere, is a <s>siddhānta</s> — just as <s>niyoga</s> (injunction) is the sentence-meaning in the <s>Prābhākara</s> [school], or analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) is a <s>pramāṇa</s> in <s>Nyāya</s> — to this he says: 'the word <s>samāna</s> (similar) is a synonym.' Just as the words <s>taru</s> and <s>vṛkṣa</s> have the same meaning. Even so, a single [entity],

children.text:
samānaśabdavācyaṃ bhavatītyata āha---naiyāyikānāṃ hīti /
vyatirekapradhānaṃ
children.translated_text: in dependence on multiple relations, can be denoted by the word '<s>samāna</s>' — to this he says: 'for of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>...' This is primarily [a matter of]

children.text: caitat /
children.translated_text: exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>).

children.text: ekatra kutracit siddho na sarvatrasiddha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: what is established in one [system] somewhere is not established everywhere.

children.text: etāvatyeva lakṣaṇe siddhe paratantrāsiddhapadamimarthaṃ sphuṭayitum /
children.translated_text: [The purpose is] to elucidate precisely this meaning of the term 'not established in another system' (<s>paratantrāsiddha</s>), once just this much of the definition has been established.

children.text: anyathā sarvatantrasiddho 'pi samānatantrasiddha eveti bhramaḥ syāditi //29 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be the error that even what is established in all systems (<s>sarvatantrasiddha</s>) is merely established in a similar system — this is the meaning.

children.text: yatsiddhāvanyaprakaraṇasiddhiḥ so 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntaḥ //30 //
children.translated_text: That whose establishment [leads to] the establishment of another topic is the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> (topically established doctrine).

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: evaṃ vācanikasiddhāntadvayaṃ lakṣayitvā talliṅgatvādabhiprāyasyābhiprāyikasiddhāntadvayopakrame nyāyapradhānatvādasya śāstrasya nyāyānuṣaḍgiṇaṃ tāvadāha---yatsiddhāvityādi sūtram //30 //
children.translated_text: Having thus defined two types of verbal (<s>vācanika</s>) <s>siddhānta</s>, and since intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>) has these as its marks — in the introduction of the two types of intentional (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>) <s>siddhānta</s>, since this <s>śāstra</s> is primarily about <s>Nyāya</s>, he first states what is incidental to <s>Nyāya</s>: 'that whose establishment...' and so forth, the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text:
etacca bhūṣaṇaprabhṛtayo dvidhā vyācakṣate /
yasyārthasya sarvajñatvāderviśeṣasya siddhau kṣityādeḥ sakartṛkatvasya pratikriyamāṇasya siddhiḥ sa sarvajñatvādirviśeṣo 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntaḥ /
atha vā yasya sakartṛkatvādeḥ siddhāvantarbhūtā anye 'bhiprāyaprakāntāḥ sarvajñatvādayo 'pi viśeṣāḥ sidhyanti so 'dhikaraṇasiddhānta iti /
tadatra pakṣadvaye 'pi phalato na kaścid viśeṣa iti manvānaḥ śliṣṭaṃ bhāṣyaṃ vyācaṣṭe, sādhyasya vā hetārveti /
prathamapakṣe sādhyaviśeṣasya hetuviśeṣasya vetyarthaḥ /
dvitīye tu sugamam /
yatsiddhāvityatra nimittaviṣayabhāvapratibhāsanād vyākhyātṛvipratipatteśca saptamyarthe sandehaḥ, tamapākaroti---viṣayasaptamīti /
upapattimāha---dvayoriti /
idānīmekaṃ vyākhyānamupādāya sphuṭabhāṣyānusāreṇa tāvadāha---teneti /
nanu ca pakṣo vā heturvā kaṇṭhata eva niyatatantrābhyupagamāt pratitantrasiddhāntānna bhidyata ityata āha---anena rūpeṇeti /
yadyapi svarūpato 'sya vācanika evābhyupagamaḥ, tathāpyanene rūpeṇabhiprāyika evetyatastato bhidyata ityarthaḥ /
udāharati---pakṣastāvaditi /
nanu pratītameva kartṛmattvaṃ kṣityāderaparyavasyat sarvajñatvādiviśeṣamākṣipati /
tato na vyākhyātaviṣayasaptamyudāhaṇamidamityata āha---atreti /
nanvetadantarbhāvamantareṇa kimupalabdhimatpūrvakatvameva pratyetuṃ na śakyata ityata āha---nānyatheti /
na hi yathā tārṇapārṇatvādisaṃdehe 'pi vahniniścayasaṃbhavaḥ, tathā paramāṇvādyadṛṣṭāntābhijñānābhijñatvasaṃdehe tatprayoktṛtvaviniścayasaṃbhavaḥ, jñānacikīrṣaikaviṣayaprayatnavattvameva hi prayoktṛtvaṃ kartṛtvamiti vocyate /
tacca jñānaṃ dvyaṇukādyadṛṣṭaparyantapakṣīkaraṇe yadi sarvaviṣayaṃ na sidhyet, na sidhyedeveti /
tasmād yathā gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityatra tīralakṣaṇāmantareṇa gaṅgāpadārtho na ghoṣapadārthamanveti yathā sakartṛkapadārtho 'pi
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūṣaṇa</s> and others explain this in two ways. [First:] when a specific [feature] such as omniscience is established, the establishment of the property being proved — such as the having-a-maker of earth and the like — [follows]; that specific [feature] such as omniscience is the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s>. Alternatively: that whose establishment includes within it the establishment of other specific [features] such as omniscience and the like, which are matters of intention — that [doctrine] such as having-a-maker is the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s>. Considering that in both alternatives there is no difference in result, he explains the concise <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'of the <s>sādhya</s>, or of the reason...' In the first alternative, the meaning is: of the specific <s>sādhya</s>, or of the specific reason. In the second, it is straightforward. Since 'whose establishment' gives the appearance of a relation between occasion, object, and state — and since there is disagreement among commentators regarding the meaning of the locative — he removes the doubt: 'locative of object...' He states the justification: 'of both...' Now, taking up one interpretation, he states [the explanation] first in accordance with the clear <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'thereby...' Now, the thesis or the reason — being explicitly accepted by the particular system — does not differ from <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> (system-specific doctrine) — to this he says: 'in this form...' Although the acceptance of this is, in its intrinsic nature, merely verbal, nevertheless, in this form it is intentional alone — and therefore it differs from that — this is the meaning. He gives an example: 'the thesis, to begin with...' Now, the having-a-maker of earth and the like, being directly cognized, leads, without [further] termination, to the particular feature of omniscience and the like. Therefore, this is not an instance of the explained object-locative — to this he says: 'here...' Now, without this inclusion, can one not simply understand that [it has the property of] being preceded by something that possesses apprehension? — to this he says: 'not otherwise...' For just as even when there is doubt about whether [the fuel] is grass, leaves, and the like, certainty about fire is possible, it is not the case that when there is doubt about being or not being acquainted with examples such as atoms and the like, there can be certainty about being the producer of those — for what is called 'being a producer' or 'being a maker' is indeed having effort directed toward the single object of knowledge and desire-to-do. And that knowledge — if, in including atoms and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> and the like within its scope, it is not established as having all objects [in its scope] — then it simply would not be established. Therefore, just as in 'there is a village on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' the meaning of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' does not apply to the meaning of the word 'village' without the figurative usage of the bank — so too, the meaning of 'having-a-maker'

children.text: tatkāraṇaparamāṇvādyabhijñamanupasthāpya na kṣityādipadārthamanvetīti pratītyaparyavasānamevetyarthaḥ /
na caivaṃ kevalavyatirekividhvaṃsaḥ, abhiprāyāvyāptasya tadviṣayatvādityuktam, vakṣyate ceti /
children.translated_text: And thus, there is no destruction of the purely negative method [of reasoning] — since what is not pervaded by the intention is nonetheless its object — this has been stated, and will be stated [further].

children.text: tadevaṃ prathamaṃ vyākhyānaṃ bhāṣyānusāreṇa samarthya dvitīye vārttikaṃ sphuṭamityāha---tadetaditi /
children.translated_text: Having thus examined the first interpretation in accordance with the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, he says that the <s>Vārttika</s> is clear in the second [interpretation]: 'this very...'

children.text: sarvāvarodhārya sādhyānuṣaṅgihetvanuṣaṅgyavarodhārtham /
children.translated_text: 'Encompassing all' — for the purpose of encompassing the reason incidental to the <s>sādhya</s>, and [the entities] incidental [to it].

children.text: etadeva sphuṭayati---heturīdṛśa iti //30 //
children.translated_text: He clarifies this very point: 'the reason of such a form...'

does not apply to the meaning of earth and the like without presenting [the idea of being] acquainted with those causal atoms and the like — the meaning is that this is merely the terminus of understanding.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: vārttikakārīyābhyupagamasiddhāntodāharaṇe sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ yojayati---pramāṇādhikaraṇo yata iti /
children.translated_text: He applies the general definition to the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>'s example of <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (accepted doctrine): 'since it is the topic of <s>pramāṇa</s>...'

children.text: nanu bhāṣyamata eva sūtraṃ sphuṭārthamityata āha---sūtraṃ caivamiti /
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>sūtra</s> is clear in meaning precisely because of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — to this he says: 'and the <s>sūtra</s> thus...'

children.text: indriyatvenāsūtritasyāpi manasa indriyatvaṃ parīkṣitaṃ sūtrakamṛtā //
children.translated_text: Even though not formulated in the <s>sūtra</s> as a sense-faculty, the sense-faculty-nature of the mind has been examined by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>.

children.text: jñāturjñānasādhanopapatteḥ saṃjñābhedāmātram //
children.translated_text: Since the means of the knower's cognition is justified, it is merely a difference of terminology.

children.text: iti //
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text:
atra hi yathā rūpādijñānaviśeṣasādhanāni cakṣurādīnyupapadyante, tathā sukhādijñānasādhanaṃ mano 'pyupapadyate /
manaḥparihāre vā sarvendriyavilopaḥ prasajyata ityabhihite punaḥ sūtrakāreṇa rūpādijñānaṃ cakṣurādisādhanamasatu niḥsādhanameva tu sukhādijñānamityāśaṅkya sūtritam---
children.translated_text: For here, just as the eye and the like are established as the instruments for producing specific cognitions of form and the like, so too the mind is established as the instrument for producing the cognition of pleasure and the like. Or, if the mind were excluded, the consequence would be the loss of all sense-faculties — having stated this, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> again, suspecting that the cognition of form and the like has the eye and the like as its instrument, but the cognition of pleasure and the like has no instrument at all, formulated [the <s>sūtra</s>]:

children.text: niyamaśca niranumānaḥ
children.translated_text: 'And the restriction is without inference'

children.text:
iti /
tadidamasūtritasya viśeṣasya parīkṣaṇamabhyupagamādevopapadyate /
yadi hyanabhimata evāyamartho 'sya, kathaṃ parīkṣyaṃ vyavasthāpayedityarthaḥ /
idaṃ ca svābhimatonnayanaprakārāviṣkaraṇaṃ sūtrakṛtaḥ śiṣyahitatayetyato lakṣaṇārthamāha---so 'yamiti uktārthānuṣaṅgiṇaḥ arthasyābhyupagamo 'bhyupagamasiddhānta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this revealing of the manner of bringing out one's own accepted [doctrine] by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>, being for the benefit of the students — therefore he states it as the meaning of the definition: 'this is...' The meaning is: the acceptance of a meaning incidental to the stated meaning is <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (accepted doctrine).

children.text: nanu bhāṣyakārābhimatasyābhyupagamasiddhāntasya tallakṣaṇayoge kimayuktatvena?ayoge ca tadevocyatām /
children.translated_text: Now, if the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> intended by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> fits that definition, what is the problem? And if it does not fit, let that alone be stated.

children.text: tathāpi kimayuktatvenetyata āha---pramāṇatantreti /
children.translated_text: Even so, what is the problem? — to this he says: 'the <s>pramāṇa</s>-system...'

children.text: tamimaṃ vibhāgalakṣaṇaprapañcaṃ sarva evāyaṃ pakṣa iti pūrvapakṣavārttikavivaraṇavyājena saṃkalayyāha---sarvatantretyādi //31 //
children.translated_text: Compiling this entire elaboration of the classification and definition under 'this is all a preliminary view' — by way of explaining the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>-<s>vārttika</s>, he says: '<s>sarvatantra</s>...' and so forth.

— thus. This examination of a specific [doctrine] not [explicitly] formulated in the <s>sūtra</s> is tenable only from acceptance [of that doctrine]. For if this meaning were simply not intended by him, how could he establish what is to be examined? — this is the meaning.

children.text: // iti nyāyāśrayasiddhāntalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the definition of <s>siddhānta</s>, the basis of <s>Nyāya</s>.

children.text: // nyāyalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: The section on the definition of <s>Nyāya</s> (syllogism).

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: evaṃ ca yatra nyāyalakṣaṇaṃ karaṇamupaneyam, tatprakaraṇaṃ samarthya, upaneyanyāyaprakaraṇam ārabhyata iti sphuṭārthaṃ bhāṣyam---athāvayavā iti /
children.translated_text: And thus, having examined the topic where the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — namely the definition of <s>Nyāya</s> — is to be applied, the section on the <s>Nyāya</s> to be applied is commenced — the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is clear in meaning: 'now the components (<s>avayavas</s>)...'

children.text: ataḥ siddhavat sūtraṃ pratyāharati---prati---vāḥ //32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, he cites the <s>sūtra</s> as if established: '<s>prati</s>—<s>vāḥ</s>'...

children.text:
ekāvākyatā viśiṣṭaikārthadharūpakāryasaṃbandhaḥ /
viśiṣṭaścārtho 'tra prakṛtatvāt samastarūpopapannaṃ liṅgam /
saṃśayaḥ kathāsu vipratipattija eva /
sa cānuvidhayastheyagato, yathāyogaṃ vicāryavastugocarastajjñānagocaraśceti vicāramātre tu sārvahetukaḥ, svaparaniṣṭhaśca /
prayojanaṃ kathāsu pratītijayau /
anyatra prakṛtopayogino 'jñātasya jñānaṃ jñāpanaṃ ca /
jijñāsā kathāsu anuvidheyastheyānām /
anyatra svagatā śakyaprāptiḥ sarvatra padapadārthavākyapramāṇatadābhāsapāṭavam /
saṃśayavyudāsaṃ tu samyagityabhidhāyaikapakṣaparigrahaṃ kecit manyante /
sa cādau vipratipattyā paścāt pratijñayā gatārtha iti matvā tarkābhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe---yadi śabdo nityaḥ syāditi /
vyudasyate hi tena saṃśayaḥ phalataḥ svarūpataśca /
tadāha---pramāṇābhyanujñānadvāreṇeti /
saṃśayo hi dve koṭī parispṛśya vartamānāṃ jijñāsāmapi tathābhūtāmeva janayati /
nyāyastu śrotriyavadviruddhadharmasaṃkaramanicchan kulabadhūmiva ekakoṭiniyatāmeva jijñāsāmanurudhyate /
tadevaṃ tāvantarā vartamānastarka ekasyāṃ koṭau pramāṇabādhitaṃ kañcidarthamāharan tadgatāmicchāṃ vicchidya dvitīyakoṭau niyamayati /
seyaṃ jñeyecchā niyataikakoṭikā pramāṇābhyanujñetyucyate /
enāṃ ca janayatā tarkeṇa saṃśayaphalaṃ prabalecchā tadaiva vyudasyate /
taddvāreṇa pramāṇaṃ pravartayatā saṃśayasvarūpamapīti /
tadetannyāyapravṛtterutpatyaṅgapañcakamutpattimātreṇa, na tu jñāptimapekṣate /
ato naitasya jñāpakacintā kriyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, no consideration of a communicative mark (<s>jñāpaka</s>) is made for this.

children.text: utpatticintaivopayogitvāt tatra tatra kṛtā, kariṣyate ca /
children.translated_text: Only the consideration of arising is useful — and has been made here and there, and will be made [further].

children.text: pratijñādyarthāstu jñātā eva nyāyamupakurvantastatphalasiddhāvupayujyante /
children.translated_text: The meanings of the <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis) and the like, being already known, assist the method (<s>nyāya</s>) and are employed in the establishment of its result.

children.text: asteṣāṃ jñāpakacintā kriyata iti //32 //
children.translated_text: For these, the inquiry into their indicators is undertaken. // 32 //

Sentential unity (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) is the relation of being a product having a single qualified purpose. And the qualified purpose here, because it is the topic at hand, is the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) that is established in its complete form. Doubt, in [the context of] debates, arises only from disagreement. And that pertains to what is to be followed and what is to be upheld — and, as appropriate, concerns the matter under investigation and the cognition thereof — but in [the context of] mere investigation, it has all [kinds of] causes, and pertains to one's own and another's position. The purpose, in debates, is conviction and victory. Elsewhere, it is the cognition and communication of what is unknown and useful to the topic at hand. Inquiry (<s>jijñāsā</s>), in debates, pertains to what is to be followed and upheld. Elsewhere, it is the accessible attainment pertaining to oneself; in all cases, [it requires] skill in words, word-meanings, sentences, <s>pramāṇas</s> and their semblances. Some think that 'properly' refers to the removal of doubt through the adoption of one alternative. And since that is accomplished — first by disagreement, and later by the thesis — thinking that the meaning has been conveyed, he explains with the intention of <s>tarka</s> (suppositional reasoning): 'if sound were eternal...' For doubt is removed by that [<s>tarka</s>] both in terms of result and in terms of its own nature. He states this: 'through the avenue of <s>pramāṇa</s>-sanction...' For doubt, touching both alternatives, generates inquiry too of exactly that nature [i.e., touching both]. But <s>Nyāya</s>, like a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who does not wish for the mixing of contradictory properties, like a well-born bride, accommodates only inquiry that is fixed on one alternative. Thus, <s>tarka</s>, operating in the interim, bringing some matter contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s> in one alternative, cuts off the desire pertaining to it and fixes [the inquiry] on the second alternative. This desire-to-know, fixed on one alternative, is called '<s>pramāṇa</s>-sanctioned.' And by the <s>tarka</s> that generates it, the result of doubt — namely the strong desire — is removed at that very moment. Through that [removal], even the intrinsic nature of doubt is [removed] by the <s>pramāṇa</s> that is set in motion. This then is the pentad of generative components of the operation of <s>Nyāya</s> — [it is needed] merely for the arising [of <s>Nyāya</s>], and does not require communication.

children.text: // pariśuddhi //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: parigṛhyate 'neneti svīkriyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That by which something is accepted (<s>parigṛhyate</s>)' means 'that by which it is embraced' — this is the meaning.

children.text: tena sādhyatayā svīkriyamānasyārthasya vacanaṃ pratijñeti sūtrārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: the statement of the object being embraced as what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) is the <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis).

children.text: apohya bhedaḥ siddhānto jijñāsā sādhanārhatā /
children.translated_text: Exclusion, distinction, <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), the desire to know, fitness for being proved,

children.text: karmadharmaśca lokaśca prastāvaśca niyāmakāḥ //
children.translated_text: the topic of action, common usage, and the occasion — these are the determinants.

children.text:
iti atiprasaṅgāsamādhivārtikasya prapañcasaṃkṣepaḥ /
na hi vyaṅgyamityādi /
yathā ca neyaṃ bhrāntiḥ tathā dvitīye nivedayiṣyate /
tadāloketi, candraśabdo 'yaṃ śaśivācakaḥ prayojyavṛddhaṃ prati asati vṛttyantare tatpratyayajanakatvāt /
tatpratyayajanakaścāyaṃ svapratyayena tadgocaravyavahārahetutvāditi /
hetudoṣo 'siddhatvādireveti /
asiddhatvādyarthatvamityarthaḥ /
evamuttaratra yastu naivaṃvidho na vācyo na lakṣya ityarthaḥ /
nanu tathāpi vācyavallakṣayo 'pi
children.translated_text: Thus is the summary of the elaboration of the <s>vārttika</s> on undue extension and lack of resolution. 'Not indeed the suggested meaning...' and so on. And how this is not an error will be explained in the second [section]. 'That illumination' — this word <s>candra</s> (moon) denotes the hare-marked one; with respect to the instructed elder, in the absence of another semantic function, it generates the cognition of that [referent]. And this, generating the cognition of that [referent], is the cause of practical usage regarding that object through its own cognition — thus [the argument goes]. The fault of the reason is precisely non-establishment and the like — this is the meaning. The meaning is: it has the sense of non-establishment and the like. Similarly, in what follows, 'but one who is not of such a kind is neither the denotable nor the indicated' — this is the meaning. Now, even so, to show that the indicated meaning, like the denotable, is

children.text: pakṣa eveti darśayitumiṣṭagrahaṇaṃ bhaviṣyatītyata āha---na ca kvacidapīti /
bhavedevaṃ yadi vidhādvayaṃ syāt, na tvetadastītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It would be so if there were a twofold injunction, but that does not exist — this is the meaning.

children.text: etaccānvitābhidhānanirākaraṇena draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: And this should be seen in the light of the refutation of the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (related denotation) [theory].

children.text: na tvaśakyatvāsadācāratve avadhīrya śāstrānapekṣamabhyupagacchanto dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: But those who, having disregarded the impossibility and improper conduct, accept [a position] independently of the <s>śāstra</s>, are not observed.

children.text: na ca sāmānyalakṣaṇāyogaḥ //
children.translated_text: Nor is there an inapplicability of the general definition.
itself the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), the qualification 'desired' (<s>iṣṭa</s>) will be employed — anticipating this, he says: 'Not even anywhere...'

children.text: tantrādhikaraṇābhyupagamasaṃsthitiḥ
children.translated_text: The establishment through acceptance of the topic of the treatise (<s>tantrādhikaraṇa</s>)

children.text:
ityasya kathādhikaraṇābhyupagamasaṃsthitirityevamapyavirodhāt /
tasmād yathābhāṣyameva jyāya ityata āha---yastāvaditi /
etena vārttikakārīyo 'bhyupagamasiddhāntastāvaducita iti darśayatā chalataḥ pañcamasiddhāntāpattirdaśitā /
na hyayameteṣvantarbhavatīti satīrthyānām /
parān prati tu doṣamāha---yastviti /
yadi hi pramāṇīkṛtaśāstraviruddho 'pyartho 'bhyupagamyamānaḥ siddhāntatāmupayāyāt, na vādino kadācidapyapasiddhāntena nigraho bhavet /
yatra yatra pramādike 'pyarthe śāstravirodhaścodyeta tatra tatrābhyupagamasiddhānto 'yaṃ mametyevamapi nistārāt parāvṛttya ca tenaiva niranuyojyānuyogena nigrahe kathāsamāptau tadvyutpādanaprayāsasyāpyabhāvāt /
na caivamastviti vācyam /
śāstraprāmāṇyābhyupagamatadviruddhārthābhyupagamayorvirodhasya durvāratvāt /
śāstraprāmāṇyābhyupagame tadasamānārthasya svavacanasya
children.translated_text: — since there is no contradiction even with the reading 'establishment through acceptance of the topic of the discourse (<s>kathādhikaraṇa</s>).' Therefore, since the <s>bhāṣya</s> reading itself is preferable, he says: 'Now, that which...' By this, showing that the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>'s acceptance-based <s>siddhānta</s> is indeed appropriate, he has indicated the incurrence of a fifth <s>siddhānta</s> from sophistical reasoning (<s>chala</s>). 'For this does not fall within these' — this is from the standpoint of co-doctrinalists. Against opponents, however, he states the fault: 'But that which...' For if an object contradicting an accepted <s>śāstra</s> were to attain the status of <s>siddhānta</s> merely through being accepted, then a debater would never be defeated by a counter-doctrine. Wherever, even in a carelessly [held] position, a contradiction with <s>śāstra</s> is objected, there one could escape by saying 'this is my acceptance-based <s>siddhānta</s>,' and having turned back with that very reproach of an unreproachable [position], at the conclusion of the debate even the effort of instruction would be absent. Nor should one say 'let it be so,' because the contradiction between accepting the authority of <s>śāstra</s> and accepting an object contradicting it is irresolvable. When the authority of <s>śāstra</s> is accepted, one's own statement having a different meaning [from the <s>śāstra</s>]

children.text: prāmāṇyābhyupagamavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: contradicts the acceptance of [its] authority.

children.text: tadanuguṇasya prāmāṇyābhyupagame tadvyāhatābhidhāyinaḥ punarapasiddhāntāpātāt /
children.translated_text: If one accepts the authority of what conforms to it, then the statement of what contradicts it again incurs a counter-doctrine.

children.text: tasmāt na hi śāstrāśrayā vādā bhavantīti svapnavilāpaḥ ityarthaḥ //33 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'debates do not indeed rest on <s>śāstra</s>' is mere sleep-babbling — this is the meaning. // 33 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
iha pratijñārthaḥ sarvathaiva kathāsu nopayujyate, arthopalabdhyā yukto 'pyanyathaiva labdhaḥ? ādye vipratipattimapi na vibhāvayet /
avibhāvayaṃśca tāṃ kathamiva prativadet? aprativadataśca vacanaṃ kathaṃ kathāśarīratāmiyāt? tathā ca kathakaḥ kathaṃ nigṛhyeta, nigṛhnīyād veti na saṃpratītirnaca vijayo gardabhīkṣīramathanavadanarthakaḥ prayāsaḥ /
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, sa hi vivādād vā avayavāntarād vā? vivādādapi vyavahitād vā, avayavāntaraikavākyatāpannād vā? avayavāntarādapi sākṣād vā, ākṣepato veti? na tāvadādyaḥ, āsatteḥ abhāvādekavākyatvānāpatteḥ /
āpattau vā āntarālikāsādhanāṅgavacanena nigṛhyeta /
anigrahe vā paraḥ paryanuyojyopekṣaṇamāsādayet /
dvitīye tvavivāda eva /
vayamapi hi parābhyupetapakṣaviparītāṃ koṭimupanīya tatsiddhaye 'vayavāntaramabhidadhyāditi brūmaḥ /
na hyevaṃbhūtakoṭyupadarśanavyatirekeṇa pratijñāyāḥ śṛṅgamasti /
nāpi tṛtīyaḥ, na hi hetvādibhiḥ caturbhiḥ pratijñārtho 'bhidhīyata iti vakṣyāmaḥ /
nāpi caturthaḥ, sa hyapekṣākāle vā, anyadā veti /
tatra prathamamurarīkatyāha---tathāhīti /
yad bubhutsante yadeti śeṣaḥ /
pratipannavivādaviṣayā hi tannirṇayaheluṃ
children.translated_text: Here, is the thesis-object not employed in debates at all, even when its apprehension is proper but [the object] is apprehended otherwise? In the first case, one would not even discern the disagreement. And without discerning it, how could one respond to it? And without responding, how could the statement become the body of the debate? And in that case, how would the debater be defeated or defeat [the other]? — there would be no proper understanding, nor would there be victory; the effort would be pointless, like churning donkey's milk. Nor is it the second [alternative], for is that [apprehension] from the dispute or from another component of the syllogism? If from the dispute, is it from a remote [dispute] or from one that has entered into a single sentence with another component? If from another component, is it directly or by implication? Not the first, because of the absence of proximity and the consequent non-attainment of single-sentence unity. Or if it were attained, one would be defeated by the intervening statement of a non-proving component. Or without defeat, the opponent would incur the fault of neglecting a reproachable [party]. In the second case, there would simply be no dispute. For we too say that having presented the alternative contrary to the opponent's accepted thesis, one would state another component to establish that. For there is no horn of the thesis beyond the presentation of such an alternative. Nor is it the third, for we shall say that the thesis-object is not stated by the four — reason and the like. Nor is it the fourth, for that would be either at the time of expectation or at another time. There, accepting the first, he says: 'For thus...' 'What they wish to know' — supply 'what.' For having undertaken the subject of the established dispute, we wish to know the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) that is the reason for its determination.

children.text:
sādhanamanububhutsāmahe /
na tu tannirṇayahetubhūtasādhanāvabodhavanato vivādaviṣayaṃ nirṇayasya nirṇeyarūpamantareṇa nirūpayitumaśakyatvāt /
tadanirūpaṇe tatsādhanasyāpi tathātvenāśakyanirūpaṇatvāt /
anirūpitasya caiṣitumaśakyatvāt /
tathā ca tasyaiva prathamābhidhāne prāpte 'nyasyābhidhānānavakāśāt ākṣepasyāpi kuto 'vakāśa iti? nanvapekṣitānabhidhāne 'pyapekṣitaṃ kurvāṇaḥ kathamavavadheyavacano nāmetyata āha---yathā ceti /
yatrāpekṣitamanyathāpi śakyasaṃpādanam, tatrāpi tadanabhidhāne viparītabuddhiḥ kimaṅgaḥ yatra vacanenaivāpekṣitasiddhirityarthaḥ anyadeti pakṣamupasthāpayati /
yat kṛtakamityādi /
dūṣayanti---na parasparāśrayaprasaṅgāditi /
yo hi yena yat sādhayitum udyataḥ sa tatsāmagrīmapratikūlayanneva tathā kartumarhati /
yathākālamapekṣitāmidhānaṃ ca vākyasāmagrī, tadanādare tūdāharaṇīyodāharaṇakramaniyamamapi nādriyeta, pratipādyāpekṣāniyamānurodhena tatra tatheti cet? tadihāpi samānam /
tathā ca tatkālātikrameṇākṣepo 'pi nopayogī, śiromuṇḍanāntaraṃ nakṣatraparīkṣāvat /
upayogo vā parasparāśrayaprasaṅgaḥ ayakṣārādhanasādhyadhanena yakṣārādhanavadityarthaḥ /
katha tarhi,
children.translated_text: But we do not [wish to know the dispute-subject itself separately], since the determination of the dispute-subject cannot be ascertained without the object to be determined, because the determination-reason is the means of proof. When that is not ascertained, the means of proof for it also cannot be ascertained as such. And what is not ascertained cannot be desired. And thus, since that very [thesis-object] should be stated first, there being no scope for stating anything else, whence even the scope for implication? — Now, even without stating what is expected, how can one who performs the expected be said to have a dismissible statement? — to this he says: 'Just as...' Even where the expected can be accomplished otherwise, there too, if it is not stated, the wrong understanding [arises] — how much more so where the establishment of the expected is only through statement — this is the meaning. 'Otherwise' — he presents the alternative. 'What is produced' and so on. They refute: 'Because of the fallacy of mutual dependence.' For one who undertakes to prove something by some [means] should do so without obstructing the apparatus of that [proof]. And the statement of what is expected at the proper time is the sentence-apparatus; if that is disregarded, one would not respect even the rule of the order of the illustrandum and illustration, and because of conformity to the rule of the expectation of what is to be established, 'there, thus' — if so, the same applies here. And thus even implication through transgression of that time is not useful, like examining the lunar mansion after shaving the head. Or [if it is] useful, then the fallacy of mutual dependence [arises] — like accomplishing the worship of a <s>Yakṣa</s> with wealth obtainable only through worshipping the <s>Yakṣa</s> — this is the meaning. How then,

children.text: mantrāyurvedaprāmāṇyavacca tatprāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: just as the authority of <s>mantra</s> and <s>Āyurveda</s>, so too is that authority?

children.text:
ityādau pratijñāmanabhidhāyaiva udāharaṇādyupādānamityata āha---na ceti /
tathāpi hetvabhidhānena kiṃ tatsvarūpasyopanayenaiva sākṣādabhidhānādityata āha---anityaḥ śabda iti tvapekṣita ukta iti /
tatrāpyākāṅkṣaiva vijayate /
na hyanityaḥ śabda ityukte kṛtakatvānityatvavyāptau vā kṛtakatvasya vā śabdadharmisaṃbandhe śroturākāṅkṣā kiṃ nāma kuta etatpratipattavyamiti syāt /
iyaṃ cāpekṣāsādhanatvābhivyañjakavibhaktyantebhyaḥ kṛtakatvādityādipadebhya eva nivartata ityarthaḥ /
ata eva gamakatvādetasya mārgasya sarvaśāstrakārā evamevopādadate /
saugato 'pi hi
children.translated_text: In such cases where illustration and the like are adopted without stating the thesis — to this he says: 'Not so...' Even so, what is the purpose of stating the reason, since the essential nature of that [thesis] is directly stated through the application (<s>upanaya</s>) alone? — to this he says: 'The statement "sound is non-eternal" is the expected [thesis] that has been stated.' Even there, expectation alone prevails. For when 'sound is non-eternal' is stated, would the hearer's expectation regarding the pervasion between being produced and non-eternality, or regarding the connection of the property of being produced with the subject 'sound,' [not arise as] 'from what is this to be understood'? And this expectation is resolved by the very words such as 'because of being produced' with case-endings that express the capacity for proving — this is the meaning. And precisely because of its indicative power, all treatise-authors adopt this very method. For even the <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist)

children.text: mānu tu dvividhaṃ meyadvaividhyāt //
children.translated_text: 'But cognition (<s>māna</s>) is twofold, because of the twofold nature of the knowable (<s>meya</s>)'

children.text: asanto 'kṣaṇikāḥ tasyāṃ kramākramavirodhataḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Non-existents and non-momentary things are [excluded] from it, because of the contradiction of sequence and simultaneity'

children.text: iti pratyakṣaraṃ pratijñāhetū upādāya vyavaharati /
kathāyāṃ tu paravañcanārthaṃ tāvupekṣate /
children.translated_text: But in debate, he neglects those [formal components] for the purpose of deceiving the opponent.

children.text: śāstraṃ tadviti cet /
children.translated_text: If [one objects]: the <s>śāstra</s> is that [i.e., the debate format] —

children.text: atha śāstre kimanarthakamabhidhīyate? tatrāsti vā pratijñādeḥ kiñcit prayojanamiti? ādye, sādhu paravyutpādakatvamasya nirarthakaṃ pralapataḥ /
children.translated_text: then what is stated purposelessly in the <s>śāstra</s>? Is there or is there not some purpose for the thesis and the like therein? In the first case, well done — the capacity to instruct others is pointless babbling.

children.text: dvitīye tu śabdoccāraṇasya nārthagaterapyadhikaṃ prayojanaṃ nāma, prathamopakrame vivaraṇaśaṅkāyā apyabhāvāditi //
children.translated_text: In the second case, however, the utterance of words has no purpose beyond the conveyance of meaning, since at the very outset there is not even the apprehension of the need for elaboration.
— thus, word by word, he adopts the thesis and reason and operates [with them].

children.text:
nanu sāmānyalakṣaṇamantareṇa na viśeṣalakṣaṇāvasara ityata āha---śrutyarthābhyāmiti /
sādhyate niścīyate 'neneti /
natvevaṃ sati liṅgamuktaṃ syāt /
tathā ca kathaṃ vākyāvayava ityata āha---yadyapīti /
nanvalamupalakṣaṇena yāvatā vacanameva sādhanamastu, sādhyate pratipādyate tenāpi hi svārtha ityata āha---yadi tviti /
evaṃ hi sādhyasādhanaṃ sādhyapratipādakaṃ vacanamityarthaḥ /
tathā ca pratijñaiva hetuḥ syāt /
atha sādhyapadaṃ vihāya sādhanaṃ pratipādakaṃ vacanamityarthaḥ, tatrāha---atheti /
tadetadarthāntarāvivakṣāyāṃ dūṣaṇamuktam /
yadi tvevaṃ kriyeya liṅgapratipādanadvāreṇa sādhyasādhanaṃ niścāyakaṃ vacanamiti /
tadā aśrutādhyāhāraḥ /
udāharaṇasādharmyāditisahitasya tvavyāptiralābho vā sāmānyalakṣaṇasyeti draṣṭavyam /
evaṃ ca vyākhyāne
children.translated_text: Now, without the general definition there is no occasion for the specific definition — to this he says: 'By <s>śruti</s> (scripture) and meaning...' 'That by which something is proved, i.e. ascertained.' But if so, the reason (<s>liṅga</s>) would have been stated [already]. And then how is it a component of the sentence? — to this he says: 'Although...' Now, enough with the indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>); let the statement itself be the means of proof, since even by that, the intended meaning is established — to this he says: 'But if...' For thus, the 'means-of-proving-the-provable' would mean 'the statement that communicates the provable' — this is the meaning. And then the thesis itself would be the reason. Now, if setting aside the word <s>sādhya</s> (provable), 'means of proof' means 'the statement that communicates' — to that he says: 'Now...' This very refutation has been stated when there is no intention of a different meaning. But if it were done thus: 'the statement that ascertains the means-of-proving-the-provable through the communication of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>)' — then there is the importation of what is not heard. But with the combined reading including 'from the similarity of the illustration,' there should be seen either non-pervasion or the failure to obtain the general definition. And in this interpretation,

children.text:
vacanapadamasūtrasthameva ṭīkākṛtā svayamupanīyavirodhātivyāptī kutaḥ śaṅkite iti śaṅkā nivartate /
nanu tathāpyupanaye prasaṅga ityata āha---upanayādapīti /
sādhyasādhanavacanamityatra hi sādhanatvaviśiṣṭārthavacanam ityartho gamyate /
na copanayaḥ /
koṣṭhagatyā tathābhūtārthagocaro 'pi tathābhūtamabhidhatte, sādhanatvābhivyañjakavibhaktiviśeṣaśūnyatvāt /
ata eva kuta ityākāṅkṣā /
tathācāyaṃ kṛtaka ityasmānna nivartate, api tu kṛtakatvādityasmādeva /
tarhi kiṃbhūtamupanayāt pratīyata ityata āha---kiṃ tviti /
svaniṣṭhaṃ sādhanatvādidharmarahitam /
kutaḥ? prātipadikārthapradhānatayā /
tatparatayā tāvanmātrābhidhāyakavibhaktimataḥ prayuktatvāditi śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because it is employed with a case-ending that expresses only that much, with reference to that [nominal stem meaning] — this is the remainder.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati, na hi hetuvadupanayo 'pi kuta ityākāṅkṣāyā pravartate, api tūdāharaṇena vyāptau pradarśitāyām /
children.translated_text: What has been said amounts to this: neither does the application, like the reason, proceed from the expectation 'from what?', but rather [it proceeds] when the pervasion has been demonstrated by the illustration.

children.text: bhavatu tāvadetat, tathāpi prakṛto vivādaviṣayaḥ kiṃ vyāptadharmaviśiṣṭo na vetyapekṣāyāṃ sā ca tathā cāyaṃ kṛtaka ityanenaiva paraṃ nivartyate, na tu kṛtakatvādityanena /
children.translated_text: Granted that this is so; nevertheless, when the question arises whether the subject under discussion is qualified by the pervaded property or not, that [expectation] is resolved precisely by 'and this is produced,' not by 'because of being produced.'

children.text: tasmānna hetūpanayayorarthato rūpataḥ prayojanato vā saṃkara ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no conflation of reason and application in meaning, form, or purpose — this is the meaning.

the doubt is resolved that the commentator, having himself introduced the word 'statement' which is not in the <s>sūtra</s>, whence are the objections of contradiction and over-extension raised? Now, even so, there is the problem regarding the application (<s>upanaya</s>) — to this he says: 'From the application too...' For in 'the statement of the provable and the means of proof,' the meaning understood is 'the statement of the object qualified by the property of being a means of proof.' But the application is not [such]. By way of order, even though it pertains to an object of such a nature, it states [it] as such [only incidentally], because of the absence of the specific case-ending that expresses the property of being a means of proof. For that very reason, the expectation 'from what?' does not cease from 'and this is produced,' but rather ceases from 'because of being produced' alone. Then what kind of thing is understood from the application? — to this he says: 'But rather...' What rests in itself, devoid of properties such as the property of being a means of proof. Why? Because of the predominance of the nominal stem meaning.

children.text:
nanu ca vacanalakṣaṇāyāṃ yadyapi jñāner'the vā na prasaṅgaḥ, tathāpi sādhyasādhanamiti kṛtakatvamatra heturityādau vacana eva prasaṅgaḥ /
etasyāpi tathābhūtārthapratipādakatvādityata āha---nyāyavākyeti /
anenākāṅkṣaupayikatā
children.translated_text: Now, even though in the definition by 'statement' there is no problem regarding cognition or object, nevertheless there is a problem regarding the very statement in such [formulations] as 'the means-of-proving-the-provable' and 'producedness is the reason here' — since these too communicate an object of that nature — to this he says: 'The <s>Nyāya</s>-sentence...' By this, the suitability for [resolving] expectation

children.text:
darśitā /
na ca kuta ityākāṅkṣāyāṃ sādhyasādhanamiti vā kṛtakatvaṃ heturiti vā vacanamaupayikam /
ato naivaṃbhūteṣu prasaṃga ityarthaḥ /
tena viśeṣaparatvena heturiti lakṣyanirdeśo nānupapanna iti śeṣaḥ /
viśiṣṭavidhānasyeti /
na kvacit pradeśo sādharmyaṃ hetulakṣaṇatvena vihitam, yeneha saviśeṣaṇatayā viśeṣaṇamātropasaṃkrānto vidhiḥ syāt /
nāpyatra viśeṣaṇaśūnyasyaiva sādharmyasyopādānam yena tāvanmātragocaro vidhirbhavet, parasparasvatantrobhayarthatve vākyabhedācca /
tasmāt ananyagatikatayā lohitoṣṇīṣavad viśiṣṭavidhirevāyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just like [the rule regarding] one wearing a red turban, this is precisely a qualified injunction.

children.text: tathā ca alohitoṣṇīṣavadanudāharaṇasādharmyasyārthasiddhaḥ pratiṣedha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, just as [the exclusion of] one not wearing a red turban, the negation of the dissimilar illustration is established by the force of the matter itself — this is the meaning.

children.text: pakṣāntaramāheti /
children.translated_text: He states an alternative thesis —

children.text: abhyupagamasyāpyaviśiṣṭasādharmyamātravidhone 'pi na doṣa iti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even in the case of what is accepted [by the opponent], no fault obtains when there is merely the production of an undistinguished similarity — this is the purport.

has been shown. And in the expectation 'from what?', neither the statement 'the means-of-proving-the-provable' nor the statement 'producedness is the reason' is suitable. Therefore there is no problem in such [cases] — this is the meaning. Thus, the specification of the definiendum as 'reason' (<s>hetu</s>) with a particular purport is not inappropriate — this is the remainder. 'Of the qualified injunction' — nowhere is a passage prescribed as having similarity as the definition of reason, such that here, with the qualification, the injunction would have migrated to the qualification alone. Nor is similarity without qualification adopted here, such that the injunction would pertain to just that much; and because of sentence-splitting in the case of both being independently intended.

children.text:
nanu yadyaviśiṣṭavidhānenaiva prakṛtasiddhiḥ, kimudāharaṇagrahaṇena? na cet kimaviśiṣṭavidhānenetyata āha---sādharmyādityata iti /
parisaṃkhyā atiprasaktinivartanamapākariṣyati /
tadudāharaṇapradarśanena parisaṃkhyāyakaṃ hetvābhāsalakṣaṇam /
parisaṃkhyā parivarjanabuddhiḥ /
viśeṣato jñātānāṃ teṣā svavākye parivarjanādimukhena bhavatvityetadarthamarthalabdhamapi kaṇṭhoktyābhidhīyate /
tallakṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
na vidhāyakaṃ na sarvathaivālabdhavidhāyakamityarthaḥ /
sugamo dignāgabhaṅgaḥ /
hetāvudāhartavye pratijñoktiḥ kimarthamityata āha---atreti /
udāhṛte hetau lakṣaṇaṃ yojayituṃ hetvarthe ca vivecayitavye prasaṅgāt pratijñārthaṃ vivecayitumiti bhāvaḥ /
tathāpi pradhvaṃsasya nānātvāt jātyāderupasaṃgrāhakasya vā bhāvāt kathaṃ vyāptyādisiddhiḥ? upalakṣyābhedamātreṇa ca tatsiddhau kuṇḍalavatā devadattena sādhyo vyavahāro daṇḍavatāpi sādhyetetyata āha---virodhīti /
yathā hyabhāvamātrasya bhāvapratiyogitayaivaupādhikasāmānyasaṃbandhādekavyavahārahetutvaṃ tathā tadviśeṣasyāpi pūrvāparetarerāśrayāntarabhāvapratiyogitayā tattadvyavahārāvirodha ityarthaḥ /
na caivaṃ labdhotpattinīti /
sarvatra hi dhātvarthoparaktā bhāvanā ākhyātārthaḥ /
bhāvanā ca kārakavyāpāraḥ /
utpadyate ghaṭa ityatra tu ghaṭo na kārakamasattvāt /
tataśca akārakasyaiva kārakairatyantasannidhestathopacāro vā kārakāṇāmeva kāryaśabdopacāro vā /
ubhayathāpi vyāpārāveśasamaya evākhyātaprayogo na tu dhātvarthamātrāveśasamaye /
children.translated_text: in both cases, the <s>ākhyāta</s> (verbal form) is employed precisely at the time of the infusion of the operation, not at the time of merely taking up the verbal meaning.

children.text: na hi pakve dhātvarthamātramupādāya pacyata iti prayujyate lokaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For when [food] is cooked, people do not employ [the form] "it is being cooked" by taking up the mere verbal meaning.

children.text: tat kasya hetoḥ? vyāpārāveśābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because there is no infusion of operation [at that point].

children.text: tathehāpīti //34 //
children.translated_text: So too here.

Now, if the accomplishment of the topic at hand is achieved by the undistinguished production alone, what is the need for the statement of an example? And if not, what is the need for the undistinguished production? — therefore

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
nanu na sapakṣatābhāvo 'tra sūtre śrūyate, nāpyārtho 'vadhāraṇasya ca vyāptyā /
