pakṣe sattvenopapatteraikāntikaṃ sapakṣe sattvaṃ mā prasāṃkṣīt /
pākṣikaṃ tu prasaktameva /
tathā ca kevalavyatirekilābhe 'pi nānvayavyatirekī nirākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the absence of the co-present instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is not heard in this <s>sūtra</s>, nor is it the meaning [established] through the pervasion of restriction. Because of the establishment by mere existence in the thesis —

children.text:
evaṃ sapakṣābhāve 'pi pakṣavyāpakasya vipakṣaikadeśavṛttestadavasthaiva prasaktirityāha---tathāpīti /
udāharaṇenaivetyavadhāraṇasya pakṣavyāptiparasya sapakṣābhāvapradarśanaudāsīnyamāviṣkartumanityo mūrtatvādityudāhṛtam /
vastutastu, nedaṃ nirātmakaṃ jīvacchīrīraṃ māṃsādimayatvāt ityasaṃkīrṇamudāharaṇaṃ draṣṭavyam /
etaddvayamapi nirākarta vaidharmyameva codāharaṇeneti pūrvāvadhāraṇena pakṣavyāptau labdhāyāṃ vaidharmyamevetyanena sādharmyarūpatā nirākṛtāvayamarthaḥ syāt /
pakṣasya vyāpako dharmastaditaravaidharmyarūpa eveti tathā cebhayorapi kaḥ prasaṃgaḥ? kevalamasādhāraṇaḥ prasajyate /
sa ca vipakṣodāharaṇeneti viśeṣayatā sapakṣābhāvapradarśanena nirastaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [over-extension] is removed by the specification through the counter-example, [which serves as] the display of the absence of the co-present instance.

children.text: yadi hi sati sapakṣe anvayo vivakṣitaḥ tadā tathā vaidharmyādityanārabhyameva, pūrvalakṣaṇenaiva gatārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: For if the positive concomitance were intended when the co-present instance exists, then the [<s>sūtra</s>] beginning with "by dissimilarity" need not have been commenced at all, since it would have been already obtained by the previous definition.

children.text: vyatirekaśced vivakṣito vipakṣeṇeti vyartham /
children.translated_text: If the negative concomitance is intended — then [the word] "by the counter-example" is purposeless.

children.text: tasmād vaidharmyāvadhitayā upāttaṃ vipakṣapadaṃ sapakṣābhāvapratipattiphalamevetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the word "counter-example" is taken as delimited by [the expression] "by dissimilarity" — the meaning being that its fruit is precisely the apprehension of the absence of a co-present instance.
even in the absence of a co-present instance, the over-extension remains the same, since what pervades the thesis may occur in part of the counter-example — therefore he says: "Even so..."

children.text:
nanu tathāpi vaidharmyādityatra tathāśabdārtha udāharaṇeneti /
udāharaṇaṃ ca sapakṣo 'pi bhavatīti kathaṃ viśeṣalābha ityāśaṅkya vyācaṣṭe---vipakṣeti /
vyākhyānato viśeṣapratipattirna hi sandehādalakṣaṇamiti bhāva iti tatra tatroktamityarthaḥ /
nanvavadhāritakāryasvabhāvor'thaḥ kevalavyatirekisādhyo 'nyathātiprasaṅgāditi vakṣyati, tathābhūtaścātra prāṇādyapekṣayā prayatnaḥ /
tasmiśca sādhye sidvāsādhanaṃ vyatirekyasaṃbhavaśca svaśarīre prāṇasya prayatnapūrvakatvāvadhāraṇena svapakṣānvayasyāpi saṃbhavādityata āha---prāṇādineti /
tathāpyasmadāyatte śabdaprayoge kiścityavācakaṃ prayokṣyāmaha ityata āha---prāṇādikāraṇecchādikāraṇarahitamiti /
paraśarīre pakṣapraviṣṭe hetusiddhyarthaṃ vipakṣībhūte ca ghaṭādau sādhyarahite hetuvyatirekasiddhyarthaṃ tathoktamityarthaḥ /
nanvicchādisamavāyikāraṇavirahaniṣedhena tadvatvaṃ sidhyet /
tathā ca punarapi nātmasiddhiḥ /
na ca kevalavyatirekī tāvanmātrasyānvayenaiva siddherityata āha---yaśceti /
anvayinā hi tatkāraṇamātraṃ siddham, anena tu tadeva pṛthivyādivilakṣaṇaṃ sidhyatīti na niravakāśo vyatirekī /
na ca nātmasiddhiḥ tathābhūtasya tasyaivātmaśabdavācyatvādityarthaḥ /
gṛhītāvinābhāvo hītyādīnā vyāptyasiddhirdarśitā /
children.translated_text: Now, even so, in "by dissimilarity," the meaning of the word "thus" is "by the example." And the example can be a co-present instance too — how then [is the absence of a co-present instance established]?

children.text: pakṣadharmatāsiddhirapyanayaiva diśohanīyā /
children.translated_text: The establishment of the property-of-the-thesis too should be directed through this very approach.

children.text: jijñāsitadharmaviśiṣṭasya pakṣatvāt, sandigdhasya ca jijñāsyatvāt viśeṣasmaraṇe ca saṃśayāt, anupalabdhacare ca tadabhāvāditi //
children.translated_text: Because that which has the desired property qualifies as the thesis, and because what is doubtful qualifies as what is to be desired, and because there is doubt when the specific [property] is recalled, and because non-apprehension —

children.text:
dvidhā hi prakṛtavyatirekigatiḥ, kāryaṃ kāryavattā ca /
tatra kāryamanumānalakṣaṇe darśitam /
tad yathā, icchādayo dravyāṣṭakātiriktadravyāśritāḥ, tadanāśritatve sati kāryatvāditi /
iha tu kāryavattā darśitā nedaṃ nirātmakaṃ jīvaccharīraṃ necchādisamavāyikāraṇībhūtadravyaviśeṣarahitamityarthaḥ /
icchādimattvāt icchadirūpakāryavattvādityarthaḥ /
tadetadubhayamatraivāntarbhāvya vyutpādayan prathamatastāvat kāryaṃ pradhānīkṛtyāha---ayamarthaiti /
icchādikāryāḥ santastān gamayanti /
te 'pyanityatayā kāryā iti śeṣaḥ /
kiṃ cāta ityāha---akṣaṇikatva iti /
hetorviśeṣaṇāsiddhiṃ nirākaroti---śarīrendriyeti /
na śarīrendriyamanaḥsvanyatamasminnete samavayanti, mānasaikapratyakṣatvāditi niṣedhe satītyarthaḥ /
niścodyaścaiṣa kevalavyātirekī /
children.translated_text: is a purely negative inference — this too is to be examined.

children.text: evaṃ prathamamupapādya tadīyāprasiddhaviśaṣaṇatvasaṃśayānupapattī sādhāraṇanyāyena nirākurvanneva dvitīyamupapādayati---tadasyeti /
children.translated_text: Having first established [this], while removing the [objections regarding] the unestablished qualifier and the impossibility of doubt of that [purely negative inference] through the general principle, [he proceeds to] the second —

children.text: etacca tatraiva sphuṭīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: and this was clarified in that very [context].

children.text: nanu yadi nāma sāmānyata icchādisamavāyikāraṇamātravyāvṛttirghaṭādau pratipannā kimāyātaṃ nairātmyasyetyata āha---nirātmakaśabdenāpīti //
children.translated_text: Now, if the exclusion from merely the inherence-cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of desire and the like has been generally apprehended in pots and the like, what [additional bearing] does the doctrine of non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>) have?
for the progress of the negative inference under discussion is twofold: the effect and effect-possessing-ness. Among these, the effect was shown in the definition of inference. That which

children.text:
evamarthagati pariśodhya vārttikaṃ yojayitvā dvatīyaṃ pradhānīkṛtyāha---etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
śaṅkate---na
children.translated_text: Having thus refined the understanding of the meaning and construed the <s>vārttika</s>, making the second [point] primary, he says: "This amounts to saying..." He raises the objection —

children.text:
cetir /
iśvarānumāna iva pakṣadharmatāvalenaiva vivakṣito viśeṣaḥ setsyatītyarthaḥ /
nanvanvayinā viśeṣaṃ sādhayatā kevalavyatirekiṇaḥ kiṃ khaṇḍitam, yenāyaṃ tasmin sambhavatyevodāste, khaṇḍane vā, atha tenaiva viparyayasyāpi vaktuṃ sukaratvādityata āha---ṛjumārgeṇeti /
vyāptirhi siddhimārgaḥ /
tasyāparivarta eva ṛjutvam, parivartastaṃ vakratetyarthaḥ pariharati---kāraṇamātrasyeti /
uktamatra yathāsminnarthe pakṣadharmatā na prabhavati /
ābhiprāyikohyarthastadgocaraḥ /
sa cābhiprāyeṇa vyāpyate, yatsiddhimanyareṇa śabdārthaḥ pratyetuṃ na śakyate /
children.translated_text: and that is pervaded by intention — without the establishment of which, the meaning of the sentence cannot be understood.

children.text: na ca dravyāṣṭakātiriktamapratītya teṣāṃ samavāyikāraṇameva pratyetuṃ na śakyate /
children.translated_text: And without cognizing [something] beyond the eight substances, their being merely the inherence-cause of those [desires etc.] cannot be cognized.

children.text: na hīcchādīn prati pṛthivyāḥ samavāyikāraṇatve teṣāṃ tadvattā abhidhīyamānā virudhyate /
children.translated_text: For when the inherence-cause-hood of earth with respect to desires and the like is asserted, the statement that those [desires] possess that [earth as cause] is not contradicted.

children.text: yathā dvyaṇukādikāraṇajñāne teṣāṃ paridṛṣṭasāmarthyakārakaprayoktṛlakṣaṇakartṛpūrvakatvaṃ śabdopāttamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Just as, in the cognition of the cause of dyads and the like, their being preceded by a maker characterized as an agent possessing observed capacity is taken up by the word [of the <s>sūtra</s>] —

[the word] "<s>cet</s>" (if). Just as in the inference of <s>Īśvara</s> (God), the desired specific [conclusion] will be established by the very strength of the property-of-the-thesis — that is the meaning. Now, by the positive [inference], [the objection is:]

children.text:
punaḥ śaṅkate---pariśeṣāditi /
āśritatvaṃ tāvadeteṣāmanvayina eva siddham /
dravyāṣṭakāśritatvaniṣedho 'pyanvayina eva sidhyati /
tatkimaparamavaśiṣyate yatkevalavyatirekiṇā setsyatītyarthaḥ /
uttaram---sa eveti /
ayamarthaḥ /
pūrvasmād āśritatvaṃ siddhaṃ tadanyasmādapi dravyāṣṭakānāśritatvam /
tadatiriktārthāśritatvasiddhistu naikasmādapi /
tadabhāve cānayorapi varodha eva /
tasmādarthād aṣṭātiriktāśritatvasiddhiḥ sa cārthastāvannānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore, the establishment of dependence on something beyond the eight [substances] is by implication. And that meaning is, to begin with, not a positive concomitance.

children.text: na hi dravyāṣṭakānāśritatve sati yadāśritam, tadatiriktadravyāśritamityastyanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that there is a positive concomitance: "whatever is dependent, when the eight substances are not its substrata, is dependent on a substance beyond those."

children.text: vakroktikaścānvayī, kevalavyatirekiprapañca e vivakṣābhedāt /
children.translated_text: And the positive [inference] is one that speaks crookedly — being, in the elaboration of the purely negative [inference], [merely] a difference of intended formulation.

children.text: tasmāt vyatireka evārthaḥ, tadvān pariśeṣo vyatirekīti suṣṭhūktam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning is negative concomitance alone; what possesses that [negative concomitance] is the method of residues — [which is itself] a negative inference. Well said!

he raises the objection again: "By the method of residues..." To begin with, the dependence of these [desires etc. on something] is established for the positive [inference] itself. The negation of their dependence on the eight substances —

children.text:
idānīṃ viśeṣaṇasiddhaye pramāṇaṃ sūcayati---yadi hīti /
viparyayeṇa prayogaḥ /
śarīrendriyāṇi necchādisamavāyikāraṇāni bhūtatvād ghaṭādivaditi /
nanu yatra dravyāṣṭakātiriktadravyāśritā iti pratijñā, tatra yuktametat /
yatra tu nedaṃ nirātmakamiti tatra nirātmakaśabdenāpi ayamevārtha ucyata iti vadatā icchādisamavāyikāraṇavirahaniṣedha eva pratijñārthaḥ svīkṛtaḥ /
tathā ca kathamaṣṭadravyātiriktecchādisamavāyikāraṇavattā śarīrasya ityāśaṅkāmupasaṃharanneva pariharati---tasmāditi /
atrāpi pṛthivyādivilakṣaṇecchādisamavāyikāraṇavat jīvaccharīramiti pratijñārthaḥ /
tatsamavetecchādikāryavattvāditi hetvarthaḥ /
nanu
children.translated_text: Now he indicates the <s>pramāṇa</s> for establishing the qualifier: "For if..." The argument [is] by the converse. The body and sense-organs are not desire —

children.text: tathāpi---bauddhaṃ prati siddhasādhanaṃ bhavatyeva, so 'pi pṛthivyādyatiriktamevecchādīnām upādānamicchatītyata āha---na caiṣāmiti /
children.translated_text: even so — against the Buddhist, this would amount to proving what is already proved, for even he accepts that the substratum of desires and the like is something beyond earth and the like —

children.text: sthairye satīti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The completion is: "when stability obtains."

children.text:
nanu tathāpi ghaṭādibhyo nirātmakebhya icchādivyatirekaḥ kiṃ tathābhūtadravyavyāvṛttikṛtaḥ? kiṃ vā bhūtānāmeva pariṇatibhedavyāvṛttikṛta iti sandigdhopādhikatvādagamaka evetyata āha---yathā ceti /
vyatirekamukheṇāpīti /
yadi sādhyenāsya kvacidapyanvayo nāsti, tadā viruddha evāyamityarthaḥ /
na svābhāvikamiti /
na vayamasyopeyamanvayaṃ vyāsedhāmo 'pi tūpāyamityarthaḥ /
tathāpi nāsyānvayino bheda upeyabhūtenāpyanvayenānvayitvādityata āha---etāvataiveti /
nanu vastutaḥ sādhyadharmavāneva dharmī sapakṣaḥ /
sa ca tathājñāto vyavahriyate param /
children.translated_text: And that [similar instance] is known as such and is used [in argumentation] only subsequently.

children.text: tataśca tadanvito 'pi heturanvayavyatirekyeva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when conjoined with it [the probandum], the reason is simply a [reason operating through] positive and negative concomitance.

children.text: ajñaistu tathā na vyavahriyata ityanyadetaditi śaṅkate---na ca pakṣa eveti /
children.translated_text: But the ignorant do not use it as such — suspecting that this is something different, he raises the doubt: 'and not in the thesis alone.'

children.text: vyavahāreturanvayaścintyate, na tu vyavahārya ityāśayavān pariharati---jijñāsiteti //
children.translated_text: With the intention that the positive concomitance under consideration is the cause of usage, not the thing to be used, he responds: 'what is desired to be known.'

Now, even so, is the exclusion of desire and the like from pots and the like, which are devoid of <s>ātman</s>, brought about by the exclusion from substances of such a kind? Or by the exclusion from a modification-difference of the elements themselves? — because the condition (<s>upādhi</s>) is doubtful, [the reason] is inconclusive — therefore he says: 'and just as.' 'Through the negative concomitance as well' — the meaning is: if there is no positive concomitance of this [reason] with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) anywhere, then this is simply a contradictory [reason]. 'Not natural' — the meaning is: we do not deny that this [reason] has a positive concomitance to be accepted, but rather [we deny] the means [of establishing it]. Even so, the difference of this positive-concomitant [reason] from [a reason that has] positive concomitance with the desired [conclusion] is [impossible] because of the positive concomitance even of the positive concomitant with the [desired] positive concomitance — therefore he says: 'by just this much.' Now, in reality, only a subject (<s>dharmin</s>) that possesses the property to be proved is a similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>).

children.text: nanu yadyasya sapakṣavyatirekāpratiṣedhaḥ, kathaṃ nāsādhāraṇyam? tatpratiṣedhaścet kathaṃ nānvayaḥ? atha tatpratiṣedhe 'pi tāvanmātramave nānvayaḥ, evaṃ tarhi sapakṣavat pakṣe 'pi nairātmyapratiṣedhe 'pi nātmasadbhāva iti parākṣepaṃ parihṛtya tadgranthaṃ paṭhati śarīrādiṣviti /
vipakṣe hi sati sata eva kasyacid vyatirekaḥ pratīta iti pramāṇena pratīta iti pratipāditam /
children.translated_text: For in the dissimilar instance, the negative concomitance of something that indeed exists has been cognized — thus it has been established that it is cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasya ca pramāṇapratītasya vyatirekasya pakṣe 'pi satyeva niṣedhaḥ pramāṇena kriyata iti yuktā niṣedhalakṣaṇā vidhisiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And the negation in the thesis too of that negative concomitance — which has been cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s> — is accomplished by a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Hence the establishment of a positive fact through negation is justified.

children.text: sapakṣastu na kenacit pramāṇena pratīta iti na tatrānvayavyatirekatanniṣedhāḥ paramārthataḥ kenacitpramāṇena śakyate pratyetum /
children.translated_text: But the similar instance is not cognized by any <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, the positive concomitance, negative concomitance, and negation of those in that [similar instance] cannot ultimately be cognized by any <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: tatkathaṃ vidhiniṣedhayoranyataraprasaktirityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then how can there be the applicability of either positive assertion or negation? — this is the meaning.

Now, if [you hold that] the non-negation of [the reason's] absence from the similar instance [is sufficient], how is there non-uncommonness? And if that [absence] is negated, how is there not [already] positive concomitance? But if, even when that [absence] is negated, just that much alone is not yet positive concomitance — then similarly, even in the thesis, the negation of non-selfhood does not [entail] the existence of <s>ātman</s> — having thus averted the cross-objection, he reads the text: 'in the body and the like.'

children.text:
sapakṣāvyatirekī cet sapakṣavyatirekaniṣedhāvanityarthaḥ /
anvayī sapakṣānvayī /
athaivamapi nānvayī, api tu vyatirekyeva /
atha sapakṣavyatirekaniṣedhasyāpi vyatirekaniṣedhamātraparyavasāyitayānvayāparyavasānāditi manyase, tadā pakṣe 'pi nairātmyaniṣedhe 'pi tāvanmātraparyavasāyitayā na sātmakatvaparyavasānamiti vārttikārthaḥ /
tadetannirākṛtam
children.translated_text: If [you say the reason is] one that does not deviate from the similar instance — the meaning is: in the sense of negating the absence from the similar instance. 'Positively concomitant' means positively concomitant with the similar instance. But even so, it is not positively concomitant, but simply negatively concomitant. Now, if you think that even the negation of absence from the similar instance terminates in mere negation of absence, and does not terminate in positive concomitance — then even in the thesis, the negation of non-selfhood terminates in just that much and does not terminate in being possessed of <s>ātman</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>Vārttika</s>. This has been refuted,

children.text:
avastuni pāramārthikavidhiniṣedhānabhyupagamāt /
tathāpi svavacanavirodhapratihatametadityata āha---etaccāsmābhiriti /
na tasya vyatirekavyabhicāro 'pi tasya vyatirekadharmatayā tadabhāve 'nupapatterityarthaḥ /
pariharatītyādi /
vyabhicāravadavyabhicāro 'pi taddharma eva so 'pi kathaṃ tadabhāve bhavedityarthaḥ /
tato vyāvṛttyabhāveneti vyāvṛttinirūpaṇābhāvenetyarthaḥ /
āgāmivārttika bhramanirāsārthaṃ sphuṭamapi vyācaṣṭe---atra ceti /
children.translated_text: In order to remove a misunderstanding regarding the forthcoming <s>Vārttika</s>, he explains what is clear: 'and here.'

children.text: bhramaṃ nivārayati---na punariti /
children.translated_text: He prevents the misunderstanding: 'but not again.'

children.text: nanvetāvatyeva sūtrārthe ko doṣaḥ syādityata āha---tathā satīti /
children.translated_text: Now, what fault would there be in just this much as the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>? — therefore he says: 'this being so.'

children.text: śeṣamanumānalakṣaṇa iti sapakṣe siddha ityādi vṛttipadāntaradūṣaṇaśeṣam //
children.translated_text: The remainder is: in the definition of inference — the rest [belongs to the section] refuting other terms in the definition, [beginning with] 'established in the similar instance' and the like.

because positive assertion and negation in the ultimate sense are not accepted regarding what is not a real entity. Even so, this [objection] is repelled by the self-contradiction of one's own statement — therefore he says: 'and this by us.' The meaning is: even the deviation of that [reason] is not a property of that [reason], since in the absence of that [deviation] there is no basis [for the property of deviation]. He responds and so forth. The meaning is: just as deviation is a property of precisely that [reason], so too non-deviation — how could it [non-deviation] exist in the absence of that [reason]? Therefore, by the absence of exclusion — the meaning is: by the impossibility of determining the exclusion.

children.text:
sautrāntiketi vaibhāsikamatavyudāsārtham /
tanmate nityasyāpyākāśāderakāryasyāpi saṃbhavāt /
yadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Sautrāntika</s>' — for the purpose of setting aside the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view. For in that view, even what is eternal, such as <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the like, and even what is without effect, is possible. As they say:

children.text: ākāśaṃ dvau nirodhau ca trayametadasaṃskṛtam
children.translated_text: 'Space and the two cessations — these three are the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)'

children.text: iti /
children.translated_text: — thus.

children.text: sadṛśakṣaṇa sabhāgasantānalakṣaṇanirodhabhedena nirodhau dvau vināśau yayorapratisaṃkhyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhāviti paribhāṣā //
children.translated_text: The two cessations [are distinguished] by the division of cessation into cessation of homogeneous moments and cessation of a homogeneous continuum — the two destructions of which are called <s>apratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (cessation without deliberation) and <s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (cessation with deliberation) — this is the convention.

children.text: atra dignāgena
children.translated_text: Here, by <s>Dignāga</s>,

children.text: sapakṣe sannityādinā
children.translated_text: through [the verse] 'present in the similar instance' and so forth,

children.text: hetutadābhāsān, tadudāharaṇārthaṃ
children.translated_text: the [valid] reasons and their semblances [were classified]; for the purpose of illustrating those,

children.text: nityānityetyādinā
children.translated_text: through [the verse] 'eternal and non-eternal' and so forth,

children.text: sādhyavargaṃ
children.translated_text: the class of <s>sādhyas</s> (probanda) [was presented];

children.text: prameyetyādinā
children.translated_text: through [the verse] 'knowable' (<s>prameya</s>) and so forth,

children.text: sādhanavargaṃ
children.translated_text: the class of <s>sādhanas</s> (probantia) [was presented];

children.text: sapakṣaḥ khaṃ ghaṭo buddhirviyadgaganamambaram //
children.translated_text: 'The similar instance is space, a pot, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), the sky, the firmament, the atmosphere'

children.text: taḍidvyomnī taḍitkumbhau paramāṇurviyat tathā //
children.translated_text: 'lightning and space, lightning and a pot, an atom, and space likewise'

children.text: iti sapakṣavargaṃ
children.translated_text: — thus the class of similar instances [was presented];

children.text: kumbho viyat taḍidvyomnī ghaṭaḥ kumbhastaḍiddhaṭau /
children.translated_text: 'A pot, space, lightning and space, a pot, a pot, lightning and a pot,'

children.text: kumbho vayad ghaṭo buddhirvipakṣo 'sya yathākramam //
children.translated_text: 'a pot, wind, a pot, <s>buddhi</s> — the dissimilar instance of each in order'

children.text: iti vipakṣavargaṃ prapañcya
children.translated_text: — thus, having elaborated the class of dissimilar instances,

children.text: tatretyādinā
children.translated_text: through 'there' and so forth,

children.text: heturnirdhāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: the [valid] reason was determined.

children.text: tatra prapañcaṃ vihāya yāvanmātreṇa heturnirdhāryate tāvadupanyasyati---atreti //35 //
children.translated_text: Setting aside the elaboration, he presents just so much as suffices to determine the [valid] reason: 'here.' //35//

children.text: sādhyasādharmyāttaddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam //36 //
children.translated_text: An example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is a case (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) that possesses the property of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) by virtue of similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>. //36//

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> //

children.text: prayoge kiṃ sautra eva kramo grāhyaḥ, kramāntaraṃ veti sandehamudāharaṇasya prayojanaṃ darśayan nivārayati---hetāviti /
children.translated_text: Showing the purpose of the example while removing the doubt — 'should the order of the <s>sūtra</s> itself be adopted in the application, or a different order?' — he says: 'in the reason.'

children.text: yato nāvyāpto nāpratītavyāptiko hetubhāve vyavatiṣṭhate sādhyasiddhāvekāgrībhavati, ato vyāpterbubhūtsitatvāt saiva pratipādayituṃ yujyata iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The remainder is: since [a probans] that is neither non-pervasive nor one whose pervasion has not been ascertained does not remain in the status of a reason [but rather] becomes single-pointed upon the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s>, therefore, since the pervasion is what is desired to be known, it alone is appropriate to be demonstrated.

children.text: tathāpyudāharaṇasya ko 'vasara ityata āha---na ceti //
children.translated_text: Even so, what occasion is there for the example? — therefore he says: 'and not.'

children.text:
pratītasāmarthyaṃ hi sādhanaṃ sādhye upanayanti /
na tūpanīya paścāt sāmarthyaṃ jijñāsanta iti sarvalokasiddhamiti saṃgatisaṃkṣepaḥ /
tathāpi sāmānyalakṣaṇavibhāgau vinā nāvasaro viśeṣalakṣaṇasyetyata āha---sūtramitīti /
nanūdāharaṇopalakṣaṇamaprakṛtamapi kasmādupādīyate? kasmācca vibhyatā lakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtamapahīyata
children.translated_text: For people apply the probans, whose capacity has been ascertained, to the <s>sādhya</s>. They do not first apply it and then seek to know its capacity — this is established by universal practice — this is the summary of the connection. Even so, without the general definition and its division, there is no occasion for the specific definition — therefore he says: 'the <s>sūtra</s>.' Now, why is the indication through the example taken up even though it is not the primary topic? And why is the definition, though the primary topic, abandoned out of fear?

children.text:
ityata āha---dṛṣṭānta iti /
prakṛtalakṣaṇasiddhyarthamevopalakṣaṇābhidhānamiti nobhayadoṣa ityarthaḥ /
anenetyādinā vyavacchedyasamānāsamānajātīyapradarśanaṃ sūcitasāmānyalakṣaṇābhiprāyam /
tacca dṛṣṭāntavacanam udāharaṇamiti draṣṭavyam /
viśeṣalakṣaṇapakṣe tūdāharaṇaviśeṣo lakṣyaḥ /
udāharaṇaṃ sapakṣodāharaṇamityarthaḥ /
śeṣaṃ lakṣaṇam /
tena hi samānajātīyād vipakṣodāharaṇād vijātīyācca pratijñāderidaṃ vyavacchidyata iti boddhavyam /
children.translated_text: For by this [definition], this [example] is distinguished from the dissimilar-instance illustration, which is of the same class [as what is to be excluded], and from the thesis and the like, which are of a different class — this should be understood.

children.text: viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ca śrautam /
children.translated_text: And the specific definition is scriptural [i.e., directly from the <s>sūtra</s>].

children.text: tadvyākhyānabhāṣyamanūdya vyācaṣṭe---sādhyeneti /
children.translated_text: Having cited the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that explains that [definition], he comments: 'by the <s>sādhya</s>.'

children.text: tena tādṛśena dṛṣṭāntena sādhanadharmaprayuktasādhyadharmavatā upalakṣitaṃ viṣayatayā tadviṣayaṃ vacanamudāharaṇaṃ sapakṣodāharaṇamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: a statement that has as its object, by way of indication, an illustrative instance that possesses the property to be proved, which is conjoined with the property of the probans — that statement is the example, the illustration of the similar instance.

— therefore he says: 'the illustrative instance.' The statement of the indication is for the purpose of establishing the primary-topic definition itself — hence there is no fault on either count — this is the meaning. By 'by this' and so forth, the showing of things of the same and different class as what is to be excluded indicates the intention of the general definition. And that statement of the illustrative instance is the example — this should be understood. But on the view of specific definition, a specific example is what is defined. 'Example' means 'illustration of the similar instance' — this is the meaning. The remainder is the definition.

children.text:
yasmādityādivārttikaṃ yadyapi ke 'pi nānumanyante, tathāpi vākyaśeṣabhūtenāpyanena bhavitavyamiti manyamānaḥ tadantarbhāvyaiva śaṅkāmutthāpayati---yasmāditi /
iyaṃ cāśaṅkā tairāgāmivāvārttikaṃ dṛṣṭvā sādhyenaivetyavadhāraṇākṣepiketi buddham /
tacca mandaprayojanam, hetulakṣaṇarītimatidiśataiva tatprayojanasya darśitaprāyatvāt /
mā bhūccāvadhāraṇasamarthane 'pi taddharmabhāvigrahaṇānarthakyaśaṅkāśeṣasthitiriti matvā vyācaṣṭe---avadhāraṇeti /
tathāpi śaṅkānurūpaṃ nottaramityata āha---śiṣyopādhyāyeti /
ayamarthaḥ /
sādhyenaiva
children.translated_text: Although some do not accept the <s>Vārttika</s> beginning with 'since,' nevertheless, thinking that it must at least be a continuation of the sentence, he raises the doubt by subsuming it: 'since.' And this doubt should be understood as prompted by the restrictive objection upon seeing the forthcoming <s>Vārttika</s> beginning with 'by the <s>sādhya</s> alone.' And that [objection] has little purpose, since the purpose of that [restriction] has been mostly shown in the manner of the definition of the reason. And thinking: 'let there not remain even the residual doubt of the purposelessness of the expression possessing the property of that [sādhya], even when the restriction is established' — he comments: 'the restriction.' Even so, the answer does not correspond to the doubt — therefore he says: 'student and teacher.' The meaning is this: 'by the <s>sādhya</s> alone —

children.text:
sādharmyamiti viśeṣyasaṃgata evakāro 'nyayogaṃ vyavacchinatti, na tu sādharmyasyāprayojakatvamapi /
na ca pakṣasapakṣābhyāmanyena maitratanayatvāderyogaḥ sandigdho 'pi /
na ca pakṣo 'pi vipakṣa iti tatra tatra darśitameva /
sādharmyamevetyayamapi viśeṣaṇasaṃgata evakāro 'yogaṃ vyavacchindyāt, na tu tasyāprayojakatvamapi /
na hyaprayojakasyāyogavyavacchedo virudhyate /
prayojakatāyāṃ tu darśitāyāṃ tathābhūtasyāyogavyavaccheda prakṛtasiddhiḥ /
evaṃ ca sati prathamamavadhāraṇaṃ mandaprayojanamapi paraśucchedyatāṃ ko vā nakhacchedye sahiṣyata iti nyāyena darśitam /
aprayojake tūdāhartavye anaikāntikodāharaṇaṃ dvayorapyubhayakoṭisparśāviśeṣāditi /
nanvevaṃ sati hetulakṣaṇaṃ nyūnamaprayojakāvyudasanādityata āha---hetulakṣaṇe tviti /
ubhayavikalapradarśanenāśrayavikalamapi pradarśitaprāyam /
children.translated_text: By showing what deviates from both [terms], what deviates from the substratum is also mostly shown.

children.text: yathā, yat kramayaugapadyarahitaṃ tadasat /
children.translated_text: For example: 'what is devoid of both succession and simultaneity is non-existent,'

children.text: yathā vājiviṣāṇamiti /
children.translated_text: 'like the horn of a horse.'

children.text: evamarthadvārakamudāharaṇābhāsacatuṣṭayaṃ darśayitvā śabdadvārakaṃ dvayaṃ darśayituṃ pīṭhamāracayati---pañcamīti //36 //
children.translated_text: Having thus shown the four pseudo-examples through meaning, he prepares the ground to show the two [pseudo-examples] through verbal formulation: 'the fifth.' //36//

similarity' — the restrictive particle, being connected with the qualificand, excludes the conjunction with the other, not however the non-productivity of the similarity as well. Nor is even the doubtful conjunction of being the son of <s>Maitra</s> and the like with anything other than the thesis and the similar instance [a problem]. Nor is the thesis also a dissimilar instance — this has been shown in the respective [contexts]. 'Similarity alone' — this restrictive particle too, being connected with the qualifier, would exclude non-conjunction, not however the non-productivity of that as well. For the exclusion of non-conjunction of what is non-productive is not contradictory. But when its productivity has been shown, the exclusion of non-conjunction of what is of such a kind accomplishes the primary-topic [establishment]. And this being so, the first restriction, though of little purpose, has been shown by the principle 'who would tolerate even a nail-scratch when the head is to be cut off?' But when what is to be illustrated is non-productive, an inconclusive illustration [applies] to both [the productive and non-productive] equally, since both touch both extremes. Now, this being so, the definition of the reason is deficient because it does not exclude the non-productive [illustration] — therefore he says: 'but in the definition of the reason.'

children.text: tadviparyayādvā viparītam //37 //
children.translated_text: Or, the reverse [example] by virtue of the opposite of that [similarity]. //37//

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> //

children.text:
savyākhyānaṃ parivartitapadam /
udāharaṇaṃ vipakṣodāharaṇam /
yadyapyataddharmabhāvitvāt sādhyavaidharmyavān dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇamiti vyatyayo yujyate, tathāpyārjavānurodhād yathāśruti vyācaṣṭe---sātmakatayeti /
ata eva padāni vibhajya saṃkalitamarthamāha---etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
atrāpi sādhyasādhanobhayāvyāvṛttā āśrayavikalaśceti /
arthadvārakamābhāsacatuṣṭayaṃ vyudastam, yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvāt /
yat punarna nityaṃ tadaśrāvaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam, yathākāśam, yathā dhvaniḥ, yathā śabdatvam, yathā śaśaviṣāṇamiti /
śabdadvārakaṃ ca dvayamanupadarśitavyāvṛttikam, viparyayopadarśitavyāvṛttikaṃ ceti /
yathā nedaṃ nirātmakaṃ jīvaccharīramicchādimattvāt, ghaṭavaditi /
yat punaricchādimanna bhavati, tannirātmakaṃ thā ghaṭa iti ceti /
sūtrasthaśceti /
samuccaye svarūpasamuccaye /
na kevalaṃ sādhyasādharmyāt taddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam, api tu tadviparyayād viparītaṃ cetyarthaḥ /
na punarviṣayasamuccaye /
ekasmin viṣaye nirapekṣatvasāpekṣṭvābhyāṃ vṛttirvikalpasamuccayau /
na caivamatra /
kutaḥ vyatirekiviṣayatvād
children.translated_text: The word-order is reversed, with explanation. The example is the dissimilar-instance illustration. Although, because of possessing the property that is the absence of that [sādhya's property], the exchange 'an illustrative instance that possesses dissimilarity with the <s>sādhya</s> is the example' is justified, nevertheless, in deference to straightforwardness, he comments according to the literal [sūtra] reading: 'by virtue of having <s>ātman</s>.' For this very reason, having divided the words, he states the combined meaning: 'this amounts to saying.' Here too, the four pseudo-[examples] that deviate from the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>sādhana</s>, and both, or that lack a substratum, have been excluded through meaning. For example: 'sound is eternal, because of being audible. But what is non-eternal is seen as non-audible — like space, like reverberation, like sound-hood, like the horn of a hare.' And the two [pseudo-examples] through verbal formulation: one that does not show the exclusion, and one that shows the exclusion in reverse. For example: 'this living body is not devoid of <s>ātman</s>, because of possessing desire and the like — like a pot.' 'But what does not possess desire and the like is devoid of <s>ātman</s> — like a pot.' And the particle 'ca' (and) in the <s>sūtra</s> — is in the sense of aggregation, [specifically] aggregation of the [two] forms. Not only is an example that possesses the property of the <s>sādhya</s> by virtue of similarity with the <s>sādhya</s> an illustrative instance, but also the reverse [example] by virtue of the opposite — this is the meaning. But not in the sense of aggregation of objects. In a single object, the [two] operations — due to independence and dependence — are optionality and aggregation. But that is not the case here. Why? Because of being the domain of the purely negative [concomitant],

children.text: vaidharmyodāharaṇasyeti /
mātreti pūraṇīyam /
children.translated_text: 'Alone' is to be supplied.

children.text: upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat, anvayiviṣayatvāt sādharmyodāharaṇamātrasyetyapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: And this is merely indicative — it should also be seen that the similarity-example alone belongs [to the domain] of the purely positive [concomitant], because of being its domain.

children.text: tathāpyanvayavyatirekiviṣayatayā samuccayavikalpau bhaviṣyataḥ, yathā bhāṣyakṛdudāharaṇamityāśaṅkānirākaraṇavārttikaṃ yojayitumāha---atreti /
children.translated_text: Even so, aggregation and optionality will [both] obtain by virtue of being the domain of the positive-and-negative [concomitant] — in order to construe the doubt-removing <s>Vārttika</s> as such, he says: 'here.'

children.text: sarvatra hi anvayapūrvikaiva vyatirekapratipattiḥ, pratiyoginirūpaṇamantareṇābhāvasyānirūpaṇāt //
children.translated_text: For everywhere, the apprehension of negative concomitance is preceded by positive concomitance, because absence cannot be determined without determining the counter-positive.
the dissimilarity-example belongs [to that domain].

children.text:
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ kevalavyatirekiṇi sāmānyato 'nvayavyatirekiṇi tu viśeṣato 'pi /
yathā ca kevalavyatirekī satyapi sāmānyānvaye na tenopasaṃhartuṃ śakyaḥ, tathoktam /
anvayavyatirekiṇā tu vyatirekopasaṃhāreṇa yāvānarthaḥ sādhyaḥ, tāvānanvayopasaṃhāreṇaiva siddhaḥ ityadhikaṃ tāvat tadabhidhānam /
punaruktaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: But the distinction is this: in the case of the purely negative [concomitant], [the positive concomitance is] general; but in the case of the positive-and-negative [concomitant], it is also specific. And just as the purely negative [concomitant], even though there is a general positive concomitance, cannot be subsumed by it — so it has been stated. But for the positive-and-negative [concomitant], whatever is to be established through the negative-concomitance subsumption is already established by the positive-concomitance subsumption alone — hence that much at least is an additional statement. And it is redundant.

children.text:
niyamavatoranvayavyatirekayorekatarasiddhāvanyatarasiddherarthāpannatvāt /
yadyevam, kevalavyatirekiṇyapi tarhi vyatirekasiddhāvanvayasiddhiḥ apyarthāt /
tathā ca na kevalavyatirekīti /
satyam, sidhyatyanvayo na tu sapakṣe, kiṃ tu pakṣa eveti viśeṣaḥ /
sa copeyo nopāya ityuktam /
nanvanvayavyatirekiṇo 'pi pakṣādeva vyatirekapratyayo mā bhūdityetadarthaṃ vipakṣe niyamo darśayitumucitaḥ /
na, tatra hetūpasaṃhāreṇaiva śaṅkāyā nivartitatvāt /
nanvevaṃ sati kevalānvayinyapi arthād vyatirekasiddhiprasaṅgaḥ /
tathā ca na kevalānvayīti cet---na, aviśeṣavidhitvāt /
yatra hi sapakṣataditarau staḥ, tatra viśeṣavidhau śeṣaniṣedho gamyate, yathā nityānityapratītau /
anitya eva kṛtakatvamityukte arthād gamyate na nitya iti /
children.translated_text: when it is said "what is made (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is in the non-eternal alone," by implication it is understood: "not in the eternal."

children.text: na cābhidheyānabhidheyakoṭidvayasaṃbhavo, yato 'bhidheya eva prameyatvamityukte gamyatāṃ nānabhidheya iti /
children.translated_text: And there is no possibility of the two categories of what can be denoted and what cannot be denoted, such that when <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) is said to be only in what can be denoted, one should understand "not in what cannot be denoted."

children.text: ata evānvayavyatirekiṇi vyāpyavyāpakayoranyayogāyogavyavacchedena vyāptinirūpaṇam /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in the positive-and-negative inference, the ascertainment of pervasion is by the exclusion of mutual non-connection (<s>anyayoga</s>) and of mutual connection (<s>ayoga</s>) between the pervaded and the pervader.

children.text: kevalānvayini tu vyāptikriyāmupādāyātyantāyogavyavacchedeneti naivakārārthacodyāvakāśaḥ //
children.translated_text: But in the purely positive inference (<s>kevalānvayin</s>), taking up the act of pervasion, [the ascertainment is] by the exclusion of absolute non-connection — therefore there is no scope for the objection regarding the meaning of the particle "<s>eva</s>" (only).

Because for one possessing the restriction, when one of the two — positive or negative concomitance — is established, the other is automatically established. If so, then even in the purely negative inference, from the establishment of the negative concomitance

children.text:
nanvadhikapunaruktabhiyā mā bhūt samuccayo, vikalpastu bhavedityata āha---ṛjumārgeṇeti /
na hi kevalavyatirekiṇīvānvayavyatirekiṇyapyanvayād vyatirekā viśeṣaḥ /
kiṃ nāma? sa evārthaḥ /
tathā cānvayaṃ pratītya tanniṣedho vyatirekaḥ pratyetavyaḥ /
upalabhya ca tanniṣedhaṃ sa evānvayaḥ? so 'yaṃ prāk yadi pakṣa eva pratipannaḥ kimadhikaṃ vyatirekeṇa sādhitam? sapakṣe cet /
sa eva pakṣe kiṃ nopasaṃhṛtaḥ? na hyayamasādhako, nāpi prathamaṃ buddhāvupanipatito, nāpi na ṛjuriti, sapakṣāddhi kṛkāṭikābhaṅgena vipakṣagamanam, vipakṣācca tathaiva pakṣāgamanamiti vakro mārgaḥ /
pūrvastu sapakṣādabhimukhameva pakṣasaṃkrāntiritṛjuḥ /
na ca vakrarucernedamaniṣṭamiti vācyam, asāṃvyavahārikatvaprasaṅgāt /
na hi ghaṭamānayeti vaktavye 'naghaṭaṃ na mānaiṣīriti vaktāro bhavanti /
children.translated_text: for when one should say "bring the pot," people do not say "do not refrain from bringing the non-pot."

children.text: yathā svayamanvayamapratītya vyatirekāpratipattiḥ, tathā tamapratipādya tadabhāvapratipādanamaśakyamityavaśyamanvayoktau tadevādhikaṃ punaruktaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Just as there is no apprehension of the negative concomitance without first apprehending the positive concomitance oneself, so too, without conveying it, the conveyance of its absence is impossible — therefore the statement of the positive concomitance is necessarily

children.text: anuktau tu na vyatirekasyābhidhīyamānasyāpi pratipattirityapārthakamiti /
children.translated_text: but when it is not stated, even the negative concomitance, though being stated, is not apprehended — and [its statement] would be purposeless.

children.text: evamudāharaṇayorviśeṣavyavasthāṃ darśayatā vāśabdasya vyavasthitavibhāṣāvacanatve 'pi saṅgatirityapi darśitam //37 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by showing the specific arrangement of the two examples, it has also been shown that even when the particle "or" (<s>vā</s>) has the function of a settled option, the coherence [is maintained].

Now, [one might say:] let there not be a conjunction [of both types] out of fear of superfluity and redundancy; but let there be an alternative — therefore he says: "By the direct method..." For the positive-and-negative inference is not like the purely negative inference —

children.text: udāharaṇāpekṣastathetyupasaṃhāro na tatheti vā sādhyasyopanayaḥ //38 //
children.translated_text: "<s>Upanaya</s> (application) is the drawing together of the <s>sādhya</s> [with the thesis-subject], whether [the conclusion] is 'so it is' based on the example, or 'not so'" // [Sūtra] 38 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
saṃgatiṃ karoti---udāharaṇānantaramiti /
ānantaryamevakuta ityata āha---parāmarśeti /
etadeva kuta ityata āha---udāharaṇeti /
viṣayabhūtayorvyāptipakṣadharmatayorniyatapaurvāparyapratipattitvena viṣayaviṣayiṇorapyudāharaṇopanayayoḥ paurvāparyaniyama ityarthaḥ /
nanu nāvaśyaṃ jñānakramaniyamaṃ tadvacanakramaniyamo 'nurudhyate, viparyayeṇāpyabhidhānadarśanādityata āha---svapratipattāviti /
vyāptipakṣadharmatājñāne hi anumityupayoginī /
te ca yathā svasyotpadyete tathā parasyāpyutpādanīye, svapratipattyanusāreṇa parāvabodhanāt /
svayaṃ ca vyāptijñānādindriyādisahāyāt pakṣadharmatāvagamo na tu viparyayaḥ /
tataḥ parasyāpyudāharaṇavacanena vyāptijñānumutpādya tatsahacaritenopanayavacanena pakṣadharmatāpratyaya utpādanīyaḥ, kevalasya vyāptismaraṇasya
children.translated_text: He makes the connection: "After the example..." Whence the immediate succession? — therefore he says: "Reflective consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>)..." Whence even this? — therefore he says: "The example..."

children.text: vyāptismaraṇasya tadanutpādakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the mere recollection of pervasion is not productive of that [reflective consideration].

children.text: indriyādisthānīyasya cāparasya abhāvāt /
children.translated_text: And because of the absence of another [factor] occupying the place of the sense-organ and the like.

children.text: tasmādarthasiddhaḥ paurvāparyaniyama udāharaṇopanayayorityartha iti antataḥ phakvikā yojyeti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the rule of sequence between example and application is established by implication — this is the meaning. "At least the roasted chickpea [analogy] should be applied."

children.text:
tathātvātathātvayoriti /
tathātvenopasaṃhārasyātathātvenopasaṃhārasyetyarthaḥ /
hetoḥ upasaṃhāraḥ sādhyadharmiṇīti śeṣaḥ /
atrāpīti /
yathāśrutyarthābhyāmudāharaṇasūtram ubhayamupalakṣayati, tathedamapi sūtram ityarthaḥ /
tatrārthaṃ tāvadāha---udāharaṇeti /
sādhyasya hetumattayeti prakṛtam /
śrautaṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇadvayamāha---tatheti /
udāharaṇātideśenaiva vāśabdo 'pi sautro vyākhyātaḥ /
vyutpannāvyutpannatayeti /

yadyapi pāñcarūpyopapannaliṅgānusandhānaṃ vyutpannasyāpi pratipattisādhanaṃ niyatameva, tathāpi pratisandhānaṃ pratyaniyamaḥ, saṃskāratāratamyenodbodhakasyāniyamāt, tena tasya durunneyatvāt kṛtṛrāsadivādivad avyutpannaṃ pratyanaṅgatvācca /
children.translated_text: Although the connection of the mark endowed with the five characteristics is necessarily the means of apprehension even for the educated person, nevertheless, the reconnection [of specific mark with specific subject] is not necessarily [the same for all] —

children.text: yāvatā yādṛśā vopāyena svayamarthaḥ pratītaḥ, tāvattādṛgupāyapratipādanena para pratipādyaḥ /
children.translated_text: to the extent and by whatever means one has oneself apprehended the meaning, to that extent and by such means the other is to be made to apprehend.

children.text: tasya svātmanyevopāyatayā pramāṇasiddhatvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because [the means] is established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> as a means in one's own self.

children.text: etadeva na ca yathetyādinā darśitam //
children.translated_text: This very point has been shown by "and not as" and so forth.

"Of being-so and being-not-so" — the meaning is: of the conclusion in the manner of being-so, and of the conclusion in the manner of not-being-so. The completion is: the drawing together of the reason in the <s>sādhya</s>-subject.

children.text:
nanu vacanena svabodhasaṃkrāntiḥ pratipādanam, sacārthaḥ pratipādyaḥ svaśabdena yaḥ śabdāntareṇākṣipto 'pi na /
upanayārthastu hetunaivākṣipta iti codyārthamāha---yadyapītyādi /
etāvadatra syādupanayārthaṃ vyutpannaḥ svayaṃ vā ūheta, hetuvacanād vā pratipadyeta, tadākṣepato vā niścinuyāt? ādyo vyutpannetyādinā dūṣitaḥ /
dvitīyaṃ dūṣayati---yatpara iti /
tṛtīyaṃ dūṣayati---sāmarthyāditi /
athaivaṃ manvīthā yadyapi kṛtakatvāditi sādhanaparaṃ vacanam
children.translated_text: Now, communication (<s>pratipādana</s>) is the transfer of one's own understanding through utterance; and the meaning is what is to be communicated; and [the meaning] that is what is expressed by one's own word, which — even if implied by another word — is not [the same]. The purpose of <s>upanaya</s> —

children.text:
tathāpi dvidhā hi tatparatā śabdānām, upapannatayā upapādanīyatayā ca /
tatra prathama upapannatayā svārthamavabodhayan tannāntarīyakamarthamākṣipati, yathā jitaṃ nakuleneti siddhāvasthāyāṃ sarpaparājayam /
dvitīyastu upapādanīyatayā svārthaṃ pratipādayannapi kathaṃ tannāntarīyakamapyarthamākṣipet, yathā sa eva nakulavijayaḥ sādhanīyāvasthāyām /
tathātve vā pratijñaiva sarvamākṣipediti gataṃ hetunāpi /
children.translated_text: or, in the case of being-so, the thesis itself would imply everything — and this holds through the reason as well.

children.text: tasmāt sādhanatvenoddiṣṭe 'pi kṛtakatve tādrūpyasyāsiddhatvāt na tena vyāpterākṣepa iti nānarthakam udāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when being-made (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) has been pointed out as a means of proof, since the conformity-of-that-type is not established [merely by stating the reason], the implication of the pervasion is not [achieved] by that [alone] — therefore the example is not purposeless.

children.text: nanvetat samānamupanaye 'pītyāśayavānāha---tadvidhasyāpīti /
children.translated_text: Now, the same [objection] applies to <s>upanaya</s> as well — with this intention he says: "Of that type too..."

children.text: etena nigamanaṃ vyākhyātam // 38 //
children.translated_text: By this, <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) has been explained.

even so, the referentiality of words is twofold: by way of being already established, and by way of being yet to be established. Among these, the first — making the other understand its own meaning by way of being established —

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
nanu yathā hetvanurodhena tadupasaṃhāra upanaye dvividhaḥ, tathā sādhyānurodhena tadupasaṃhāro 'pi dvividha eva prāptaḥ /
avaśyaṃ ca sādhyena dvividhenaiva bhāvyam, sādhanānurodhāt /
na hyanvitād vyatirekaḥ sākṣāt sidhyati, vyatiriktād vānvayaḥ, liṅgasyānyāpohaviṣayatvānabhyupagamāt /
tasmāt pratijñānigamanayorapi dvaividhyaṃ prāptamiti kuto nābhihitaṃ iti sūtrakṛtā pratijñālakṣaṇe śaṅkitumucitamapi granthalaghimne sukhapratipattaye vā /
children.translated_text: therefore, the twofold nature of the thesis and the conclusion too has been obtained — so why has it not been stated? — the doubt that the <s>sūtrakāra</s> should have raised, even in the definition of the thesis, [about this point] —

children.text: iha śaṅkābhāṣyam---dvividhasyeti /
children.translated_text: Here the objection-<s>bhāṣya</s>: "Of the twofold..."

children.text: tad vyācaṣṭe---sādharmyavaigharmyeti /
children.translated_text: He explains that: "By similarity and dissimilarity..."

children.text: hetvādīnāmavayavānāṃ yeṣāṃ yatsaṃbandhi nigamanaṃ tasya samānamekaṃ lakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: Of the members — reason and the like — whichever <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) is related to whichever [type], the definition is the same, being one.

Now, just as the drawing together of the reason in accordance with the reason is twofold in <s>upanaya</s>, so too the drawing together of the <s>sādhya</s> in accordance with the <s>sādhya</s> should also be twofold —

children.text:
na hi vidhiniṣedhayoḥ pratijñātayorniṣedhavidhyupasaṃhāre pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanamiti lakṣaṇaṃ lagati, yenātiprasaṅgabhiyā sūtrakṛt tanniyamayedityarthaḥ /
etena pratijñāpi vyākhyātā /
na hyanvayivyatirekiṇorhetvoḥ vyatiriktanvitapratijñāne sādhyanirdeśa itilakṣaṇaṃ lagati, tayostadasādhyatvāt /
tasmād vivakṣito 'pyayamartho na sūtrito nyāyalabhyatvāt /
ata eva tatra vārttikam---anityaḥ śabdo, nedaṃ nirātmakamiti /
tat kiṃ kṛtakatvādityādika eva hetūpadeśaḥ kartavyaḥ? netyāha---tasmāditi /
na ca vācyaṃ tathaiva kiṃ na syāt, anupasaṃhāratvaprasaṅgāt /
tathā ca pūrvoktarūpānusandhānaviparītaprasaṅganivāraṇayoralābhe nigamanānarthakyāt /
sarvanāmno mahimā ca yat pūrvoktānusandhānam /
upasaṃhārasyaiṣa ca guṇo yad viparītakalpanāvilopanaṃ nāma /
na cānayoranyatarāpratītāvapi sādhyasiddhiḥ /
evaṃ ca satyavaśyakartavyatayā tasmāditi kṛte kṛtakatvāditi mandaprayojanam, vivaraṇamātratayā tu bhāṣyakāreṇoktam, ye tu nipuṇaṃmanyāḥ sarvanāmnā hetuvat pratijñābhidhānamapi manyante, teṣāṃ tathāśabdaḥ svarūpavacano vā syāt, prakāravacano vā? ādye tasmāt sa ityarthaḥ syāt /
tathā ca nigamanābhāso 'yaṃ lakṣaṇāyogādarthāyogācca /
dvitīye tu tādṛśa ityarthaḥ syāt /
tathāpi na tenaiva tādṛśatvam, anyasādṛśyaparāmarśe tu na nigamanalakṣaṇayogaḥ /
atha yathoktaḥ tathetyarthaḥ, tathāpi kathaṃ tatheti nityasāpekṣatvādanupasaṃhāratvam? gamyamānatvāt avacane pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanamiti lakṣaṇāyogaḥ /
pratipādanamātraparametaditi cet? nigamanārthakyam /
omiti cet? tatra vakṣyāma ityāśayavānāha---anityaḥ śabda iti pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanamiti /
ārambhopasaṃhāratayaiva cānayo rūpāviśeṣe sādhyasiddhanirdeśatā /
paṭārambhopasaṃhārayoriva paṭārambhakāstantava eva eta iti /
vacanamiti /
ata eva na paunarutkyavirodhāvityāha---
children.translated_text: For the definition "the restatement of the thesis in the form of the conclusion of negation or assertion of [what was] asserted as negation or assertion" does not apply — for fear of over-extension —

children.text:
yadyapīti /
tadidamuktam, yasyaiva sādhyatvamāsīdityādi /
na brūmaḥ siddhasya nirdeśo nigamanamapi tu siddhatayā nirdeśa iti /
tathaiva tataḥ pāñcarūpyapratīteḥ na hyupapādanīyatayā nirdeśaḥ sādhanasya rūpāntarasampadamākṣeptumapyalamityuktam /
tadetadabuddhā yastu
children.translated_text: "Although" — this is what was stated: "Of that very [proposition] whose <s>sādhya</s>-hood existed" and so forth. We do not say that the statement of what is established is the <s>nigamana</s>; rather, the statement in the mode of being established —

children.text: manyate ityādi taṃ pratyabhyupetyeti //39 //
children.translated_text: "he considers" and so forth — having accepted [the position] vis-à-vis that [opponent].

children.text: // iti nyāyalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on the definition of <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning) //

children.text: // nyāyottarāṅgalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // The section on the definition of the subsequent limbs of <s>nyāya</s> //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: evaṃ nyāyasvarūpaprakaraṇaṃ samarthya taduttarāṅgaprakaraṇasyāvakāśaḥ tatrāpītikartavyatāyatnatvāt phalasyeti tarko 'vasaraprāpta iti saṃgatibhāṣyamavatārya pūraṇena tadarthamāha---uddeśeti //
children.translated_text: Having thus established the section on the nature of <s>nyāya</s>, there is occasion for the section on its subsequent limbs — and there too, since the fruit is of the nature of the effort of what-is-to-be-done, <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) is necessary —

children.text:
abhyanujñātavyo niyatajijñāsāviṣayīkartavyaḥ /
viparyayāśaṅketi /
tatphalaṃ jijñāsā grāhyā /
ubhayakoṭisamasaṃśayaprabhavasamajijñāsāmapanīya niyataviṣayāṃ janayatā tarkeṇa pramāṇaviṣayo 'bhyanujñāto bhavati /
tenāyaṃ sūtrārthaḥ, pramāṇābhyanujñāvyāpāreṇa phalasiddhau vyāpriyamāṇa ūhastarka iti /
sa cāpāditasandehe sandehāpanne ca pravartata iti jñāpanārthamavijñātatattva ityuktam /
kāraṇepapattiḥ pramāṇābhyanujñā /
tasyāśca tarkavyāpārabhūtāyāḥ svarūpamuktamiti nātiprasaṅgaḥ /
evaṃvyāpāraścohaḥ prasaṅga ityeveti tathaiva ṭīkākṛtā uktam /
sa cāhāryahetorutpadyata iti jñāpanārthaṃ kāraṇopapattita iti padaṃ tadarthatayāpi kvacid vyākhyātam /
tadasya viṣayo 'vijñātatattvaḥ /
kāraṇamāhāryaliṅgotthāpyo vyāpāraḥ pramāṇābhyanujñā /
phalaṃ pramāṇaparatantrasya sataḥ phalavatsannidhāvaphalaṃ tadaṅgamiti nyāyena tattvanirṇayaḥ /
svarūpamaniṣṭaprasaṅgaḥ /
sa cātmāśrayetaretarāśrayacakrakānavasthāpramāṇabādhitārthaprasaṅgabhedena pañcavidhaḥ /
ete hi ekatra bhavanto 'nyataram abhyanujānanti /
etatsarvaṃ pratipipādayiṣorvākyalāghave 'nādaraḥ sūtrakṛtaḥ /
ata eva vivaraṇakārāṇāṃ saṃkulānīva vacāṃsīti tadatra nipuṇena pratipattrā bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the words of the commentators appear as if confused — and hence a discerning reader is required here.

children.text: tathā hi vyāpāravyāpāriṇoraniṣṭāpattyetyādinā bhedaṃ vyutpādyābhedaṃ vivakṣannāha---tayā pramāṇasyopapatyeti /
children.translated_text: Thus, having explained the difference through 'by the entailment of an undesired consequence for the function and the one who functions' and the like, and intending to state the non-difference, he says: 'by that, the justification of the <s>pramāṇa</s>...'

children.text: tarkakāraṇe kāraṇopapattipadaṃ saṃcārya tatkāryabhūtatarkādabhedaṃ vivakṣannāha---na copapattireveti /
children.translated_text: Transferring the term '<s>kāraṇopapatti</s>' (justification of the cause) to the cause of <s>tarka</s>, and intending to state its non-difference from <s>tarka</s> which is its effect, he says: 'and the justification is not merely...'

children.text: prapañcitaṃ caitat prathama sūtra eva ṭīkākṛtā iti kṛtaṃ prapañceneti //40 //
children.translated_text: And this has been elaborated by the sub-commentator in the very first <s>sūtra</s> — so enough with elaboration.

That which is sanctioned by <s>pramāṇa</s> is to be made the object of fixed inquiry. 'The apprehension of the contrary...' — the result of that, namely inquiry, is to be understood. By <s>tarka</s> (suppositional reasoning) which, having removed the balanced inquiry arising from a doubt equipoised on both alternatives, generates [inquiry] fixed on [one] object — the object of <s>pramāṇa</s> becomes sanctioned. Therefore, this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>: suppositional reasoning (<s>ūha</s>) is <s>tarka</s>, which operates through the function of <s>pramāṇa</s>-sanction in establishing the result. And it operates both in a doubt that has been brought about and in one that has been encountered — to communicate this, 'one whose real nature is unknown' is said. The justification of the cause is <s>pramāṇa</s>-sanction. And since the intrinsic nature of that [sanction], which is the function of <s>tarka</s>, has been stated — there is no over-extension. And [since] suppositional reasoning has such a function, it is <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) — thus it was stated by the sub-commentator in just that way. And since it arises from a hypothetically assumed reason — to communicate this, the word '<s>kāraṇopapatti</s>' (justification of the cause) has also been explained somewhere with that meaning. Thus, its object is [something] whose real nature is unknown. Its cause is the function aroused by the hypothetically assumed inferential mark; [its function is] <s>pramāṇa</s>-sanction. Its result — according to the principle 'what is dependent on <s>pramāṇa</s>, being present in the proximity of what has a result, [itself] without result, is a component thereof' — is the ascertainment of reality. Its intrinsic form is the entailment of an undesired consequence (<s>aniṣṭaprasaṅga</s>). And that is fivefold, by the division into self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>), mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>), circularity (<s>cakraka</s>), infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>), and entailment of a meaning contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s>. For these, occurring in one [alternative], sanction the other. All of this the <s>sūtrakāra</s>, wishing to convey, disregards economy of expression.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: evaṃ sādhanasampattau darśitāyāṃ so 'yaṃ parikarabandhaḥ kimavadhikaḥ kiṃparaśceti jijñāsāyāṃ nirṇayo 'vasaraprāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus shown the plenitude of the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), [the question arises:] what is the limit of this preparatory effort, and what comes after it? — in this inquiry, determination (<s>nirṇaya</s>) has its occasion.

children.text: tatrārthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇaya iti vaktavye tarkaikaviṣayatāpratipādanaṃ bhāṣyakṛtaḥ kvopayujyata ityata āha---naitaditi /
children.translated_text: Where he should have said 'determination is the ascertainment of the meaning,' the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s teaching that [determination] has <s>tarka</s> alone as its object — where is that useful? — to this he says: 'this is not...'

children.text: avyāptibhiyaivamuktam ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: it was stated thus out of fear of under-extension.

children.text:
mukhyātikrame bījamāha---atreti /
yadyapi vādagatau lakṣaṇīyāviti prakṛtānupayogi, tathāpi yadiha sādhanopālambhaśabdau vivṛṇeti, vāde ca pakṣapratipakṣaśabdau vivariṣyati, tena jānīmor'thasannidheḥ śabdārthasannidheḥ supratipadamiti mattvā bhāṣyakārasya tadgatalakṣaṇaivābhimateti hṛdi nidhāya tadanurodhenoktam---vādasūtragatāviti /
lakṣaṇānibandhanaṃ niyataṃ bandhanaṃ niyāmakamityarthaḥ /
nanu nāyaṃ kathānirṇayo lakṣyate, tatkuto vādiprativādyupakrabheṇa codyamityata āha--atreti /
vādeti kathopalakṣaṇam /
atha kathānirṇayalakṣaṇamevedaṃ kiṃ na syāt? yena codyaparihārāvapi saṃgatau syātāmityata āha---na tāvaditi /
śaṅkāyāḥ śaṅkitatvāt na tathetyarthaḥ /
kṛtaṃ tarhi parihāreṇetyata āha---abhyupetya tviti /
ayamarthaḥ, yadyapi parīkṣāyāṃ na vādiprativādinau staḥ, pṛcchopakramamātreṇa dvitīyopayogāt, saṃbhave 'pi tayorviṣayamātrākhyānaparyavasānāt, stheyasyava parīkṣakatvam, tathāpi pūrvapakṣottarapakṣaṃ pratyākalitaniṣkarṣabhedena catuṣpādavyavahārapradarśanāt phalato na kaścid viśeṣaḥ, ekavaktṛkatve 'pi tāvata eva vyāpārakalāpasya vicāre 'pi vidyamānatvāt /
tasmād yadyapyanipuṇaścodakastathāpi codyaṃ sāvakāśameveti yathāśrutameva abhyupetya pariharatīti /
nanu kathaṃ śāstre saṃśayānapekṣo nirṇayo mīmāṃsāyā vaiyarthyaprasaṅgādityata āha---nahīti /
śāstrameva hi tatra vicāryate /
tatra ca saṃśayo na pratiṣidhyate, tannirṇayasya parīkṣāsādhyatvāt /
tadarthanirṇaye tu śāstreṇa kartavye kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ? śāstrārthasya sarvathānupalabdhacaratayā saṃśayānāspadatvādityarthaḥ /
atha kathānirṇaye saṃśayaḥ kiṃ na syāt? kathamanyathā caturthe bhāṣyakṛd eva vādasya saṃśayavyudāsaṃ phalaṃ vakṣyatītyata āha---niścitayoreveti /
vādāt pūrvaṃ sandigdhāvapi pravṛttikāle niścitāvevābhimānāt, nānyathā tayoḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigrahasaṃbhava iti bhāvaḥ /
nanu bhāṣyakāreṇa codyopasaṃhāre yo 'vatiṣṭhate tena nirṇaya iti vadatā tābhyāmiti tṛtīyā darśitā /
sā ca pakṣācca pratipakṣācceti vadatā vārttikakṛtā avadhīritā kayā śaṅkayetyata
children.translated_text: He states the reason for the departure from the primary [meaning]: 'here...' Although [the statement] that 'they are to be defined in the context of debate' is not useful to the topic at hand, nevertheless — if he explains the terms '<s>sādhana</s>' (proof) and '<s>upālambha</s>' (censure) here, and will explain the terms '<s>pakṣa</s>' (thesis) and '<s>pratipakṣa</s>' (counter-thesis) in [the context of] debate — then, knowing that 'we shall easily understand [them] from the proximity of the meaning, [rather than] from the proximity of the word-meaning,' and holding in mind that the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s intention is the very definition contained therein, he states in accordance with that: 'in the <s>sūtra</s> pertaining to debate...' 'The binding of the definition' means 'the fixed binding, i.e., the determining factor' — this is the meaning. Now, this determination of debate is not what is being defined here — then whence the objection in terms of the division into proponent and opponent? — to this he says: 'here...' '<s>Vāda</s>' (debate) is an indication of <s>kathā</s> (discussion) [in general]. Now, could this not be the very definition of the determination of discussion — such that objection and reply too would be connected? — to this he says: 'to begin with, not...' The meaning is: since the doubt is [itself] doubted, it is not so. 'Then the reply should suffice' — to this he says: 'but having accepted...' The meaning is this: although in investigation there are no proponent and opponent — since merely the commencement of questioning suffices for the second [person's] usefulness, and since even when they are possible, [the inquiry] terminates in the mere narration of the subject-matter, and only the examiner has the role of the upholder — nevertheless, by the demonstration of a four-fold procedure with the analyzed distinctions of the prima facie view and the conclusive view, there is in result no difference [from debate], since even when there is a single speaker, the very same aggregate of functions exists in investigation too. Therefore, although the objector is unskilled, nevertheless the objection has scope — and thus he resolves [the matter] as literally stated, having accepted [the objection]. Now, how can determination in a <s>śāstra</s> be independent of doubt — since there would follow the pointlessness of <s>mīmāṃsā</s> (inquiry)? — to this he says: 'for not...' For it is the <s>śāstra</s> itself that is investigated therein. And therein, doubt is not prohibited, since the determination of that [<s>śāstra</s>-meaning] is to be accomplished through investigation. But in the determination of its meaning, which is to be done by the <s>śāstra</s>, whence is there doubt? — because the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s>, being of the nature of never having been apprehended in any way, is not a ground for doubt — this is the meaning. Now, should there not be doubt in the determination of debate? For how else will the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> himself state in the fourth [<s>āhnika</s>] that the removal of doubt is the result of <s>vāda</s> (debate)? — to this he says: 'of those who are already certain...' Although they were in doubt before the debate, at the time of engaging [in debate] they are [already] certain, from [their own] conviction — otherwise, their adoption of thesis and counter-thesis would not be possible — this is the purport. Now, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, in saying 'he who stands firm at the summing-up of the objection, by him is [reached] the determination' — showed the instrumental case 'by those two.' And that was overridden by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>'s saying 'from the thesis and from the counter-thesis' — with what apprehension?

children.text:
āha---nanviti /
tat kiṃ vādasamānayogakṣematayā śāstre 'pi pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmeva nirṇayaḥ? na caitat saṃbhavatītyata āha śāstre tu nirṇaya eveti /
na vimarśo nāpi pakṣapratipakṣāvityarthaḥ /
tadevāha---na tviti /
yat taduktaṃ vārttike sphuṭībhaviṣyatīti, tadāha---arthagrahaṇa iti /
nanu catuḥpañcādikakṣāpi kvacit kathā bhavati, tat kathaṃ kakṣātraye niyama ityata āha---prathamaṃ sādhanamiti /
children.translated_text: Now, debate sometimes proceeds in four, five, or more stages — then how is there restriction to three stages? — to this he says: 'the proof is first...'

children.text: kakṣāsahasramapyatraivāntarbhavatīti /
children.translated_text: Even a thousand stages are included in these very [three] —

children.text: anantarbhāve tvarthāntaratvaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: but if not included, the consequence would be irrelevance to the topic.

children.text: na hi sādhanadūṣaṇataduddhārabahirbhāvaḥ prakṛtopayogītyarthaḥ //41 //
children.translated_text: For what falls outside of proof, refutation, and their rescue is not useful to the topic at hand — this is the meaning.

— he says: 'now...' Then, is determination in the <s>śāstra</s> also by the thesis and counter-thesis alone, since it shares the same conditions as debate? But this is not possible — to this he says: 'but in the <s>śāstra</s>, determination alone...' The meaning is: not deliberation, nor thesis and counter-thesis. He states that very point: 'but not...' What was said — that it will become clear in the <s>Vārttika</s> — that he states: 'in the grasping of the meaning...'

children.text: // ityaudayana tātparyapariśuddhau prathamādhyāye prathamāhnikam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first lesson of the first chapter of <s>Udayana</s>'s <s>Tātparyapariśuddhi</s>.

children.text: // iti nyāyottarāṅgaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the subsequent components of <s>Nyāya</s>.

children.text: // prathamādhyāye dvitīyāhnikam //
children.translated_text: The second lesson of the first chapter.

children.text: // kathālakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: The section on the definition of <s>kathā</s> (discussion/debate).

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
evaṃ prathamāhnike sāṅgopāṅgo nyāyastāvallakṣitaḥ /
sa ca parārtho 'pi pṛcchopakramapratiyoginyekavaktṛke vicāre vivicya pravarttanīyaḥ /
tatra ca siddhiparatvam /
nyāyasya dūṣaṇopakramapratiyoginī tu nānāpravaktṛke kathānāmni kriyāvyatihāre pravartyaṃ vivecanīyaḥ /
tatra copālambhaparatvaṃ tasya /
evaṃ ca pravartanīyavivecanīyasiddhiparasāṅganyāyalakṣaṇaṃ prathamāhnikārthaḥ /
dvitīyāhnikārthastu pravartanavivecana upālambhaparapadārthalakṣaṇamiti yukta idānīṃ tasyārambhaḥ /
tatrāpi pravartyavivecanīyadvāreṇa pravṛttiprakāratvācca kathāyāḥ prathamaṃ kathāprakaraṇamārabhyate /
yadyapi ca kathā sākṣāt noddiṣṭā, tathāpyasaṃgatibhitā bhāṣyakāraḥ tadupasaṃgraheṇaiva vādādīn vibhajate /
anyathā hi vādādilakṣaṇasya pūrvāparaprakaraṇāpraveśāt āhnikāpraveśe śāstrabahirbhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
atha sūtrakṛtaiva kathā kathaṃ sākṣāt noddiṣṭa, vivakṣitaphale ekānekatvānurodhena sāmānyaviśeṣayoryathāyathamuddeśāt? tad yathā caturṣu pramaiva vivakṣitaṃ phalamiti pramāṇatvena, saiva dvādaśaviṣayiṇī vivakṣiteti prameyatvena, hānameva vivakṣitamiti sukhaṃ duḥkhatvena /
iha tu tattvanirṇayaḥ, jalpe svaśaktiparāśaktikhyāpanam, vitaṇḍāyāṃ parāśaktimātraprakhyāpanaṃ ca phalāni vivakṣitāni /
tāni ca na kathāmātrasādhyānīti viśeṣata evoddeśaḥ /
tatra yaugikaṃ kathāśabdamupādāyānavasaradusthatayā bhāṣyam ākṣipya vārttikena samādhatte---tadayuktamityādinā /
nāyaṃ kathāśabdo yogamātrānurodhī, api tu satyeva tasmin rūḍhiniyata iti /
anavasaradoṣaṃ pariharannāha---api tviti /
nanu pūrvapakṣottarapakṣabalābalanirūpaṇaṃ vicāraḥ, sa ca na kathāyā āśrayaḥ kiṃ tu viṣaya ityata āha---vicāraviṣayeti /
prauḍhagauḍanaiyāyikamate catasraḥ kathāḥ /
sa pratipakṣasthāpanāhīno vitaṇḍā /
ityatra jalpavad vādasyāpi parāmarśāt /
puruṣābhiprāyānurodhena caturthodāharaṇasyāpyupapatteriti sānātaniḥ /
eka evāyaṃ kathāmārga iti bāhyāḥ /
te dve api tisra eveti niyamayatā nirākṛte /
tattvabubhutsukathā ca vitaṇḍā ceti vyāhatam /
na hi prathamasādhananivṛttāveva tattvanirṇayaḥ, niḥsādhanasya tasyānupapatteḥ /
nāpi pratipakṣasādhanamanivartya prathamasya sādhanatvāvasthitiḥ, śaṅkitapratipakṣatvāt /
yadi tu pratipakṣasādhanamanirūpyaiva vijigīṣuvitaṇḍāvat tāvataiva vādinau kṛtinau, na tarhi tattvabubhūtsū /
evaṃ ca yadi vijigīṣuḥ, kathamapratibhādyanudbhāvanam /
na ca vijayatattvanirṇayābhyāṃ phalāntaramavaśiṣyate kathāyāḥ, yadarthaṃ vādavitaṇḍā /
children.translated_text: And no result of <s>kathā</s> remains beyond victory and the ascertainment of reality, for the sake of which <s>vāda</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> [would exist].

children.text: anutpannasya hi tattvanirṇayasyotpādanam, utpannasya pālanam, pālitasya ca viniyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the production of the ascertainment of reality that has not yet arisen, the protection of that which has arisen, and the application of that which has been protected —

children.text: sa ca svayamabhyāsaḥ, kāruṇikatayā paravyutpādanam /
children.translated_text: that [application] is practice for oneself, and, out of compassion, the instruction of others.

children.text: etacca sarvaṃ kathātrayaparyavasitam, nāpyekakathānirvāhyamiti //
children.translated_text: And all of this is encompassed by the three types of <s>kathā</s>, and cannot be accomplished by a single type of <s>kathā</s> alone.

Thus, in the first lesson, <s>Nyāya</s> with all its components and sub-components has been defined. And that [<s>Nyāya</s>], although for the sake of others, when practiced in investigation where a single speaker is the counterpart of questioning, is to be applied with discrimination. And therein, the orientation is toward establishment. But <s>Nyāya</s>, whose counterpart is the commencement of refutation, is to be applied and discriminated in the activity-exchange called <s>kathā</s> (debate), which has multiple speakers. And therein, its orientation is toward censure. And thus, the meaning of the first lesson is the definition of <s>Nyāya</s> with its components, oriented toward establishment, to be applied and discriminated. The meaning of the second lesson, then, is the definition of the categories relating to the application and discrimination, oriented toward censure — therefore its commencement is now appropriate. Therein too, since <s>kathā</s> (debate) is the mode of engagement through what is to be applied and discriminated, the section on <s>kathā</s> is commenced first. And although <s>kathā</s> is not directly enumerated [in the <s>sūtra</s>], nevertheless, fearing disconnection, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> classifies <s>vāda</s> and the rest through the subsumption of that [<s>kathā</s>] alone. For otherwise, since the definition of <s>vāda</s> and the rest would not enter into either the preceding or the following sections, if it did not enter into any lesson, the consequence would be its falling outside the <s>śāstra</s>. Now, if <s>kathā</s> was [intended] by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> himself, why was it not directly enumerated? — because, in accordance with the intended result being one or many, the general and the specific are enumerated as appropriate. Just as among the four [<s>pramāṇas</s>], valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) alone is the intended result — hence [they are enumerated] as <s>pramāṇas</s>; that very [valid cognition], having twelve objects, is intended — hence as <s>prameyas</s>; cessation alone is intended — hence pleasure as suffering. But here, the intended results are: in <s>vāda</s>, the ascertainment of reality; in <s>jalpa</s>, the display of one's own and the other's ability; and in <s>vitaṇḍā</s>, the display of the other's ability alone. And these are not achievable by mere <s>kathā</s> alone — therefore the enumeration is specifically [of the three types]. Therein, taking the etymological word '<s>kathā</s>' and objecting to the <s>Bhāṣya</s> as being without occasion [for this term], he resolves it with the <s>Vārttika</s>: 'that is unjustified...' and so forth. This word '<s>kathā</s>' does not follow mere etymology alone, but rather, even with that [etymology], is fixed by conventional usage — this is [the point]. Removing the fault of being without occasion, he says: 'but rather...' Now, the examination of the strength and weakness of the prima facie and conclusive views is investigation (<s>vicāra</s>) — and that is not the locus of <s>kathā</s>, but its object — to this he says: 'the object of investigation...' In the view of the mature <s>Gauḍa</s> <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, there are four types of <s>kathā</s>. 'That which lacks the establishment of the counter-thesis is <s>vitaṇḍā</s>' — here, since <s>vāda</s> too is referred to, like <s>jalpa</s>, [a fourth is possible]. Since, in accordance with the intention of the person, even a fourth example is tenable — thus [say] the traditionalists (<s>sānātanas</s>). 'This is the only path of <s>kathā</s>' — thus [say] the outsiders. They are refuted by one who restricts [the types] to 'these two are also just three.' And [the claim that] '<s>kathā</s> seeking to know reality is also <s>vitaṇḍā</s>' is contradictory. For the ascertainment of reality does not [occur] merely upon the cessation of the first proof — since that [reality], being without proof, is untenable. Nor does the first [proof] remain established as proof without refuting the counter-proof — because its counter-thesis is doubted. But if, without examining the counter-proof, the debaters consider themselves accomplished — as in desire-to-win <s>vitaṇḍā</s> — merely by that much, then they are not seekers of reality. And thus, if [they are] desirous of victory, how [can there be] the non-production of [the defeat-grounds such as] non-response and the like?

children.text:
nanvetāvatāpi na sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ vibhāvitamityata āha---tathā ceti /
nānāpravaktṛkā mithaḥ karmatayā yuddhavadāliṅganavacca /
etena vākyasaṃdṛbdhirmahāvākyamuktaṃ syāt, mithaḥ karmatayā sākāṅkṣatvāt, vijayādyanekaprayojanavattvācceti /
vaktrośca praśabdena prakarṣo darśitaḥ /
sa ca kathārūpamahāvākyanirvāhakatvam /
tathā ca svasthaḥ sarvañjanapratyayānapalāpī matamātrāvalambī avahito 'kalahakāraśceti kathādhikāriṇo darśitāḥ /
viparyayeṇa heyā iti /
vasatīti niruktibhaṅgabhayādāha---arthābhidhāneti vādeti /
anadhikāriṇo hātumiti bhāvaḥ /
te 'pi prakṛtoktiko 'vipralambhako yathākālasphūrtikaḥ anākṣepako yuktisiddhasaṃpratyayī ceti pañca vāde upādeyāḥ viparyayeṇa heyāḥ /
evaṃ bhūtāśca viṣyādaya eva prāyeṇeti ta evoktāḥ /
evaṃ ca sati heyān vihāya yo yathābhūtaḥ sa tathābhūtena vaktumarhati /
tathā sati kathā mahāvākyasiddhau phalasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: This being so, <s>kathā</s> [achieves its purpose] through the accomplishment of the great-sentence that results in the establishment of the result.

children.text: na hi yuyutsuriraṃsū pratipadya ciraṃ asiddhaṃ saṃbhūya samīhitaṃ sādhayataḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who desires to fight and one who desires to play, having engaged for a long time, do not accomplish together what is unaccomplished as the desired goal.

children.text: yathoddeśamiti /
children.translated_text: 'In the order of enumeration...'

children.text: tattvapratipattihetutvād vādasyādāvuddeśaḥ //
children.translated_text: Since <s>vāda</s> (honest debate) is the cause of the ascertainment of reality, it is enumerated first.

Now, even by this much, the general definition has not been elucidated — to this he says: 'and thus...' [<s>Kathā</s>] with multiple speakers, having mutual activity, is like a battle and also like an embrace. By this, a composition of sentences — a 'great sentence' (<s>mahāvākya</s>) — would be stated, because of having mutual activity and hence expectancy, and because of having multiple purposes such as victory and the like. And the excellence of the speaker is shown by the prefix '<s>pra</s>' — and that excellence is the capacity to carry out the great-sentence that is <s>kathā</s>. And thus, one who is composed, who does not deny what is known by all, who relies only on accepted views, who is attentive, who is non-quarrelsome — these are shown as the qualified participants in <s>kathā</s>. The opposite [qualities] are to be rejected. Lest there be fear of the destruction of the etymology, he says: 'the expression of meaning is <s>vāda</s>' — the purport being: to exclude the unqualified. And these too — five [qualities] are to be adopted in <s>vāda</s>: speaking about the topic at hand, non-deceptiveness, spontaneous expression at the proper time, non-offensiveness, and conviction established through reasoning — and the opposite [qualities] are to be rejected. And those who are such are, for the most part, just the disputants and the like — therefore only they are mentioned. And this being so, having set aside the rejectable [qualities], whoever is of a certain nature is fit to speak with one of a similar nature.

children.text:
vārttikamupaveśayituṃ pīṭhamāracayati---tadanavasāyāditi /
evamiti /
atideśārthamāha---na vicāramiti /
śrutivyavacchedyatayā vitaṇḍāṃ tāvad vyavacchinattiyadyapīti /
tātparyavyavacchedyatayā idānīṃ jalpaṃ vyavacchinatti---yadyapi ceti /
pramāṇamūlaiḥ pramāṇamūlābhimatairniyameneti śeṣaḥ /
nābhiprāyaniyamaḥ śrūyata ityata āha---yathā caitaditi /
sādhane ca tarkasya pramāṇāpekṣā, upālambhe tu kevalo 'pi samarthaḥ, pratitarkapratihatasyāsādhanatvāt /
āgāminaṃ bhāvasādhanatvasvīkāramiva dṛṣṭvā prāha---ubhayatheti /
tadgatākṣepastu uddeśa eva pramāṇatarkaśabdasya sādhanopālambhaśabdavat svavācakalakṣaṇayā vā, śabdāvāntaravyāpāratayā vā śabdapratipāditatayā vā samarthitaprāyaḥ /
tataḥ siddhavadāha---yada tviti /
aparādhapratipādanaṃ hyupālambhaḥ /
na ca acetano 'parādhyati, nāpi pratipādyate, kiṃ puruṣaḥ /
tadidamuktam---puruṣadharmopālambheti /
karmakaraṇayorhi pradhānavyāpāraḥ, phalamekameva /
taddvārā ca viṣayaḥ /
prakṛte karmakaraṇayorapi karmaiva /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ, yat karmatvadaśāyāṃ śabdāderanityatvaṃ dharmo karmakaraṇayorapi karmaiva /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ, yat karmatvadaśāyāṃ śabdāderanityatvaṃ dharmo jijñāsitatayā, viṣayatvadaśāyāṃ tu vastutayetyāśayavān yathāśrutavārttikānurodhena vyācaṣṭe---dharmīti /
anyathā tu viṣayaḥ śaktiviṣayaḥ śakyaṃ kāryamiti yāvadityevamapi sugamametat /
atra hi jalpe nigrahasthānaviniyogādityādibhāṣye na hiṃsyāt sarvabhūtāni /
itivad vāde sarvanigrahasthānapratiṣedhe agnīṣomīyaṃ paśumālabheta itivat siddhāntāviruddha ityādiviśeṣavidhirityarthaḥ /
sphuṭaḥ pratīyate /
vārtikakārastu rāgataḥ sarvapañcanakhabhakṣaṇaprāptivat upālambhagrahaṇāt sarvanigrahasthānaprāptau pañca pañcanakhā bhakṣyāḥ itivat parisaṃkhyānārthamuttarapadārambha iti vyākhyātavān /
tadetadatikuśalatayā mithaḥ avirodhayannāha---jalpa iti /
tathāpi niyamārthe ityasaṃgatam /
pākṣikavyavacchedaphalo hi niyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: for restriction has the result of excluding what is partial.

children.text: na cātrāpratibhādi pākṣikam, upālambhapadena nirāśaṅkameva pratipāditatvāt ityata āha---niyamaḥ parisaṃkhyeti /
children.translated_text: And here, non-response (<s>apratibhā</s>) and the like are not partial, since they are communicated without doubt by the word 'censure' — to this he says: 'Restriction means enumeration...'

children.text: ayamarthaḥ, yadyapi vidhiratyantamaprāptau niyamaḥ pākṣike sati /
