children.translated_text: The meaning is this: although an injunction [applies] in the case of complete non-obtainment, restriction [applies] when there is a partial [obtainment].

children.text: tatra cānyatra ca prāptau parisaṃkhyeti kīrtyate //
children.translated_text: And when there is obtainment both there and elsewhere, it is called enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>).

In order to introduce the <s>vārttika</s>, he constructs the platform: 'From the non-determination of that...' 'Thus...' He states it for the purpose of extension: 'Not investigation...' By way of excluding through <s>śruti</s> (literal meaning), he first excludes <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil): 'Although...' By way of excluding through purport, he now excludes <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling): 'And although...' 'By those rooted in <s>pramāṇa</s>' — the remainder is: 'necessarily by those accepted as rooted in <s>pramāṇa</s>.' [If one objects:] no restriction of intention is heard — to this he says: 'And as this...' And <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) depends on <s>pramāṇa</s> in proof, but in censure it is capable even by itself, since what is countered by a counter-reasoning is not a proof. Seeing as if the future acceptance of proof-through-existence [is coming], he says: 'In both ways...' But the objection directed toward that — whether the word '<s>pramāṇatarka</s>' in the enumeration, like the words 'proof and censure,' is [to be explained] by indirect indication of its own denotation, or by way of a sub-operation of the word, or by way of being communicated by the word — has been mostly established. Therefore he speaks as if it were settled: 'But when...' For censure is the communication of fault. And what is non-conscious does not commit fault, nor is [a fault] communicated [about it]; rather, it is a person [who does so]. This is what was stated: 'Censure of a person's property...' For with respect to the object and the instrument, the principal operation [is the same], and the result is one and the same. And through that, the object [is determined]. In the topic at hand, even of the object and instrument, it is the object alone [that is primary]. But the distinction is this: in the state of being the object, the impermanence of sound and the like is a property as something to be investigated; but in the state of being the object [of another operation], it is as a real thing — with this intention, in accordance with the <s>vārttika</s> as literally read, he explains: 'The property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>)...' Otherwise, the object [means] the object of capacity, i.e. the possible effect — even thus this is easily understood. Here, in the <s>bhāṣya</s> [passage] 'in debate, the application of points of defeat' and the like — just as 'one should not harm any living being' [is a general prohibition], so in debate, when there is a general prohibition of all points of defeat, 'one possessed of five members and not contradicting established conclusions' [is a specific rule] — just as 'one should sacrifice the animal to <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>' — the meaning is that this is a specific injunction. [This] is clearly understood. But the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, out of attachment, explained: just as from the consumption of all five-clawed animals [being generally permitted], [the specific rule] 'five five-clawed animals may be eaten' serves as an enumeration — so too the subsequent clause serves as enumeration when all points of defeat are obtained from the word 'censure.' Harmonizing both [interpretations] with great skill without mutual contradiction, he says: 'Debate (<s>jalpa</s>)...' Even so, [saying] 'in the sense of restriction' is inappropriate,

children.text:
iti bhedo darśitaḥ, tathāpyalpīyānayamiti manyamānena parisaṃkhyāyāmapi niyamapadaṃ prayujyate, itaravyavacchedalakṣaṇasya phalasyāviśiṣṭatvāditi /
iha vāde caturdhā nigrahasthānagatiḥ /
kiñcidasaṃbhāvanīyameva yathā, hāniḥ sannyāso nirarthakamarthāntaramavijñātārthamapārthakamiti ṣaṭkam /
kiñcit saṃbhavadapyanudbhāvyameva yathā, pratijñāntaraṃ hetvantaramajñānamapratibhā vikṣepo matānujñā paryanuyojyopekṣaṇamiti saptakam /
kiñcit tūdbhāvyamātraṃ yathā, virodho 'prāptakālaṃ nyūnamadhikaṃ punaruktamayathānubhāṣaṇamapasiddhānta iti saptakam /
kiñcicca kathāvasānikaṃ yathā, hetvābhāso niranuyojyānuyogaśceti dvayamiti /
tatra hānyādīnāmaśaktisaṃguhanaprakāratvāt, tattvabubhutsutayā ca vāde tadabhāvāt teṣāmasaṃbhavaḥ /
saṃbhavatāmanudbhāvane hetumāha---na khalviti /
kathāmaparyavasāyayatāmapyudbhāvane hetumāha---adhikaṃ tviti /
tattvapratipatteḥ sākṣād vyāghāto viparītapratipattiryathā, hetvābhāsānudbhāvane niranuyojyānuyogānudbhāvane ca pāramparyavyāghāto vyāsaṅgādīnā tatsāmagrīpratirodhaḥ /
tatrādhikānudbhāvane prathamo yadi na syāt, tathāpi dvitīyaḥ syādeva /
tathā hi, virodhe yogyatāvirahaḥ /
aprāptakāle ākāṅkṣāvirahaḥ /
nyūne ākāṅkṣitāsamabhivyāhāraḥ /
sa cānāsaktiviśeṣaḥ /
adhike anākāṅkṣitasamabhivyāhāraḥ /
punarukte 'pyevam /
so 'pyākāṅkṣāvirahaviśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: and that too is a specific kind of absence of expectancy.

children.text: ayathānubhāṣaṇe uktāpratisandhānam /
children.translated_text: In incoherent restatement, failure to connect what was stated.

children.text: apasiddhānte saṃmukhapramāṇabādhākrāntiriti ākāṅkṣāyogyatāsattimattayā pratisaṃhitaṃ pramāṇāntarāpratihataṃ ca vākyaṃ tattvapratipatteraṅgam, nānyathā /
children.translated_text: In counter-established conclusion, being overwhelmed by direct <s>pramāṇa</s>-sublation — thus a sentence that is properly connected, possessing expectancy, fitness, and contiguity, and not impeded by another <s>pramāṇa</s>, is a component of the apprehension of truth, and not otherwise.

children.text: tasmādetadarthamidamudbhāvyamiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for this purpose, this is to be demonstrated.

Thus the distinction has been shown; nevertheless, considering this [distinction] to be minor, the word 'restriction' is used even for enumeration, since the result — characterized by the exclusion of the other — is not different. Here, in debate, the application of points of defeat is fourfold. Some [points of defeat] are simply inconceivable, namely the six: abandonment [of the thesis], renunciation, meaninglessness, irrelevancy, unintelligibility, and purposelessness. Some, though possible, are simply not to be demonstrated, namely the seven: shifting the thesis, shifting the reason, ignorance, non-response, evasion, admission of the opponent's view, and neglecting what should be cross-questioned. Some are merely to be demonstrated, namely the seven: contradiction, untimeliness, deficiency, redundancy, repetition, incoherent restatement, and counter-established conclusion. And some [mark] the conclusion of the discussion, namely the two: fallacious reason and cross-questioning what need not be questioned. Among these, abandonment and the like — since they are modes of concealing incapacity — and since in debate, due to the desire to know the truth, they are absent, their occurrence is impossible. He states the reason for not demonstrating those that are possible: 'For indeed...' He states the reason for demonstrating those that do not conclude the discussion: 'But additionally...' Direct contradiction with the apprehension of truth is the contrary apprehension — as when fallacious reasons are not demonstrated and when what need not be questioned is not cross-questioned — there is indirect contradiction: the obstruction of the causal complex through attachment and the like. Therein, even if the first [kind of contradiction] were absent when the additional [points] are not demonstrated, the second would certainly obtain. Namely: in contradiction, absence of fitness; in untimeliness, absence of expectancy; in deficiency, non-co-statement of what is expected;

children.text:
tadetat sarvamabhiprāyaṃ niyamayataḥ sūtrakārasya saṃmataṃ sūtrādeva ca labhyate /
vārttikakṛtā tu nyūnādicatuṣṭayamudāharaṇārthaṃ darśitam, na tu niyamaḥ kṛta iti vyājena darśayati---tathā ceti /
nanu vyatisaṅgo vyatihāraḥ /
sa ca sādhanopalambhavānityetāvataivokte gamyate /
tataḥ pramāṇatarkagrahaṇamatiricyata ityata āha---pūrvasminniti /
tathāpyasmin pakṣe kimasya prayojanamityata āha---sādhanopālambhaviśeṣaṇāya ceti /
anuvidheyastheyasabhyapuruṣavatī janatā sabhetyucyate /
tatrānuvidheyasya yathāśakti yathāniyamaṃ saṃmānāsaṃmānavyañjakaṃ karma /
naitad vāde /
tatra hi tattvabubhutsutayā svayamavātattvajñaḥ tattvajñāninamupāsīta /
stheyānāṃ tu vādasthānakathāviśeṣavyavasthāpanaṃ pūrvottaravādasthāpanaṃ vivadamānayorguṇadoṣāvadhāraṇaṃ bhagnaprativādiprabodhanaṃ loke niṣpannakathāphalapratipādanaṃ ca karmāṇi /
etadarthaṃ ca tatra prāśnikopayogo yad vādinau kāraṇagraheṇa evaṃ kartumaśaktau /
na caivaṃ vāde /
children.translated_text: But this is not so in debate (<s>vāda</s>).

children.text: tatra tayoreva vītarāgatayā śaktatvādityāśayavānāha---na vāde prāśnikānāmiti /
children.translated_text: Since there, because of their dispassion, both [debaters] are themselves capable — with this intention he says: 'In debate, the assessors are not [needed]...'

children.text: tat kiṃ parivarjanameva tatra teṣām? netyāha---daivāgatānāṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: Then is there complete exclusion of them there? He says no: 'But of those who come by chance...'

children.text: savādenaprāmādikakathābhāsaśaṅkāmapanetuṃ natūktakarmāṇi kārayitumiti bhāvaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: to remove the suspicion that the discussion along with the debate is a non-genuine semblance of discussion due to carelessness, but not to make them perform the stated duties.

All this is the intention of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> who restricts [the points of defeat], and it is obtainable from the <s>sūtra</s> itself. But the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> showed the four — deficiency and the like — as illustrations, and did not make a restriction — he shows this by way of a pretext: 'And thus...' Now, <s>vyatisaṅga</s> (engagement) means exchange. And that is conveyed by saying merely 'possessing proof and censure.' Therefore the mention of '<s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>' is superfluous — to this he says: 'In the prior...' Even so, what is the purpose of this [mention] in this interpretation? — to this he says: 'And for qualifying proof and censure...' A gathering that has persons who are followers, presiders, and assessors is called an assembly (<s>sabhā</s>). Among these, the follower's duty is to express approval or disapproval according to ability and according to rule. This is not [so] in debate. For there, one who is himself ignorant of the truth, desiring to know the truth, would approach one who knows the truth. But the duties of the presiders are: establishing the particular types of debate, establishing the previous and subsequent debate-positions, ascertaining the merits and faults of the disputants, enlightening the defeated opponent, and communicating to the public the result of the completed discussion. And for this purpose, the use of assessors (<s>prāśnika</s>) is there [in jalpa], because the debaters are unable to do this through their own apprehension of reasons.

children.text: yathoktopapannaśchalajātinigrahasthānasādhanopālambho jalpaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: Wrangling (<s>jalpa</s>) is proof and censure as described, together with sophistry (<s>chala</s>), futile rejoinder (<s>jāti</s>), and points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>). // [Sūtra] 1 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
ubhayasādhanavattvasādharmyād vādānantaraṃ jalpoddeśasiddhiḥ /
tatsiddhau satyāṃ saṃgatim āha---uddeśeti /
nanu jalpasyobhayasādhanavattvāsaṃbhavānna vitaṇḍāvyavacchedaḥ /
tathā hi yadi pūrvasādhanaṃ dūṣitam, nigṛhītastarhi vādī, jitaṃ dvitīyena /
nivṛttā kathā /
na dūṣitaṃ cet---uttarābhāsavacanena cāvacanena ca nigṛhītastarhi dvitīyo, jitaṃ prathamena, nivṛttā katheti nāsti dvitīyasādhanāvasara iti /
naitadevam /
yathā hi vāde svasādhanasthitau parasādhananivṛttau ca tattvanirṇayo na viparyaye, tathā jalpe 'pi svasādhanasthitau parasādhananivṛttau ca vijayo viparyaye bhaṅgaḥ /
ubhayasthitinivṛttyoḥ pariṣadeva vijayate /
tadayaṃ jalprapavṛttikramaḥ vādini sādhanamātraṃ prayujya saṃkṣepato vistarato vā ābhāsān uddhṛtya virate sati ucyamānagrāhyanigrahāprāptau ābhāsabahiruktagrāhyanigrahālābhe tadvacanārthamavagamyānūdya dūṣayitvā prativādīsvapakṣe sthāpanāṃ prayuñjīta /
aprayuñjānastu dūṣitaparapakṣo 'pi navijayī /
ślādhyastu syādātmānamarakṣan paraghātīva vīraḥ /
tasminnapyevaṃ virate sati anuktocyamānagrāhyanigrahālābhe tadvavacanamavagamyānūdya dūṣaṇāṅgaṃ prati dūṣyābhāsabahiruktagrāhyanigrahālābheda prathamavādī sthāpanāṃśaṃ dūṣayet /
adūṣayaṃsatu rakṣitasvapakṣo 'pi na vijayī /
ślādhyastu syāt vañcitaparaprahāra iva tamapraharamāṇaḥ /
anuktocyamānagrāhyābhāsabahiruktagrāhyanigrahalābhe tu tāvataiva kathāviratirna sādhanavicārāvakārśaḥ /
śarasandhānasamaya eva yo mūrcchitaḥ tadvāṇavāraṇatatpraharaṇānuṣṭhānavad viphalatvāt /
tatrānuktagrāhyamapratibhādi /
ucyamānagrāhyamaprāptakālādi /
ābhāsabahiruktagrāhyaṃ pratijñāvirodhādi /
children.translated_text: The semblance-external-stated-graspable are contradiction with the thesis and the like.

children.text: eṣvasatsu ābhāsacintā /
children.translated_text: In the absence of these, the examination of semblances [takes place].

children.text: tataḥ punaḥ pratidūṣaṇoktau ābhāsabahiḥpratijñāhānyādi /
children.translated_text: Then again, when counter-refutation is stated, semblance-external [points of defeat such as] abandonment of the thesis and the like [apply].

children.text: etacca pañcame prapañcanīyamiti //
children.translated_text: And this is to be elaborated in the fifth [section].

Because of the similarity of possessing both proofs [i.e., proof and censure], the definition of <s>jalpa</s> comes immediately after <s>vāda</s>. When that is established, he states the connection: 'Enumeration...' Now, the exclusion of <s>vitaṇḍā</s> is not [achieved] by the possession of both proofs in <s>jalpa</s> — for if the prior proof is refuted, the proponent is defeated, the second [debater] has won, and the discussion is concluded. If not refuted, then by uttering a semblance of a reply or by silence, the second [debater] is defeated, the first has won, and the discussion is concluded — so there is no occasion for a second proof. This is not so. For just as in debate, when one's own proof stands firm and the opponent's proof is refuted, truth is determined, but not in the reverse case — so too in <s>jalpa</s>, when one's own proof stands firm and the opponent's proof is refuted, there is victory; in the reverse, defeat. When both stand firm or both are refuted, the assembly alone decides the victor. This then is the procedure of <s>jalpa</s>: the proponent, having adduced merely the proof, and having extracted the semblances briefly or in detail, when he pauses — when there is no obtainment of a stated-graspable point of defeat and no obtainment of a semblance-external-stated-graspable point of defeat — having understood and restated the meaning of that statement, having refuted it, the respondent should adduce the establishment of his own position. But one who does not adduce [his own position], even though he has refuted the opponent's position, is not victorious — though he would be praiseworthy, like a hero who strikes the enemy without protecting himself. When that [respondent] too pauses in the same way — when there is no obtainment of an unstated-being-stated-graspable point of defeat and no obtainment of a semblance-external-stated-graspable point of defeat relating to the censure-component — the first debater should refute the establishment-portion. But one who does not refute, even though he has defended his own position, is not victorious — though he would be praiseworthy, like one who does not strike an opponent whose blow has been parried. But when there is obtainment of an unstated-being-stated-graspable or semblance-external-stated-graspable point of defeat, the discussion concludes with that much alone — there is no occasion for the examination of proofs. Like one who faints at the very moment of fitting the arrow — [any response] is fruitless, like warding off his arrow and striking him. Among these, the unstated-graspable [points of defeat] are non-response (<s>apratibhā</s>) and the like. The being-stated-graspable are untimeliness (<s>aprāptakāla</s>) and the like.

children.text:
yadyapi nigrahasthānapadenāviśeṣāt sarvaprāptau siddhāntāviruddhaḥ pañcāvayavopapanna iti padadvayātideśo mandaḥ, tathāpi gorbalīvardanyāyenāpi yathāśrutabhāṣyopapattau kṛtaṃ tadbhāṅgeneti manyamāno bhāṣyaṃ vārttikena samañjasayannāha---uktamātramityādi /
yadyapyaparādhasaṃgūhanārthaṃ pratijñāhānipratijñāntarapratijñāsaṃnyāsahetvantarārthāntaranirarthakāvijñātārthavikṣepāpasiddhāntānāmupādānaṃ saṃbhavati, tathāpi na sarvanigrahopādānasaṃbhavaḥ /
api ca pramādaskhalite 'pi chalādibhireva pratyavasthātumucitam, nigrahasthānāpekṣayā teṣāmanudbhaṭāparādhatvāt /
tasmādudbhāvyatayaivāmīṣāṃ sarveṣāmavatāraḥ /
tathā ca nāyuktatvamityabhiprāyavānāha---tat kimiti /
sādhusādhanopādāne ca vādinā kṛta ityupalakṣaṇam /
pareṇa sādhusādhanopādāne ca kṛta ityapi draṣṭavyam /
nanu bhāṣyaṃ dūṣayitvā kimadhikamamihitam? tenāpi tattvarakṣaṇārthatvapratipādanādityata āha---tadanena prakāreṇeti /
children.translated_text: Now, what more is intended beyond refuting the <s>bhāṣya</s>? Since even by that [interpretation], the communication of the purpose of protecting truth [is achieved] — to this he says: 'By this method, then...'

children.text: prakāre bhāṣyam asaṃgatam, na tu prayojane /
children.translated_text: The <s>bhāṣya</s> is inappropriate in method, but not in purpose.

children.text: tatastadapyevameva neyamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even that should be interpreted in just this way.

children.text: chalādivyutpādanaṃ prayojyatayeti śeṣaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: The remainder is: the explanation of sophistry (<s>chala</s>) and the like is as what is to be employed.

Although from the word 'point of defeat,' because of non-specification, all [points of defeat] are obtained, and therefore the extension of the two phrases 'not contradicting established conclusions' and 'endowed with five members' is weak — nevertheless, thinking that even by the maxim of 'cow-and-bull,' when the <s>bhāṣya</s> as literally read is supportable, there is no need to break it — harmonizing the <s>bhāṣya</s> with the <s>vārttika</s>, he says: 'Merely stated...' and so forth. Although the adoption of abandonment of the thesis, shifting the thesis, renunciation of the thesis, shifting the reason, irrelevancy, meaninglessness, unintelligibility, evasion, and counter-established conclusion is possible for the purpose of concealing faults — nevertheless, the adoption of all points of defeat is not possible. Moreover, even when one slips through carelessness, it is appropriate to respond with sophistry (<s>chala</s>) and the like, since those [slips] are faults not brought forth in comparison to points of defeat. Therefore, the entry of all of these is only as things to be demonstrated. And thus there is no impropriety — with this intention he says: 'Then what...' And 'when the proponent has adopted a sound proof' is indicative — 'when the opponent too has adopted a sound proof' should also be understood.

children.text: sa pratipakṣasthāpanāhīno vitaṇḍā //3 //
children.translated_text: That [debate] which lacks the establishment of the counter-position is <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil). // [Sūtra] 3 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
nanu vitaṇḍāyāḥ pratipakṣasthāpanāhīnatvamasaṃgatam, ekasādhanatāyāṃ puruṣaśakterapyanirūpaṇāt /
tathātve vā kṛtaṃ jalpena prayāsabahulena, antataḥ satpratipakṣatayāpi dvitīyasādhanapraveśāt /
naitadevam, puruṣaśaktinirūpaṇāviśeṣe 'pi jalpe pratyavekṣāparāghātobhayagocaraśaktinirūpaṇāt, kṛtavidyakṣatriyadvayayuddhavat /
vitaṇḍāyāṃ tu daśarathadaśānanatanayatamasivamīyuddhavat, kākolūkayuddhavad vā /
ekasya svapratyavekṣāśaktiraparasya parāghātanaipuṇaṃ nirūpyate /
kathamayaṃ viśeṣa iti cet? vādinorabhiprāyavaśādanuvidheyastheyānurodhāt veti na kiñcidetat dvitīyasādhanapraveśasatu dūṣaṇatayā na pratiṣidhyate /
api tu sthāpanātvena /
na cāyaṃ niyamaḥ, asiddhatvādudbhāvanenāpi kathāparyavasānāditi, samākhyānirvacanasāmarthyāt eva gamyata iti /
children.translated_text: And this restriction [does not hold], since even by raising the charge of non-establishment the debate can conclude — this is understood from the very force of the etymological derivation of the term.

children.text: na caivamastviti vācyam, jalpe 'pi parapakṣāghātasya gatatvenātivyāpakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor should one say 'let it be so,' because in <s>jalpa</s> too, since the striking of the opponent's thesis is already included, there would be over-extension.

children.text: mātragrahaṇāt tu tannivṛttiriti cet---na, tena sādhanānivṛtteḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one objects] that the exclusion of that [over-extension] is by the word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>) — no, because that would not exclude the proof [component].

children.text: tatra sādhanopālambhasamudāye dūṣaṇamātraṃ vitaṇḍetyevamapyupapatteriti //3 //
children.translated_text: Even with the interpretation that in the collection of proof and censure, refutation alone constitutes <s>vitaṇḍā</s>, the account is coherent. // 3 //

Now, the characterization of <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive debate) as lacking counter-thesis establishment is inconsistent, since even in establishing a single proof, the capacity of the person is not ascertained. Or if that were so, then the effort-laden <s>jalpa</s> (disputatious debate) would be rendered purposeless, since even through the status of a counter-argument, the entry of a second proof [is possible]. This is not so, because even though there is no difference in ascertaining the capacity of the person, in <s>jalpa</s> the capacity pertaining to both self-examination and striking the opponent is ascertained — like a battle between two trained warriors. But in <s>vitaṇḍā</s>, it is like the battle of the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> and <s>Daśānana</s> (ten-headed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>) in the <s>Tamasī</s> episode, or like the battle of crows and owls. The self-examination capacity of one and the skill in striking of the other are ascertained. If one asks how this distinction [obtains], it is because [the distinction] follows from the intentions of the debaters, in accordance with the rules that must be followed — this amounts to nothing. The entry of a second proof in that [vitaṇḍā] is not prohibited as refutation, but rather as [counter-]establishment.

children.text: // iti kathālakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // Thus ends the section on the definition of debate (<s>kathālakṣaṇa</s>) //

children.text: // hetvābhāsalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // The section on the definition of fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsalakṣaṇa</s>) //

children.text: // pariśuddhi //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
evaṃ kathāprakaraṇaṃ samarthimatam /
tasyāśca śarīraṃ sādhanaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ ca /
tatra sādhanavādinā prathamatastadābhāsaparihāre dūṣaṇavādināpi saduttaraparigrahe yatnavatā bhavitavyam /
saduttarālābhe hi asaduttarāvatāra iti śikṣārthaṃ hetvābhāsāḥ prathamaṃ chalādibhya uddiṣṭā iti saiva saṃgatirihāpītyāha---uddeśeti /
atra triṣoḍaśyāṃ vyāpakāvyāpakabhedena yā dviṣoḍaśī sā asiddhaviśeṣaṇāsiddhaviśeṣyā samarthaviśeṣaṇā samarthaviśeṣyasandigdhaviśeṣaṇasandigdhaviśeṣyabhedena vivakṣitā dvānavataṃ śataṃ bhavatīti /
saivāsiddhisandehayorvādiprativādisaṃbandhādaṣṭāviṃśataṃ śataṃ bhavet /
saivānyatarāsiddhyā vyadhikaraṇasamarthasandigdhaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhedāt dvāvanataṃ śatamaparaṃ syāt /
saivomayānyatarāśrayāsiddhaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṃbandhādaparamaṣṭāviṃśataṃ śataṃ bhavet /
saivāśrayāsiddhaviśeṣaṇāvyadhikaraṇāsamarthasandigdhaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṃbandhādaparaṃ dvānavataṃ śatam /
saiva sandigdhavyadhikaraṇāsamarthasandigdhaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṃbandhādaparaṃ dvānavataṃ śatam /
iyamevāśrayāsiddhiprakṣepeṇāparaṃ dvānavataṃ śatam /
saiva sandigdhatāṃ parityajyānyathāsiddhimupādāyāparaṃ dvānavataṃ śatam /
iyamevāśrayāsiddhiprakṣepeṇāparaṃ dvānavataṃ śantam /
saivānyathāsiddhiṃ vihāya viruddhatāmupādāyāparaṃ dvānavataṃ śatam /
atraiva punarāśrayāsiddhiṃ prakṣipyāparaṃ dvānavataṃ śatam iti /
so 'yamasiddhaviruddhānaikāntikānāṃ prapañcaḥ /
prakaraṇasamaṃ prapañcayituṃ vastugatiṃ tāvadāhetyāha---tanneti /
children.translated_text: To elaborate on the <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (counterbalanced reason), he first states the actual state of affairs, saying: 'That not...'

children.text: antata iti /
children.translated_text: 'At the very least' —

children.text: agṛhyamāṇaviśeṣadaśāyāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: meaning: in the stage where the distinction is not apprehended.

children.text: kālātyayāpadiṣṭastūddeśa eva prapañcitaḥ iti //
children.translated_text: But the <s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s> (reason vitiated by temporal lapse) has been elaborated in the very enumeration.

Thus the section on debate has been validated. And its body consists of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) and refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>). Therein, one stating a proof must first be diligent in avoiding its semblances, and one stating a refutation must be diligent in accepting [only] valid replies. For when a valid reply is not obtained, an invalid reply enters — therefore, for the purpose of instruction, the fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) were enumerated before <s>chala</s> (equivocation) and the like. That very connection [applies] here too — he says: 'The enumeration...' Here, within the set of thirteen, when distinguished by the pervading and the pervaded, the set of twelve [becomes]: with the distinction of unestablished-qualifier, unestablished-qualificand, competent-qualifier, competent-qualificand, doubtful-qualifier, and doubtful-qualificand, [these] become one hundred and ninety-two. That same [set], with the relation of the proponent and opponent regarding non-establishment and doubt, becomes one hundred and twenty-eight. That same [set], with the addition of one-sided non-establishment and the distinction of non-co-located competent and doubtful qualifier and qualificand, becomes another one hundred and ninety-two. That same [set], with the relation of both-sided and one-sided substratum-unestablished qualifier and qualificand, becomes another one hundred and twenty-eight. That same [set], with the relation of substratum-unestablished qualifier and non-co-located incompetent and doubtful qualifier and qualificand, becomes another one hundred and ninety-two. That same [set], with the relation of doubtful non-co-located incompetent and doubtful qualifier and qualificand, becomes another one hundred and ninety-two. This very [set], with the addition of substratum-non-establishment, becomes another one hundred and ninety-two. That same [set], abandoning doubt and adopting otherwise-establishment, becomes another one hundred and ninety-two. This very [set], with the addition of substratum-non-establishment, becomes another one hundred and ninety-two. That same [set], abandoning otherwise-establishment and adopting contradictoriness, becomes another one hundred and ninety-two. And here again, adding substratum-non-establishment, another one hundred and ninety-two. This is the elaboration of non-established, contradictory, and inconclusive [reasons].

children.text:
atra cātītakālo mandatamaprayogaḥ, kālābhāvāt /
yasya hyavasaro nāsti, tasyārthakriyā prati vicārataḥ sattvaṃ nāstīti /
mandataraprayogastvasiddhaḥ, sati svakāle svayamevābhāvāt /
yastu svayameva nāsti, tasya deśakālāvasthāvirodhasāmarthānāṃ nāvakāśaḥ /
mandaprayogastu satpratipakṣaḥ, satoḥ kāladeśavattvayoravasthābhāvāt /
avasthābhāve 'virodhasāmarthyayoranavakāśāt /
sāvakāśaprayogastu viruddhaḥ, kāladeśāvasthāsu satīṣu virodhāt /
yastvevaṃ tasya kutaḥ sāmarthyam? prāyaḥprayogastu savyabhicāraḥ, kāladeśāvasthāvirodheṣu satsu sāmarthyamātrābhāvādityanena hetunā savyabhicārādikramoddeśaḥ /
yad vā sugrahaḥ savyabhicāraḥ, vicchedamātrasiddhau tatsiddheḥ, upadarśitaviparītagrahaṇe tatsiddhiḥ /
yatnagrāhyo vireddhaḥ /
atiyatnagrāhyaḥ prakaraṇasamaḥ, taditarasamastarūpasampannamanyadapanīya tatsiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (counterbalanced reason) requires excessive effort to grasp, since its establishment [comes] from removing something else that possesses all the forms of everything other than that [reason].

children.text: durgraho 'siddhaḥ, asiddhāśrayo 'pi kaścit heturiti paramatanirākaraṇāvaṣṭambhena tatsiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished reason) is hard to grasp, since its establishment [comes] from relying on the refutation of the opponent's doctrine, [given] that even some reason with an unestablished substratum [may appear valid].

children.text: durgrahataraḥ kālātyayāpadiṣṭaḥ, bādhakasyānanyathāsiddhyā prāmāṇyaṃ vyavasthāpya tatsiddheriti /
children.translated_text: The <s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s> (reason vitiated by temporal lapse) is harder yet to grasp, since its establishment [comes] from first establishing the authority [of the invalidating cognition] through the non-otherwise-establishability of the invalidator.

children.text: tadvivakṣayā kramaniyama iti //4 //
children.translated_text: With the intention of [showing] that, the restriction of order [is established]. // 4 //

And here, the past tense [indicates] the weakest application, because of the absence of [the right] time. For that which has no occasion — its existence with respect to efficacious action does not hold upon examination. But the weaker application is the unestablished [reason], since at its own proper time it does not itself exist. And that which does not itself exist — for it there is no scope for the capacities of place, time, and state, or for non-contradiction. The weak application, however, is the <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counterbalanced reason), because for the two that exist, there is no [relevant] state despite having time and place. In the absence of state, there is no scope for non-contradiction and competence. The application with scope, however, is the <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory reason), because of contradiction when time, place, and state are present. But for one that is of this nature, whence [comes] competence? The predominant application, however, is the <s>savyabhicāra</s> (inconclusive reason), because when there is contradiction of time, place, and state, there is merely the absence of competence — by this reasoning, the enumeration in the order of inconclusive and the like [is established]. Alternatively, the <s>savyabhicāra</s> is easy to grasp, since its establishment is accomplished by the mere establishment of deviation, [and] its establishment [comes] from the apprehension of the contrary as demonstrated. The <s>viruddha</s> requires effort to grasp.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
nanu vibhāgasūtre savyabhicāra ityuddiṣṭaṃ padamiha māṣyakāro lakṣaṇatvenaiva vyācaṣṭe /
evaṃ coddiṣṭaṃ na lakṣitam, lakṣitaṃ ca noddiṣṭamityata āha---atra ceti /
tathāpi lakṣaṇe vaktavye padaniruktiḥ kvopayujyate ityata āha---etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
kiṃ tvekasminnante yo niyata iti anvayato vyatirekato vā sādhyenaiva sahacarito dṛṣṭa ityarthaḥ /
tadviparyayādanaikāntiko 'niyataḥ sādhyenaiva sahito na dṛṣṭaḥ /
ubhayapakṣagāmīti yāvaditi ubhayapakṣaprasañjaka ityarthaḥ /
etena sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇānupasaṃhāryāḥ saṃgṛhītā iti sphuṭam /
bodhābhāsaprasañjitāmativyāptimanena vyākhyānena vyudastāmāha---na caivaṃbhūtā /
etacca tatra tatra vakṣyate /
tadevamiti /
anaikāntikapadavat savyabhicārapadamapi vyākhyeyamityarthaḥ /
nanvetāvataiva sarvaṃ vyākhyātam, tat kimaparamavaśiṣyate yadarthaṃ sarvo 'yamityādi vārtikamityata āha---avagatam iti /
na nu anyatra prameyāditi asaṃgatam /
sādhyatadviparyayau hyantadvayam /
na ca tadasya nāsti /
athāyamarthaḥ, na tatrāyamanvayato vyatirekato vā niyata iti /
tathāpi nāyamevaivaṃbhūtaḥ, sarveṣāmevānaikāntikānāmevaṃrūpatvāt /
tadasyaiva varjanamanupapannam /
udāharaṇamātrārthatvānna doṣa ityapi na yuktam, nityaścānityaścetyādisaṃgrāhyakoṭāvanaikāntikasyāpradarśanādityata āha---prameyapadārthasya tviti /
tadayaṃ vārttikārthaḥ, kaścid dharmaḥ sarvasyaprameyatvādilakṣaṇaḥ, kaścit kasyacideva nityatvādilakṣaṇaḥ /
tatra sarvasya vā kasyacid vā yo dharmo hetutayopātta ubhāvantau sādhyadharmatadviparyayau āśritya prasajya pravartate dharmiṇi so 'naikāntika iti /
vyatirekyavyatirekitayā dharmadvaividhyapradarśanenānaikāntikasya viṣayavivecanaṃ sūcitam /
vyatirekiṇyeva hi dharme sādhye 'naikāntikaḥ saṃbhavatprayogo na tvavyatirekiṇi /
na nu paryudāsābhiprāyeṇaiva prāk vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: Now, was this not previously explained with the intention of nominal negation (<s>paryudāsa</s>)?

children.text: tat kathaṃ tatpratiṣedha ityata āha---paryudāsapakṣa iti /
children.translated_text: Then how is that negated? — to this he says: 'The <s>paryudāsa</s> alternative...'

children.text: tathāpi nābrāhmaṇa iti prasajyapratiṣedhodāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: Even so, '<s>abrāhmaṇa</s>' (non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>) is an example of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (verbally-bound negation).

children.text: na hi goghaṭādāvabrāhmaṇa iti vaktāro bhavanti, api tu kṣatriyādāvityāha---na punarityādi subodham //5 //
children.translated_text: For people do not use '<s>abrāhmaṇa</s>' with respect to cows, pots, and the like, but rather with respect to <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and the like — he says: 'But not...' and so on. This is easily understood. // 5 //

Now, the word <s>savyabhicāra</s> (inconclusive) that was enumerated in the division-<s>sūtra</s> is here explained by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) as being itself the definition. And thus what was enumerated is not defined, and what is defined was not enumerated — to this he says: 'And here...' Even so, when a definition is to be stated, where is the etymological explanation of the word useful? — to this he says: 'What has been said amounts to this...' Rather: one that is restricted to one side — meaning one observed as accompanying only the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), either through positive or negative concomitance. By the converse of that, the <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive) is unrestricted — not observed as accompanying only the probandum. 'Going to both sides' means 'applicable to both alternatives' — this is the meaning. By this, the <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (common), <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon), and <s>anupasaṃhārya</s> (unsubsumable) [inconclusives] are clearly included. He states that the over-extension, which would make it applicable to semblances of cognition, is removed by this interpretation: 'And not of such a nature...' And this will be stated in the respective places. 'That being so' — the meaning is that the word <s>savyabhicāra</s> too, like the word <s>anaikāntika</s>, should be so interpreted. Now, if everything has been explained by just this much, then what more remains for which the entire <s>vārttika</s> beginning with 'all this' was composed? — to this he says: 'It is understood...' Now, [the objection] 'elsewhere than in the knowable (<s>prameya</s>)' is incoherent. For the <s>sādhya</s> and its contrary are the two sides. And it is not the case that [the reason] does not have those. If then the meaning is 'it is not restricted there either through positive or negative concomitance' — even so, this one alone is not of such a nature, since all <s>anaikāntikas</s> are of that form. Therefore the exclusion of this one alone is unjustified. Nor is it right [to say] it is merely for the sake of an example, since in the alternative to be included — 'both eternal and non-eternal' and the like — the <s>anaikāntika</s> has not been shown — to this he says: 'But of the category <s>prameya</s> (knowable)...' The meaning of the <s>vārttika</s> is this: some property, such as knowability, belongs to everything; some property, such as eternality, belongs to certain things only. Among these, a property adopted as a reason — whether it is of everything or of certain things — that operates by applying to both sides, namely the probandum-property and its contrary, in the subject, is <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive). By showing the twofold nature of properties through what has negative concomitance and what does not, the domain-analysis of the <s>anaikāntika</s> is indicated. For it is only when the probandum-property has negative concomitance that the <s>anaikāntika</s> has possible application, not when it lacks negative concomitance.

children.text: siddhāntamabhyupetya tadvirodhī viruddhaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: That which contradicts what has been accepted after embracing a <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory). // 6 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
sūtre samānakartṛkatvābhāvāt ktvāpratyayānupapattyā śabdadoṣamāha---na khalviti /
arthadoṣamāha---na ca pakṣa iti /
upalakṣaṇa caitat /
etasmin sati virodhāpasiddhāntau nigrahasthāne niravakāśe /
tayoḥ satorayaṃ vā mīmāṃsakābhimato viśeṣavirodho 'pi viruddha syādityapi /
abhyupagameti /
siddhāntaśabdenātra pakṣo vivakṣito 'to na prakṛtahānaṃ nāpyapasiddhāntavaiyarthyamityarthaḥ /
viśeṣaviruddhaprasaṅganivārayati---viśeṣeti /
abhyupetya ityanena pratijñāyeti vivakṣitam, na tvabhipretyeti /
na ca viśeṣaḥ pratijñāyate 'pi tu abhipreyate na ca tathābhūtena virodhopalambhasaṃbhavo 'siddhidaśāyāmanupambhena siddhidaśāyāṃ sahopalambhenānavasaraparāhatatvāt /
evaṃbhūtasyābhiprāyagocaratvamapi kathamityapi na yuktam, svārthānumānasamaye prakṛtopapādakatayā tatsiddheḥ anupapādakastu viśeṣo na sidhyati /
ata eva nābhiprāyagocaro 'pi /
children.translated_text: For that very reason, it is not even the object of intention.

children.text: tadāpi kathaṃ sarvathānupalabdhacaraḥ sidhyatītyapi na vācyam, ākāṅkṣādisaṃpattau padārthānāmivāpūrvārthapratipādane vyāptipakṣadharmatāmāhātmyasyāpahnotumaśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor should one say 'how then is something whose operation is entirely unapprehended established?' — because when the conditions of expectation and the like are fulfilled, just as with word-meanings in conveying a novel meaning, the greatness of pervasion and thesis-property-hood cannot be denied.

children.text: tasmād yayoreva parasparadharmiparihāreṇa niyamavatoḥ sthitirūpalabhyate, tayoreva virodho nānyathetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, contradiction holds only between those two that are found to have a stable restriction through the mutual exclusion of their subjects — not otherwise — this is the meaning.

children.text: anuktaśca saṃgṛhītaśceti vipratiṣiddhamityata āhar---idṛśaṃ vyākhyānamiti //
children.translated_text: If [one objects] that 'unstated and yet included' is self-contradictory — to this he says: 'Such an interpretation...' //

He states a verbal fault in the <s>sūtra</s>: since there is no identity of agent, the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix is inapplicable — he says: 'Indeed not...' He states the substantive fault: 'Nor is the thesis...' And this is an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). If this [fault] obtains, then contradiction and counter-doctrine as points of defeat would be without scope. Given those two, even the specific contradiction accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> would be [a case of] <s>viruddha</s>. 'By acceptance' — by the word <s>siddhānta</s> here, the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is intended; therefore there is neither departure from the topic nor purposelessness of the counter-doctrine — this is the meaning. He prevents the incurrence of specific contradiction: 'The specific...' By 'having accepted,' what is intended is 'having stated in the thesis,' not 'having intended.' And the specific [property] is not stated in the thesis but rather intended; and with something of that nature, the apprehension of contradiction is not possible — in the stage of non-establishment, because of non-apprehension, and in the stage of establishment, because of being precluded by co-apprehension. Even the question 'how can something of this nature be the object of intention?' is not proper, since its establishment is achieved through being a corroborator of the topic at the time of inference for oneself. But a specific [property] that is not a corroborator is not established.

children.text:
syādetat, virodhe hi heturna syāt sādhya vā /
ādye 'siddha eva /
dvitīye tu kālātyayāpadiṣṭaḥ /
kvedānīṃ viruddhaḥ? anyatarāniścaye 'pi sandigdhāsiddha ityāśakṅkyoktaṃ vārttikakṛtā yasmādamyupagataṃ bādhata iti /
nāsiddhaḥ, pakṣe niścitatvāt /
nāpi kālātītaḥ, pramāṇāntareṇa balavatā abādhanāt, kiṃ tvayameva sisādhayipitaṃ bādhata iti vārttikārthaḥ sugama eva /
dvitīyaṃ vārttikamabhyupagatena bādhyate iti /
tadapi yadyapi pratijñārthena tadbādhane 'siddhaḥ syāt, tathāpi virodhasyaiva yatrodbhaṭatvam, tatra tadullaṅghanena prayatnasādhyamasiddhatvaṃ nodbhāvyameva, daivatastatpratīkāre niranuyojyānuyogāpatteḥ, viruddhadvāreṇaivāsiddherapi vyavasthāpane tadudbhāvanasyāvaśyakatvācceti /
sugamam /
uttaravārttikānurodhena tu vyācaṣṭe---svarūpeṇa hetutvena vetyarthaḥ /
atrodāharaṇabhāṣyamityādi /
uktamityartha iti /
antaṣṭīkāyāṃ bhāṣyasyeti śeṣaḥ /
virodhanigrahasthānādetasyāmedamāśaṅkya yathā parihṛtaṃ vārttikakṛtā, tadanurodhena vyākhyātam /
pratijñāśritatvamiti /
virodhavaibhavena codāharaṇāni vārttike /
vastutastu svamate mānāntarasiddhasyārthasyānyathāvacanamapasiddhāntaḥ /
vākyāṃśayorekārthabhāvābhāvaviṣayatvena vyādhātī virodhaḥ /
viparyayavyāptatvena niścito viruddho hetvābhāsaḥ /
sa ca vidhisādhane svabhāvānupalabdhirvyāpakānupalabdhirvyāpakaviruddhopalabdhiriti trividhaḥ /
tadyathā dhūmavānayaṃ yogyasya satastadvattayā anupalabhyamānatvāt, niragnikatvāt, jalāśayatvāditi /
niṣedhasādhane 'pi svabhāvopalabdhirvyāpyopalabdhiriti dvividhaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the proof is a negation as well, [the contradictory reason] is of two kinds: <s>svabhāvopalabdhi</s> (apprehension of the intrinsic nature) and <s>vyāpyopalabdhi</s> (apprehension of the pervaded).

children.text: tadyathā niragniko 'yam, tadvattayopalabhyamānatvāt, dhūmavattavāditi /
children.translated_text: For example: 'this is devoid of fire — because of being apprehended as possessing that [fire],' 'because of possessing smoke.'

children.text: sarvaścāyaṃ viśeṣaṇadvārāpi pratisandheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And all of these should be reconsidered through the door of the qualifier as well.

children.text: yathā kṛṣṇāgururāruprabhavavahnimānayam, kaṭukāsurabhivipāṇḍuradhūmavattvāditi saṃkṣepaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: For example: 'this has fire originating from black aloe wood — because of possessing pungent, malodorous, and pale smoke' — this is the summary. //6//

One might say: in the case of contradiction, the reason would either not be [a reason] or the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) [would not be a probandum]. In the first case, it is simply unestablished. In the second, it is a case of 'charged after the time has passed' (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>). Where then is the contradictory [reason]? Even without certainty of one [alternative], it would be doubtfully unestablished — anticipating this, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> says: 'because it contradicts what is accepted.' It is not unestablished, because it is ascertained in the thesis. Nor is it a case of time having passed, because it is not sublated by another, stronger <s>pramāṇa</s>. Rather, this very [reason] contradicts what is desired to be proved — the meaning of the <s>Vārttika</s> is easily understood. The second <s>Vārttika</s> is: 'it is contradicted by what is accepted.' That too, although if [the reason is contradicted] by the thesis-meaning it would be unestablished, nevertheless, where contradiction itself is prominent, there one should not, by transgressing that [contradiction], raise the unestablished-ness which is achievable only with effort — because there would follow the consequence of being questioned when there is no [proper] question, since the remedy for that [contradiction] is providential; and because raising [the charge of] contradiction is necessary even for establishing the unestablished-ness through the door of contradiction. This is easily understood. But in accordance with the later <s>Vārttika</s>, he comments: 'in its own form or as a reason' — this is the meaning. 'Here the example in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>' and so forth. 'Has been stated' — this is the meaning — the remainder is: in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> within the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. From the point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) of contradiction — having anticipated this, he explains how it was resolved by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, in accordance with that. 'Because of being dependent on the thesis.' And the examples in the <s>Vārttika</s> display the full range of contradiction. But in reality, stating otherwise what has been established by another <s>pramāṇa</s> in one's own system is <s>apasiddhānta</s> (deviation from established doctrine). Contradiction is that which vitiates, by having as its object the presence or absence of a single meaning in two parts of the sentence. A pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) ascertained as pervaded by the opposite [of the <s>sādhya</s>] is the contradictory [reason]. And that is of three kinds: <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the intrinsic nature), <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader), and <s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s> (apprehension of what contradicts the pervader) — when the proof is a positive assertion. For example: 'this has smoke — because of not being apprehended as possessing that [smoke] when fit and present,' 'because of being devoid of fire,' 'because of being a body of water.'

children.text: yasmātprakaraṇacintā sa nirṇayārthamapadiṣṭaḥ prakaraṇasamaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: Since [there is merely] consideration of the topic, that which is adduced for the purpose of determination is <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (balancing the topic). //7//

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> //

children.text:
iha khalu hetvābhāsānāṃ tattyānusaṃhitānāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ saṃśayo vivakṣitaviparītajñānaṃ jijñāsā ajñānaṃ vyāptibādhaśceti phalāni /
tatra phaladvārakaṃ prakaraṇasamalakṣaṇamupakramyateyasmādityādi /
tadetad bhāṣyamukhane vyācaṣṭe---prakaraṇeti /
yasmāt prakriyamāṇārthajijñāsāmātraṃ bhavati sa prakarasama iti saṃkṣepaḥ /
tathāhi, pakṣe samabalabādhakasahapravṛtterna tattvanirṇayaḥ, pratibalena pratiruddhatvāt /
nāpi tato 'nusandhānenāpi sahasā vyāptibādho 'nugṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatayā samabalatvāt /
nāpyajñānameva pakṣe vidyamānatayaikakoṭiprasañjakatvāt /
nāpi viparītajñānam, tenāvyāpteḥ /
nāpi sandehaḥ koṭidvayānupanāyakatvāt /
tasmādekāṃ koṭimupanayan samabalena pratiruddhaḥ kathamatra nirṇayo bhavatviti jijñāsāṃ janayan prakaraṇasama itarebhyo bhidyata iti /
tacca satpratipakṣatvaṃ siddhobhayahetukamasiddhobhayahetukaṃ siddhasādhyobhayahetukaṃ ca /
prathamamarūpadravyatvolabhyamānasparśādhiṣṭhānatvayoḥ /
tṛtīyaṃ śrāvaṇatvakṛtakatvayoḥ /
madhyamamihodāhariṣyate /
tadanurodhena vyācaṣṭe---sa khalviti /
yadyapi jijñāsāmātramatropayoti, tathāpi saṃśayānuvṛttinivṛttyoḥ jijñāsānuvṛttinivṛttī iti mattvoktam---tatra sandigdhe tadvā jijñāsate iti /
nanu yata eva jijñāsā kathaṃ tameva prekṣāvān tattvanirṇayāya prayokṣyata ityata āha---vicitrābhisandhitayeti /
pūrvasamayo duṣpratyayo jātu prayojyabuddhiriti hi sādhanottarābhāsaprayoge hetava ityarthaḥ /
nanvekaikapakṣaniyatatayā kathamubhayapakṣasāmyamanupalabdherityata āha---seyamiti /
nanu vyutpattimāśritya cet prakaraṇasamapadaṃ pravartate kṛtaṃ tarhi yasmādityādilakṣaṇāntareṇetyata āha---vyutpattīti /
athaitadeva pravṛttinimittaṃ kiṃ na syādityata āha---anyatheti /
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa savyabhicārāt prakaraṇasamaṃ bhedayatā tasya saṃśayahetutvamasya ca prakaraṇapravṛttihetutvamuktam /
tacca saṃmugdham, pakṣapratipakṣau prakaraṇam iti prāgvyākhyānāt, sūtravirodhācca /
na hi yasmāt prakaraṇamiti sūtramapi tu yasmāt prakaraṇacinteti /
ata āha---etaduktaṃ bhavatīti /
api tu satpratipakṣatayaiva hetvābhāsatvamiti /
jijñāsāmātrahetutayā nirṇayānutpādakatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
etena bhāṣye prakaraṇaśabdo jijñāsāpara ityuktam /
nanu nityadharmānupalabdhiḥ kādācitkī vivakṣitā, sadātanī vā? ādyā anaikāntikyeva, ākāśādāvapi kadācinnityadharmānupalabdheḥ /
dvitīyā tvasiddhaiva /
na hi nityadharmopalabdhyā śabde kadācidapi na bhavitavyam iti pramāṇamasti /
tathā cāsiddhatvaṃ vihāya kutaḥ prakaraṇasamatvamudbhāvayatītyata āha---na ca tattvānupalabdhiriti /
ayamarthaḥ, yasyaivaṃ viśeṣagrahaḥ, tasya tāvadasiddha evāyamityastu, yastūpalambhābhāvena sulabhāmanupalabdhiṃ matvā viśeṣamapratisandhāya pratibalena ca pratibandhamupanyasyati, taṃ prati kimayamābhāsatāṃ yātu na vā? na tāvanna yāti /
tathā sati sādhayet /
evaṃ ca tato 'gṛhītaviśeṣā dvitīyāpi sādhayedeva /
na caivam, na cānābhāsamasādhakamatiprasaṅgāt /
na ca tadānīṃ doṣāntaramatra parisphurati, anyatra pratibalena pratibandhāditi /
yatrāpi yugapadanekadoṣaparisphuraṇam, tatrāpi satpratipakṣatvam apyudbhāvya viramyate /
na hi yāvadasti tāvadudbhāvyam, anyatra saṃbhūya pratijñāyāṃ sarvatrodbhāvananiyamāditi /
yadyapi pratyakṣavat tattvānupalabdhirapi na kevalā, api tu samānadharmadarśanādisahitaiva saṃśayakāraṇam /
tathā ca codyacuñcorabhimatabhraṃsaḥ, tathāpi tamupekṣya svasiddhāntāvarodhena pariharati---na hyakāraṇānāmiti /
nanūbhayeti /
ekasmin pakṣe ubhayapadaṃ vihāyāparasmin vyāvṛttidvāreti padamadhyāhṛtya phakkikābodhaḥ, api tu tattvānupalabdhirevāsmaduktā prakaraṇasamodāharaṇamiti śeṣaḥ /
evaṃ jijñāsāhetutvābhāvāt prakaraṇasamalakṣaṇāyogitayā śarīrādanyatvaṃ na tadudāharaṇamityuktam /
idānīṃ saṃśayahetutayā anaikāntikalakṣaṇāyogāt /
tadudāharaṇamevedamityāśayavānāhetyāha---itaśceti /
kecit tu manyante, tattvānupalabdhireva paraṃ prakaraṇasamo hetvābhāsastannirākaraṇaṃ sūcayati---evamanyānyapīti /
nāgṛhyamāṇaviśeṣadaśāyāmanupalabdhyoranyayorvā dharmayoḥ kaścit viśeṣo gṛhyamāṇaviśeṣadaśāyāṃ tu yathānyasyānyatra hetvābhāse 'ntarbhāvaḥ tathānupalabdherapīti sāpi tyājyā /
children.translated_text: In the state where the specific [feature] is not grasped, there is no distinction between the two non-apprehensions, or between any other two properties. But in the state where the specific [feature] is grasped, just as one [of them] is subsumed under another pseudo-reason elsewhere, so too is the non-apprehension [subsumed] — hence that [view] too should be abandoned.

children.text: na cānupalabdhyorātyantikamagṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatvam /
children.translated_text: Nor is the non-grasping of the specific [feature] between the two non-apprehensions absolute.

children.text: ubhayoḥ siddhatve vastuna ubhayānubhayātmakatvaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Because if both were established, there would follow the consequence that the real entity would have the nature of both and neither.

children.text: ekasyāsiddhatve vā kathamagṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatvamātyantikamubhayorapi vāstavyāmasiddhau punarubhayānubhayātmakatvaprasaṅgāditi // 7 //
children.translated_text: Or if one were unestablished, how could the non-grasping of the specific [feature] be absolute for both? And even if both were genuinely unestablished, there would again follow the consequence of having the nature of both and neither. //7//

Now, of the pseudo-reasons, when connected with their respective [definitions], the results are, in order: doubt, cognition opposite to the intended, desire to know, ignorance, and sublation of pervasion. Among those, the definition of <s>prakaraṇasama</s>, which operates through the result [of mere desire to know], is introduced — 'since' and so forth. He explains this through the formulation of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'the topic.' The summary is: since [the reason] merely produces the desire to know about the matter under investigation, it is <s>prakaraṇasama</s>. For thus: when [a reason] operates together with an equally strong sublating [counter-reason] in the thesis, there is no determination of truth, because it is obstructed by the counter-reason. Nor is there even a sublation of pervasion through the investigation of that [reason] precipitately, because [the counter-reason] being of equal strength, the specific [reason] is being supported [equally]. Nor is there mere ignorance, because by being present in the thesis, it inclines toward one alternative. Nor is there cognition of the opposite, because [the reason] is not pervaded by that. Nor is there doubt, because [the reason] does not lead to both alternatives. Therefore, bringing forward one alternative and being obstructed by the equally strong [counter-reason] — 'how can there be determination here?' — generating [merely] the desire to know, the <s>prakaraṇasama</s> is distinguished from the others. And that status of having an equally strong counter-reason (<s>satpratipakṣatva</s>) is [either] caused by both reasons being established, or by both being unestablished, or by the [reason being] established and the <s>sādhya</s> [being established in both]. The first [occurs] between the [reasons] 'being a formless substance' and 'being the substratum of apprehended touch.' The third between 'being audible' and 'being produced.' The second will be illustrated here. In accordance with that, he comments: 'that indeed.' Although only the desire to know is useful here, nevertheless, thinking that the continuity and cessation of doubt [entail] the continuity and cessation of the desire to know, he says: 'there, when in doubt, one desires to know that.' Now, the very thing from which the desire to know [arises] — how would a discerning person employ that very thing for the determination of truth? — therefore he says: 'because of diverse intentions.' The meaning is: a former agreement [with the reason] that is hard to reject, the intellect of the person to be convinced — these are indeed the causes for the employment of a correct-seeming reason after [an earlier correct] proof. Now, since [each reason] is restricted to one thesis each, how is there equality with respect to both theses — [given that there is] non-apprehension [of such equality]? — therefore he says: 'this.' Now, if the word <s>prakaraṇasama</s> operates based on etymology, then what need is there for another definition beginning with 'since'? — therefore he says: 'etymology.' But should not this very [etymology] be the basis of usage? — therefore he says: 'otherwise.' Here, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, distinguishing <s>prakaraṇasama</s> from the inconclusive by [the criterion of] co-extensiveness with deviation, has stated that the latter [inconclusive] is a cause of doubt and the former [prakaraṇasama] is a cause of investigation into the topic. But that is confused, because of the prior explanation that 'the thesis and counter-thesis are the topic' (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), and because of contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>. For the <s>sūtra</s> does not say 'since the topic' but 'since the investigation of the topic.' Therefore he says: 'this amounts to saying.' Rather, it is a pseudo-reason precisely by virtue of having an equally strong counter-reason. The purport is: because of merely being a cause of the desire to know, because of not generating determination. By this, it is said that the word <s>prakaraṇa</s> in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is directed toward 'desire to know.' Now, is the non-apprehension of eternal properties intended as occasional or constant? The first is simply inconclusiveness, since even in <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the like, there is occasional non-apprehension of eternal properties. But the second is simply unestablished. For there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> [to the effect] that there must never be apprehension of eternal properties in sound. And thus, setting aside unestablished-ness, whence does he raise the status of <s>prakaraṇasama</s>? — therefore he says: 'nor is the non-apprehension of the real nature.' The meaning is this: for one who grasps the specific [feature] in this way, let this be simply unestablished. But one who, thinking that non-apprehension is easily available through the absence of apprehension, without considering the specific [feature], and presenting the counter-reason as equally strong — for him, should this be [counted as] a pseudo-reason or not? To begin with, it does not fail to be [a pseudo-reason]. For if so, it would prove [the thesis]. And thus, even the second [non-apprehension], without the specific [feature] being grasped from that [perspective], would indeed prove [it]. But this is not so — and [yet] a non-semblance [i.e., a valid reason] that fails to prove would be over-extended. And at that point, no other fault is apparent here, apart from the obstruction by the equally strong counter-reason. Even where multiple faults are apparent simultaneously, the status of having an equally strong counter-reason is also raised and then one desists. For it is not the case that everything that exists must be raised — except where all [faults] must be raised together in the thesis, [where they operate] collectively. Although non-apprehension of the real nature, like perception, is not by itself alone [a cause of doubt], but only together with the observation of common properties and the like — and thus the objector's intended [conclusion] collapses — nevertheless, setting that aside, he responds by encompassing it within his own established doctrine: 'for not of non-causes.' Now, 'both' — the phrasing is to be understood by leaving aside the word 'both' in one thesis and supplying the expression 'through the door of exclusion' in the other. Rather, the very non-apprehension of the real nature as stated by us is the illustration of <s>prakaraṇasama</s> — this is the remainder. Thus, because of the absence of being a cause of the desire to know, by the non-applicability of the definition of <s>prakaraṇasama</s>, 'otherness from the body' is not an illustration of that — this has been stated. Now, because of being a cause of doubt, by the non-applicability of the definition of the inconclusive — with this intention he says: 'moreover.'  Some, however, think that the non-apprehension of the real nature itself is the paramount pseudo-reason [called] <s>prakaraṇasama</s>, and indicates the refutation of that: 'thus others also.'

children.text: sādhyāviśiṣṭaḥ sādhyatvātsādhyasamaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: What is undistinguished from the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), because of being a <s>sādhya</s> [itself], is <s>sādhyasama</s> (equal to the probandum). //7//

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> //

children.text:
tasmāt sādhyatvādasiddhateti /
sādhyatayā asiddhatayā /
sādhyenāviśiṣṭaḥ sādhyāviśiṣṭaḥ /
sā cāsiddhatā kasyacidityādi sugamam /
tadevaṃ śiṣyapratipattilāghavāya vākyagauravam /
vastutastu asiddhaḥ sādhyasama ityetāvadeva lakṣaṇamuktam /
asiddha ityasyāpi pakṣadharmatayā na niścita ityarthaḥ /
parāmarśaviṣayaḥ pakṣadharmatā /
sā ca svasādhyena nirupādhisaṃbandhasya pakṣasaṃbandhaḥ /
tathāpi ca vyāptiniścayasahitena saṃbandhidvayaniścayena niścīyate /
vyāptiliṅgapakṣeṣu tvekatamāniścaye 'pi neti /
tatra pakṣāniścayādāśrayāsiddha /
liṅgasyaivāniścayāt svarūpāsiddhaḥ /
vyāpteraniścayādanyathāsiddhaḥ /
eteṣāṃ cāniścayaḥ sandehād vā, abhāvaniścayād veti na kaścit phalaṃ prati viśeṣaḥ /
etena vyomapadmāṃ sugandhi padmātvāt ityādayo 'pi saṃgṛhītā bhavanti /
anyathā yaḥ pakṣe 'sanniti lakṣaṇenaitallabhyate /
yathā hi, asati sapakṣe vipakṣe ca pratiṣedhaḥ kartu na śakyate, tathā pakṣe 'pīti /
satyā eveti satyenābhyupagatāyā ityarthaḥ /
tasyā nityatvābhāvāditi /
tadasiddhamiti cet---na, kadācidupalambhalakṣaṇenāpi anityatvena sādhyasiddheḥ teṣāṃ vyañjakavaicitrye 'pi vyaktyāśrayasaṃbandhināmupalambhamantareṇānupalambhaniyamāt /
upalambhe vā tattvānupapatte /
sadopalambhaprasaṅgācca /
tejasābhibhūtatvāt na tatheti cet---na, āśrayānabhibhave teṣāmanabhibhāvāt /
tadabhibhave tu teṣāmupalambhe tadupalambhaprasaṅgāt /
ata eva na bhābhāvasya tadvyañjakatvam /
tasmāt kadācidupalambha evāsyāḥ sāmānyāvirūpatāṃ pratikṣipatīti /
nāpi karmeti /
svāśrayaṃ prāgdeśād vibhajya deśāntaraṃ prāpayat karma tattāyāṃ vyavatiṣṭhate /
nāto 'nyathā, calanavyavahārasyānākasmikatvāt, anyanimittābhāvāt /
evaṃbhūtārthānvayavyatirekānuvidhānācca chāyāyāstvāśraya eva tāvannopalabhyate, prāgeva tasya viprayojanasaṃprayojane ityarthaḥ /
na guṇo dravyāsamavāyāditi /
dravyāsamavetaṃ hyadravyasamavetaṃ vā, asamavetameva vā syāt? ubhayathāpi guṇave vyāghātaḥ, sāmānyavataḥ svatantrasya dravyatvāpatteḥ /
niḥsāmānyasya guṇalakṣaṇavyāghātāt /
sāmānyavānaguṇaḥ ityādi hi tat /
guṇakarmaṇāṃ nirguṇatayā guṇasya tatra samavāyavirodhena tatsamavāye sāmānyarūpatvopapatterityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: since qualities and actions, being qualityless, and since [this property's] inherence in quality would conflict with inherence, its inherence there is justified as being of the nature of a universal.

children.text: dravyāsamavāyāditi /
children.translated_text: "Because of non-inherence in substance" —

children.text: hetuṃ sādhayati---na mana iti teṣāṃ viśeṣaguṇavirahāt sāmānyaguṇo 'yaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: he establishes the reason: "Not by the mind" — because of the absence of specific qualities in those [qualities and actions], this [property] would be a general quality.

children.text: tathā cāśrayasahopalambhaniyame tadapratyakṣatāyāṃ niyamādapratyakṣatvaprasaṅga ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, since there is a rule of co-perception with the substratum, when that [substratum] is non-perceptible, by the rule [of co-perception] there would follow the consequence of non-perceptibility — that is the meaning.

Therefore, because of being a <s>sādhya</s>, it is unestablished. 'Because of being a <s>sādhya</s>' means 'because of being unestablished.' Undistinguished from the <s>sādhya</s> is <s>sādhyāviśiṣṭa</s>. And that unestablished-ness belongs to some — and so forth — this is easily understood. Thus, for the ease of the student's comprehension, the sentence is weighty. But in reality, just this much is the definition that has been stated: 'unestablished is <s>sādhyasama</s>.' And the meaning of 'unestablished' too is: not ascertained as a property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>). The object of the reflective consideration (<s>parāmarśa</s>) is the property-of-the-thesis status (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>). And that [property-of-the-thesis status] is the connection of the unconditional relation with its own <s>sādhya</s> to the thesis. And yet, it is ascertained through the ascertainment of both relata together with the ascertainment of the pervasion. But when even one of the pervasion, the mark, or the thesis is not ascertained — it is not [ascertained]. Among those: from the non-ascertainment of the thesis, [there results] the substratum-unestablished (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>). From the non-ascertainment of the mark itself, the self-unestablished (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>). From the non-ascertainment of the pervasion, the otherwise-unestablished (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>). And the non-ascertainment of these [three] is either from doubt or from the ascertainment of absence — and there is no difference with respect to the result. By this, [examples] such as 'the sky-lotus is fragrant, because of being a lotus' and the like are also included. Otherwise, by the definition 'what does not exist in the thesis' — this [inclusion] is obtained. For just as, when the similar instance does not exist, the negation in the dissimilar instance cannot be made, so too in the thesis — this is the meaning. 'Of what is real alone' — the meaning is: of what is real and accepted. 'Because of the absence of its eternality.' If that is unestablished? — no, because the <s>sādhya</s> is established even by the mark of occasional apprehensibility as non-eternal. For despite the variety of manifestors, there is a rule that [eternal properties] are not apprehended without the apprehension of what is connected with the substratum of the manifestation. Or if [they were] apprehended, the real nature [of being eternal] would be untenable. And there would follow the consequence of constant apprehension. 'Because of being overpowered by light' — if so said: no, because when the substratum is not overpowered, those [properties] are not overpowered. But when that [substratum] is overpowered, upon the apprehension of those [properties], there would follow the consequence of its [the substratum's] being apprehended. For this very reason, the absence of light is not their manifestor. Therefore, even occasional apprehensibility rejects the non-incompatibility of this [being eternal] with the universal [of being apprehensible]. 'Nor action' — an action, separating its own substratum from the prior place and causing it to reach another place, is established in that [activity]. Not otherwise — because the usage of 'motion' is not causeless, and because of the absence of any other cause. And because shadow [i.e., what follows this pattern] conforms in its positive and negative concomitance to what has a nature of such a kind — to begin with, even its substratum is not apprehended, much less its disjunction and conjunction — this is the meaning. 'Nor a quality, because of not inhering in substance' — for what does not inhere in substance would either inhere in a non-substance, or simply not inhere at all. In either case, there is conflict with being a quality — because of the consequence of substance-hood for what is independent and possesses a universal. Because of the conflict with the definition of quality for what lacks a universal. For 'what possesses a universal and is not a quality' and the like — that is [the definition].

children.text:
nāpyātmaguṇa iti /
iyaṃ hi bāhyakaraṇapratyakṣatā idantāsāmānādhikaraṇyena vyāptā /
tadātmaguṇatāmādāya nivartamānamanātmaguṇatāyāṃ viśrāmyatītyarthaḥ /
nāpi nabhonabhasvatoriti /
cākṣuṣato hi guṇānāṃ rūpidravyasamavāyena vyāptā /
tacca rūpitvaṃ gaganapavanābhyāṃ vyāvartamānaṃ cākṣuṣaguṇasaṃbandhamapi vyāvartayatītyarthaḥ /
nāpi tejasaḥ tadguṇatvaṃ hi pratītau tadavirodhitvena vyāptam, anyathā guṇinaḥ svaguṇapratītiparipanthitve guṇasya nityānupalambhaprasaṅgāt, sati samavāye upalambhavirodhāt, asati samavāye cāsattvāt /
taccāto nivartamānaṃ tadguṇatvamapi nivartayatītyarthaḥ /
tatsahacaritaguṇāntarānupalabdheśceti /
ayamarthaḥ, na tāvat chāyā tejaso rūpametadrūpasya śuklabhāsvaratvaniyamātṛ /
na cendranīlaprabhārūpavadāśrayovidhānāt /
tasmāt guṇāntaramevedaṃ tasyeti vācyam /
tathā ca cakṣuṣopalabhyamānaṃ na rūpamanantarbhāvyopalabdhuṃ śakyate, cakṣuṣastathaiva sāmarthyākalanāditi /
ata eveti /
ayamarthaḥ, cakṣurmātragrāhyatayā tāvacchāyā na guṇāntaratvena śaṅkāspadam, rūpaṃ tu saṃbhāvyeta /
taccopalabhyamānaṃ pāthasa upalabhya śaityadravatvādivyāptam, atādṛśastoyatvāyogāt /
pṛthivyāstu upalabhyagandhādivyāptam, atathābhūtasya pṛthivītvāyogāt /
tacca śaityagandhādisāhacaryamato nivartamānamanupalambhena tadguṇatāmapi nivartayatīti /
api ceti /
children.translated_text: "Moreover" —

children.text: ataijasadravyarūpagrahaṇe hi bāhyālokavyāptasyaiva cakṣuṣaḥ sāmarthyamadhigatam /
children.translated_text: for in the grasping of form belonging to non-fiery substance, the capacity of the eye, which is pervaded by external light, has been ascertained.

children.text: na ca yatsahitasya yasya yatra sāmarthyaṃ tadrahitena tena tatkaraṇam /
children.translated_text: And when something has the capacity for something when accompanied by [a factor], it does not perform that without that [factor].

children.text: tathā sati vahnirahitamapyārdramindhanaṃ dhūmaṃ vidadhyādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: if it were so, even wet fuel without fire would produce smoke.

"Nor a quality of the self" — for this perceptibility by an external instrument is pervaded by co-referentiality with "this-ness" (<s>idantā</s>). Taking self-quality-hood, [the argument] that ceases from [proving] non-self-quality-hood

children.text:
virodhakastvadhika ityāha---tasmistviti /
etena pārthivaṃ rūpamāropitaṃ tama iti nirastam, bāhyālokasahakārivirahe cakṣuṣastathārope 'pyasāmarthyāt tadeva hi dharmyantare vā samāropyeta pittapītimavat, tatraiva vā niyatadeśe 'vagamyamāne aniyatadeśatvamiti nedīyasyaṇīyasyapi mahattvavat /
ubhayathāpi tatprathamamantareṇānupapattirekatrāropyatvādanyatrāropaviṣayatvāt tasyaiva /
na cālokamantareṇa rūpagrahaṇe cakṣuṣaḥ sāmarthyamityuktam /
na cāropyāropaviṣayāprathane bhrāntisaṃbhavaḥ /
na cobhayoranyatarasminnavyāpṛtasyaivacakṣuṣo bhrāntijanakatvam, na cāyamacākṣuṣaḥ pratyayaḥ, tadanvayavyatirekayorananyathāsiddhatvāditi /
nāpi dravyamiti /
na pṛthivyagandhatvāt /
na jalamarasatvāt /
na tejaḥ anuṣṇatvāt /
na vāyurasparśatvāt /
nākāśamaśabdasamavāyikāraṇatvāt /
na dikkālo paratvāparatvāsamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogānādhāratvāt /
nātmā buddhyanādhāratvāt /
na mano jñānāsamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogānādhāratvādityarthaḥ /
nāpyanyaditi /
nedamadravyaṃ rūpidravyam, asmadādipratyakṣatvāt /
asmadādipratyakṣaṃ hīndriyeṇa vyāptam /
tacca niyataviṣayasāmarthyena vyāptam /
tacca vipakṣānnivartamānamindriyaṃ nivartayat pratyakṣatvamapi nivartayatītyarthaḥ /
asparśatvāditi /
nedamanekadravyaṃ dravyamasparśatvāt /
asparśatā hi dravyasyānārabhyatayā vyāptā /
sa ca niṣedhyādanekadravyānnivartamānā svavyāpyaṃ sparśarahitatvaṃ gṛhītvā tadviparīte viśrāmyatītyarthaḥ /
anārambhakatveneti /
children.translated_text: "By virtue of being non-productive" —

children.text: avidyamānamārabhbhakaṃ yasya tat tathoktam /
children.translated_text: that of which there is no productive [capacity] for anything existing — that is so called.

children.text: tasya bhāvastatvattvamiti /
children.translated_text: "The state of that is its reality" —

children.text: etenāśrayāsiddhiḥ parihṛtā //
children.translated_text: by this, the unestablished-substratum [objection] has been resolved.

But the contradicting [argument] is stronger — he says: "But in that..." By this, the [view that] "darkness is [merely] an earthy form superimposed" is refuted — since in the absence of the auxiliary of external light, the eye [would have] such superimposition —

children.text:
yat tūktam, manasā dravyāntarānārambhe vaiyarthyamupādhiḥ, na punarasparśatvam, tat kiṃ vaiyarthyādanārambhakatvamunnīyate, anārambhakād vā vaiyarthyamiti? na tāvadādyaḥ, sarvotpattimatprayojanasyāsmadādibhiḥ piśitalocanairanākalanāt /
tasmād yadyārambhakasvabhāvatvaṃ manasastadā kadācidārambhe prayojanamapi kiñcid bhaviṣyatīti /
na cet tatsvabhāvakatvaṃ prayojanasahasreṇāpi nārambhaḥ /
svabhāvānuvidhāyīni hi prayojanāni /
na tu prayojanānuvidhāyinaḥ svabhāvāḥ /
pratyakṣabādhastu tadā syāt yadi tama evāpahnūyeta /
dravyatve pratyakṣasyājāgarukatvāt, nīlimaguṇaśālinaḥ pratīteḥ /
kathamevametaditi cetṛ---na, vastuto 'sya nīlatve 'cākṣuṣatvaprasaṅgāt /
ālokasahakāriṇa eva cakṣuṣaḥ tatra sāmarthyāvadhāraṇādityuktam /
śuklabhāsvaravirodhitāsāmyāt tu tathā vyavahāraḥ /
evaṃ tarhi raktādivyavahāro 'pi prasajyata iti cet---na, vyavahāre hi sati nimittānusmaraṇāt /
na tu nimittāmastītyeva vyavahāraḥ yathā śaṣayoḥ śavyavahāro gauḍānāṃ varṇatvanimittāviśeṣe 'pi na kādivyavahāraḥ /
adṛṣṭādisāmagrīviśeṣānniyamo nātrāpi daṇḍavāritaḥ iti /
tat kiṃ na kiñcidevac chāyetyata āha---tasmād bhābhāva evac chāyeti /
na ca vācyam, so 'pi kathamālokamantareṇa pratiyogismaraṇādhikaraṇagrahaṇavirahe vidhimukhena cākṣuṣo viṣaya iti /
yadgrahe hi yadapekṣaṃ cakṣustadabhāvagrahe 'pi tadapekṣameva /
evaṃ hi taditarasāmagrahīsākalyaṃ syāt /
tadihāpyālokābhāve tadālokāpekṣā syāt, yadyāloke 'pi tadapekṣā bhavet /
na caitadasti /
pratyuta virodha eva tasmin sati hi tadabhāva eva na syāt /
kiṃ tatsāpekṣeṇa cakṣuṣā gṛhyeta divā ca pratiyoginaḥ prabhāmaṇḍalasya grahe eva pradeśāntare tadgrahaṇamiti na kiñcidanupapannam /
anyadāpi na rātrimapratisandhāyāndhakāragrahaḥ /
rātrijñānaṃ ca na divasamapratisandhāya /
tathā hi nirastaitaddvīpavartiraviraśmijālaḥ kālaviśeṣo 'tra rātrirityucyate /
giridarīvivaravartinastu yadi yogino na timirālokinaḥ /
timiradarśinaścet---nūnaṃ smṛtālokā iti /
adhikaraṇam api dṛṣṭamanumitaṃ smṛtaṃ vā ihedānīmandhakāra iti pratyayāt /
vidhimukhastu pratyayo 'siddhaḥ /
na hi nāprayogamātreṇa vidhitvam, pralayavināśāvasthānādiṣu vyabhicārāt /
nārthāntarbhāvena vākyārthe padaprayogādadoṣa iti cet? ihāpi mātsaryamapanīya eṣaiva rītiranugamyatāmiti suṣṭhūpasaṃhṛtam---tasmād bhābhāva evac chāyeti /
deśāntaraprāptimattvaprayuktaṃ hi gatimattvam /
na tu deśāntaradarśanaprayuktam tacca prayojakamiha niścitavyāvṛtti /
tathā hi svātantrayeṇa deśāntaraprāptau vārakānuvidhānaniyamo na syāt /
children.translated_text: For thus: if [light] independently reaches another place, there would be no rule of conformity to obstructions.

children.text: prabhātulyatve tejaḥprabhāśrayeṣu ratnaviśeṣeṣuc chāyā divase na syāt /
children.translated_text: If [darkness] were similar to radiance, there would be no shadow in the daytime in specific gems that are substrata of the radiance of fire.

children.text: chāyayaivābhibhave vā bahalatame tamasi teṣāmāloko na syāt /
children.translated_text: Or, if [darkness] were suppressed by shadow alone, in the densest darkness there would be no illumination of those [gems].

children.text: ālokāntareṇaivābhibhave chāyāyā apyudbhāvo na syāditi //
children.translated_text: If [shadow] were suppressed by another light alone, there would be no emergence of shadow either.

As for what was said — "the <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) regarding the non-production of another substance by the mind is purposelessness, not non-tangibility" — does non-productivity follow from purposelessness, or [vice versa]?

children.text:
saṃkalayati---seyamiti /
asiddhiḥ anirūpaṇam /
na caitāvateti /
vācyamiti śeṣaḥ /
kutaḥ? savyabhicāratvāditi /
ayamarthaḥ, yadyapi tatrāpi svābhāvikasaṃbandhavirahādastyeva hetutvāsiddhiḥ, na hyasti saṃbhavaḥ svabhāvapratibaddhaśca savyabhicārādiśceti /
tathāpi na tāvat svarūpata āśrayato vā tatrāsiddhirudbhāvayituṃ śakyate, tayorniścitatvāt /
nāpyupādhita upādhyapekṣayā vyabhicārāderlaghupratipattikatvāt, upādhestu taddvāraiva pratipatteḥ /
yadi ca tena dūṣayituṃ na śakyate taddvārāpyapādhirevodbhāvyeta /
na caitadasti /
vyabhicārādau hyudbhāvite sutarāṃ nivartate /
upādhau tu kadācid vipratipadyate, tasya durūhatvāditi /
astu tarhi savyabhicāravat aprayojako nāma ṣaṣṭho hetvābhāsaḥ, tasyāpyevaṃrūpaviśeṣaśālitvādityata āha---anyathāsiddhasya tviti /
bhavedevam, yadyaupādhikatvaṃ svābhāvikasaṃbandhavirahādanyatṛ /
na tvetadasti /
anaupādhikatvaṃ hi saṃbandhasya svābhāvikatvam /
aupādhikatvaṃ ca tadvarahaḥ /
tasmād viśeṣāntarābhāvāt, sādhyasamasamānalakṣaṇavattvācca tatraiva tasyāntarbhāva ityarthaḥ /
bhāṣye gatimattvāditi sandigdhaḥ /
vārttike satī chāyā gatimatī deśāntare darśanāditi viśeṣaṇadvārā āśrayāsiddhaḥ /
ayameva sattvaṃ vihāya niścitopādhisahavṛttiranyathāsiddhaḥ /
tadetāvanta evāsiddhabhedā iti bhramanirāsārthamudāharati---ta eta iti /
children.translated_text: that these are exactly the varieties of unestablishedness — he illustrates for the purpose of removing confusion: "These very ones..."

children.text: cākṣuṣatvāditi niścitāsiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Because of being visual" — this is a certainly unestablished [reason].

children.text: aśarīratvāditi dharmita evāśrayāsiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Because of being bodiless" — this is substratum-unestablished in the very subject (<s>dharmin</s>).

children.text: maitratanayatvāditi saṃndigdhopādhisahavṛttiranyathāsiddhaḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: "Because of being the son of <s>Maitra</s>" — this is otherwise-established due to co-occurrence with a doubtful <s>upādhi</s>.

He correlates: "This is..." "Unestablishedness" means non-determination. "Nor is this much" — the completion is: "to be said." Why? "Because of being accompanied by deviation" — the meaning is this: although

children.text: kālātyayāpadiṣṭaḥ kālātītaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: "Objected-as-time-barred" (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>) means: whose time has passed // [Sūtra] 9 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
atra yathāśrutabhāṣyavārttikadarśanāt sarvamasamañjasamiti mattvā svavyākhyāṃ sthānāntarīyabhāṣyādyupanyāsena saṃvadannāha---atretyādinā /
anuṣṇa ityādinā pratiṣedhyavidheyadharmagrāhakapramāṇabādho darśitaḥ /
dharmigrāhakapramāṇabādhastu ghaṭo vyāpakaḥ sattvādākāśavaditi pratyakṣeṇa /
paramāṇuḥ sāvayavo mūrtatvād ghaṭavadityanumānena /
meruḥ pāṣāṇamayaḥ parvatatvād vindhyavadityāgamena /
hetugrāhakapramāṇabādhastu, jalānilāviṣṇau pṛthivīto viparītasparśavatvāt tejovaditi pratyakṣeṇa /
mano vibhujñānāsamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogādhāratvāt ātmavadityanumānena /
brāhmaṇasya rājasūyaṃ karma, svargasādhanatvāt agniṣṭomavadityāgamena /
evaṃ navavidho 'yamekavidhopamānabādhena saṃkṣepato daśavidha iti /
nanu bādho nāma nāvinābhāvabhaṅgādaparaḥ kaścit /
so 'pi na trairūpyapracyavādanya ityata āha---bādheti /
na hi bādham avyavasthāpyānaikāntikatvamapakṣadharmatvaṃ vāvatārayituṃ śakyam /
ato 'syāvaśyodbhāvyatayāvaśyābhyupagantavyaḥ, anyathā virodhamapi nābhyupagacchet /
virodhe hi hetorabhāve svarūpāsiddhiḥ /
sādhyābhāve 'pakṣadharmatā durnivārā /
atha virodhasyaiva prathamaṃ buddhāvupanipātāt tadudbhāvanamantareṇa pakṣadharmatvasyodbhāvayitumaśakyatvācca so 'vaśyābhyupagantavyaḥ /
tadetat samānamanyatrāpītyuktamityarthaḥ /
yadyevam, bhāṣyamidānīṃ kathamityata āha---evamiti /
atha yadyayamartho bhāṣyakārasya vivakṣitaḥ, kimiti naitadanurūpamudāharaṇamityata āha---atra ceti /
tathāpyaihikamudāharaṇamasaṅgatamityata āha---paramatenaiveti /
athaitadudāharaṇaṃ svamate pañcakoṭiṣu kvāntarbhaviṣyatītyata āha---sa punariti /
tat kimiti nodbhāvayāṃbabhūva evamityata āha---sthūlatayeti /
children.translated_text: Why then did he not demonstrate it thus? — to this he says: 'Because of its grossness...'

children.text: vārttikamidānīṃ kathamityata āha---yasyāpadiśyamānasyetyādi /
children.translated_text: How is the <s>vārttika</s> [to be understood] now? — to this he says: 'Of what is being designated...' and so forth.

children.text: bhadantaṃ pratyekadeśinaḥ parīhāraḥ---samīkṛte 'bhidhānāditi /
children.translated_text: The reply to the venerable partial teacher is: 'Because of the statement when equalized...'

children.text: tad vivṛṇoti---ayamartha iti // 9 //
children.translated_text: He explains that: 'This is the meaning...'

Here, seeing that according to the literally read <s>bhāṣya</s> and <s>vārttika</s>, everything is incoherent, and proposing his own interpretation as consistent with <s>bhāṣya</s> passages from other places, he says: 'Here...' and so forth. By 'neither hot...' and so forth, the sublation by <s>pramāṇa</s> grasping the property to be negated and the property to be enjoined has been shown. But sublation by <s>pramāṇa</s> grasping the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) [is illustrated as follows]: 'The pot is a pervader, because of existence, like space' — by perception. 'The atom is composite, because of corporeality, like a pot' — by inference. '<s>Meru</s> is made of stone, because of being a mountain, like <s>Vindhya</s>' — by scripture (<s>āgama</s>). But sublation by <s>pramāṇa</s> grasping the reason [is illustrated as follows]: 'Water is distinct from earth in regard to touch, because of having a touch contrary to fire, like wind' — by perception. 'The mind is a substance, because of being a substratum of conjunction that is the non-inherence cause of cognition, like the self' — by inference. 'The <s>Rājasūya</s> is a rite for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, because of being a means to heaven, like the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>' — by scripture.
