Thus, this is ninefold; and with the one type of sublation by analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), it is in summary tenfold. Now, sublation is nothing other than the breaking of invariable concomitance. And that too is nothing other than the displacement from the three-fold characteristics (<s>trairūpya</s>) — to this he says: 'Sublation...' For sublation cannot be reduced to either inconclusiveness or non-thesis-property-hood without first being established [as sublation]. Therefore, since it must necessarily be demonstrated, it must necessarily be accepted; otherwise one would not accept even contradiction (<s>virodha</s>). For in contradiction, the absence of the reason [constitutes] essential non-establishment. In the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, inescapable non-thesis-property-hood [results]. Or, since contradiction first strikes the cognition, and since without demonstrating it, thesis-property-hood cannot be demonstrated, it must necessarily be accepted. This is the same elsewhere too — that is the meaning of what was stated. If so, how is the <s>bhāṣya</s> [to be understood] now? — to this he says: 'Thus...' Now, if this is the meaning intended by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>, why is not an illustration fitting to this [given]? — to this he says: 'And here...' Even so, the worldly illustration is inappropriate — to this he says: 'By the opponent's doctrine itself...' Now, where will this illustration fit among the five alternatives in one's own doctrine? — to this he says: 'That, again...'

children.text: // hetvābhāsalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: — The section on the definition of fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) —

children.text: // chalaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: — The section on equivocation (<s>chala</s>) —

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text: evaṃ yatnenodbhāvanīyapariharaṇīyahetvābhāsavaprakaraṇaṃ samarthitam /
atha sādhanavādī pramādī prativādī vā saduttarasamādhānayoraparisphūrtau tayorvijigīṣuḥ tadābhāsamapi brūyāditi tadābhāsavyutpādanāvasaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, a proponent stating a proof, if careless, or a respondent — when the proper reply and resolution are not manifest — desiring to win, may state even a semblance of those [replies]. Therefore there is occasion for the explanation of those semblances.

children.text: tatrāpi jāteḥ svapakṣavyāghātāpādakatvena jaghanyatvāt chalasya tu tātparyato duṣṭatve 'pi vacanato 'duṣṭattvādasphūrtidaśāyāmapi tadeva prayoktavyam /
children.translated_text: Among those too, since <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder) is inferior because of leading to the contradiction of one's own position, but <s>chala</s> (equivocation), although faulty in purport, is not faulty in verbal expression and should be employed even in the stage of non-manifestation [of the proper reply],

children.text: tasyāpyasphūrtau jātiriti viśeṣajñāpanārthaṃ jāteḥ pūrvaṃ chaloddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: and when even that [chala] is not manifest, [one resorts to] <s>jāti</s> — to convey this distinction, the enumeration of <s>chala</s> precedes that of <s>jāti</s>.

children.text: saiva lakṣaṇe 'pi saṃgatiriti bhāṣyārthamāha---uddeśeti //
children.translated_text: That very [ordering applies] to the definition too — he states the meaning of the <s>bhāṣya</s>: 'Enumeration...'
Thus, the section on fallacious reasons that must be diligently demonstrated and avoided has been validated.

children.text: nanvativyāpakamidaṃ lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Now, this definition is over-extensive.

children.text: arthavaicitryopapattyā vacanavighātasya jātāvapi saṃbhavādityata āha---yathā vakturiti /
children.translated_text: Since the disruption of speech through the justification of diversity of meaning is possible even in <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder) — to this he says: 'As of the speaker...'

children.text: iha vāgvṛttiviparyāsena pratyavasthānaṃ na tu tatreti bheda ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the distinction is that here, the response is through the reversal of the mode of speech, but not so there [in <s>jāti</s>].

children.text: nanu vibhāgo nodāhṛtaḥ tatkathaṃ vibhāge tūdāharaṇānīti bhāṣyamityata āha---vibhajyata iti // 10 //
children.translated_text: Now, the division was not illustrated — so how is the <s>bhāṣya</s> 'but in the division, the illustrations' [to be explained]? — to this he says: 'It is divided...'

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text: yadyevaṃ kathaṃ vibhāgaśceti kṛtvā vibhāgasūtrameva paṭhatītyata āha---vibhajyate 'neneti /
children.translated_text: If so, how is there a division? — with this thought, he simply reads the division-<s>sūtra</s> — to this he says: 'It is divided by this...'

children.text: uktipūrvakatvāt tātparyasya tadanusaṃdhānapūrvakatvādupacārasyoddeśakamaniyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since purport is preceded by utterance, and since figurative usage is preceded by the investigation of that [purport], the [ordering of] enumeration is not fixed.

children.text: tadanurodhācca lakṣaṇakramaniyamaḥ // 1.1 //
children.translated_text: And due to conformity with that, the ordering of definitions is also not fixed.

children.text:
pariśuddhiḥ
abhidhāvṛttisaṃcāro yatrac chale tadvākchalamiti lakṣaṇārthaḥ, vācīti viṣayasaptamī, bhramaṃ nivārayati---vāci nimitta iti /
nanvetat sarvacchalasādhāraṇamityata āha---navakambala ityādi /
tadidaṃ vākchalamuttaradaśāyāṃ navavidham /
tadyathā bhūbhṛdayaṃ vīryaśālī mahāvayavattvādityatra dharmipadasaṃcāreṇa na nakhaprasūnāñcitakarapallavo 'yaṃ nityakarmakaratvādityatra sādhyapadasaṃcāreṇa /
atā garbhavatī raktavilocanatvādityatrobhayapadasañcāreṇa /
tadetat pratijñāśrayaṃ trayam /
āḍhyo 'yaṃ navakambalatvādityatrāsiddhatvodbhāvanena /
gajo 'yaṃ viṣāṇītvādityatra virodhodbhāvanena /
durāloko 'sau rājā tejomayatvādityatrānaikāntikatvodbhāvanena /
tadetat hetvāśrayaṃ trayam /
duvyaṃ vāyuḥ sāvayavatvāt ambaravadityatra sādhanavikalatvena /
asmadādidurāsadāḥ tārakā gaganecaratvāt pataṅgavadityatra sādhyavikalatvena /
paśureṣa viṣāṇitvād govadityatrobhayavikalatvena /
tadetad dṛṣṭantāśra trayam /
pratyuttaradaśāyāṃ tu pratipakṣasādhane navavidhameva /
anyatra tu yāvaddūṣaṇabhedam /
tad yathā, anyathāsiddho 'siddhaśceti vyāghātaḥ kathamapi siddhatvāt /
sādhyaviparyayavyāpto 'yamiti, guṇa evānyathā sādhyābhedaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: 'This is pervaded by the opposite of the probandum' — then in the quality alone [it is] otherwise, because of the consequence of non-difference from the probandum.

children.text: ambareṇānaikāntikamityasaṅgatam, tasyāpyanityatvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Inconclusive through space' — this is inappropriate, since that [space] too is impermanent.

children.text: nāyaṃ pakṣī kuto 'sya pakṣabādhasaṃbhāvanetyādi svayamūhyam /
children.translated_text: 'This is not a bird (<s>pakṣin</s>), whence would there be the possibility of thesis-sublation (<s>pakṣabādha</s>) for it?' — and so forth is to be worked out by oneself.

children.text: asya pratyavasthānamityādi bhāṣyaṃ na pūrvasūtravyākhyānaṃ nottarasūtraparaṃ vetyata āha---tadetacchalamiti // 1.2 //
children.translated_text: 'The response to this...' and so forth — the <s>bhāṣya</s> is neither an explanation of the prior <s>sūtra</s> nor pertaining to the subsequent <s>sūtra</s> — to this he says: 'That very equivocation...'

<s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification). Where there is transference of the operation of expression — that is <s>vākchala</s> (verbal equivocation) — this is the meaning of the definition. '<s>Vāci</s>' — the locative is one of domain. He removes confusion: 'In the speech, the ground...' Now, this is common to all types of <s>chala</s> — to this he says: 'New-blanket...' and so forth. This verbal equivocation is, in the later stage [of counter-response], ninefold. Namely: 'This king is mighty, because of having great limbs' — by transference of the property-bearer word, [responding:] 'This one, adorned with fingernails and flowers on his palm, is not one who always performs action, because of [his being what the words literally denote].' 'This [woman] is one with child (<s>garbhavatī</s>), because of having red eyes' — by transference of both words [in the thesis]. This makes three [cases] based on the thesis. 'This man is wealthy, because of having new blankets' — by demonstrating unestablishedness [in the reason]. 'This is an elephant, because of having a tusk' — by demonstrating contradiction. 'That king is hard to approach, because of being radiant' — by demonstrating inconclusiveness. This makes three based on the reason. 'Wind is a substance, because of having parts, like space' — by showing the example as deficient in the proof. 'The stars, unreachable by us and others, because of moving in the sky, like moths' — by showing the example as deficient in the probandum. 'This is an animal, because of having horns, like a cow' — by showing the example as deficient in both. This makes three based on the example. But in the later stage [of counter-response], in establishing the counter-position, it is likewise ninefold. In other [stages], it is as extensive as the varieties of faults. For example: 'otherwise-established and unestablished' — this is self-contradictory, because it is somehow established.

children.text: sambhavator'thasyātisāmānyayogādasambhūtārthakalpanā sāmānyacchalam // 1.3 //
children.translated_text: The attribution of a non-existent meaning through the over-general applicability of a meaning that is possible — that is <s>sāmānyachala</s> (equivocation through generality). // [Sūtra] 1.3 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
yatra tātparyasaṃkrāntistat sāmānyacchalamiti sūtrārthaḥ /
tacca kvacit saṃbhavavidhiviśeṣyeṣu /
yathā saṃbhavadvidyācaraṇasaṃpadayaṃ brāhmaṇatvāt /
anityaḥ śabdaḥ /
śataṃ dvijātayo bhojitā iti /
kvacit tu hetutvoddeśaviśeṣaṇeṣu yathā brāhmaṇādupajāto 'yaṃ brāhmaṇatvāt /
anityaṃ kāryaṃ dvijaśataṃ bhojitamiti /
tadetat sarvaṃ vivakṣitamāpnoti cātyeti cobhayasamānaṃ cetyatisāmānyamucyate /
etannimittakaṃ chalaṃ sāmānyacchalamiti /
bhāṣyānurodhāt viśeṣaniṣṭhaṃ vyācaṣṭe---saṃbhavata iti /
tatrādyamudāharaṇaṃ sphuṭameva /
dvitīyaṃ tu, anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvādityukte dhaṭo 'pyanityaḥ tarhi kṛtakatvāt śabdaḥ syāt /
tṛtīyaṃ tu, śataṃ dvijātayo bhojitā ityukte śatasaṃkhyāvacchinnā api bhojitāḥ sanakādayo na dvijātaya iti /
caturthaṃ tu, brāhmaṇājjāto 'yaṃ brāhmaṇatvādityukte saṃbhāvanāviṣayo 'yamabhihito na heturiti /
children.translated_text: The fourth: when it is said 'this one is born from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, because of being a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' [the equivocator responds:] 'what has been stated is the domain of possibility, not a reason.'

children.text: pañcamaṃ tu, anityaṃ kāryamanityatvādityukte sādhyāviśiṣṭo heturiti /
children.translated_text: The fifth: when it is said 'the product is impermanent, because of impermanence,' [the equivocator responds:] 'the reason is not different from the probandum.'

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu, dvijaśataṃ bhojitamityukte dvijā bhojitāḥ, na tu tadmatā śatasaṃkhyeti /
children.translated_text: The sixth: when it is said 'a hundred twice-born have been fed,' [the equivocator responds:] 'twice-born were fed, but not the number hundred belonging to them.'

children.text: evaṃ pratyuttaradaśāyāmapyetat ṣaḍvidhameveti // 1.3 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the later stage [of counter-response] too, this is sixfold alone.

Where there is transference of purport — that is <s>sāmānyachala</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. And that [transference occurs] sometimes in qualifiers of the mode of possibility. For example: 'This one, possessing the possible combination of learning and conduct, because of being a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' 'Sound is impermanent.' 'A hundred twice-born have been fed.' And sometimes in qualifiers of the reason and the enumeration. For example: 'This one is born from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, because of being a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' 'The product is impermanent.' 'A hundred twice-born have been fed.' All this — what is intended, what is reached, and what exceeds, and what is common to both — is called 'over-general.' The equivocation based on this is <s>sāmānyachala</s>. In conformity with the <s>bhāṣya</s>, he explains it as resting on the specific: 'What is possible...' There, the first illustration is clear. But the second: when it is said 'sound is impermanent, because of being produced,' [the equivocator responds:] 'then a pot too is impermanent, because of being produced — [so] sound would be [identical to a pot].' The third: when it is said 'a hundred twice-born have been fed,' [the equivocator responds:] 'even the <s>Sanaka</s> sages and others, delimited by the number hundred, who were fed, are not twice-born.'

children.text: dharmavikalpanirdeśer'thasadbhāvapratiṣedha upacāracchalam // 1.4 //
children.translated_text: The denial of the existence of a meaning through the indication of a distinction of property is <s>upacārachala</s> (equivocation through figurative usage). // [Sūtra] 1.4 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
upacāravṛttivyatyayo yatra tadupacāracchalamiti lakṣaṇārthaḥ /
etadapyuttare najavidham /
tad yathā, ayaṃ māṇavakaḥ siṃhaḥ, ayaṃ siṃho rājñaḥ, ayaṃ puruṣasiṃho rājaśārdūlasyeti pratijñāmāritya trayam /
varṣāṣu nausaṃcāryeyaṃ bhūmirgaṅgātvāt, ghoṣāṇāṃ sukhavasatihetavaste deśā gaṅgātvāt, sa pradeśo dhanakāśādivano gaṅgātvāditi hetumāśrityatrayam /
ye dhvanihetavaste krośanti yathā mañcāḥ, ye krośanti te dhvanihetavo yathā mañcāḥ, ye krośanaprayojanavantaste krośanti yathā mañcāḥ, iti dṛṣṭāntamāśritya trayam /
pratyuttare tu pratisādhane tāvadeva /
anyatra tu yāvaddoṣabhedam /
tadyathā, aśarīratvāditi heturayamāśrayāsiddha ityukte naivam, hetvāśrayasyākāśasya siddhatvāt /
na ca heturasiddhatvādīnā dūṣyate api tu liṅgameva /
children.translated_text: And a reason is not vitiated by unestablished-ness and the like, but rather it is the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) itself [that is vitiated].

children.text: ato niranuyojyānuyogo bhavata ityādi dharmavikalpanirdeśaśabdenābhidhānadharmo dvedhābhidhīyata iti vārttikaikavākyatām āpādayituṃ bhūmiṃ racayitvā yathāśrutabhāṣyamupekṣya khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ vyācaṣṭe---śabdasyeti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'this constitutes cross-questioning what need not be questioned on your part' — and so forth. In order to bring into syntactic unity with the <s>vārttika</s> the word 'indication of a property-distinction' (<s>dharmavikalpanirdeśa</s>) — [meaning] that the property of expression is expressed in two ways — having prepared the ground and setting aside the <s>bhāṣya</s> as literally read, he explains segment by segment: 'Of the word...'

children.text: dyayapi neha sphuṭam tathāpyekatra vastusadbhāvaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: Although in neither [interpretation] is it clear here, nevertheless, in one case the real existence [of the meaning] is denied.

children.text: naiva kroṣṭāro mañcā iti parīkṣāvārttikamanāgatamavekṣyāha---vārttikamate tviti // 1.4 //
children.translated_text: 'Platforms do not cry out' — looking ahead to the examination-<s>vārttika</s> that has not yet come, he says: 'But in the view of the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>...'

Where there is reversal of figurative usage — that is <s>upacārachala</s> — this is the meaning of the definition. This too, in the counter-response stage, is ninefold. Namely: 'this boy is a lion,' 'this lion belongs to the king,' 'this man-lion [belongs to] the tiger-king' — by attacking the thesis, three. 'This land should be navigated by boat in the rainy season, because of being a <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' 'those regions are causes of comfortable habitation for cowherds, because of being a <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' 'that area is a forest of <s>Dhanakāśa</s> and the like, because of being a <s>Gaṅgā</s>' — by attacking the reason, three. 'Those that are causes of sound cry out, like platforms,' 'those that cry out are causes of sound, like platforms,' 'those that have the purpose of crying cry out, like platforms' — by attacking the example, three. In the counter-response, in counter-proof, it is just that much. In other [stages], it extends to the varieties of faults. For example: when it is said 'because of bodilessness, this reason has an unestablished substratum,' [one responds:] 'not so, because space, the substratum of the reason, is established.'

children.text: vākchalamevopacāracchalaṃ tadaviśeṣāt // 1.5 //
children.translated_text: Verbal equivocation is itself figurative equivocation, because of there being no distinction between them. // [Sūtra] 1.5 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
saṃgatirhi dvedhā bhavavati, antarbhāvalakṣaṇā ānantaryalakṣaṇā ca /
tatra na tāvat pūrvā chalaparīkṣāsūtrāṇāṃ lakṣaṇasyādhyāyārthatvāt /
adhyāyānantarbhūtasya cāhnikaprakaraṇayoḥ antarbhāvāt, parīkṣātvena dvitīyādāvevāntarbhāvārhatvācca /
children.translated_text: And because what is included in the chapter is included in the daily lesson and the section; and because, by virtue of being an examination, it deserves inclusion in the second [chapter] onward.

children.text: nāpyuttarā ṣoḍhāpyatra saṃbhāvyate, smārakābhāvena prasaṅgābhāvāt, tayā vinaiva prakṛtasiddheḥ, upodghātābhāvāt, jātinigrahasthānalakṣaṇāvarodhenāvasarābhāvāt, uttaraprabandhaṃ prati akāraṇatvena hetutvāyogāt, chalaparīkṣāyā uttaratrāvyavahāreṇānirvāhakatvāt, chalaparīkṣājātyādilakṣaṇasūtrāṇāṃ prakṛtopayogyekakāryāyogena tannibandhanāya api saṃgaterabhāvādityata āha---parīkṣāparvaṇa iti /
children.translated_text: Nor is the second [kind of connection] conceivable here in any of six ways: because of the absence of a reminder and hence the absence of a pretext; because the topic at hand is established even without it; because of the absence of a preliminary introduction; because of the absence of occasion due to the encroachment of the definitions of <s>jāti</s> and <s>nigrahasthāna</s>; because of the unsuitability of being a cause with respect to the subsequent text; because of the non-functionality of the examination of <s>chala</s> in the subsequent [context]; and because of the absence even of a connection based on the binding together of the <s>sūtras</s> defining <s>chala</s>-examination, <s>jāti</s>, and the like, since they do not serve a single purpose relevant to the topic at hand — to this he says: 'By the section of examination...'

children.text: prāsaṅgikī saṃgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: The connection is incidental (<s>prāsaṅgikī</s>).

children.text: prasaṅgāśca parīkṣāparvasannidhānenopodvalita ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the occasions [for discussion] are supported by the proximity of the examination-section — that is the meaning.

For connection is of two kinds: that characterized by inclusion and that characterized by sequence. Among these, the first, to begin with, [does not apply] to the <s>sūtras</s> examining equivocation, because the definition has the purpose of the chapter.

children.text: pṛthaksūtraṇāt sādharmyasahitāyā viśeṣānupalabdheśca saṃśaya /
children.translated_text: Because of separate formulation in a <s>sūtra</s> and because of the non-apprehension of a distinction along with similarity — [there is] doubt.

children.text: parīkṣitaṃ satsu vivacitaṃ sugrahaṃ supariharaṃ chalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti parīkṣāprayojanaṃ sphuṭīkṛtya pūrvapakṣamāha---yathā hīti /
children.translated_text: Having clarified the purpose of the examination — that equivocation, when examined among the established [categories], having been discriminated, will be easy to grasp and easy to counter — he states the prima facie view: 'For just as...'

children.text: lakṣaṇābhedādekatvamityarthaḥ // 1.5 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: unity, because of non-difference of definition.

children.text: na tadarthāntarabhāvāt // 1.6 //
children.translated_text: Not [so], because of the existence of that [equivocation] as a different matter. // [Sūtra] 1.6 //

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: — <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) —

children.text:
na tadarthāntarabhāvāditi siddhāntasūtram /
tatra ca bhāṣyam---anyārthāntarakalpanā, anyor'thasadbhāvapratiṣedha iti /
tadetadaviśadam, arthāntarakalpanāyā ubhayatrāpi pūrvapakṣe darśitatvāt /
arthasadbhāvapratiṣedhastu yathākathañcit sarvasādhāraṇaḥ anyathā vacanavidhātatvalakṣaṇakṣateḥ /
paramārthatastu na kvacidapi /
vārttikaṃ tu ekatra dharmaḥ pratiṣidhyate 'nyatra dharmīti /
etaccāsiddham /
na hyatra mañcā eva dharmiṇaḥ pratiṣidhyante /
api tu kambaladharmasaṃkhyāvat mañcadharmaḥ /
krośanamihāpi pratiṣidhyata ityata āha---vidheyaṃ vastviti /
children.translated_text: Since shouting is denied here too — to this he says: 'the subject-matter to be established...'

children.text: atraivottaraśaṅkāntaramapanayati---kiṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: He removes a further subsequent doubt in this very [context]: 'but indeed...'

children.text: tadetatsamādhānaṃ prakṛtodāharaṇāpekṣaṃ draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: This resolution should be seen as relative to the example under discussion.

children.text: sarvavyāpakaṃ tu mukhyopacāravṛttyanugatatvena anayorbhedakau niyatau dharmāviti // 1.6 //
children.translated_text: But the all-pervading [resolution is this]: since [the two types] follow the primary and figurative usages, the two distinguishing properties of these are fixed.

'Not so, because it is a different matter' — this is the <s>siddhānta</s>-<s>sūtra</s> (concluding <s>sūtra</s>). And therein, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [states]: 'the postulation of another matter, the denial of the existence of another matter.' But this is unclear, since the postulation of a different matter has been shown in the prima facie view in both cases. And the denial of the existence of the matter is, in some way, common to all [cases]; otherwise, the definition characterized by being [merely] the word of injunction would be violated. But in the ultimate analysis, [it obtains] nowhere at all. The <s>Vārttika</s>, however, [states]: 'in one [case], the property is denied; in the other, the property-bearer.' But this too is unestablished. For here it is not the case that the platforms (<s>mañcas</s>) alone as property-bearers are denied — rather, just as the blanket-property has number, so too the platform-property.

children.text: aviśeṣe vā kiñcitsādharmyādekacchalaprasaṅgaḥ //17 //
children.translated_text: Or, in the case of non-distinction, from some similarity [with the original statement], there would follow the consequence of [all equivocations being just] one <s>chala</s> (equivocation).

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: avi---ṅgaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: 'Non-...-gaḥ' //

children.text: // iti chalaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on <s>chala</s> (equivocation).

children.text: // purūṣāśaktiliṅgadoṣasāmānyalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: The section on the general definition of personal incapacity, fallacious marks, and faults.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: yadyapyasaduttaratayā jāteḥ chalaprakaraṇa evāntarbhāvo yuktaḥ, tathāpi pratijñāhānyādernigrahasthānasyāpi tathābhāvāt tāṃ saṃgatimupekṣyārthadūṣaṇatvābhiprāyeṇa prayogasya sāmyāduttaraprakaraṇa evāntarbhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although, as an invalid reply, the inclusion of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder) within the section on <s>chala</s> alone would be appropriate, nevertheless, since <s>pratijñāhāni</s> (abandonment of thesis) and the like — which are <s>nigrahasthānas</s> (points of defeat) — are also of that nature [i.e., invalid replies], setting aside that connection, and with the intention [of treating <s>jāti</s>] as censure of the substance [of the argument], its inclusion is in the subsequent section, owing to the similarity of its application.

children.text: tatrāntarbhūtāyāśca jāteḥ pṛthakkaraṇe uddeśa eva prayojanamuktam, pratijñāhānyādyapekṣayā cānudbhaṭāparādhatayā paravyāmohanahetutvāt, parājayadaśāyāṃ prayoktavyatvajñāpanārthaṃ tasmāt prāguddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the purpose of separately treating <s>jāti</s>, which is included therein, was stated in the enumeration itself — and because, in comparison with <s>pratijñāhāni</s> (abandonment of thesis) and the like, it is an offence that is not conspicuous, and thus serves as a cause of confusing the opponent — its enumeration is before those, for the purpose of communicating that it is to be employed when facing defeat.

children.text: saiva saṃgatirihāpītyāha---uddeśeti //
children.translated_text: That very connection [applies] here too — he says: 'the enumeration...'

children.text: chalasya samyagdūṣaṇasya ca ityupalakṣaṇam, pratijñāhānyāderityapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>chala</s> and of valid refutation' — this is an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>); '<s>pratijñāhāni</s> and the like' should also be understood [as included].

children.text: na ca chale ityupalakṣaṇaṃ tathaiva, tathāpi samyagdūṣaṇasyāvyudāsaḥ, tasyāpi hetuto vaidharmyeṇa hetvābhāsasādharmyeṇa pratyavasthānarūpatvādityata āha---na ceti /
children.translated_text: And the indication '[from] <s>chala</s>' is not [to be taken] in just that way — even so, valid refutation is not excluded, since it too has the form of a reply by showing dissimilarity from the reason and similarity with the fallacious reason — to this he says: 'and not...'

children.text: ayaṃ ca mātraśabdārtho jātīnāmavatāraṃ vāde pratiṣedhatā asaduttaratvakhyāpanenaiva sūtrakṛtā sūcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this meaning of the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely) — by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>, who prohibits the entry of <s>jātis</s> into <s>vāda</s> (honest debate) through the very communication that they are invalid replies — has been indicated.

children.text: bhāṣye jātipada vyutpādanaprayojanaṃ darśayati---jalpe hīti //18 //
children.translated_text: He shows the purpose of etymologically explaining the word '<s>jāti</s>' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'for in <s>jalpa</s>...'

children.text: vapratipattirapratipattiśca nigrahasthānam //19 //
children.translated_text: 'Misunderstanding (<s>vipratipatti</s>) and non-understanding (<s>apratipatti</s>) are the <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat).'

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text: nigrahasthānenaiva samastakathāmudraṇādarthato 'sya paścādabhidhānam /
children.translated_text: Since the entire <s>kathā</s> (debate) is sealed by the <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat) alone, its treatment comes last in terms of content.

children.text: tat kimityatra saṃgatyanusaraṇenetyāśayavān sūtraṃ pratyāharati---vipra---namiti // 19 //
children.translated_text: With the intention [of asking] 'why then the following of the connection here?' — he cites the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>vipra</s>—<s>nam</s>'...

children.text:
yadyapi lokavyavahārakathāvyavahārayoḥ puruṣasyāparādha eva nigrahasthānam /
aparāddho hi nigrahaṃ śāstiṃ khalīkāraṃ prāpnoti /
anyatra loke śarīraviḍambanā /
kathāyāṃ tvaparādhamātrodbhāvānamātram /
anyatra vādinoḥ kāmacāraḥ /
aparādhaśca kathāyāṃ vipratipattyapratipattibhāgadvayaparyavasitaṃ tātkālikamatattvajñānameva /
tathāpi tasya svarūpeṇodbhāvayitum---aśakyatvāt, nirarthakāpārthakādisāmānādhikaraṇyānupapatteśca tadunnayanopāyopalakṣaṇatayā sūtraṃ vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, since it is impossible to bring out [this non-knowledge] in its intrinsic form — and since there is no possibility of co-referentiality with 'meaningless,' 'absurd,' and the like — the <s>sūtra</s> has been explained as indicating the means of bringing that [non-knowledge] to light.

children.text: tena kathāyāṃ pravṛttayāṃ vādinoratattvajñānajñāpikā kriyā nigrahasthānamiti sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: in an ongoing debate, the action that reveals the non-knowledge of reality of the debaters is the <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat).

children.text: etacca pratijñāhānyādisāmānādhikaraṇyena prayuktanigrahasthānapadapadārthālocanayā /
children.translated_text: And this is readily understood through the co-referentiality with <s>pratijñāhāni</s> (abandonment of thesis) and the like, [and] by examining the meaning of the word '<s>nigrahasthāna</s>' as employed.

children.text: svarūpeṇa śakyodbhāvanapratipādakavārttikadarśanācca sugamam, bhāṣye 'pyanantarameva sphuṭībhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: And since the <s>Vārttika</s> shows that [non-knowledge] can be brought out in its intrinsic form, [this] is easily understood — and it will become clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> immediately following.

Although in both ordinary usage and debate usage, it is the person's offence alone that is the <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat) — for one who has committed an offence incurs punishment, chastisement, and humiliation. In the case of ordinary [life], [the punishment is] bodily affliction. But in debate, it is merely the bringing out of the offence alone — beyond that, the debaters [act] at their discretion. And the offence in debate is precisely the occasional non-knowledge of reality, which is exhaustively divided into the two parts of misunderstanding (<s>vipratipatti</s>) and non-understanding (<s>apratipatti</s>).

children.text:
syādetat, na pratipattervirītatvādanyat kṛtsitatvamityata āha---sūkṣmeti /
kathamasau nigrahasthānamiti /
kathamasau svarūpato 'pratīyamānaiva sattāmātreṇa nigrahasthānaṃ bhaviṣyati? na hyapratītameva paradāradharṣaṇaṃ nigrahāya paryāptamityarthaḥ /
vipratipadyamāna iti /
yato vipratipadyamānaḥ prāptaparājayo bhavati, ataḥ parājayaprāptidvāreṇa unnetuṃ śakyate /
atha parājayaprāptireva kā ityata uktam---nigrahasthānaṃ pratijñāhānyādi khalu spaṣṭam parājayaprāptiriti bhāṣyaṃ sphuṭamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, what then is this 'incurring of defeat'? — to this it has been said: '<s>nigrahasthāna</s> is <s>pratijñāhāni</s> (abandonment of thesis) and the like — clearly it is the incurring of defeat' — meaning: the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is clear.

children.text: yadyapyadhike vipratipattyapratipattī saṃbhavatastadasaṃbhave nigrahasthānatvānupapatteḥ, tathāpi vipratipannavastugocaratvena na tu tatreti tadanigrahasthānatvabhramanivāraṇārthamasamāsakaraṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although misunderstanding and non-understanding are possible in something beyond [the specific <s>nigrahasthānas</s>], and since in the absence of that [additional element], the status of <s>nigrahasthāna</s> would not hold — nevertheless, by virtue of having as its object the matter that is misunderstood, 'not in that [additional element]' — [meaning:] the non-compounding is for the purpose of preventing the error that that [additional element] is a <s>nigrahasthāna</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: adhikaṃ nāmetyupalakṣaṇam, punaruktamapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: 'Something beyond' is an indication — 'repetition' should also be understood [as included].

children.text: dūṣyaṃ vā ityāgāmipakṣāpekṣayā vāśabdaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: 'Or what is to be refuted' — the word '<s>vā</s>' (or) is with reference to the forthcoming alternative.

One might think: there is nothing other than completeness that is different from the extensiveness of understanding — to this he says: 'subtle...' 'How is that a <s>nigrahasthāna</s>?' — meaning: how can something that is not itself directly apprehended become a <s>nigrahasthāna</s> by mere existence? For the violation of another's wife, when not even cognized, is not sufficient for punishment — this is the meaning. 'One who misunderstands...' — since one who misunderstands has incurred defeat, therefore, through the avenue of incurring defeat, [the non-knowledge] can be brought to light.

children.text: // pariśuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Pariśuddhi</s> (Purification) //

children.text:
yathoddeśamiti---yathoddeśakramaṃ bhavatu lakṣaṇam, na tu lakṣaṇakramānatikrameṇa parīkṣā bhaviṣyati, prathamata eva vyatikramādityata āha---yathālakṣaṇaṃ yathāsvarūpamityartha iti /
nanvevaṃ sati prathamadvitīyasūtre tātparyāntareṇāvaṣṭabdhatvānna trividhaśāstrapravṛttyantarbhāvinī /
ārthyā vṛttyā prathamasūtrasya uddeśāntarbhāve 'pi dvitīyasūtramalagnakam asaṃgatikatvādityata āha---tasmāditi /
aupodghātikyā saṃgatyā prathamoddeśamaṅgatameva dvitoyasūtramarthāt /
śrutyā ca prayojanaparatayeti na prakaraṇāsaṃgatirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And through the literal [statement], being oriented toward the purpose — therefore there is no disconnection from the section — this is the meaning.

children.text: śeṣaṃ sūbodhamiti /
children.translated_text: The remainder is easily understood.

children.text: kīrttyata iti kīrtitam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kīrtyate</s>' (it is mentioned) means 'it has been mentioned.'

children.text: tathā ca yathāyogamabhisaṃbandha iti sukhabodhamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, the connection should be understood as appropriate — the meaning is that it is easily comprehended.

'In the order of enumeration' — let the definition be in the order of enumeration, but the examination will not proceed without transgressing the order of definitions, since the transgression [occurs] from the very first [definition] — to this he says: 'in the order of definitions means in the order of intrinsic nature.' Now, if this is so, since the first and second <s>sūtras</s> have been grasped through a different purport, they do not fall within the three-fold <s>śāstra</s>-operation. And even if the first <s>sūtra</s> is included in the enumeration through an implied usage, the second <s>sūtra</s> is unattached, since it has no connection — to this he says: 'therefore...' Through the preliminary connection (<s>aupodghātikī saṃgati</s>), the second <s>sūtra</s> is an adjunct to the first enumeration, implicitly.

children.text: anabhyāsajñeyācchrutivivaragarbheṣu laghutaḥ sukhagrāhyānmandaiḥ kusumasukumārāt prathamataḥ /
children.translated_text: From [the text] whose meanings hidden in the unfolding of the <s>śruti</s> are knowable without practice, [and] which is easily grasped by the slow-witted because of its lightness, [being] tender as a flower, from the very start —

children.text: manaḥ śrīmadvācaspativacanavinyāsavisarāt
children.translated_text: the mind, from the spreading arrangement of the words of the glorious <s>Vācaspati</s>,

children.text: trasatyadyāpyetanmuhuriva muhurnirvṛtamapi // 20 //
children.translated_text: even today trembles again and again, as if, even though it has attained bliss.

children.text: // iti puruṣāśaktiliṅgadoṣasāmānyalakṣaṇaprakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the general definition of personal incapacity, fallacious marks, and faults.

children.text:
// ityaudayanatātparyapariśuddhau prathamādhyāyasya dvitīyāhnikam
samāptaḥ prathamādhyāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second lesson of the first chapter of <s>Udayana</s>'s <s>Tātparyapariśuddhi</s>. The first chapter is complete.
